* The student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe. Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their eyes is a veil, and for them is a great punishment. And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers. They deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none except themselves, and they perceive not. In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie.﴾ [Al-Baqarah 6–10]
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve...﴾. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain﴾. This is coordinated with what preceded in His words: ﴿a guidance for the righteous (2) who believe in the unseen﴾, meaning ﴿and those who believe in what was revealed﴾. We have already said that it is permissible to coordinate attributes with one another, as in His words: ﴿Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High (1), who created and proportioned (2), and who destined and guided (3), and who brought forth the pasture﴾ [Al-A'la 1–4], although the basic principle regarding attributes is that they are not coordinated.
* Among the benefits of the verse: praise of those who believe in what was revealed to the Messenger (ﷺ) and what was revealed before him, and that this is one of the characteristics of the righteous, based on His words: ﴿And those who believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you﴾.
Also among the benefits of the verse: praise of those who are certain of the Hereafter. It has already been mentioned in the commentary that by certainty of the Hereafter is not meant merely believing that there is a day on which people will be resurrected, but believing in everything that the Book and the Sunnah report about what will occur on that day. Indeed, Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said: belief in the Last Day includes belief in everything the Prophet (ﷺ) informed about what happens after death [[Al-'Aqidah al-Wasitiyyah (p. 93)]].
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful﴾. This also describes their condition and their final outcome. As for their condition, He said: ﴿upon guidance from their Lord﴾, meaning upon knowledge and clear evidence. In this there is evidence for the soundness of their methodology, based on His words: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾.
* Also among its benefits: the Lordship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is both specific and general. His words ﴿from their Lord﴾ attribute the Lordship to these people only, but it is a specific Lordship which entails complete care for them.
* Also among its benefits: the final outcome of these people is success, based on His words: ﴿and those are the successful﴾.
* Among its benefits: success is specific to them, because this sentence ﴿and those are the successful﴾ conveys restriction (ḥaṣr).
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ This describes the second category of people, because in this surah Allah mentions the types and divisions of people: the first are the sincere believers, and the second, in this verse, are the pure disbelievers.
﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾: disbelieving in whom? They disbelieve in everything that must be believed in. They disbelieve in Allah, in His messengers, in His angels, in His books, in the Last Day, in destiny, its good and its bad, or similar things. The point is that it is general to everything that must be believed in. If they disbelieve in it, these are disbelievers.
Now, what if they disbelieve in only part of it? It is the same, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to make distinction between Allah and His messengers and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to adopt a way between that (150). Those are the disbelievers in truth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾ [An-Nisa' 150–151].
His words ﴿it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾: this is a clause transformed into a verbal noun (maṣdar) without any explicit verbal-noun particle. A clause that is turned into a verbal noun must normally be preceded by a maṣdarīyah particle, such as "anna" (that), "an" (that), "mā" (what) in its maṣdarī use, or "law" (if) in its maṣdarī use. But here it has been converted into a verbal noun even though none of these particles is present. However, when the word "sawā'" (equal) comes before it, as in ﴿it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾, it is converted into a verbal noun. The meaning is: it is all the same for them, your warning or its absence. The intended meaning concerns those disbelievers upon whom the word of punishment has been fulfilled. These will not believe, whether you warn them or not, because a seal has been placed upon their hearts, and Allah forbid. This does not mean that the Messenger (ﷺ) should not call them. Rather, the purpose is that he be consoled when they do not believe, and it is said: these have had their hearts sealed by Allah, so they do not believe.
His words ﴿it is all the same for them whether you warn them﴾: ﴿sawā'﴾ means that your warning and its absence are equal to them. The word ﴿warn﴾ (indhār) means informing with intimidation and frightening. ﴿or do not warn them﴾ is the second category.
Is this "am" (or) here connected or disconnected?
* A student: Connected.
* The Shaykh: It is connected. The connected "am" is the one that comes between two equivalent things, as here. The disconnected one comes between two separate things. This is a semantic difference. The verbal difference is that with the connected "am" the word "aw" (or) may replace it, while with the disconnected one "aw" cannot replace it, but rather "bal" (rather) replaces it. ﴿It is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ This sentence is the second predicate. Where is the first predicate? ﴿It is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾ is the first predicate, and His words ﴿they will not believe﴾ are the second predicate.
In this noble verse there is consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ), may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, when the disbelievers reject him and do not accept his call.
Also in it: whoever has the word of punishment fulfilled upon him will not believe, regardless of who warns him or calls him, because he gains nothing. His heart has been sealed. ﴿Is one upon whom the word of punishment has come due [to be saved]? Would you then save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [Az-Zumar 19]. That is, these have the Fire, and their matter is finished; you cannot rescue them.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if a person does not feel fear when admonished, nor turn toward Allah, then in him there is a resemblance to whom? To the disbelievers who are not admonished by admonitions and do not believe when called to Allah.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has set a seal upon their hearts.﴾ The word "khatm" (seal) means "ṭab'" (stamping/impressing), and its origin is the "khātam" (seal ring), because when writing ends, the writing is sealed, meaning the matter is over. These are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has placed a seal. Also, it resembles a container of provisions which is sealed with red wax, as they say, so its matter is concluded. ﴿Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing﴾, meaning and upon their hearing. When the hearts are sealed they cannot understand, and when the hearing is sealed it cannot hear in a way that benefits.
He said: ﴿and over their eyes is a veil﴾. This is a new sentence. A "ghishāwah" is a covering. When there is a veil over the eyes, they cannot see. Thus the three paths to guidance are closed: the heart, which is the first; the second, hearing what is said; and the third, sight of what is seen. So all three doors are shut. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you seen one who has taken his desire as his god, and Allah has sent him astray knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his sight a veil? Who then can guide him after Allah?﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 23]. No one can.
If someone asks: does this sealing have a cause, or is it a trial and test from Allah?
The answer: it has a cause which Allah explained in His words: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [Al-An'am 110], and in His words: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate, and Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ [As-Saff 5]. So when you see someone who has gone astray, know that he himself is the cause of his own misguidance.
﴿And for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿For them﴾ means for these disbelievers who remained upon their disbelief, there is a great punishment, which is the punishment of the Fire. Allah has magnified it because nothing is more severe than the punishment of the Fire. May Allah protect us and you from it by His generosity and bounty.
The discussion of the second category of creation, the pure and outright disbelievers, is concluded.
In this last noble verse is evidence that the hearts are the locus of understanding, based on His words: ﴿Allah has set a seal upon their hearts﴾, meaning that good does not reach them.
Also among its benefits: the paths to guidance are either through hearing or through sight, because guidance may come through hearing and it may come through sight: through hearing what is said, and through sight what is observed. Likewise, the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are both recited and heard, and both clear and visible.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the threat to these disbelievers of a great punishment, based on His words: ﴿and for them is a great punishment﴾.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.﴾ The "min" in ﴿And among the people﴾ is partitive. The sign of partitive "min" is that "baʿḍ" (some) can replace it. Here, if it were outside the Quran and he said "some of the people say," the sentence would be sound. So "min" is partitive. ﴿Among the people, those who say﴾: "man" (those who) is a postponed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar). ﴿Those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day"﴾: but they say this with their tongues, not in their hearts. That is why He said ﴿but they are not believers﴾, not believers in what?
* The students: (...)
* The Shaykh: You did not hear.
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Alright, and they are not believers in their hearts. But with their tongues they say: "We believe in Allah and the Last Day." Indeed, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you﴾, after ﴿And if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 4]. They tempt people by their appearance and by hearing their words, but there is no good in them. Whoever wishes to know the characteristics of the hypocrites should consult the book Madarij al-Salikin. Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) gathered all their characteristics in a single discussion, so whoever wants to review them should do so.
He says: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day."﴾ He mentioned belief in Allah because He is the one from whom things begin, Glorified and Exalted, meaning the One from whom affairs originate. And the Last Day, because it is the end. When a person believes in Allah and the Last Day, he is set upon righteousness. That is why Allah always pairs belief in Him with the Last Day, without mentioning belief in the angels, the books, and the messengers, because the reality is that whoever does not believe in the Last Day will never believe in Allah. Why? What does he gain? What does he expect? If he does not believe in the Last Day, he will not believe in Allah.
He said: ﴿but they are not believers﴾. This is a refutation of their statement: ﴿We believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, like the saying of Allah the Exalted refuting them: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars (1). They have taken their oaths as a shield and averted [people] from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 1–2].
Then He said: ﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none except themselves, and they perceive not.﴾ [Al-Baqarah 9]. In another reading: ﴿and they do not deceive except themselves﴾. ﴿They deceive﴾: "al-mukhādaʿah" is a form of "al-khidāʿ" (deception). Deception, cunning, and scheming are all close in meaning, and this definition covers them: reaching the harming of the opponent from a direction he does not perceive. That is deception, and that is cunning. When they say they are believers, they think: we have profited now. They say: we have gained, because we have deceived Muhammad and his companions. But in reality, did they deceive the Messenger and his companions? They deceived Allah. That is why He said: ﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe,﴾ and at the head of those who believe is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: ﴿but they deceive none except themselves﴾: in reality they deceive themselves, because they have deluded themselves by showing the opposite of what they conceal, while knowing that what the Messenger (ﷺ) said is true. But they did not believe in it; rather they denied it, so they deceived themselves by that. If someone asks: what is the meaning of their deceiving Allah and those who believe? We say: the way they deceive is that when they show belief, their wealth and lives are preserved.

This deception and scheming reaches its target against the opponent without his noticing. This is deception itself. When these people say they are believers, they win (*ghanimna*). They say, "We have gained, because we have deceived Muhammad and his Companions." But in reality, did they deceive the Messenger and his Companions? No. They deceived Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe﴾ [al-Baqarah 9], and at the head of those who believe is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He the Exalted said: ﴿And they deceive none but themselves﴾, meaning they deceive themselves in reality, because they have brought ruin upon themselves (*gharrawha*) by displaying the opposite of what they conceal, while they know that what the Messenger (peace be upon him) said is true. But they did not believe in it. Rather, they denied it, and so they deceived themselves by this.

If someone asks: What is the meaning of their deceiving Allah and those who believe? We say: The meaning of their deceiving is that when they display faith, their wealth and their lives are spared from being killed, and they gain a standing (*hurmah*). So they say, "We deceived Muhammad and his Companions, when we said we are believers, while we are not believers." But by this statement they are spared from being treated as the disbelievers are treated.

He the Exalted said: ﴿And they deceive none but themselves and they perceive not﴾, meaning they have no awareness by which they could realize that they are deceiving themselves, because over their sight is a covering, their hearts are sealed, and so is their hearing.

* Student: Sometimes in the Qur'an, success (*al-falah*), faith, and reflection (*al-tadabbur*) are attributed to the heart, and sometimes they are linked to the intellect (*al-'aql*). What is the connection?
* Shaykh: For example?
* Student: ﴿And none will be reminded except those of understanding﴾ [al-Baqarah 269].
* Shaykh: Which intellects? But what is meant here by intellects is the intellect of right judgment, not the intellect of perception.
* Student: And the heart, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: The heart is the seat of the intellect. For this reason He the Exalted said: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth so that they would have hearts by which to understand?﴾ [al-Hajj 46] ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj 46].
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The Prophet (ﷺ) refrained from killing the hypocrites, lest people say that Muhammad kills his own companions. So people in this matter are of two extremes and a middle. Some people follow others in everything and watch them. Others say, "What concern is people's affairs to me, as long as I am walking the right path?" What is the criterion for watching people?
* Shaykh: The criterion is that a person is entrusted with his own religion, and no one is required to watch another in his religion, ever. The exception is when there is a strong suspicion and one wishes to verify it. Otherwise, it is not obligatory, because the principle is that the Muslim is respected: respected in his honor, respected in his wealth, respected in his self.
* Student: No, Shaykh, some people, when you tell them, "Do not do such and such, people think such and such about you," they say, "I do not care about people. Let people say what they say."
* Shaykh: Do you mean that he intends to enjoin good and forbid evil?
* Student: No, anything, even in ordinary dealings.
* Shaykh: It is not prevented. What is proper for a person is to keep away from this matter, because the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Among what people have obtained from the words of the first prophethood is: If you feel no shame, then do as you wish."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3484) from the hadith of Abu Mas'ud al-Badri.]]
* Student: Shaykh, does the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sight away, just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am 110] not support the view of some scholars that the one whose apostasy is repeated is not accepted, due to His words: ﴿the first time﴾?
* Shaykh: Yes, if it is taken as such. But sometimes Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants, so the apostasy is repeated and Allah bestows upon him sincere faith. We say that the one whose apostasy is repeated must be treated with caution. It is not enough for him merely to say that he has believed and repented for the killing to be lifted from him. Rather, we examine his case.
* Student: The Exalted says: ﴿Those who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them﴾ [al-Baqarah 3]. Is there not here evidence for the disbelief of one who abandons prayer?
* Shaykh: What is its argument?
* Student: Its argument is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: ﴿Those who believe in the unseen and establish prayer﴾, the wording of the verse, faith... (...)
* Shaykh: How?
* Student: After that He mentioned ﴿and spend from what We have provided for them﴾?
* Shaykh: Zakah?
* Student: Yes. The wording of the verse: ﴿Those who believe in the unseen and establish prayer﴾ is a condition (...)
* Shaykh: This is not clear. I have other evidence for it besides this.
* Student: May Allah forgive you. A question about the tafsir (exegesis) that has passed. Shaykh, may we affirm the attribute of mockery (*al-tahakkum*) for Allah, from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Give good tidings to the hypocrites﴾ [al-Nisa' 138]?
* Shaykh: No. If we say that "bashshir" (give good tidings) in the sense of what is harmful, Arabic usage establishes that what is meant is mockery of them. The Messenger, if he gave them good tidings of this kind, would not be giving them good news that pleases them, but would be mocking them.
* Student: Allah, glory be to Him, often mentions interrogative forms in the Qur'an as a means of mocking the disbelievers. Is it valid to mention..?
* Shaykh: The requirement of Arabic is that this interrogation be called mockery, so Allah is mocking them.
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: Yes, a verbal form.
* Student: Was Abu al-Hasan (al-Ash'ari) an Ash'arite or a Mu'tazilite?
* Shaykh: He was a Mu'tazilite. Then, after forty years of Mu'tazilism, he associated with 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Kullab, the founder of the Kullabiyyah school, and took some of his views. He remained on that for a period that was not long. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted him success to adopt the view of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him.
* Student: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?" Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah 13].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. The Blessed and Exalted Allah said: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾.
* In this noble verse there are benefits. Among them: the explicit identification of this category of people, who are the hypocrites: ﴿those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾.
* Among its benefits: the negation of the description from one in whom it is not fully realized from one side, because they say they are believers, but they are believers only outwardly, not inwardly. For this reason He said: ﴿but they are not believers﴾, meaning inwardly.
* Among its benefits: that outward submission, if it is not based on creed, is void and of no benefit, because of His saying: ﴿but they are not believers﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever inverts realities and claims attributes he does not possess resembles whom? The hypocrites. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) made the sign of the hypocrite threefold, among them: "When he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (33) and Muslim (59/107) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]
* Among the benefits of this verse and what follows it: that the hypocrites deceive Allah and those who believe, so it is derived from this that deception is among the characteristics of the hypocrites. If someone says: Tawriyah (equivocation, using a statement with a double meaning) contains a kind of deception, so does the one who uses tawriyah become characterized by the attributes of the hypocrites, because he displays the opposite of what he intends? The answer is that tawriyah, when it has a valid purpose, takes one out of resemblance to the hypocrites, and when it has no valid purpose, it is feared that the person resembles the hypocrites. For this reason Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, prohibited tawriyah except for a need or a necessity.[[See: A'lam al-Muwaqqi'in by Ibn al-Qayyim (3/234), Dar al-Jil edition.]] But most scholars say that tawriyah which does not wrong anyone is permissible.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: ﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe﴾, the permissibility of conjoining someone other than Allah with Allah by a particle that implies association, because of His saying: ﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe﴾, and He did not say: "then those who believe." The reason for this is that the cause is one: their deceiving Allah is deceiving the believers, and their deceiving the believers is deceiving Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This differs from cosmic matters. Whatever is mentioned other than Allah must be conjoined with "thumma" (then), because cosmic matters relate to lordship (*rububiyyah*), and in what relates to lordship our action follows the action of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This differs from legislative matters. For this reason Allah the Exalted said in many verses, or attributed a thing to Himself and to His Messenger with "wa" (and) in many verses, but these are in legislative matters.
* Among the benefits of this verse: whoever deceives Allah and the believers is only deceiving himself, because they will deal with him outwardly, and he continues in this falsehood. There is no doubt that this is self-deception, since he thinks he is right, so he continues in his action and deceives himself by it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these hypocrites deceive Allah and those who believe, while in reality they deceive themselves, but they have no awareness within themselves. For this reason they persisted in this, and if they had been aware that they were deceiving themselves, they would not have persisted in it.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, said: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾.

The basmalah (the phrase "In the name of Allah...") has been discussed for us many times and repeatedly. We said that the prepositional phrase is dependent on an omitted element, and this omitted element is estimated as a delayed verb appropriate to the context. So, when you say "In the name of Allah" while you want to eat, how do you estimate the verb? "In the name of Allah I eat." Good. We said that it must be estimated as dependent on an omitted element. Why? Why do we not say that it is not dependent? Because the prepositional phrase must have something it depends on:

*The prepositional phrase must have a governing element,*
*a verb or its meaning, like "murtaqi".*

Because the prepositional phrase is a governed element, and it has the position of a direct object, it must have a governing element. Why did we estimate it as a delayed verb?

For two benefits. The first benefit: seeking blessing by placing the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, first. The second benefit: restriction (*hasr*), because delaying the governing element conveys restriction, as if you were saying: "I do not eat blessing or seeking help by the name of anyone except the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Why did we estimate it as a verb? Because the original in governing is verbs. People of grammar know this: the original in governing is verbs. For this reason nouns do not govern except under conditions. The active participle governs like a verb under conditions; the verbal noun governs like a verb under conditions; the passive participle governs like a verb under conditions. Does the verb govern under conditions? No, because it is the original in governing. For this reason we estimate it as a verb. Why did we estimate it as specific? Because it is more indicative of the intended meaning. We could estimate: "In the name of Allah I begin," but begin with what? We do not know: begin eating, begin drinking, begin ablution, begin work. If you say "In the name of Allah I eat" and specify the verb, it is more indicative of the intended meaning. For this reason the Messenger (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever has not slaughtered, let him slaughter in the name of Allah,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (985) and Muslim (1960/1), from the hadith of Jundub ibn Sufyan.]] or he said: "upon the name of Allah," so he specified the verb. So we say: the prepositional phrase is dependent on an omitted element. Complete it.

* Students: Appropriate.
* Shaykh: Delayed...
* Students: Appropriate.
* Shaykh: A verb appropriate to the situation. As for ﴿Allah﴾, it is the proper name for the essence of Allah, glory be to Him, for the sacred Essence; it belongs to none but Him, and it is the root of the names. For this reason the names come following it: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," they come following it.

﴿Ar-Rahman﴾: possessor of vast mercy. For this reason it came in the pattern "fa'lan," which indicates fullness and vastness.

﴿Ar-Rahim﴾: the One who conveys mercy to whom He wills of His servants. For this reason it came in the pattern "fa'il," which indicates the occurrence of an act. So here, mercy is His attribute, indicated by ﴿Ar-Rahman﴾, and mercy is His act, meaning the conveyance of mercy to the one shown mercy, indicated by ﴿Ar-Rahim﴾.

Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim are two of Allah's names that indicate the Essence, the attribute of mercy, and the effect or ruling indicated by that meaning. Is that not so? Thus these two names combine everything that must be connected to faith in the name of Allah, because faith in the name of Allah must be: that you believe in the name, and then what? The attribute and the effect, which is the ruling that follows from it. So we say: Allah is Merciful, possessor of mercy, and He shows mercy. All of these are present in the Qur'an. ﴿Ar-Rahman﴾ as you see. Possessor of mercy: ﴿And your Lord is the Free of need, possessor of mercy﴾ [al-An'am 133]. He shows mercy: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills﴾ [al-'Ankabut 21]. ﴿Ar-Rahman﴾ is a name indicating mercy, and it is true mercy, indicated by both revelation and reason. Is the language of the Arabs Arabic or not?

* Students: Arabic.
* Shaykh: Arabic. It is indicated by revelation and reason. And what is meant by revelation?
* Students: The texts... the texts.
* Shaykh: The texts of the Book and the Sunnah. Reason: contemplation and reflection. The indication of revelation on the mercy of Allah is countless. The indication of reflection is that we say: how much blessing is there in the world? How much blessing is there in the world? And what is the answer? It cannot be counted: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [al-Nahl 18]. Thus it cannot be counted in its kinds and types, let alone its individuals. These blessings, what do they indicate? They indicate that the Bestower is merciful. They indicate that the Bestower is merciful, and had there been no mercy, the blessing would not have come about. And how much averting of calamity is there in the world? Is that not so? By what?
From the effects of mercy: had there been no mercy, calamity would not have been averted. And it is strange that a people who claim reason say that mercy is not indicated by reason, but that reason indicates the opposite. I seek refuge in Allah! Why? They said: because mercy is tenderness, softness, submission, and gentleness, and this does not befit Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Look at Satan. It does not befit Him, is that correct? We say: mercy in this sense, whose mercy is it?

* Student: Man's.
* Shaykh: The mercy of a created being. But the mercy of the Creator is not like the mercy of the created being. Then we also forbid that mercy be as you claim even in created beings. If a king of complete authority, who fears no one except Allah, shows mercy to this poor man, do we say that his mercy contradicts the power and the fitting greatness he possesses? Never. It does not contradict it, and no one says: "By Allah, this is a contemptible king, for he shows mercy to the poor and shows mercy to the weak." No, rather this is counted as part of his perfection. Then we say to them: reason indicates it. Reason indicates it. We deny your claim that reason does not indicate it, and we say that reason does indicate it. If you ask a common man in the market, after rain fell during the night and people went out walking in the rain, the dampness of the rain and the moisture in the air, and you meet a common man and say, "How wonderful, it rained last night," he will say, "Yes," and "Allah," "Praise be to Allah, the mercy of Allah is vast, the mercy of Allah is vast." And how do we know this rain came from where? From mercy. But they say: "Will" (*al-irada*) was established by reason. The will of Allah was established by reason. Fine, by what?
They say: it was established by specification (*al-takhsis*), that He specified this: make this the sky, make this the earth, this a cow, this a sheep, this a camel, this a donkey, and so on. The one who specified this from that is the will. Therefore there is a will of Allah indicated by specification. Ask a student of knowledge, not a common man: "How do you use reason to establish the will of Allah?" What will he say to you? He cannot. Perhaps he can say: "I establish the will of Allah. This whole universe is by the will of Allah." But he does not say the word "specification" and does not indicate the will. Is that right or not?
And yet, mercy, according to them, was not indicated by reason, while will was indicated by reason. We say: both will and mercy are indicated by reason, and there is no doubt about this.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 1–9 (part 6 of 6):

The basmalah: we mentioned earlier that it is undoubtedly a verse of the Qur'an, independent, not attached either to what comes before it or what comes after it, independent. But it is recited at the beginning of the surah. Every surah begins with the basmalah except one surah, which is Bara'ah (at-Tawbah). It was not established for the Companions that the Messenger ﷺ began it with the basmalah. For this reason they placed a separator between it and al-Anfal but did not write a basmalah, because they were uncertain whether it was part of al-Anfal or independent. They said: "We will place the separator but not the basmalah." The basmalah is an independent verse that begins every surah, even al-Fatihah, which is the first surah that it begins. Is it part of the surah? We say: No. On this basis, what appears in the mushaf (the codified Qur'an) today, numbered as the first verse of al-Fatihah, is the weaker view. The stronger view is that it is not a verse of al-Fatihah, and the evidence for the preponderance of this view has already passed us.

* Student: Shaykh, we pray that Allah grants us victory over the disbelievers, but we cannot fight them. So we pray to Allah and do not fight them. Either He strengthens us so we fight them, or He grants us victory over them?

* Shaykh: Yes, he asks: We pray that Allah gives us victory over the disbelieving people, and we have no weapons with which to resist them. We say: victory over the disbelieving people is that Allah prepares for us weapons with which we resist them, or destroys their weapons. The destruction of their weapons is a victory for us, or not?

* Student: Shaykh, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr 9]. The scholars differ over whether the basmalah is a verse or not. Would this not lead to the basmalah being deleted?

* Shaykh: No, no, I seek refuge in Allah! Has it been deleted from the mushaf? It has been preserved.

* Student: (...)

* Shaykh: No, we say it is a verse by consensus, that it is a verse. But is it part of the surah that follows, or not? The disagreement is about the count.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. (1) Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. (2) He has sent down upon you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it, and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel (3) before, as guidance for the people﴾ [Ali 'Imran 1–4].

* Shaykh: ﴿Before﴾ is attached to what precedes it.

* Student: ﴿And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel (3) before, as guidance for the people, and He revealed the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3–4].

* Shaykh: Enough. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. We have already discussed the basmalah in terms of its i'rab (grammatical analysis, the case endings and structure of its words), its meaning, and its position in the sentence. We have also discussed the disjointed letters with which some surahs begin.

The disjointed letters with which Allah began some surahs: it has been said that they are symbols and indications of things, and some exegetes specified what they indicate. It has also been said that they are letters whose meaning we do not know, and Allah knows best what He intended by them. It has further been said that they are simply letters of the alphabet with no meaning. This last view is the correct one, because this Qur'an was revealed in clear Arabic, and Arabic does not give these letters a meaning. Since Arabic does not give them a meaning, by the very fact that the Qur'an was revealed in it, they must have no meaning. However, some of the discerning scholars said: they have a significance (maghza), meaning these letters carry a purpose. That purpose is this: the Qur'an, which rendered the most eloquent Arab orators incapable, was composed of the very letters that they know and out of which they construct their speech, and yet it defeated them. In other words, if it had come in a non-Arabic language, they would have said: "We are powerless before it." But it came in the Arabic language, in which they form their speech, using the very letters from which this Qur'an was composed. He said: For this reason you will hardly find a surah beginning with these disjointed letters that is not followed by mention of the Qur'an. This is what az-Zamakhshari, Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and a group of scholars said.

As for His saying: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾: this is a sentence composed of a subject and predicate. Allah is the subject, and the clause ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾ is the predicate. This clause is itself a sentence, but grammarians call it the "minor sentence" (al-jumlah as-sughra), because when the predicate is a clause, it is the minor sentence. The "major sentence" (al-jumlah al-kubra) is the whole of the subject and predicate together.

As for His saying: ﴿the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾, these are two further predicates. ﴿The Ever-Living﴾ is a second predicate of ﴿Allah﴾, and ﴿the Sustainer of existence﴾ is a third predicate.

Allah (﴿Allah﴾) is a proper name designating the sanctified Essence, the proper name of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Its origin is al-Ilah, meaning "the one worshipped," and the hamzah was dropped for ease of pronunciation, just as the hamzah was dropped from khayr and sharr in the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "The best rows of men are the first of them, and the worst of them are the last of them" [reported by Muslim (440/132), from Abu Hurayrah], meaning the "more excellent" and "more evil." Similarly, the hamzah was dropped from an-nas (the people), whose origin is unas.

Allah is a proper name for the sanctified Essence, and it is the most definite of all proper nouns in an absolute sense. Its meaning is "the one worshipped with love and reverence." It is an intensive form (fa''al) used in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ul), and very often fa'al comes in the sense of maf'ul, as in ghiras meaning "planted" (maghrus) and bina' meaning "built" (mabni).

As for His saying: ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾, it means: there is no true object of worship except Him. Ilah is the noun of the negation la (la of generic negation), and its predicate is omitted, its estimated form being "true" (haqq). There are false deities, but they are called gods only because names were placed upon them without right, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You worship besides Him nothing but names that you have named﴾ [Yusuf 40]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Is the male for you and the female for Him? That, then, is an unjust division. They are not but names you have named, you and your forefathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [an-Najm 19–23].

With this estimation of the predicate in ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾, the difficulty is resolved. The difficulty is: how can deity be negated in a sentence like this, and affirmed in a verse like His saying: ﴿Their deities that they invoked besides Allah did not avail them anything﴾ [Hud 101]?

The reconciliation: those deities are false. As for the deity in ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾, it is a true deity: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾ [al-Hajj 62].

As for His saying: ﴿Him﴾, this is a pronoun and not a proper noun, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ [Muhammad 19]. Is this a proper noun or a pronoun?

* The students: A proper noun.

* Shaykh: A proper noun. And as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya' 25]. Here "Me" (anaa) is a pronoun. So we say: "Anaa" and "huwa" in His saying ﴿there is no deity except Me﴾ [an-Nahl 2] and His saying ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾ are both separate nominative pronouns. Both are separate nominative pronouns. Just as the one who remembers Allah does not say "there is no deity except I," so too the one who remembers Allah should not make "Huwa" a name of Allah. Thus, we come to know the falsehood of the dhikr of the Sufis, who remember Allah by saying "Huwa, Huwa" and believe this dhikr is the best of remembrances, and it is a false remembrance.

As for His saying: ﴿the Ever-Living﴾: the definite article here is for totality (istighraq), meaning the one who possesses complete life. The life of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is complete in its existence and complete in its duration. He is living, without beginning and without end. His life was not preceded by non-existence, nor will it be followed by cessation. It is also complete in its state of existence, and no deficiency enters it in any respect. He is complete in His hearing, His knowledge, His power, and all His attributes.

When we look at a human being, or indeed anything other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, we find that its life is deficient in duration and in existence. Its life is preceded by what? By non-existence, and followed by cessation and annihilation. Its existence is also deficient. Is it complete in hearing? The living creature is not complete in hearing, nor in sight, nor in knowledge, nor in power. Every living creature is deficient. Therefore its life is deficient in existence and in duration: in duration, it is preceded by non-existence and followed by cessation; in existence, it is deficient in all attributes.

As for His saying: ﴿the Sustainer of existence﴾, it is on the pattern fai'ul, derived from qiyam (standing), and its meaning is: the one who stands by Himself, and the one who sustains others. He stands by Himself, so He needs no one. And He sustains others, so everyone is in need of Him. In the combination of these two noble names, ﴿the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾, their combination comprises all the perfections with which Allah is described. In ﴿the Ever-Living﴾ is the perfection of attributes, and in ﴿the Sustainer of existence﴾ is the perfection of actions, and in both together is the perfection of the Essence. ﴿The Ever-Living﴾ is the perfection of attributes, ﴿the Sustainer of existence﴾ is the perfection of actions, and their combination is the perfection of the Essence. So He is perfect in attributes, actions, and essence.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. (1) Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. (2) He has sent down upon you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it, and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel (3) before, as guidance for the people, and He revealed the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution. (4) Indeed, nothing on earth or in the heaven is hidden from Allah﴾ [Ali 'Imran 1–5].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. We have already explained the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. (1) Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾, and we showed that the preponderant view regarding ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim﴾ and its counterparts is as follows.

* Student: Did they not choose (...) that the disjointed letters have no meaning?

* Shaykh: No, he did not say they have no meaning.

* Student: Does it not indicate significance, that this Qur'an, which challenges you, is composed of these letters? That is why, whenever the letters are mentioned, something of the Qur'an is mentioned after them, from its mention or (...)?

* Shaykh: Good.

* Student: We said that the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language.

* Shaykh: No, no.

* Student: They have no meaning in themselves, but they have significance.

* Shaykh: But they have significance. Good. What is the evidence that they have no meaning in themselves?

* Student: The evidence is that the Qur'an always follows them.

* Shaykh: What is the evidence that they have no meaning?

* Student: That the Qur'an is in clear Arabic, and these letters are in clear Arabic, and they have no meaning.

* Shaykh: Correct. The evidence is that the Qur'an was revealed in clear Arabic, and these letters have no meaning in the Arabic language in themselves. Therefore they have no meaning. Good. What is the evidence that they have significance?

* Student: These letters are followed by the Qur'an.

* Shaykh: The mention of the Qur'an and speaking about it.

* Student: Second point: these letters that you know and speak with, the noble Qur'an is composed of them.

* Shaykh: "Minha" (out of them) is better than "murakkab" (composed). Now, His saying: ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾: what does it mean?

* Student: There is no object of worship in truth except Allah, Glorified and Exalted.

* Shaykh: "No object of worship in truth"? There is no true object of worship except Allah. Why do we not say that the negation applies to what comes after "illa" (except)? That is, "there is no deity except Allah," meaning there is no deity other than Allah?

* Student: Because there are deities, but they are false. We confine it to the true one.

* Shaykh: Excellent. Yes, we say: it is impossible to negate divinity absolutely, because other than Allah may be called a deity.

What is the evidence for applying the term "deity" to other than Allah?

* Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they have taken besides Allah deities, that they might be for them a source of might﴾ [Maryam 81].

* Shaykh: Yes. ﴿And do not set up with Allah another deity﴾ [al-Isra' 39], ﴿Their deities that they invoked besides Allah did not avail them anything﴾ [Hud 101].

﴿The Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾: we mentioned that these two include the Greatest Name of Allah. Why?

* Student: Because they have two meanings: the temporal meaning, that non-existence did not precede it...

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: Because they are two names that include the attributes of action and of essence.

* Shaykh: Correct. The perfection of essence and of action. In ﴿the Ever-Living﴾ is the perfection of essence, and ﴿the Sustainer of existence﴾ is the perfection of action. Therefore the two include all perfection, essential and active. What is the explanation of ﴿the Ever-Living﴾?

* Student: The Ever-Living who does not die, and...

* Shaykh: That is, the one possessing complete life that was not preceded...?

* Student: By non-existence.

* Shaykh: And that cessation does not reach?

* Student: Cessation.

* Shaykh: Cessation. What is ﴿the Sustainer of existence﴾?

* Student: He is the one who stands by Himself, and who stands over...

* Shaykh: Over others. Standing by Himself and standing over others. What is the evidence for His standing by Himself?

* Student: That Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is free of need from the worlds, and needs no one.

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: As for the evidence that everything other than Him...

* Shaykh: So the description of being free of need is like His saying: ﴿He is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ and ﴿But they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was free of need, and Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [at-Taghabun 6]. This is His standing by Himself. What is the evidence for His standing over others?

* Student: That all servants are poor before Allah, Glorified and Exalted.

* Shaykh: What is the evidence? What is the rationale?

* Student: ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah﴾ [Fatir 15].

* Shaykh: And others. Is there a clear verse on the subject?

* Student: His saying: ﴿Then is He who is standing over every soul in what it has earned [like one who does not]?﴾ [ar-Ra'd 33].

* Shaykh: Correct. His saying: ﴿Then is He who is standing over every soul in what it has earned﴾ means: like one who does not stand by himself. The conjugation of al-Qayyum in the Arabic language, how is it conjugated?

* Student: On the pattern fai'ul.

* Shaykh: On the pattern fai'ul. And what does this form indicate?

* Student: It indicates (...), Glorified and Exalted.

* Shaykh: No. This form, because its root is qa'im, was changed to qayyum, so fa'il was changed to fai'ul?

* Student: He stands over others and stands by himself.

* Another student: It indicates abundance and intensification.

* Shaykh: Intensification. Correct.

* * *

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He has sent down upon you the Book in truth﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3]. ﴿Sent down﴾: tanzil (sending down) occurs from above to below, and occurs gradually, little by little, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated [in revelation] that you may recite it to the people over a duration, and We have sent it down in stages﴾ [al-Isra' 106]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart﴾ [al-Furqan 32].

That is, We sent it down not all at once. So His saying ﴿sent down﴾ indicates that this Qur'an is from Allah, and that it was sent down how? Gradually, not once. As for His saying ﴿upon you﴾, the pronoun refers to the Messenger ﷺ. Allah the Exalted has explained in another verse that it was sent down upon the heart of the Messenger ﷺ, so that it would be more conducive to his retention of this Qur'an which was revealed to him.

As for His saying ﴿He has sent down upon you the Book﴾: "the Book" is this Qur'an. It is on the pattern fa'al in the sense of maf'ul (passive participle), because it is written (maktub). It is a kitab (book) because it is written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an, in a Book well-protected﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 77–78], the Preserved Tablet. It is also a book in the scrolls held by the angels: ﴿So whoever wills will remember it. [It is] in honored scrolls﴾ [Abasa 12–13]. And it is a book in the pages that are in our hands.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 10–20 (part 1 of 5):

Then the Exalted said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10].

* In this noble verse there are benefits. First: the hypocrites are sick at heart, as His saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ indicates. He made the disease enclosed within the heart as a container, as if it has settled in the heart—may Allah protect us—﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾. So what is the disease of these people? The disease of these people is doubt, or disbelief, denial, deception and scheming, and what resembles that.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever Allah knows to have evil and wickedness in him, He increases him in his wickedness and evil. For this reason He said: ﴿so Allah increased them in disease﴾. This is stronger than His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5], because this is explicit that Allah increased them in disease, and when disease increases, the outcome is destruction.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a warning to these hypocrites of a painful, agonizing punishment, as His saying: ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾ indicates.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of causation, as His saying: ﴿because they used to lie﴾ indicates. In another reading: ﴿yukadhdhibūn﴾ (they deny), as has passed. So they are liars and deniers. This is one of the benefits of the two readings: the first indicates that they themselves lie, and the second that they deny the truth and sincerity.
Affirming causes is what the Sharia, reason and reality all indicate, and denying them is a deficiency in reason and a deficiency in religion, I mean negating them; for everyone knows that everything has a cause, but among them are causes that are known and among them are causes that are unknown to us.
The scholars of the community have differed regarding causes: some went to excess concerning them, some neglected them, and some took the middle course.
As for those who went to excess concerning them, they said: causes are effective in themselves, not by a receptive locus nor by an acting cause; they are effective in themselves, and Allah has no connection to them at all. These are the naturalists and philosophers who make things interact by themselves with no relation to Allah the Exalted. Without doubt this is shirk and denial of the Creator.
The second category neglected causes and said: causes have no effect whatsoever; if we granted them an effect we would be affirming a partner with Allah. The burning of what is burnable by fire is not by the fire; rather it burns when Allah places it there, not by it. Likewise they say regarding breaking: when a thing breaks, glass breaks by a stone. They say: the stone did not break the glass; it broke upon impact, not by the impact. Without doubt this is foolishness in reason and error in religion. As for the foolishness in reason, it is obvious: if any child among the children were to throw a stone at glass and it shattered, and you asked: what broke it? What would he say? The stone, by its nature and disposition. As for it being error in religion, it is because the Qur'an and the Sunnah are filled with the mention of causes and the effect of causes, but their effect is by what Allah deposited in them of effective powers.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah the Exalted is a just Judge who punishes only those who deserve it, because He said: ﴿for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie﴾.
* Among the benefits of the verse: that variant readings bring an increase in meaning. The saying ﴿yakdhibūn﴾ is one reading, and ﴿yukadhdhibūn﴾ is another reading. If the verse contained only ﴿yakdhibūn﴾, the threat would be upon their lying themselves, saying "We believe" while they are not believers. And if it were ﴿yukadhdhibūn﴾, the threat would also be upon their denying, not upon their lying. So when the two readings are combined, an additional meaning is achieved.
Among its parallels: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ and ﴿Owner of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4], with the alif and without it. The benefit increases by combining the two readings, that Allah is a king, what? an owner. For among the created there is one who is a king but not an owner, and there is one who is an owner but not a king. And there are similar examples, such as: ﴿If a degenerate comes to you with news, then verify﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6], and in another reading ﴿then be certain﴾. This combines two meanings: tabayyun (clarification) first and tathabbut (verification) second; that is, be certain until it becomes clear to you—tathabbut first and bayan second, the reverse of what I said: tathabbut first, then tabayyun second. ﴿And when it is said to them: do not cause corruption on the earth﴾. Who says it? The believers: ﴿do not cause corruption on the earth﴾, and by what? By their deception, their cheating and their lying.
﴿They say: we are only reformers﴾, meaning: we are nothing but reformers. Praise be to Allah that they did not say "we are the reformers"; had they said "we are the reformers" it would have been a greater claim, since if they said "we are the reformers," it means there is no reformer other than them. But when they said "we are reformers," it does not prevent others from being reformers too; yet they restricted their attributes to being reformers, meaning there is nothing of corruption in them. But Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿Surely they are the corrupters﴾. He refuted them a strong refutation. By what was it strong? Firstly: by the opening particle (alā), which conveys alertness and emphasis. Secondly: by (inna), which conveys emphasis. Thirdly: by (hum), which is a separating pronoun conveying restriction and emphasis.
So the Exalted said: ﴿Surely they—they themselves—are﴾, alone, ﴿the corrupters, but they do not perceive﴾ their corruption; because they—may Allah protect us—have had a seal set upon their hearts, so there is no awareness in them.
* In this verse there are benefits: these hypocrites were advised, but they insisted upon what they were on, thinking that it was reform.
* Among the benefits of this verse: caution, that a person should beware of blindness of the heart, whereby he does an action thinking he is a reformer while he is a corrupter. This is among the greatest losers, indeed the greatest of people in deeds. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ [al-Kahf: 103] Who? ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work﴾ [al-Kahf: 104]. So these hypocrites say: "we are only reformers"; is this a claim, or is it their assumption that they are reformers? The more apparent is the second: they assumed they were upon reform. They combined pleasing the believers and pleasing the disbelievers, so they thought they were reformers. For this reason He said ﴿but they do not perceive﴾ that they are corrupters, because their insight has become blind, may Allah protect us. In it is a warning against a person seeing falsehood as truth and truth as falsehood.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse and the one after it: a person's heart may become blind, ﴿for indeed it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46], so he sees falsehood as truth and truth as falsehood; as shown by their saying ﴿we are only reformers﴾. For this sentence undoubtedly conveys restriction and emphasis, yet despite this they have no reform.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to refute the people of falsehood and to clarify that they are misguided, because Allah did not remain silent about these people; rather He refuted them and nullified the corrupt method they were upon: ﴿Surely they are the corrupters﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person may be among the corrupters on the earth while not perceiving it, because of the rust that has settled on his heart from the darkness of sins, to the point that he does not perceive that the falsehood he is upon is falsehood.

﴿And when it is said to them: believe as the people have believed, they say: shall we believe as the foolish have believed? Surely they themselves are the foolish, but they do not know.﴾ ﴿When it is said to them﴾: by whom? By the believers, who say ﴿believe as the people have believed﴾, as so-and-so believed and so-and-so believed. They say: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾, meaning: we will not believe. The interrogative here is for negation. Moreover, they did not limit themselves to denying faith; they described the believers as foolish. This is as Allah related of the criminals, that when they saw the believers they said: ﴿Indeed these are surely astray﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 32]. So they here say: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ The foolish (sufaha') is the plural of safih, and the safih is one who does not handle affairs well. This is the general rule for the foolish: one who does not handle affairs well; if it concerns wealth, then in wealth; if it concerns authority, then in authority; if it concerns a specific task, then in that task. The point is: the foolish is one who does not handle affairs well.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Surely they themselves are the foolish﴾, and this is a defence of the believers. ﴿Surely they themselves are the foolish﴾ is to be read for emphasis as we said in the previous verse ﴿Surely they themselves are the corrupters﴾. ﴿But they do not know﴾; here He said ﴿do not know﴾, and there He said ﴿do not perceive﴾, because this matter is clear: the faith of the believers is clear, and the disbelief of the hypocrites is clear as well; but these had lost knowledge, so they had no knowledge; rather they were ignorant of the reality.
* In this verse there are benefits: these were commanded to good, and in the previous one they were forbidden from evil. ﴿And when it is said to them: do not cause corruption on the earth﴾ is a forbidding of evil; ﴿believe as the people have believed﴾ is a commanding of good. But they refused—may Allah protect us—so they did not desist from evil nor did they comply with good.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mention of those who responded to the truth, or the mention of those who responded to the truth, to encourage its acceptance, in His saying ﴿as the people have believed﴾. This is a known matter, because a person undoubtedly follows others; so if we want to call a person of great standing, we say: believe as so-and-so believed, do this as so-and-so did, so that it becomes an encouragement and motivation for him.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the manifestation of the hatred of the hypocrites toward the believers, in their denial of the faith which is the practice of whom? The foolish, as they say: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ Without doubt the greatest of people in hatred toward Islam and the Muslims are the hypocrites, as Allah said: ﴿They are the enemy﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: describing the believers, or giving the believers nicknames of evil, is something people have done from before until our day, such as describing the believers as "backward," for example, saying: these are backward, they have nothing of progress. Does this description apply to whom? To those who described them as backward, or to the believers? To those who described them as backward; because backwardness in reality is one who has not been first to good, whereas one who has preceded to good, faith and righteous deeds is the progressive one.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's defence of the believers by His saying: ﴿Surely they themselves are the foolish﴾. This defence contains two things: it removes foolishness from the believers, since it restricts foolishness to whom? To the hypocrites. And second: it describes these hypocrites with foolishness.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the deceiver who schemes, whether in religion or outside religion, is considered foolish, because Allah must make his affair manifest and expose him.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that some people are upon foolishness and misguidance, but knowledge is withheld from them, so they remain thinking they are upon the truth. We ask Allah for safety for us and for you.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you with good, explain the third category from His saying: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ In this description, would the second category not be (...)?
* The Shaykh: This division so far: people now are between a clear believer, a clear disbeliever, and a hypocrite.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but he conceals it.
* Student: Meaning he does not utter this statement.
* The Shaykh: He does not declare it.

* The Shaykh: He says it in his heart, or he says it privately to someone who said it to him.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. ﴿And when it is said to them: believe as the people have believed, they say: shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ This is among what is apparent. * The Shaykh: They have no argument, so long as the truth reached them.

But as for their saying: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67], this is not an argument.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, regarding what has passed us of the attributes of the disbelievers and hypocrites, and among the principles of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah is establishing the proof upon the specific person so that his disbelief or major hypocrisy is established. Is it valid to attribute disbelief and hypocrisy on the basis of dominant assumption, or must there be certainty after establishing the proof?
* The Shaykh: No, certainty is necessary, certainty is necessary; because dominant assumption is not sufficient. This is a ruling: you would say "this is a disbeliever, this is a hypocrite," so knowledge is necessary.

* Student: O Shaykh, you gave an illustrative example; or is the matter one of entering...
