This is one of the benefits of the two readings: the first indicates that they themselves lie, and the second that they deny the truth and sincerity.
Affirming causes is what the Sharia, reason and reality all indicate, and denying them is a deficiency in reason and a deficiency in religion, I mean negating them; for everyone knows that everything has a cause, but among them are causes that are known and among them are causes that are unknown to us.
The scholars of the community have differed regarding causes: some went to excess concerning them, some neglected them, and some took the middle course.
As for those who went to excess concerning them, they said: causes are effective in themselves, not by a receptive locus nor by an acting cause; they are effective in themselves, and Allah has no connection to them at all. These are the naturalists and philosophers who make things interact by themselves with no relation to Allah the Exalted. Without doubt this is shirk and denial of the Creator.
The second category neglected causes and said: causes have no effect whatsoever; if we granted them an effect we would be affirming a partner with Allah. The burning of what is burnable by fire is not by the fire; rather it burns when Allah places it there, not by it. Likewise they say regarding breaking: when a thing breaks, glass breaks by a stone. They say: the stone did not break the glass; it broke upon impact, not by the impact. Without doubt this is foolishness in reason and error in religion. As for the foolishness in reason, it is obvious: if any child among the children were to throw a stone at glass and it shattered, and you asked: what broke it? What would he say? The stone, by its nature and disposition. As for it being error in religion, it is because the Qur'an and the Sunnah are filled with the mention of causes and the effect of causes, but their effect is by what Allah deposited in them of effective powers.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah the Exalted is a just Judge who punishes only those who deserve it, because He said: ﴿for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie﴾.
* Among the benefits of the verse: that variant readings bring an increase in meaning. The saying ﴿yakdhibūn﴾ is one reading, and ﴿yukadhdhibūn﴾ is another reading. If the verse contained only ﴿yakdhibūn﴾, the threat would be upon their lying themselves, saying "We believe" while they are not believers. And if it were ﴿yukadhdhibūn﴾, the threat would also be upon their denying, not upon their lying. So when the two readings are combined, an additional meaning is achieved.
Among its parallels: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ and ﴿Owner of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4], with the alif and without it. The benefit increases by combining the two readings, that Allah is a king, what? an owner. For among the created there is one who is a king but not an owner, and there is one who is an owner but not a king. And there are similar examples, such as: ﴿If a degenerate comes to you with news, then verify﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6], and in another reading ﴿then be certain﴾. This combines two meanings: tabayyun (clarification) first and tathabbut (verification) second; that is, be certain until it becomes clear to you—tathabbut first and bayan second, the reverse of what I said: tathabbut first, then tabayyun second. ﴿And when it is said to them: do not cause corruption on the earth﴾. Who says it? The believers: ﴿do not cause corruption on the earth﴾, and by what? By their deception, their cheating and their lying.
﴿They say: we are only reformers﴾, meaning: we are nothing but reformers. Praise be to Allah that they did not say "we are the reformers"; had they said "we are the reformers" it would have been a greater claim, since if they said "we are the reformers," it means there is no reformer other than them. But when they said "we are reformers," it does not prevent others from being reformers too; yet they restricted their attributes to being reformers, meaning there is nothing of corruption in them. But Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿Surely they are the corrupters﴾. He refuted them a strong refutation. By what was it strong? Firstly: by the opening particle (alā), which conveys alertness and emphasis. Secondly: by (inna), which conveys emphasis. Thirdly: by (hum), which is a separating pronoun conveying restriction and emphasis.
So the Exalted said: ﴿Surely they—they themselves—are﴾, alone, ﴿the corrupters, but they do not perceive﴾ their corruption; because they—may Allah protect us—have had a seal set upon their hearts, so there is no awareness in them.
* In this verse there are benefits: these hypocrites were advised, but they insisted upon what they were on, thinking that it was reform.
* Among the benefits of this verse: caution, that a person should beware of blindness of the heart, whereby he does an action thinking he is a reformer while he is a corrupter. This is among the greatest losers, indeed the greatest of people in deeds. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ [al-Kahf: 103] Who? ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work﴾ [al-Kahf: 104]. So these hypocrites say: "we are only reformers"; is this a claim, or is it their assumption that they are reformers? The more apparent is the second: they assumed they were upon reform. They combined pleasing the believers and pleasing the disbelievers, so they thought they were reformers. For this reason He said ﴿but they do not perceive﴾ that they are corrupters, because their insight has become blind, may Allah protect us. In it is a warning against a person seeing falsehood as truth and truth as falsehood.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse and the one after it: a person's heart may become blind, ﴿for indeed it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46], so he sees falsehood as truth and truth as falsehood; as shown by their saying ﴿we are only reformers﴾. For this sentence undoubtedly conveys restriction and emphasis, yet despite this they have no reform.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to refute the people of falsehood and to clarify that they are misguided, because Allah did not remain silent about these people; rather He refuted them and nullified the corrupt method they were upon: ﴿Surely they are the corrupters﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person may be among the corrupters on the earth while not perceiving it, because of the rust that has settled on his heart from the darkness of sins, to the point that he does not perceive that the falsehood he is upon is falsehood.

﴿And when it is said to them: believe as the people have believed, they say: shall we believe as the foolish have believed? Surely they themselves are the foolish, but they do not know.﴾ ﴿When it is said to them﴾: by whom? By the believers, who say ﴿believe as the people have believed﴾, as so-and-so believed and so-and-so believed. They say: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾, meaning: we will not believe. The interrogative here is for negation. Moreover, they did not limit themselves to denying faith; they described the believers as foolish. This is as Allah related of the criminals, that when they saw the believers they said: ﴿Indeed these are surely astray﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 32]. So they here say: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ The foolish (sufaha') is the plural of safih, and the safih is one who does not handle affairs well. This is the general rule for the foolish: one who does not handle affairs well; if it concerns wealth, then in wealth; if it concerns authority, then in authority; if it concerns a specific task, then in that task. The point is: the foolish is one who does not handle affairs well.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Surely they themselves are the foolish﴾, and this is a defence of the believers. ﴿Surely they themselves are the foolish﴾ is to be read for emphasis as we said in the previous verse ﴿Surely they themselves are the corrupters﴾. ﴿But they do not know﴾; here He said ﴿do not know﴾, and there He said ﴿do not perceive﴾, because this matter is clear: the faith of the believers is clear, and the disbelief of the hypocrites is clear as well; but these had lost knowledge, so they had no knowledge; rather they were ignorant of the reality.
* In this verse there are benefits: these were commanded to good, and in the previous one they were forbidden from evil. ﴿And when it is said to them: do not cause corruption on the earth﴾ is a forbidding of evil; ﴿believe as the people have believed﴾ is a commanding of good. But they refused—may Allah protect us—so they did not desist from evil nor did they comply with good.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mention of those who responded to the truth, or the mention of those who responded to the truth, to encourage its acceptance, in His saying ﴿as the people have believed﴾. This is a known matter, because a person undoubtedly follows others; so if we want to call a person of great standing, we say: believe as so-and-so believed, do this as so-and-so did, so that it becomes an encouragement and motivation for him.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the manifestation of the hatred of the hypocrites toward the believers, in their denial of the faith which is the practice of whom? The foolish, as they say: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ Without doubt the greatest of people in hatred toward Islam and the Muslims are the hypocrites, as Allah said: ﴿They are the enemy﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: describing the believers, or giving the believers nicknames of evil, is something people have done from before until our day, such as describing the believers as "backward," for example, saying: these are backward, they have nothing of progress. Does this description apply to whom? To those who described them as backward, or to the believers? To those who described them as backward; because backwardness in reality is one who has not been first to good, whereas one who has preceded to good, faith and righteous deeds is the progressive one.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's defence of the believers by His saying: ﴿Surely they themselves are the foolish﴾. This defence contains two things: it removes foolishness from the believers, since it restricts foolishness to whom? To the hypocrites. And second: it describes these hypocrites with foolishness.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the deceiver who schemes, whether in religion or outside religion, is considered foolish, because Allah must make his affair manifest and expose him.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that some people are upon foolishness and misguidance, but knowledge is withheld from them, so they remain thinking they are upon the truth. We ask Allah for safety for us and for you.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you with good, explain the third category from His saying: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ In this description, would the second category not be (...)?
* The Shaykh: This division so far: people now are between a clear believer, a clear disbeliever, and a hypocrite.
* Student: If the hypocrite says: ﴿shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾, is he among the disbelievers?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but he conceals it.
* Student: Meaning he does not utter this statement.
* The Shaykh: He does not declare it.
* Student: Meaning he says it in his heart.
* The Shaykh: He says it in his heart, or he says it privately to someone who said it to him.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. ﴿And when it is said to them: believe as the people have believed, they say: shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ This is among what is apparent. These people will have an argument on the Day of Resurrection: they will come before the Lord of Might, the Exalted, and say: O Lord, it became apparent to us, or it was said to us, that these were foolish (...). A man comes, a caller or not, gathers some people and says: O brothers, I see this is the path of goodness and this is your reform, and this is such and such; then this one says: do you not hear? Others come and confuse them. So what is the argument of these people, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: They have no argument, so long as the truth reached them.
* Student: The truth reached them. There is a higher and a lower, O Shaykh: the higher was reached by falsehood, and the lower possesses nothing.
* The Shaykh: It is obligatory upon them, when the lower said to them: this is a mistake, this is disbelief, this is shirk, that they should stop and investigate. But as for their saying: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67], this is not an argument.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, regarding what has passed us of the attributes of the disbelievers and hypocrites, and among the principles of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah is establishing the proof upon the specific person so that his disbelief or major hypocrisy is established. Is it valid to attribute disbelief and hypocrisy on the basis of dominant assumption, or must there be certainty after establishing the proof?
* The Shaykh: No, certainty is necessary, certainty is necessary; because dominant assumption is not sufficient. This is a ruling: you would say "this is a disbeliever, this is a hypocrite," so knowledge is necessary.
* Student: You said, may Allah bless you, that loving the victory of disbelievers over believers is from hypocrisy?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Now, for example, a young man cheers for his national team or his club, and Allah decrees that a disbelieving team faces a Muslim team; he loves the disbelieving team to win.
* The Shaykh: You mean football? This football?
* Student: Would this be major or minor hypocrisy, given that he now loves the disbelievers' victory?
* The Shaykh: I do not consider these games to be anything at all, and I warn against participating in them and against watching them, whereas some people never tire of watching them; they stay up the whole night, and perhaps the congregational prayer is established while he is watching.
* Student: O Shaykh, you gave an illustrative example; or is the matter one of entering...
* The Shaykh: In any case, every person who loves the disbelievers' victory over the believers has in him some hypocrisy.
* Student: This is disbelief?
* The Shaykh: General.
* Student: Is supporting disbelievers by giving them money so they win over Muslims, in political matters, and not out of love for their victory over Muslims, considered major disbelief?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, I fear it might be considered major disbelief, because it is a political matter. And what is the meaning of "political"? Political, that a disbeliever triumphs over a believer?
* Student: They supply them with money and food.
* The Shaykh: Except if the believer is a hypocrite, meaning he pretends to faith while being an innovator in a disbelief-making innovation; that is possible.
* Student: A believer, meaning he shows Islam outwardly?
* The Shaykh: In any case, we deal with people according to the outward.
* Student: He does not become a disbeliever by this action?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know; I withhold judgment on it.
* Student: It has been heard of some who attribute themselves to knowledge, who now lead some people, so they deny, for example, the hadd penalty for apostasy, and say: the Messenger ﷺ did not punish apostates, and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved﴾ [al-Nisa': 137]. Then one of them says like this: these people apostatize several times, so why did the Messenger not impose the penalty upon them and kill them? By this he arrived at denying the hadd penalty for apostasy, and said: it is not possible that the hadiths abrogate the verse. So what is the ruling on this?

* Shaykh: The ruling on this is that it is said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa 80]. And since the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever changes his religion, kill him" [Reported by al-Bukhari (3017) from the hadith of Ibn Abbas], this is like the saying of Allah. As for these people, ﴿they believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief﴾, this is a description of a state. Did the Messenger know about them and become aware of them? There is no evidence that he became aware of them.
* Student: Is this what you claim is being said?
* Shaykh: He must fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, review himself, and not be among those who follow the ambiguous (mutashabih).
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe." But when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking." (14) Allah mocks them and extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly. (15) Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance, so their commerce has not profited, and they were not [rightly] guided. (16) Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire; and when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, not seeing. (17) Deaf, dumb, and blind, so they will not return. (18) Or like a rainstorm from the sky, within which is darkness, thunder, and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderbolts, fearing death. But Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers. (19) The lightning almost snatches away their sight. Every time it lights [the way] for them, they walk therein; and when darkness settles upon them, they stand still. And if Allah willed, He could take away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ [Al-Baqarah 14–20]
* Shaykh: Glorified and exalted is He. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe."﴾ The subject of ﴿they meet﴾ refers to the hypocrites, and ﴿those who believe﴾ means the sincere believers, such as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. ﴿They say, "We believe"﴾ only with their tongues, because Allah says at the beginning of this passage: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾. So they say with their tongues, "We believe," while they are liars. We testify that they are liars, just as they said to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him): ﴿We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 1]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars. (1) They have taken their oaths as a shield and averted [people] from the way of Allah﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 1, 2].
﴿And when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you"﴾. ﴿Alone with their devils﴾ may bring to mind the expression "when they were alone with their devils" or "when they were with their devils," but the verse says: ﴿when they are alone with their devils﴾. It has been said that the meaning of ﴿they were alone﴾ is: they withdrew from the believers, returning to their devils. It has also been said that ﴿alone﴾ has been given the meaning of "returning," and this is the more correct view. According to this last view, the verse needs no supposed omission, so the verb (khala) is taken to include the meaning of returning. This is from the eloquence of the Qur'an and its conciseness of expression, that a verb is given the meaning of another verb that is indicated by its complement or by what is connected to it. There are examples of this, among them the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah will drink, making it gush forth in abundance﴾ [Al-Insan 6]. A spring is not drunk from; rather, one drinks with a vessel. So why does He say ﴿will drink from it﴾? The scholars said: the preposition (ba') means "from it," and this is the view of the Kufans. The people of Basra said: rather, (yashrabu) has been given the meaning of (yarwa), to drink until satisfied, and then it is correct for it to take the preposition (ba') with it.
So ﴿when they are alone with their devils﴾ means: they returned to their devils, and so the meaning of returning is included. The word "devils" is the plural of "devil," and what is meant by them is their masters to whom they belong, because the hypocrites have masters. For example, Abdullah ibn Ubayy was the leader of his people. His people would go to the Messenger (ﷺ) and to the Companions and say: "We are with you." But when they returned to him and to others like him, they said: ﴿Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking﴾. ﴿Indeed, we are with you﴾ is an affirmation of their allegiance to them. But alongside the affirmation of allegiance there must be disassociation from the believers, and they expressed their disassociation from the believers by their saying: ﴿we were only mocking﴾. Mocking whom? The believers. Consider His saying: ﴿Indeed, we are with you﴾, and you will find it is a sentence emphasized with (inna). Consider His saying: ﴿we were only mocking﴾, and you will find it is a sentence containing restriction (hasr), meaning: we are nothing but mockers; that is, our situation with the believers is nothing but mockery, and we have no intention of believing.
In this noble verse there is an explanation of the deception of the hypocrites toward the believers. That is, the hypocrites deceive the believers, and this is their nature: they deceive Allah and those who believe. This is shown by their saying: ﴿Indeed, we are with you﴾, and then when they go back to their devils they say: ﴿we were only mocking﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: we only have the outward appearance, so we deal with people according to their outward state. Indeed, the Messenger (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him) said: "O people, you bring your disputes before me, and perhaps some of you are more eloquent in presenting his argument than others, so I rule for him according to what I hear. Whomever I rule for, from the right of his brother, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire." Or he said: "a coal of Fire. Let him then take it or leave it" [Agreed upon. Reported by al-Bukhari (6967) and Muslim (1713/4). The wording in al-Bukhari is: "I am only a human being, and you bring your disputes before me, and perhaps some of you are more eloquent in presenting his argument than others, so I rule according to what I hear. Whoever I rule for from the right of his brother, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire."]. So in this world we only have the outward appearance, but the reckoning in the Hereafter is based on what is hidden. The reason is that the believers deal with these hypocrites as what? Believers, because of their saying: ﴿they said, "We believe"﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the religion of the hypocrites is a religion of concealment and secrecy, which they do not declare openly, because they fear being killed. This is shown by: ﴿when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you"﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is correct to apply the term "devil" to the callers to disbelief, because of His saying: ﴿to their devils﴾.
* Among its benefits also: when something is restricted, it is mentioned with a form that indicates restriction. He said ﴿their devils﴾ and did not say "to the devils," and there is a difference between (their devils) and (the devils). Just as we say, for example, when we address a leader of disbelief, we do not say "the leader, so-and-so," but we say "the leader of his people." For this reason the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) wrote to Heraclius and said: "To Heraclius, the great one of the Romans" [Agreed upon. Reported by al-Bukhari (7) and Muslim (1773/74) from the hadith of Abu Sufyan], and he did not say "the great one," but said "the great one of the Romans." Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Rather, the largest of them did it﴾ [Al-Anbiya 63], and he did not say "the largest," but said "their largest." So this must be noticed: we do not give an unrestricted term to something that is restricted.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the strength of the hypocrites' allegiance to the disbelievers, because of their saying: ﴿Indeed, we are with you﴾, meaning in good times and bad, as the common people say, in hardship and ease.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: these hypocrites confirm to their devils that they only treat the believers with mockery, not in reality: ﴿we were only mocking﴾.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah mocks them and extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾. This is recompense of the same kind as the deed. They mock the believers, and Allah mocks these hypocrites, through what He has given the Muslims of rulings based on outward appearance. This is mockery of them, because they are treated outwardly as what? As believers. And treating a disbeliever as a Muslim is a mockery. As for His saying: ﴿and extends them in their transgression﴾, is ﴿in their transgression﴾ connected to ﴿extends them﴾, or to ﴿wandering blindly﴾? The more apparent view is the second, because it has been placed before ﴿wandering blindly﴾ to convey restriction and to match the endings of the verses.
﴿Extends them﴾: the scholars said: (yamuddu) is used for evil, and (numiddu) for good, meaning that the quadrilateral form (amadda) is used for good. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We provided them with fruit and meat of what they desire. (22) They pass around a cup therein, free of ill speech and sin﴾ [At-Tur 22, 23]. As for (madda), it is used for evil. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will extend for him of the punishment an extension﴾ [Maryam 79]. Here He said: ﴿extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, because this is evil.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: tyrants, for the most part, are blind to the truth, may Allah protect us, because of the arrogance and self-exaltation in their souls. So they wander blindly in transgression, and do not imagine that it is transgression, so they persist in this transgression.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah mocks. That is, Allah is described with mockery, but is He described with it absolutely? No, He is not described with it absolutely. Rather, He is described with it in response to those who mock Him, His messengers, and His righteous servants.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: Allah the Exalted may give respite to a person in transgression, so he continues in it until he increases in sin. For this reason, one of the signs of Allah's love for a person is that He hastens punishment for him in this world, so that the punishment expiates his misdeeds and serves as a warning to him. Every sensible believing person, when he is struck by a calamity and knows that he himself is the cause, will refrain from his corruption and disobedience. So when Allah wants to alert a believer, He hastens punishment for him, and he walks on the earth with no sin upon him, because his misdeeds have been expiated through these trials.
Then He said: ﴿Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance, so their commerce has not profited, and they were not [rightly] guided﴾. This verse is analyzed by the people of rhetoric (balaghah), because they make it a explicit metaphor (istiarah tasrihiyyah) that follows, or an implicit metaphor (istiarah makniyyah). Then they say: it contains tarshih, meaning reinforcement, which is His saying: ﴿so their commerce has not profited﴾. This is the one for the explicit metaphor. ﴿And they were not [rightly] guided﴾ is for the implicit metaphor. Since most of you have not studied rhetoric, we will set aside the details and explain the meaning. ﴿Those are the ones who have purchased error﴾, meaning they chose it, over what? Over guidance. But their choosing it is called purchasing, because the buyer buys the goods because he desires them. They desired error and so bought it, and they showed no interest in guidance and so sold it. The (bi) in His saying ﴿in exchange for guidance﴾ is the (bi) of substitution and exchange. That is, they took error, may Allah protect us, and substituted it for guidance: they purchased error in exchange for guidance. ﴿So their commerce has not profited﴾: (ma) is negating. That is, this trade they thought was profit is a loss. The hypocrites now think they are profiting. In their dealings with the believers and with their devils they think they are winning, and that they have played with the minds of both, but in reality they are with the disbelievers. So they thought they had profited, but is this profit? Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿so their commerce has not profited﴾, rather it is a loss. ﴿And they were not [rightly] guided﴾, because they remained in this conduct and were given respite in it, so they thought they were upon correctness. A person who commits wrong and thinks he is right will hardly escape from it, whether in beliefs, in statements, or in deeds.
* In this noble verse there are benefits, among them: the explanation of the foolishness of these hypocrites, in that they purchased error in exchange for guidance.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: it is permissible to express a meaning with a phrase that indicates it, even if that phrase was not originally coined for it, because Allah expressed their choosing error over guidance by saying that they purchased it. When the meaning is clear, there is no harm in using a phrase that indicates it. Indeed, this gives the meaning beauty and radiance.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person may think he is doing well while he is doing evil, because these people purchased error in exchange for guidance, thinking that they were upon correctness and that they were profiting. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿so their commerce has not profited﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: profit and loss revolve around following guidance, because Allah negated the profit of their trade since they chose error over guidance. So profit and loss revolve around guidance. This is supported by the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿By time, (1) indeed, mankind is in loss, (2) except for those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise each other to truth and advise each other to patience﴾ [Al-Asr 1–3], and His saying: ﴿O you who believe, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [As-Saff 10]. Complete the verse.
* Student: ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew﴾ [As-Saff 11].
* Shaykh: Well done. ﴿That is best for you﴾, stop. ﴿If you only knew﴾. If we connect it to what precedes it, the goodness becomes conditional on our knowing, whereas it is good whether we know or not. In any case, the profitable trade is this one: belief in Allah and His Messenger, and striving in the cause of Allah with wealth and self.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these people will never be guided, ﴿and they were not [rightly] guided﴾, because they think they are doing good, and so they will not return. Likewise, every corrupt person or innovator who thinks he is upon the truth will never return. The ignorant simple person is better than this one, because this one is ignorant in a compound way: he thinks he is upon correctness while he is not. O Allah, guide us to Your straight path.
* Student: Sometimes, Shaykh, you begin with the benefits before finishing the explanation of the tafsir. Should I point it out?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: In the previous lesson, ﴿in their hearts is a disease﴾ we did not explain, and you began with the benefits?
* Shaykh: Correct.
* Student: And today too, ﴿Allah mocks them and extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, ﴿in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, you did not explain this and began with the benefits...
* Shaykh: No, we explained it.
* Student: "Wandering blindly" means...
* Shaykh: We did not explain the mockery, that is correct, we did not explain the mockery, but the mockery is known.
* Student: He means the verb "wandering blindly."
* Shaykh: What? No, we said the meaning of "wandering blindly" is that they wander aimlessly in transgression, so they are not guided.
* Student: True, Shaykh, but you mentioned benefits directly without a separation. However, if you had clarified the rhetorical question, since the purpose of repeating the explanation is to correct the omission from the first explanation, that would be better so we can write it down.
* Shaykh: No, not at all. If we were to address the implicit metaphor, the explicit metaphor, the following metaphor, the reinforcement, the abstraction and the absolute, we would need five lessons. They require lessons.
* Student: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased their disease﴾. Did you not explain this?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 10–20 (part 3 of 5):

* The Shaykh: This is correct. This requires explanation, and the sickness of the hearts needs to be divided: it may be the sickness of hypocrisy, it may be the sickness of desire, it may be the sickness of love of this world. Yes.
* The student: The next lesson, God willing?
* The Shaykh: Remind us, God willing.
* A student: O Shaykh, may God bless you. Does the apparent meaning of the two verses in which the Ulul-'Azm (the resolute messengers) are mentioned indicate that Noah is superior to Jesus, peace be upon them?
* The Shaykh: This is possible. This is because ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham﴾ [ash-Shura 13] mentions Abraham after Noah. It may be that this is chronological order. In any case, here we are contemplating and reflecting on the matter from a long time.
* The student: Did we say from the time Muhammad, peace be upon him, came?
* The Shaykh: No, no; because He legislated ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We revealed to you﴾, because He combined the first of the messengers and the last of the messengers, then mentioned those between them.
* The student: (...)
* The Shaykh: It does not appear to me. I have contemplated it a great deal and it has not become clear to me. It has become clear that we either say they are in one rank, and their merit before God is something we do not speak about, but what appears to us is this; or we say we remain silent.
Finished, let us begin.
* * *
* A student: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him, God took away their light and left them in darkness, not seeing (17). Deaf, dumb, blind, so they will not return (18). Or like a rainstorm from the sky, in which are darknesses, thunder and lightning; they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps, for fear of death, and God encompasses the disbelievers (19). The lightning nearly snatches away their sight; whenever it lights up for them they walk in it, and when darkness falls upon them they stand still. And if God willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed God is over all things competent﴾ [al-Baqarah 17–20].
* The Shaykh: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* A student: Shaykh, the verse before it: ﴿Those are the ones who purchased error in exchange for guidance﴾.
* The Shaykh: What are the lessons? Finish them.
* The student: ﴿God mocks them﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: We have taken the lessons.
* The Shaykh: Have you taken them?
* The student: Yes, and among its lessons: God is described with mockery in response to those who mock His messengers and righteous servants.
* The Shaykh: Yes, among the lessons of the noble verse ﴿God mocks them﴾, there remains for us a subtle note, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are but reformers." (11) Unquestionably, they are the corrupters, but they do not perceive (12). And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?" Unquestionably, they are the foolish, but they do not know﴾.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿In their hearts is a sickness, so God increased their sickness﴾. Sickness is of two kinds: sickness of doubt (shubha) and sickness of desire (shahwa).
As for the sickness of doubt, it is ignorance, for ignorance is blindness, and it is a sickness. The ignorant person commits error without realizing it. As for the sickness of desire, it is generally a sickness of arrogance. The sickness of the hypocrites is either a sickness of doubt or a sickness of desire. Whoever the matter is confused for, his sickness is a sickness of what? Doubt. And whoever the matter is not confused for, his sickness is a sickness of desire.
Among the sicknesses of the hearts is what befalls a person from the sickness of desire for women, as in His saying: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a sickness should covet, but speak in an honorable manner﴾ [al-Ahzab 32].
As for the two verses you mentioned: in the first, He said: ﴿Unquestionably, they are the corrupters, but they do not perceive﴾, and in the second He said: ﴿Unquestionably, they are the foolish, but they do not know﴾. So what is the reason for the distinction between the first and second endings? The reason for the distinction is clear to whoever contemplates it. Is corruption on the earth perceived by the senses or by the intellect? By the senses. For this reason He negated perception (shu'ur) in it, and perception relates to sensible things. For this reason you say, "I did not perceive this thing," meaning I did not apprehend it with my senses. As for foolishness, it is apprehended through knowledge and reflection, so one looks to see whether this person is foolish or not. For this reason He negated knowledge ('ilm) from them, because foolishness is among intelligible matters, not sensible matters. I have only pointed this out because verses like these occur in the Noble Qur'an, meaning that God varies the expression and brings two expressions that one supposing them to be one would think identical, but upon reflection a great difference appears. Similar to this is that God, mighty and majestic, brings what a person does not expect, as in His saying: ﴿And God judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him judge nothing﴾ [Ghafir 20]. The expected phrasing would have been "they judge falsehood," the opposite of truth, but to show the incapacity of those invoked besides Him, and that they have no judgment at all, He said: ﴿those they invoke besides Him judge nothing﴾, neither truth nor falsehood, because they are too incapable to judge anything.
The Qur'an, in reality, when a person contemplates it, increases him — glory be to God — in insight, knowledge and light. But it requires a condition which Shaykh al-Islam, may God have mercy on him, indicated in al-'Aqidah al-Wasitiyyah, and how blessed that creed is. He said: Whoever reflects upon the Qur'an seeking guidance from it, the path of truth becomes clear to him. Thus he made two conditions: reflection and good intention, "seeking guidance from it," meaning not seeking victory, such as to overcome others, or seeking his desire, hoping to find in the Qur'an what supports his opinion. This may be forbidden, and we seek refuge in God. But whoever reflects upon it seeking guidance from it, the path of truth becomes clear to him, and he finds in it knowledge, insights, and the reform of hearts that a person cannot describe. We ask God to make us and you of its people. Amin. O God, send blessings upon Muhammad.
Now let us return to what we stopped at: ﴿God mocks them and extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse, as we said: the affirmation of the attribute of mockery to God, mighty and majestic, but it is an attribute restricted to those who mock; this makes clear that God is above the mockery of these people.
* Among the lessons of the noble verse: a person may be extended in transgression and given respite, so he increases in transgression, until when God seizes him He does not let him escape, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed God gives respite to the wrongdoer until when He seizes him, He does not let him escape." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (4686) and Muslim (2583/61) from the hadith of Abu Musa.] Therefore, when you see the blessings of God following one another upon you, pause and look: if you are steadfast in obedience to Him, they are blessings; if you are not, they are a punishment and gradual deception.
* Among the lessons of the noble verse: the tyrant is in error — we seek refuge in God — and his path to the truth is blocked, as shown by His saying: ﴿wandering blindly﴾. So beware, my brother, of being among those who have tyranny toward the right of God and tyranny toward the rights of the servants of God, for you will surely increase in misguidance.
Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those are the ones who purchased error in exchange for guidance, so their commerce did not profit, nor were they guided﴾. We have taken it and its lessons. Yes.
* Among its lessons: those who purchased error in exchange for guidance, meaning they chose error over guidance, have no profit at all. Even if they profit in this world, it is a gradual deception, and profit in this world does not mean profit in reality, because the outcome of worldly profit, such as wealth, children, luxury and comfort, is what? Its cessation. God said about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind (25), and crops and noble station (26), and luxury they had been enjoying (27). Thus it was, and We bequeathed them to another people﴾ [ad-Dukhan 25–28]. The bounties of this world are nothing, because they are transient and pass away. Therefore He said: ﴿their commerce did not profit﴾. Even if a person is given respite and gains profit in his transgression, he is in loss.
* Among the lessons of the noble verse: the eloquence of the Noble Qur'an, in depicting intelligible matters as if they were sensible. Its aspect? ﴿purchased error in exchange for guidance﴾, and buying and selling occur in sensible things; ﴿so their commerce did not profit﴾, again commerce is in sensible things; ﴿nor were they guided﴾.
* Among the lessons of the noble verse: whoever takes the path of error is veiled from the path of guidance, as shown by His saying: ﴿nor were they guided﴾.
There are witnesses to this. God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am 110], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter﴾ [Qaf 5]: disordered, in doubt, in heedlessness.
Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire﴾. God struck for these hypocrites two examples: a fire example and a water example, according to their conditions. He said: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire﴾, meaning like a man who does not have fire with him, but he kindled (istawqada), that is, he asked someone else to kindle his fire, because istaf'ala carries the meaning of seeking, like istaghfara (sought forgiveness), istansara (sought victory). It may also come for other than that: it may come for emphasis; the sin and the ta' may come for emphasis, like istakbara, which does not mean he sought greatness, but rather he increased in his pride. So istaf'ala comes for what? For seeking, and it may come for emphasis.
﴿Istawqada naran﴾ means he sought the kindling of a fire. This indicates that he was in what? In darkness. But he sought the kindling of fire; as for himself, he has no fire and no light.
﴿Istawqada naran, fa-lamma adā'at mā ḥawlahu dhahaba Allahu binūrihim﴾. ﴿Adā'at﴾ means the fire he kindled. ﴿Mā ḥawlahu﴾ means what is around the one who kindled, not what is around the fire. If the intended meaning were around the fire, He would have said "mā ḥawlahā." And since He said ﴿mā ḥawlahu﴾, meaning what is around the kindler, it did not go far; it illuminated what was around him.
﴿Dhahaba Allahu binūrihim﴾: so the heat and darkness remained, because the habit of fire, when it dies down, is to be hot and dark with smoke; the light went, and the heat and darkness remained. ﴿Dhahaba Allahu binūrihim wa-taraka-hum fī ẓulumātin lā yubṣirūn﴾. ﴿Ẓulumāt﴾ is plural. We must understand what this plural is. First: the darkness of the night. How is the darkness of the night? From where do we know that this is at night?
* The students: ﴿Istawqada naran﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Adā'at mā ḥawlahu﴾: in daytime the fire does not illuminate what is around it, because the light of the sun veils every light. The second darkness: when darkness comes after light, it becomes more intense. Try it yourself: turn off the lamp while your eyes are open and you will find darkness, and after a little while you see what is around you. For this reason I advise everyone who wants to turn off the lamp to close his eyes when turning it off, because if he closes them at the moment of turning off and then opens them, the matter is normal, is it not so? Good. No, I want your medical confirmation.
* A student: Correct.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: Because while light is present the pupil of the eye is constricted.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: And in darkness it is open.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: So time passes until this happens.
* The Shaykh: Yes, praise be to God. We grasped this by experience, and our brother grasped it theoretically by medicine. In any case, when the light goes quickly it becomes intense darkness, correct?
The third darkness: the darkness of smoke, because the habit of fire, if it is extinguished without the fuel being finished, is that it produces smoke, and here the fuel has not finished, because He said: ﴿istawqada﴾ ﴿fa-lamma adā'at﴾; the moment it lit up, God took away the light. This means the fuel has not yet finished, and then there will be smoke. So the darknesses are now three; they became three: ﴿fa-lamma adā'at mā ḥawlahu dhahaba Allahu binūrihim wa-taraka-hum fī ẓulumāt﴾. ﴿Nūr﴾ is singular, ﴿binūrihim﴾; ﴿ẓulumāt﴾ is plural, because light is one; it does not repeat or multiply, it is one, whether it is strong or weak. ﴿Wa-taraka-hum fī ẓulumātin lā yubṣirūn﴾, meaning they do not see.
﴿Ṣummun bukmun ʿumyun fa-hum lā yarjiʿūn﴾. I seek refuge in God; this is their state. That is, after mentioning the example, He mentions the condition. ﴿Ṣummun﴾ deaf to hearing the truth; ﴿bukmun﴾ dumb regarding speaking the truth; ﴿ʿumyun﴾ blind regarding seeing the truth. So they, we seek refuge in God, have had the doors closed upon them from every side: they do not listen to the truth, and if they heard it they would not benefit. The second: ﴿bukmun﴾, they do not speak it, because they speak falsehood: ﴿When they meet those who have believed, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you; we were only mocking"﴾, and they never speak the truth at all; even if they speak it, it is only with the tongue. ﴿ʿUmyun﴾, meaning they do not see the truth. ﴿Fa-hum lā yarjiʿūn﴾, meaning, based on these three attributes, they do not return from what they were upon.
Let us return to the lessons of the verse.
* In this noble verse is evidence of the eloquence of the Qur'an, in that it strikes examples for intelligible matters with what? Sensible things, because a sensible thing is closer to the intellect than an intelligible thing. But among the eloquence of the Qur'an is that God strikes sensible examples for intelligible meanings so that a person may grasp them well.
* Among the lessons of the noble verse: the affirmation of analogy (qiyas), meaning that it is a proof to be relied upon. What is the basis for this?
* A student: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire﴾.
* The Shaykh: No, this is the verse; this is the evidence. But we want the basis of the inference?
* The student: The particle "kaf" (like).
* The Shaykh: The "kaf" is also for comparison.
* The student: God, mighty and majestic, compared these people with ﴿the one who kindled a fire﴾.
* The Shaykh: He wanted us to analogize their condition to the condition of the one who kindled. Every example in the Qur'an is evidence for affirming analogy. Any example in the Qur'an is a proof, and thereby it is a refutation of those who deny analogy. That is, after we establish this, we say: there is a refutation in it. You read the Qur'an every day and night and you find examples in it, and these are without doubt clear, evident analogies.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: these hypocrites have no light in their hearts; by His saying: ﴿like one who kindled a fire﴾, meaning he sought its kindling from another. And so it is: these hypocrites seek guidance, knowledge and light, but when it reaches their hearts, as soon as it arrives it diminishes and vanishes, because these hypocrites are brothers of the believers by lineage, paternal and maternal uncles and relatives. Perhaps one sits with a true believer, who speaks to him of genuine faith and calls him to it, and this faith sparks in his heart, but it quickly vanishes. We ask God for steadfastness for us and for you.
* Among the lessons of the noble verse: faith must have its effect even on the heart of the hypocrite, as shown by His saying: ﴿fa-lamma adā'at mā ḥawlahu﴾. Faith illuminated some of what is in their hearts, but since it was not on firm foundations, it did not settle. For this reason God said in Surah al-Munafiqun, which is the broadest account God gives about the hypocrites: ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed﴾ [al-Munafiqun 3]. This faith that sparked in their hearts vanished immediately.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the light of faith in the hearts of the hypocrite does not extend beyond their chests, as shown by His saying: ﴿adā'at mā ḥawlahu﴾, and it did not advance forward. They did not believe in the Hereafter nor in the earlier messengers, but this small amount of faith occurred, so it illuminated what was around it, then went away.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: after this light went away, intense darkness, indeed darknesses, followed it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 10–20 (part 4 of 5):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, exalted is He, recompensed them according to what was in their hearts. ﴿Allah took away their light﴾, as if He had taken it by force.
If someone says: Does this not indicate the doctrine of the Jabriyya (determinists)? The answer is no, because this which came from the Lord of the worlds, mighty and majestic, was caused by them. Always keep in mind the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, until it becomes clear to you that whoever Allah describes as having been led astray by Him, the cause is themselves; they are the cause of their own misguidance.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's abandonment of them, by His saying: ﴿and left them﴾. Allah abandoned them. It follows from this that whoever Allah abandons is ruined; he has no light, no guidance, and no righteousness. ﴿And left them in darkness, they do not see﴾, meaning it is not possible for them to have any.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Or like a rainstorm from the sky, in which are darkness, thunder, and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps, for fear of death. And Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers (19). The lightning nearly takes away their sight. Every time it lights for them, they walk in it; and when it darkens over them, they stand still. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ [Al-Baqarah 19–20].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. That concludes the first parable which Allah struck for the hypocrites, because Allah struck for them two parables: the first is a parable of fire, and the second is a parable of water. We have concluded the discussion of the first parable, its benefits and its rulings, is that not so?
* Student: Yes. Regarding the benefits of ﴿deaf, dumb, blind﴾, what have you mentioned?
* The Shaykh: Good. Among the benefits of this verse: these people, may Allah protect us, Allah has made their ears deaf so they do not hear the truth, and even if they heard, they would not benefit. It is permissible to negate a thing because its benefit is negated, as in the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ [Al-Anfal 21].
﴿Dumb﴾: It is also derived from it that these hypocrites do not speak the truth, like the mute.
* It is also derived from this verse that they do not see the truth, like the blind.
* It is derived from this that they will not turn back from their error, because they believe that they are doing good, and that they have become companions of the believers and companions of the disbelievers. They are companions of the believers outwardly, and companions of the disbelievers inwardly. Whoever finds something good hardly ever turns away from it. This is also a benefit.
* A final benefit: when a person finds something good, his turning away from it is far-fetched.
As for the second parable, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or like a rainstorm from the sky﴾. The "or" here is for variety, not for doubt, because Allah, glorified is He, is All-Knowing of everything, so doubt cannot enter into His report. It is therefore for variety. Is this type another parable that applies to the people of the first parable, or is it a parable for different categories of hypocrites? On this there are two opinions among the scholars. Some said: the state of the hypocrites resembles both the first parable and the second parable. Others said: each parable is for a group of these hypocrites. After we explain this parable, God willing, it will become clear which of the two opinions is more correct.
His saying: ﴿Or like a rainstorm﴾. It was said: there is an omitted element, and the estimate is "like the people of a rainstorm," evidenced by His saying: ﴿they put their fingers﴾, i.e., the people of this rainstorm put their fingers in their ears. It was also said: this does not need this estimate; rather Allah struck the parable with the rainstorm itself. The ṣayyib is the rain, and it was named so because it descends, and everything descending is called ṣayyib. Its root is from ṣāba yaṣūb. Now we find that one of the two yāʾs is converted from a wāw. Which one? The first yāʾ or the second?
* The students: The first.
* The Shaykh: Its original form is ṣayyib (ṣaywib), so it is the second. However, the wāw and the yāʾ came together in one word and the first of them was preceded by a sukūn, so the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and assimilated into the first yāʾ. This is a morphological rule that perhaps someone who has not studied ṣarf may not know, but it is a morphological rule: when a wāw and a yāʾ come together in a word and one of them is preceded by a sukūn, the wāw must be changed into a yāʾ and then merged with the existing yāʾ.
﴿Or like a rainstorm from the sky﴾. The phrase ﴿from the sky﴾ is a clarification of the actual situation, not a restrictive qualifier excluding what contradicts the explicit statement. The ṣayyib must necessarily be from the sky, because we said it is what descends, namely rain. The benefit of mentioning it is to clarify the reality from one aspect, and to show that this ṣayyib is great, because what descends from the sky frightens more than what flows on the earth, since what flows on the earth can be escaped, but what descends from the sky cannot be escaped.
﴿Or like a rainstorm from the sky, in which are darkness, thunder, and lightning﴾. ﴿Darkness﴾ is the plural of ẓulma. What are these darknesses? The darkness of the night, that is one. The second: the darkness of the clouds. The third: the darkness of the ṣayyib, which is the rain, for it causes darkness: ﴿in which are darkness﴾. ﴿And thunder﴾, which is the sound heard from the clouds. ﴿And lightning﴾, which is the light or brightness seen in the clouds. Lightning precedes thunder, because the thunder is delayed by the distance between it and the earth, and sound is slower than light, because light is perceived by the eye and sound is perceived by the ear.
﴿And thunder and lightning; they put their fingers﴾. The subject of "they put" returns to the people of the rainstorm, not to the rain. The rain has no fingers and no ears. Rather, "they put," i.e., those who were struck by this rainstorm, so the meaning is: "or like a rainstorm from the sky, in which are darkness, thunder, and lightning, which struck a people, and so they put their fingers in their ears." Fingers are well known, and ears are likewise well known.
But in His saying ﴿their fingers﴾, how is this correct, given that the finger does not enter the ear; only the fingertip enters it? Yet because of the intensity of their inserting the finger, it is as if they try to get all their fingers in, so as not to hear the sound of the thunder, and this is evidence of their cowardice and fear.
﴿Their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps﴾. The "min" here is causal: because of the thunderclaps that the clouds send.
The thunderclap is a great electrical charge that Allah, mighty and majestic, sends, striking whom He wills. Allah sends it and strikes whom He wills. Glory be to Allah, it may strike a man on his bed with his wife, killing the man while the woman is spared; or it may strike a sheep being pulled by its owner, and the owner is spared; or it may strike one who drives it, and the driver is spared. This is because Allah, exalted is He, sends it and strikes whom He wills. The matter is not random; rather everything with Allah is in due measure. They say that even if all the electricity generators in the world were combined at their strongest, they would not reach what this charge carries. This is something clear. When you see the lightning, glory be to Allah the Mighty, how far is it from us? Distances. Yet when it flashes, you find it sometimes as wide as a span, meaning its width, despite its distance. An aircraft at its level, if it were below it, would not be as visible as a faint star. You find something enormous, and the light that falls on the earth from it shows that it is something great.
And His saying: ﴿against the thunderclaps for fear of death﴾. ﴿Thunderclaps﴾ is the plural of ṣāʿiqa, which is what strikes a person and destroys him. ﴿For fear of death﴾ is an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), and its governing verb is ﴿they put﴾. The meaning is that they do this so that they will not die. But does this avail them anything? It does not avail. It is like the act of the ostrich that thrusts its head into the sand so as not to see the hunter, yet the hunter sees it, and so it is not saved by that. Likewise, those who put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps are not saved by this; if Allah wills to strike them, He strikes them. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers﴾, so this caution will not benefit them.
Then Allah explained the severity of this for them, the severity of the light. Having shown the intensity of the sound and that they flee from it and cannot bear it, ﴿they put their fingers in their ears﴾, He showed the intensity of the light upon them, saying: ﴿The lightning nearly takes away their sight﴾, because their sight is weak and cannot bear it. It nearly takes their sight, meaning it snatches it quickly, because it comes swiftly, and then swift darkness follows it, which may be a cause of losing sight. Then He said: ﴿Every time it lights for them, they walk in it; and when it darkens over them, they stand still.﴾ Notice the difference: for the illumination He said: ﴿every time it lights for them, they walk in it﴾, as if they seize the opportunity of the illumination, not delaying from the light for an instant, seizing the opportunity in ﴿every time it lights for them, they walk in it﴾, even if only a little. And this is a small thing: if the lightning is not successive in quick succession, its flash is very brief; they do not take a step before the darkness has come upon them.
﴿Every time it lights for them, they walk in it; and when it darkens over them, they stand still﴾, meaning they stop. ﴿They stand still﴾ means they stop. ﴿When it darkens over them, they stand still.﴾ How does it darken over them? Because the flash of lightning produces darkness upon the darkness of the night. We mentioned at the beginning of the verse that there are darknesses: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the clouds, and the darkness of the rain. When it darkens over them, they stand still. So this is a fourth darkness, namely the loss of light, for when the light is lost, the thing becomes darker than it actually is. Thus the darknesses become four. ﴿And when it darkens over them, they stand still﴾, meaning they stop.
﴿And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight﴾, without the thunderclaps occurring and without the lightning occurring, because Allah, exalted is He, is competent over all things. He is able to take away hearing and sight without causes. Hearing without thunderclaps, because the thunderclaps have a great sound that may deafen the ears, and the lightning has a great light that may snatch the sight. ﴿If Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight﴾ without this happening. ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾.
Let us now see to what this parable applies. This parable applies to a people who were hypocrites and never believed at all. They never believed. Their origin is hypocrisy, and they are the Jewish hypocrites, because among the hypocrites were Arabs from the Khazraj and the Aws, and among them were Jews from the Children of Israel. The Jews never tasted the flavor of Islam at all. Why? Because they were disbelievers from the origin. But they showed Islam out of fear of the Prophet ﷺ after Allah strengthened him at Badr. These are not upon guidance like the first group. The first group kindled the fire, and they had some light from this fire, then, may Allah protect us, they overturned. But these were in darkness from the origin.
Therefore this parable is other than the first parable, rather it is for a different people. The hypocrites are without doubt of different categories, and the state of these, who never entered Islam from the origin, is like the state of those people whom the rainstorm struck, and their state became what you see. So let us consider.
* "The thunderclaps" represent what the Qur'an contains of warning and fear, and therefore Allah says of them in another verse: ﴿They think every cry is against them﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 4].
* "The lightning" represents the light of Islam, but it is not a light that lasts. The light of lightning, as you know, what is it? It ends in an instant, a flash. These did not let faith enter their hearts at all, nor did they reflect on it, but they see this great light that shone, and they benefit from it merely for a step they take, and after that they stand still.
Likewise: ﴿The lightning nearly takes away their sight﴾, because they cannot bear to see the light that the Prophet ﷺ brought. Rather, because of their arrogance and envy toward the Arabs, this lightning nearly blinds their sight, because it is strong against them, and they cannot resist or face it. So the apparent preferred view is that these two are two parables that apply to two categories of hypocrites.
Now, if someone says: How can we say that the first category had faith enter their hearts? We say: Yes, Allah says: ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 3]. Faith entered them, but it did not take root in their hearts. They became like the Bedouins who said: ﴿We believe﴾ [Al-Hujurat 14], and Allah said: ﴿Say, "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted'"﴾ [Al-Hujurat 14]. Otherwise, when faith enters the heart with true entry, settling the person in it, he will not leave it, by Allah's permission. For this reason Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan about the companions of the Messenger, peace be upon him, who entered Islam: "Has anyone of them apostatized from his religion?" He said: No. He said: "This is faith; when it penetrates the heart, it does not leave it." [Narrated by al-Bukhari (7) from the hadith of Abu Sufyan, with the wording: "Does anyone turn back out of displeasure with his religion after entering it?" I mentioned that no. And likewise faith, when its radiance mingles with the hearts.]
But the fragile faith that has not taken root in the heart is what should be feared for its owner. May Allah protect us and you.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the perfection of the eloquence and clarity of the Qur'an, by striking tangible parables to reach knowledge of intelligible meanings.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the establishment of analogy (qiyas) in the Sharia. We mentioned earlier the principle that every parable in the Qur'an indicates what? It indicates the establishment of analogy, because its purpose is to join this thing to that thing.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whenever darkness intensifies, a person becomes more terrified, by His saying: ﴿in which are darkness, thunder, and lightning; they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps﴾.
* Among its benefits also: fear of thunder and lightning was a natural matter, because thunder sometimes causes thunderclaps. If it were merely a sound or a light, people would not be frightened, but people fear what? They fear the thunderclaps. As for mere sound, even if it were stronger than this, it does not frighten people, but they are frightened by this. However, it has been said: when you hear the sound of thunder, you have been spared from the thunderclap; is that correct?
* Student: Correct.
* The Shaykh: Why? Because light is faster, so this electrical charge reaches the earth before you hear the sound. When you hear the sound, know that you have been spared from this thunderclap that is in this thunder.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of a person's stinginess with his life, by His saying: ﴿they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps, for fear of death﴾. It is known that if a person pushes his finger far into his ear, he will feel pain, but he endures it out of fear of what is more painful, namely death. Can it be derived from this that one may commit the lesser of two harms to avert the greater of them?
* The students: Yes.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 10–20 (part 5 of 5):

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is possible, but as you know, this is a natural matter, not a legal one. An example of committing the lesser of two harms to avert the greater is what happened with al-Khidr when he damaged the ship in order to preserve it; for the ship was going to pass by a king who seizes sound ships by force. If it passed by him while it was damaged, he would leave it alone. Thus, damaging part of it was for the sake of preserving the whole.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning to the disbelievers that Allah encompasses them, based on His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِين﴾ (And Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers).
* Among its benefits: the move from the sensory meaning to the intellectual meaning. For Allah did not say "encompassing them," but rather ﴿مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِين﴾, and the example that was struck is struck as an example for the human being; that is, any person, if there are darknesses, thunder and lightning, will fear and grieve.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse, which comes after what? ﴿يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ﴾ (The lightning nearly snatches away their sight). Among its benefits: that intense lightning snatches away the sight, and for this reason a person is forbidden to look at lightning when the sky is flashing, lest his sight be snatched away.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: seizing opportunities; ﴿كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِيه﴾ (Whenever it lights up for them, they walk in it), and that seizing opportunities is among the deeds of the wise.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: avoiding ruin; ﴿وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا﴾ (And when it darkens over them, they stand still).
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's will, based on the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾ (Had Allah willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight).
* Among its benefits: that a person should turn to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, asking Him to let him enjoy his hearing and his sight. In the transmitted supplication: "Let us enjoy our hearing and our sight for as long as You keep us alive"[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (3502) with the wording: "Let us enjoy our hearing, our sight and our strength for as long as You keep us alive."]]; based on His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of this name of Allah, which is: al-Qadir (the All-Powerful).
* Among its benefits: the generality of Allah's power over everything. He, Majestic and Exalted, is All-Powerful over everything: He is able to bring the non-existent into existence, to annihilate what exists, to change the righteous into corrupt and the corrupt into righteous, and other than that.
* Student: Shaykh, we have said that if you hear thunder, you are safe from the thunderbolt. Does this verse say: ﴿فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ﴾ (in it are darknesses and thunder), and do they put their fingers in their ears because of the thunderbolts?
* The Shaykh: This is their assumption, their assumption that they are safe. But they are not safe, because Allah said: ﴿وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِين﴾.
* The Student: So this saying is not absolute?
* The Shaykh: No, it is absolute.
* Student: If it repeats..?
* The Shaykh: Leave it: if it repeats, this is a new charge. That is why we said: the earlier charge, upon hearing the thunder, no longer strikes.
* Student: One may be struck by the thunderbolt in this same rain?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but from a new charge. That is, if it is supposed that the lightning repeats, this can come without you having heard it first.
* Student: Sound and light are very different.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Shaykh, if it is said: among the benefits of this verse, from the standpoint of rhetoric, is that it expressed the whole and meant the part, does that necessarily imply the affirmation of metaphor (majaz)?
* The Shaykh: Which one? ﴿يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُم﴾ (They put their fingers)? No, it does not necessarily imply it, because everyone knows that the intended meaning of "fingers" is not the entire finger.
* Student: If it is said like this, he expressed the whole and meant the part?
* The Shaykh: Yes, for emphasis.
* Student: He expressed the part and meant...
* The Shaykh: No, he expressed the whole and meant the part.
* Student: Does the lightning's snatching of these people's sight apply only to them?
* The Shaykh: No. This is the reality: it nearly snatches away their sight. For this reason, when a person wants to turn off the lamp, he should close his eyes or cover his face; this is something observed.
* Student: Shaykh, the mention of lightning and thunder as a warning: is it only for the hypocrites and disbelievers, or is it general? That is, we now do not fear things like lightning. Is this a sign of faith?
* The Shaykh: No, this is natural fear, may Allah bless you. Every person fears.
* Student: But now no one fears the intensity of thunder and lightning except when in the desert?
* The Shaykh: No one fears? Except al-Hajjaj, if what is reported about him is authentic: when he besieged Mecca, Allah sent clouds containing thunder and lightning, and they would frighten him, and he would say: "No, what is this? These are merely the thunderclaps of Hijaz," or a word similar to that. That is, he was reckless, and Allah forbid. Otherwise, by his nature a person must fear.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 10–20 (part 1 of 5):

Then the Exalted said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10].

* In this noble verse there are benefits. First: the hypocrites are sick at heart, as His saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ indicates. He made the disease enclosed within the heart as a container, as if it has settled in the heart—may Allah protect us—﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾. So what is the disease of these people? The disease of these people is doubt, or disbelief, denial, deception and scheming, and what resembles that.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever Allah knows to have evil and wickedness in him, He increases him in his wickedness and evil. For this reason He said: ﴿so Allah increased them in disease﴾. This is stronger than His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5], because this is explicit that Allah increased them in disease, and when disease increases, the outcome is destruction.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a warning to these hypocrites of a painful, agonizing punishment, as His saying: ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾ indicates.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of causation, as His saying: ﴿because they used to lie﴾ indicates. In another reading: ﴿yukadhdhibūn﴾ (they deny), as has passed. So they are liars and deniers. This is one of the benefits of the two readings: the first indicates that they themselves lie, and the second that they deny the truth and sincerity.
Affirming causes is what the Sharia, reason and reality all indicate, and denying them is a deficiency in reason and a deficiency in religion, I mean negating them; for everyone knows that everything has a cause, but among them are causes that are known and among them are causes that are unknown to us.
The scholars of the community have differed regarding causes: some went to excess concerning them, some neglected them, and some took the middle course.
As for those who went to excess concerning them, they said: causes are effective in themselves, not by a receptive locus nor by an acting cause; they are effective in themselves, and Allah has no connection to them at all. These are the naturalists and philosophers who make things interact by themselves with no relation to Allah the Exalted. Without doubt this is shirk and denial of the Creator.
The second category neglected causes and said: causes have no effect whatsoever; if we granted them an effect we would be affirming a partner with Allah. The burning of what is burnable by fire is not by the fire; rather it burns when Allah places it there, not by it. Likewise they say regarding breaking: when a thing breaks, glass breaks by a stone. They say: the stone did not break the glass; it broke upon impact, not by the impact. Without doubt this is foolishness in reason and error in religion. As for the foolishness in reason, it is obvious: if any child among the children were to throw a stone at glass and it shattered, and you asked: what broke it? What would he say? The stone, by its nature and disposition. As for it being error in religion, it is because the Qur'an and the Sunnah are filled with the mention of causes and the effect of causes, but their effect is by what Allah deposited in them of effective powers.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah the Exalted is a just Judge who punishes only those who deserve it, because He said: ﴿for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie﴾.
* Among the benefits of the verse: that variant readings bring an increase in meaning. The saying ﴿yakdhibūn﴾ is one reading, and ﴿yukadhdhibūn﴾ is another reading. If the verse contained only ﴿yakdhibūn﴾, the threat would be upon their lying themselves, saying "We believe" while they are not believers. And if it were ﴿yukadhdhibūn﴾, the threat would also be upon their denying, not upon their lying. So when the two readings are combined, an additional meaning is achieved.
Among its parallels: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ and ﴿Owner of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4], with the alif and without it. The benefit increases by combining the two readings, that Allah is a king, what? an owner. For among the created there is one who is a king but not an owner, and there is one who is an owner but not a king. And there are similar examples, such as: ﴿If a degenerate comes to you with news, then verify﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6], and in another reading ﴿then be certain﴾. This combines two meanings: tabayyun (clarification) first and tathabbut (verification) second; that is, be certain until it becomes clear to you—tathabbut first and bayan second, the reverse of what I said: tathabbut first, then tabayyun second. ﴿And when it is said to them: do not cause corruption on the earth﴾. Who says it? The believers: ﴿do not cause corruption on the earth﴾, and by what? By their deception, their cheating and their lying.
﴿They say: we are only reformers﴾, meaning: we are nothing but reformers. Praise be to Allah that they did not say "we are the reformers"; had they said "we are the reformers" it would have been a greater claim, since if they said "we are the reformers," it means there is no reformer other than them. But when they said "we are reformers," it does not prevent others from being reformers too; yet they restricted their attributes to being reformers, meaning there is nothing of corruption in them. But Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿Surely they are the corrupters﴾. He refuted them a strong refutation. By what was it strong? Firstly: by the opening particle (alā), which conveys alertness and emphasis. Secondly: by (inna), which conveys emphasis. Thirdly: by (hum), which is a separating pronoun conveying restriction and emphasis.
So the Exalted said: ﴿Surely they—they themselves—are﴾, alone, ﴿the corrupters, but they do not perceive﴾ their corruption; because they—may Allah protect us—have had a seal set upon their hearts, so there is no awareness in them.
* In this verse there are benefits: these hypocrites were advised, but they insisted upon what they were on, thinking that it was reform.
* Among the benefits of this verse: caution, that a person should beware of blindness of the heart, whereby he does an action thinking he is a reformer while he is a corrupter. This is among the greatest losers, indeed the greatest of people in deeds.
