* Shaykh: ﴿then produce a surah like it﴾. This is the aspect of defence, because the command here is a challenge. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, challenges these people to bring forth something opposing what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, brought.
Among them: the excellence of the Prophet, ﷺ, by describing him with servitude. Servitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the ultimate freedom, because whoever does not worship Allah must worship something else. If he does not worship Allah, the One deserving of worship, he worships Satan and his desires, as Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Nuniyyah:
"They fled from the bondage for which they were created,
and were afflicted with the bondage of the self and Satan."
* Among the benefits of this verse: the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. This is based on His saying ﴿what We have sent down﴾. The reason it is the speech of Allah is that the Qur'an is speech, and speech is not bodies that are created and separate from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Rather, it is an attribute of the speaker. From this we know that whoever claims the Qur'an is created, and says that Allah said ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 3], and ﴿We have sent down to you the Reminder﴾ [An-Nahl 44], and similar verses, then his statement is rejected. He has no proof in verses such as His saying ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾ [Al-Hadid 25], and His saying ﴿He sent down for you eight kinds of livestock﴾ [Az-Zumar 6], and His saying ﴿He made the darknesses and the light﴾ [Al-An'am 1]. All of this is not proof for them, because there is a difference between the entities that subsist by themselves, which Allah attributes to Himself, and the attributes which do not subsist by themselves.
* Among the benefits of the verse: the loftiness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is because once it is established that the Qur'an is His speech and that it was sent down from Him, it necessarily follows that the speaker is elevated. The loftiness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is a matter of natural (fitri) and rational ('aqli) knowledge. We have previously mentioned five types of evidence for it, which are: the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus (ijma'), reason, and the innate nature (fitrah).
If someone says: "You mentioned that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was honoured by the attribution of his servitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, although the disbelievers and the wicked of creation are also servants of Allah, as He said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]?"
The answer to this is that servitude has several meanings: general servitude, which is the universal, predestined servitude (al-'ubudiyyah al-kawniyyah al-qadariyyah). This encompasses everyone, and no one can avoid submitting to this servitude. So the disbeliever and the wicked person is a servant of Allah, meaning that Allah does with him whatever He wills. And there is specific servitude, which is the servitude of obedience, specific to those who believe in Allah and follow His law. This specific servitude can also be divided into a general specific and a more specific specific. So the servitude of the Messengers is different from the servitude of the truthful ones (siddiqin), the martyrs, and the righteous. The former is more perfect and more specific.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Qur'an is inimitable even by a single short sura, as shown by His words ﴿a sura like it﴾. Allah, mighty and majestic, challenged them to produce a sura like it, and to produce ten suras like it, and He informed them that no one would ever produce the like of this Qur'an even if mankind and the jinn gathered together. At the least, we know that they cannot produce a single statement like it, meaning even one sentence. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, they do not believe. So let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾ [al-Tur 33–34]. The word "hadith" applies to a sentence, however short. Accordingly, the challenge takes four forms: with the whole Qur'an, with ten of its suras, with a single sura, and with a single statement.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the challenge is addressed to these worshippers together with the objects they worship. This is more humiliating than being challenged alone. It is as if He is saying: "You and your gods, produce a sura like it." This is the utmost in disgrace, humiliation, shame and ignominy.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: no one can oppose the speech of Allah, as shown by His words ﴿and you will never do it﴾. In this statement there are two arguments. The first is the argument of those who hold the doctrine of *al-sarfah* (the doctrine that Allah diverted people from producing its like), meaning that man by his nature is able to produce the like of the Qur'an, but he was diverted from it. On this view, the challenge is possible, but an obstacle was present, namely that Allah diverted them from opposing it, so that they did not want to.

The second argument is that they will never do it by the nature of their creation, not that they were diverted while they are able to oppose the Qur'an. This second view is the one that is definitive, because the first view or the first possibility does not show that the Qur'an is inimitable in itself, since they could produce its like but Allah diverted them, and they did not pay attention to it or think about it. But we say: this is wrong. The correct view is that man by himself cannot produce the like of the Qur'an, because the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and speech is an attribute of the speaker. Just as man cannot resemble Allah in His attributes, he cannot resemble Allah in what? In His speech. It is absolutely impossible. This is why those who claimed prophethood and produced what they called a Qur'an became a mockery to the servants and a laughingstock, as is related of Musaylimah the Liar and others. Therefore the correct view is that His words ﴿you will never do it﴾ do not mean "you will be diverted from it and will not do it." Rather, the meaning is that you are incapable by the nature of man. The reason for what we have said is that speech is an attribute of the speaker, and the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, mighty and majestic. Just as men do not resemble the attributes of Allah in knowledge, power, hearing, sight and other things, likewise man cannot resemble Allah in speech.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever wants to oppose the Qur'an, his abode is the Fire, as shown by His words ﴿so fear the Fire which﴾.

* Among the further benefits of this noble verse: people are fuel for the Fire, just as fire is kindled with firewood. The Fire burns them at the same time, and they are also the fuel with which it is kindled. Thus the punishment comes upon them from two aspects. The first aspect: they are the material with which it is kindled. The second: they are burned by it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the humiliation of these disbelievers by the degradation of their gods and their being cast into the Fire, according to one of two interpretations of His words ﴿the stones﴾. It is well known that a person is jealous of those he worshipped and does not want harm to befall them. So when these worshipped objects are burned in front of their worshippers, this is part of the complete humiliation and disgrace of the latter.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Fire exists now, as shown by His words ﴿it has been prepared﴾. It is well known that this construction is a past verb, the sentence is in the past tense, and the past tense indicates the existence of the thing. This is a matter indicated by the Sunnah. The Prophet ﷺ was shown Paradise and the Fire, and he saw their people being punished in it. He saw 'Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire.[[Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari (3521, 4623) and Muslim (2856/50, 51).]] He saw the woman who imprisoned a cat until it died of hunger; she had neither fed it nor released it to eat the insects of the earth. He also saw in it the owner of the *mihjan* being punished. He was a man who had a *mihjan* (a staff bent at the head), and he used to rob pilgrims on this road. When the pilgrims passed by him, he pulled them with the *mihjan*. If the owner of the baggage noticed, he claimed that it was the *mihjan* that pulled it, by Allah, it was this *mihjan* that pulled it. If he did not notice, he took it and walked on. So he was punished — may Allah protect us — "with his *mihjan* in the fires of Hell."[[Related by Muslim (904/10).]]

Then, does the Fire remain or does it perish? Some scholars mentioned a consensus (*ijma'*, scholarly agreement) of the early generations (*al-salaf*) that it remains and does not perish. Others mentioned a disagreement from some of the early generations that it perishes. The correct view is that it remains forever and ever. The evidence for this from the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic, is in three verses of the Qur'an: in Surat al-Nisa', Surat al-Ahzab and Surat al-Jinn.

As for the verse in Surat al-Nisa', it is His words:
* Student: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged, Allah would never forgive them nor guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Nisa' 168–169].
* Shaykh: Well done, may Allah bless you.

And the one in Surat al-Ahzab. Those at the back, join us, may Allah bless you.
* Student: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and has prepared for them a blazing Fire. Abiding therein forever, they will find no protector or helper﴾ [al-Ahzab 64–65].
* Shaykh: Well done. ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and has prepared for them a blazing Fire. Abiding therein forever, they will find no protector or helper.﴾ And the one in Surat al-Jinn?
* Student: ﴿The Fire of Hell, abiding therein.﴾
* Shaykh: That is not enough. Recite the verse from its beginning.
* Student: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, indeed for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Jinn 23].
* Shaykh: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, indeed for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.﴾ And there is no speech after the speech of Allah. I even recall a comment by our shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'di, may Allah have mercy on him, on the book *Shifa' al-'Alil* by Ibn al-Qayyim. He said that this is from the category of "every good horse stumbles, and every sharp sword blunts." How is it that the author, may Allah have mercy on him, cites these proofs for the view that the Fire perishes, when the matter is clear in them? It is strange, and unlike Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, that he cites evidence with such strength for the view that the Fire perishes. In any case, as our shaykh said on this issue: every good horse stumbles, and every sharp sword blunts. This is one of the stumbles of Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him. The correct view, which is beyond doubt and which I hold as certain, is that the Fire remains forever and ever. For if the one who abides in it abides eternally, it necessarily follows that the Fire is also everlasting, since the dweller of a house whose dwelling is eternal must have an eternal dwelling-place as well. As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾ [Hud 107], it is like His words about the people of Paradise: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾ [Hud 108]. But since the bliss and reward of the people of Paradise are a bounty and favour, He made clear that this bounty is not cut off, saying: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾ [Hud 108]. And since the punishment of the people of the Fire is a matter of justice and the absolute authority of the Lord, mighty and majestic, He said at the end of the verse: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends﴾ [Hud 107]. The meaning is not that your Lord accomplishes what He intends in that He will bring them out of the Fire, or that He will cause the Fire to perish. No. The meaning is that they remain in it as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as Allah wills, in accordance with the action of Allah, mighty and majestic, who has complete authority.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Fire is the abode of the disbelievers, as shown by His words ﴿it has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾. As for those among the sinners who enter it, they do not remain in it. They are in it like visitors and guests; they must leave it. So the Fire is not called their abode. Rather, it is the abode of the disbeliever alone. As for the believing sinner, if Allah does not pardon him, he is punished in it as long as Allah wills, and then he leaves it, either by intercession or by Allah's favour and grace. But as for the people of the Fire, who are its inhabitants, it has been prepared for them and they will not leave it. May Allah protect us and you from it.
* The students: Amen.
* Shaykh: When Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned this threat to the people of the Fire, He said: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. But before we move past the verse we are explaining, if someone says: what is the aspect of the inimitability of the Qur'an, and how did it render mankind unable? This is the first question. Second: Allah, mighty and majestic, related sayings of the prophets and messengers and of those who opposed them. This narration relates the statement of the one about whom it is related, so the statement of these people would be inimitable. For example, Pharaoh said to Moses: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 29]. Allah relates this about Pharaoh. So whose statement is it? It is the statement of Pharaoh. How then can Pharaoh's statement be inimitable, when inimitability belongs only to the speech of Allah, mighty and majestic?

The answer to the first: in what way was it inimitable? It is inimitable in all aspects of inimitability: in its style, eloquence and clarity, and in that it does not bore one who recites it. A person may recite the Qur'an morning and evening, and may complete it in two or three days, and never become bored with it at all. But if one repeats any other text, one becomes bored. Second: it is inimitable in that whenever a person recites it with reflection, something appears to him in the second reading that did not appear in the first. This is so for one who truly reflects.

* * *
* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds, that for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom as provision, they say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in likeness. And for them therein are purified spouses, and they will abide therein forever﴾ [al-Baqarah 25].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. The connection of the verse with what precedes it is that when Allah mentioned the threat to the disbelievers who denied the Messenger ﷺ, He mentioned the promise to the believers in him. So He said: ﴿And give good tidings﴾. Good tidings (*bushra*) is the report of what pleases, and it is so named because the complexion of the one addressed changes with joy. When a person is told what pleases him, his face brightens, his soul becomes content, and his chest is expanded. The term "good tidings" may also be used for the report of what grieves, as in His words: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran 21], either in mockery of them, or because they receive from this news something similar to what those who are given good news receive. But the first is closer, because they do not believe in what they are given tidings of, namely the punishment, so this is a kind of mockery of them, as in His words about their punishment on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Then pour over his head some of the torment of boiling water. "Taste it; indeed you were the mighty, the honourable"﴾ [al-Dukhan 48–49].

﴿And give good tidings to those who believe﴾. The address in His words ﴿give good tidings﴾ is either to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, or to everyone who is addressed. That is, "Give good tidings, O addressee, to those who possess these qualities, that for them are gardens." His words ﴿those who believe﴾ refer to those who believe in what must be believed in of what Allah and His Messenger have informed. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, explained the foundations of faith as: "Faith is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, both its good and its evil."[[Related by Muslim (8/1).]] But faith in these matters is not merely affirming them; there must be acceptance and submission, otherwise faith would not be valid.

As for His words ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, it is the fruit of faith, that a person does righteous deeds. And righteous deeds are those built upon two foundations: sincerity to Allah, and following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. What lacks sincerity is corrupt, according to Allah's words in the sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners from partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his association."[[Related by Muslim (2985/46).]]

And what is not in accordance with the Prophet's way is also rejected and not accepted, according to the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."[[Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/17, 18); the wording is Muslim's.]] So what is righteous? It is what is sincerely for Allah and follows the law of Allah. It is related from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: what is sincere and correct.[[Tafsir al-Baghawi (8/176).]]

He said: ﴿that for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. This is the good tidings given: ﴿that for them﴾ with whom? With Allah, mighty and majestic. ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. These gardens agree with what is in this world in name, but they differ from it in reality and essence, according to the words of Allah, exalted: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]. For this reason, it is never permissible in any circumstances to imagine that these gardens resemble the gardens of this world. Whatever gardens, trees and fruits exist in this world, what Allah has promised the righteous cannot be like them, according to His words: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾. And according to His words in the sacred hadith: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[[Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari (3244) and Muslim (2824/2).]]

﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾. ﴿The rivers﴾ is the subject of (flow), and ﴿beneath it﴾ — the scholars said: beneath its trees and palaces, not from below its surface. No, for if they were below its surface there would be no benefit in them. Rather they flow beneath these trees and palaces. How beautiful is the flowing of these rivers when they are beneath the trees and palaces. A person finds delight in them before he partakes of them. Allah, exalted, has explained that these rivers are of four kinds, as He said: ﴿The description of Paradise which the righteous are promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 15]. Allah, mighty and majestic, creates them without bees, without cows, and without camels. Likewise the wine. And the water is not from rain or springs; rather Allah created it from the beginning. I ask Allah not to deprive me and you of them, for He is powerful over all things.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 21–25 (part 4 of 5):**

﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا﴾: Rivers flow beneath them. Whenever they are provided with some fruit from them as sustenance.
﴿رُزِقُوا﴾ means "were given." ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ means "from these fruits." ﴿مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا﴾ means "a gift."
﴿قَالُوا هَذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾: They will say, "This is what we were given before," because it resembles what came before. It resembles it in size, in color, and in texture. These are all sensory qualities that a person assumes to be similar to what came before in its color, what? and its size and texture. But in taste, no. It differs enormously. For this reason He said: ﴿أُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾: they will be brought it resembling one another. How beautiful and how delightful it is for a person who sees this fruit and considers it to be one thing. Then when he tastes it, the taste differs enormously. You will find that he experiences a stirring in himself, a delight, and wonder: how can something so greatly different have the same appearance? ﴿وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾. Now, if fruits were presented to you whose colors were the same, whose sizes were the same, and whose textures were the same, and then when you tasted them, one was pure sweet, and another was bitter, meaning sweet mixed with sourness, and another was sour, you would find more delight than if they were all equal or all different.
﴿وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾: Is "أُتُوا" from (آتى) or from (أتى)? The second or the first?
* The students: The first, the first.
* The Shaykh: From (آتى) or from (أتى)?
* The students: From (آتى), the first.
* The Shaykh: No, the second. ﴿أُتُوا بِهِ﴾, because if it were from the first, he would say: "أُوتوا به." But ﴿أُتُوا بِهِ﴾ means it was brought to them, resembling one another. Resembling one another in what? We said: in three things. This is what comes to mind now, and Allah knows best what it will be: in color, size, and texture. But not in taste, because if it agreed in taste too, this would be that and that would be this, with no difference. ﴿وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾.
﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾: Glory be to Allah! Whenever Allah mentions fruit, He mentions spouses. Reflect on this in all the verses. Why? Because they, and their spouses, will enjoy these gifts and this provision. ﴿إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ الْيَوْمَ فِي شُغُلٍ فَاكِهُونَ (٥٥) هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ فِي ظِلَالٍ عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾ [Ya-Sin 55–56]. You find that Allah joins this with that, because all of it is enjoyment (tafakkuh). But this enjoyment is of one kind, and that is of another kind. This is enjoyment in taste and food, and that is another enjoyment of a second kind, because with it the blessing is complete.
﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ﴾: "أَزْوَاجٌ" is plural. Does the meaning mean that each one has spouses? Or that each individual has a wife, but since they are a group, the plural is matched with the plural?
* The students: The first.
* The Shaykh: The first. Because a person in the Hereafter has multiple spouses. "Azwaj" is the plural of "zawj," and "zawj" is applied to both the male and the female. For this reason, "zawj" is said of a woman and of a man. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزْوَاجُكُمْ﴾ [An-Nisa 12]: "And for you is half of what your wives leave." But in the terminology of the faraid scholars (scholars of inheritance), they began to add the feminine ending (ta') for the female, to distinguish her from the male when dividing the inheritance. ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾. Now, if a woman died while young and had never married, will she have a husband in the Hereafter?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes, she will have a husband in the Hereafter, either from the people of this world or from those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will create. This is because there will remain in Paradise a surplus beyond those who have entered it from the people of this world. Allah will create for her men, and He will admit them into Paradise by His bounty and mercy.
His saying: ﴿مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾ includes purity of the outward and the inward. She is purified from filth and impurity: there is no urine, no feces, no menstruation (hayd), no postnatal bleeding (nifas), no irregular bleeding (istihadah), no sweat, and no bad breath. She is purified from every outward sensory impurity. She is also purified from inward defilements such as rancor, spite, hatred, enmity, and other things. She is purified from everything, from every outward or inward filth and harm. This is unlike the spouses of this world. But the spouses of this world are perfectly suited to their male spouses, because if she is not purified of this, then her husband? Her husband is like her. But in the Hereafter, all are purified.
﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾: This is the completion of blessing, that they will abide forever in these Gardens. They will not desire any change from them, nor will they be removed from them. As it came in the hadith: "Indeed, for you is that you will be healthy and never fall ill, and that you will be youthful and never grow old, and that you will live and never die." [Recorded by Muslim (2837/22) with the wording: "Indeed for you is that you will be healthy and never fall sick, and that you will live and never die, and that you will be youthful and never grow old, and that you will be blessed and never be miserable."] Through this their bliss is completed. But the highest bliss that the people of Paradise will have is looking upon the Face of Allah, Glory be to Allah and Exalted. This is the highest bliss, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنَى وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾ [Yunus 26]: "For those who did good is the best reward and an increase." The Prophet (ﷺ) explained "an increase" as looking upon the Face of Allah. [Recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (18935, 18941), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11170).]
* In this verse there are benefits, among them: the legitimacy of giving a person good news of what pleases him, based on His saying: ﴿بَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾, and Allah's saying: ﴿وَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِإِسْحَاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ [As-Saffat 112]: "And We gave him good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous." ﴿بَشَّرْنَاهُ بِغُلَامٍ حَلِيمٍ﴾ [As-Saffat 101]: "We gave him good news of a forbearing boy." So giving good news of what pleases a person is one of the practices of the messengers, peace be upon them.
(Now) but if what pleases a person is an act of disobedience to Allah, would you give him good news? For example, a person who has committed theft: you come and tell him, "Mashallah, may Allah congratulate you on what you stole!" Never. Rather, good news is only for what pleases and has no bad consequence. Is it among this to give someone good news of the seasons of worship, such as if he reached Ramadan and you said, "May Allah congratulate you on this month"? The answer is yes. Likewise, if he completed the fast and you said, "May Allah congratulate you on this festival, and accept your worship," and the like, there is no harm in that, and this was the custom of the early generations (al-salaf).
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Gardens are only for those who combine these two qualities: faith (iman) and righteous deeds.
If someone says: "The Quran contains what indicates that the qualities are four: faith, righteous deeds, mutual enjoining of truth, and mutual enjoining of patience."
We say: Mutual enjoining of truth and mutual enjoining of patience are among righteous deeds. But sometimes some individual instances of a general category are mentioned for a reason and a cause.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever does a bad deed will not be given good news of these Gardens, based on His saying: ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾. But whoever does a bad deed: if he was striving and erred, he has a reward and is safe from sin. If he was not striving and did not exert his effort, he is sinful, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "When a judge rules and strives and is correct, he has two rewards, and when he rules and strives and errs, he has one reward." [Agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari (7352) and Muslim (1716/15) with the wording: "When a judge rules and strives and then is correct, he has two rewards, and when he rules and strives and then errs, he has one reward."]
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the reward of the believers who did righteous deeds is far greater than what they did, and more magnificent. Because however much they believe and act, their lifespan is limited and ends. But the reward, what? The reward never ends. They abide in it forever, endless ages upon ages. Likewise, the deeds they offer may be mixed with laziness, mixed with fatigue, mixed with things that diminish them. But if Allah bestows His favor on them and they enter Paradise, the bliss is complete.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the Gardens are of various kinds, based on His saying: ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾. It may be said that this is not conclusive evidence, because "Jannat" is a plural matched with a plural, namely His saying: ﴿لَهُمْ﴾, ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾. But the Sunnah, indeed the Quran, shows that the Gardens are of various kinds. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتَانِ﴾ [Ar-Rahman 46]: "And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two Gardens." Then He said: ﴿وَمِنْ دُونِهِمَا جَنَّتَانِ﴾ [Ar-Rahman 62]: "And beneath them are two more Gardens." So they are of various kinds. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Two Gardens of gold, their vessels and all that is in them; and two Gardens of silver, their vessels and all that is in them." [Agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari (4878) and Muslim (296/180) with the wording: "Two Gardens of silver, their vessels and all that is in them, and two Gardens of gold, their vessels and all that is in them."]
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the completeness of Allah's power, the Mighty and Majestic, in creating these rivers without any known cause in this world. For water in our world has known causes, and the sources of water rivers are known. Likewise, milk: it is known from where it is produced. Honey is known. And the fourth? Wine is known. But in Paradise, no. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings it into being: rivers flowing. It has been reported in a narration: "They flow without a trench" [Recorded by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (34954) from Masruq, who said: "The rivers of Paradise flow without a trench."]; meaning no pits have been dug for them, and no banks have been set up to contain them. Rather, the river flows, and a person may direct it as he wishes, turning it wherever he likes. Glory be to Allah! Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Its rivers flowed without a trench,
Glory be to the One who holds them back from overflowing.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: among the bliss of the people of Paradise is that they are brought provision resembling one another, and ﴿كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا قَالُوا هَذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾. This is part of the completeness of bliss and of enjoying what they eat.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of marriage in the Hereafter, and that it is part of the completeness of bliss. Based on this, does intercourse take place or not? It does take place. But if intercourse takes place, does the harm that occurs with the intercourse of the women of this world occur? The answer is no. For this reason there is no semen (mani) nor sperm (manyah) in Paradise. The semen which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created was created only for the continuation of offspring, because this semen contains the material from which the fetus is formed, and it emerges, by Allah's permission, as a child. But in the Hereafter, in Paradise, no. They have no need of that, because there is no need for the continuation of offspring, since those who exist will remain forever, endless ages upon ages, and none of them will perish. Furthermore, they have no need for anyone to assist them or serve them. The youths (wildan) will circulate among them with cups, jugs, and a glass from a flowing spring. Also, they will not need anyone to climb the tree to pick its fruit. Rather, as Allah the Exalted said about them: ﴿وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍ﴾ [Ar-Rahman 54]: "And the fruit of the two Gardens is near at hand." Scholars even mentioned that a man looks at the fruit on the tree and feels he desires it, so the branch draws near to him until he takes it. Allah is greater! Do not be surprised by this. We in this world witness something similar: that a thing draws near to another without any apparent cause or visible connection. But in the Hereafter it is even more profound, and more profound still.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the people of Paradise abide in it forever, endless ages upon ages, and it is impossible for it to perish, and impossible for those in it to perish. Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) unanimously agreed upon this. Those who denied it were the philosophers (ahl al-falsafah), who said: "It is impossible for Allah to continue acting in eternity past and eternity future" (may Allah protect us). Thus they made Allah inactive at the beginning and inactive at the end. Some of them even said (may Allah protect us): "Paradise will perish along with those in it, while a person is raising his morsel to his mouth. Then annihilation occurs, and he remains with his morsel raised, eating, the morsel remaining while his hand is perishing." As Ibn al-Qayyim said in the Nuniyyah: "Indeed al-Allaf came with a ridiculous laugh." Likewise, a person with his family and wife, copulating with her, then the time of annihilation comes, and he remains with her, perishing, endless ages upon ages. We ask Allah for well-being.
In any case, the people of Paradise abide in it forever, endless ages upon ages, by the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah. And the Fire is likewise, according to the established view. What is the preponderant view? That it does not perish. The Fire, according to the established view, does not perish, and it remains endless ages upon ages by the explicit words of the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic. We have explained that Allah stated this explicitly in three verses of the Book of Allah, and we have repeated this often. We did not think that anyone among the people who belong to Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah would say that it perishes. Our Shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'di, may Allah have mercy on him, was surprised that Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah pardon him, tried to prefer the view of its annihilation in his book Shifa' al-'Alil. Our Shaykh said: "This is considered a stumble from this steed and a great error." He wrote this in the margin of the book. There is no doubt that what our Shaykh said is true, and a person is astonished that such a stallion among scholars would go to strengthen this school, although he did not explicitly declare that he chose it. But he went to strengthen it, although it is false by the explicit text of the Quran.
The people of Paradise abide in it forever, by the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah, endless ages upon ages, and the Fire is likewise according to the established view. What is the preponderant view that it perishes? The Fire, according to the established view, does not perish, and it remains endless ages upon ages by the explicit words of the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic. We have explained that Allah stated this explicitly in three verses of the Book of Allah, and we have repeated this much. We did not think that anyone among the people of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah would say it perishes. Our Shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'di, may Allah have mercy on him, was surprised that Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah pardon him, tried to prefer the view of its annihilation in his book Shifa' al-'Alil. Our Shaykh said: "This is considered a stumble from this steed and a great error." He wrote this in the margin of the book. There is no doubt that what our Shaykh said is true, and a person is astonished that such a stallion among scholars would go to strengthen this school, although he did not explicitly declare that he chose it. But he went to strengthen it, although it is false by the explicit text of the Quran: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَظَلَمُوا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ طَرِيقًا (١٦٨) إِلَّا طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا﴾ [An-Nisa 168–169]: "Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged, Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah." And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَنَ الْكَافِرِينَ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ سَعِيرًا (٦٤) خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا لَا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾ [Al-Ahzab 64–65]: "Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever; they will find no protector or helper." And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا﴾ [Al-Jinn 23]: "And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever." How is it correct for us, or how is it right for us, to say that the Fire perishes, while Allah the Exalted says: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا﴾? What is the benefit of His saying: ﴿أَبَدًا﴾? In any case, the school of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah, which is nearly a consensus, is that the Fire does not perish, just as Paradise does not perish, by clear agreement.
From the noble verse it is derived that if a person spent his entire life in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, bowing, prostrating, and standing, that would be little compared to this great reward he receives on a day in which whoever among the servants of Allah is wretched will be wretched, and will be in the blazing Fire, may Allah protect us. We ask Allah the Exalted to help us and you to remember Him, thank Him, and worship Him well. May Allah reward you with good.
* Student: May Allah be gracious to you, O Shaykh. If the opponent said: the intended meaning of His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ بَعْدَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ [An-Nisa 165]: "So that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers," is that this applies to the legal rulings (shara'i'), and otherwise the proof stands regarding monotheism (tawhid) and the foundations of religion through the covenant (al-mithaq) and the fitrah (natural disposition), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ (١٧٢) أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ [Al-A'raf 172–173]: "And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we testify.' Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, 'Indeed, we were unaware of this,' or say, 'Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them.'" So here He affirmed that it is the covenant...?

The Shaykh: The covenant that was taken from them is that they should believe in what the messengers brought. There must be messengers, and the verse is general. ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that people would have no argument against God after the messengers.﴾ [An-Nisa 165] is general. ﴿We would never punish until We send a messenger.﴾ [Al-Isra 15] ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the towns until He sends in their mother-town a messenger reciting to them Our verses.﴾ [Al-Qasas 59] ﴿We would never destroy the towns unless their people were wrongdoers.﴾ [Al-Qasas 59] ﴿God would never lead a people astray after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should beware of.﴾ [At-Tawbah 115] The verses on this are many.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. "O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous (21). He who made for you the earth a bed and the sky a canopy, and sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know [better] (22). And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you should be truthful (23). But if you do not and you will never do so, then fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers" [al-Baqarah: 21–24].

The Shaykh: Well done. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: "O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you." The address here comes with "O mankind," even though the surah is Madani. Most of those addressed in Madani surahs are the believers, and for this reason the scholars of the principles of tafsir (usul al-tafsir) said that one of the marks of Madani surahs is that the address in them is directed to the believers, unlike Makki verses, because most of those addressed in them are non-believers. But this verse is the first verse in which there is a nida' (vocative address). The first verse containing a nida' is this verse, "O mankind, worship your Lord," and therefore the address, or the call through it, is directed to all people, as in the saying of Allah: "Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all."

If someone said: Perhaps this is a Makki verse that was placed in a Madani surah? We say: the original state is that this is not the case. For this reason we see in some headings of surahs: "Makki except verse such-and-such, Madani except verse such-and-such." This is not accepted unless it is established by a sound proof. Otherwise, the original position is that all the verses of a Madani surah are Madani and all the verses of a Makki surah are Makki, unless there is an established proof.

"O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you." In "worship your Lord, who created you" is the affirmation of divinity (al-uluhiyyah), that is, the affirmation of tawhid al-uluhiyyah and tawhid al-rububiyyah. "Worship" (u'budu) is tawhid al-uluhiyyah, because tawhid al-uluhiyyah is called tawhid uluhiyyah with reference to its attribution to Allah, and tawhid 'ibadah with reference to its attribution to the servant.

Allah says: "worship your Lord." So what is the worship we have been commanded to perform? The worship we have been commanded to perform is humbling oneself before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with a complete humility that necessarily entails love and veneration. It is essential, otherwise a person would not be a servant, that he humble himself before Allah completely, what? Entailing love and veneration. With love, one performs the commands until the worshipper reaches his Beloved, and with veneration, one flees from the prohibitions lest his great Lord punish him, the Mighty and Majestic. This is the meaning of worship: humbling oneself before Allah, what? A complete humility entailing love and veneration. Good. This is the explanation of worship with respect to the action of the servant. Worship may also be explained with respect to what the servant does, with respect to its object, so it is said, for example: prayer is worship, zakah is worship, fasting is worship. On this basis Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it, where he said, may Allah have mercy on him: "Worship is a comprehensive term for everything that Allah loves and is pleased with, of statements and actions, both inward and outward." Then he gave examples with prayer, zakah and others. At this point we say: worship is applied to two meanings. The first meaning: the act of worshipping (ta'abbud). The second meaning: that by which one worships, which is the object of the servant's action, meaning what the servant does. Is it clear, O brothers? Good. What is intended by the verse? Both meanings or the first meaning? Apparently both, and they are mutually entailing.

And His saying: "worship your Lord, who created you." The Lord (al-Rabb) is the Creator, the Owner, the Manager (al-mudabbir). The Creator, the Owner, the Manager. On this basis, His saying "who created you" is a descriptive attribute that reveals and clarifies the reality, and it is not a restrictive attribute (sifah ihtiraziyyah), because we do not have two lords, one of whom is a creator and the second not a creator. Rather our Lord is the Creator. So the attribute here is a revealing attribute, not a restrictive one. "worship your Lord who created you." Creation (al-khalq) is bringing into existence from non-existence, and no one created people except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. A father does not create them, nor a mother, nor an angel, nor anyone; none creates them except Allah. And since Allah the Exalted says: "They could not create a fly even if they gathered together for it" [al-Hajj: 73], the non-creation of the children of Adam is a fortiori.

"And those before you," meaning: and He created those who were before you. For this reason we find, glory be to Allah, that the children of Adam succeed one another. You look at the mosque or at a gathering and you find that this one is seventy years old, this one fifty, this one forty, this one thirty, this one twenty, this one ten, this one five, so that the world may be populated; they succeed one another. When you reflect on this, you know the perfection of the authority of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the perfection of His wisdom. Those who came before us are created, and we are their descendants: "And We made his descendants the survivors" [al-Saffat: 77], the descendants of Noah; we are their descendants. Therefore whoever descends from a created being is created. "And those before you." Based on this, His saying "and those before you" is conjoined to what?

Student: The pronoun.

The Shaykh: To the kaf in "khalaqakum" (created you). Yes. "And those before you, that you may become righteous" (la'allakum tattaqun): here la'alla is for causation, i.e., so that you may attain taqwa. It is known that taqwa is a high rank, to the extent that Allah the Mighty and Majestic said about Paradise: "prepared for the righteous" [Al 'Imran: 133], and the Exalted said: "Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good" [al-Nahl: 128], and the Exalted said: "And know that Allah is with the righteous" [al-Baqarah: 194].

"That you may become righteous (21). He who made for you the earth a bed and the sky a canopy, and sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you." This is by way of enumerating types, or enumerating kinds of His actions, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah made the earth a bed for us, smoothed, on which a person settles with complete settledness; it is not rough and not painful when sleeping upon it, or sitting upon it, or the like. Allah the Exalted has described the earth with many attributes: He described it as a bed, as subservient (dhalul), and other things that occur in the Qur'an. The bed, as we know, is something smoothed and prepared for a person, on which he rests.

"And the sky a canopy": as the Exalted said: "And We built above you seven strong [heavens]" [al-Naba': 12]. Allah made the sky a canopy, that is, in the position of a building and in the position of a roof: "And We made the sky a protected ceiling" [al-Anbiya': 32].

"And sent down from the sky water": "sent down from the sky" is not the first sky; rather the word "sky" in the second instance means height (al-'uluww), because the water which is rain descends from the clouds. Allah the Exalted said: "Have you not seen that Allah drives the clouds, then joins them, then makes them into a heap, and you see the rain emerging from within them?" [al-Nur: 43]. So the water which is rain does not descend from the sky which is the building, but descends from the clouds which are on high. By this we know that the word "sky" is applied to two meanings: the first meaning: the building above us; the second meaning: height.

"And sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you." "Brought forth thereby" means: by means of it. Look at the wisdom and the wonderful subtlety: He attributed the matter to Himself, the Majestic and Exalted, yet through a means. The means only conveys; otherwise, does rain bring forth vegetation? No, the one who brings forth is Allah, but the means is rain. "Thereby" means: by means of it. "Fruits as provision for you." The plural "fruits" is used because they are varied; if a person wanted to count their types he would be unable, let alone their individual instances.

"Fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know [better]." "Do not set up rivals to Allah" in worship. "While you know" that He has no equal in creation, provision, sending down rain, and similar acts of lordship; for the polytheists acknowledge that the Creator is Allah, the Provider is Allah, and the Manager of the affair is Allah. They acknowledge this with complete acknowledgment, and they know that there is no god along with Allah in this. But in worship they deny this; they associate partners, they make another god along with Allah, and they deny those who affirm the oneness of Allah. They even said about the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing" [Sad: 5]. We say: "Mashallah," who brought the strange thing? They did. As for the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, he brought the correct matter, but they brought the strange thing. We ask Allah for well-being. So "do not set up rivals to Allah" in what?

Students: In worship.

The Shaykh: "While you know" that He has no equal in lordship, in creation, provision, and other matters, and your acknowledgment that creation and provision belong to Allah alone necessitates that you make worship belong to Allah alone. If you do not do so, you are contradictory. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: tawhid al-uluhiyyah includes tawhid al-rububiyyah, and tawhid al-rububiyyah necessitates tawhid al-uluhiyyah. That is, whoever acknowledges the lordship is obliged to acknowledge the divinity, and whoever acknowledges the divinity has not acknowledged it until he has acknowledged the lordship. So tawhid al-uluhiyyah includes tawhid al-rububiyyah, and tawhid al-rububiyyah entails tawhid al-uluhiyyah.

From the benefits of this verse: first, the concern with worship. This is derived from two aspects. The first aspect: the opening of the command with the vocative. The second aspect: the generalization of the address to all people, which indicates that worship is the most important matter, and indeed it is so. Rather, people were not created except for worship: "And I did not create jinn and humankind except to worship Me" [al-Dhariyat: 56].

From the benefits of this noble verse: that the obligation of worship upon us is required by reason in addition to the Sharia, because of His saying "worship your Lord." The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, deserves to be worshipped and that no other be worshipped. What is strange is that these polytheists, who did not comply with this command, when harm befalls them and their means are cut off, turn to whom? To Allah: "When a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion" [Luqman: 32], because their natural disposition (fitrah) compels them to that and inevitably so.

From the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the sole Creator, and that He is the Creator of the first and the last; by His saying "who created you and those before you." Yes.

From the benefits of this noble verse: that it is the way of the Qur'an that when it mentions a ruling, it generally mentions the cause. The ruling: "worship," and the cause: that He is a Lord and Creator of us and of those before us.

From the benefits of the noble verse: that taqwa is a high rank which not everyone attains except one who sincerely devotes worship to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; by His saying "that you may become righteous."

Can we derive from this verse a warning against innovations (bid'ah)? Perhaps we can derive from it a warning against innovations, because the worship of Allah is not realized except by following the path that He legislated for worship, since we cannot know how to worship Allah, how to perform ablution, except through revelation and the Sharia; how to pray. That is, what informed us that when a person stands, recites, then bows, then prostrates, this is the worship required of us, except after what? After revelation. Based on this, it may be said that the command to worship entails the command to follow.

And can it be derived from the verse an exhortation to seek knowledge?

Students: Yes.

The Shaykh: Yes. How so? Because worship cannot be realized except with knowledge. For this reason al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, titled his chapter on this matter with his saying: "Chapter: Knowledge before speech and action" [Sahih al-Bukhari (1/24)].

Then the Exalted said, reminding His servants: "He who made for you the earth a bed." From this noble verse is derived: the explanation of the mercy of Allah the Exalted and His wisdom in making the earth a bed; for if He had made it rough and hard, a person could not settle on it, and no one's mind would be at rest. But out of His mercy, kindness and benevolence, He made it a bed.

From the benefits of the noble verse: making the sky a canopy. But what is our benefit from making the sky a canopy? Our benefit from making the sky a canopy is that we know thereby the power of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; for this sky encompassing the entire earth from all sides, we know that it is very large and vast, as the Exalted said: "And the sky We built with might, and indeed, We are expanding it" [al-Dhariyat: 47].

From the benefits of the noble verse: the demonstration of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in sending down rain from the sky; by His saying "and sent down from the sky water." Had all creation gathered to create a single drop of water, they would not be able to do so, while Allah sends down this great rain in an instant, does He not? Yes. And the story of the man who entered while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the Friday sermon: he said: "Pray to Allah that He give us rain." So he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, give us rain." Before he had descended from the pulpit, the rain was pouring from his beard [agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (1014) and Muslim (897/8)].

From the benefits of the noble verse: the wisdom and mercy of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, in sending down rain from the sky. Its reasoning: if the water by which the earth lives flowed upon the earth, it would harm people; and if it flowed upon the earth, many lands would be deprived of it. Which lands would be deprived? The elevated ones; nothing reaches them. But from the blessing of Allah, it descends from the sky. Then there is another thing too: it descends as a fine drizzle, drop by drop; if it descended like the mouths of waterskins, it would harm people. But out of the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it descends in the manner you are accustomed to.

From the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of means; by His saying "and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you."

And from its benefits: that means are not means except by the will of Allah; by His saying "and brought forth thereby."

And from its benefits, a benefit of conduct (masluki): a person should attribute a matter to Allah while mentioning the means. For example, if someone drowned and a man came and brought him out, rescuing him from drowning, then he should say: "Allah rescued me through so-and-so." He may also say: "So-and-so rescued me," and he may say that, because he actually rescued him. And he may say: "Allah rescued me, then so-and-so." How many forms is this?

Students: Three.

The Shaykh: And he is not to say: "Allah and so-and-so rescued me," because that is associating a partner with Allah. What confirms this, that is, the preferred option, is that one attribute the matter to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while mentioning the means: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he invited the Jewish boy to Islam, and this boy was in the throes of death, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, offered him to embrace Islam, and he embraced it, but he embraced it after consulting his father. He turned to look at him, seeking his counsel, and he said: "Obey Abu al-Qasim." The ignorant one, he gave permission to his child; rather he ordered his child to become Muslim while he himself had not become Muslim in that state. We do not know what came after, Allah knows best. But in any case the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, left saying: "Praise be to Allah who rescued him through me from the Fire" [related by al-Bukhari (1356)]. See the expression!! "rescued him through me from the Fire." Thus it is fitting for us too: when something happens by means of something, we should attribute it to Allah, the Exalted, what? Accompanied by mention of the means. Good.

*Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 21–25 (part 2 of 5):*

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His favour in bringing these fruits forth from water. As for power, it is evident. You see the earth barren and dry, with no green leaf in it. Then rain falls, and within a short time this vegetation emerges in every beautiful pair, by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So there is power in it, and there is favour in it. For this reason He said: ﴿as a provision for you﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse, yes, is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, bestows blessings upon the human being, whether he is a disbeliever or a Muslim. From where do we know this?
* Student: From His saying (...)
* Shaykh: ﴿for you﴾. He addresses people in general at the outset. So Allah, the Exalted, has favour upon people, both their disbelievers and their believers. Each has favour. But Allah's favour upon the believer, may Allah make me and you among them, is lasting and connected to the favour of the Hereafter, whereas Allah's favour upon the disbeliever ends with his departure from this world.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the prohibition of setting up rivals (andad) to Allah, based on His saying: ﴿So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know﴾. Are rivals (andad) major shirk or minor shirk? Are they manifest shirk or hidden shirk? This has detail in the science of Tawhid ('Aqidah). If one sets up a rival to Allah in worship, by worshipping other than Allah in the same way as worshipping Allah, then this is, what? Major shirk. If he sets up a rival to Him in lordship (rububiyyah) and says, for example, "This creation was created by two," then this is major shirk. If it is less than that, it is minor shirk. Among minor shirk is attributing a thing to its cause and mentioning Allah alongside it with the particle "and" (wa). This is minor shirk, so long as he does not believe that this cause has an action like the action of Allah, in which case it becomes major shirk.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse is that whoever addresses someone should explain to him what establishes the proof against him. This is from His saying: ﴿So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know﴾, and from His saying at the beginning of the verse: ﴿Worship your Lord, who created you and those before you﴾. His saying ﴿who created you and those before you﴾ contains the establishment of the proof for the obligation of worshipping Him alone, because He is the sole Creator.
The grammatical analysis (i'rab, the grammatical parsing of words) of His saying ﴿while you know﴾: the clause is a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah) in a position of accusative case (nasb).
* Student: Honourable Shaykh, what is the wisdom behind the large number of verses that indicate Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (oneness of Lordship), given that the addressees in this Qur'an acknowledge Tawhid al-Rububiyyah?
* Shaykh: Yes, to establish the proof.
* Student: They affirm it.
* Shaykh: Yes, but if they affirm it, it becomes binding on them to make Him one in worship (Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah).
* Student: But some of the callers (du'at) who call to Allah give much emphasis to (...) and calling to Tawhid al-Rububiyyah, even though people have a deficiency in Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, and they cite many verses in the Qur'an for this.
* Shaykh: Yes, this is as I said. If one is addressing people who deny the Divinity, meaning they deny Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, then let him mention many verses about Lordship. But if he is speaking to people who affirm Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, then he should bring them other verses, verses about the Attributes and verses about the actions of Allah.
* Student: They are Muslims.
* Shaykh: That does not contradict it. If they are Muslims, then they may be reminded of Lordship so that their faith may increase.
* Student: (...) worship is humbling oneself which entails love and veneration. This belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If someone directs love alone, or veneration alone, to other than Allah, is he a major polytheist (mushrik shirk akbar)?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. If he loves someone the way he loves Allah, or more, then he is a major polytheist.
* Student: Or venerates someone?
* Shaykh: Or venerates someone like the veneration of Allah or more. Even if he venerates the Ka'bah like the veneration of Allah, or venerates the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, like the veneration of Allah, he is a major polytheist.
* Student: Shaykh, what should we say to those who are at the graves (...) the saints (awliya'). They love them and venerate them, but we do not know whether they love them as they love Allah or not?
* Shaykh: We say it this way. We say it in detail, and then we say to him: "Do you love this one more than the love of Allah?"
* Student: He loves him and venerates him, but, I mean..?
* Shaykh: There are people today who love the Messenger more than they love Allah. I remember that some pilgrims, while we were in Jeddah in the mosque, came at the time when travel to Madinah was prohibited, because I think after the fourth of Dhu al-Hijjah they prohibit them from traveling to Madinah out of concern that they would be delayed. So he began to weep intensely. Why? He said: "The light of my eye." Whose light of the eye? Meaning the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. "I only came for this." Now you see, he is coming to perform Hajj, and he says: "I am the light of my eye, and I came only for him." In my view, this is perhaps the love of the Messenger in his heart being greater than the love of Allah. So such people must be made to understand. It should be said: "Were it not for the love of Allah, we would not have loved the Messenger. And were it not that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, we would not have loved him with this love, nor would we have put his love above ourselves, our families, and our children. From where did it become obligatory for us to venerate the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him? Because he is the Messenger of our Lord, not because he is Muhammad bin 'Abdullah. Is this known?" So these common people must be explained to. It is said: "Do not make anyone a partner with Allah at all." ﴿And among the people are those who take rivals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah 165].
* Student: Shaykh, what if a person develops love and veneration (...).
* Shaykh: No, no. A person loves his parents and venerates his parents. He loves his teacher and venerates his teacher. He loves the one older than him and venerates him. The main thing is that there must be no excess (ghuluw).
* * *
* Student: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it, and call your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful (23). But if you do not and you will never do, then fear the Fire, whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers (24). And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom as provision, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before," and it will be given to them in likeness, and they will have therein purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 23–25].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ and so on to the end. The address is to those who set up rivals to Allah, because He said: ﴿So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know (22). And if you are in doubt﴾. The mention of this verse concerning the message of Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, contains an allusion to the two testimonies of Tawhid, which are: the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
The first testimony, "there is no god but Allah," is Tawhid al-Qasd (oneness of intention), and the second is Tawhid al-Mutaba'ah (oneness of following). Both are Tawhid, but the first is Tawhid al-Qasd, that the act is sincerely for Allah, and the second is Tawhid al-Mutaba'ah, that the act follows the Messenger of Allah. If you reflect on the Qur'an, you will find it this way: it mentions what indicates Tawhid, then what indicates the Message.
Another example: ﴿Then have they not reflected upon the word, or has there come to them that which did not come to their forefathers of old?﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 68]
Then He said: ﴿Or did they not recognize their Messenger, so they deny him?﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 69]. This is consistent throughout the Noble Qur'an.
He says ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾. Many people interpret ar-raib (doubt, ريب) as shakk (doubt). There is no doubt that it is close in meaning to shakk, but it differs from it in that ar-raib implies anxiety, and that the person is in great unease about what doubt has fallen upon. This is because what the Messenger brought is true, and one who doubts it must inevitably feel anxiety, since he doubts a matter that must be affirmed. This differs from doubt about trivial matters, which is not called raib. Raib is used only for great matters, in which, when a person doubts, he finds within himself anxiety and turmoil.
His saying ﴿what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ refers to the Qur'an, because Allah sent it down upon Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family. His saying ﴿Our servant﴾ refers to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, described His Messenger with servitude ('ubudiyyah) in the most elevated stations: in defending him, in showing his honour through the Mi'raj (ascension) and the Isra' (night journey), and in showing his honour through the sending down of the Qur'an: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾ [Al-Furqan 1], ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ [Al-Isra' 1], ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ [Al-Baqarah 23]. This is in the context of challenge and defence. The best of the Messenger's attributes, peace and blessings be upon him, are servitude and messengership. For this reason he said: "Indeed I am only a slave, so say: the slave of Allah and His Messenger" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (3445), with the wording: "For indeed I am His slave, so say: the slave of Allah and His Messenger."]
Servitude ('ubudiyyah) is humbling oneself before one who is loved and venerated, and the worshipper takes pleasure in it. For this reason the poet said, describing his beloved:
"Do not call me except 'O slave of her,'
for indeed it is the most noble of my names."
That is, do not say "So-and-so, so-and-so." Say: "O slave of So-and-so," because this is the most noble of his names to him, since he belongs to her. We seek refuge with Allah from abandonment. So the most noble attributes of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, are two: servitude and messengership. ﴿upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it﴾. (ائتوا) (ta'tu): is a command intended as a challenge. That is: if you are in doubt about this Qur'an, We challenge you to produce a single surah like it. The phrase "like it" (min mithlihi) may mean "like Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him," that is, from among humans, and it may mean "like it," that is, like what We sent down upon Our servant, that is, of its kind. Both are correct, since no human can ever produce anything like what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, brought. Indeed, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants﴾ [Al-Isra' 88].
﴿then produce a surah like it, and call your witnesses other than Allah﴾. ﴿call your witnesses﴾ refers to those whom you testify to be divine and worship as you worship Allah. Call them to help you. This is the utmost in challenge: to challenge the worshipper, and what? And the worshipped, challenging both the worshippers and the worshipped to produce a surah like it.
﴿and call your witnesses other than Allah﴾, meaning: besides Allah, ﴿if you are truthful﴾. The answer to this is that it is impossible. No matter how many helpers and supporters they bring, they will never produce a surah like it.
﴿But if you do not﴾, meaning: if you do not produce a surah like it, ﴿and you will never do﴾, [this is] when He said ﴿But if you do not﴾, and the conditional particle is followed by cutting off their hopes with His saying ﴿and you will never do﴾, meaning: do not even try to do it, because this is impossible. ﴿then fear the Fire, whose fuel is people﴾. The fa' (فَ) here is in the response of the condition, which is ﴿But if you do not﴾. That is: if you do not do it, and you oppose the Qur'an with its like, then the Fire is your abode. Fear the Fire. They will find nothing to protect them from the Fire except to believe in what was sent down upon Muhammad, ﷺ.
﴿whose fuel is people and stones﴾. (التي) (allati) is a relative pronoun describing "the Fire." (وقود) (wuqud) is the subject (mubtada'), and (الناس) (an-nas) is its predicate (khabar). ﴿its fuel﴾: al-wuqud is that which something is kindled with, like firewood, for example, in the fire of this world. In the Hereafter, the fuel of the Fire is people and stones. The Fire burns them and blazes with them. We ask Allah for well-being.
﴿the stones﴾. Some scholars said: what is meant by them is the worshipped stones, that is, idols, because they worship idols. Their idols will be with them in the Fire, as He said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will come to it﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 98]. It was also said: the stones are fiery stones, and we seek refuge with Allah, by which the heat of the Fire increases, and they do not cool. We ask Allah for well-being. But there is no objection to the meaning being both: the worshipped stones and the kindled stones that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created to be kindled with the Fire.
﴿prepared for the disbelievers﴾. (أعدت) (u'iddat): the hidden pronoun refers to the Fire, and the one who prepared it is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The meaning of "i'dad" is making something ready. His saying ﴿for the disbelievers﴾ means: for every disbeliever, whether he disbelieved in the Message or disbelieved in the Divinity or in anything else.
* There are several benefits in these verses. First, the clarification of Allah, the Exalted, defending His Messenger, ﷺ, based on His saying?
* Student: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah﴾.
* Shaykh: Recite all the verses and then say: "It is derived from these verses." Specify.
* Student: ﴿Our servant﴾.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾, meaning that Our servant is not one about whom doubt can be raised.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: From what We have sent down upon Our servant.
* Shaykh: ﴿then produce a surah like it﴾. This is the aspect of defence, because the command here is a challenge. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, challenges these people to bring forth something opposing what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, brought.
Among them: the excellence of the Prophet, ﷺ, by describing him with servitude. Servitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the ultimate freedom, because whoever does not worship Allah must worship something else. If he does not worship Allah, the One deserving of worship, he worships Satan and his desires, as Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Nuniyyah:
"They fled from the bondage for which they were created,
and were afflicted with the bondage of the self and Satan."
* Among the benefits of this verse: the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. This is based on His saying ﴿what We have sent down﴾. The reason it is the speech of Allah is that the Qur'an is speech, and speech is not bodies that are created and separate from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Rather, it is an attribute of the speaker. From this we know that whoever claims the Qur'an is created, and says that Allah said ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 3], and ﴿We have sent down to you the Reminder﴾ [An-Nahl 44], and similar verses, then his statement is rejected. He has no proof in verses such as His saying ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾ [Al-Hadid 25], and His saying ﴿He sent down for you eight kinds of livestock﴾ [Az-Zumar 6], and His saying ﴿He made the darknesses and the light﴾ [Al-An'am 1]. All of this is not proof for them, because there is a difference between the entities that subsist by themselves, which Allah attributes to Himself, and the attributes which do not subsist by themselves.
* Among the benefits of the verse: the loftiness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is because once it is established that the Qur'an is His speech and that it was sent down from Him, it necessarily follows that the speaker is elevated. The loftiness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is a matter of natural (fitri) and rational ('aqli) knowledge. We have previously mentioned five types of evidence for it, which are: the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus (ijma'), reason, and the innate nature (fitrah).
If someone says: "You mentioned that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was honoured by the attribution of his servitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, although the disbelievers and the wicked of creation are also servants of Allah, as He said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]?"
The answer to this is that servitude has several meanings: general servitude, which is the universal, predestined servitude (al-'ubudiyyah al-kawniyyah al-qadariyyah). This encompasses everyone, and no one can avoid submitting to this servitude. So the disbeliever and the wicked person is a servant of Allah, meaning that Allah does with him whatever He wills. And there is specific servitude, which is the servitude of obedience, specific to those who believe in Allah and follow His law. This specific servitude can also be divided into a general specific and a more specific specific. So the servitude of the Messengers is different from the servitude of the truthful ones (siddiqin), the martyrs, and the righteous. The former is more perfect and more specific.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Qur'an is inimitable even by a single short sura, as shown by His words ﴿a sura like it﴾. Allah, mighty and majestic, challenged them to produce a sura like it, and to produce ten suras like it, and He informed them that no one would ever produce the like of this Qur'an even if mankind and the jinn gathered together. At the least, we know that they cannot produce a single statement like it, meaning even one sentence. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, they do not believe. So let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾ [al-Tur 33–34]. The word "hadith" applies to a sentence, however short. Accordingly, the challenge takes four forms: with the whole Qur'an, with ten of its suras, with a single sura, and with a single statement.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the challenge is addressed to these worshippers together with the objects they worship. This is more humiliating than being challenged alone. It is as if He is saying: "You and your gods, produce a sura like it." This is the utmost in disgrace, humiliation, shame and ignominy.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: no one can oppose the speech of Allah, as shown by His words ﴿and you will never do it﴾. In this statement there are two arguments. The first is the argument of those who hold the doctrine of *al-sarfah* (the doctrine that Allah diverted people from producing its like), meaning that man by his nature is able to produce the like of the Qur'an, but he was diverted from it. On this view, the challenge is possible, but an obstacle was present, namely that Allah diverted them from opposing it, so that they did not want to.

The second argument is that they will never do it by the nature of their creation, not that they were diverted while they are able to oppose the Qur'an. This second view is the one that is definitive, because the first view or the first possibility does not show that the Qur'an is inimitable in itself, since they could produce its like but Allah diverted them, and they did not pay attention to it or think about it. But we say: this is wrong. The correct view is that man by himself cannot produce the like of the Qur'an, because the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and speech is an attribute of the speaker. Just as man cannot resemble Allah in His attributes, he cannot resemble Allah in what? In His speech. It is absolutely impossible. This is why those who claimed prophethood and produced what they called a Qur'an became a mockery to the servants and a laughingstock, as is related of Musaylimah the Liar and others. Therefore the correct view is that His words ﴿you will never do it﴾ do not mean "you will be diverted from it and will not do it." Rather, the meaning is that you are incapable by the nature of man.
