Whatever gardens, trees and fruits exist in this world, what Allah has promised the righteous cannot be like them, according to His words: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾. And according to His words in the sacred hadith: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[[Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari (3244) and Muslim (2824/2).]]

﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾. ﴿The rivers﴾ is the subject of (flow), and ﴿beneath it﴾ — the scholars said: beneath its trees and palaces, not from below its surface. No, for if they were below its surface there would be no benefit in them. Rather they flow beneath these trees and palaces. How beautiful is the flowing of these rivers when they are beneath the trees and palaces. A person finds delight in them before he partakes of them. Allah, exalted, has explained that these rivers are of four kinds, as He said: ﴿The description of Paradise which the righteous are promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 15]. Allah, mighty and majestic, creates them without bees, without cows, and without camels. Likewise the wine. And the water is not from rain or springs; rather Allah created it from the beginning. I ask Allah not to deprive me and you of them, for He is powerful over all things.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 21–25 (part 4 of 5):**

﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا﴾: Rivers flow beneath them. Whenever they are provided with some fruit from them as sustenance.
﴿رُزِقُوا﴾ means "were given." ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ means "from these fruits." ﴿مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا﴾ means "a gift."
﴿قَالُوا هَذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾: They will say, "This is what we were given before," because it resembles what came before. It resembles it in size, in color, and in texture. These are all sensory qualities that a person assumes to be similar to what came before in its color, what? and its size and texture. But in taste, no. It differs enormously. For this reason He said: ﴿أُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾: they will be brought it resembling one another. How beautiful and how delightful it is for a person who sees this fruit and considers it to be one thing. Then when he tastes it, the taste differs enormously. You will find that he experiences a stirring in himself, a delight, and wonder: how can something so greatly different have the same appearance? ﴿وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾. Now, if fruits were presented to you whose colors were the same, whose sizes were the same, and whose textures were the same, and then when you tasted them, one was pure sweet, and another was bitter, meaning sweet mixed with sourness, and another was sour, you would find more delight than if they were all equal or all different.
﴿وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾: Is "أُتُوا" from (آتى) or from (أتى)? The second or the first?
* The students: The first, the first.
* The Shaykh: From (آتى) or from (أتى)?
* The students: From (آتى), the first.
* The Shaykh: No, the second. ﴿أُتُوا بِهِ﴾, because if it were from the first, he would say: "أُوتوا به." But ﴿أُتُوا بِهِ﴾ means it was brought to them, resembling one another. Resembling one another in what? We said: in three things. This is what comes to mind now, and Allah knows best what it will be: in color, size, and texture. But not in taste, because if it agreed in taste too, this would be that and that would be this, with no difference. ﴿وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾.
﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾: Glory be to Allah! Whenever Allah mentions fruit, He mentions spouses. Reflect on this in all the verses. Why? Because they, and their spouses, will enjoy these gifts and this provision. ﴿إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ الْيَوْمَ فِي شُغُلٍ فَاكِهُونَ (٥٥) هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ فِي ظِلَالٍ عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾ [Ya-Sin 55–56]. You find that Allah joins this with that, because all of it is enjoyment (tafakkuh). But this enjoyment is of one kind, and that is of another kind. This is enjoyment in taste and food, and that is another enjoyment of a second kind, because with it the blessing is complete.
﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ﴾: "أَزْوَاجٌ" is plural. Does the meaning mean that each one has spouses? Or that each individual has a wife, but since they are a group, the plural is matched with the plural?
* The students: The first.
* The Shaykh: The first. Because a person in the Hereafter has multiple spouses. "Azwaj" is the plural of "zawj," and "zawj" is applied to both the male and the female. For this reason, "zawj" is said of a woman and of a man. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزْوَاجُكُمْ﴾ [An-Nisa 12]: "And for you is half of what your wives leave." But in the terminology of the faraid scholars (scholars of inheritance), they began to add the feminine ending (ta') for the female, to distinguish her from the male when dividing the inheritance. ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾. Now, if a woman died while young and had never married, will she have a husband in the Hereafter?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes, she will have a husband in the Hereafter, either from the people of this world or from those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will create. This is because there will remain in Paradise a surplus beyond those who have entered it from the people of this world. Allah will create for her men, and He will admit them into Paradise by His bounty and mercy.
His saying: ﴿مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾ includes purity of the outward and the inward. She is purified from filth and impurity: there is no urine, no feces, no menstruation (hayd), no postnatal bleeding (nifas), no irregular bleeding (istihadah), no sweat, and no bad breath. She is purified from every outward sensory impurity. She is also purified from inward defilements such as rancor, spite, hatred, enmity, and other things. She is purified from everything, from every outward or inward filth and harm. This is unlike the spouses of this world. But the spouses of this world are perfectly suited to their male spouses, because if she is not purified of this, then her husband? Her husband is like her. But in the Hereafter, all are purified.
﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾: This is the completion of blessing, that they will abide forever in these Gardens. They will not desire any change from them, nor will they be removed from them. As it came in the hadith: "Indeed, for you is that you will be healthy and never fall ill, and that you will be youthful and never grow old, and that you will live and never die." [Recorded by Muslim (2837/22) with the wording: "Indeed for you is that you will be healthy and never fall sick, and that you will live and never die, and that you will be youthful and never grow old, and that you will be blessed and never be miserable."] Through this their bliss is completed. But the highest bliss that the people of Paradise will have is looking upon the Face of Allah, Glory be to Allah and Exalted. This is the highest bliss, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنَى وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾ [Yunus 26]: "For those who did good is the best reward and an increase." The Prophet (ﷺ) explained "an increase" as looking upon the Face of Allah. [Recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (18935, 18941), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11170).]
* In this verse there are benefits, among them: the legitimacy of giving a person good news of what pleases him, based on His saying: ﴿بَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾, and Allah's saying: ﴿وَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِإِسْحَاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ [As-Saffat 112]: "And We gave him good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous." ﴿بَشَّرْنَاهُ بِغُلَامٍ حَلِيمٍ﴾ [As-Saffat 101]: "We gave him good news of a forbearing boy." So giving good news of what pleases a person is one of the practices of the messengers, peace be upon them.
(Now) but if what pleases a person is an act of disobedience to Allah, would you give him good news? For example, a person who has committed theft: you come and tell him, "Mashallah, may Allah congratulate you on what you stole!" Never. Rather, good news is only for what pleases and has no bad consequence. Is it among this to give someone good news of the seasons of worship, such as if he reached Ramadan and you said, "May Allah congratulate you on this month"? The answer is yes. Likewise, if he completed the fast and you said, "May Allah congratulate you on this festival, and accept your worship," and the like, there is no harm in that, and this was the custom of the early generations (al-salaf).
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Gardens are only for those who combine these two qualities: faith (iman) and righteous deeds.
If someone says: "The Quran contains what indicates that the qualities are four: faith, righteous deeds, mutual enjoining of truth, and mutual enjoining of patience."
We say: Mutual enjoining of truth and mutual enjoining of patience are among righteous deeds. But sometimes some individual instances of a general category are mentioned for a reason and a cause.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever does a bad deed will not be given good news of these Gardens, based on His saying: ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾. But whoever does a bad deed: if he was striving and erred, he has a reward and is safe from sin. If he was not striving and did not exert his effort, he is sinful, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "When a judge rules and strives and is correct, he has two rewards, and when he rules and strives and errs, he has one reward." [Agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari (7352) and Muslim (1716/15) with the wording: "When a judge rules and strives and then is correct, he has two rewards, and when he rules and strives and then errs, he has one reward."]
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the reward of the believers who did righteous deeds is far greater than what they did, and more magnificent. Because however much they believe and act, their lifespan is limited and ends. But the reward, what? The reward never ends. They abide in it forever, endless ages upon ages. Likewise, the deeds they offer may be mixed with laziness, mixed with fatigue, mixed with things that diminish them. But if Allah bestows His favor on them and they enter Paradise, the bliss is complete.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the Gardens are of various kinds, based on His saying: ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾. It may be said that this is not conclusive evidence, because "Jannat" is a plural matched with a plural, namely His saying: ﴿لَهُمْ﴾, ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾. But the Sunnah, indeed the Quran, shows that the Gardens are of various kinds. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتَانِ﴾ [Ar-Rahman 46]: "And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two Gardens." Then He said: ﴿وَمِنْ دُونِهِمَا جَنَّتَانِ﴾ [Ar-Rahman 62]: "And beneath them are two more Gardens." So they are of various kinds. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Two Gardens of gold, their vessels and all that is in them; and two Gardens of silver, their vessels and all that is in them." [Agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari (4878) and Muslim (296/180) with the wording: "Two Gardens of silver, their vessels and all that is in them, and two Gardens of gold, their vessels and all that is in them."]
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the completeness of Allah's power, the Mighty and Majestic, in creating these rivers without any known cause in this world. For water in our world has known causes, and the sources of water rivers are known. Likewise, milk: it is known from where it is produced. Honey is known. And the fourth? Wine is known. But in Paradise, no. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings it into being: rivers flowing. It has been reported in a narration: "They flow without a trench" [Recorded by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (34954) from Masruq, who said: "The rivers of Paradise flow without a trench."]; meaning no pits have been dug for them, and no banks have been set up to contain them. Rather, the river flows, and a person may direct it as he wishes, turning it wherever he likes. Glory be to Allah! Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Its rivers flowed without a trench,
Glory be to the One who holds them back from overflowing.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: among the bliss of the people of Paradise is that they are brought provision resembling one another, and ﴿كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا قَالُوا هَذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾. This is part of the completeness of bliss and of enjoying what they eat.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of marriage in the Hereafter, and that it is part of the completeness of bliss. Based on this, does intercourse take place or not? It does take place. But if intercourse takes place, does the harm that occurs with the intercourse of the women of this world occur? The answer is no. For this reason there is no semen (mani) nor sperm (manyah) in Paradise. The semen which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created was created only for the continuation of offspring, because this semen contains the material from which the fetus is formed, and it emerges, by Allah's permission, as a child. But in the Hereafter, in Paradise, no. They have no need of that, because there is no need for the continuation of offspring, since those who exist will remain forever, endless ages upon ages, and none of them will perish. Furthermore, they have no need for anyone to assist them or serve them. The youths (wildan) will circulate among them with cups, jugs, and a glass from a flowing spring. Also, they will not need anyone to climb the tree to pick its fruit. Rather, as Allah the Exalted said about them: ﴿وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍ﴾ [Ar-Rahman 54]: "And the fruit of the two Gardens is near at hand." Scholars even mentioned that a man looks at the fruit on the tree and feels he desires it, so the branch draws near to him until he takes it. Allah is greater! Do not be surprised by this. We in this world witness something similar: that a thing draws near to another without any apparent cause or visible connection. But in the Hereafter it is even more profound, and more profound still.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the people of Paradise abide in it forever, endless ages upon ages, and it is impossible for it to perish, and impossible for those in it to perish. Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) unanimously agreed upon this. Those who denied it were the philosophers (ahl al-falsafah), who said: "It is impossible for Allah to continue acting in eternity past and eternity future" (may Allah protect us). Thus they made Allah inactive at the beginning and inactive at the end. Some of them even said (may Allah protect us): "Paradise will perish along with those in it, while a person is raising his morsel to his mouth. Then annihilation occurs, and he remains with his morsel raised, eating, the morsel remaining while his hand is perishing." As Ibn al-Qayyim said in the Nuniyyah: "Indeed al-Allaf came with a ridiculous laugh." Likewise, a person with his family and wife, copulating with her, then the time of annihilation comes, and he remains with her, perishing, endless ages upon ages. We ask Allah for well-being.
In any case, the people of Paradise abide in it forever, endless ages upon ages, by the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah. And the Fire is likewise, according to the established view. What is the preponderant view? That it does not perish. The Fire, according to the established view, does not perish, and it remains endless ages upon ages by the explicit words of the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic. We have explained that Allah stated this explicitly in three verses of the Book of Allah, and we have repeated this often. We did not think that anyone among the people who belong to Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah would say that it perishes. Our Shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'di, may Allah have mercy on him, was surprised that Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah pardon him, tried to prefer the view of its annihilation in his book Shifa' al-'Alil. Our Shaykh said: "This is considered a stumble from this steed and a great error." He wrote this in the margin of the book. There is no doubt that what our Shaykh said is true, and a person is astonished that such a stallion among scholars would go to strengthen this school, although he did not explicitly declare that he chose it. But he went to strengthen it, although it is false by the explicit text of the Quran.
The people of Paradise abide in it forever, by the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah, endless ages upon ages, and the Fire is likewise according to the established view. What is the preponderant view that it perishes? The Fire, according to the established view, does not perish, and it remains endless ages upon ages by the explicit words of the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic. We have explained that Allah stated this explicitly in three verses of the Book of Allah, and we have repeated this much. We did not think that anyone among the people of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah would say it perishes. Our Shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'di, may Allah have mercy on him, was surprised that Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah pardon him, tried to prefer the view of its annihilation in his book Shifa' al-'Alil. Our Shaykh said: "This is considered a stumble from this steed and a great error." He wrote this in the margin of the book. There is no doubt that what our Shaykh said is true, and a person is astonished that such a stallion among scholars would go to strengthen this school, although he did not explicitly declare that he chose it. But he went to strengthen it, although it is false by the explicit text of the Quran: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَظَلَمُوا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ طَرِيقًا (١٦٨) إِلَّا طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا﴾ [An-Nisa 168–169]: "Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged, Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah." And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَنَ الْكَافِرِينَ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ سَعِيرًا (٦٤) خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا لَا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾ [Al-Ahzab 64–65]: "Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever; they will find no protector or helper." And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا﴾ [Al-Jinn 23]: "And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever." How is it correct for us, or how is it right for us, to say that the Fire perishes, while Allah the Exalted says: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا﴾? What is the benefit of His saying: ﴿أَبَدًا﴾? In any case, the school of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah, which is nearly a consensus, is that the Fire does not perish, just as Paradise does not perish, by clear agreement.
From the noble verse it is derived that if a person spent his entire life in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, bowing, prostrating, and standing, that would be little compared to this great reward he receives on a day in which whoever among the servants of Allah is wretched will be wretched, and will be in the blazing Fire, may Allah protect us. We ask Allah the Exalted to help us and you to remember Him, thank Him, and worship Him well. May Allah reward you with good.
* Student: May Allah be gracious to you, O Shaykh. If the opponent said: the intended meaning of His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ بَعْدَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ [An-Nisa 165]: "So that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers," is that this applies to the legal rulings (shara'i'), and otherwise the proof stands regarding monotheism (tawhid) and the foundations of religion through the covenant (al-mithaq) and the fitrah (natural disposition), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ (١٧٢) أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ [Al-A'raf 172–173]: "And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we testify.' Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, 'Indeed, we were unaware of this,' or say, 'Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them.'" So here He affirmed that it is the covenant...?

The Shaykh: The covenant that was taken from them is that they should believe in what the messengers brought. There must be messengers, and the verse is general. ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that people would have no argument against God after the messengers.﴾ [An-Nisa 165] is general. ﴿We would never punish until We send a messenger.﴾ [Al-Isra 15] ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the towns until He sends in their mother-town a messenger reciting to them Our verses.﴾ [Al-Qasas 59] ﴿We would never destroy the towns unless their people were wrongdoers.﴾ [Al-Qasas 59] ﴿God would never lead a people astray after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should beware of.﴾ [At-Tawbah 115] The verses on this are many.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example of a mosquito or what is above it. As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?" He misleads thereby many and guides thereby many, and He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient.﴾ [Al-Baqarah 26].

* The Shaykh: No, stop at ﴿مَثَلًا﴾ (mathalan).

* The student: ﴿And as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?" He misleads thereby many and guides thereby many, and He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient. [26] Those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation, and sever what Allah has ordered to be joined, and cause corruption on the earth - it is those who are the losers. [27] How can you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then give you life; then to Him you will be returned.﴾ [Al-Baqarah 26-28].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example of a mosquito or what is above it﴾, ﴿is not ashamed to present an example﴾. Even if the example is a humble one, so long as the truth is established by it, what matters is the purpose. As for His saying ﴿an example of what﴾, the word (ma) here, they say, is an indefinite descriptive noun, meaning: an example, whatever example. As for His saying ﴿a mosquito﴾, it is an explanatory apposition (ʿatf bayan) to (ma), meaning: an example, a mosquito or what is above it. As for ﴿a mosquito﴾, the mosquito is well known, and it is used as a proverb for insignificance.

They have mentioned that the occasion of revelation of this verse[[See Tafsir al-Tabari (1/400), al-Durr al-Manthur (1/225).]] was that the polytheists objected: how does Allah cite as an example the fly, in His saying, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿O mankind, an example has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Hajj 73]. They said: a fly, which Allah mentions in a context of argument?! So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made clear that He is not ashamed of the truth, even if He cites as an example a mosquito or what is above it.

As for His saying ﴿an example, a mosquito or what is above it﴾: does ﴿what is above it﴾ mean what is above it in lowliness, so the meaning is something smaller than a mosquito, or what is above it in height, so the meaning is what is higher than a mosquito? Which of the two examples is greater in creation, the fly or the mosquito? The fly is undoubtedly larger and stronger. Nevertheless, the meaning of the verse may be "what is above it," i.e., what is below it, since "above" (fawq) can apply to both the lower and the higher, just as "behind" (waraa') can mean both "in front" and "behind," as in His saying: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force﴾ [al-Kahf 79].

﴿a mosquito or what is above it. As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Lord﴾. ﴿As for those who believe, they know that it﴾, i.e., the example that Allah presented, is the truth from their Lord, and they believe in it, and they see that in it are clear signs. ﴿But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾, because the truth has not become clear to them due to their turning away from it. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples." (13) No! Rather, what they have been earning has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 13-14]. ﴿They say, "What does Allah intend..."﴾. ﴿What does Allah intend﴾: is the word (ma) here an interrogative noun?

* The students: Interrogative.

* The Shaykh: Interrogative. And (dha) is a demonstrative noun, meaning: "What is this that Allah intends?" But it is said that (dha) here is a relative noun, meaning: "What is it that Allah intended by this as an example?" As Ibn Malik said:

*And like "mā dhā" after an interrogative, or "man" when it is not cancelled in speech.*

So in its grammatical analysis there are two possibilities: we may make (mādhā) a single word and say it is entirely an interrogative noun, or we may make (mā) an interrogative noun in the nominative (mubtada'), and (alladhi) its predicate, meaning: "What is it that Allah intended by this as an example?"

* A student: (dha), O Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: Yes, (dha), which is in the sense of (alladhi).

﴿What does Allah intend by this as an example?﴾, ﴿What does Allah intend by this﴾ with it being an example, so ﴿mathalan﴾ here is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from (dha). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He misleads thereby many﴾. This is not the speech of those who disbelieved; for this reason it is appropriate to stop at His saying ﴿What does Allah intend by this as an example?﴾. ﴿He misleads thereby﴾, i.e., by the example, ﴿many, and guides thereby many﴾. Allah the Mighty and Majestic mentioned that people, in face of examples, divide into two categories: a category that goes astray, may Allah protect us, and a category that is guided. Who is it that goes astray? He said: ﴿And He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient﴾, because Allah the Exalted does not mislead anyone except when there is deviation in him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff 5]. The misguidance of whom Allah misguides is not merely by bare will, but because he is not fit for guidance. ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾. ﴿And He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e., those who depart from obedience to Allah. The intended meaning here is absolute departure, which is disbelief, because fisq (defiant disobedience) may be meant as disbelief, and may be meant as something less. In His saying, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿And as for those who defied (fasaqu), their refuge is the Fire﴾ [al-Sajdah 20], the meaning of fisq here is what? Disbelief. Likewise here, its meaning is disbelief.

In this noble verse: affirmation of modesty (hayaʾ) for Allah, by His saying ﴿Allah is not ashamed to present an example﴾. Is the modesty that is affirmed for Allah like the modesty of created beings? No; because the modesty of a created being is a sense of being overcome by something that overwhelms the person and that he is unable to resist, so you find him becoming subdued and not speaking, or not doing the thing for which he feels shame. The Sunnah has come with an explicit affirmation of modesty in the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «Indeed Allah is modest and generous»[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (1488), al-Tirmidhi (3556), who said: this is a hasan gharib hadith; some of them narrated it without raising it to the Prophet; and Ibn Majah (3865), from the hadith of Salman al-Farisi.]]. But as is our established principle, every attribute that Allah affirmed for Himself differs from the attributes of created beings, by His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura 11].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah the Exalted cites examples, because examples are tangible matters by which intelligible matters are inferred. Consider His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The example of those who take other than Allah as protectors is like the spider, which takes a house﴾ [al-Ankabut 41]. Does this house protect it (...) from the calamities of time? No: ﴿And indeed, the weakest of houses is the house of the spider﴾. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those they invoke other than Him do not respond to them with anything, except like one who stretches his hands out to water so that it may reach his mouth, but it will not reach it﴾ [al-Ra'd 14]. A person who stretches out his hands to the water, a pool or a river for example, stretching his hands like this toward the water wanting the water to reach his mouth: this is impossible. Those who stretch their hands to idols are like one who stretches his hands toward the river so that it reaches his mouth. Examples undoubtedly bring meanings close to a person, either to make the meaning understood, or for their wisdom and the clarification of the aspect of that example.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the mosquito is among the most insignificant of creatures; as His saying: ﴿a mosquito or what is above it﴾. And despite being among the most insignificant of creatures, it disturbs the sleep of tyrants, does it not? Yes, and it may even destroy a person if it were empowered over him; it is this small, despised insect.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of faith, and that the believer cannot oppose what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has sent down with his intellect; as His saying: ﴿As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth﴾. They do not object, nor say "why?" or "how?"; they say: "We hear and we obey and we accept," because they believe that Allah the Mighty and Majestic possesses perfect wisdom in what He legislates and decrees.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of special lordship (rububiyyah khassah); as His saying: ﴿from their Lord﴾. Know that the lordship of Allah divides into two categories: general and special, and both are combined in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds (121) the Lord of Moses and Aaron"﴾ [al-A'raf 121-122]. The first is general lordship and the second is special. Likewise, the opposite, servitude, divides into general servitude, as in His saying, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93], and special servitude, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾ [al-Furqan 1].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the habit of the disbelievers is objection, objecting to the judgment of Allah and the wisdom of Allah; as His saying: ﴿But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾. Whoever objects, even to a part of the Sharia, has a resemblance to the disbelievers. For example, if he says: "Why does eating camel meat nullify wudu, but eating donkey meat, for instance, does not?" What do we say? We say: this is an objection, and it is evidence of deficiency in faith. I only said "donkey meat does not nullify": because donkey meat is impure and unclean; if a person eats it out of necessity, his wudu is not nullified, but eating it without necessity is not permissible.

The proof that objecting to the Sharia of Allah the Mighty and Majestic and His rulings is a habit of the disbelievers is His saying: ﴿But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the word "much" (kathir) does not indicate "most"; as His saying: ﴿He misleads thereby many and guides thereby many﴾. Here, if we took the apparent meaning of the verse, the misguided and the guided would be equal, and that is not so, because of the sons of Adam, nine hundred and ninety-nine out of a thousand are astray and one out of a thousand is guided. So the word (kathir) does not mean "the majority." On this basis, if a person says, "I have many dirhams for you," and gives him three, is that valid?

* The students: (...).

* The Shaykh: Why? Because "kathir" is applied to the few and to the many, and to the majority, in other words.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the misguidance of one who goes astray is not merely by bare will, but because there exists a cause which was the reason for Allah's misguiding the servant; as His saying: ﴿And He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the refutation of the Qadariyyah who said that the actions of servants have no connection with the act of Allah; as His saying: ﴿And He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient﴾.

* And in it also: a refutation of the Jabriyyah, because the defiance of these defiant ones was a cause and by His will; so in it there is a refutation of both groups: the Qadariyyah who negate, and the Qadariyyah who affirm (the Jabriyyah).

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification﴾. "After its ratification" (min ba'di mithaqihi): that is, the covenant that is between them and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which is faith in the messengers when they come to them with the truth. This is binding upon every person: when a messenger comes who confirms [what came before him] and is confirmed by what he brings of signs, it is obligatory upon every person to believe in him. These people broke the covenant of Allah and did not believe in His messengers.

﴿And sever what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾. What is meant by this? Is it the ties of kinship, or everything Allah has commanded to be joined? The generality: the ties of kinship, supporting the messengers, supporting the truth, and defending the truth. Everything we have been commanded to maintain enters into this verse: ﴿and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾.

﴿And cause corruption on the earth﴾. Is the corruption on the earth here meant as physical corruption or moral corruption? It is meant as moral corruption, though physical corruption includes moral corruption, since it is aggression and injustice. But what is meant by corruption on the earth is corrupting it through acts of disobedience, because acts of disobedience are a cause of corruption. What is the evidence for this?

* A student: The words of the Most High: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾ [al-Rum 41].

* The Shaykh: Yes, the evidence is the words of the Most High: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾. Likewise, the early scholars, regarding the words of the Most High: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾ [al-A'raf 56], said: its corruption is by acts of disobedience, because acts of disobedience are the cause of every calamity. Allah the Most High said: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾ [al-A'raf 96]. So, they cause corruption on the earth by what? By acts of disobedience. This corruption is moral corruption, which is accompanied by physical corruption. They do not take bulldozers to cut trees and destroy crops, no; but they do what becomes a cause for that.

﴿Those are the losers﴾. This is a nominal sentence emphasized by an emphasizer. Where is it?

* A student: The pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl).

* The Shaykh: Yes, (hum) is the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl), because the pronoun of separation has three benefits. The first benefit: emphasis. The second: restriction (ḥaṣr). The third: removing ambiguity between the attribute and the predicate. An example of that: you say, "Zaydun al-fadil" (Zayd the virtuous). The word "al-fadil" may be a predicate, and it may be an attribute. So if you say, "Zaydun al-fadilu mahbub" (Zayd the virtuous is beloved), it is determined that it is an attribute. If you say, "Zaydun al-fadilu" (Zayd the virtuous), it may be an attribute, and the predicate has not yet come; or it may be a predicate. If you say, "Zaydun huwa al-fadil" (Zayd is the virtuous one), it is determined to be a predicate, yes, because of the presence of the pronoun of separation. For this reason it is called the pronoun of separation.

Second, it gives emphasis: you say, "Zaydun huwa al-fadil," you have emphasized his virtue. Third, it gives restriction. Does it have a grammatical position (maḥall min al-i'rab)? The answer: No, as in the words of the Most High: ﴿Perhaps we shall follow the sorcerers if they are the victors﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 40]. Had it had a grammatical position, he would have said "al-ghalibun" (the victors). So it has no grammatical position, but it is used in Arabic style for these three benefits. It may sometimes be accompanied by the lam: ﴿Indeed, this is the clear trial﴾ [al-Saffat 106], so the addition of the lam to it gives extra emphasis.

As for His words: ﴿al-khasirun﴾ (the losers): the loser (khasir) is the one who has lost the profit. This is because these people have lost the profit that was gained by whom? The profit was gained by the one who did not break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and who did not sever what Allah commanded to be joined.

There are benefits in this verse. Among them: breaking the covenant of Allah is a sign of wickedness (fisq), by His words: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification﴾. So whenever you see a person who has neglected an obligation or committed a prohibited act, this is a breaking of the covenant after its ratification.

Among them: a warning against breaking the covenant of Allah after its ratification, because that is a cause of wickedness.

Also among them: a warning against severing what Allah has commanded to be joined, of the ties of kinship, meaning relatives and others; because Allah mentioned it in a context of blame, that is, He mentioned severing ties in a context of blame, and severing the ties of kinship is among the major sins, by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «The one who severs ties of kinship will not enter Paradise»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5984), and Muslim (2556/18), from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im. His words "i.e., one who severs the ties of kinship" are from the statement of Ibn 'Uyayna, as in Muslim's narration.]], meaning one who severs the ties of kinship.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: acts of disobedience and wickedness are a cause of the corruption of the earth, by His words: ﴿and cause corruption on the earth﴾. Therefore, when rain is withheld and the land becomes barren, and the people return to their Lord, establish the prayer for rain, supplicate to Him and repent to Him, what happens? Allah relieves them. Noah (peace be upon him) said to his people: ﴿So I said, "Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed, He is ever Forgiving. He will send down rain upon you in abundance, and provide you with wealth and sons and make for you gardens and make for you rivers"﴾ [Nuh 10–12].

If someone says: Are there not, on the earth, righteous people who establish the command of Allah and fulfill the rights of the servants of Allah, and yet we still find corruption on the earth? We say: This objection was raised by Zaynab (may Allah be pleased with her) to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), when he said: «Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near», and she said: "Shall we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us?" He said: «Yes, when wickedness increases»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3346), and Muslim (2880/1), from the hadith of Zaynab bint Jahsh.]]. "When wickedness increases" may refer to the doer as well as to the act: that is, when wickedness increases even among the righteous, or the wickedness of all people. For example, when disbelievers increase in a land, that is a cause of evil and calamity, because wickedness has increased; and when acts of disobedience increase, that is also a cause of evil and calamity.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: those who oppose Allah, break His covenant, sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on the earth think that they are doing good, but in reality they are the losers who have lost both this world and the Hereafter. The Blessed and Most High said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection"﴾ [al-Zumar 15]. And the Most High said: ﴿By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise each other to truth and advise each other to patience﴾ [al-Asr 1–3]. May Allah, by His bounty and generosity, make us and you among them.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life again, then to Him you will be returned?﴾ (2:28) ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth. Then He turned to the heaven and made it seven heavens, and He is Knower of all things.﴾ (2:29) ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it those who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."﴾ (2:30) ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful."﴾ (2:31) ﴿They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise."﴾ (2:32) ﴿He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." And when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing?"﴾ (2:33)

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life again, then to Him you will be returned?﴾ The interrogative here is for denunciation and amazement, or if you wish, say: for denunciation and making [others] marvel, i.e., so that others may be astonished at this state. ﴿How can you disbelieve﴾: disbelief in Allah is denial and rejection, derived from "kafara al-shay'" when one covers something; from it comes "al-kufra," the sheath covering the spathe of the date palm. ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah﴾, i.e., you deny Him and reject Him, and you are arrogant toward worshipping Him, although you know your origin. ﴿And you were dead﴾: that is, before the soul is breathed into a human being, he is dead, inanimate matter. ﴿Then He gave you life﴾ by breathing the soul into you. ﴿Then He will cause you to die﴾ again; that is after the soul has been breathed into him, he dies either in his mother's womb and is born dead, or after he has come out into this world. ﴿Then He will bring you to life﴾ — the life of the Hereafter, after which there is no death. ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾: after the second revival you will be returned to Allah, and He will inform you of your deeds and recompense you for them.

* In this noble verse: a denunciation of the one who disbelieves in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while he knows his state and his end.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the term death is applied to what has no soul, even if life has not previously inhabited it. That is, it is not a condition for describing something as dead that life must have preceded it, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿you were dead and He gave you life﴾. As for the belief of some people that one is only called dead if his life had previously existed, this is not correct; rather Allah, Exalted, applied the description of death to inanimate things, as He said concerning the idols: ﴿They are dead, not alive﴾ (16:21).

* Among the benefits of this verse: if a fetus emerges before the soul is breathed into it, it does not acquire the ruling of a living being. Therefore it is not washed, shrouded, prayed over, does not inherit nor is inherited from. Why? Because it is dead, inanimate matter, and does not deserve any of what the living deserve.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the completeness of Allah's power, the Mighty and Majestic, for this dead body receives the soul breathed into it by Allah, so it lives and becomes a human who moves, speaks, stands, sits, and does what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wills.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of resurrection; through His saying after the second death: ﴿then to Him you will be returned﴾. Resurrection was denied and deemed unlikely by some people, and they said: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ (36:78). So Allah, blessed and exalted, established the possibility of this with eight proofs in Surah Yasin, at its end: ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time"﴾ (36:79). This is evidence that He can give life to bones when they are decayed, and His saying "who produced them the first time" is a decisive proof and clear demonstration of the possibility of their restoration, as Allah said: ﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ (30:27). ﴿And He is Knower of every creation﴾ (36:79): this is a second proof; how could He be incapable of restoring them when He is All-Knowing of every creation, knowing how to create things and how to form them? So He is not incapable of re-creating. ﴿He who made for you from the green tree fire, and then from it you ignite﴾ (36:80). The green tree contains coolness and moisture, while fire contains dryness and aridity; this dry fire comes out of a cool, moist tree. ﴿He who made for you from the green tree fire﴾: how is that? People in former times would strike branches of certain trees with a flint called "zund" among them; when they struck them, fire sparked, and they had something flammable that ignited quickly. Therefore He said: ﴿and then from it you ignite﴾, confirming this. This tree varies; some of it is clear and easy to extract fire from. Regarding this the Arabs say: "In every tree there is fire, and al-Murkh and al-Ghaffar have excelled," meaning that it surpassed others and held more fire.

﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ (36:81). ﴿Yes﴾: this is the fourth proof; the fifth is ﴿And He is the Creator, the Knowing﴾. At the beginning of the verses: ﴿And He is Knower of every creation﴾ (36:79), and here He said: ﴿the Creator﴾ (al-Khallaq). Al-Khallaq is His attribute and His constant description; and if He is Creator and creation is His constant description, He will not be incapable of restoring a human after his death. ﴿His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (36:82): this is also a proof, whatever He wills of anything, and you know "shay'" (thing) is indefinite in a conditional context and thus general. ﴿His command﴾: that is, His affair in this, that He says to it "Be," and it is; or ﴿His command﴾, which is the matter, singular of "awamir," so the meaning is: His command is only to say "Be," so He does not need to repeat it. ﴿So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾ (36:83): this is the seventh proof; everything is owned by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; He causes the existent to cease and brings the non-existent into being, for He is the Lord of all things. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾: this is the eighth proof; it is not wise for Allah to create this creation, command and forbid it, send messengers to it, and have what occurs of fighting between believer and disbeliever, and then the matter simply goes to waste. Rather there must be a return. This is a rational proof. The point is that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is capable of returning the dead to life.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the creatures' return and ultimate destination is to whom? To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 29:

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿It is He who created for you whatever is on the earth, all of it﴾. When He, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned that He is able to give life and cause death, He clarified His favour upon the servants by saying that He created for them whatever is on the earth, all of it. "Created" (khalaqa) means brought into existence without any prior model, but according to what His wisdom and knowledge, exalted is He, required. As for His words ﴿for you﴾, the lam (ل) here has two meanings. The first meaning is permission (al-ibahah), as when you say: "I have permitted it to you." The second meaning is causation (al-ta'lil), i.e., He created for your sake whatever is on the earth, all of it.

As for His words ﴿whatever is on the earth﴾, this "ma" (ما) is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul) that encompasses everything on the earth. So it is created for us: from trees, crops, rivers, mountains, and everything else. ﴿Then He rose (istawa)﴾, meaning after He created whatever is on the earth, all of it, ﴿He rose to the heaven and made them seven heavens﴾. "He rose to it" means He ascended to it; this is how Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it. It was also said: "He rose to it" means He intended it, and this is what Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose. So the scholars have two views on the interpretation of ﴿istawa ila﴾. The first is that istawa here means qasd (intending/directing oneself), and when the intention is complete it is said "istawa," because istiwa' in its essence indicates completeness, as Allah says: ﴿And when he reached his maturity and became perfect (istawa)﴾, meaning he became complete. Whoever considers that this verb is followed by "ila" says that "istawa" here is implicitly meaning "qasada" (intended). And whoever considers that istiwa' only occurs in height makes "ila" mean "ala" (upon). But this is weak, because Allah, exalted is He, never "rose upon the heaven"; rather He rose upon the Throne. So the closer view is that the correct interpretation is what Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, held, namely that istawa here means complete intention and firm will. As for His words ﴿to the heaven﴾, this means the height, and the heaven was smoke, i.e., like smoke. ﴿So He made them seven heavens, perfectly formed﴾, strong and firmly constructed. ﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾; and from His knowledge, the Mighty and Majestic, is that He knows how to create these heavens.

* There are many benefits in this noble verse. Among them: Allah's favour upon His servants in creating for them whatever is on the earth, all of it. Everything is subjugated for us, and praise be to Allah. It is striking that some of us have become subjugated to what was subjugated for us: they serve the world but it does not serve them, and their greatest concern becomes the world, gathering wealth, seeking status, and similar things.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the原 principle regarding what is on the earth is permissibility (al-hill). Everything on the earth is originally permissible, whether trees, water, fruits, animals, or other things; the original state of them is permissibility. This is a great rule. Based on this, if a person eats something from the trees, and another person says to him, "This is forbidden," which of them must be asked for proof? The one who declares it forbidden must bring the proof. Likewise, if a person finds a bird flying, shoots it, hits it, it dies, and he eats it, and the other says, "This is forbidden," who is required to provide evidence? The one who forbids it, the one who must bring the evidence. Therefore nothing on the earth is forbidden except what is established by evidence.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the emphasis on this generality by His words ﴿all of it﴾, even though "ma" as a relative pronoun already denotes generality. But He, glorified and exalted is He, emphasized it so that no one would object that some individual members of this generality had been excluded from the original rule.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming that Allah performs voluntary actions, i.e., that He does what He wills; from His words ﴿then He rose﴾, and "istawa" is a verb. So He, exalted is He, does what He wills, and there occur through Him actions that none can count except Allah, just as there occur through Him speech that none can count except Allah.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the heavens are seven, from His words ﴿seven heavens﴾.

* Among its benefits: the perfection of the creation of the heavens, from His words ﴿so He made them perfect﴾, meaning He made them even and harmonious, not discordant.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge, from His words ﴿and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

We may derive behavioural lessons from this verse, among them: that we thank Allah for this blessing, that He created for us everything on the earth. Everything on the earth is created for our sake and made lawful for us, so we must thank Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for this blessing.

Likewise, among the behavioural lessons: that we fear and are apprehensive. Why, my brothers? Because Allah is Knowing of all things. If Allah knows everything, even what we conceal in our breasts, this obliges us to guard against what displeases Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, whether in our actions, our words, or anything else relating to us.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels﴾, and so on to the end.

* Student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh. Some scholars mentioned that the lowest heaven is the smallest of the heavens, and that it encompasses the earth on every side, i.e., the heaven is like an egg, and the next one is likewise, meaning the heaven is like an egg and we are inside it. What evidence did they rely on?

* The Shaykh: This is clear. Now, the heaven encompasses the earth from every side, does it not?

* The student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: From every side. And between the lowest heaven and the second heaven there is a distance, a distance of five hundred years if the hadith is authentic, or less or more. The point is that there is a distance between them, based on the hadith of the Night Journey: "Then he ascended with me to the second heaven, then he ascended with me to the third heaven," and so on. Accordingly, the cosmos encompasses one another up to the seventh heaven. This is why the lote tree there is called the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha), because everything ends at it.

* The student: Shaykh, does this mean there are small circles, then larger, and larger, and larger?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. And what prevents that? It is a great cosmos.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, the heavens, we say, are a body, and is there any objection?

* The Shaykh: The heavens are a body. There is nothing in them; it is a body that has gates: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant towards them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾ [al-A'raf 40].

* Student: Shaykh, could someone say that the connection of the verse to what precedes it is that it concerns the creation of the heavens and the earth and Allah's rising over the heaven, and then mention of the story of Adam...

* The Shaykh: Then mention of what?

* The student: The story of Adam was mentioned after this verse, which includes the creation of the heavens. Is it a proof of resurrection?

* The Shaykh: It needs reflection. For instance, Allah wanted to show His power to resurrect by saying He created whatever is on the earth, all of it, then mentioned the story of Adam. It needs reflection; it is not clear.

* Student: The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that the earth was created before the heavens, but some verses indicate that the earth was created after the heavens. What is your view?

* The Shaykh: This needs an answer. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? He constructed it. He raised its height and made it proportioned. And He darkened its night and extracted its daylight. And the earth after that He spread it﴾ [al-Nazi'at 27–30]. Is this "after" (ba'diyyah) a temporal after or an after of mention? Some said it is an after of mention, meaning that in addition to that He spread the earth. Others said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created the earth before the heavens, as is the custom in construction, where the base is first; then after that He spread the earth. They say that "spreading" (al-dahw) is explained within the same verse: ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾ [al-Nazi'at 31]. This is closer, because the basic principle is that "after" is temporal, not after of mention.

* Student: May Allah be good to you, Shaykh. Those who permit the use of qat.

* The Shaykh: What?

* Student: Those who permit the use of qat, the qat plant. Does this verse give them evidence?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Qat is not known among us, praise be to Allah. It is known in Yemen and they use it. But the careful scholars of Yemen, in view of what they have witnessed of its harmful effects, hold that it is forbidden and not lawful. Now, if someone said, for example, "Tobacco is lawful because it is among what Allah created on the earth," what do we say to him? We say: Yes, this is the original principle, but the evidences have shown its prohibition because of the harm that results from it, the squandering of wealth, the squandering of time as well, and many other things that we mentioned previously.

* Student: They also cite, O Shaykh, His words: ﴿Say: I do not find within what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it﴾ [al-An'am 145]. Do they cite this verse as evidence?

* The Shaykh: This was mentioned after the mention of animals. ﴿Say: I do not find within what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it﴾ refers to animals, which is why He said: ﴿unless it be carrion, or blood poured out, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure﴾. There is no carrion among plants.

* Student: Shaykh, if a person...

* The Shaykh: What?

* Student: If a man is, for example, an ordinary ignorant person, not much versed in the Shari'ah, and he travels in the earth...

* The Shaykh: What did he do?

* Student: He travelled in the earth.

* The Shaykh: He travelled?

* Student: That is, he journeyed or something similar.

* The Shaykh: He wandered about?

* Student: He wandered, so in application of this verse, then...

* The Shaykh: Is this what you mean: ﴿It is He who created for you﴾ [al-Baqarah 29]?

* Student: Yes, that is it. I do not remember the verse. You say everything is lawful for a human being. Now, for example, if he doubts something, does he act? Does he use it in application of the verse?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. If we doubt the permissibility of a food or drink, the original principle is permissibility. Yes indeed.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know." (30) And He taught Adam the names, all of them. Then He presented them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful." (31) They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise." (32) He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." And when he informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal?"﴾ [al-Baqarah 30–33].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successive authority (khalifah)"﴾. The word (idh) ("when") occurs frequently in the Noble Qur'an. The grammarians (al-mu'ribun) said it is an object of an omitted verb; the estimate is: "Remember when He said," so it is in the accusative by a verb that is omitted, and this is its estimate.

﴿And when your Lord said to the angels﴾: the address in His words ﴿your Lord﴾ is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and since the address is to him, the lordship here becomes one of the particular kinds of lordship. The lam in ﴿lil-malā'ikah﴾ ("to the angels") is for transitivity, i.e., it transmits the speech to the one addressed. The word malā'ikah is the plural of (malak), and its origin is (ma'alak), because it is derived from (al-alūkah), which means a message. But there occurred a modification by transposition, i.e., moving a letter to another place, like (ashyā') whose origin is (shay'ā'). That is why you may wonder: why is (asmā'), the plural of (ism), not diptote, and (ashyā'), the plural of (shay'), not diptote? The reason is that in (asmā'), which is the plural of (ism), the hamzah is original, while in (ashyā') the hamzah is the hamzah of feminine marking. Alright, the point: (al-malā'ikah): we say it is derived from what? From (al-alūkah), which is the message, and for this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾ [Fatir 1]. The angels are an unseen world, created from light, who do not need to eat or drink, and they belong to the unseen realm and are not seen. Otherwise they are present with us, attending gatherings of knowledge and gatherings of remembrance, and standing at the doors of the mosques on Friday, recording the first and then the first; then when the imam arrives they roll up the scrolls and come to listen to the khutbah. But do we see them? We do not see them, and this is from the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic and His trial, that Allah and His Messenger inform us about these beings with these attributes, so that He may test us as to whether we believe or do not believe. Yet sometimes they take the forms of humans, as Allah said about Gabriel when he met Maryam: ﴿He took for her the form of a well-proportioned man﴾ [Maryam 17], an ordinary man with nothing unusual. Likewise Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was sitting among his companions in the form of a man, as ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: extremely white clothing, extremely black hair, no trace of travel was seen on him, and none of the Companions knew him. He sat before the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the manner of one seeking instruction, placing his knees against his knees and his palms on his thighs, and he asked the well-known questions.[[Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab.]] And likewise the Angel of Death came to Musa (peace be upon him) to seize his soul in the form of a human, and Musa (peace be upon him) was strong and mighty, so he struck him to defend himself.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1339) and Muslim (2372/157) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] This was because he did not know that he was a messenger of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; had he known, he would not have done this. But it is the habit of humans that a person defends himself, and as is well known of Musa (ﷺ), he was a strong, mighty man, who when the man from his own party sought his help against the man from his enemies, struck him with one blow and it finished him.

In any case, the basic reality of the angels is that they are an unseen world. He said to them: ﴿Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successive authority﴾. A successor to Allah? Or a successor to those who preceded him? Or one succeeding one another by procreation? Or what?

As for the first, it is possible that Allah the Exalted intended from this creation, Adam and his progeny, that He would make from them successors who represent Allah the Exalted among His servants by conveying His Shariah and calling to it, not out of ignorance of Allah, glory be to Him and far be it from Him, nor out of incapacity, but He bestows upon whomever He wills of His servants, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O Dawud, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people﴾ [Sad 26]. He is a successor who represents Allah in judging among His servants. Likewise they succeed those who came before them: ﴿khalifah﴾, succeeding those who preceded them. On this interpretation, is khalifah here in the sense of the active or the passive? The active; and on the first, in the sense of the passive.

Or they succeed one another, meaning by procreation: this one dies and this one lives. On this explanation, khalifah is suitable for both the active participle and the passive participle; all of this is possible and all of it occurs.

But the words of the angels: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood﴾ indicate that they are successors of whom? What? Of those who preceded them, and that there were creatures on the earth before that which shed blood and caused corruption in it. So the angels asked their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, meaning: the situation will change and will not be like the one that preceded.

And their words: ﴿while we exalt You with praise﴾: "exalt" (nusabbih) means to declare free of imperfection. What is declared free of Allah is two things: first, deficiency; second, deficiency in His perfection. And add a third if you wish: resemblance to created beings. All of this is declared free of Allah. Deficiency means every attribute of deficiency cannot be ascribed to Allah at all, neither as a continuous description nor as a report. The second: deficiency in His perfection, so His perfection cannot have any deficiency: His power cannot be affected by incapacity, His strength cannot be affected by weakness, His knowledge cannot be affected by forgetfulness, and so on. That is why He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38]. Neither little nor much. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, has perfect attributes and no deficiency can affect His perfection. The third?

Students: Resemblance to created beings.

Shaykh: Regarding the resemblance of created beings — "similitude" (mumāthalah), not "resemblance" (mushābahah) — regarding the similitude of created beings. If we wish, we single it out for mention, because Allah the Exalted singled it out, saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [ash-Shura 11], and He said: ﴿And to Him belongs the highest description﴾ [ar-Rum 27], and He said: ﴿So do not strike forth examples for Allah﴾ [an-Nahl 74]. And if we wish, we include it under which categories? The first category: deficiency, because likening the Creator to the created means deficiency; indeed, comparing the perfect with the deficient makes the perfect deficient, as the poet said:

Do you not see that the sword's worth diminishes
when it is said: the sword is sharper than the staff?

If you say: "So-and-so has a sword sharper than a staff," what do you say? It becomes clear that the sword is weak or inferior? Inferior. Sharper than a staff?! It means it is nothing. So perhaps we include this third point, perhaps we include it in the first category, which is deficiency.

In any case, the tasbih: when we say "Subhan Allah," or "I glorify Allah," or similar, we should bring to mind these meanings. We should not say them merely as a formula; we say them as a remembrance, most welcome, but we bring to mind what they indicate: when you say "Subhan Allah," the meaning is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic is exempt from every deficiency, exempt from every defect, exempt from any deficiency in His perfection.

And His words: ﴿with His praise﴾, ﴿nusabbihu bi-hamdik﴾. The scholars said: the bāʾ here is for accompaniment, meaning glorification accompanied by praise. So the two clauses include takhliyah and what? Tahliyah: negation of deficiency and affirmation of perfection, because praise is describing the one praised with perfection. Do not say it is "praise for voluntary acts," as some scholars of kalam say; rather it is describing the one praised with perfection, and in addition love and magnification. If you describe Him again with perfection, call it thanks (thana'). The evidence for this is what is in the authentic hadith: "Allah the Exalted said: I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant into two halves. When he says: 'All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds,' He says: My servant has praised Me. When he says: 'The Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate,' He says: My servant has extolled Me."[[Narrated by Muslim (395/38) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

﴿And we exalt You with praise and sanctify You﴾: tasbih was placed before hamd so that takhliyah comes before tahliyah; negation of deficiency comes before affirmation of perfection, so that perfection arrives at a place free of deficiency. His words ﴿and sanctify You﴾: taqdis means purification, and it is an addition to tanzih, because tanzih is clearing and emptying, while purification is an additional matter. That is why in the opening supplication we say: "O Allah, distance between me and my sins as You distanced between the east and the west. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth. O Allah, wash me of my sins with water, snow and hail."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (744) and Muslim (598/147) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] So taqdis means purification, and the person combines the declaring of Allah free from every defect and deficiency with purifying Him, so that no trace whatsoever of any deficiency that might come to mind remains. ﴿And sanctify You﴾: the lam here is for specification, which conveys sincerity, and it is also for entitlement, because Allah, may He be exalted, is worthy of being sanctified.

How did Allah answer them? ﴿He said: Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾. Stop. What follows is speech: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾. Is (mā) here a relative pronoun or an indefinite qualified noun? Does the meaning become "Indeed, I know something you do not know," or "Indeed, I know that which you do not know"? It admits of both, and it is suitable for both. Alright: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, and the situation will change.

* In this noble verse: affirmation that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has speech. ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels﴾. This is what the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) held: we believe that Allah the Exalted has speech; He speaks.

And affirmation that His speech is with letters and sound. From where do we take that it is with letters? From His words: ﴿Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successive authority﴾; the phrase ﴿Indeed, I will place﴾ is the content of the speech, and it consists of letters. And we take that it is with sound: He said to the angels, meaning speech reaching the angels, and it is impossible for His speech to reach the angels unless it is by sound, and so it is. Then sound may be faint or may be loud; due to His saying: ﴿And We called to him from the right side of the mountain and brought him near in confidence﴾ [Maryam 52]. This is the position of the People of the Sunnah, and in reality it is the ultimate perfection of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; indeed, it is among the greatest attributes of perfection that Allah the Mighty and Majestic speaks whatever He wills, both in creation and in legislation. Everything that happens in the universe comes to be by a word. The evidence: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82]. And everything is willed by Allah, so everything comes to be by speech. As for legislative speech, it is what Allah sent down to the messengers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the angels are possessors of intellect. Its basis: Allah the Exalted addressed them and they responded, and address cannot be directed except to one who understands, nor can one answer it except one who understands speech and can respond to it. This is in contrast to those who said that the angels are not described as such, or who said they are intellects without bodies.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of voluntary action for Allah the Mighty and Majestic. This will be repeated to you often. What is the meaning of voluntary action? It means that among the people of innovation are those who say that voluntary actions do not subsist in Allah: so He does not come, does not descend, does not ascend the throne, does not speak, does not laugh, does not rejoice, does not wonder, because these are matters of will that occur by choice; and if it were correct to describe Allah with them, He would be originated, since these are originated events, and originated events subsist only in something originated. This is a corrupt analogy against an explicit text. Glory be to Allah the Mighty! How grave it is to describe the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, as not acting! This is the greatest defect: that the Lord should not act. That is why some of the predecessors explained "al-Hayy" in His words ﴿al-Hayy al-Qayyum﴾ [al-Baqarah 255], saying: "al-Hayy" is the one who acts much, because from the perfection of life is doing what He wills; and if He does not do what He wills, then He is certainly deficient. As for these people — may Allah protect us — by their feeble, weak, corrupt intellects they stripped Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of His perfection. Add to this saying: they then negate from Allah both speech and action, since He does not speak; He does not speak voluntary speech. Thus they negated from Allah both speech and action. What remains? Nothing remains. This is the greatest deficiency that could be attributed to Allah: that it be said He does not speak and does not act. This verse indicates the affirmation of actions: ﴿Indeed, I will place﴾, and ﴿jā'il﴾ is an active participle: is it for the future or the past?

Students: For the future.

Shaykh: What is your evidence for the future?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No, it is that it is in the accusative, and an active participle does not govern in the accusative except when it refers to the future. On this basis, there is evidence for the affirmation of voluntary actions for Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

Student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh. Many scholars of tafsir follow the first possibility we mentioned, that khalifah here means a successor on behalf of Allah, and they proceed on this. But I read Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah rejecting this view very strongly, and he says: a successor is not appointed except one who is, for example, deficient, or needing, or absent, or the like?

Shaykh: No, that is not correct. The Shaykh has words other than this.

Student: I read it, Shaykh.

Shaykh: Perhaps there is another statement in a second place. We only say, as Allah said: ﴿O Dawud, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth﴾ [Sad 26].

Student: And what you said, Shaykh, I am convinced by it.

Shaykh: We say: the verse admits of all three possibilities.

Student: But what do we say about the words of Shaykh al-Islam, regarding the interpretation you mentioned?

Shaykh: We do not say this; he has words in another place. Or perhaps — the book is not before me now, so I can look — there may be indications that the context is one of rejection, aimed at the interpretation of those people.

Student: Shaykh, "qaddis," Shaykh, "nuqaddisu laka": al-Bayhaqi... the Holy, the Most Holy, the meaning that He is described with attributes of perfection, this means...

Shaykh: Yes indeed, the Pure.

Student: The explanatory... the opposite...

Shaykh: The Quddus means the Pure, free of every defect.

Student: Affirmation of the attribute of perfection is the opposite of tasbih?

Shaykh: Because there cannot exist a negated attribute of Allah except that it includes perfection; there is no pure negation.

Student: Shaykh, if someone says: you said the angels have intellects, and you argued from their being addressed and understanding; alright, Shaykh, if someone says: the ant understood Sulayman, when he said ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings﴾ [an-Naml 18]?

Shaykh: It is addressed (...).

Student: Yes, Shaykh, but...

* The Shaykh: I expected you to say that Allah said to the earth: ﴿Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly﴾ [Fussilat 11]. So we say: all these created things, relative to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, have intellect. The principle is that whoever Allah addresses is rational. But when there are indications that intellect is attributed to them only for the sake of being addressed by Allah, we act on that. Otherwise, the principle is that only a rational being is addressed.
* Student: Has our evidence not been established, Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: It is not established, because what excludes the earth from this is that we observe it, and it is not rational. But relative to Allah's address, it is rational.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. Does our saying that the angels possess intellect necessarily mean that they also possess hearts?
* The Shaykh: No, it does not necessarily mean that.
* Student: Shaykh, Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾ [al-A'raf 179]?
* The Shaykh: Who is being addressed?
* Student: People are being addressed.
* The Shaykh: People are being addressed.
* Student: Shaykh, in a place in the explanation of Kitab al-Tawhid, at the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾ [Saba' 23], you stated, may Allah reward you, that from this verse it is taken that the angels have hearts...
