* The Shaykh: Allah does not establish them by that. But the hearts are not an organ. It may be said that "hearts" here means the figurative heart, because it is well known among the early generations (al-salaf) that the angels are solid, without hollow interiors, and for this reason they do not eat or drink and do not need food or drink.
* Student: Then what establishes the figurative heart rather than the physical one, Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, the figurative heart. Yes. But His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But it is hearts within the breasts that are blinded﴾ [al-Hajj 46] refers to the physical heart, because He described it by its place.
* Student: (...)
* The Shaykh: Did we not say this? We said this.
* Student: Shaykh, have we not reached this?
* The Shaykh: Until now we have not reached it. We have reached ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾. We have not reached it in the benefits (fawa'id).
* * *
* Student: ﴿They said: Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. (32) He said: O Adam, inform them of their names. And when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal? (33) And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 32–34].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them; then He presented them to the angels﴾. In ﴿taught﴾, the doer is Allah the Mighty and Majestic.
* Student: We have not taken the benefits, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Which ones?
* Student: The previous verse.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority"﴾. We took four benefits from it.
* Student: Three, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Count them.
* Student: The affirmation that Allah speaks; the affirmation that His speech is with a letter and a voice; that the angels possess intellect; the affirmation that Allah performs voluntary actions. That is what we took, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: * Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the children of Adam succeed one another, according to one of the opinions regarding the meaning of khalifah (successor). This is the reality: the children of Adam succeed one another. You find one who is a hundred years old alongside one who is a year old, and what lies between them. This is from the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, for if people remained as they were, with no one dying, the earth would be too narrow for them despite its vastness, affairs would not be set right, mercy would not be realized for the young, nor guardianship over them, and other great interests.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the angels' worship of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, by their saying: ﴿while we glorify You with praise and sanctify You﴾.
* And among them: the angels' dislike of corruption on the earth, by their saying: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾.
* And among the benefits of this verse: that a person describing himself with the good that is in him is not a fault, by their saying: ﴿while we glorify You with praise and sanctify You﴾. So if the intent is merely to report, there is no harm. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I am the master of the children of Adam, and I say this without boasting."[[Related by al-Tirmidhi (3148) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri; its beginning is related by al-Bukhari (3340) and Muslim (2278/3) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] But if the intent is boasting and self-praise, this is not permissible.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the intense veneration of the angels for Allah the Mighty and Majestic, in that they said: ﴿we glorify You with praise﴾, and the second: ﴿and sanctify You﴾. This resembles His saying (ﷺ): "Cleanse me of sins and faults... and wash me of my errors."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (744) and Muslim (598/147) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of comparative preference between Allah and creation, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, I know what you do not know﴾. Here ﴿a'lam (I know)﴾ is an elative form (ism tafdil), and this is the truth. Some who claim they are exalting Allah disagreed and said that ﴿a'lam﴾ is not on its usual pattern but means ʿalim (knowing). They did not realize that if they interpret it as ʿalim, this becomes a greater deficiency for Allah, because the word ʿalim does not exclude sharing, and it is known that among creation there are knowing beings, as Allah blessed and exalted says: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Nahl 78], and He said to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿He taught you what you did not know﴾ [al-Nisa' 113].
And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you know them to be believing women, then do not return them﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 10]. Accordingly, we say that ﴿a'lam﴾ here is on its usual pattern, just as it is said: "Allah is the most merciful of the merciful." And in the noble Qur'an: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin 8].
* Student: (...)
* The Shaykh: Deriving benefits has no questions.
* Student: (...)
* The Shaykh: Which one?
* Student: (...)
* The Shaykh: Yes, well done, that is the conclusion.
* Student: No, Shaykh, we have taken...
* The Shaykh: In any case, it is good, God willing; what we imagined in it is good. Regarding ﴿a'lam﴾, there is no harm in saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided﴾ [al-Nahl 125]. I say: some scholars interpreted ﴿a'lam﴾ as meaning ʿalim and said that comparative preference between Allah and creation in attributes is not permissible. But this is a false statement, because the evidences show its falsity. As for the verse before us, ﴿Indeed, I know (a'lam)﴾, it is a present-tense verb. Then He said: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾. In ﴿taught﴾, who is the doer? Allah the Mighty and Majestic. And Adam is the father of mankind.
* Student: So we drop this last benefit?

Shaykh: Which one... The last benefit regarding words like "a'lam" — yes, but it has a benefit for you, though it does not belong to the tafsir itself. ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾: Allah the Exalted taught Adam, the father of mankind, all the names. ﴿The names﴾: is the definite article here for generality, as His words ﴿all of them﴾ indicate, or is it for a specific group? The names, meaning the names of what was present, as evidenced by His words ﴿Tell Me the names of these﴾, and His words ﴿the names, all of them﴾, meaning all those present. That is because Allah the Exalted created things and said to Adam: this is such-and-such, and this is such-and-such, and this is such-and-such, of what he and his offspring would need. ﴿Then He presented them﴾: the pronoun "hum" (them) here is the sign of the plural, and it is only used for rational beings, while the names are not rational. So what is the answer? The answer is that we say: He presented the named things (al-musammayat) and did not present the names, because of His words ﴿Tell Me﴾ ... ﴿the names of these﴾. So ﴿He presented them﴾ means He presented the named things to the angels. Then He said: ﴿Tell Me the names of these﴾, and they did not know, they did not recognize them. ﴿They said: Glory be to You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾. Then He said: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names﴾. He, the Mighty and Majestic, intended by this that the angels should know that they do not encompass all things in knowledge, and that there are things that escape them in which Adam surpasses them. ﴿So He said: Tell Me the names of these﴾. ﴿Tell Me﴾: is this an imperative verb intended to make the one commanded carry out what he was directed to, or is it a challenge? The apparent meaning is the second: it is a challenge, ﴿if you are truthful﴾, that you have knowledge of things; so tell Me the names of these. Because the angels had said previously: ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?﴾ So Allah said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, and then He tested them with this. ﴿He said: Tell Me the names of these, if you are truthful﴾. ﴿These﴾: to whom does the pointing refer? To the present named things. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in that you have knowledge. ﴿They said: Glory be to You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾, meaning: exalting You above futility and foolishness; You, our Lord, did not do this except for a great wisdom. And their words ﴿We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾ are an acknowledgment from the angels that they know only what Allah has taught them, even though they are angels brought near to Allah, and despite that they know only what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has taught them. ﴿Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise﴾. The phrase ﴿Indeed You﴾ is emphasized by "inna" and by "anta", which is the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl), because the kaf is the noun of "inna", and "anta" is a separating pronoun with no place in i'rab, and ﴿the Knowing﴾ is the predicate of "inna". ﴿Indeed, You are the Knowing﴾: meaning the One possessing vast, all-encompassing knowledge that surrounds past, present and future.

His words ﴿the Wise﴾: meaning the One possessing wisdom and judgment, because "hakim" (wise) is derived from "hukm" (judgment) and "hikmah" (wisdom). So these are two of Allah's names: al-'Alim and al-Hakim.

In these two verses there is a clarification that Allah the Exalted may bestow favour upon His servants, or upon some of His servants, with knowledge that others do not know. Its aspect is that Allah taught Adam the names of named things that were present while the angels were ignorant of that.

Among them: languages are tawqifi (divinely taught) and not tajribi (acquired by experiment). Tawqifi means that Allah is the One who taught people them, and had Allah not taught them, they would not have understood them. It has been said that they are tajribi, in the sense that people formed these letters and sounds through experience, so that man was at first mute, not knowing what to say, but he heard the sound of thunder, the rustling of trees, the sound of water flowing on the earth, and similar things, and he took from what he heard sounds that indicate his intention. But this is not correct.

The correct view is that the origin of languages is tawqifi, and many of them are acquired through experience, known by people from the course of events. That is why you find that things come into existence which had no name before, and then people create a name for them, either from experience or otherwise. Hence, most of the names of modern things that you find match the meaning for which they were named.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of examination, testing a person in what he claims to excel at. We are in these days a time of examinations, and questions will be put to you, saying: tell me the ruling on such-and-such. Yes, as a test: if you answer ﴿We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise﴾, then what have you gained? Zero. And if you answer with what Allah has opened to you, then this is justice, each in his own degree.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of challenge with expressions that contain some severity, since he did not restrict himself to His words ﴿Tell Me the names of these﴾, but said ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the angels speak. From where is this derived? From His words: what? ﴿They said: Glory be to You! We have no knowledge﴾, and His words ﴿Tell Me﴾ also ﴿the names of these, if you are truthful﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the acknowledgment by the angels, peace be upon them, that they have no knowledge except what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has taught them. It follows from this that a person should know his own worth, so he does not claim what is not his, nor claim what he has not attained.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the great exaltation of Allah the Mighty and Majestic by the angels, in that they acknowledged His perfection and His transcendence above ignorance in their words ﴿Glory be to You﴾, acknowledged their own lack of knowledge, and acknowledged to Allah His grace in His words ﴿except what You have taught us﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, al-'Alim and al-Hakim. Now, is al-'Alim one of the intransitive (lazima) names or the transitive (muta'addiya) names?
* A student: Intransitive.
* Another student: Transitive.
* Shaykh: Transitive, ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Baqarah 255]. So it is among the transitive names. The scholars say: faith in a transitive name is not complete except with three things: affirming it as a name of Allah, affirming the attribute it indicates, and third, affirming the judgment or effect that follows from it. For example, al-'Alim: we affirm al-'Alim as a name of Allah, and we must affirm the knowledge that al-'Alim indicates, which is the attribute, and we affirm the effect that follows from it, and that it extends to others, namely that He, the Mighty and Majestic, knows. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass anything of His knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha 110]. Al-Hakim is likewise: we must believe in al-Hakim as a name of Allah, and believe in the attribute it indicates, and al-Hakim indicates two attributes: hukm (judgment) and hikmah (wisdom), for it is derived from both.

Hukm: the scholars say it is divided into two kinds: kawni (cosmic/decreed) and shar'i (legislative). The words of Allah the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Do they then seek the judgment of ignorance? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 50] — what is meant by it? The legislative. And His words in Surah al-Mumtahanah: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 10] — this too is legislative. And His words, the Blessed and Exalted, about the brother of Yusuf: ﴿So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me﴾ [Yusuf 80] — this is cosmic. And His words, the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾ [al-Anbiya' 112] — cosmic; because Allah has already judged legislatively, so it does not need supplication, but ﴿judge with truth﴾ means between us and our enemies.

So judgment is divided into what? Two kinds: legislative and cosmic. As for the cosmic, O brothers, the cosmic must come to pass: when Allah judges a thing cosmically, it must occur. If He decrees sickness upon a person, he becomes sick; poverty, and he becomes poor, whether he wills or refuses. As for the legislative judgment, is it binding upon everyone? No; it is binding only upon whom? The believers. As for the disbelievers, they are not bound by it.

Wisdom is, as the scholars say: placing a thing in its proper place. This excludes foolishness, which is when the doer places a thing in other than its place. If wisdom is placing a thing in its fitting place, then let us consider: wisdom has two relations: a relation to the cosmic judgment and a relation to the legislative judgment. If you reflect on Allah's legislative judgments, you find them in the utmost wisdom and perfection, and that they are suited to every time, place and nation, especially the rulings brought by the Sharia of Muhammad ﷺ; as for other rulings, they may be unsuitable for every time and place.

Likewise the cosmic judgment: if you reflect on the actions of Allah the Mighty and Majestic in His creation, you find them in the utmost wisdom, and in a state that dazzles the intellects: ﴿And in yourselves; will you not then see?﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 21]. And if you went to anatomists so that they might explain to you what is in this body of wonders that dazzle the intellects, you would know thereby the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

Moreover, wisdom in both the cosmic and legislative judgments has two states: a state in placing a thing as it is, and a state in the purpose intended from it. Note this: placing the thing as it is is called the formal end (al-ghayah al-suwariyyah), and the expected goal is called the cause or the final wisdom (al-hikmah al-ghā'iyyah). So, for example, if you look at Allah's legislative rulings, let us say: look at the prayer. The prayer in this form: standing, then bowing, then standing, then prostration, there is no doubt that in this form it is at its best, and its goal too is praiseworthy and commendable. And look at the Hajj as well: its form, without doubt, is in accord with wisdom, and its goal is also in accord with wisdom.

And likewise the decreed rulings: you find that Allah the Mighty and Majestic judges by the decreed rulings in accordance with wisdom. For example, He sends down rain where its sending contains benefit, but rain may also be a punishment, when it increases and becomes excessive. And is its being a punishment a matter of wisdom or not? It is wisdom, because Allah said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of that which they have done, so that they might return﴾ [ar-Rum 41]. His words ﴿that He may let them taste﴾ are a causal explanation of His act, the Mighty and Majestic, and His words ﴿so that they might return﴾ are a causal explanation of the object: that is, this disliked matter occurred so that these people might return.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Some people, Shaykh, of limited knowledge say: sometimes some matters of Allah's wisdom come to me on my own, in some creatures or some of Allah's many signs. Should we say to such a person, first acknowledge that Allah the Mighty and Majestic is All-Wise, and does nothing except for a great wisdom, and you must stop, if you do not know this, from reflecting on the actions of Allah, glorified and exalted be He?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: So we say: you must investigate, reflect, and ask the people of knowledge until knowledge settles in you?
* Shaykh: We say: whenever the wisdom of something from the Sharia or the decree becomes unclear to a person, he must submit, ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair﴾ [al-Ahzab 36]. ʿĀ'ishah said to the woman who asked her: "What is the matter with the menstruating woman who makes up the fast but does not make up the prayer?" * Student: ﴿And I know what you disclose and what you conceal (33). And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant, and he was among the disbelievers (34). And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it freely wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers" (35). Then Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, some of you enemies to others, and for you on earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time" (36). Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful (37).﴾ [al-Baqarah 33–37].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said, after mentioning that He taught Adam all the names: ﴿Then He presented them﴾, meaning He presented the named things (al-musammayat). The evidence is that He did not say "then He presented them" in the feminine form (ʿaradahunna), and if the pronoun referred to the names, He would have said ʿaradahunna. Also, He said: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful﴾. This shows that what was presented is the named things. He said: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful (31). They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise."﴾ Here, knowledge was given to Adam, and the angels were ignorant, so that Allah the Mighty and Majestic might show them the virtue of Adam, peace be upon him. This matter has already been discussed, along with its benefits.

Shaykh: Which one... The last benefit regarding words like "a'lam" — yes, but it has a benefit for you, though it does not belong to the tafsir itself. ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾: Allah the Exalted taught Adam, the father of mankind, all the names. ﴿The names﴾: is the definite article here for generality, as His words ﴿all of them﴾ indicate, or is it for a specific group? The names, meaning the names of what was present, as evidenced by His words ﴿Tell Me the names of these﴾, and His words ﴿the names, all of them﴾, meaning all those present. That is because Allah the Exalted created things and said to Adam: this is such-and-such, and this is such-and-such, and this is such-and-such, of what he and his offspring would need. ﴿Then He presented them﴾: the pronoun "hum" (them) here is the sign of the plural, and it is only used for rational beings, while the names are not rational. So what is the answer? The answer is that we say: He presented the named things (al-musammayat) and did not present the names, because of His words ﴿Tell Me﴾ ... ﴿the names of these﴾. So ﴿He presented them﴾ means He presented the named things to the angels. Then He said: ﴿Tell Me the names of these﴾, and they did not know, they did not recognize them. ﴿They said: Glory be to You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾. Then He said: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names﴾. He, the Mighty and Majestic, intended by this that the angels should know that they do not encompass all things in knowledge, and that there are things that escape them in which Adam surpasses them. ﴿So He said: Tell Me the names of these﴾. ﴿Tell Me﴾: is this an imperative verb intended to make the one commanded carry out what he was directed to, or is it a challenge? The apparent meaning is the second: it is a challenge, ﴿if you are truthful﴾, that you have knowledge of things; so tell Me the names of these. Because the angels had said previously: ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?﴾ So Allah said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, and then He tested them with this. ﴿He said: Tell Me the names of these, if you are truthful﴾. ﴿These﴾: to whom does the pointing refer? To the present named things. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in that you have knowledge. ﴿They said: Glory be to You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾, meaning: exalting You above futility and foolishness; You, our Lord, did not do this except for a great wisdom. And their words ﴿We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾ are an acknowledgment from the angels that they know only what Allah has taught them, even though they are angels brought near to Allah, and despite that they know only what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has taught them. ﴿Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise﴾. The phrase ﴿Indeed You﴾ is emphasized by "inna" and by "anta", which is the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl), because the kaf is the noun of "inna", and "anta" is a separating pronoun with no place in i'rab, and ﴿the Knowing﴾ is the predicate of "inna". ﴿Indeed, You are the Knowing﴾: meaning the One possessing vast, all-encompassing knowledge that surrounds past, present and future.

His words ﴿the Wise﴾: meaning the One possessing wisdom and judgment, because "hakim" (wise) is derived from "hukm" (judgment) and "hikmah" (wisdom). So these are two of Allah's names: al-'Alim and al-Hakim.

In these two verses there is a clarification that Allah the Exalted may bestow favour upon His servants, or upon some of His servants, with knowledge that others do not know. Its aspect is that Allah taught Adam the names of named things that were present while the angels were ignorant of that.

Among them: languages are tawqifi (divinely taught) and not tajribi (acquired by experiment). Tawqifi means that Allah is the One who taught people them, and had Allah not taught them, they would not have understood them. It has been said that they are tajribi, in the sense that people formed these letters and sounds through experience, so that man was at first mute, not knowing what to say, but he heard the sound of thunder, the rustling of trees, the sound of water flowing on the earth, and similar things, and he took from what he heard sounds that indicate his intention. But this is not correct.

The correct view is that the origin of languages is tawqifi, and many of them are acquired through experience, known by people from the course of events. That is why you find that things come into existence which had no name before, and then people create a name for them, either from experience or otherwise. Hence, most of the names of modern things that you find match the meaning for which they were named.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of examination, testing a person in what he claims to excel at. We are in these days a time of examinations, and questions will be put to you, saying: tell me the ruling on such-and-such. Yes, as a test: if you answer ﴿We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise﴾, then what have you gained? Zero. And if you answer with what Allah has opened to you, then this is justice, each in his own degree.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of challenge with expressions that contain some severity, since he did not restrict himself to His words ﴿Tell Me the names of these﴾, but said ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the angels speak. From where is this derived? From His words: what? ﴿They said: Glory be to You! We have no knowledge﴾, and His words ﴿Tell Me﴾ also ﴿the names of these, if you are truthful﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the acknowledgment by the angels, peace be upon them, that they have no knowledge except what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has taught them. It follows from this that a person should know his own worth, so he does not claim what is not his, nor claim what he has not attained.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the great exaltation of Allah the Mighty and Majestic by the angels, in that they acknowledged His perfection and His transcendence above ignorance in their words ﴿Glory be to You﴾, acknowledged their own lack of knowledge, and acknowledged to Allah His grace in His words ﴿except what You have taught us﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, al-'Alim and al-Hakim. Now, is al-'Alim one of the intransitive (lazima) names or the transitive (muta'addiya) names?
* A student: Intransitive.
* Another student: Transitive.
* Shaykh: Transitive, ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Baqarah 255]. So it is among the transitive names. The scholars say: faith in a transitive name is not complete except with three things: affirming it as a name of Allah, affirming the attribute it indicates, and third, affirming the judgment or effect that follows from it. For example, al-'Alim: we affirm al-'Alim as a name of Allah, and we must affirm the knowledge that al-'Alim indicates, which is the attribute, and we affirm the effect that follows from it, and that it extends to others, namely that He, the Mighty and Majestic, knows. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass anything of His knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha 110]. Al-Hakim is likewise: we must believe in al-Hakim as a name of Allah, and believe in the attribute it indicates, and al-Hakim indicates two attributes: hukm (judgment) and hikmah (wisdom), for it is derived from both.

Hukm: the scholars say it is divided into two kinds: kawni (cosmic/decreed) and shar'i (legislative). The words of Allah the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Do they then seek the judgment of ignorance? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 50] — what is meant by it? The legislative. And His words in Surah al-Mumtahanah: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 10] — this too is legislative. And His words, the Blessed and Exalted, about the brother of Yusuf: ﴿So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me﴾ [Yusuf 80] — this is cosmic. And His words, the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾ [al-Anbiya' 112] — cosmic; because Allah has already judged legislatively, so it does not need supplication, but ﴿judge with truth﴾ means between us and our enemies.

So judgment is divided into what? Two kinds: legislative and cosmic. As for the cosmic, O brothers, the cosmic must come to pass: when Allah judges a thing cosmically, it must occur. If He decrees sickness upon a person, he becomes sick; poverty, and he becomes poor, whether he wills or refuses. As for the legislative judgment, is it binding upon everyone? No; it is binding only upon whom? The believers. As for the disbelievers, they are not bound by it.

Wisdom is, as the scholars say: placing a thing in its proper place. This excludes foolishness, which is when the doer places a thing in other than its place. If wisdom is placing a thing in its fitting place, then let us consider: wisdom has two relations: a relation to the cosmic judgment and a relation to the legislative judgment. If you reflect on Allah's legislative judgments, you find them in the utmost wisdom and perfection, and that they are suited to every time, place and nation, especially the rulings brought by the Sharia of Muhammad ﷺ; as for other rulings, they may be unsuitable for every time and place.

Likewise the cosmic judgment: if you reflect on the actions of Allah the Mighty and Majestic in His creation, you find them in the utmost wisdom, and in a state that dazzles the intellects: ﴿And in yourselves; will you not then see?﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 21]. And if you went to anatomists so that they might explain to you what is in this body of wonders that dazzle the intellects, you would know thereby the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

Moreover, wisdom in both the cosmic and legislative judgments has two states: a state in placing a thing as it is, and a state in the purpose intended from it. Note this: placing the thing as it is is called the formal end (al-ghayah al-suwariyyah), and the expected goal is called the cause or the final wisdom (al-hikmah al-ghā'iyyah). So, for example, if you look at Allah's legislative rulings, let us say: look at the prayer. The prayer in this form: standing, then bowing, then standing, then prostration, there is no doubt that in this form it is at its best, and its goal too is praiseworthy and commendable. And look at the Hajj as well: its form, without doubt, is in accord with wisdom, and its goal is also in accord with wisdom.

And likewise the decreed rulings: you find that Allah the Mighty and Majestic judges by the decreed rulings in accordance with wisdom. For example, He sends down rain where its sending contains benefit, but rain may also be a punishment, when it increases and becomes excessive. And is its being a punishment a matter of wisdom or not? It is wisdom, because Allah said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of that which they have done, so that they might return﴾ [ar-Rum 41]. His words ﴿that He may let them taste﴾ are a causal explanation of His act, the Mighty and Majestic, and His words ﴿so that they might return﴾ are a causal explanation of the object: that is, this disliked matter occurred so that these people might return.

* Student: ﴿And I know what you disclose and what you conceal (33). And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. * Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said, after mentioning that He taught Adam all the names: ﴿Then He presented them﴾, meaning He presented the named things (al-musammayat). The evidence is that He did not say "then He presented them" in the feminine form (ʿaradahunna), and if the pronoun referred to the names, He would have said ʿaradahunna. Also, He said: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful﴾. This shows that what was presented is the named things. He said: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful (31). Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise."﴾ Here, knowledge was given to Adam, and the angels were ignorant, so that Allah the Mighty and Majestic might show them the virtue of Adam, peace be upon him. This matter has already been discussed, along with its benefits.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 33:

﴿He said: "O Adam, inform them of their names."﴾ He said: "O Adam, inform them of their names, so he informed them." Adam (ʾĀdam) is apparently a proper name for our father and not a descriptive term. Linguistically it is derived from al-udmah (admah), which is a color between pure white and black. ﴿Inform them of their names﴾, i.e., the names of these named things. ﴿So when he informed them﴾: who is the agent? Adam, when he informed them; he informed the angels of their names. ﴿He said﴾, i.e., God said: ﴿"Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal?"﴾ This was in response to their statement: ﴿"Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."﴾ Then God, exalted is He, wished to show the extent of the angels' knowledge regarding a matter they witnessed yet did not know, by presenting the named things to them and asking them to know their names. ﴿"Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth"﴾, i.e., what is hidden in them. ﴿"And I know what you reveal"﴾, i.e., what you make apparent. ﴿"And what you conceal."﴾

There are several benefits in this verse. Among them: the affirmation that speech belongs to God, as shown by His saying ﴿"O Adam"﴾, and that it is with a letter and an audible voice, since Adam heard and then informed them. This is the belief of the People of the Sunnah and the Community and the righteous predecessors (al-Salaf al-Salih): that God speaks with audible speech, speech arranged in sequence, some of it preceding other parts.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Adam, peace be upon him, complied and obeyed without hesitation; this is shown by ﴿"So when he informed them"﴾. Hence the mention of his saying "so he informed them" is omitted, indicating that he hastened and informed the angels. From this is derived the swiftness of Adam's compliance with the command of God, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: it is permissible to put the addressee to acknowledgment of something he cannot refute, and acknowledgment (taqrir) can only be of this kind, that is, of a matter that cannot be repelled. This is shown by ﴿"Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth"﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the demonstration of the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, and that it pertains to both the witnessed and the unseen; this is shown by ﴿"I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth"﴾.

* Among the benefits: the heavens are plural in number, as shown by ﴿"the heavens"﴾, while the earth is mentioned in singular form, which is intended generically (jins), because God, exalted is He, said: ﴿"It is God who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them"﴾ [al-Talaq 12].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the angels have wills which they reveal and conceal; this is shown by ﴿"I know what you reveal and what you conceal."﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God, exalted is He, knows what is in hearts, whether it is revealed or not revealed; this is shown by ﴿"what you reveal and what you conceal."﴾

Note the phrase: knowing what is in hearts. If someone says: what is your evidence that the angels have hearts?

We say: the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿"Until, when fear is removed from their hearts, they say, 'What has your Lord said?' They say, 'The truth. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.'"﴾ [Saba' 23].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 34:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated﴾. It means: "Remember when..." Such an expression is repeated frequently in the Qur'an, and the scholars supply the word "remember" (udhkur), and they need this supplied element, because (idh) is an adverb of time (zarfiyyah), and an adverb must have something to which it relates, either stated or omitted. There must be this. In the verses of Nazm al-Jumal:

"The prepositional phrase must have a connection
to a verb or its meaning, such as 'murtaqi'."

The adverb of time is similar. On this basis we supply: "Remember when, ﴿And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam'﴾." The discussion of the mention of the angels and whence this word is derived has already preceded, has it not? Yes. ﴿"Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis﴾. ﴿Prostrate﴾: sujud is prostration upon the earth, by which a person places the highest part of his body upon the ground in submission and humility. It is not intended to be mere bowing (ruku'), because Allah distinguished between bowing and prostration: ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating﴾ [al-Fath 29]. ﴿"Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated﴾ without delay, so the fa' here indicates sequence and immediacy. ﴿Except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾. And we seek refuge in Allah. Iblis is the devil, and he was named Iblis because he was made despairing (ublisa) of the mercy of Allah, that is, he despaired of it with a despair after which there is no hope.

As for His saying ﴿except Iblis﴾, someone may say: does this verse indicate that Iblis was of the angels? And it is established that the angels were created from what? From light. And Iblis? From fire. The answer to this difficulty is that Iblis was outwardly among the angels, because he would come, gather with them, and worship Allah as the angels worship Him, until the hidden thing in his heart appeared, and it became clear that he was a disbeliever, may Allah protect us. He says: ﴿except Iblis, he refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾. This phrase occurs in the Qur'an in three ways: sometimes refusal is mentioned without arrogance, sometimes arrogance without refusal, and sometimes both refusal and arrogance are mentioned. In which surah are both refusal and arrogance mentioned? Here, in Surat al-Baqarah. And in which surah is refusal mentioned without arrogance?

* Student: In al-Kahf.

* The Shaykh: In al-Kahf? No, in al-Hijr: ﴿He refused to be among the prostrators﴾ [al-Hijr 31]. And in which surah is arrogance mentioned without refusal?

* Student: Ghafir.

* The Shaykh: No.

* Student: Sad.

* The Shaykh: Sad, where arrogance is mentioned without refusal. Does this mean that the devil is described by this once, by that once, and by that once? Or do we say he is described by both together, but there is no objection to a described subject being characterized by one of two attributes in one place and by both attributes in another place, since there is no contradiction?

﴿Refused﴾ means he declined. ﴿And was arrogant﴾, that is, he became one possessing pride. ﴿And was among the disbelievers﴾. Some scholars claimed that it means he was among the disbelievers in Allah's knowledge, based on the fact that (kana) is a past-tense verb, and the past indicates something prior, so the meaning of ﴿was among the disbelievers﴾ would be "in the knowledge of Allah." But there is a better interpretation than this: that we say (kana) sometimes comes stripped of time, and what is intended is the realization of the described subject's being characterized by this attribute. Among examples of this is His saying the Exalted: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa' 96], ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty, Wise﴾ [an-Nisa' 158], ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing﴾ [an-Nisa' 134], and what resembles them. In these, the meaning is not that He was so in the past, but that He still is. So (kana) here is stripped of time, and what is intended is the realization of the subject's attribution of what the sentence indicates. This is the closest view, and there is no interpretation (ta'wil) in it; the statement is taken according to its apparent meaning. ﴿And was among the disbelievers﴾, because he was not all the disbelievers, but he was one of them.

In this noble verse there is an indication of Adam's superiority over the angels. What is its basis?

* Student: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾.

* The Shaykh: This verse, but what is the point of inference from the verse?

* Student: Because Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to him.

* The Shaykh: Because Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to him, and it is known that one who prostrates to another is in a rank below him, lower than him.

There is a difficulty in the verse: Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, and prostration to other than Allah is shirk. So how would He command them to shirk, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when they commit an immorality they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us with it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command immorality"﴾?

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you, this was a prostration of greeting, like the prostration of Joseph's brothers to Joseph.

* The Shaykh: Yes, and it was not a true prostration (?). What is the evidence for diverting it?

* Student: What is known (...) from the religion of Islam.

* The Shaykh: From the religion of Islam.

* Student: The approval of Joseph, peace be upon him, of his brothers' deed?

* The Shaykh: Do not take us elsewhere, people; answer about this place.

* Student: The command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in itself to that which He forbade, namely shirk, shows it is not shirk.

* The Shaykh: So you mean, as the brother said, that prostration is a greeting of submission with the head, like this?

* Student: No, a true prostration, true and a greeting.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: But is it now impossible that Mu'adh ibn Jabal prostrated to the Prophet? [[This is a hadith from Mu'adh ibn Jabal: that when he returned from Yemen, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw men in Yemen prostrating to one another, so should we not prostrate to you?" He said: "If I were to command a human to prostrate to another human, I would command the woman to prostrate to her husband." Narrated by Ahmad (21986).]] And the Prophet ﷺ said to him.

* The Shaykh: There is no power nor strength except with Allah.

* Student: Shaykh, we say: this occurred by the command of Allah.

* The Shaykh: Yes, and when it occurred by the command of Allah, it became worship, even if it was to other than Allah. Prostration is the right of Allah, the Exalted, so if He commands it to be made to another, who prevents it? Is not killing a sanctified soul one of the greatest major sins? Yet the killing of Ibrahim, who was commanded to slaughter his son, became one of the noble acts of obedience. Killing a soul is undoubtedly forbidden and a sin, especially if a person kills his child, his father, or his relative, but when it was by the command of Allah it became obedience to Allah. Hence worship is defined as humbling oneself before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by what? By carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. So the correct view is that we take the Qur'an according to its apparent meaning and say: it was a true prostration, but when Allah commanded it, that became His right, and complying with it became worship.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever attributes himself outwardly to someone is treated in accordance with that. From where is this derived?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: How? What is the point of inference?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: But what is the point of inference that he attributed himself to the angels?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Because the address directed to them became inclusive of him. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ treated the hypocrites as he treated the Muslims, and he was asked permission to kill them, although he knew some of them by name, but he said: "People should not say that Muhammad kills his companions" [[Agreed upon. al-Bukhari (4905) and Muslim (2584/63) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.]], and even the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The client of a people is from them" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (1650), al-Tirmidhi (657), al-Nasa'i (2612), and Ahmad (18992), from the hadith of Abu Rafi', the wording being that of al-Nasa'i and Ahmad.]], although he is not of their lineage.

Among the benefits of this verse: whoever displays goodness while his heart harbours evil, his affair will necessarily become evident.

* Student: (...) refused and was arrogant, this indicates that he was not of them.

* The Shaykh: That in his heart there is a wicked disease. Yes. From this we proceed to the training of a person in himself, that a person should look into his heart: if there is a wicked secret in it, let him beware of it, for a person may do the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to people while he is of the people of the Fire. Purify your heart. Purifying the heart is more important than purifying the body, and submission to Allah with the heart is more important than submission with the head, and the prostration of the heart to Allah is more important than the prostration of the body. We ask Allah to help us in that. Be keen on this, be keen on rectifying the heart. Do not carry hypocrisy (riya') or shirk, nor malice toward the believers, nor spite or envy. Purify your hearts, so that you are not ended with a bad end. "Indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to people, while he is of the people of the Fire" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2898) and Muslim (112/179) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi.]]. O Allah, we seek refuge in Your Majesty from that.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: Iblis, may Allah protect us, combined all the attributes of blame: refusal to obey the command, arrogance toward the truth and toward creation, and disbelief as the third. Iblis was arrogant toward the truth because he did not comply with the command of Allah, and arrogant toward creation because he said: ﴿I am better than him﴾ [al-A'raf 12], so he was proud within himself and humiliated others. Pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.

* Student: Shaykh, we said: must one whose inner intention is evil necessarily display it? Necessarily?

* The Shaykh: Yes. Al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "No man conceals a secret except that Allah reveals it through the slips of his tongue and the features of his face."

* Student: The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the Prophet ﷺ about the hypocrites: "And among them are those..." He said to him that some of them he does not know; those who died believing they were believers and the Prophet ﷺ did not know?

* The Shaykh: Allah said: ﴿And you will surely know them by the tone of speech﴾ [Muhammad 30].

* Student: And this verse?

* The Shaykh: Which verse?

* Student: The one in which it says that the Prophet ﷺ does not know some of the hypocrites?

* The Shaykh: But their hypocrisy must be made clear; it must be made clear.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed. ﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it freely wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers." So Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, some of you to others an enemy, and for you on earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time." Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs – those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally."﴾ [al-Baqarah 35–39].

**Shaykh:** Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And We said, "O Adam"﴾. We have already taken the lessons of what preceded. ﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it freely wherever you wish"﴾. The doer of the speech is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. As for His words ﴿dwell, you and your wife﴾, the word "wife" (zawj) is conjoined to the subject in ﴿dwell﴾, or to ﴿you﴾? It is conjoined to the subject in ﴿dwell﴾, because ﴿you﴾ is an emphasis of the subject and not the subject itself. This is because ﴿dwell﴾ is an imperative verb, and the subject of an imperative verb cannot appear explicitly, since it is obligatorily concealed (mustatir). On this basis, ﴿you﴾ is a detached pronoun serving as an emphasis of the attached pronoun. As for His words ﴿and your wife﴾, she is Eve, as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari and elsewhere.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3330, 3399) and Muslim (1470/62, 63) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with the wording: "Had it not been for Eve, a woman would never have betrayed her husband." ?.?]]

As for His words ﴿the Garden﴾, the scholars have differed. First, the Garden (jannah) is a garden abounding in trees, and it was so named because it is concealed by its trees.

Is the intended meaning of "the Garden" the Garden of Eternity, or is it a garden other than the Garden of Eternity? The apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the Sunnah is that it is the Garden of Eternity, and not merely a garden; that is, not simply a garden abounding in trees, with sweet waters and pleasant air. No, it is the Garden of Eternity, because the definite article here is for mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni). As for His words ﴿and eat from it freely wherever you wish﴾: ﴿from it﴾ means from this Garden; ﴿freely﴾ means eating that is pleasant and free of any disturbance; ﴿wherever you wish﴾ means in any place within this Garden. We also say: and at any time, because ﴿eat from it﴾ is an unrestricted action, not limited by time. So they may eat from any place and at any time.

﴿But do not approach this tree﴾. Allah pointed to the tree as ﴿this tree﴾, and He did not say "a tree such-and-such" or "such-and-such a tree." Rather, He indicated it specifically, and the definite article in "the tree" is for presential reference (al-'ahd al-huduri), because whatever comes with the definite article after a demonstrative is for presential reference, since the demonstrative signifies pointing to something near. Is there any benefit for us in identifying its species? No. For this reason Allah did not specify it in the Qur'an, nor did the Prophet ﷺ specify it in the Sunnah. ﴿Or you will be among the wrongdoers﴾: the verb is ﴿you will be﴾ (takuna), and it was not said "fa-takunani" (you two will be), because it is the answer to a demand, which is His words ﴿do not approach﴾. So the fa here indicates causation, and the verb following it is in the subjunctive by an implied "an" after the fa of causation. It has also been said that the verb is in the subjunctive by the fa itself. The first view belongs to the Basrans and the second to the Kufans. The second is the one we choose, based on the rule that whenever grammarians differ over the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of a word or a clause, we adopt the easier, provided the meaning allows it.

﴿Or you will be among the wrongdoers﴾. The wrongdoer (zalim) is the transgressor, because the root of injustice (zulm) is deficiency. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce and did not fall short therein at all﴾ [al-Kahf 33]. Injustice occurs in one of two ways: either by neglecting an obligation or by excess in it, or by violating what is forbidden. The intended meaning here is the violation of what is forbidden; that is, if you do it, then you two are wrongdoers, because you have disobeyed Allah.

In this noble verse there is an affirmation that speech belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. From where do we derive this?

**Student:** ﴿And We said, "O Adam"﴾.

**Shaykh:** It also contains evidence that Allah's speech is with an audible voice and sequenced letters. From where is this derived? From His words ﴿O Adam, dwell﴾, and had Adam not heard it, there would be no benefit in it.

Also, it is sequenced, because He said ﴿O Adam, dwell, you and your wife﴾, and this is the sequencing of letters: ﴿O﴾, ﴿Adam﴾, ﴿dwell﴾, ﴿you﴾, ﴿and your wife﴾, ﴿the Garden﴾. We say this because some people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah) claim that Allah's speech is not sequenced, and that His words ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [al-Fatihah 1] came out all at once; that is, the sin, the ba and the mim came out together, unsequenced. These people are called the Iqtiraniyyah (the "Conjunctionists"), who say that Allah's speech is some of it conjoined with some of it, because they claim that if we affirmed its sequencing and that some of it precedes some of it, it would follow that it is originated (hadith). And, as you know, their principle is that an originated thing can only subsist in an originated thing. We have explained many times that this principle is false.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the favor of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon Adam and Eve, in that He settled them in the Garden from the very beginning of their creation.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the legitimacy of marriage for the children of Adam, from His words ﴿dwell, you and your wife﴾. This is the Sunnah of our father Adam. If someone asks: "Whose daughter was his wife?" We say: she was created from his rib; Allah created her from his rib. If someone says: "Then she would be his daughter, so how could he marry his daughter?"

The answer: Allah, the Exalted, may decree whatever He wills. Allah may decree whatever He wills. Just as it was permissible for a brother to marry his sister among the first children of Adam, so too it was permissible for Adam to marry one whom Allah created from his rib, and Allah, the Exalted, judges as He wills.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the command comes for permissibility. From His words – what? – ﴿And eat from it﴾; this is for permissibility, as evidenced by His words ﴿wherever you wish﴾, as He gave them the choice to eat from any place. There is no doubt that a command may come for permissibility, but its default is that it is a demand, until evidence establishes that it is for permissibility.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the apparent meaning of the text is that the fruits of the Garden have no limited time, but are available at all times. From where is this derived? From ﴿wherever you wish﴾: generality in place necessitates generality in time. Allah, the Exalted, said regarding the fruits of the Garden: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 32–33].

Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah, the Exalted, may test a servant by forbidding him something to which his soul may be attached; from His words ﴿But do not approach this tree﴾. The reasoning: had the soul not been attached to it, there would have been no need to prohibit approaching it.

Also among them: one may be forbidden to approach a thing while the intended meaning is performing the act directly, for the sake of emphasizing the warning against it. Allah's words ﴿do not approach this tree﴾ mean: do not eat from it. But since approaching it may lead to eating, approaching it was forbidden.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: a person should leave undefined what Allah left undefined. The proof: had Allah wanted us to believe in a specific tree, then the proper conduct with Allah would be to leave undefined what He left undefined and to specify what He specified.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of causes. From where is this derived? From His words ﴿And do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers﴾.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that disobedience to Allah, the Exalted, is injustice, an injustice to oneself and a transgression against it, from His words ﴿And do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 36:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So the Shaytan caused them to slip from it﴾. In another reading: ﴿So the Shaytan caused them to depart from it﴾ (fa-azalahuma / fa-azalahuma). The difference between them is that ﴿azallahuma﴾ means he caused them to fall into error (zalal), and ﴿azalahuma﴾ means he removed them. On the first reading, the Shaytan caused them to err, so they slipped from it and were expelled from it. On the second reading, the meaning is: he removed them, that is, he was the cause of their being removed.

﴿The Shaytan caused them to slip﴾: which Shaytan is meant? The apparent answer is the Shaytan who refused to prostrate to Adam. He wanted to mislead them so that they would be like him in disobeying Allah.

﴿The Shaytan caused them to slip from it﴾: from it, meaning from the Garden or from the tree?

* The students: From the Garden.

* The Shaykh: From the Garden. That is why He says: ﴿so He removed them from that in which they had been﴾, removed them from that in which they had been of bounty, because they were in the best of places, a garden, and they were permitted to eat from wherever they wished, yet the Shaytan expelled them from what they were in.

﴿And We said﴾, that is, Allah said to them: ﴿Go down, some of you to others an enemy, and for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾. ﴿Go down﴾ is addressed in the plural, and He did not say "go down" (in the dual). Who was joined with Adam and his wife? The Shaytan. That is why He says: ﴿some of you to others an enemy﴾.

﴿And We said: Go down, some of you to others an enemy﴾: who is the enemy of whom? The Shaytan is an enemy to Adam and Eve.

﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾: meaning, you will settle on the earth and enjoy it with the bounties Allah has given you, but not permanently; rather ﴿for a time﴾, which is the establishing of the Hour.

There are benefits in the verse. First: caution against falling into error, which the Shaytan incites; from His saying: ﴿so the Shaytan caused them to slip from it﴾.

One of its benefits, when combined with another verse: the Shaytan deceives the children of Adam as he deceived their father. The Shaytan did not find it easy to say to them, "Do not eat from this tree," but rather he lured them with deception: ﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors"﴾ [al-A'raf 21], and he said: ﴿O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾. So he brought the things that would entice them to eat from the tree. Therefore a person should beware of the whisperings of the Shaytan. The Shaytan may come to a person and whisper to him, making the sin seem small in his eyes; then if it is a major sin and he cannot make it seem small, he promises him that he will repent from it, so that it becomes easy for him to undertake it. Either way, beware of your enemy, beware of your enemy lest he deceive you.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the Shaytan is an enemy to the human being; from His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿some of you to others an enemy﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the Shaytan is eager to remove good from the children of Adam and to cast them into evil. Among this: the Shaytan casts into the heart of a person sorrow, worry and grief, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Secret conversation is only from the Shaytan, that he may grieve those who believe, but it will not harm them at all, except by permission of Allah﴾ [al-Mujadila 10]. Here He says: ﴿removed them from that in which they had been﴾, from bounty to what they would not find that in.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the speech of Allah the Exalted may be legislative (shar'i) and may be decreed (kawni). His saying: ﴿O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it﴾ is legislative. His saying: ﴿And We said: Go down, some of you to others﴾ is apparently decreed (kawni), because He, glorified and exalted, knows that if the matter had returned to them they would not have descended. But this is a decreed statement. It is possible that it is a legislative statement, but the closer view in my opinion is that it is a decreed statement, and Allah knows best.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the Garden is in a high place. From where is this taken?

* The students: From His saying: ﴿Go down﴾.

* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿Go down﴾, and descent is from a higher place to a lower one.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the Shaytan was with them in the Garden; from His saying: ﴿Go down, some of you to others an enemy﴾. Consider this benefit: is it correct or not?

* A student: It is not correct.

* A student: It is correct.

* A student: It is possible.

* The Shaykh: It may be said: ﴿Go down﴾ means from the heaven, from the Garden with respect to Adam and Eve, and from the heaven with respect to the Shaytan. It is also possible that the Shaytan entered the Garden as a test, in order to mislead our parents.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: it is not possible for the children of Adam to live except on the earth. They cannot live except on the earth; from His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾. This is supported by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought out﴾ [al-A'raf 25]. Based on this, we know that the attempt of the disbelievers to live somewhere other than the earth, whether on some of the planets or in some vehicles, is an attempt that will achieve nothing, because their settlement must be the earth.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: there is no permanence for the children of Adam in this world; from His saying: ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance﴾. (Talaqqa) means that he took, accepted and was pleased with words from Allah the Exalted. In another reading: ﴿Then there reached Adam from his Lord words﴾, so the agent here is the words. What are these words? The words are His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [al-A'raf 23]. So the words are the acknowledgment of Adam and Eve that they had sinned and wronged themselves, and their humble supplication to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that if He does not forgive them and have mercy on them, they would be among the losers.

* A student: O Shaykh, does it follow from the creation of Eve from Adam's rib that she is from him?

* The Shaykh: That she is from him?

* The student: From himself?

* The Shaykh: From where was she created?

* The student: From his rib.

* The Shaykh: That is, from him. The Messenger ﷺ said about Fatimah: "She is a part of me" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3714, 3729) and Muslim (2449/93, 94), from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah]. But she is not like the creation of the children of Adam; that is, she was created from gushing water, created in a manner that Allah knows best.

* A student: We have said here that ﴿Go down﴾ is a command to Adam, Eve and the Shaytan. In Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿He said: Go down﴾ [Ta-Ha 123]. What is your view?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, this supports that the address in ﴿Go down﴾ was directed to the Shaytan: with respect to the Shaytan, from the heaven; with respect to Adam and Eve, from the Garden.

* A student: What is najwa (secret conversation)?

* The Shaykh: Najwa is private speech between a man and his companion. When the Prophet ﷺ or another of the Companions approached the hypocrites, they would whisper among themselves, to enrage the believer and frighten him, as if they were discussing killing him, harming him or beating him.[[See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (8/42) and al-Durr al-Manthur (14/317), which attributes this action to the Jews.]]

* A student: How can secret conversation be from the Shaytan?

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is, he is the one who inspires it; he inspires it in the one who does it.

* A student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh. Can it be understood from His saying: ﴿and a provision for a time﴾ the permissibility of what is on the earth, what Allah created on the earth?

* The Shaykh: Meaning (...) the provision? Yes, it is possible, it can be derived. And in another verse that is more explicit: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah 29].

* A student: How was the Shaytan able to whisper to Adam and Eve while they were in the Garden, when he is cast out from Allah's mercy?

* The Shaykh: If we say that His saying ﴿Go down from it﴾ means from the Garden, then he was with them, and if we say that he was not with them in the Garden, then it is possible that he whispered to them even from afar. Is it not possible that a person is in his house while a man in the street addresses him and speaks to him privately?

* A student: Was the Shaytan visible, so that Adam and Eve could see him?

* The Shaykh: How?

* The student: Could Adam and Eve see the Shaytan?

* The Shaykh: It is evident, and the apparent view, and Allah knows best, is that he was seeing them. He certainly sees them, but the apparent view is that they were seeing him.

* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah bless you, what is the validity of the saying of some that Adam was created without a father or a mother, that Eve was created without a mother, and that Jesus, peace be upon him, was created without a father? Is this saying correct?

* The Shaykh: Correct. Adam was created from clay, with neither father nor mother; Eve from a father without a mother; and Jesus from a mother without a father.

* A student: May Allah be good to you. We all know that Adam, Eve, and the Messenger ﷺ entered the Garden before the Hereafter. Were there other prophets and messengers besides them who entered the Garden?

* The Shaykh: We do not know. I do not know.

* A student: Shaykh, what is your view of those who say, based on: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis﴾, that the exception here indicates that Iblis was among the angels?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. We respond to this by saying that Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord﴾. And he was among the angels, that is, he was among them, with them, but his element differs from theirs. That is why he returned to his own element, which is fire, and they returned to their element, which is that they were created from light.

* A student: In the explanation of His saying: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾, is this preceded by (...)?

* The Shaykh: What is the difficulty meant?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: When He said: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3], and the disbelievers... does anyone recall the verse before it?

* The student: ﴿Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me﴾.

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is a good difficulty. He says: ﴿Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me﴾. The fa' is undoubtedly connective and shows that what follows is a consequence of what precedes. So how did He forbid fearing them when He had informed that they had despaired? What is the answer? Did you not understand the difficulty?

* A student: That they have despaired, but they have not despaired of attempting to turn the Muslims away.

* The Shaykh: The apparent meaning is that they have despaired of your religion and considered it unlikely that you would turn away from it. But if they come at you again, do not fear them in this matter. This is what appears, but Allah knows best.

Student: "Indeed, He is the Oft-Returning, the Most Merciful." (37) We said: "Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve." (38) "But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever." (39) "O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you, and fulfill My covenant, I will fulfill your covenant, and fear Me alone." (40) "And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you, and do not be the first to disbelieve in it. And do not exchange My verses for a small price, and fear Me alone." (41) "And do not mix the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth while you know." (42) [Al-Baqarah 37-42].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾. (Talaqqa) means: he took, when Allah cast these words to him; he accepted and received them. These words are His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [Al-A'raf 23]. His saying ﴿from his Lord﴾: this contains the attribution of lordship to Adam, which is the special lordship. His saying ﴿and He accepted his repentance﴾: the doer is who? Allah, meaning his Lord accepted his repentance. ﴿Indeed, He is the Oft-Returning, the Most Merciful.﴾ Repentance is: the lifting of blame and pardoning the sinner when he returns to his Lord, mighty and majestic. ﴿Indeed, He is the Oft-Returning, the Most Merciful﴾: this sentence is a reason (ta'lil) for His saying ﴿He accepted his repentance﴾, because this is what these two great names require: ﴿the Oft-Returning, the Most Merciful﴾. His saying ﴿He is the Oft-Returning﴾: "He" is a pronoun of separation (damir fasl), which conveys restriction (hasr), and what else? And emphasis (tawkid). Here we do not say: separation between the predicate and the attribute, because what precedes the attribute, or what precedes what may be an attribute, is a pronoun, and the grammarians say that a pronoun is neither described nor used to describe. Therefore we derive from the pronoun of separation here only two benefits: emphasis and restriction.

His saying ﴿At-Tawwab﴾ is an intensive form (sigha mubalaghah) from "tab" (he repented), and that is due to the great frequency of Allah the Mighty and Majestic accepting repentance from His servants. How much Allah accepts repentance from us, upon every individual of us, and how much repentance there is considering the number of those who repent. For this reason Allah named Himself At-Tawwab.

Know that Allah the Exalted has two kinds of repentance toward the servant: the first repentance is before the servant's repentance, and it is: granting success (tawfiq) to repent; the second repentance is: accepting the repentance, meaning that He grants the servant success to repent, so he repents, and Allah accepts his repentance. Both are in the Qur'an. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And [He forgave] the three who were left behind, until the earth, for all its vastness, closed in on them, and their souls confined them, and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so they might repent﴾ [At-Tawbah 118]: He turned (taba) so that they might repent (liyatubu). So this is the first repentance: the repentance of granting success to repent, and "liyatubu" means: that they might repent to Allah, and then Allah accepts their repentance as acceptance.

As for the repentance of acceptance, it is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons evil deeds﴾ [Ash-Shura 25]. So "At-Tawwab" is an intensive form from "tab", and Allah's repentance (toward servants) has two types or kinds: the first: granting success for repentance, and the second: accepting repentance, and both are in the great Qur'an.

﴿Ar-Rahim﴾ means: the possessor of wide mercy that reaches whomever He wills of His servants. On this basis, Ar-Rahman is included within Ar-Rahim, because when Ar-Rahman is mentioned alone, or Ar-Rahim alone, one of them enters within the other; and if both are mentioned together, Ar-Rahman refers to the attribute and Ar-Rahim refers to the act.

From the benefits of this noble verse: the favor of Allah, glorified be He, and exalted, upon our father Adam when He granted him success in these words by which repentance was made; due to His saying: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾.

* And from its benefits: that Allah's favor upon our father is in reality a favor upon us, because every person feels that if Allah bestows favor upon one of his ancestors, He has bestowed favor upon him.

And from the benefits of this noble verse: that the statement of a person: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [Al-A'raf 23] is a cause for Allah's acceptance of His servant's repentance.

And in it, i.e., in ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾, there are kinds of tawassul (seeking a means): the first is tawassul by lordship; the second: tawassul by the servant's state, ﴿we have wronged ourselves﴾; the third state: entrusting the matter to Allah; and the fourth: perhaps he says ﴿we will surely be among the losers﴾ as well. In it is mention of the servant if he is not forgiven, and so it is tawassul.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah the Exalted speaks with an audible voice. How is that? Words were received from Him, and receiving words is only through hearing a voice, and this is what Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah hold: that Allah the Exalted speaks with speech that is heard, with an audible voice and readable letters.

And from the benefits of this noble verse: the favor of Allah, mighty and majestic, upon Adam by accepting repentance; so in that there are two favors: the first, granting success for repentance, in that words were received from Allah; and the second, acceptance of repentance, where He said: ﴿Then He accepted his repentance﴾.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that when a person is sincere in entrusting the matter to Allah and returns to obedience to Allah, Allah the Exalted accepts his repentance. This has many evidences, that Allah is more generous than His servant: "Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I draw near to him a cubit; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running" [Agreed upon. al-Bukhari (7405), and Muslim (2675/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah]. So the generosity of Allah, mighty and majestic, is higher and more complete than the generosity of a human being.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of these two noble names: At-Tawwab and Ar-Rahim.

And from the benefits of this noble verse: the specialty of Allah with repentance and mercy, by the evidence of the pronoun of separation; but what is meant is His specialty with the repentance that no one else can grant, not with every repentance, because a person may repent to his servant, his son, his nation, and the like; but the repentance that none can grant except Allah, which is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ [Al 'Imran 135], that is specific to Allah. Likewise, the mercy meant is the mercy that exists only with Allah; as for the mercy of creatures toward one another, this is established and is not restricted to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Those who show mercy, the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman) will have mercy on them" [Abu Dawud (4941), and at-Tirmidhi (1924), who said: hasan sahih, and Ahmad (6494), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As].

Then the Most High said: ﴿We said: "Go down from it, all of you"﴾. ﴿Go down﴾: the waw (و) indicates the plural. Is the intended meaning the plural, or the dual, based on the view that the least plural is two? The scholars differ: is the least plural two, or three? Whoever says the least plural is two says the intended ones here are Adam and Eve alone. Whoever says the least plural is three says: Adam, Eve and Iblis, because Iblis, although he was not in the Garden, had been expelled from it when he refused to prostrate to Adam, yet he was around it, whispering to them and speaking to them. So it was said to them all: ﴿Go down from it, all of you﴾. Is there in the Qur'an "ihbita" (اهبطا) with an alif? Yes: "ihbita", and this supports that the waw here indicates only two: ﴿Go down from it, both of you﴾ [Ta-Ha 123], meaning the two of them, and it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the waw in ﴿Go down﴾.

﴿So if there comes to you from Me guidance﴾: "imma" originally is (in ma), where "in" is the conditional particle and "ma" is an added particle for emphasis. And ﴿ya'tiyannakum﴾ is also a verb emphasized with the energetic nun (nun al-tawkid), and for that reason it was not jussive but was built on what? 

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Why? Because it is joined to the energetic nun, both verbally and in its underlying form. ﴿So if there comes to you from Me guidance, then whoever follows My guidance﴾: "guidance" here means knowledge, namely by the revelation that Allah sends to His prophets and messengers. ﴿Then whoever follows﴾: the fa' here links the response to the conditional. The clause after the fa' is the response of the condition; is the clause after the fa' here nominal or verbal? Nominal. In ﴿whoever follows﴾, "man" is conditional and "tabi'a" is the conditional verb. The fa' in ﴿then there is no fear﴾ also links the response; "la" is negative and "khawf" is the subject. Notice the interlocking of conditions now.
