And His statement, the Exalted: ﴿So We sent upon those who did wrong a plague﴾, meaning: a punishment, due to His statement, the Exalted: ﴿If you remove from us the plague﴾. Pharaoh said to Musa: ﴿If you remove from us the plague, we will surely believe in you and we will surely send with you the Children of Israel﴾ [al-A'raf 134]. That is, the punishment, and it is other than ar-rijs (filth), because ar-rijs is impurity and filth, while ar-rijz is punishment.

And His statement ﴿a plague from the sky﴾ means: a punishment from it. Like what? What punishment descends from the sky? Like stones, thunderbolts, hail, and others.

* A student: Winds.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

And His statement ﴿from the sky﴾: what is meant by "sky" here is height. It does not necessarily mean the preserved sky, because everything above you is called sky, unless there is a contextual indication, such as His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling, yet they, from its signs, are turning away﴾ [al-Anbiya' 32].

He said: ﴿because they were defiantly disobedient﴾. The ba' here is for causation, meaning "because of." The ma is verbal (masdariyyah), meaning "because of their having defiantly disobeyed." When it is verbal, it has already passed with us that the verbal particle transforms what follows it from a verb, indeed from the whole clause, into a verbal noun. His statement ﴿because they were defiantly disobedient﴾: kanu (were) refers to the past, or the intended meaning is (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 60–61 (part 1 of 5):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when Moses asked for water for his people, We said: "Strike the rock with your staff," and there gushed forth from it twelve springs﴾ [al-Baqarah 60]. His words: ﴿istasqa﴾ means he asked for water to be given to him, and that was when they were in the wilderness (al-tih), or it applies in every place where there is a need for water, so he asks for water and they are given relief.

His words: ﴿Strike with your staff﴾. The staff is well known, and this staff had three great signs in it:
First: he would throw it down and it would become a crawling serpent.
Second: he would strike the rock with it and springs would gush forth.
Third: he struck the sea with it and it split apart, so that each part was like a great mountain.

His words: ﴿the rock﴾. It has been mentioned before that the correct view regarding it is that what is meant is the genus, i.e. any rock, and not a particular known rock, because this is more eloquent as a miracle and in the verse.

﴿There gushed forth from it﴾. Infijar (infijar) means opening up and splitting, and from it the word fajr (dawn) is derived, because the horizon is split by it. So the meaning of ﴿gushed forth﴾ is that these springs burst out from it.

﴿Twelve springs﴾. ﴿Springs﴾ is a tamyiz (specification) of the number, because ithnatā ʿashrah (twelve) is ambiguous, i.e. twelve of what? So he specified it by his words ﴿springs﴾. The difference between the hal (circumstantial accusative) and the tamyiz is that the tamyiz is understood as if preceded by (min, "of"), and the hal is understood as if preceded by (fi, "in"). You say, for example: "The man came riding" (rakiban), i.e. in a state of riding; and you say: "The shame broke out in sweat" (ʿaraqan), i.e. from sweat.

﴿Twelve springs﴾, i.e. twelve of the springs, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We caused springs to gush forth in it﴾ [Yasin 34]. Both of them clarify an ambiguous term, both are in the accusative, and both are indefinite, but the tamyiz clarifies the essences, while the hal clarifies the states.

The second difference: the tamyiz is understood as (min) and the hal as (fi).

﴿Twelve springs﴾ means not one spring but twelve. Why? Because the Children of Israel were twelve tribes, so each tribe had one spring.

Allah said: ﴿Each group already knew its drinking place﴾ [al-Baqarah 60], i.e. among the tribes, ﴿each group knew its drinking place﴾, the place where they drank, so that they would not mix with one another and crowd one another. This was a blessing of Allah upon them, i.e. upon the Children of Israel, and it was also a blessing of Allah upon Moses. As for the blessing upon Moses, it is because it was a sign that established him and confirmed him; and as for the blessing upon the Children of Israel, it is because it removed their thirst and parching.

The scholars said: There is no sign of the messengers except that the Messenger ﷺ has something of its kind or something greater than it. All the signs of the messengers are found for the Messenger ﷺ, of its kind or greater, but some of them happened to him personally and some happened to his followers, for the miracles (karamat) of the saints are a sign of the prophets. They said: What happened to the Messenger ﷺ regarding the gushing of springs is greater than what happened to Moses, because springs gushed forth from between his fingers, ﴿the water was gushing from between his fingers﴾ [agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (200) and Muslim (2279/4) from the hadith of Anas, with the wording: Anas said: I began to look at the water welling up from between his fingers.] like springs, while he was in a vessel, and a vessel is not customarily something from which water gushes, whereas stones customarily are such that rivers gush from them: ﴿And indeed, among stones are those from which rivers burst forth﴾ [al-Baqarah 74]. So what happened to the Messenger ﷺ became greater than what happened to Moses ﷺ.

﴿Each group already knew its drinking place. Eat and drink﴾. Is this command for permission (ibahah) or for obligation (wujub)?
* The students: For permission.
* The Shaykh: For permission. Know that what is permissible in origin may sometimes be obligatory, sometimes forbidden, sometimes recommended, and sometimes disliked; for what is permissible may be subject to the five rulings. ﴿Allah has made trade lawful﴾ [al-Baqarah 275], or not, but sale may be obligatory and may be forbidden, is it not so?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: It may be recommended and it may be disliked. So here, if we take it as permission, ﴿Eat and drink﴾ includes obligation in the case where a person fears for his own life from perishing, for then it is obligatory upon him to eat and drink. As for if we say that this command which is for obligation departs from what is other than it, of permission and other than it.

His words: ﴿from the provision of Allah﴾, i.e. from His giving, since He brought forth fruits for you and provided you with water, and did not place upon you anything that would diminish you.

﴿And do not commit abuse on the earth, causing corruption﴾. Because the reality of the matter is that the one upon whom Allah bestows provision in eating and drinking must, in return for that, do what? We say:
* The students: Thanks.
* The Shaykh: Gratitude, which is righteousness and reform. Therefore He said: ﴿do not commit abuse on the earth﴾. The meaning of ﴿do not commit abuse﴾ is do not walk about as corrupters. The ʿathw or ʿathiyy means corruption, hastening in corruption. Hence we say: his words ﴿causing corruption﴾ is a hal from the waw in His words ﴿do not commit abuse﴾, emphasizing its governing verb, emphasizing its governing verb. How is it emphasizing its governing verb? Because ʿathw or ʿithiyy means corruption, so this hal is emphatic, meaning: do not corrupt, causing corruption.

His words: ﴿do not commit abuse on the earth, causing corruption﴾. By what does the corruption of the earth occur? By sins. The corruption of the earth occurs through sins, due to His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾ [al-Rum 41]. This indicates that corruption on earth happens through sins, and that the responsibility for corruption on earth, whether wars, trials, earthquakes, famine, drought, or illness, lies with whom? With the people of sin. They are the cause and they are the ill omen upon the children of Adam, because Allah says: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth; but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾ [al-A'raf 96]. So no calamity befalls except through sin: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura 30]. This provision of Allah that they received, in eating and drinking, was something they should have thanked Allah for, should have persisted in His obedience, should have kept away from corruption, and should have begun reform. But what happened?

﴿And when you said: "O Moses, we will not endure one kind of food"﴾ [al-Baqarah 61]. Manna and quails are among the best foods, the most beneficial for the body, and the most pleasant in taste, and among the finest that could be. But the Children of Israel, because of their baseness, did not endure this. They said: ﴿we will not endure one kind of food﴾; we do not want only manna and quails, we want varied foods. But these foods, compared to the foods that they were provided, are inferior; base in comparison to them, meaning they are not noble, exalted, or high, but are considered very inferior in comparison to this.

They said: ﴿we will not endure one kind of food﴾. If someone says: "One kind of food" — but they were two foods, manna and quails? We say: manna is usually used for drink, soaked in water and drunk; or it is said: the meaning of "food" here is the genus, i.e. we do not endure this genus, since we have nothing but manna and quails, and there are other things besides them.

﴿So call upon your Lord for us﴾. This is a tawassul on their part through Moses, that he should supplicate Allah the Mighty and Majestic for them: ﴿So call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth grows﴾. The words ﴿call upon your Lord for us﴾ indicate great rudeness on their part. They did not say "call upon our Lord" or "call upon Allah"; rather they said "call upon your Lord for us," as if they were disassociated from Him, and Allah forbid. This was from their foolishness, arrogance, and pride.

﴿Bring forth for us﴾: "bring forth" is in the jussive mood; what is it that makes it jussive?
* The students: The response to the imperative (jawab al-talab).
* The Shaykh: The response to the imperative. "Call (ud'u), He will bring forth (yukhrij)": as if they were saying: by merely your supplication, this thing will come forth; therefore they made it a response to the imperative.

﴿Bring forth for us from what the earth grows﴾. We do not want what descends from heaven, manna and quails; we do not desire it. They were earthly, not heavenly: ﴿Bring forth for us from what the earth grows﴾, and we do not want what descends from the sky.

His words: ﴿from its herbs﴾. "From its herbs": first, the min in "from" (min al-ula): what is its meaning? In ﴿Bring forth for us from what﴾, min is for the beginning (ibtida'); meaning the starting point of bringing forth, and the place from which it comes forth is what the earth grows.

His words: ﴿from its herbs﴾: the min here is min bayaniyyah (explanatory), explaining what? The relative pronoun (ma), because the relative pronoun is ambiguous and needs clarification. ﴿from what the earth grows, from its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions﴾ — these are unfamiliar words. ﴿from its herbs﴾: al-baql is the plant that has no stem, like the greens and the like; this is al-baql.

﴿Its garlic﴾: it is garlic; it is said: thum, and it is said: fum. It is said that al-fum is wheat, but the first view is closer, that what is meant by fum is garlic. ﴿Its lentils﴾: lentils, I think, are well known.
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Their lentils are well known. ﴿Its onions﴾ are also well known.

﴿Its cucumbers﴾: also, qiththa' is well known, the small melons, the jarawa; all of these, compared to manna and quails, are nothing. Therefore Moses ﷺ rebuked them, saying: ﴿Would you exchange that which is lower for that which is better?﴾. The meaning of ﴿exchange﴾ (tastabdilun) is that you take a substitute; you substitute one thing for another, you take it in its place. "You exchange": you take a substitute. What do you take? ﴿That which is lower﴾ you exchange it ﴿for that which is better﴾.

Regarding His words ﴿that which is lower﴾: what is meant by "that which is lower"?
* The students: The thing they asked for.
* The Shaykh: The garlic, which they asked for. ﴿From its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions﴾: five things; this is what is lower. ﴿For that which is better﴾: manna and quails.

Regarding His words ﴿that which is lower﴾: what is your opinion on omitting the first part of the relative clause here? Perhaps we should go back to grammar and see whether it is permissible or not?
* A student: It is permissible, yes, it is permissible.
* The Shaykh: Is it permissible? Frequently?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Wrong.
* A student: It is not permissible.
* The Shaykh: It is not permissible except rarely, because the relative clause is not long.
* A student: And the relative pronoun is other than "ayy."
* The Shaykh: Yes, the relative pronoun is other than "ayy," and Ibn Malik says:
......................... And in this omission, "ayyan" other than "ayyin" follows,
If the connection is lengthened, and if it is not lengthened, then omission is rare...
And likewise also: ﴿for that which is better﴾; if you say "bi-lladhi khayrun," this would be rare, and of course this usage is not permissible in the Qur'an whatever the case, whether the attribute is lengthened or not; but in other than the Qur'an, yes.

﴿That which is lower in exchange for that which is better﴾: exchanging that which is lower for that which is better; what indicates its exchange?
* A student: Foolishness.
* The Shaykh: It indicates foolishness and debasement, like a person to whom you offer a cup of milk and he says: "By God, I desire a cigarette." This is the situation of those who smoke tobacco, may Allah grant us well-being. A good, clean drink is offered to him and he says: "No, I want a cigarette."

So the sum is that these matters show that exchanging the lower for that which is better indicates, in reality, the foolishness and debasement of a person; and just as this occurs with tangible things, it also occurs with abstract and intellectual matters, that a person goes to choose base morals and dealings and the like, and leaves what is better. This is an error. Yes, if it were assumed that the person found nothing other than this, and nothing else was possible, would he be blamed or not?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: He is not blamed. He is not blamed if the thing is something permitted to him, even if it is lower. But that there is something higher than what you were upon, and you seek it and leave this, there is no doubt that this is foolishness. For this reason Lot ﷺ said to his people: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives? Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾ [al-Shu'ara 165-166]. Moses ﷺ said to them: ﴿Go down to a city﴾, meaning this does not need that he should supplicate Allah; and it seems Moses ﷺ rebuked them for this and made clear to them that this is not fitting for Moses ﷺ to supplicate Allah the Exalted for them with this supplication. As for the saying of some exegetes that he supplicated and it was said to him: "Tell them to go down to a city, for they will have what they asked," this is not correct; for how would he rebuke them for asking that and then he would go and supplicate Allah for it? This is something impossible and far-fetched. The correct view is that Moses rebuked them for what they asked and rejected it from them, and said to them: this matter you asked for is not difficult; the whole world is filled with it. Therefore he said: ﴿Go down to a city﴾. "Misr" — is it Misr, the Nile (Egypt), or other than it?
* The students: Other than it.
* The Shaykh: Misr of the Nile?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: But we say: no, therefore it is indefinite (nukkirat), and Misr of the Nile is not made indefinite; it is not declined, Misr of the Nile is not declined, nor is it declined from it. But "misran" here is declined now; meaning: go down to any city among the cities, you will find that.

﴿For you will have what you asked﴾: meaning this is not something rare, but go to any city among the cities and you will find it. What is missing among the causes for non-declension (ghayr al-sarf) here in the word "misran"?
* A student: The meaning.
* Another student: The definiteness.
* The Shaykh: Yes, definiteness, because this is indefinite, this is indefinite; and the names of lands have the features of proper nouns (ʿalamiyyah) and feminine gender. Here there is — yes, we may say: there is the feminine, because "Misr" is the singular of amsar; and we may not say it is feminine, we may say it is masculine. ﴿For you will have what you asked﴾.

* Student: Shaykh, this: ﴿its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic﴾ [al-Baqarah 61] — was the first of these known to them, or, I mean, was it Moses?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is apparent; it is apparent that they knew these things, that they know from what the earth grows these items.
* Student: Fum instead of ful (fava beans)?
* The Shaykh: Ful? I do not know, but the closest thing is that it is garlic, thum with the thaʾ; and it may be said: ful, because it is close to lentils, close to this.
* Student: Al-baql, Shaykh, al-baql is the fava bean that is eaten...
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: Like the green beans, the things you put in water and they swell up; that is the baql that is in the market currently...
* The Shaykh: This is a terminology.

He said: ﴿And humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them﴾. "Were stamped upon them": now look, there is a shift in address (iltifat): ﴿And when you said: "O Moses, we will not endure one kind of food"﴾ up to the end.

Then He said: ﴿And they were stamped with humiliation and poverty﴾. So the speech is now a new sentence, a report from Allah the Exalted about the Children of Israel that humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them.

﴿Humiliation (al-dhilla)﴾: this is in courage; they are humble (adhilla), they do not face an enemy, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿They will not fight you all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls﴾ [al-Hashr 14]. And poverty (maskana) refers back to need; so they have no courage and they have no wealth, neither generosity with wealth nor generosity with the self. First, courage: what is it? Generosity with what?
* The students: With the self.
* The Shaykh: With the self: a person gives his self freely to raise the word of Allah; and generosity (karam) is giving of wealth. They, may Allah forbid, did not attain either of these; rather the opposite: humiliation was stamped upon them, so there is no courage among them, and poverty, so there is no giving among them. For this reason there is no nation poorer than the Jews, or rather poorer in heart, not in wealth. Wealth is abundant among them, but their hearts are poor; and this is what caused wealth to be plentiful among them, because they are still, like a fire in dry firewood, consuming and consuming. They were described with this description: it was stamped upon them.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 60–61 (part 2 of 5):**

His words: ﴿Humiliation was stamped upon them﴾. This is of the type that they call the implicit metaphor (al-isti'ara al-makniyya), if it is correct to say that there is figurative usage (majaz) in the speech. It is as if He made them like the blank coin (al-sikka al-niqt) upon which the stamp (al-taba') is struck. So this humiliation and destitution are as if they have become a stamp upon them that does not leave them, just as the stamp does not leave the coin. The coin here means gold and silver, the dinar and the dirham, which are stamped with a stamp. For this reason it is said: "the dirham was struck" and "the dinar was struck," meaning it was struck with the stamp by which it is sealed. Every state stamps its currency with whatever it deems suitable for its policy. So this humiliation, may Allah protect us, is struck upon them, and likewise the destitution.

If someone says: "The reality now is contrary to this." We say: it is not possible for reality to contradict the words of Allah and His Messenger. The error lies in what?

* The student: In the understanding.
* The Shaykh: In the understanding and the conception. Otherwise, the word of Allah is not broken. The reports cannot differ; the report of Allah and His Messenger is true. We say: this verse is unrestricted (mutlaq). In His saying, the Exalted, in Al 'Imran: ﴿Humiliation was stamped upon them wherever they are found, except with a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 112], it restricts this verse, so that it becomes: ﴿Humiliation and destitution were stamped upon them﴾ [al-Baqara 61], except with a rope from Allah and a rope from the people. So when Allah connects them, or the people connect them, the humiliation departs from them and courage and strength come to them. Have you understood?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: What is the rope from Allah? It has been said: it is Islam. And the rope from the people is that people other than the Jews support them with what they support them with. The Jews existing now are in a rope from the people, who support them, and they are the Christians. The Christians support them everywhere, because Allah says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another﴾ [al-Ma'ida 51]. This is a report, a report from Allah that does not fail. The Christians support them from all the regions of the world, either openly or secretly, either directly or indirectly.

As for the rope from Allah, we have said that it is Islam, as many scholars have mentioned. But it is possible in my view that it is more general than Islam, because when they embrace Islam, the description of Judaism departs from them and they become among the Muslims. However, in my view, it is a rope from Allah that Allah may empower them over others as a punishment for them. They may be empowered over others and have dominance, as a punishment upon the others, so that perhaps they will return to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is especially so if they are from the nation of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and they disobey and deviate from this religion, for then Allah empowers over them whomever He wills of His creation, so that perhaps they will return. This is a matter that is the reality. If we look at those who have made themselves in the service of these Jews, namely the Arabs, we would find most of them astray, especially those among them who hold leadership, deviating from the truth. Indeed, the matter may reach in some of them the point of absolute disbelief, may Allah protect us. Therefore, these people are empowered over them, and what happens happens.

And if you see that the Messenger, peace be upon him, at Hunayn, the defeat befell the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, because of self-admiration, and the defeat befell them at Uhud because of disobedience. And if you apply the matter to our situation now, you will find that both of these traits exist in those who have given their chests to the Jews: self-admiration and opposition to the command. To the extent that a certain person told me, when I heard of the Six-Day War, I began to weep, saying: an announcer among the Arab announcers was boasting, saying: "We will do, we will do," and the Jews, two days later, were carrying their bags to the sea, and tomorrow Umm Kulthum will be singing in Tel Aviv. Look at what this is! The reward of a blessing is gratitude for the blessing, and disobedience toward the Bestower! I seek refuge in Allah! This boasting, this arrogance, this haughtiness, and this self-admiration did not occur among the Companions with the best of creation. It did not occur, nor half of it, nor a quarter of it, nor anything of it worth mentioning. They only said: «We will not be defeated today because of few numbers»[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (1943) from the hadith of al-Rabi' ibn Anas as a mursal report.]], and what happened, happened. Likewise, the act of disobedience that occurred at Uhud was also a simple act of disobedience, and they also departed from their positions under an interpretation (ta'wil). Is that not so?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: They said: now the defeat has befallen the polytheists, and the Muslims have prevailed, and there is no benefit except that we go and collect the spoils. The matter became that the horsemen came upon them from behind, and what happened happened by the decree, the predestination, and the wisdom of Allah. One act of disobedience. So how are these many acts of disobedience now? Do some of the leaders of those who have given their chests to the Jews think that the rule by the Shari'a of Allah has been delayed and is backwardness, I seek refuge in Allah? How then will they be given victory over the Jews?

So the point is that we say: I see that His saying, the Exalted: ﴿except with a rope from Allah﴾ is not Islam, because Islam in reality removes them from Judaism and places them among the best of nations. Rather, what is meant is a rope from Allah, a means that becomes a victory for them so that He empowers them over whomever He wills of His servants. Otherwise, Allah says to the Messenger, peace be upon him, addressing the believers, not addressing one who says: "I am a Muslim."

﴿They will not fight you all except within fortified towns or from behind walls﴾ [al-Hashr 14]. Now they fight us from above our heads and over our walls, is that not so?

* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: This is the reality. Because the address in His saying: ﴿They will not fight you﴾ is to those who are characterized by what the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) were upon. It is not merely until now. Indeed, the reality, unfortunately, is that we do not fight them with Islam. With what do we fight them?

* The students: With Arabism.
* The Shaykh: With Arabism and nationalism. They fight with a religion, but a false one, because they say: "This is a holy land, the land of the prophets, we want to reclaim it from these usurping Arabs, according to their claim."

This is a difference between this and that. Even though their religion is false and is nothing, they come with a religious characteristic. As for us, we have abandoned the religious characteristic and gone to a characteristic by which we will never be victorious. We are not made victorious as Arabs, because we are Arabs. We are made victorious because we are believers: ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾ [al-Rum 47]. Not the Arabs will be helped; the believers will be helped. It is strange that some people say: "Yes, it was truly incumbent to help the believers, but the believers in their cause, not the believers in their religion." The believers in the cause do not know that the believer in a cause, after all, is also the Kremlin, the White House, and the palace of Britain in London. All of them believe in their causes. Is it then incumbent upon Allah to help them?

* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: Never. Far is He, glorified and exalted. Rather, the help of the believers is in Him, glorified and exalted, and in His messengers and His books, those who apply His Shari'a. This is what Allah has made incumbent upon Himself, that He help them: ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾.

So the confusion regarding His saying: ﴿Humiliation and destitution were stamped upon them﴾ is removed. Why do we see them now in this state, while the verse is a report from Allah, and the report of Allah is true and certain and cannot be contradicted?

The answer: this verse is restricted by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Humiliation was stamped upon them wherever they are found, except with a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾. Look at the restriction in Al 'Imran. The restriction is only on the humiliation. But the destitution is not restricted. For this reason, destitution is stamped upon them wherever they are. They cannot spend a single piastre except while hoping to obtain a dirham in return, never. If the Jewish societies give donations, all of this is for an aim that they see will return to them with more than what they spent. Otherwise they would not spend anything. So the destitution is unrestricted, and the humiliation is restricted: ﴿except with a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 112].

* The student: Among the humiliation and destitution, there was a Jew who went to Damietta and paid one qirsh, the tariffa as we say, and he said to him: "Uncle, I want to dine, and amuse myself, and feed the donkey." Truly, this is not merely clowning.

* The Shaykh: He dines?!

* The student: He dines, amuses himself, and feeds the donkey.

* The students: "Amuses himself" means he amuses himself.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* The student: So the Damietta man went out and proved smarter than him. He went and brought him a watermelon, from which he himself dined, and the other took its seeds to amuse himself with, and gave its rind to the donkey. So he said: "By Allah, I will not spend the night in this town," because the town... Indeed, this is a common saying among us, truly, meaning the Jews.

* The Shaykh: In any case, this matter was related about them. He said: ﴿And they returned with anger from Allah﴾. They returned.

* The student: ﴿They will not fight you all﴾ [al-Hashr 14]. The address is to the Jews?

* The Shaykh: Yes. No, the address is to the believers. That is, if we had true faith, the Jews would never have been able to confront us, they could not.

* The student: They have not confronted us, O Shaykh, up to now, up to this time of ours. Truly, not this Six-Day War (...), but in the war of '73 they did not confront us.

* The Shaykh: Praise be to Allah, because with us there is some faith.

* A student: The war of '73, O Shaykh.

* Another student: Meaning everyone who crossed the Canal, O Shaykh, Allahu Akbar, with the banner. Truly, there were people, and even Shaykh 'Abd al-Halim Mahmud said there were people, we found people in front of us walking in front of us with banners.

* The Shaykh: Praise be to Allah, praise be to Allah.

* A student: O Shaykh, a soldier related that he was alone during the war of '73, O Shaykh. Then there was a Jewish platoon passing by. This soldier was going to al-Marj to bring breakfast to eat. Suddenly the platoon, he had a can of fava beans. He attacked them with the can of fava beans, and they all surrendered. When they went to the commanders, they said: "How did you surrender to one soldier?" They said: "We did not surrender to one soldier. We surrendered to one soldier wearing green clothing, around whom was a platoon wearing white clothes."

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. In any case, the address ﴿They will not fight you﴾ is to the believers. So if we fight them with faith, they will not fight us face to face ﴿except within fortified towns or from behind walls﴾ [al-Hashr 14]. But if we fight them without faith, they will fight us from above our roofs, not from behind walls.

* A student: O Shaykh, is the context now about the hypocrites?

* The Shaykh: What?

* The student: ﴿They will not fight you all﴾.

* The Shaykh: No, no, it is not the hypocrites, it is the Jews.

* A student: "Misran," not Misr of the Nile. Then which Misr?

* The Shaykh: Any misr of the amsar (cities). 'Unayza is called a misr.

* The student: The form of the command (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, no. He says: go (...), it is not in (...). We say: "What is this? We ask Allah to bring forth for us from what the earth grows." This exists in every land. This is an additional rebuke upon them.

* The student: Because they are originally wandering.

* The Shaykh: They are in the wilderness (al-tih). When Allah sent down upon them the manna and the quails, they asked Allah, instead of what was sent down to them from the sky, for the beneficial and pleasant things from the earth. So He said: How can I ask Allah to replace what is better?

He said: ﴿And they returned with anger from Allah﴾. ﴿Baw bi-ghadab﴾, they returned, that is, they went back. The "ba'" here is for accompaniment in the anger, and the anger is from Allah, glorified and exalted. ﴿Bi-ghadabin min Allah﴾: "min" here is for the starting point, meaning the anger is from Allah, that Allah became angry with them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry, and made of them apes and swine, and those who worshipped the false deity (al-Taghut)﴾ [al-Ma'ida 60]. The anger of Allah, glorified and exalted, is one of His attributes, but it does not resemble the attributes of created beings. It does not resemble the attributes of created beings. When we become angry, our veins swell, our face reddens, our hair stands up, and the person loses his composure, is that so?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Do these symptoms occur in the anger of Allah?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, because ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 11]. Rather, it is an anger befitting Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When we say this and affirm that anger is a real attribute, our duty is discharged, and we proceed according to what Allah and His Messenger commanded. Some people, some of the people of distortion (ahl al-tahrif), say: anger means revenge (al-intiqam), and it is not an attribute of Allah. Others say that it is the will for revenge. So the meaning of ﴿and Allah became angry with him﴾ [al-Nisa 93] is that He willed to take revenge upon him. According to the first, it says: the anger of Allah upon him means He took revenge upon him. Those who say anger is revenge are those who do not affirm the will, nor affirm any of the attributes, but affirm only the separate created acts. Those who say it is the will are those who affirm for Allah how many attributes?

* The students: Seven attributes.

* The Shaykh: Seven attributes. They are the Ash'ariyya. The first view belongs to the Mu'tazila and the Jahmiyya, who say that Allah does not will, but has created things. So anger is that punishment and retribution separate from Allah. Both matters are false, both opinions are false. As for the first, which is the view of the Mu'tazila, we say: Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿So when they angered Us, We took revenge upon them﴾ [al-Zukhruf 55]. And ﴿angered Us (asafuna)﴾, what does it mean? It means "made Us angry." "We took revenge." And the conditional is other than the conditioned, is it not?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Because if "asafuna" meant "angered Us" in the sense of "took revenge upon them," the statement would have no benefit. The meaning would be: "When We took revenge upon them, We took revenge upon them," which is meaningless. The meaning is: "When they angered Us, We took revenge upon them." This clearly shows that anger is other than revenge.

As for the others, we say to them: if you affirm the will, what prevents you from affirming anger? If they say: anger is the boiling of the heart, the swelling of the veins, the reddening of the eyes, and this is not befitting to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, we say to them: the will also is a human inclination toward what benefits him or repels harm, and this too is a deficiency that is not befitting to Allah. So what applies to anger applies to will. If you affirm will, you must affirm anger. If you negate anger, you must negate will. Is it clear?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: The People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunna wa al-Jama'a) are not bound, praise be to Allah, by anything of this. They say: we affirm anger, we affirm will, and we affirm all the attributes of Allah, glorified and exalted, but we declare Allah far above resembling or being like created beings. Furthermore, we do not imagine His attributes either. We do not imagine them. We hold that it is forbidden for a person to imagine the attributes of Allah, glorified and exalted, because Allah is greater than that the intellects can encompass Him. He is not perceived by sights, and likewise intellects do not encompass Him.

So what do we say about anger according to the People of the Sunnah and the Community? It is one of the attributes of Allah, the Exalted, established for Him in reality, without modality (takyif) and without likening (tamthil).

His saying: ﴿And they returned with anger from Allah. That is because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾. ﴿That﴾ refers to everything mentioned before. The apparent meaning is that it refers to everything mentioned before, not merely ﴿Humiliation was stamped upon them﴾ and ﴿they returned with anger﴾. Everything mentioned before, even their asking for the lower in exchange for the better, this is among the causes of disbelief, because the believer is guided to good, recognizes good from evil, and is granted success in following good. ﴿That is because they﴾, so ﴿that﴾ means everything mentioned.

His saying: ﴿because they﴾, the "ba'" is for causation. ﴿They used to disbelieve﴾: were they like this in the past, or are they characterized by it?

* The students: They are characterized by it.

* The Shaykh: They are characterized by it. ﴿They disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾. The scholars said: "kufr" (disbelief) is derived from covering, and from it comes "kafur" of the palm tree, because it covers the fruit, and thus it is called "kafur" because it covers the fruit. Disbelief in the signs of Allah means covering them and not acknowledging them. For this reason, the word has been given the meaning of denial (al-jahd), so it takes the preposition "bi." He said ﴿they disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾ and did not say "they disbelieve the signs of Allah." His saying, the Exalted: ﴿in the signs of Allah﴾, are these the cosmic signs (al-kawniyya) or the legislative signs (al-shar'iyya)?

* The students: Both.

* The Shaykh: Both, the cosmic and the legislative. The legislative relates to worship, and the cosmic relates to lordship. So they disbelieve in this and in that.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 60–61 (part 3 of 5):

Second: ﴿And they kill the prophets﴾. I seek refuge in Allah from such audacity towards Allah. They kill the prophets! They do not merely deny them; they kill the prophets, ﴿without right﴾. There are two readings of ﴿the prophets (al-nabiyyin)﴾, yes, there are two readings for it. ﴿And humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them﴾ has three readings: ﴿'alayhimu﴾, which is the well-known one now; the second is ﴿'alayhumu﴾; and the difference between them? The ha' is vowelled with a damma: ﴿'alayhumu﴾, or ﴿'alayhimu﴾, or ﴿'alayhimi﴾. ﴿Humiliation was stamped upon them﴾, three readings.

His words ﴿the prophets (al-nabiyyin)﴾: there are two readings: ﴿al-nabiyyin﴾, and the second: ﴿al-nabi'in﴾, from al-naba', which is news/information.

His words ﴿and they kill the prophets without right﴾ mean: rather, by falsehood.

His words ﴿without right﴾: this restriction serves to describe the reality and to denounce their act, to denounce them for their deed. Let me say: this restriction is to describe the reality and is not a condition. Why is it not a condition?

* Student: Because it is impossible to kill a prophet.

* The Shaykh: Because it is impossible to kill a prophet rightfully, ever. Every killing of the prophets (...) because he (ﷺ) said: "This is the time of the cutting of my aorta" [[Narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad (no. 8007), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with the wording: "This is the time my aorta was cut."]] after he had said: "The poison of Khaybar's morsel has continued to affect me." But Allah, glorified and exalted, prevented it until his appointed term was fulfilled. They, may Allah protect us, have this great audacity, which is killing the prophets without right.

* Student: Shaykh, does the verse ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67] apply to the Messenger?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it applies to him. "And Allah will protect you from the people" — so Allah protected him until he delivered the message, because Allah said: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord; and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67]. That is, until he conveyed the message, and he did convey the message.

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. If we say that he died because of this morsel, he died a martyr, because what these Jews did to him was oppression.

* Student: Does this contradict ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾, [al-Ma'idah 67]... regarding the message only?

* The Shaykh: When He said: ﴿Convey﴾, meaning: if it is established that the Messenger died because of this morsel, then the meaning of the verse is: O Messenger, convey, and Allah will protect you; that is, no one will be able to prevent you from conveying your message. But when the term comes, the conveying ends.

Then He said: ﴿That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress﴾. His words ﴿that﴾: is the reference of this demonstrative the same as the first demonstrative?

Would it then be a repetition for emphasis? Or is the reference of the demonstrative disbelief and killing? The apparent meaning is disbelief and killing. On this basis, the sins mentioned after it, ﴿That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress﴾, are a ladder to disbelief and killing. That is, they disbelieved and killed because of what they disobeyed, due to their disobedience and transgression.

His words ﴿That is because they disobeyed﴾: the particle bi (ba') is causal, and the ma in His words ﴿bima 'asaw﴾ is verbal-masdariyyah, meaning "because of their disobedience." His words ﴿and they used to transgress﴾ are coordinated with His words ﴿bima 'asaw﴾, meaning "and because they used to transgress"; that is, "and because they were transgressors."

The difference between disobedience (ma'siyah) and transgression ('udwan) when both are mentioned together: disobedience is doing what is forbidden, and transgression is exceeding what was commanded. Doing what is prohibited is called disobedience, and transgression is exceeding what was commanded, such as praying five rak'ahs, for example. It has also been said the reverse: disobedience is abandoning what was commanded, and transgression is committing what is forbidden. Whichever of these is meant, the important point is that these people transgressed and disobeyed. They neither fulfilled the obligation nor refrained from what was forbidden. Therefore, matters carried them step by step until they disbelieved in the signs of Allah and killed His messengers. In this is evidence for the view held by some scholars that sins are the courier of disbelief, and this is so. When a person commits a sin, he takes it lightly; then he takes lightly the second, then the third, and so on. Verses of poetry have passed us in explaining taqwa (God-consciousness), which you may recall. It says:

Leave off sins, small and great; that is taqwa.
And act like one walking over a field of thorns, fearful of what he sees.
Do not belittle any small sin; indeed, mountains are made of pebbles.

This is correct: when sins pile up on hearts, they come between them and guidance and light. ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14].

(...) Because the law of those before us is law for us, unless our law states otherwise. How much more so when it agrees with ours?

* Second: It is also derived from it that Allah, glorified and exalted, is the refuge of creation. When harm touches them, they turn to Allah, glorified and exalted.

* Third: The messengers, peace be upon them, are like others in their need of Allah, glorified and exalted. So it should not be said that messengers are capable of everything and that no harm touches them.

* It also contains evidence of Musa's compassion for his people, from His words: ﴿And when Musa asked for water for his people﴾ [al-Baqarah 60].

* It contains evidence for the permissibility of seeking tawassul (intercession/means) through the righteous. But tawassul through what?

* Students: Through their supplication.

* The Shaykh: Through their supplication. As for through their persons or their status, that is not permitted, because that is not a means. The intended meaning of tawassul is taking the paths that lead to the goal. Are you understanding?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: This is tawassul, and that this path leads to the goal is established only by evidence from the Law. Accordingly, whatever the Law has not stated, seeking tawassul to Allah through it is among introducing into the religion of Allah what is not part of it. For this reason, the verifying scholars counted seeking tawassul through the status of the Messenger (ﷺ) among the kinds of shirk.

* It also contains evidence that Allah, glorified and exalted, is capable and generous, because the incapable is not asked for water and the miser does not give. Is that not so?

* Students: Indeed.

* The Shaykh: For this reason Allah responded. This also contains evidence affirming Allah's hearing, glorified and exalted, from His words: ﴿So We said﴾, because the fa' here is causal. ﴿So We said﴾, meaning: when he asked for water, We said. This shows that Allah heard his request and answered him.

* It also contains evidence, and this is among the important proofs, for the existence of Allah, exalted, for the deniers. The answering of supplication is evidence for the existence of the One supplicated to. There are many Qur'anic verses mentioning that Allah answered those who call upon Him: ﴿And Nuh, when he called out before; so We responded to him﴾ [al-Anbiya' 76], ﴿And Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful." So We responded to him﴾ [al-Anbiya' 83-84], and others besides these.

* It contains evidence for the perfect power of Allah, glorified and exalted, since Musa (ﷺ) struck the rock with the staff and it gushed forth springs. Is this of a kind that is customary?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: Not of its kind.

* Student: That is, from a rock?

* The Shaykh: Yes, but not in this form. It is not customary of this kind. So it is evidence of Allah's power, and that the matter is not as the naturalists claim, that it is nature. If matters were by nature, they would not change and would remain as they are.

* It contains evidence of one of the signs of Allah, glorified and exalted, by which He confirmed His prophet Musa. Is that correct or not?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Several signs are connected to this staff. Among them: he struck the sea with it and it split, and he struck the rock with it and it gushed forth.

* Students: And it swallowed the magicians' magic.

* The Shaykh: And it swallowed the magic of the magicians.

* Student: And it turned into a serpent.

* The Shaykh: And its turning into a serpent, yes indeed. It also contains evidence of the wisdom of Allah, blessed and exalted, in making this gushing water into twelve springs, for two benefits:

First benefit: abundance for the Children of Israel, because if it had been one spring, they would have suffered hardship from crowding.

Second: keeping away enmity and hatred among them, because they were twelve tribes. If they had been gathered in one place, with the constriction and need for water, severe strife would have arisen among them, perhaps leading to fighting. This is from the mercy of Allah, blessed and exalted, toward the Children of Israel, in that He caused it to gush into twelve springs. For this reason Allah pointed to this blessing with His words: ﴿Every people knew their drinking place﴾ [al-Baqarah 60]. Every people from where?

* Students: From the Children of Israel.

* The Shaykh: From the Children of Israel, yes. It also contains evidence that Allah, glorified and exalted, reminds the Children of Israel of these great blessings so that they may give thanks. For this reason He said: ﴿Eat and drink from the provision of Allah, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption﴾. And in His words: ﴿Eat and drink﴾:

* It is derived from this that the basic ruling on whatever Allah created of food and drink for man is permissibility and lawfulness, because the command here, as has passed, is for permissibility. So whatever Allah brings forth for us from the earth or sends down from the sky, the basic ruling concerning it is lawfulness. Whoever disputes the lawfulness of any part of it, claiming it is not lawful but forbidden, we say: the burden of proof is on you. What is the matter whose basic ruling is prohibition?

* Students: Acts of worship.

* The Shaykh: Acts of worship. As for transactions and the benefits of what Allah created, the basic ruling is lawfulness and permissibility.

* It is also derived from this verse: the prohibition of corruption on the earth, from His words: ﴿and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption﴾, and the basic ruling of a prohibition is that it is forbidden.

* It is also derived from it: that forbidden things are made more ugly according to the state of the doer, from His words: ﴿Eat and drink from the provision of Allah and do not commit abuse﴾. It is not fitting for one whom Allah has granted abundant provision and given what meets his needs to do this; rather, the perfection of such a person does not allow him to do it.

* Students: To strive on the earth in corruption.

* The Shaykh: To strive on the earth in corruption. Rather, what is fitting for him is to give thanks for these blessings, striving for righteousness for himself and for the reform of others. Is there something in the verse?

* Student: That sins on the earth are a cause of corruption of the earth.

* The Shaykh: That sins are a cause of the corruption of the earth, because Allah, exalted, says: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, so that He may let them taste part of what they have done﴾ [al-Rum 41]. This mentions the cause. And He said: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been righteous, We would have opened upon them blessings from the sky and the earth; but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾ [al-A'raf 96]. This is a verse mentioning the second. And the Exalted says: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened upon them the gates of everything﴾ [al-An'am 44]. Look at the trial: ﴿We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair﴾. Here the meaning of "rejoicing" is the rejoicing of arrogance.

* Student: His words, exalted be He: ﴿Eat and drink﴾, meaning He mentioned eating together with drinking?

* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. Because eating is understood from the manna and quail mentioned earlier. He mentioned the manna and quail, which is a form of eating.

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: (...) Seeking water by request, or from his own initiative? And Allah knows best.

* * *

Then Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will not endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions." He said, "Would you exchange what is better for what is less? Go down to a city, for indeed you will have what you asked for." And humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them, and they returned with anger from Allah. That is because they used to deny the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress﴾ [al-Baqarah 61].

From this noble verse, several benefits are also derived:

* First: the baseness and foolishness of the Children of Israel, since they asked that Allah change for them this provision which has no equal, from their saying: ﴿We will not endure one kind of food﴾. What is "one kind of food"?

* Students: The manna and quail.

* The Shaykh: The manna and quail. The meaning of it being one food is two foods; that is, one routine and one state. This is the meaning: "We cannot endure this state; we have only this, and we want other things."

* It also contains evidence of their arrogance, from their saying: ﴿call upon your Lord for us﴾. They did not say "call upon our Lord" or "call upon Allah for us"; they said ﴿your Lord﴾, as if there was in them, may Allah protect us, a sense of disdain, even though they were the ones who believed in Musa. Yet they say: ﴿call upon your Lord for us﴾, just as they said: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here﴾ [al-Ma'idah 24]. So they, may Allah protect us, have baseness and arrogance and pride.

* It also contains evidence of the low aspiration of the Children of Israel, since they sought the lesser instead of the greater. Is this correct?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Also: whoever chooses the lesser over the greater has a resemblance to the Jews. Among this are those who choose the forbidden over the lawful. I have told you the story of the man who was beside me on the airplane, to whom they gave a sweet as is customary. Is that right or not?

* Students: No, Shaykh, you have not told it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, I told you. Let me tell it now. They gave him a sweet, and he said: "What does a person want with a sweet?" I said: "This sweet, because he had never boarded a plane except this one time." I said: "They say this sweet relieves the pressure on a person." He said: "By Allah, I crave a cigarette." I said to him: "This is better." But if you are determined, go there, or be patient until you reach Qassim airport. Look, he said to me: "I cannot be patient." In any case, we ask Allah for safety. He chooses this over that. And we hear that those afflicted with smoking, at the breaking of the fast in Ramadan, the first thing they begin with is the cigarette. This is what we have heard. That is, they do not do the Sunnah of breaking the fast with dates. May Allah protect us. This resembles the Children of Israel, indeed it is worse than the Children of Israel, because the Children of Israel chose something permissible, while these choose something forbidden.

* It also contains evidence that the loftiness of a person's aspiration is to look to what is most perfect and most excellent in all matters; he looks to what is most perfect and most excellent.

* It also contains evidence that expanding in food and drink, as long as it does not reach the level of extravagance, is praiseworthy for a person; and that whoever forbids himself, or abstains from something Allah has made lawful for him, is in the blameworthy kind of scrupulousness. The reason is that these people exchanged what is lesser for what is better. Whoever abandons some permissible things without a legitimate purpose, but out of scrupulousness and asceticism, is blameworthy. But if it is for a legitimate purpose, such as what is related about the Commander of the Faithful, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that "in the year of the ashes he avoided meat and said: 'I cannot make my condiment anything but date vinegar.'" [[Narrated by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat (3/313), from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam from his father, with the wording: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab forbade meat for himself in the year of the ashes until the people ate it." And from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik who said: "The stomach of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab rumbled, and he used to eat oil in the year of the ashes."]] That is, "I will not eat meat, because how can I see people hungry this year while I am sated with meat?" If it is for a legitimate purpose, there is no harm in it. But as for asceticism, this is neither a legislated matter nor a praiseworthy one. Indeed, Shaykh al-Islam said: this is a blameworthy matter. [[Al-Fatawa al-Kubra (5/548).]]

* Student: Shaykh, asceticism (zuhd) is not a legitimate purpose?

* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed.

* Student: Asceticism itself is not a legitimate purpose?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is (not).

* Student: Because hadiths have been related praising it.

**Shaykh:** In asceticism? Yes. But what is *zuhd* (asceticism)?

**Student:** What is it?

**Another student:** Does it mean wearing a patched robe and dressing like the ascetics?

**Shaykh:** No, that is *tazahhud* (affecting asceticism). *Zuhd* is leaving what does not benefit one in the Hereafter, and *wara'* (scrupulousness) is leaving what harms one in the Hereafter. *Zuhd* is leaving what is not beneficial, and *wara'* is leaving what is harmful. Some people think that *wara'* and *zuhd* have the same meaning, but this is not correct. For example, someone who avoids permissible things, having chosen in place of them what is more beneficial, what is he called?

**Students:** An ascetic (*zahid*).

**Shaykh:** An ascetic. Whoever leaves them in order to attain what is more beneficial in the Hereafter is considered an ascetic. Whoever abandons the forbidden things by occupying himself with permissible things, even if they are not more beneficial in the Hereafter, is called a *wari'* (scrupulous person). When we say that *zuhd* does not mean that a person practices austerity, austerity is not praiseworthy unless it serves a legitimate purpose. A legitimate purpose is like what we mentioned about 'Umar. Or, for example, (...) a person is among people who are poor, and if he wears something unbecoming to himself and his wealth, he breaks their hearts and that has an effect on their souls. Leaving this is also among the matters for which a person may be praised.

And in this is evidence for the permissibility of *buqul* (herbs), *qithha'* (cucumbers), garlic, lentils and onions. From where is this derived?

**Student:** From God bringing them forth.

**Shaykh:** Yes. ﴿Go down to a city﴾?

**Student:** No, it comes forth.

**Shaykh:** No, God brings forth the *sumum* (the fruits of the earth).

**Student:** ﴿For you shall have what you asked for﴾.

**Shaykh:** ﴿Go down to a city, for you shall have what you asked for﴾. ﴿For you shall have﴾ means: what you ask for is permitted to you.

If someone says: This was in the law of Moses? We say: Our law did not come to oppose it, rather it came in agreement with it. For it was reported that "a pot containing herbs was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he disliked eating them. When he disliked eating them, some of his companions also disliked them. The Messenger said: 'Bring them near.' Then he said: 'Eat, for I converse with one with whom you do not converse.'"[[Agreed upon; recorded by al-Bukhari (855) and Muslim (564/73) from Jabir.]] So he permitted them for them. Likewise, "in Khaybar, when the people ate onions and they knew that the Prophet (ﷺ) disliked them, they said: 'They have been forbidden.' He said: 'Indeed, it is not for me to forbid what God has made lawful.'"[[Recorded by Muslim (565/76) from Abu Sa'id, with the wording: "Indeed, it is not for me to forbid what God has made lawful."]] So he made clear that it is lawful, and so it is lawful even in our law. The Islamic law came in agreement with this matter. Even if it had not come in agreement with it, nor in opposition to it, the correct view is that it is:

**Student:** That it remains on its original basis.

**Shaykh:** That it remains on its original basis.

And in this is evidence for the permissibility of attributing a thing to its place rather than to its first agent, due to His saying: ﴿of what the earth brings forth﴾. And who causes it to grow?

**Students:** God.

**Shaykh:** God, glorified and exalted be He.

From this we derive the second benefit: attributing a thing to its true cause, which is established as a cause either by the law or by the senses, without associating it with God, is not obligatory. For example, if you say: This man is almost dead from hunger, and you bring him bread and give it to him, and you say: "Had it not been for his eating the bread, he would have perished." Is this permissible or not?

**Students:** It is permissible.

**Shaykh:** It is permissible. This is allowed. Attributing a thing to its cause, which is established by the senses or the law as its cause, is not objectionable. What is prohibited is that you mention the first cause, which is God's decree, together with the second cause joined by *wa* (and). What is that?

**Student:** Association (*tashrik*).

**Shaykh:** It is not merely association (*tashrik*); association implies equality. As for association without equality, there is no harm in it. We say: "By God, then so-and-so." The point now is that in this verse there is evidence that attributing a thing to its true cause, legally or by the senses, is not objectionable. But what is the "but"?

**Students:** The prohibited matter.

**Shaykh:** The prohibited matter is that it is joined with God by the particle *wa* (and), which implies equality.

If someone says: Did not God, blessed and exalted, censure Qarun when he said: ﴿I was given it only on the basis of knowledge I have﴾ [Al-Qasas 78]? So he attributed the acquisition of this wealth to knowledge, and this is correct, since knowledge may be the cause?

We say: This man denied that it came from God. It is known that when a person attributes a thing to its cause as if it were the sole cause, first and last, it is prohibited and not permissible. Even if you say: "I am the one who made this, and had it not been for me, it would not have been completed," and similar things, such as "Had I not built this building, it would not have stood," if you intend that you are independent of God in it, this is not permissible. But if you attribute it to the true cause indicated by the law or the senses, without having the belief that this cause is independent in its effect, there is no harm in it. It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said regarding his uncle Abu Talib: "Had it not been for me, he would have been in the lowest level of the Fire."[[Agreed upon; recorded by al-Bukhari (3883) and Muslim (209/357) from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib.]] So he attributed the lessening of the punishment for Abu Talib to himself (ﷺ), saying: "Had it not been for me."

**Student:** Shaykh, the *tafsir* of Ibn 'Abbas (...).

**Shaykh:** This report must be examined. If it is authentically from Ibn 'Abbas, then his intention was to block the means (*sadd al-dhara'i'*, closing the doors that lead to harm) for people who are feared to fall into error.

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** Who?

**Student:** The permissibility of this. Is it better to say: "Had it not been for such-and-such"?

**Shaykh:** No, it is better to say: "Had it not been that God decreed such-and-such." This is better.

In this also is evidence for the rebuke of Moses (peace be upon him) toward the Children of Israel, and that such people, who exchange what is better for what is inferior, deserve rebuke, because Moses rebuked them when he said: ﴿Would you exchange what is better for what is inferior?﴾

And in it is evidence that a person may decline to act as an intercessor when there is no reason for it, because he said: ﴿Go down to a city, for you shall have what you asked for﴾. Is there any need for me to supplicate to God that He bring forth for you what the earth grows, or not?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** So sometimes some people come to you and say: "Intercede for me with so-and-so," (...) this is a task, and then you say: "Go yourself and try; if you cannot, then I am ready." Or is it better that you immediately take on the task and intercede?

**Students:** The first is better.

**Shaykh:** The first is better, for two reasons.

The first reason: you protect the dignity of this man from groveling before you, for if you intercede for him, this will be on his forehead until the Day of Resurrection. That is one.

The second matter: if you do this, it may open for you doors that you cannot close, and then the door is shut on you from above. Do you understand the meaning of this expression?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** It may be that if everyone who comes to you, you immediately intercede for, people will come to you whom you cannot get rid of, and then the door will be closed on you from above. How will it be closed? When they see that every day they have three or four intercessions from you, they will consider that they need not accept your intercession, and your refusal will become easy for them. Then they will refer you to a matter in which it may be important that they accept your intercession. A person should be firm in such matters, giving precedence to reason over emotion. Otherwise, sometimes a person feels mercy for someone and says: "Why not intercede?" If he has the readiness, when he sees the correct point of view, and he has the readiness that if the doors are closed before him he will intercede, this will be better for both parties and for the general interest. We have seen the effect of this in many matters: a person should not always be interceding; this is safer, and it also gives him more standing with the first official. As for Moses (peace be upon him) refraining from asking God, even though supplication itself is an act of worship (the supplication itself is worship), and he did not ask God on their behalf but said: ﴿Go down to a city, for you shall have what you asked for﴾, meaning: any city that is available to you, you will find what you asked for, after the wandering (*tih*), after the wandering this thing will happen.

**Student:** Is it said that this is trivial, so one should not supplicate to God?

**Shaykh:** No, not at all. It has come in a hadith: "Let one of you ask his Lord for everything, even for the strap of his sandal."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in his Jami' (3604/m8) from Anas with the wording: "Let one of you ask his Lord for all his needs, even asking for the thong of his sandal if it breaks."]] No, this does not contradict it. A person should ask God for everything, every need.

**Student:** (...) he says to them: "Go down to a city."

**Shaykh:** The meaning is that any city that is available to you, after the wandering, after the wandering this matter occurs.

**Student:** They will argue about Egypt, which is Egypt, actually Egypt, or is this Egypt our country?

**Shaykh:** No, it is not your country.

**Student:** And did our Lord reveal to Moses that they should go to Egypt and take it?

**Shaykh:** No, no. God, glorified and exalted be He, had given Egypt to them from the day Pharaoh drowned. He said: ﴿And luxury in which they had been delighting. Thus; and We bequeathed them to another people﴾ [Ad-Dukhan 27–28]. And in Ash-Shu'ara He said: ﴿And We made the Children of Israel inherit it﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 59].

**Student:** Regarding the Children of Israel's denial of the blessing, their contempt for it, and their seeking the inferior while the superior was available, what is your opinion, may God pardon you (...)? That things may be (...)

**Shaykh:** By God, our opinion is that this is an error. People have relied in this matter on a legal opinion (*fatwa*) that they attribute to some scholars, and I think it is not authentic. They say: "Food is only considered property and food when it is eaten and has an effect." These crumbs are not food. But I do not think this attribution is correct. I believe that for such matters we should set aside something specific for food. Otherwise, I do not think they will commit to it, or else they will commit to stuffing these things, stuffing them before washing them, in a way that leaves no trace of the food. Otherwise, this is a problem. The current problem is that we hear that the sewage systems in cities do not allow cesspits to be connected.

**Student:** Inside the house.

**Shaykh:** In the house, they do not prevent even this?

**Student:** This is general. This is inside the house. It is only near the wall (...).

**Shaykh:** That is not contrary to it. In this is evidence for the imposition of humiliation and destitution upon the Children of Israel. We have mentioned that this verse is absolute and is restricted by another verse. Is it restricted regarding humiliation or regarding destitution?

**Students:** Regarding humiliation.

**Shaykh:** Regarding humiliation only; destitution remains. By destitution here, is the intended meaning spiritual poverty or material poverty?

**Students:** Spiritual.

**Shaykh:** Spiritual. It may also be material. But considering the present reality, and the fact that the Jews have come to control the economy of the entire world, all the economy in East and West is now in the hands of the Jews, it is known that the intended meaning of destitution here is the heart, spiritual destitution. As for humiliation, God, exalted be He, restricted it in Surat Al 'Imran, saying: ﴿Except by a covenant from God and a covenant from people﴾ [Al 'Imran 112]. Destitution is absolute: ﴿Except by a covenant from God and a covenant from people﴾, ﴿and destitution was stamped upon them﴾ without exception.

And in this is evidence that the Children of Israel will not stand before the Muslims if they fight them, by reason of Islam. From where is this derived?

**Students:** From the imposition of humiliation.

**Shaykh:** Because the imposition of humiliation is due to disobedience. If that is so, then if they are fought by obedience and Islam, there is no doubt that the ruin will fall upon them. God, exalted be He, said: ﴿They will not fight you all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls﴾ [Al-Hashr 14].

**Fourteenth benefit:** The Children of Israel deserve anger, due to His saying: ﴿And they returned with anger from God﴾, and the anger befell them as a deserved consequence from the verb "returned" and as an actual occurrence from His saying: ﴿with anger from God﴾, glorified and exalted be He.

**Fifteenth benefit:** Affirmation of causes, due to His saying: ﴿That was because﴾, since the *ba'* (because) indicates causation.

**Sixteenth benefit:** Disbelief in the signs of God is a cause of anger, humiliation and destitution, due to His saying: ﴿That was because they disbelieved in the signs of God﴾.

**Seventeenth benefit:** The transgression of the Children of Israel, beyond which there is no limit as far as we know, in that they combined disbelief in God with the killing of the prophets of God, due to His saying: ﴿and killed the prophets without right﴾.

**Eighteenth benefit:** The killing of prophets is killing without right, since we have mentioned that the restriction here is not a restriction whose implication excludes other cases; rather, it is a restriction to describe the reality and to give the reason.

**Nineteenth benefit:** Sins are a cause of disbelief. From where is this derived?

**Students:** ﴿That was because they disobeyed﴾.

**Shaykh:** ﴿That was because they disobeyed﴾, meaning their disbelief in the signs of God and their killing of the prophets have as their cause disobedience, because when they disobeyed, they rebelled. For this reason the scholars said: sins are the road to disbelief (*barid al-kufr*, the postal route to disbelief). This is a reality, because sins, God forbid, tear the protective wall of the heart until disbelief reaches it: ﴿No! Rather, what they have been earning has rusted over their hearts﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 14].

We have mentioned in the commentary that some scholars say: the second ﴿that﴾ is the first, so that they are said to have been given cause by disbelief, the killing of the prophets, disobedience and transgression. They consider disbelief to be disobedience, and the killing of the prophets to be transgression. They say: ﴿That was because they disobeyed﴾ is the meaning of His saying: ﴿That was because they disbelieved in the signs of God﴾. And ﴿and they used to transgress﴾ is the meaning of ﴿and killed the prophets without right﴾. The repetition of the demonstrative is for emphasis. But the original principle is that this is not the case, because it is one of the well-known rules in the principles of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*) that when the matter is between establishing a new meaning (*ta'sis*) and emphasis (*tawkid*), the original principle is establishment, because emphasis means increasing one of them for emphasis, whereas establishment means that each of them is an original principle. This is the basic principle in speech.

And in this is evidence that the Children of Israel combined, God forbid, sins that are opposition to the Creator with transgression, between sins and transgression. It has been said that disobedience is the violation of what is prohibited, and transgression is exceeding the bounds of what is obligatory, adding to the obligatory in excess or deficiency. As for disobedience, it is the doing of what is forbidden. So, the abandonment of prayer, for example, do we call it transgression, or do we call it disobedience?

**Students:** Disobedience.

**Shaykh:** Disobedience, because it is the abandonment of an obligation. Violating what is forbidden, such as fornication, is transgression.

And in this verse: affirmation of anger for God, glorified and exalted be He, due to His saying: ﴿And they returned with anger from God﴾. We have explained that it is a real attribute that must be affirmed for God in its true sense.

And also in it: a demonstration of God's wisdom, in that He linked things to their causes: ﴿That was because they﴾ and ﴿That was because they disobeyed﴾. This is part of wisdom, that causes should be effective. But notice that causes may have impediments. Causes may exist, but stronger impediments may also exist, and this too is part of wisdom, because weighing matters against one another, and an impediment may overcome a cause, and a cause may fall upon an impediment, this is undoubtedly part of wisdom. God, glorified and exalted be He, has wisdom in all His decree and in all His legislation. Is there anything further?

**Student:** The limit of extravagance (*israf*)?

**Shaykh:** Extravagance is exceeding the limit. Exceeding the limit is extravagance, and it is measured in each case according to its context, because an act may be extravagance here but not extravagance in another land, and an act may be extravagance for one person but not for another, and an act may be extravagance in this time but not in another time.

**Student:** Regarding their saying "(*ya'thaw*)" with the letter *tha'* and "(*'asaw*)": what is the difference between them?

**Shaykh:** *Ta'thaw*? *Al-'athw* is corruption, and disobedience is opposition to a command.

**Student:** So the meaning is one, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** No, they are not one, but they are mutually connected, because corruption occurs through sins. They are interrelated, but *'atha* does not mean *'asa*. It is not possible for *'asa* to mean *'atha*.

Student: "How is that, Shaykh? Is it bad manners between the students and their prophet, calling him by his bare name, saying, 'O Musa'?"

Shaykh: "Indeed, by Allah, it may be taken as bad manners. This applies if it is established that they were commanded to address him by his title of Messenger, for example, and not to call him by his name. I do not know about that. But in any case, by our customary standards now, setting that aside: does calling a great person by his name count as a form of bad manners or not?"

Students: "Yes."

Shaykh: "Even if you say to someone older than you in age, 'O so-and-so' using his name, people consider it bad manners. So how much more so when he is greater in rank and standing with Allah, exalted is He? It is in reality bad manners. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of some of you to others﴾ [al-Nur: 63]. The grammar here is that *du'a'* (calling) is a verbal noun that may be construed as attached to the subject or to the object. If it is attached to the object, it means: do not make your calling of the Messenger like your calling of one another, that is, do not call him by his name as one of you calls another. If we take it as attached to the subject, it means: do not make the Messenger's calling of you, when he summons you to something, like the calling of one another, so that you oppose it as some of you oppose one another. This is supported by His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves. So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial strike them﴾ [al-Nur: 63]."

Student: "Shaykh, does Allah's giving people power over the messengers mean that He is testing them?"

Shaykh: "What? What did you say?"

Student: "I mean, is this a test from Allah for the messengers and prophets?"

Shaykh: "No, not at all. In reality, this is an increase in their reward for their patience, and a demonstration of the wisdom of Allah, exalted is He, in that these people take revenge. Yet no messenger who was commanded to fight was ever killed. Everyone who was commanded to fight achieved victory, because Allah says: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir: 51]. This is the reconciliation between this verse I have just recited and His saying: ﴿and they kill the prophets without right﴾. This is a point we forgot to mention: the reconciliation between the two verses. Some scholars say the reconciliation between them is that those who were killed were not commanded to fight, and that whichever of the prophets was commanded to fight was granted victory. Others say that their victory in this world is by establishing the proof against their enemies and showing their truthfulness, so it is victory in speech and argument. Others also say that ﴿We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe﴾ [Ghafir: 51] refers to the preservation of their remembrance and its perpetuation: their good mention, and that they conveyed the message of Allah and fulfilled the trust, even though their enemies killed them. But the closer view is the first, that it applies to all who were commanded to fight. If they had been commanded to fight and the outcome had been total defeat, the command to fight would have been pointless, and Allah is exalted above that. So the closest of these opinions is that this verse, ﴿We will surely help Our messengers﴾, refers to those who were commanded to fight."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 60–61 (part 1 of 5):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when Moses asked for water for his people, We said: "Strike the rock with your staff," and there gushed forth from it twelve springs﴾ [al-Baqarah 60]. His words: ﴿istasqa﴾ means he asked for water to be given to him, and that was when they were in the wilderness (al-tih), or it applies in every place where there is a need for water, so he asks for water and they are given relief.

His words: ﴿Strike with your staff﴾. The staff is well known, and this staff had three great signs in it:
First: he would throw it down and it would become a crawling serpent.
Second: he would strike the rock with it and springs would gush forth.
