Even the one who does not understand the meaning is called ummī, because reading the wording without understanding its meaning is of no benefit. The ummī includes the one who does not know how to read and the one who knows how to read but does not know the meaning. For this reason He said: ﴿They know not the Book except wishful thinking﴾: ﴿They know not the Book﴾, that is, they do not understand it, and its knowledge does not reach their hearts. ﴿Except wishful thinking﴾: ﴿illā﴾ here is an exceptive particle of disconnection, meaning: but only wishful thinking. It could also be connected, meaning: they know it only with the knowledge of wishful thinking. And ﴿amānī﴾ is the plural of umniyyah (wish, desire), and umniyyah may have two meanings:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 75–78 (part 2 of 3):

The first of the two meanings is what a person wishes in his own self (tamanni, "wishing"). The second is recitation. The second meaning is more fitting to the verse, meaning: they do not understand the Qur'an, but they recite it without understanding. This is shown by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, Satan threw [something] into his wish﴾ [al-Hajj 52], meaning: into his recitation. From this is the saying of the poet about 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him:

*He recited the Book of Allah at the beginning of his night*
*and at its end he met the death of the watering places.*

Tamanna here means: he recited the Book of Allah. So His words ﴿except wishful thinking (amani)﴾ are the plural of umniyyah, and it means recitation. How many of them there are today among the Muslims! Most Muslims today do not know the Qur'an except as wishful recitation, and they are not eager to understand its meaning. This is contrary to reality, as Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said. He would say: Now, if a person were to read medicine, or read arithmetic, or read grammar, would he go over the books of these things, passing over them verbally and moving on? Or would he not reflect on their meanings and seek someone to explain and clarify them to him until he understands? Which is the reality? The second. So then, if you seek guidance through the Noble Qur'an, how will you be guided by it while you do not know its meaning? It is not possible. Yet with this Noble Qur'an, if you contemplate it, it will be made easy for you. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar 17].

Most people do not concern themselves with this aspect, namely reflecting on and contemplating the Noble Qur'an and knowing its meaning. Few have this as their way with the Qur'an. For this reason, the blessing of the Qur'an has now been removed from many people, because they seek blessing from it only verbally. To the extent that you hear some brothers in their shops, where they have a recorder of the Noble Qur'an, a recorder, and this recorder recites the Qur'an at a loud volume, while in the shop there are people who curse, revile, laugh, mock, lie in sales, and everything else. What is the reality of a person's position while the Book of Allah is over his head being heard? It is mockery of the Qur'an. Yet they say: this is their blessing. This is not its blessing. The blessing of the Qur'an lies in acting upon it and in the reward that follows from it. As for you humiliating the Qur'an, by Allah... meaning: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest description (al-mathal al-a'la)﴾ [al-Nahl 60]. If the king were in front of you now speaking through a loudspeaker, and the eyes were upon you, and he were speaking, and you were talking, mocking, laughing, and what (...)?

* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: You do not know (...). So how much more so with the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? The point is that I now say: with the great regret, many Muslims, in relation to the Book of Allah, are in this state, they know it only as wishful recitation.

He said: ﴿They only assume﴾. They do not know, because a person who does not know the words has no knowledge; he has nothing but assumption. And His words ﴿in them they only assume (in hum illa yazunnun)﴾: is this (in) operating or not operating?

* A student: Not operating.
* Another student: Because the negation has been annulled.
* The Shaykh: Because the negation has been annulled. This is non-operating, because the negation has been annulled, meaning: they are only assuming (...).

From His words ﴿Do you hope that they will believe for you﴾ to the end.

From this noble verse ﴿Do you hope that they will believe for you while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah and then distort them﴾ are derived several benefits:

* First: whoever does not believe in what is more apparent is further from believing in what is more hidden, because the one who hears the speech of Allah and then distorts it is further from believing the words of these people, meaning the Messenger ﷺ and his companions. The essence of the benefit: whoever does not believe in what is more apparent is further from believing in what is more hidden. ﴿Do you hope that they will believe for you while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah and then distort them﴾.
* The second benefit: Allah, glorified and exalted, consoles His Messenger ﷺ with what removes from him sorrow and grief, because the Messenger would grieve if these people did not believe. But Allah informs him that these are stubborn people, so the fault is not yours, but their evil state is what prevented their acceptance.
* The third benefit: the affirmation that Allah speaks, by His words ﴿hear the words of Allah﴾. The speech of Allah, blessed and exalted, is a true attribute that includes wording and meaning. He, glorified and exalted, speaks with letters and audible sounds. For this reason He said: ﴿hear the words of Allah﴾.
* The fourth benefit: the speech of Allah, glorified and exalted, is one of His active attributes (sifat fi'liyyah), considered in terms of what?

* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Its individual instances (al-aahad), considering its individual instances. As for the root of the attribute, it is an essential attribute (sifah dhatiyyah). The difference between essential and active attributes is that essential attributes are inseparable from the Essence of Allah, inseparable from His Essence eternally and everlastingly. What does "eternally" (azalan) mean? It means in the past. And "everlastingly" (abadan) means in the future. These are essential attributes. Active attributes are those connected to His will, so they occur when He wills. Based on this, we say: anger, is it of which of the two types?

* The students: Active.
* The Shaykh: Active. Pleasure is active, love is active, and many other actions: the istiwa' (rising) over the Throne, is it active? His elevation above creation?

* The students: Essential.
* The Shaykh: Essential.

* The fifth benefit: the refutation of the Ash'arites and others who hold that the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in the self, and that these letters are an expression of our speech and not the speech of Allah. They say: speech is the meaning subsisting in the soul, not the speech that is heard. They argue for their view with the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they say within themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ [al-Mujadilah 8], so Allah has made what is in the self a saying. And with the poet's words:

*Indeed speech lies in the heart,*
*and the tongue was only made a sign of the heart.*

They also argue: if it were said that Allah speaks with letters and sounds, He would be a locus for temporal events, and whatever is a locus for temporal events is itself temporal. But Allah, glorified and exalted, is the First before whom there is nothing, and the Last after whom there is nothing. Therefore His speech is a meaning subsisting in His self, and He creates sounds that are heard, which express what is in His self. Their speech is false. As for their argument from the verse ﴿they say within themselves﴾ [al-Mujadilah 8], we say: this saying is a restricted saying, ﴿within themselves﴾, and it is a proof against you, not for you, because it indicates that unrestricted speech is in the self, or otherwise?

* A student: Otherwise.
* The Shaykh: Otherwise. Had it not indicated this, the restriction "within themselves" would not have been needed. So praise be to Allah, no person argues with a sound proof except that his argument turns against him.

As for their saying, "Indeed speech lies in the heart," and so on, we say: firstly, this saying is attributed to al-Akhtal, and al-Akhtal came after the corruption of the tongue (Arabic). He was also a Christian man whose word is not relied upon. Then who said that he said it? It needs to be established that he said it, and even if it reaches him, there are defects beyond its reaching him.

As for their argument, the third point: that if His speech were with letters and sounds, He would be a locus for temporal events, and whatever is a locus for temporal events is temporal. It is said: who told you this proposition, that whatever is a locus for temporal events is temporal? Then we say: if what we commit to, that He is a locus for temporal events (...), the Creator and our restriction, does not imply a deficiency in the Creator, as if one said: eating is an attribute of perfection in the created being, and the one who does not eat is less than the one who eats. Therefore a person does not eat when he is ill and his health is impaired. And sleep is an attribute of perfection for the created being, so will you affirm it for Allah? We say: no, we do not affirm it for Allah, because it is an attribute of deficiency, and it is at the same time, in the created being, an attribute of deficiency. For this reason, when the created being is perfected in Paradise, does he need sleep or not? He does not need sleep for the perfection of his life. As for eating, he also does not need eating for his continuance, because he is eternal, but he needs eating for enjoyment and delight in it. Yes indeed.

The conclusion: His words ﴿until he hears the speech of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah 6] indicate that the speech of Allah, the Exalted, is audible, and that it is with a voice.

We still have a question remaining: are the letters with which Allah spoke the same letters that people use in their languages? What do you say?

* The students: They are.
* The Shaykh: Yes, they are the letters with which people speak in their languages. But the manner of their articulation and the sound with which they are uttered, this is what nothing resembles. We cannot say that the vocalization of Allah, glorified and exalted, with these words is like the vocalization of a human; this is not permissible, because ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 11]. As for the letters, they are the letters.

From this verse it is derived: were these Jews distorting the words of Allah, or not? Due to His words ﴿then they distort it after they had understood it﴾.

* The benefit, which I think is the seventh: the explanation of the ugliness of the distortion of these Jews, because they distorted after they had understood, after they had understood it. Is distortion after understanding (after understanding the meaning) greater or not?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Because the ignorant person may be excused for his ignorance, but the knowing person who understood the matter, his action is uglier, may Allah protect us, because he, may Allah keep us safe, has dared to disobey while knowing it. So it is greater.

* And in it also: evidence for the ugliness of distorting the words of Allah, and that this is one of the characteristics of the Jews, or not? Has this ummah also committed it? Yes, they have committed it. But verbal distortion is preserved; it is not possible to change the Qur'an in wording. If it were changed, I would be informed of it. Likewise in meaning: it is not possible for a meaning to be changed and for the distorted meaning to become established. Rather, Allah must raise up from the scholars of the Muslims someone who will nullify this meaning and refute it. But the point is that there has existed someone who distorted this Book, who distorted the speech of Allah. There have existed people who are fanatical and distort the verses according to their schools of thought, to the extent that you find some scholars, may Allah pardon us and them, distorting verses in a reprehensible way. How could they utter such a thing! If you wish for examples of this, refer to the books of branches of jurisprudence (furu') in fiqh, and also refer to the books of principles (usul) in creed, and you will find great distortion. Among the most distorting sects are the Rafidah (Rawafid). They have, in their interpretation of the Qur'an, may Allah protect us, great, large, and monstrous distortions. May Allah grant us well-being. They and others who have been afflicted with this calamity distort the speech of Allah after they had understood it.

His words ﴿while they know﴾: it is also derived from it that these Jews distorted after understanding while they knew that their act was reprehensible. So two reprehensible things were combined in them: the first reprehensible act: distortion after understanding the meaning; the second reprehensible act: knowing that this method is forbidden, and yet they distorted it. Do you know some of what they distorted verbally?

* A student: ﴿Say, "Hittah"﴾ [al-Baqarah 58].
* The Shaykh: It was said to them: ﴿Say, "Hittah"﴾, and they said: "Hintah" (wheat). And it was said: ﴿Enter the gate prostrating﴾, and they entered crawling on their backsides. Is this distortion or not?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Distortion in wording and meaning, and likewise in application: they distorted in application. In the Torah, the ruling of stoning was revealed for the adulterer if he was married (muhsan), and they distorted it, replacing this ruling with the claim that their faces are to be blackened, and the adulterer and adulteress are to be mounted on a donkey facing backward, and paraded through the markets. And they distorted, although the text of stoning is present in the Torah. Yes indeed.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal?﴾ From this verse is derived: a rebuke of these Jews for the distortion, meaning: are they in ignorance that ﴿Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal﴾?

* Also in it: a rebuke of the one who deserves it, and this is also legislated: that the one who deserves rebuke should be rebuked, and there is no transgression against him in that.
* Also among its benefits: the affirmation of the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge, by His words ﴿He knows what they conceal and what they reveal﴾.
* Also in it: the warning against opposing the command of Allah. From where does it include a warning against opposition?

* A student: ﴿that Allah knows﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, because the fact that Allah knows what a person conceals and what he reveals is undoubtedly a warning, meaning: beware lest Allah punish you. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾ [al-Baqarah 235].

In any case, these are four benefits from this verse, and let us return to what we had forgotten.

He said: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾, to the end of the verse.

* From it is derived: that among the Jews there are hypocrites, due to His words ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾, as He said at the beginning of the surah about the hypocrites: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you"﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].
* Also in it: evidence that treachery is one of the characteristics and natures of the Jews. From where is this taken?

* A student: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾.
* The Shaykh: What is the connection?
* The student: ﴿But when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you"﴾.
* The Shaykh: Meaning: this is a kind of treachery, or not? A kind of treachery against the believers, and treachery and deception are their nature.

* The third benefit: that some of them blame others when they return to their own people: ﴿And when some of them are alone with others, they say, "Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you?"﴾.
* The fourth benefit: knowledge is a opening (fath), due to His words ﴿what Allah has opened to you﴾, or not?

* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that knowledge is an opening. Allah opens to a person through it the various kinds of sciences and insights by which He illuminates his heart, so it is an opening.
* The fifth benefit: that the believer and the disbeliever will dispute before Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection, due to His words ﴿so that they may argue with you before your Lord﴾.
* The sixth benefit: the foolishness of these Jews who make their own action into a weapon against themselves. From where is this taken?

* A student: ﴿Will you not reason?﴾
* The Shaykh: ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ How can you tell them something that is a weapon against you? A weapon against yourself. At least if you have no shame, do what you wish. At least if you do not want to believe in the Messenger ﷺ, then do not inform them that the Messenger is true, because they say, "We believe," meaning that the Messenger is true, but they are, may Allah protect us, arrogant hypocrites.
* And in it: evidence for praising reason and wisdom, because their words ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ are a rebuke for this act, and that a person must be rational, such that he does not take a step without knowing where to place his foot. He should not walk blindly. Rather, a person should in all his affairs not speak without seeing what the result of his speech will be, and not act without seeing the result of his action. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or remain silent." [Agreed upon; recorded by al-Bukhari, no. (6018), and Muslim, no. (47/74), from Abu Hurayrah.]

As for a person speaking at random without caring about the consequences, this contradicts reason. Is it clear, O people?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: If you have other benefits, there is no harm. The matter is open to discussion.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, that their disbelief in the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is with knowledge, due to His words ﴿Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you?﴾. For this reason they became those upon whom is wrath, since they opposed the truth while knowing it.
* A student: ﴿so that they may argue with you before your Lord﴾: this is said by some of them to others. How do we derive a benefit from their words?
* The Shaykh: It is known, because Allah only mentioned it as an affirmation of it. We also mentioned in the commentary as a witness to it His words: ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will separate between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 3].

He said: ﴿And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Book except wishful recitation, and they only assume﴾.

**Commentary of Ibn ʿUthaymin (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Karim) on Surah 2, verses 75–78 (part 3 of 3):**

* It may be deduced from this verse that the term *ummi* (unlettered) applies to one who does not read, and also to one who reads but does not understand. Or not?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: By His saying: ﴿Unlettered, they know not the Scripture, except wishful thoughts﴾. The meaning of *amani* here is recitation.
* The second benefit: the censure of one who does not understand the meanings of Allah's Book. Is *ummi* a description of fault or a description of praise?
* Students: A description of fault.
* The Shaykh: It is a description of fault in origin, except in the case of the Messenger ﷺ, for it is a description of perfection for him, since it adds further confirmation of his prophethood (ﷺ).
* Also in it is evidence that whoever does not understand the meaning speaks only on the basis of conjecture (*ẓann*), by His saying: ﴿and they do not but conjecture﴾. The one who does not understand the meaning, the layman, now reads the Qur'an from beginning to end but does not understand its meaning. So when he speaks about a legal ruling of Allah's rulings indicated by the Book, what is his speech?
* Students: Conjecture.
* The Shaykh: Based on conjecture. For in reality he does not know, and knowledge is not possible except when one understands the meaning.
* Also in it: evidence for the censure of judging by conjecture, and that it is a trait of the Jews. This is found often among some people who love to be called scholars. You find him issuing fatwas without knowledge, and perhaps he issues a ruling that contradicts the Qur'an and Sunnah while not knowing. Can we deduce from this that the *muqallid* (one who follows *taqlid*, blind imitation) is not a scholar?
* A student: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: What is the reason?
* A student: Because he does not understand.
* The Shaykh: Yes, because he does not understand. In reality he does not understand the meaning. The *muqallid* does not understand, so he is not a scholar. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: the scholars agreed (*ijma'*, scholarly consensus) that the *muqallid* is not counted among the scholars. The *muqallid* is not a scholar. At most he is a copy of a book, and the book is more precise than him, for the book does not forget, whereas he may forget. But this does not mean we censure taqlid absolutely. Taqlid in its proper place is obligatory. And when is its place? When one is unable to derive proof (*istidlal*). If one does not know, it becomes obligatory for him to follow taqlid, by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know, with clear proofs and scriptures﴾ [An-Nahl 43–44]. The one who does not know: is his duty to ask, or what should he do?
* A student: Shaykh, judging by conjecture: are there some hadiths that are speculative?
* The Shaykh: No, these are certain. It is knowledge.
* The student: Are single-transmission (*aḥad*) reports speculative?
* The Shaykh: No. First, *aḥad* reports are not all speculative. Second, it is knowledge, because you are commanded to judge by it, and its meaning as knowledge is that you know you have hit the correct position. "Speculative" would mean that I conjecture I have hit the truth. But I am commanded to rule in this situation. If it becomes preponderant for me, I am commanded to act on it. So this is knowledge.
* A student: The evidence is speculative.
* The Shaykh: No, the evidence is speculative, but what does "speculative" mean? It means: I am not certain I am correct, because I am a *mujtahid* (one who exercises *ijtihad*, independent reasoning). Is that clear? But my judging by it when it has become preponderant for me, what happens?
* A student: Knowledge.
* The Shaykh: This is knowledge. But my being certain that I am correct is not possible, except in matters whose indication is definitive, such as: ﴿Prohibited to you is carrion﴾ [Al-Ma'ida 3], and ﴿Fasting is prescribed for you﴾ [Al-Baqara 183], and ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾ [An-Nisa 19], and ﴿For you is half of what your wives leave﴾ [An-Nisa 12], and what is similar to these.
* A student: Is the citing of this verse for legal matters or for general matters?
* The Shaykh: Which verse?
* A student: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance﴾ [An-Nahl 43].
* The Shaykh: It is general.
* A student: Meaning, for anything a person does not know, he asks about it?
* The Shaykh: Yes, he asks about it, (...) but not like the Bedouin who drinks water and says, "Boy, it is sweet!" That is not appropriate.
* A student: Shaykh, in general worldly matters, did Allah, Exalted is He, clarify in the revelation of the Book?
* The Shaykh: Yes, in two verses: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [Al-Anbiya 7]. And He said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know (43), with clear proofs and scriptures. And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may clarify to the people what has been sent down to them﴾ [An-Nahl 43–44].
* A student: ﴿with clear proofs and scriptures﴾: what is its place in *iʿrab* (grammatical analysis)?
* The Shaykh: It is connected to ﴿you do not know﴾: if you do not know with clear proofs and scriptures. It is also possible that ﴿with clear proofs and scriptures﴾ is connected to ﴿the people of remembrance﴾: the people of remembrance with clear proofs and scriptures. If the verse does not include it verbally, it includes it in meaning, that is, by *qiyas* (analogical reasoning). Whatever you do not know, ask about it.
* A student: Is one not to deduce from the verse regarding worldly matters?
* The Shaykh: Yes, one deduces it, because we said: if the absolute verse does not include it. For there are two verses: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾, and a second verse: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know, with clear proofs and scriptures﴾. Did you understand? The first is absolute, the second is restricted. If we say the verse does not include worldly matters verbally, it includes them by analogy. This is the method now. Take someone who does not know the way out, for example, when he travels to Makkah, and does not know the road.
* A student: No, we believe in that, but we say: do we carry the verse on this?
* The Shaykh: Yes, we carry the verse either by verbal inclusiveness or by inclusiveness in meaning, which is *qiyas*.
* A student: Is there not a rank between taqlid and ijtihad?
* Another student: That is, if absolute ijtihad has a rank, it is ijtihad within a specific school.
* Another student: One does not do ijtihad within a specific school. Is it one mujtahid and another *muqallid*?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is possible for a mujtahid to become a *muqallid*. That is, a mujtahid in some matters and a *muqallid* in others.
* A student: But people's explanation of taqlid is that it is not *ittiba'* (following). Some say there is a difference: something called taqlid and something called *ittiba'*?
* The Shaykh: No. If it is without evidence, it is taqlid. That is, accepting another's saying without evidence is taqlid. If it is with evidence, it is not taqlid. Therefore it is not correct to call our following of the Messenger ﷺ taqlid. It is not correct to call it taqlid, but *ittiba'*, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Aal ʿImran 31]. Why? Because his ﷺ saying and Sunnah are evidence.
* A student: So does one who follows evidence become a *muqallid*, or does he become something else?
* The Shaykh: No, he is not a *muqallid* and he is not merely a follower. He is a follower of evidence.
* A student: So there is a difference, a rank?
* The Shaykh: No, there is no rank. There is a difference in meaning. The *muqallid* is one who follows someone whose saying it is not obligatory to accept, and the *mutabaʿ* (follower) is one who follows someone whose saying it is obligatory to accept.
* A student: And is he not a mujtahid?
* The Shaykh: The mujtahid judges by evidence. And the evidence comes from where? From the Messenger ﷺ, from the Book and Sunnah. So whoever rules by that is called a mujtahid and is called a *mutabaʿ*. As for the one who cannot know that himself from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, he is called a *muqallid*.
* A student: (...)
* The Shaykh: This evil: we say, do not do it if you know it is evil. An evil is not to be done. But the matter is: if you want to know it, whom do you ask?
* A student: Those who know it.
* The Shaykh: You ask those who know it. Yes.
* A student: Shaykh, can we take from the verse that (...)?
* The Shaykh: It may be taken from it that the person who confines himself to mere recitation resembles those Jews in this respect. We mentioned this earlier in the tafsir: it is obligatory upon us to read Allah's Book, reflect on its meaning, and apply it, as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to do.
* A student: Shaykh, regarding *amani* being from knowledge, He said: ﴿they know not the Scripture except amani﴾. Are *amani* from knowledge?
* The Shaykh: Yes. Recitation is from knowledge, meaning you know its wording. Some say the exception here is disconnected (*munqatiʿ*), and the meaning is: except in the sense of that. But the correct view is that it is connected, and there is no problem, for knowing the wording is a type of knowledge.
* A student: What is the *iʿrab* of *amani*?
* The Shaykh: *Amani* is governed by ﴿they know not﴾. So ﴿the Scripture﴾ is the first object, and *amani* is the second object.
* A student: It has become *mufarragh* (an exception where the stated object is missing).
* The Shaykh: Yes, *mufarragh*. The second object.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 75–78 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you, when a group of them used to hear the speech of Allah and then distort it after they had understood it, while they knew?﴾ [al-Baqarah 75].

﴿Afa-tatma'una﴾ The hamza (the interrogative particle) is for asking a question, and what is meant is denial and despair: that is, to make the Muslims despair that these Jews would believe them. His words ﴿tatma'una﴾: ṭama' (hope, desire) means hope accompanied by strong desire. That is, "you hope for something with eagerness," because one who hopes for a thing with desire for it is said to be "ṭami'a fīhi" (he longed for it). So it means you long for this thing.

His words ﴿an yu'minū lakum﴾: the word īmān (faith) here means taṣdīq (affirming as true), that is, that they would affirm you as true and follow you. This is a remote matter, as shown by His words ﴿and when a group of them﴾. The wāw here is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāl), and qad is for emphasis (taḥqīq), so the clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the wāw in ﴿yu'minū lakum﴾. That is, "while in fact a group of them used to hear the speech of Allah."

His words ﴿wa-qad kāna farīqun minhum﴾: farīq means a group (ṭā'ifa). His words ﴿minhum﴾ mean: from the Jews who were in Madinah.

His words ﴿yasma'ūna kalāma Allāh﴾: is this hearing actually hearing the speech of Allah, glorified and exalted, or hearing the Torah being recited, as in His words: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection until he hears the speech of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah 6]? Both possibilities are open. For this reason some scholars said: the group here refers to those whom Musa chose, seventy men, for the appointed time of Allah, glorified and exalted. When Allah spoke to him and they heard him speaking with Allah, they said: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly﴾ [al-Baqarah 55], and they distorted the speech of Allah. Others said: rather, what is meant by hearing the speech of Allah is their hearing of the Torah being recited, and yet they distorted it after they had understood it. In that case His words ﴿yasma'ūna kalāma Allāh﴾ mean "from someone else," as in His words: ﴿until he hears the speech of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah 6].

His words ﴿thumma yuḥarrifūnahu min ba'di mā 'aqalūhu﴾: taḥrīf (distortion) means change. From it comes their saying: "ḥarraftu al-dābba," meaning I changed its direction. Taḥrīf means change, and it is of two kinds: verbal change and meaning change. As for verbal change, it means changing the wording itself, like the Jews' statement when they were told: ﴿Enter the gate prostrating and say: "Ḥiṭṭah"﴾ [al-Baqarah 58]. They said: "Ḥinṭah fī sha'īrah" (wheat in barley). Look, ḥiṭṭah: they changed it, saying "ḥinṭah." Do we call this a change?

* Student: Verbal.

* The Shaykh: Verbal, a verbal change. And like what some innovators (mubtadi'ah) from this Ummah changed in the speech of Allah: ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa with direct speech﴾ [al-Nisa' 164], where they read it as "wa-kallama Allāha Mūsā taklīman," so that the speaking would come from Musa, because they said: Allah does not speak, and Allah forbid. So "wa-kallama Allāha Mūsā taklīman." We call this a verbal distortion. It is followed by meaning distortion. Sometimes the meaning is not changed by it. A verbal distortion may not change the meaning, but it is still a crime and an aggression. For example, if one says "al-ḥamdu lillāhi" and says "al-ḥamdu lillāhi" with a different vowel, the meaning does not change, but the wording has changed. Usually this kind of verbal distortion that does not change the meaning happens only from an ignorant person, or from a person who wants to confuse people, even if the meaning does not differ. These people distorted the words, and an example of distorting words is what we said: ﴿and say "Ḥiṭṭah"﴾ [al-Baqarah 58], and they said "Ḥinṭah."

Meaning distortion is to leave the wording as it is, but change its meaning and say: "what is meant by it is such-and-such," which Allah does not intend by it. For example, those who said regarding ﴿He established Himself over the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf 54] that it means "istawlā 'alā al-'arsh" (He seized the Throne). And they said regarding the two hands that they mean power and blessing and similar things. These people distorted the meaning and did not distort the wording. The wording remains as it is, but they changed the meaning. Because istawā 'alā al-'arsh, what does it mean? It means He rose above it and settled on it. It does not mean "istawlā 'alayhi" (seized it). Rather, its meaning is He rose above it and settled. Likewise, the hand is meant as a real hand, but it is not like our hands, because Allah says: ﴿There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura 11].

They distort the speech of Allah. The speech of Allah, that is, the Torah with respect to the Jews, because it is the speech of Allah, glorified and exalted; Allah wrote it for Musa with His own hand. They distort the speech of Allah.

His words ﴿min ba'di mā 'aqalūhu﴾: ﴿'aqalūhu﴾ means they understood it. The purpose of this phrase ﴿min ba'di mā 'aqalūhu﴾ is to establish that their distortion was done knowingly. Some people distort the words out of ignorance. If someone came and read the Qur'an and broke it, not pronouncing its letters properly, do we say: this is a distorter or not?

* Student: A distorter.

* The Shaykh: A distorter, but not knowingly. The one who incurs punishment is the one who does it after knowledge. For this reason He said: ﴿after they had understood it﴾. They understood it and comprehended it, but they, may Allah protect us, distorted it and changed it.

﴿wa-hum ya'lamūn﴾ means: they know that distortion is prohibited and impermissible, but they transgressed the limits and distorted the speech of Allah. If this is the case regarding their own book, that they distort the speech of Allah after they understood it while they knew, then does anyone hope that they would believe in the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him? No. For this reason they did not believe. None of the Jews believed except a small group. Most of them remained in their disbelief, and what happened, praise be to Allah, happened: their being attacked and expelled from their homes, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿He made you inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth﴾ [al-Ahzab 27]. So it is far-fetched that these people would believe you, because they distort the speech of Allah ﴿after they had understood it, while they knew﴾.

By the way, they say that... The Kuwaiti newspaper "al-Mujtama'" reported last year, on the twenty-fourth of Rabi' al-Thani, that the Christians abridged the Gospel. They abridged about forty percent of it, because they said: these words serve no purpose. What is this considered? A distortion on top of a distortion, because its origin is distorted, and the Torah too is distorted. Then these people came and found the text too long, and said: then let us shorten it. Let us take sixty percent of it, since there is blessing in it. Perhaps after some years they will take another forty percent, leaving twenty percent. O Allah, protect us.

In short, the habit of the Jews and Christians is distortion. But unfortunately, some from this Ummah have committed what the Jews and Christians committed, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "You will surely follow the ways of those before you" [agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari, no. 7320, and Muslim, no. 2669/6, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri; and Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 21897, from the hadith of Abu Waqid al-Laythi, and the wording is his]. So they distorted the Book of Allah and distorted the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is known. This is not distortion of the text. This is arrogance against acting upon it. Yes. Distortion is when one leaves the wording but says: its meaning is such-and-such. This is distortion. Distortion has occurred in the Book and the Sunnah, as we illustrated, with examples from this.

﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say: "We believe."﴾ The pronoun in ﴿idhā laqū﴾ refers to whom? It refers to the Children of Israel, and the Jews present in Madinah. ﴿When they meet those who believe﴾ means: when they encounter them and gather with them. His words ﴿alladhīna āmanū﴾ mean: those who believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Qālū﴾ is the answer to "idhā": when they meet, they say. Does speech happen with the tongue or with belief?

* The students: With the tongue.

* The Shaykh: With the tongue and with belief, but here they speak with the tongue.

﴿Qālū āmannā﴾ means: we believe as you believe. ﴿Āmannā⁠﴾ means: in the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). This is when they meet the believers.

﴿And when some of them are alone with others﴾ means: some of them withdraw. He did not say "bi-ba'ḍ" (with others) but said ﴿ilā ba'ḍ﴾ (to others), because "ilā" indicates going toward or retiring. That is, when some of them retreat to others, are alone with them, and withdraw with them: ﴿they say: "Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?"﴾ That is, some of them say to others: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you?﴾ The interrogative here is for denial. The pronoun in ﴿atuḥaddithūnahum﴾ refers to the believers in the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. That is: the Jews say to one another when they gather: how do you tell the believers, that is, those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, how do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord? That is: why do you tell them about the thing Allah disclosed to you through His knowledge, since you know it? The Jews know the Messenger (ﷺ) as they know their own sons, they have no doubt about him, but they abandoned belief in him out of arrogance. So they say: how do you tell these people about what Allah has disclosed to you, when He informed you of it?

﴿Afa-lā ta'qilūn﴾ is for rebuke. That is: where are your minds? If you tell them this and say: this one who was sent is true and is a prophet, and they argue with you about it before Allah, how will they argue with it before Allah? When? On the Day of Resurrection. In this is evidence that Allah, the Exalted, will set up a dispute between believers and disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, as many verses indicate, such as His words: ﴿Neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will separate you, and Allah is seeing of what you do﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 3], and His words: ﴿Thus those who do not know say the like of what they say. Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ﴾ [al-Baqarah 113]. Likewise, in the surah beginning with "Ha-Mim" [i.e., the surahs with that opening], that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is judged by Allah between him and his adversaries. The point is that Allah sets up a judgment between the believers and their adversaries on the Day of Resurrection. So here He says: ﴿that they may argue with you about it before your Lord﴾. The believers will say to the Jews on the Day of Resurrection: you informed us that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a true messenger, yet you disbelieved in him and took up arms against him. This is a clear proof...

* Student: Because of their saying: "We believe" (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, "we believe as you believe," that is, that the Messenger is true and that the religion is true.

﴿That they may argue with you about it before your Lord﴾: ﴿before your Lord﴾ means Allah, glorified and exalted, on the Day of Resurrection. Is the lām in His words ﴿li-yuḥājjūkum bihi﴾ a lām of purpose (ta'līl) or a lām of consequence (ʿāqiba)?

* Student: Of consequence.

* The Shaykh: The lām is a lām of consequence, because the lām attached to the present-tense verb, which puts it in the subjunctive, can be a lām of purpose and can be a lām of consequence. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, so that he would become an enemy and a grief to them﴾ [al-Qasas 8]. What do you think of this lām?

* The students: Of consequence.

* The Shaykh: Of consequence. They did not pick him up for this purpose. Had they known he would become an enemy and a grief, they would not have picked him up but would have killed him. But the consequence was that he became an enemy and a grief. Here, ﴿atuḥaddithūnahum bimā fataḥa Allāhu 'alaykum li-yuḥājjūkum bihi 'inda rabbikum﴾: is this a lām of consequence, or did they not tell the believers about the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, what Allah disclosed to them about his matter so that the believers would argue with them? Rather, in reality this establishes a proof against them without doubt, a clear proof that they acknowledged the Messenger (ﷺ), that Allah the Exalted sent him, and then they denied him and opposed him. A clear, evident proof.

His words ﴿afa-lā ta'qilūn﴾: I said the hamza is for asking and the meaning is rebuke. Here is the fā'. What is it coordinating with? I say that this occurs frequently in the Qur'an: ﴿afa-lā ta'qilūn﴾, ﴿afa-lā tadhakkarūn﴾, ﴿afa-lam yasīrū﴾, ﴿awa-lam yasīrū﴾, ﴿athumma idhā mā waqa'a āmantum bihi﴾ [Yunus 51], and similar. That is, the interrogative hamza comes before the coordinating particle. And it is known that the interrogative hamza has precedence (ṣadr) in its clause, correct?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: And there is no precedence when the wāw is present, because the wāw is coordinating. Some grammarians said: between the hamza and the wāw there is an omitted clause to which the other clause is coordinated, and this omitted clause is estimated according to what the context requires. Others said: rather, the hamza is placed first, and the coordinating particle has been delayed. That is, the coordinating particle has been moved from its place and the hamza placed in its position. According to this, what is the estimate?

* Student: Fa-alā ta'qilūn.

* The Shaykh: Fa-alā ta'qilūn. The estimate would be this. As for the first view, the estimate would be: "Have you been ignorant, so that you do not understand?" Or: "Have you been foolish, so that you do not understand?" In short, one estimates something appropriate according to the context. The first view is in reality more precise: the one who says the hamza enters upon something omitted is more precise. The second is easier, because the second does not require the hardship and effort of what one must estimate, and there is no need for it. So which does the beginning student of knowledge prefer?

* The students: The second.

* The Shaykh: The second view. Because it says, for example: the fā' here is a coordinating particle, the hamza precedes it, and it is coordinated with what came before. There is no need to burden oneself with the effort of estimation and finding the appropriate meaning.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they disclose?﴾ [al-Baqarah 77]. That is: how does one of them rebuke another for this matter, when, if they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and those with him and denied his prophethood and did not believe, Allah the Exalted would not be hidden from the matter? That is, whether they acknowledged or did not acknowledge before the Companions that the Messenger is true, Allah the Exalted knows about them.

His words ﴿Do they not know﴾: the interrogative here is for rebuke and denunciation of them. His words ﴿Do they not know that Allah﴾: is this a rebuke in which they have placed themselves in the position of the ignorant? Yes, it is like that. It does not appear to me that its meaning is confirmation (taqrīr), like His words: ﴿Did We not expand your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh 1], meaning: We have already expanded it for you. Although it is possible that the meaning is ﴿Do they not know?﴾, that is: they have already known that Allah knows what they conceal and what they disclose. But its being a rebuke is more emphatic, because rebuke indicates that they knew and were rebuked for it, for the action they took. This action they took is only the action of one who thinks that Allah does not know.

His words ﴿what they conceal and what they disclose﴾: what is meant by concealing here, O people? Is it what they hide within themselves, or the talk among some of them with others in secret?

* The students: It includes both.

* The Shaykh: Both? And ﴿what they disclose﴾?

* The students: The talk among some of them with others.

* The Shaykh: What they show to people. So His words ﴿what they conceal﴾ include what a person conceals in himself, and what he conceals from his people and his close companions. ﴿What they disclose﴾ is what a person announces to the general public. Allah the Exalted knows both, and nothing is hidden from Him.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾. ﴿Minhum﴾: from whom? From the Jews. ﴿Ummiyyūn﴾ is the plural of ummī, and the ummī is the one who does not understand reading, either he does not understand its wording or he does not understand its meaning. Even the one who does not understand the meaning is called ummī, because reading the wording without understanding its meaning is of no benefit. The ummī includes the one who does not know how to read and the one who knows how to read but does not know the meaning. For this reason He said: ﴿They know not the Book except wishful thinking﴾: ﴿They know not the Book﴾, that is, they do not understand it, and its knowledge does not reach their hearts. ﴿Except wishful thinking﴾: ﴿illā﴾ here is an exceptive particle of disconnection, meaning: but only wishful thinking. It could also be connected, meaning: they know it only with the knowledge of wishful thinking. And ﴿amānī﴾ is the plural of umniyyah (wish, desire), and umniyyah may have two meanings:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 75–78 (part 2 of 3):

The first of the two meanings is what a person wishes in his own self (tamanni, "wishing"). The second is recitation. The second meaning is more fitting to the verse, meaning: they do not understand the Qur'an, but they recite it without understanding. This is shown by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, Satan threw [something] into his wish﴾ [al-Hajj 52], meaning: into his recitation. From this is the saying of the poet about 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him:

*He recited the Book of Allah at the beginning of his night*
*and at its end he met the death of the watering places.*

Tamanna here means: he recited the Book of Allah. So His words ﴿except wishful thinking (amani)﴾ are the plural of umniyyah, and it means recitation. How many of them there are today among the Muslims! Most Muslims today do not know the Qur'an except as wishful recitation, and they are not eager to understand its meaning. This is contrary to reality, as Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said. He would say: Now, if a person were to read medicine, or read arithmetic, or read grammar, would he go over the books of these things, passing over them verbally and moving on? Or would he not reflect on their meanings and seek someone to explain and clarify them to him until he understands? Which is the reality? The second. So then, if you seek guidance through the Noble Qur'an, how will you be guided by it while you do not know its meaning? It is not possible. Yet with this Noble Qur'an, if you contemplate it, it will be made easy for you. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar 17].

Most people do not concern themselves with this aspect, namely reflecting on and contemplating the Noble Qur'an and knowing its meaning. Few have this as their way with the Qur'an. For this reason, the blessing of the Qur'an has now been removed from many people, because they seek blessing from it only verbally. To the extent that you hear some brothers in their shops, where they have a recorder of the Noble Qur'an, a recorder, and this recorder recites the Qur'an at a loud volume, while in the shop there are people who curse, revile, laugh, mock, lie in sales, and everything else. What is the reality of a person's position while the Book of Allah is over his head being heard? It is mockery of the Qur'an. Yet they say: this is their blessing. This is not its blessing. The blessing of the Qur'an lies in acting upon it and in the reward that follows from it. As for you humiliating the Qur'an, by Allah... meaning: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest description (al-mathal al-a'la)﴾ [al-Nahl 60]. If the king were in front of you now speaking through a loudspeaker, and the eyes were upon you, and he were speaking, and you were talking, mocking, laughing, and what (...)?

* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: You do not know (...). So how much more so with the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? The point is that I now say: with the great regret, many Muslims, in relation to the Book of Allah, are in this state, they know it only as wishful recitation.

He said: ﴿They only assume﴾. They do not know, because a person who does not know the words has no knowledge; he has nothing but assumption. And His words ﴿in them they only assume (in hum illa yazunnun)﴾: is this (in) operating or not operating?

* A student: Not operating.
* Another student: Because the negation has been annulled.
* The Shaykh: Because the negation has been annulled. This is non-operating, because the negation has been annulled, meaning: they are only assuming (...).

From His words ﴿Do you hope that they will believe for you﴾ to the end.

From this noble verse ﴿Do you hope that they will believe for you while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah and then distort them﴾ are derived several benefits:

* First: whoever does not believe in what is more apparent is further from believing in what is more hidden, because the one who hears the speech of Allah and then distorts it is further from believing the words of these people, meaning the Messenger ﷺ and his companions. The essence of the benefit: whoever does not believe in what is more apparent is further from believing in what is more hidden. ﴿Do you hope that they will believe for you while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah and then distort them﴾.
* The second benefit: Allah, glorified and exalted, consoles His Messenger ﷺ with what removes from him sorrow and grief, because the Messenger would grieve if these people did not believe. But Allah informs him that these are stubborn people, so the fault is not yours, but their evil state is what prevented their acceptance.
* The third benefit: the affirmation that Allah speaks, by His words ﴿hear the words of Allah﴾. The speech of Allah, blessed and exalted, is a true attribute that includes wording and meaning. He, glorified and exalted, speaks with letters and audible sounds. For this reason He said: ﴿hear the words of Allah﴾.
* The fourth benefit: the speech of Allah, glorified and exalted, is one of His active attributes (sifat fi'liyyah), considered in terms of what?

* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Its individual instances (al-aahad), considering its individual instances. As for the root of the attribute, it is an essential attribute (sifah dhatiyyah). The difference between essential and active attributes is that essential attributes are inseparable from the Essence of Allah, inseparable from His Essence eternally and everlastingly. What does "eternally" (azalan) mean? It means in the past. And "everlastingly" (abadan) means in the future. These are essential attributes. Active attributes are those connected to His will, so they occur when He wills. Based on this, we say: anger, is it of which of the two types?

* The students: Active.
* The Shaykh: Active. Pleasure is active, love is active, and many other actions: the istiwa' (rising) over the Throne, is it active? His elevation above creation?

* The students: Essential.
* The Shaykh: Essential.

* The fifth benefit: the refutation of the Ash'arites and others who hold that the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in the self, and that these letters are an expression of our speech and not the speech of Allah. They say: speech is the meaning subsisting in the soul, not the speech that is heard. They argue for their view with the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they say within themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ [al-Mujadilah 8], so Allah has made what is in the self a saying. And with the poet's words:

*Indeed speech lies in the heart,*
*and the tongue was only made a sign of the heart.*

They also argue: if it were said that Allah speaks with letters and sounds, He would be a locus for temporal events, and whatever is a locus for temporal events is itself temporal. But Allah, glorified and exalted, is the First before whom there is nothing, and the Last after whom there is nothing. Therefore His speech is a meaning subsisting in His self, and He creates sounds that are heard, which express what is in His self. Their speech is false. As for their argument from the verse ﴿they say within themselves﴾ [al-Mujadilah 8], we say: this saying is a restricted saying, ﴿within themselves﴾, and it is a proof against you, not for you, because it indicates that unrestricted speech is in the self, or otherwise?

* A student: Otherwise.
* The Shaykh: Otherwise. Had it not indicated this, the restriction "within themselves" would not have been needed. So praise be to Allah, no person argues with a sound proof except that his argument turns against him.

As for their saying, "Indeed speech lies in the heart," and so on, we say: firstly, this saying is attributed to al-Akhtal, and al-Akhtal came after the corruption of the tongue (Arabic). He was also a Christian man whose word is not relied upon. Then who said that he said it? It needs to be established that he said it, and even if it reaches him, there are defects beyond its reaching him.

As for their argument, the third point: that if His speech were with letters and sounds, He would be a locus for temporal events, and whatever is a locus for temporal events is temporal. It is said: who told you this proposition, that whatever is a locus for temporal events is temporal? Then we say: if what we commit to, that He is a locus for temporal events (...), the Creator and our restriction, does not imply a deficiency in the Creator, as if one said: eating is an attribute of perfection in the created being, and the one who does not eat is less than the one who eats. Therefore a person does not eat when he is ill and his health is impaired. And sleep is an attribute of perfection for the created being, so will you affirm it for Allah? We say: no, we do not affirm it for Allah, because it is an attribute of deficiency, and it is at the same time, in the created being, an attribute of deficiency. For this reason, when the created being is perfected in Paradise, does he need sleep or not? He does not need sleep for the perfection of his life. As for eating, he also does not need eating for his continuance, because he is eternal, but he needs eating for enjoyment and delight in it. Yes indeed.

The conclusion: His words ﴿until he hears the speech of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah 6] indicate that the speech of Allah, the Exalted, is audible, and that it is with a voice.

We still have a question remaining: are the letters with which Allah spoke the same letters that people use in their languages? What do you say?

* The students: They are.
* The Shaykh: Yes, they are the letters with which people speak in their languages. But the manner of their articulation and the sound with which they are uttered, this is what nothing resembles. We cannot say that the vocalization of Allah, glorified and exalted, with these words is like the vocalization of a human; this is not permissible, because ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 11]. As for the letters, they are the letters.

From this verse it is derived: were these Jews distorting the words of Allah, or not? Due to His words ﴿then they distort it after they had understood it﴾.

* The benefit, which I think is the seventh: the explanation of the ugliness of the distortion of these Jews, because they distorted after they had understood, after they had understood it. Is distortion after understanding (after understanding the meaning) greater or not?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Because the ignorant person may be excused for his ignorance, but the knowing person who understood the matter, his action is uglier, may Allah protect us, because he, may Allah keep us safe, has dared to disobey while knowing it. So it is greater.

* And in it also: evidence for the ugliness of distorting the words of Allah, and that this is one of the characteristics of the Jews, or not? Has this ummah also committed it? Yes, they have committed it. But verbal distortion is preserved; it is not possible to change the Qur'an in wording. If it were changed, I would be informed of it. Likewise in meaning: it is not possible for a meaning to be changed and for the distorted meaning to become established. Rather, Allah must raise up from the scholars of the Muslims someone who will nullify this meaning and refute it. But the point is that there has existed someone who distorted this Book, who distorted the speech of Allah. There have existed people who are fanatical and distort the verses according to their schools of thought, to the extent that you find some scholars, may Allah pardon us and them, distorting verses in a reprehensible way. How could they utter such a thing! If you wish for examples of this, refer to the books of branches of jurisprudence (furu') in fiqh, and also refer to the books of principles (usul) in creed, and you will find great distortion. Among the most distorting sects are the Rafidah (Rawafid). They have, in their interpretation of the Qur'an, may Allah protect us, great, large, and monstrous distortions. May Allah grant us well-being. They and others who have been afflicted with this calamity distort the speech of Allah after they had understood it.

His words ﴿while they know﴾: it is also derived from it that these Jews distorted after understanding while they knew that their act was reprehensible. So two reprehensible things were combined in them: the first reprehensible act: distortion after understanding the meaning; the second reprehensible act: knowing that this method is forbidden, and yet they distorted it. Do you know some of what they distorted verbally?

* A student: ﴿Say, "Hittah"﴾ [al-Baqarah 58].
* The Shaykh: It was said to them: ﴿Say, "Hittah"﴾, and they said: "Hintah" (wheat). And it was said: ﴿Enter the gate prostrating﴾, and they entered crawling on their backsides. Is this distortion or not?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Distortion in wording and meaning, and likewise in application: they distorted in application. In the Torah, the ruling of stoning was revealed for the adulterer if he was married (muhsan), and they distorted it, replacing this ruling with the claim that their faces are to be blackened, and the adulterer and adulteress are to be mounted on a donkey facing backward, and paraded through the markets. And they distorted, although the text of stoning is present in the Torah. Yes indeed.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal?﴾ From this verse is derived: a rebuke of these Jews for the distortion, meaning: are they in ignorance that ﴿Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal﴾?

* Also in it: a rebuke of the one who deserves it, and this is also legislated: that the one who deserves rebuke should be rebuked, and there is no transgression against him in that.
* Also among its benefits: the affirmation of the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge, by His words ﴿He knows what they conceal and what they reveal﴾.
* Also in it: the warning against opposing the command of Allah. From where does it include a warning against opposition?

* A student: ﴿that Allah knows﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, because the fact that Allah knows what a person conceals and what he reveals is undoubtedly a warning, meaning: beware lest Allah punish you. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾ [al-Baqarah 235].

In any case, these are four benefits from this verse, and let us return to what we had forgotten.

He said: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾, to the end of the verse.

* From it is derived: that among the Jews there are hypocrites, due to His words ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾, as He said at the beginning of the surah about the hypocrites: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you"﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].
* Also in it: evidence that treachery is one of the characteristics and natures of the Jews. From where is this taken?

* A student: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾.
* The Shaykh: What is the connection?
* The student: ﴿But when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you"﴾.
* The Shaykh: Meaning: this is a kind of treachery, or not? A kind of treachery against the believers, and treachery and deception are their nature.

* The third benefit: that some of them blame others when they return to their own people: ﴿And when some of them are alone with others, they say, "Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you?"﴾.
* The fourth benefit: knowledge is a opening (fath), due to His words ﴿what Allah has opened to you﴾, or not?

* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that knowledge is an opening. Allah opens to a person through it the various kinds of sciences and insights by which He illuminates his heart, so it is an opening.
* The fifth benefit: that the believer and the disbeliever will dispute before Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection, due to His words ﴿so that they may argue with you before your Lord﴾.
* The sixth benefit: the foolishness of these Jews who make their own action into a weapon against themselves. From where is this taken?

* A student: ﴿Will you not reason?﴾
* The Shaykh: ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ How can you tell them something that is a weapon against you? A weapon against yourself. At least if you have no shame, do what you wish. At least if you do not want to believe in the Messenger ﷺ, then do not inform them that the Messenger is true, because they say, "We believe," meaning that the Messenger is true, but they are, may Allah protect us, arrogant hypocrites.
* And in it: evidence for praising reason and wisdom, because their words ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ are a rebuke for this act, and that a person must be rational, such that he does not take a step without knowing where to place his foot. He should not walk blindly. Rather, a person should in all his affairs not speak without seeing what the result of his speech will be, and not act without seeing the result of his action. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or remain silent." [Agreed upon; recorded by al-Bukhari, no. (6018), and Muslim, no. (47/74), from Abu Hurayrah.]

As for a person speaking at random without caring about the consequences, this contradicts reason. Is it clear, O people?

* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: If you have other benefits, there is no harm. The matter is open to discussion.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, that their disbelief in the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is with knowledge, due to His words ﴿Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you?﴾. For this reason they became those upon whom is wrath, since they opposed the truth while knowing it.
* A student: ﴿so that they may argue with you before your Lord﴾: this is said by some of them to others. How do we derive a benefit from their words?
* The Shaykh: It is known, because Allah only mentioned it as an affirmation of it. We also mentioned in the commentary as a witness to it His words: ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will separate between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 3].

He said: ﴿And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Book except wishful recitation, and they only assume﴾.

**Commentary of Ibn ʿUthaymin (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Karim) on Surah 2, verses 75–78 (part 3 of 3):**

* It may be deduced from this verse that the term *ummi* (unlettered) applies to one who does not read, and also to one who reads but does not understand. Or not?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: By His saying: ﴿Unlettered, they know not the Scripture, except wishful thoughts﴾. The meaning of *amani* here is recitation.
* The second benefit: the censure of one who does not understand the meanings of Allah's Book. Is *ummi* a description of fault or a description of praise?
* Students: A description of fault.
* The Shaykh: It is a description of fault in origin, except in the case of the Messenger ﷺ, for it is a description of perfection for him, since it adds further confirmation of his prophethood (ﷺ).
* Also in it is evidence that whoever does not understand the meaning speaks only on the basis of conjecture (*ẓann*), by His saying: ﴿and they do not but conjecture﴾. The one who does not understand the meaning, the layman, now reads the Qur'an from beginning to end but does not understand its meaning. So when he speaks about a legal ruling of Allah's rulings indicated by the Book, what is his speech?
* Students: Conjecture.
* The Shaykh: Based on conjecture. For in reality he does not know, and knowledge is not possible except when one understands the meaning.
* Also in it: evidence for the censure of judging by conjecture, and that it is a trait of the Jews. This is found often among some people who love to be called scholars. You find him issuing fatwas without knowledge, and perhaps he issues a ruling that contradicts the Qur'an and Sunnah while not knowing. Can we deduce from this that the *muqallid* (one who follows *taqlid*, blind imitation) is not a scholar?
* A student: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: What is the reason?
* A student: Because he does not understand.
* The Shaykh: Yes, because he does not understand. In reality he does not understand the meaning. The *muqallid* does not understand, so he is not a scholar. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: the scholars agreed (*ijma'*, scholarly consensus) that the *muqallid* is not counted among the scholars. The *muqallid* is not a scholar. At most he is a copy of a book, and the book is more precise than him, for the book does not forget, whereas he may forget. But this does not mean we censure taqlid absolutely. Taqlid in its proper place is obligatory. And when is its place? When one is unable to derive proof (*istidlal*). If one does not know, it becomes obligatory for him to follow taqlid, by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know, with clear proofs and scriptures﴾ [An-Nahl 43–44]. The one who does not know: is his duty to ask, or what should he do?
* A student: Shaykh, judging by conjecture: are there some hadiths that are speculative?
* The Shaykh: No, these are certain. It is knowledge.
* The student: Are single-transmission (*aḥad*) reports speculative?
* The Shaykh: No. First, *aḥad* reports are not all speculative. Second, it is knowledge, because you are commanded to judge by it, and its meaning as knowledge is that you know you have hit the correct position. "Speculative" would mean that I conjecture I have hit the truth. But I am commanded to rule in this situation. If it becomes preponderant for me, I am commanded to act on it. So this is knowledge.
* A student: The evidence is speculative.
* The Shaykh: No, the evidence is speculative, but what does "speculative" mean? It means: I am not certain I am correct, because I am a *mujtahid* (one who exercises *ijtihad*, independent reasoning). Is that clear? But my judging by it when it has become preponderant for me, what happens?
* A student: Knowledge.
* The Shaykh: This is knowledge. But my being certain that I am correct is not possible, except in matters whose indication is definitive, such as: ﴿Prohibited to you is carrion﴾ [Al-Ma'ida 3], and ﴿Fasting is prescribed for you﴾ [Al-Baqara 183], and ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾ [An-Nisa 19], and ﴿For you is half of what your wives leave﴾ [An-Nisa 12], and what is similar to these.
* A student: Is the citing of this verse for legal matters or for general matters?
* The Shaykh: Which verse?
* A student: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance﴾ [An-Nahl 43].
* The Shaykh: It is general.
* A student: Meaning, for anything a person does not know, he asks about it?
* The Shaykh: Yes, he asks about it, (...) but not like the Bedouin who drinks water and says, "Boy, it is sweet!" That is not appropriate.
* A student: Shaykh, in general worldly matters, did Allah, Exalted is He, clarify in the revelation of the Book?
* The Shaykh: Yes, in two verses: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [Al-Anbiya 7]. And He said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know (43), with clear proofs and scriptures. And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may clarify to the people what has been sent down to them﴾ [An-Nahl 43–44].
* A student: ﴿with clear proofs and scriptures﴾: what is its place in *iʿrab* (grammatical analysis)?
* The Shaykh: It is connected to ﴿you do not know﴾: if you do not know with clear proofs and scriptures. It is also possible that ﴿with clear proofs and scriptures﴾ is connected to ﴿the people of remembrance﴾: the people of remembrance with clear proofs and scriptures. If the verse does not include it verbally, it includes it in meaning, that is, by *qiyas* (analogical reasoning). Whatever you do not know, ask about it.
* A student: Is one not to deduce from the verse regarding worldly matters?
* The Shaykh: Yes, one deduces it, because we said: if the absolute verse does not include it. For there are two verses: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾, and a second verse: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know, with clear proofs and scriptures﴾. Did you understand? The first is absolute, the second is restricted. If we say the verse does not include worldly matters verbally, it includes them by analogy. This is the method now. Take someone who does not know the way out, for example, when he travels to Makkah, and does not know the road.
* A student: No, we believe in that, but we say: do we carry the verse on this?
* The Shaykh: Yes, we carry the verse either by verbal inclusiveness or by inclusiveness in meaning, which is *qiyas*.
* A student: Is there not a rank between taqlid and ijtihad?
* Another student: That is, if absolute ijtihad has a rank, it is ijtihad within a specific school.
* Another student: One does not do ijtihad within a specific school. Is it one mujtahid and another *muqallid*?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is possible for a mujtahid to become a *muqallid*. That is, a mujtahid in some matters and a *muqallid* in others.
* A student: But people's explanation of taqlid is that it is not *ittiba'* (following). Some say there is a difference: something called taqlid and something called *ittiba'*?
* The Shaykh: No. If it is without evidence, it is taqlid. That is, accepting another's saying without evidence is taqlid. If it is with evidence, it is not taqlid. Therefore it is not correct to call our following of the Messenger ﷺ taqlid. It is not correct to call it taqlid, but *ittiba'*, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Aal ʿImran 31]. Why? Because his ﷺ saying and Sunnah are evidence.
* A student: So does one who follows evidence become a *muqallid*, or does he become something else?
* The Shaykh: No, he is not a *muqallid* and he is not merely a follower. He is a follower of evidence.
* A student: So there is a difference, a rank?
* The Shaykh: No, there is no rank. There is a difference in meaning. The *muqallid* is one who follows someone whose saying it is not obligatory to accept, and the *mutabaʿ* (follower) is one who follows someone whose saying it is obligatory to accept.
* A student: And is he not a mujtahid?
* The Shaykh: The mujtahid judges by evidence. And the evidence comes from where? From the Messenger ﷺ, from the Book and Sunnah. So whoever rules by that is called a mujtahid and is called a *mutabaʿ*. As for the one who cannot know that himself from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, he is called a *muqallid*.
* A student: (...)
* The Shaykh: This evil: we say, do not do it if you know it is evil. An evil is not to be done. But the matter is: if you want to know it, whom do you ask?
* A student: Those who know it.
* The Shaykh: You ask those who know it. Yes.
* A student: Shaykh, can we take from the verse that (...)?
* The Shaykh: It may be taken from it that the person who confines himself to mere recitation resembles those Jews in this respect. We mentioned this earlier in the tafsir: it is obligatory upon us to read Allah's Book, reflect on its meaning, and apply it, as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to do.
* A student: Shaykh, regarding *amani* being from knowledge, He said: ﴿they know not the Scripture except amani﴾. Are *amani* from knowledge?
* The Shaykh: Yes. Recitation is from knowledge, meaning you know its wording. Some say the exception here is disconnected (*munqatiʿ*), and the meaning is: except in the sense of that. But the correct view is that it is connected, and there is no problem, for knowing the wording is a type of knowledge.
* A student: What is the *iʿrab* of *amani*?
* The Shaykh: *Amani* is governed by ﴿they know not﴾. So ﴿the Scripture﴾ is the first object, and *amani* is the second object.
* A student: It has become *mufarragh* (an exception where the stated object is missing).
* The Shaykh: Yes, *mufarragh*. The second object.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 75–78 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you, when a group of them used to hear the speech of Allah and then distort it after they had understood it, while they knew?﴾ [al-Baqarah 75].

﴿Afa-tatma'una﴾ The hamza (the interrogative particle) is for asking a question, and what is meant is denial and despair: that is, to make the Muslims despair that these Jews would believe them. His words ﴿tatma'una﴾: ṭama' (hope, desire) means hope accompanied by strong desire. That is, "you hope for something with eagerness," because one who hopes for a thing with desire for it is said to be "ṭami'a fīhi" (he longed for it). So it means you long for this thing.

His words ﴿an yu'minū lakum﴾: the word īmān (faith) here means taṣdīq (affirming as true), that is, that they would affirm you as true and follow you. This is a remote matter, as shown by His words ﴿and when a group of them﴾. The wāw here is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāl), and qad is for emphasis (taḥqīq), so the clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the wāw in ﴿yu'minū lakum﴾. That is, "while in fact a group of them used to hear the speech of Allah."

His words ﴿wa-qad kāna farīqun minhum﴾: farīq means a group (ṭā'ifa). His words ﴿minhum﴾ mean: from the Jews who were in Madinah.

His words ﴿yasma'ūna kalāma Allāh﴾: is this hearing actually hearing the speech of Allah, glorified and exalted, or hearing the Torah being recited, as in His words: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection until he hears the speech of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah 6]? Both possibilities are open. For this reason some scholars said: the group here refers to those whom Musa chose, seventy men, for the appointed time of Allah, glorified and exalted. When Allah spoke to him and they heard him speaking with Allah, they said: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly﴾ [al-Baqarah 55], and they distorted the speech of Allah. Others said: rather, what is meant by hearing the speech of Allah is their hearing of the Torah being recited, and yet they distorted it after they had understood it. In that case His words ﴿yasma'ūna kalāma Allāh﴾ mean "from someone else," as in His words: ﴿until he hears the speech of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah 6].

His words ﴿thumma yuḥarrifūnahu min ba'di mā 'aqalūhu﴾: taḥrīf (distortion) means change. From it comes their saying: "ḥarraftu al-dābba," meaning I changed its direction. Taḥrīf means change, and it is of two kinds: verbal change and meaning change. As for verbal change, it means changing the wording itself, like the Jews' statement when they were told: ﴿Enter the gate prostrating and say: "Ḥiṭṭah"﴾ [al-Baqarah 58]. They said: "Ḥinṭah fī sha'īrah" (wheat in barley). Look, ḥiṭṭah: they changed it, saying "ḥinṭah." Do we call this a change?

* Student: Verbal.

* The Shaykh: Verbal, a verbal change. And like what some innovators (mubtadi'ah) from this Ummah changed in the speech of Allah: ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa with direct speech﴾ [al-Nisa' 164], where they read it as "wa-kallama Allāha Mūsā taklīman," so that the speaking would come from Musa, because they said: Allah does not speak, and Allah forbid. So "wa-kallama Allāha Mūsā taklīman." We call this a verbal distortion. It is followed by meaning distortion. Sometimes the meaning is not changed by it. A verbal distortion may not change the meaning, but it is still a crime and an aggression. For example, if one says "al-ḥamdu lillāhi" and says "al-ḥamdu lillāhi" with a different vowel, the meaning does not change, but the wording has changed. Usually this kind of verbal distortion that does not change the meaning happens only from an ignorant person, or from a person who wants to confuse people, even if the meaning does not differ.
