A student: O Shaykh, you said that the objection to this is His saying ﴿kadhdhabtum﴾ ("you denied") together with ﴿taqtulun﴾ ("you kill"). It is said that denial became an inherent characteristic of them, so it does not need to be specified, and the attribute is continuous?

The Shaykh: If it were in the nominal sentence, this explanation would be valid, because the nominal sentence indicates continuity. But the verbal sentence does not. Indeed, they said that the verbal sentence in the present tense indicates occurrence and continuity.

The student: But is the past tense not less than the present?

The Shaykh: It does not appear so to me. And for this reason, it appears to me, and Allah knows best, that observing the endings of the verses is the strongest thing; it is a verbal consideration.

A student: Poison him (...)?

The Shaykh: No, they poisoned him with it. They said: "If you are a prophet, it will not harm you; and if you are a liar, we will be rid of you." Thus they said, but it did not harm him, until Allah the Exalted completed what He willed of his call.

﴿And they said: our hearts are ghulf﴾ [al-Baqarah 88]. We ask Allah for well-being. This is a corrupt argument. Who said it? The Children of Israel. ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾: the plural of aghlaf, and the aghlaf is the one upon which there is a covering (ghilaf), meaning covered, so that what these messengers call to does not reach it. It is like the saying of some people: "By Allah, Allah did not guide us to pray," or "Allah did not guide us to do such-and-such." This is a lie, for Allah says: ﴿We guided him to the two paths﴾ [al-Balad 10], meaning We clarified for him the path of good and the path of evil. This is what is incumbent upon Allah. ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance, and indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾ [al-Layl 12-13]. So what is incumbent upon Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, He has completed; what remains is what is incumbent upon you. These people say: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾. "Ghulf" is the plural of aghlaf, which is that which has been covered with something, with a sheath that prevents matters from reaching it. They say this as an excuse on their own behalf for not accepting the truth, meaning they excuse themselves from accepting it by saying that their hearts are ghulf. Is this true? No. If they had returned to their natural disposition (fitrah), their hearts would not have been ghulf. But what happened is that what became the cause of the covering over the hearts, which is disbelief, occurred. For this reason He said: "Bal" ("rather"). And "bal" here is for al-idrab al-ibtali ("the retractive/annulling 'rather'"), not for al-idrab al-intiqali ("the transitional 'rather'"), the annulling idrab.

You know that idrab (the use of "bal") divides into two types: the transitional idrab, which does not necessarily entail the nullification of what was negated, and the annulling idrab, which entails the nullification of what was negated. Do you understand? You say: "I struck Zayd, rather 'Amr." What is this? This is annulling. That is, you have nullified the first and attributed the judgment to the second. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has caught up regarding the Hereafter; rather, they are in doubt about it; rather, they are blind to it﴾ [al-Naml 66]. That is transitional: their states changed. Their knowledge regarding the Hereafter was lost, then doubt occurred to them, then blindness, and Allah forbid. Here, however, it is annulling idrab: Allah nullified what they claimed and clarified the real cause, which is Allah's curse upon them, and Allah forbid: ﴿Rather, Allah cursed them﴾. ﴿Cursed them﴾ means He expelled them and removed them from His mercy. The curse means expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah. But is this curse an injustice, or is it due to something from themselves?

The students: Due to something from themselves.

The Shaykh: And what is it?

The students: Lying and (...).

The Shaykh: ﴿Allah cursed them for their disbelief﴾. The "bi" here is causal, meaning: because of their disbelief they were cursed, so a seal was placed upon their hearts, as in His saying: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14], those who, when the Qur'an is recited to them, say: ﴿This is only the legends of the former peoples﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 13]. Why do they say of these magnificent, impactful, stirring verses that they are the legends of the ancients? Because a covering was placed over their hearts. For this reason He followed it with: ﴿No!﴾, meaning they are not the legends of the ancients, ﴿rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts﴾. Thus they did not reach the truth. We have said many times that if a person reads the Qur'an and does not find it affecting his heart, let him know that there are sins that have covered the heart, because when the Qur'an reaches the heart, it must affect it. ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart out of fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that they may reflect﴾ [al-Hashr 21]. If the Qur'an reached the heart, it would necessarily affect it. So if a person is not affected by reciting the Qur'an, that is evidence that there is a barrier preventing the Qur'an from reaching his heart, namely sins. Let him seek help from Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, seek forgiveness, and repent, so that Allah may remove this effect from him. ﴿Rather, Allah cursed them for their disbelief, so little﴾. ﴿For their disbelief﴾: the word "kufr" (disbelief) is a verbal noun (masdar) annexed to what? 

A student: To its object.

Another student: To its subject.

The Shaykh: It is annexed to its subject, because they are disbelievers. He said: ﴿so little is it that they believe﴾.

A student: The "ba" (bi), O Shaykh?

The Shaykh: The "ba" is causal.

﴿So little is it that they believe﴾. Pay attention to this verse. In ﴿qalilan ma yu'minun﴾ ("little is it that they believe") there is a difficulty here, because His saying ﴿bi-kufrihim﴾ ("for their disbelief") followed by ﴿qalilan ma yu'minun﴾ implies that they did not disbelieve in a way that expels them from the religion, because ﴿qalilan ma yu'minun﴾ means: there is faith among them, there is faith among them but it is little. The scholars differed in interpreting this verse. Some said: the paucity refers to the subject, not to the faith. And what is meant by "refers to the subject"? It means: few of them are believers. Do you understand? Others said: the paucity refers to the faith, but the Arabs use "little" to mean "none," as you say: "qalla ma ra'aytuhu qatt" ("I have hardly ever seen him"). This is the Arabic expression, and the meaning of "qalla ma ra'aytuhu qatt" is: I have never seen him at all. So "qalilan" here means that their faith is nonexistent. They view paucity as meaning non-existence. A third view on this matter: according to both of these views, "ma" is extra (za'idah), extra for emphasizing the paucity, because the meaning is: "they believe a little," whether we say it refers to the faith or refers to the believers, to the subject.

Some say that "ma" is not extra but negating, and the construction is: "fa-ma yu'minuna qalilan" ("so they do not believe, a little"). They say that this also has an implied omission, meaning: "nor much," as in His saying: ﴿And He made for you garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you from your violence﴾ [al-Nahl 81], meaning: they do not believe a little nor much. That is, if the little is absent from them, then the much is absent a fortiori. So they do not believe, neither a little nor much. For this reason the light of revelation does not reach them; their hearts are ghulf, good does not reach them. This is closer in meaning.

This is what raises a difficulty regarding "little." But it is problematic from the standpoint of the rules of the Arabic language, because it is well established in Arabic that the negating "ma" does not govern what comes after it over what comes before it. Here what came after it governed what came before it. This speaker says: who told you that the negating "ma" does not govern what follows it over what precedes it? Do you have a text on this from the Qur'an? A text from the Sunnah? What is the answer? No, but we have not seen it govern what precedes it. He says: "I have seen it." This verse shows that what follows it governs what precedes it. As long as no text has come saying that the negating "ma" does not govern what follows it over what precedes it, I say: this verse indicates that what follows it may govern what precedes it, and there is no objection to this.

Furthermore, by saying this I remove two difficulties. The first difficulty: I am freed from saying that "ma" is extra, because (...) "ma" is extra. The second: I am freed from the difficulty concerning the word ﴿qalilan﴾. Because in reality, when we read the verse, to what does the paucity refer? To the faith, or to the subject? ﴿ma yu'minun﴾: does it refer to the "waw" (the plural subject) or to the verb, which is the faith? The reality is that it refers to the faith, although these people have no faith, little or much. So by taking this course I have freed myself from these two difficulties, and the paucity remains as it is, and the meaning is: they do not believe, a little; and if the little is absent from them, the much is absent.

In any case, these people argued for their unbelief by saying that their hearts are ghulf. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that they are not ghulf, and that what made them ghulf is their disbelief. Allah cursed them, expelled them, and removed them from His mercy because of their disbelief. Therefore faith does not reach their hearts. As for hearts in themselves, they are open and receptive to faith, because the natural disposition (fitrah) is one with which all creation is created. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah"[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (1385) and Muslim (2658/22), and the wording is al-Bukhari's, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. And what is the fitrah? ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind﴾ [al-Rum 30].

Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, said: ﴿And when there came to them﴾ [al-Baqarah 89]. Of course, this aspect is closer to me.

A student: The last one.

The Shaykh: The last one is closer.

A student: (...).

The Shaykh: Who said that?

The student: (...).

The Shaykh: Yes. We say: yes, if it indicates (...) that it governs, it governs. You say: "Zaydan ma darabtu (...)": "I did not strike Zayd."

A student: O Shaykh, if the subject is "qalil," can "ma" not be a relative pronoun?

The Shaykh: ﴿fa-qalilan﴾? No. It creates a difficulty for us that (...). You say: "fa-qalil," meaning: "so those who believe are few."

﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and they had previously been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Baqarah 89], to the end. This, Allah forbid, is the conclusion of the matter: all the previous messengers they denied, and they did not accept what they brought. Then a Book came to them from Allah: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah﴾. Where is the response to ﴿lamma﴾ ("when")? ﴿they disbelieved in it﴾: this is the response. ﴿When there came to them a Book from Allah﴾, which is the Qur'an. He made it indefinite here for glorification: ﴿a Book﴾, and He emphasized its glory with His saying: ﴿from Allah﴾. But what is the evidence that it is from Allah? If they say: this is the speech of Muhammad ﷺ, what is the evidence?

The evidence is that Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, testified to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that it is from Him. He testified to him by His support of him. The Messenger says: this Qur'an is from Allah, and I struggle against you with it and upon it, and I will prevail over you. If it were from other than Allah, would he prevail by it? He could not; he would not prevail by it. If he prevailed by it, that would mean Allah supports falsehood, and this contradicts the wisdom of Allah. Therefore it is from Allah by the testimony of Allah to him, as Allah says: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness﴾ [al-Nisa' 166], to the end. Allah bears witness to what He sent down to you with both verbal testimony and practical testimony. His saying ﴿from Allah﴾ ascribes it to ﴿the Presence of Allah﴾ because it is His speech, as will come to us, Allah willing, in the benefits of the verse.

His saying: ﴿confirming what is with them﴾: ﴿confirming﴾. We have previously said that the confirmation of the Qur'an of what preceded it has two aspects:

A student: The confirmation of the Qur'an?

The Shaykh: For what preceded.

The student: That it is from Allah.

The Shaykh: No, it confirms what preceded. We mentioned that it has two aspects?

The student: First, that it is from Allah.

The Shaykh: No.

A student: The first aspect: that it is news of the past and the future.

The Shaykh: What kind?

The student: That is, its information in the past and in...

The Shaykh: No, no, that is not it.

A student: Because it agrees in the fundamentals, the fundamentals of the laws.

The Shaykh: No, no. We said: "confirming" (musaddiq), meaning that it judges that they are true. It says that they are truthful: ﴿The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers; each believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah 285]. So it says about the Torah that it is true, about the Gospel that it is true, about the Psalms that it is true. It confirms them, just as if a informant told me something and I said: "You have spoken truly," would I be confirming him?

The students: Yes.

The Shaykh: I would be confirming him. The second aspect of its confirmation of them is that it came in agreement with what they had announced. They announced it, and it came confirming it, coming in agreement with what they had foretold. Jesus, son of Mary, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ﴿I am the Messenger of Allah to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah, and giving good tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ [al-Saff 6]. So this Book came confirming this good tiding. This is the meaning of its being confirming of what preceded: it says that they are true, and that it came in agreement with what they had announced.

And His saying ﴿what is with them﴾: from where? From the Torah and the Gospel. This is clear that the Torah foretold the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, either by his name or by his description which applies to no one else. And His saying ﴿and they had previously﴾, meaning: before it came to them. Here, why is ﴿min qabl﴾ ("previously") vowelled with a dammah, and "min" is a preposition? Because it is indeclinable. We have already learned that "qabl" ("before"), "ba'd" ("after"), "fawq" ("above"), "taht" ("below") and similar words have four states, one of which is being built on the dammah when the genitive complement is omitted and its meaning is intended. In that case it is indeclinable on the dammah. So: ﴿and they had been, before it came to them, seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾.

﴿Yastaftihun﴾ ("they sought victory") means: they sought help, and they said: "Victory will be ours over you," meaning: victory over you. And His saying ﴿those who disbelieved﴾: from where? From the polytheists, who were the Aws and the Khazraj, because the Aws and the Khazraj were in disbelief; they were not People of the Book, as is well known. So they used to say: "A prophet will be sent, and we will follow him, and we will prevail over you." ﴿They sought victory﴾. But when it came to them, they did not recognize it and disbelieved in it, Allah forbid. There came to them the thing they knew, as they know their own sons, but they disbelieved in it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 87–89 (part 3 of 4):

﴿Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter. Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be helped.﴾ [al-Baqarah 86]. (...) They disbelieve in His signs; they only want by this the life of this world, because the reference in His words ﴿Those﴾ is to those previously mentioned, who believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part.

* The second benefit of this verse: this world and the Hereafter are rivals (ḍarratān), meaning that whoever wants one of them in full harms the other. As for the one who wants this world, there is no doubt that he harms his Hereafter. As for the one who wants the Hereafter, nothing of this world is lost to him, because of the Most High's words: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [al-Shura 20].
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Except when a person wants one of them in full, and especially when he wants this world; if he wants it, it harms his Hereafter. On the contrary, it does not harm him if we say that His words ﴿We will increase him in his tilth﴾ mean that He also gives him from this world.
* It also contains proof that the punishment continues for those who prefer this world over the Hereafter and make it a substitute for it, because of His words: ﴿Their punishment will not be lightened.﴾
* The fourth benefit: these people have no helper who can support them and protect them from the punishment of God, neither their gods nor their leaders. Rather, they will curse their leaders on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way."﴾ [al-Ahzab 67]. Likewise, their leaders will disown them: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed.﴾ [al-Baqarah 166]. The third verse: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister.﴾ [al-A'raf 38].

Then Allah the Most High said: ﴿And We gave Moses the Book, and followed him up with messengers.﴾

* From this noble verse is derived: the affirmation of the prophethood of Moses, because of His words: ﴿And We gave Moses the Book.﴾
* And from it is derived: the emphasis of an important report even when the addressee does not deny it, because of His words: ﴿And We gave﴾, which is emphasized with three emphasizers, although it was not addressed to someone who denies it. It has already passed us that emphasis of speech occurs in three situations:
First: when it is addressed to one who denies it. The scholars of rhetoric (balaghah) said that in this case emphasis is obligatory (wujūban).
When it is addressed to one who is hesitant, the scholars of rhetoric said that in this case emphasis is recommended (istiḥsānan).
The third: when the report is of extreme importance, it is emphasized even if it is addressed to someone who neither denies it nor is hesitant. Even if you address it to a person at the outset, and he is one of those concerned with important matters, then emphasizing it is good.
* The third benefit: the messengers who came after Moses followed his law among the Children of Israel, because of His words: ﴿and followed him up with messengers﴾. This is supported by the Most High's words: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted judge for those who were Jews, as did the rabbis and the scholars.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 44].
* The next benefit: the prophethood of Jesus is established, because of His words: ﴿And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, the clear proofs.﴾
* The next benefit: whoever has no father in the sharia sense is attributed to his mother, just as whoever has no father by destiny (qadar). Jesus son of Mary had no father by destiny; he had no father by the natural order (kawnan). Whoever has no legal father is like him, attributed to his mother, such as the child of illegitimacy, may Allah protect us. By this we know that the preponderant opinion among the scholars is that his mother is his ʿaṣabah (agnatic heir), and he is not an ʿaṣabah of his mother. This is because the scholars differed regarding one who has no legal father: does his mother take her share of the inheritance and the rest goes to her agnatic relatives, or does she take her share as a fixed portion (farḍ) and the rest as agnatic (taʿṣīb)? Is she a father to him, or a mother of a father? This second opinion is the correct and preponderant one, because her agnatic relatives relate through her. Her agnates relate through her; how then can they be agnates while she is not an agnate? For this reason, no agnate is found relating through a fixed-share holder; all agnates relate through agnates. Sometimes a fixed-share holder relates through a fixed-share holder, such as the maternal siblings, who relate through the mother and are themselves fixed-share holders. A fixed-share holder may relate through an agnate, such as the son's daughter, who relates through the son and is herself a fixed-share holder. But an agnate relating through a fixed-share holder is impossible. Therefore the correct view is that the ʿaṣabah of one who has no legal father is first his mother, then his agnates.
* A student: O Shaykh of hadith, the saying of the Prophet: «To the closest male man»? [[Agreed upon; reported by al-Bukhari (6732) and Muslim (1615/2) from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas.]]
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. (...) By consensus, it is not restricted; it specified males because most of them are males. Otherwise, full sisters along with daughters are agnates by consensus, and they are not males. A hadith in the Sunan also says: «A woman inherits three kinds of inheritance: her freed slave, her foundling, and her child whom she cursed (in li'an) over.» [[Reported by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (2906) and al-Tirmidhi in his Jami' (2115) from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa'.]]
* A student: Shaykh, what is the meaning of: «her child whom she cursed over»?
* The Shaykh: «Her child whom she cursed over» means: if a husband accuses his wife of adultery, may Allah protect us, claiming she committed adultery and that her child is not his, and the well-known mutual cursing (li'an) in Surat al-Nur takes place, then the child belongs to his mother and not to his father.
Also among the benefits: the next benefit: Allah gave Jesus son of Mary clear signs, both cosmic and legislative. His cosmic signs are more evident than his legislative signs, because he was given the signs of raising the dead and bringing them out of their graves, healing the blind and the leper, and that he would shape from clay the form of a bird, then breathe into it, and it would fly by Allah's permission. Likewise, he would inform them of what they eat and what they store in their houses. So these are many clear signs for Jesus son of Mary. It is said that the wisdom behind this is that medicine in his time had advanced greatly, so he came with signs that physicians could not match.
* The next benefit: Allah the Most High strengthened Jesus with Gabriel: ﴿And We supported him with the Holy Spirit.﴾
* The next benefit, also: among the ways God subjects creation to the angels is that they support whomever God commands them to support. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Hassan ibn Thabit: «O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit.» [[Its takhrij has already been mentioned.]]
* The next benefit: a demonstration of the arrogance (ʿutuww) of the Children of Israel and that they do not desire the truth: ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you became arrogant?﴾
* The next benefit, also: whoever of this nation is arrogant toward the truth when it does not agree with his desire is similar to the Children of Israel. Whether he tricks his way around it by distortion, or acknowledges that this is the truth but is arrogant toward it, he resembles the Children of Israel. We know that those who deviate from the truth fall into two categories: one category acknowledges it but openly denies it and admits being disobedient; his matter is clear and his path is what he has chosen. The other category is arrogant toward the truth and tries to distort the texts to suit its desires. This latter is worse than the first, more harmful to Islam than the first, because people are deceived by it. An example: some Arab states called to socialism; they invited people to it, made it widespread and praised it extensively. They began to bring ambiguous verses and hadiths and distort them to prove what they had adopted. They said that God says: ﴿He has coined for you an example from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein?﴾ [al-Rum 28]. They said: ﴿so that you are equal therein﴾, so this is partnership. «People are partners in three things: water, pasture, and fire» [[Reported by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (3477) from the hadith of a man from the Muhajirun, with the wording: «Muslims...».]]; also «Whoever has land, let him cultivate it, or let him lend it for cultivation» [[Agreed upon; reported by al-Bukhari (2340) and Muslim (1536/88) from the hadith of Jabir; the wording is Muslim's.]]; and the land cannot be leased (...) from these people. ﴿Those who have been favored with provision will not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess so that they would be equal in it.﴾ [al-Nahl 71].
In summary, we say that this is a kind of arrogance, but it is arrogance through deception, and it is worse than the first. So whoever follows this path from this nation resembles the Jews.
* A student: O Shaykh, is the first one denial (judūd) or arrogance?
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: The first is arrogance?
* The Shaykh: Yes, the first is arrogance, and this one is also arrogance, but this one plays tricks with the texts. Some people are arrogant toward the truth because it opposes their own desire, and some people are arrogant toward the truth because it came from someone they believe is beneath them. So they say: "You teach us? Who are you? You are a suckling infant (...)."
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: "What is this new religion?" and the like. This is arrogance toward the truth. Therefore, the obligation is that a person does not measure the truth by its speaker, but measures the truth by evidence. If he has evidence, praise be to Allah, that is what a person should seek.
* The next benefit: a clarification that the Children of Israel divided regarding those who came with what their souls did not desire into two groups: one group denied them, and another group killed them. Who do they deny and kill? It seems, and Allah knows best, that when a person has a strong and influential call, they rid themselves of him by killing him; and when the matter is less, they are content with denial, because when they deny him, people withdraw from him. This also exists in this nation. When they see a powerful preacher whom they cannot persuade people against by saying "this man is not upon the truth," if they tell people "this man is not upon the truth," people will not follow them. So what do they do? They kill him, plot against him either by trickery or openly, they put him on trial and to the gallows. So whoever follows this path from this nation resembles the Jews, and in him the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ) is fulfilled: «You will surely follow the ways of those who came before you.» [[Reported by al-Tirmidhi in his Jami' (2180) and Ahmad in al-Musnad (21897); the wording is Ahmad's.]]

Allah the Most High said: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are uncovered." Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.﴾

* From this verse is derived: those who did not accept the truth argued with what is not a valid proof. They said: ﴿Our hearts are uncovered (ghulf)﴾. What is the meaning of ghulf? Closed, so your speech does not reach them.
* The next benefit: whoever does what they did resembles them. Some people now, when you command them to do good, say: "By Allah, Allah did not guide us," may Allah protect us. They say: "Allah did not guide us." This is like those who said: ﴿Our hearts are uncovered﴾, and like those who said: ﴿Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you. It is the same for us whether we bear it impatiently or patiently; there is no escape for us.﴾ [Ibrahim 21]. The point is that there are people, and we always hear that when they advise their children, or a wife advises her husband, or the like, they say: "By Allah, Allah did not guide us, Allah did not guide us," may Allah protect us.
* A student: Smokers say the same.
* The Shaykh: And smokers, yes, smokers, that is correct. The point is that we say they said the same as the Jews' saying: ﴿Our hearts are uncovered.﴾
* Third: the hearts by their natural disposition (fiṭrah) are not uncovered; this is because of His words: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them﴾. This "rather" is for negation: the hearts are not uncovered so as to refuse the truth; rather, there is something else that prevented the truth from reaching them, namely Allah's cursing them because of their disbelief. In this is proof that the natural disposition, as a disposition, accepts the truth, but it has obstacles.
* The next benefit: causes, however strong they may be, have no effect if obstacles are added to them. Hearts, although created upon the upright religion, if obstacles are present, may Allah protect us, they are not enabled to attain guidance. It has been said: matters are not accomplished except by the presence of their causes and the absence of their obstacles.
* The next benefit: faith among these Jews is little, because of His words: ﴿so little is it that they believe.﴾ I think it has previously passed us that there is a difference among the exegetes and the grammarians (al-muʿribīn, those who analyze i'rab, grammatical case endings) regarding His words: ﴿so little is it that they believe.﴾ Is this littleness relative to the faith in a person's heart, or relative to quantity? There are two opinions here too. Some say it refers to quantity, meaning few of them believed (...). Others say it refers to quality, meaning they do not believe at all, neither little nor much. Faith is nonexistent; if one has no faith, whether little or much, then it is absent.
* A student: O Shaykh, is there a benefit in the cursing?
* The Shaykh: Yes, the establishment of causes, as in His words: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief.﴾ Is this what you want?
* The student: No, the cursing; is it permissible to curse? That they were cursed because of...?
* The Shaykh: No, no, it is a report, a report. It is a report: they were cursed for their disbelief. There is nothing else in it.
* The student: A benefit is taken from the report.
* The Shaykh: And what is it?
* The student: Whoever has the causes of cursing, is he cursed?
* The Shaykh: No. If we found a disbeliever, we do not say "may Allah curse you," but it is not permissible for us to invoke a curse upon him, because Allah forbade His Messenger (ﷺ) from this and said: ﴿You have no part in the matter; He either accepts their repentance or punishes them.﴾ [Al 'Imran 128]. But if he dies in disbelief, it is permissible to curse him by name. As for general curses, such as "the curse of Allah upon the disbelievers," there is no harm in it. The point is that it contains the establishment of causes, and this is important: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief.﴾
Based on this benefit, we refute the view of the Jahmiyyah who deny causes. It has already passed us in the study of Tawhid that the Jahmiyyah deny causes and say that God's acts are not for wisdom but only by mere will. The Ash'ariyyah became clever and said: "We do not affirm causes as the Qadariyyah affirm them, nor do we deny them as the Jahmiyyah deny them; rather, we say that the thing occurs at causes, not by them." They say: "We do not deny causes, but a cause is not that by which a thing occurs; rather, a thing occurs at it." So if you break a bottle with a stone, and the stone strikes it and collides with it, it did not break by the stone, but it broke at the stone. Likewise, if you slaughter a sheep and it dies, they say: it did not die by slaughter, but at slaughter. This talk is truly a fable, incomprehensible speech.
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: The Ash'ariyyah; yes (...).
* The student: And they claim soundness of intellect.
* The Shaykh: The point is that in this verse we have established causes, and this is a matter of natural disposition. Even if a person is left alone, even an animal knows the cause. Does it not seek water when thirsty, seek fodder when hungry, and seek shelter from heat and cold? It knows, for example, that entering this cave protects it from rain, cold, or sun; it knows that going to water and drinking saves it from destruction, and so on. So the affirmation of causes is in reality a natural matter upon which one is created; even animals are created upon it.

﴿When there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them, and they had previously been seeking victory over those who disbelieved.﴾

* From this noble verse is derived: first, that the Qur'an is from Allah, because of His words: ﴿a Book from Allah﴾.
* Second: the Qur'an is the speech of the Most High; the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, spoken in reality, because of His words: ﴿from Allah﴾. It is known that speech is not a body that subsists by itself, so as to say it is created. ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not too proud to worship Him﴾ [al-A'raf 206]. Who are these?
* The students: The angels.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 87–89 (part 4 of 4):

* The Shaykh: Can we say that the angels are an attribute of Allah, since Allah attributed them to Himself by saying "from Him"? No, because they are entities that subsist by themselves. But ﴿a Book from Allah﴾: "kitab" here means "maktub" (that which is written), and it is speech written down, which cannot stand on its own. So it is the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Is the Qur'an the speech of Allah in its wording and its meaning?
* The students: In its wording and its meaning.
* The Shaykh: In its wording and its meaning. Who are those who said that it is only meaning and not wording?
* The students: The Ash'aris.
* The Shaykh: The Ash'aris. The Jahmiyya and the Mu'tazila say: it is the speech of Allah in wording and meaning, but it is created, like the rest of creation. Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah say: it is the speech of Allah in wording and meaning, and it is uncreated; rather, it is one of the attributes of Allah.
* The next benefit, which is the third, I think: the highlighting of the virtue of the Qur'an, by His saying ﴿confirming what is with them﴾, and by His saying ﴿from Allah﴾. This is known, because whatever is an attribute of Allah is perfect. But His saying ﴿confirming what is with them﴾ is a highlighting of its virtue, and that it did not come with anything that contradicts those earlier books.
* The next benefit: that these Jews knew that the Prophet ﷺ would be sent, by His saying ﴿and before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved﴾, meaning they would seek help, that is, they would ask for victory or speak of it. So before the Qur'an was revealed, before the Messenger ﷺ came, they would say to the Arabs: a prophet will be sent who will descend with a book, and we will be victorious over you by means of him. When the matter came, ﴿when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it﴾. Notice that He said ﴿what they recognized﴾ and did not say "what they knew," because recognition (ma'rifa) is more specific than knowledge ('ilm), since, as they said, it is the unveiling after confusion. After they had anticipated the matter and awaited it, there came to them what they recognized with a definite recognition, as they recognize their own sons.
And also in it: * The next benefit: that the Jews, may the curses of Allah be upon them, did not submit to the truth, not even to what they acknowledged; they disbelieved in it, which shows their arrogance and stubbornness.
* The next benefit: that the disbeliever deserves the curse of Allah, and it is obligatory upon him, by His saying ﴿so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾. And cursing has already been explained to us as expulsion and distancing from the mercy of Allah.
* A student: Some scholars and exegetes cited, but (...), the permissibility of cursing a specific person from the verse of al-Baqara ﴿the curse of Allah and the angels and the people, all together﴾ [al-Baqara 161], and from the hadith "Do not curse him, for he loves Allah and His Messenger." They said: he prohibited cursing because he loves Allah and His Messenger, and the disbeliever certainly does not love Allah and His Messenger?
* The Shaykh: But this is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) texts. As for the first, there is no proof in it, because it is general, and generality clearly permits cursing them. As for the second, the meaning of the curse there is either that we say the intended cursing is reviling, or we say that this cursing of that man implies by its implication (mafhum) that whoever does not love Allah and His Messenger may be cursed. But this implication is opposed by an explicit statement (manțuq), which is stronger than it, namely that Allah, glorified and exalted, forbade His Prophet ﷺ to curse the leaders of disbelief, such as saying "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so," naming them, when they are leaders of disbelief (...) this.
* A student: Is this in prayer?
* The Shaykh: No, no, because Allah explained the reason, saying ﴿It is not for you to decide anything, whether He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them﴾ [Ali 'Imran 128] (...). Because it is in prayer, and what is forbidden in prayer is forbidden outside it, since supplication in prayer is permissible in itself, and the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said about Satan: "I curse you with the curse of Allah." So whoever deserves cursing may be cursed in prayer. The reason was indicated by Allah in His saying ﴿It is not for you to decide anything, whether He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them﴾ [Ali 'Imran 128]. As long as they are alive, Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Turner of hearts, and how many people were among the tyrants and leaders of disbelief and then became leaders of Islam.
* A student: 'A'isha forbade that when they would greet the Prophet ﷺ saying: "As-sam 'alayka?" (death upon you)
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, he forbade it, because this is a case of vulgarity (fuhsh and tafahhush). He said: "Allah does not love obscenity nor the use of obscenity."
* The student: Is this of that category?
* The Shaykh: It is possible, or it is by way of reciprocity, because they say "as-sam 'alayka," and it is permissible for you to invoke against whoever invokes against you in the same manner, but not with this harshness.
﴿ ﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 87–89 (part 1 of 4):

﴿And We followed up after him with messengers﴾. This expression recurs often, as in "laqad" (indeed/certainly): the lam is a lam of preparation for an oath (lam al-muwatti'ah), and qad is for emphasis (tahqiq). Accordingly, such an expression is emphasized by three emphatics: the implied oath, the lam that prepares for it, and qad.

And His saying: ﴿And We gave﴾ means We gave. Giving (al-iti'a') from Allah, glory be to Him, is divided into two kinds: legislative giving (iti'a' shar'i) and cosmic, decreed giving (iti'a' kawni qadari). If it is revelation, it is legislative giving; if it is something that nourishes the body, it is cosmic decreed giving. However, what nourishes the body may also be meant as legislative giving, by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, "Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger"﴾ [at-Tawbah 59]. The point is that what is revelation, by which souls are nourished, is legislative giving, and what is a substance by which bodies are nourished is cosmic decreed giving.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We gave them a great kingdom﴾ [an-Nisa' 54]. What is this? It is decreed giving. And His saying: ﴿We gave Musa the Book﴾ is legislative giving; that is, what is given in the legislative sense is a legislative matter.

His saying: ﴿Musa﴾ has already been mentioned: he is the greatest of the prophets of the Children of Israel, peace be upon him, and he was sent to Pharaoh and to the Children of Israel.

And His saying: ﴿al-Kitab﴾ means "the written," and writing is well known. It is derived from kathb, meaning gathering together, from which comes kataybah (a battalion) of horsemen, because they are gathered together. The meaning of "the Book" here is "the written," so it is fa'al in the sense of maf'ul. And what Book is it? The Torah.

﴿And We followed up﴾ means We caused to follow; ﴿qaffayna﴾ means "we made to follow," because the follower comes at the back (qafa)...
Everyone who came after him judged by his law. For this reason He said: ﴿And We followed up after him with messengers﴾, until the sequence reached ﴿And We gave Isa son of Maryam the clear proofs﴾. ﴿ataynaa﴾ means "We gave him," and it is legislative giving. And His saying: ﴿Isa son of Maryam﴾ — He attributed him to his mother; why?
* The students: Because he had no father.
* The Shaykh: He had no father. And His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿al-bayyinat﴾ (the clear proofs) is an adjective of an elided noun, its estimate being: "the clear signs." So what are these clear signs? Are they the miracles that Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah? Or are they the Gospel? Or both? Both: this and that. The Gospel is among the clear signs, and likewise the perceptible, sensory signs which are the miracles are also clear signs, such as reviving the dead and bringing them out of graves, healing the one born blind and the leper, and creating from clay the form of a bird, then breathing into it, so that it becomes a bird by Allah's permission [Aal 'Imran 49]. In the second reading: ﴿fa-yakunu ta'iran bi-idhni Allah﴾, meaning it actually flies. All of these are among the signs which 'Isa son of Maryam was given. For this reason He said: "We gave him the clear proofs," meaning the manifest clear signs that indicate he was a prophet, because what he brought cannot be accomplished by human beings. Scholars have mentioned that in the time of 'Isa, peace be upon him, medicine flourished and advanced greatly; yet however much physicians advance, they cannot heal the one born blind or the leper, nor revive the dead. Indeed they cannot even preserve the life of one whom death has come upon, let alone return his soul to him after his death. ﴿And We gave 'Isa son of Maryam the clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit﴾ [al-Baqarah 87]. ﴿ayyadnahu bi-ruh al-qudus﴾: ﴿ayyadnahu﴾ means "We strengthened him," like His saying: ﴿So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾ [as-Saff 14], meaning We strengthened them against their enemies. Its derivation is well known, being from al-ayd, meaning strength, as Allah said: ﴿And the heaven We built with power (bi-ayd)﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 47], meaning with strength. So the meaning of "ayyadnahu" is "We strengthened him."

And His saying: ﴿bi-ruh al-qudus﴾ is of the type of attributing a noun to its adjective, that is, "with the holy spirit." Al-qudus and al-qudss mean pure. What is meant by the Holy Spirit? The exegetes differed. It has been said: the intended meaning is the spirit of 'Isa, because it is a holy, pure spirit, which did not descend from the loins of a male, nor came out of the womb of a menstruating woman (i.e., one in her courses). He is therefore purified, so ﴿ayyadnahu bi-ruh al-qudus﴾ means: We strengthened him by his having come without a father. This is one view. The second view is that ﴿ruh al-qudus﴾ means the Gospel, because revelation is a spirit, as Allah said: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was]﴾ [ash-Shura 52]. It was also said: the intended meaning of ﴿ruh al-qudus﴾ is "His spirit," attributed to Allah, as in His saying: ﴿So We breathed into it of Our spirit﴾ [al-Anbya' 91], meaning the spirit of Allah. In that case it is not an attribution of a noun to its adjective, but an attribution of the created to its Creator. That is what is said.

The fourth view is that ﴿ruh al-qudus﴾ means Jibril, peace be upon him, by His saying: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 193–194], and His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr 4], and the Prophet's ﷺ saying to Hassan ibn Thabit when he was satirizing the polytheists: "O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (453) and Muslim (2485/152) from the hadith of Hassan and Abu Hurayrah.]], meaning with Jibril. This is the most correct of the views: that ﴿ruh al-qudus﴾ means that he was supported by Jibril, peace be upon him, who would accompany him, support him, strengthen him, and inspire him with the proof for his delivery. So the views become four:
* First: that ﴿ruh al-qudus﴾ is the spirit attributed to Allah, and on this view it is an attribution of the created to its Creator, and Allah, blessed and exalted, is al-Quddus and al-Quddus, ﴿the King, the Holy (al-Quddus)﴾ [al-Hashr 23].
* Second: the intended meaning of ﴿ruh al-qudus﴾ is the Gospel, because revelation is a spirit.
* Third: the intended meaning of ﴿ruh al-qudus﴾ is his own holy spirit, so it is not an attribution; "his spirit" means it is his spirit. The difference between it and the first view is that the first view makes "al-qudus" refer to Allah, whereas these make "al-qudus" the spirit itself.
* The fourth view is the most correct: that it is Jibril. The reason we prefer it is that if we say "We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit," whether we say the holy spirit or the spirit of Allah, there is no sense in that as a support for him, because his spirit preceded his existence before he was a prophet, and support by a thing requires that thing to be accompanying him at the time of the support.

As for the view that it is the Gospel, meaning he was supported by the Gospel, the saying of Allah refutes it: ﴿Remember My favour upon you and upon your mother, when I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit, you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and when I taught you the Book and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [al-Ma'idah 110]. The meaning of ﴿I taught you the Book and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel﴾ along with "I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit" would be close to repetition, and the Qur'an, when the speech can be made to carry new information (ta'sis) it is preferable to it being emphasis (ta'kid). In the Qur'an and other speech, when it is uncertain whether a sentence is establishing (ta'sis), each clause having its own independent meaning, or emphasizing (ta'kid), each clause repeating the meaning of another, the establishing reading is preferable. This is what we have preferred, and it is what Ibn Jarir and Ibn Kathir preferred: that the intended meaning of ﴿ruh al-qudus﴾ is who? Jibril, peace be upon him.

Here Allah has explained that He gave Musa the Book, gave 'Isa son of Maryam the clear proofs, and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit, and the messengers came in succession.

So what was the condition of the Children of Israel with these supported messengers? The answer: ﴿Whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant﴾. ﴿Afa-kullama﴾: "kullama" (whenever) is a particle of repetition; it is conditional, but it also conveys repetition, conditional and conveying repetition. Accordingly we say: this reprehensible act is repeated from them. ﴿Whenever a messenger came to you﴾ — from where? From Allah, a messenger from Allah; ﴿with what﴾ means with a law; ﴿your souls do not desire﴾ means your souls do not want; ﴿you were arrogant﴾ is the answer of the condition: "came" is the verb of the condition, and "you were arrogant" is the answer of the condition.

In His saying: ﴿Whenever a messenger came to you, you were arrogant﴾ there is evidence that they confront the messengers with what? With arrogance; they did not hesitate. Whenever he came to them, they immediately became arrogant, because this is the result of the consequent following the condition: whenever the condition exists, the consequent exists immediately. So whenever those Israelites were visited by a messenger with what their souls did not desire, they were arrogant. The implication of the verse is that if a messenger came to them with what their souls desire, they would not be arrogant; but not because they accepted it, no, no, but they did not accept it because he is a messenger, rather because their souls desired it. So these people did not worship Allah by guidance but by their desires, and one who worships Allah by his desire is not a worshipper. Rather, the true worshipper of Allah is the one who worships Allah by guidance, not by desire.

There is no difference in worship between belief, speech, or action; do you understand? There is no difference. A person (...) accepts from belief only what his intellect indicates, as he claims. Is he truly a believer? No, rather he is arrogant. The one who says, "I do not believe this attribute of Allah, because my intellect does not accept it, the intellect rejects this thing," we say: then you have not believed in the Book; you have believed in your intellect. And it is known that every intellect that opposes the Qur'an and the Sunnah is a corrupt intellect. For this reason Allah, glory be to Him, condemns those who deny the Book and the Sunnah by saying they do not reason. Every intellect whose owner claims it is intellect while it opposes the Book and the Sunnah is not considered intellect. This is true, because intellect, as Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Sound transmission agrees with clear reason." Sound transmission agrees with clear reason, meaning pure reason that has no doubts or desires.

So we say: this group, the Children of Israel, when a messenger came to them with what their souls desired, they were not arrogant in accepting him; but is this evidence that they are believers (...) because he is a prophet? No, they only believed in what agreed with their desires. Is there in this nation anyone resembling them in this respect? Yes, there are many who resemble them in creed and in deeds. Many people seek legal tricks and interpret in creed, in the names and attributes, as we have often encountered. Among them are those who use tricks in deeds: Allah forbids something, for example, and then they devise a trick against it by permitting it, and they distort the texts for this purpose. When a matter comes to them that agrees with their desires, they are at ease with it and their hearts are expanded by it; and when a matter comes that does not agree with their desires, may Allah protect us, they feel constricted by it. Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that which is in dispute between them and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full] submission﴾ [an-Nisa' 65]. That is, it is not enough that there be no discomfort in you afterward; three things are necessary: first, judgment (tahkim); second, expansion of the breast and absence of discomfort; third, complete submission, ﴿and submit in [full] submission﴾. If any one of these three matters is lacking, the faith is deficient, and it may disappear altogether. Among this nation are those who resemble them greatly in creed, I said, and in deeds.
* Student: What is its counterpart?
* The Shaykh: What do you mean by its counterpart?
* The student: I mean their arrogance?
* The Shaykh: That is the answer: whenever a messenger came to them, they were arrogant.
* The student: No, I mean what comes after the conjunction.
* The Shaykh: It has already been explained to us that this form, according to the grammarians, has two views: either the hamzah (interrogative) enters at the beginning of the sentence, and the sentence into which the hamzah enters is elided and estimated according to what suits the context; or the hamzah is in the middle of the sentence and the fa' is a conjunction but displaced from its place, and the original is: "fa-a-kullama jaa'akum." We told you this is easier, because the first, in reality, sometimes makes it hard for you to estimate the suitable thing.

And His saying, exalted: ﴿you were arrogant﴾. What is the meaning of "istakbara"? It means: he took the path of pride, haughtiness and elevation over what the messengers brought. This is one of the two categories of disbelief, because it has been explained to us that disbelief revolves around two things: denial (jahd) and arrogance (istikbar). If you examine all disbelief, its kinds, you will find it returns to these two matters: either denial or arrogance; but it has types and individuals, and nothing falls outside these two matters.

﴿istakbartum﴾: what is the meaning of ﴿istakbartum﴾? You took the path of pride, haughtiness and elevation over what these messengers brought.
* Student: Is denial arrogance?
* The Shaykh: No. How is denial arrogance? And likewise abandonment?
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed (...) either denial (takdhib) or arrogance. Denial is clear: one says "this is false," and this is usually in reports. Arrogance is in actions: one is told "do," but he does not do it, while confirming that it is obligatory and that the law brought it, yet he is arrogant toward it and does not do it.
* Student: Shaykh, what about mockery?
* The Shaykh: Mockery does not fall outside these two matters: either he is a denier, and usually it comes from arrogance, because one who mocks a thing belittles it and despises it.
* Student: I say: is denial arrogance?
* The Shaykh: Denial is rejection.
* Student: Is it truly arrogance?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not arrogance (...). Arrogance means there is affirmation with it: arrogance is that a person affirms but does not act, while denial is saying, "It is not correct, we do not accept this, it is not correct," he does not submit.

He says: ﴿you were arrogant, and a group you denied﴾. ﴿Fariqan﴾: a group. It is in the accusative as the fronted object of what? Of ﴿kadhdhabtum﴾ — the fronted object of ﴿kadhdhabtum﴾. ﴿And a group you kill﴾, meaning another group you kill, and it is also fronted, so it is the fronted object of ﴿taqtuluna﴾. We have read from the rules of rhetoric that fronting what should be postponed gives what meaning?
* The students: Restriction (hasr).
* The Shaykh: It gives restriction. Here there is a division: one group and another group, and this conflicts with restriction, because "group" means that if it is set against another group, then there is no restriction. But we say that in reality there is restriction here with respect to both parties: the approach of these people toward the messengers is restricted to two groups: either killed or denied. Some they deny with denial but do not attack with killing, and some they also kill; with denial they kill them. Here He said ﴿kadhdhabtum﴾ and said ﴿taqtuluna﴾, a present-tense verb; the first is a past-tense verb. As for the first being past, the matter is clear, because denial did occur from them; right?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: As for using a present-tense verb for killing, first it is for the sake of the rhythm of the verses' endings (fawasil); for if he had said "wa-fariqan qad qataltum," it would not have matched what precedes and follows it. Then some scholars have noted a subtle point in it: these Jews continued killing even against the Messenger ﷺ, for they killed the Messenger, peace be upon him, with the poison they put for him at Khaybar, and he continued to feel its effect until in his final illness he said: "The morsel of Khaybar has never ceased to trouble me, and this is the time of the severing of my aorta"[[Related by al-Bazzar in his Musnad (8007) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "This is the time it cut my aorta."]]. Al-Zuhri said: the Prophet ﷺ died a martyr because they were the cause of his death. This is not far-fetched, that this too is one of the subtle points in the expression: the present tense in killing. Though it might be objected that denial also continued even up to the Messenger ﷺ, isn't that so?
* The students: Indeed.

The Shaykh: Why did it not say: "a group you call liars and a group you kill"? This raises an objection, but we say that observing the endings of the verses (fawasil) is stronger for us. So if the intent were to show the continuation of their killing of the prophets, it would also have to observe the continuation of their denial, because they denied the Messenger openly and plainly. Indeed, in the story of the conversion of 'Abdullah ibn Salam, when he testified to the truth of the Messenger, they had previously said: "He is the best of us and the son of the best of us." When he testified to the truth of the Messenger ﷺ, what did they say? They said: "He is the worst of us and the son of the worst of us."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3329) from the hadith of Anas.]] They spoke ill of him. This expresses rebuke and blame of the Children of Israel, and it clarifies their method regarding the laws and regarding those who brought the laws. Regarding the laws, they accept only what agrees with their desires. Regarding those who brought the laws, they divided into two groups: toward those who brought what their souls did not desire, a group they called liars and a group they killed.

A student: O Shaykh, His saying ﴿تَقْتُلُونَ﴾ ("you kill")... the denial is undoubtedly occurring from them, and the killing (...) they kill (...)?

The Shaykh: And the killing, did it not occur?

The student: It occurred.

The Shaykh: No, all of it (...), because He says: ﴿They kill the prophets without right﴾ [Al 'Imran 112], in many verses.

The student: The denial has occurred without doubt.

The Shaykh: And the killing has occurred.

The student: No, all of this has occurred, and this is only part of it.

The Shaykh: What appears from them: that they kill. Whomever they wished to kill, they killed, just as they deny.

A student: (...) ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67].

The Shaykh: Yes indeed, He protects you from the people during the time of conveying the message. Its meaning is: convey, and you are protected while conveying. For this reason, no one ever attacked him during his conveying and killed him.

A student: O Shaykh, you said that the objection to this is His saying ﴿kadhdhabtum﴾ ("you denied") together with ﴿taqtulun﴾ ("you kill"). It is said that denial became an inherent characteristic of them, so it does not need to be specified, and the attribute is continuous?

The Shaykh: If it were in the nominal sentence, this explanation would be valid, because the nominal sentence indicates continuity. But the verbal sentence does not. Indeed, they said that the verbal sentence in the present tense indicates occurrence and continuity.

The student: But is the past tense not less than the present?

The Shaykh: It does not appear so to me. And for this reason, it appears to me, and Allah knows best, that observing the endings of the verses is the strongest thing; it is a verbal consideration.

A student: Poison him (...)?

The Shaykh: No, they poisoned him with it. They said: "If you are a prophet, it will not harm you; and if you are a liar, we will be rid of you." Thus they said, but it did not harm him, until Allah the Exalted completed what He willed of his call.

﴿And they said: our hearts are ghulf﴾ [al-Baqarah 88]. We ask Allah for well-being. This is a corrupt argument. Who said it? The Children of Israel. ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾: the plural of aghlaf, and the aghlaf is the one upon which there is a covering (ghilaf), meaning covered, so that what these messengers call to does not reach it. It is like the saying of some people: "By Allah, Allah did not guide us to pray," or "Allah did not guide us to do such-and-such." This is a lie, for Allah says: ﴿We guided him to the two paths﴾ [al-Balad 10], meaning We clarified for him the path of good and the path of evil. This is what is incumbent upon Allah. ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance, and indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾ [al-Layl 12-13]. So what is incumbent upon Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, He has completed; what remains is what is incumbent upon you. These people say: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾. "Ghulf" is the plural of aghlaf, which is that which has been covered with something, with a sheath that prevents matters from reaching it. They say this as an excuse on their own behalf for not accepting the truth, meaning they excuse themselves from accepting it by saying that their hearts are ghulf. Is this true? No. If they had returned to their natural disposition (fitrah), their hearts would not have been ghulf. But what happened is that what became the cause of the covering over the hearts, which is disbelief, occurred. For this reason He said: "Bal" ("rather"). And "bal" here is for al-idrab al-ibtali ("the retractive/annulling 'rather'"), not for al-idrab al-intiqali ("the transitional 'rather'"), the annulling idrab.

You know that idrab (the use of "bal") divides into two types: the transitional idrab, which does not necessarily entail the nullification of what was negated, and the annulling idrab, which entails the nullification of what was negated. Do you understand? You say: "I struck Zayd, rather 'Amr." What is this? This is annulling. That is, you have nullified the first and attributed the judgment to the second. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has caught up regarding the Hereafter; rather, they are in doubt about it; rather, they are blind to it﴾ [al-Naml 66]. That is transitional: their states changed. Their knowledge regarding the Hereafter was lost, then doubt occurred to them, then blindness, and Allah forbid. Here, however, it is annulling idrab: Allah nullified what they claimed and clarified the real cause, which is Allah's curse upon them, and Allah forbid: ﴿Rather, Allah cursed them﴾. ﴿Cursed them﴾ means He expelled them and removed them from His mercy. The curse means expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah. But is this curse an injustice, or is it due to something from themselves?

The students: Due to something from themselves.

The Shaykh: And what is it?

The students: Lying and (...).

The Shaykh: ﴿Allah cursed them for their disbelief﴾. The "bi" here is causal, meaning: because of their disbelief they were cursed, so a seal was placed upon their hearts, as in His saying: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14], those who, when the Qur'an is recited to them, say: ﴿This is only the legends of the former peoples﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 13]. Why do they say of these magnificent, impactful, stirring verses that they are the legends of the ancients? Because a covering was placed over their hearts. For this reason He followed it with: ﴿No!﴾, meaning they are not the legends of the ancients, ﴿rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts﴾. Thus they did not reach the truth. We have said many times that if a person reads the Qur'an and does not find it affecting his heart, let him know that there are sins that have covered the heart, because when the Qur'an reaches the heart, it must affect it. ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart out of fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that they may reflect﴾ [al-Hashr 21]. If the Qur'an reached the heart, it would necessarily affect it. So if a person is not affected by reciting the Qur'an, that is evidence that there is a barrier preventing the Qur'an from reaching his heart, namely sins. Let him seek help from Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, seek forgiveness, and repent, so that Allah may remove this effect from him. ﴿Rather, Allah cursed them for their disbelief, so little﴾. ﴿For their disbelief﴾: the word "kufr" (disbelief) is a verbal noun (masdar) annexed to what? 

A student: To its object.

Another student: To its subject.

The Shaykh: It is annexed to its subject, because they are disbelievers. He said: ﴿so little is it that they believe﴾.

A student: The "ba" (bi), O Shaykh?

The Shaykh: The "ba" is causal.

﴿So little is it that they believe﴾. Pay attention to this verse. In ﴿qalilan ma yu'minun﴾ ("little is it that they believe") there is a difficulty here, because His saying ﴿bi-kufrihim﴾ ("for their disbelief") followed by ﴿qalilan ma yu'minun﴾ implies that they did not disbelieve in a way that expels them from the religion, because ﴿qalilan ma yu'minun﴾ means: there is faith among them, there is faith among them but it is little. The scholars differed in interpreting this verse. Some said: the paucity refers to the subject, not to the faith. And what is meant by "refers to the subject"? It means: few of them are believers. Do you understand? Others said: the paucity refers to the faith, but the Arabs use "little" to mean "none," as you say: "qalla ma ra'aytuhu qatt" ("I have hardly ever seen him"). This is the Arabic expression, and the meaning of "qalla ma ra'aytuhu qatt" is: I have never seen him at all. So "qalilan" here means that their faith is nonexistent. They view paucity as meaning non-existence. A third view on this matter: according to both of these views, "ma" is extra (za'idah), extra for emphasizing the paucity, because the meaning is: "they believe a little," whether we say it refers to the faith or refers to the believers, to the subject.

Some say that "ma" is not extra but negating, and the construction is: "fa-ma yu'minuna qalilan" ("so they do not believe, a little"). They say that this also has an implied omission, meaning: "nor much," as in His saying: ﴿And He made for you garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you from your violence﴾ [al-Nahl 81], meaning: they do not believe a little nor much. That is, if the little is absent from them, then the much is absent a fortiori. So they do not believe, neither a little nor much. For this reason the light of revelation does not reach them; their hearts are ghulf, good does not reach them. This is closer in meaning.

This is what raises a difficulty regarding "little." But it is problematic from the standpoint of the rules of the Arabic language, because it is well established in Arabic that the negating "ma" does not govern what comes after it over what comes before it. Here what came after it governed what came before it. This speaker says: who told you that the negating "ma" does not govern what follows it over what precedes it? Do you have a text on this from the Qur'an? A text from the Sunnah? What is the answer? No, but we have not seen it govern what precedes it. He says: "I have seen it." This verse shows that what follows it governs what precedes it. As long as no text has come saying that the negating "ma" does not govern what follows it over what precedes it, I say: this verse indicates that what follows it may govern what precedes it, and there is no objection to this.

Furthermore, by saying this I remove two difficulties. The first difficulty: I am freed from saying that "ma" is extra, because (...) "ma" is extra. The second: I am freed from the difficulty concerning the word ﴿qalilan﴾. Because in reality, when we read the verse, to what does the paucity refer? To the faith, or to the subject? ﴿ma yu'minun﴾: does it refer to the "waw" (the plural subject) or to the verb, which is the faith? The reality is that it refers to the faith, although these people have no faith, little or much. So by taking this course I have freed myself from these two difficulties, and the paucity remains as it is, and the meaning is: they do not believe, a little; and if the little is absent from them, the much is absent.

In any case, these people argued for their unbelief by saying that their hearts are ghulf. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that they are not ghulf, and that what made them ghulf is their disbelief. Allah cursed them, expelled them, and removed them from His mercy because of their disbelief. Therefore faith does not reach their hearts. As for hearts in themselves, they are open and receptive to faith, because the natural disposition (fitrah) is one with which all creation is created. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah"[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (1385) and Muslim (2658/22), and the wording is al-Bukhari's, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. And what is the fitrah? ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind﴾ [al-Rum 30].

Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, said: ﴿And when there came to them﴾ [al-Baqarah 89]. Of course, this aspect is closer to me.

A student: The last one.

The Shaykh: The last one is closer.

A student: (...).

The Shaykh: Who said that?

The student: (...).

The Shaykh: Yes. We say: yes, if it indicates (...) that it governs, it governs. You say: "Zaydan ma darabtu (...)": "I did not strike Zayd."

A student: O Shaykh, if the subject is "qalil," can "ma" not be a relative pronoun?

The Shaykh: ﴿fa-qalilan﴾? No. It creates a difficulty for us that (...). You say: "fa-qalil," meaning: "so those who believe are few."

﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and they had previously been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Baqarah 89], to the end. This, Allah forbid, is the conclusion of the matter: all the previous messengers they denied, and they did not accept what they brought. Then a Book came to them from Allah: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah﴾. Where is the response to ﴿lamma﴾ ("when")? ﴿they disbelieved in it﴾: this is the response. ﴿When there came to them a Book from Allah﴾, which is the Qur'an. He made it indefinite here for glorification: ﴿a Book﴾, and He emphasized its glory with His saying: ﴿from Allah﴾. But what is the evidence that it is from Allah? If they say: this is the speech of Muhammad ﷺ, what is the evidence?

The evidence is that Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, testified to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that it is from Him. He testified to him by His support of him. The Messenger says: this Qur'an is from Allah, and I struggle against you with it and upon it, and I will prevail over you. If it were from other than Allah, would he prevail by it? He could not; he would not prevail by it. If he prevailed by it, that would mean Allah supports falsehood, and this contradicts the wisdom of Allah. Therefore it is from Allah by the testimony of Allah to him, as Allah says: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness﴾ [al-Nisa' 166], to the end. Allah bears witness to what He sent down to you with both verbal testimony and practical testimony. His saying ﴿from Allah﴾ ascribes it to ﴿the Presence of Allah﴾ because it is His speech, as will come to us, Allah willing, in the benefits of the verse.

His saying: ﴿confirming what is with them﴾: ﴿confirming﴾. We have previously said that the confirmation of the Qur'an of what preceded it has two aspects:

A student: The confirmation of the Qur'an?

The Shaykh: For what preceded.

The student: That it is from Allah.

The Shaykh: No, it confirms what preceded. We mentioned that it has two aspects?

The student: First, that it is from Allah.

The Shaykh: No.

A student: The first aspect: that it is news of the past and the future.

The Shaykh: What kind?

The student: That is, its information in the past and in...

The Shaykh: No, no, that is not it.

A student: Because it agrees in the fundamentals, the fundamentals of the laws.

The Shaykh: No, no. We said: "confirming" (musaddiq), meaning that it judges that they are true. It says that they are truthful: ﴿The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers; each believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah 285]. So it says about the Torah that it is true, about the Gospel that it is true, about the Psalms that it is true. It confirms them, just as if a informant told me something and I said: "You have spoken truly," would I be confirming him?

The students: Yes.

The Shaykh: I would be confirming him. The second aspect of its confirmation of them is that it came in agreement with what they had announced. They announced it, and it came confirming it, coming in agreement with what they had foretold. Jesus, son of Mary, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ﴿I am the Messenger of Allah to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah, and giving good tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ [al-Saff 6]. So this Book came confirming this good tiding. This is the meaning of its being confirming of what preceded: it says that they are true, and that it came in agreement with what they had announced.

And His saying ﴿what is with them﴾: from where? From the Torah and the Gospel. This is clear that the Torah foretold the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, either by his name or by his description which applies to no one else. And His saying ﴿and they had previously﴾, meaning: before it came to them. Here, why is ﴿min qabl﴾ ("previously") vowelled with a dammah, and "min" is a preposition? Because it is indeclinable. We have already learned that "qabl" ("before"), "ba'd" ("after"), "fawq" ("above"), "taht" ("below") and similar words have four states, one of which is being built on the dammah when the genitive complement is omitted and its meaning is intended. In that case it is indeclinable on the dammah. So: ﴿and they had been, before it came to them, seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾.

﴿Yastaftihun﴾ ("they sought victory") means: they sought help, and they said: "Victory will be ours over you," meaning: victory over you. And His saying ﴿those who disbelieved﴾: from where? From the polytheists, who were the Aws and the Khazraj, because the Aws and the Khazraj were in disbelief; they were not People of the Book, as is well known. So they used to say: "A prophet will be sent, and we will follow him, and we will prevail over you." ﴿They sought victory﴾. But when it came to them, they did not recognize it and disbelieved in it, Allah forbid. There came to them the thing they knew, as they know their own sons, but they disbelieved in it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 87–89 (part 3 of 4):

﴿Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter. Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be helped.﴾ [al-Baqarah 86]. (...) They disbelieve in His signs; they only want by this the life of this world, because the reference in His words ﴿Those﴾ is to those previously mentioned, who believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part.

* The second benefit of this verse: this world and the Hereafter are rivals (ḍarratān), meaning that whoever wants one of them in full harms the other. As for the one who wants this world, there is no doubt that he harms his Hereafter. As for the one who wants the Hereafter, nothing of this world is lost to him, because of the Most High's words: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [al-Shura 20].
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Except when a person wants one of them in full, and especially when he wants this world; if he wants it, it harms his Hereafter. On the contrary, it does not harm him if we say that His words ﴿We will increase him in his tilth﴾ mean that He also gives him from this world.
* It also contains proof that the punishment continues for those who prefer this world over the Hereafter and make it a substitute for it, because of His words: ﴿Their punishment will not be lightened.﴾
* The fourth benefit: these people have no helper who can support them and protect them from the punishment of God, neither their gods nor their leaders. Rather, they will curse their leaders on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way."﴾ [al-Ahzab 67]. Likewise, their leaders will disown them: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed.﴾ [al-Baqarah 166]. The third verse: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister.﴾ [al-A'raf 38].

Then Allah the Most High said: ﴿And We gave Moses the Book, and followed him up with messengers.﴾

* From this noble verse is derived: the affirmation of the prophethood of Moses, because of His words: ﴿And We gave Moses the Book.﴾
* And from it is derived: the emphasis of an important report even when the addressee does not deny it, because of His words: ﴿And We gave﴾, which is emphasized with three emphasizers, although it was not addressed to someone who denies it. It has already passed us that emphasis of speech occurs in three situations:
First: when it is addressed to one who denies it. The scholars of rhetoric (balaghah) said that in this case emphasis is obligatory (wujūban).
When it is addressed to one who is hesitant, the scholars of rhetoric said that in this case emphasis is recommended (istiḥsānan).
The third: when the report is of extreme importance, it is emphasized even if it is addressed to someone who neither denies it nor is hesitant. Even if you address it to a person at the outset, and he is one of those concerned with important matters, then emphasizing it is good.
* The third benefit: the messengers who came after Moses followed his law among the Children of Israel, because of His words: ﴿and followed him up with messengers﴾. This is supported by the Most High's words: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted judge for those who were Jews, as did the rabbis and the scholars.﴾ [al-Ma'idah 44].
* The next benefit: the prophethood of Jesus is established, because of His words: ﴿And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, the clear proofs.﴾
* The next benefit: whoever has no father in the sharia sense is attributed to his mother, just as whoever has no father by destiny (qadar). Jesus son of Mary had no father by destiny; he had no father by the natural order (kawnan). Whoever has no legal father is like him, attributed to his mother, such as the child of illegitimacy, may Allah protect us. By this we know that the preponderant opinion among the scholars is that his mother is his ʿaṣabah (agnatic heir), and he is not an ʿaṣabah of his mother.
