The point is that the person who wishes that another's blessing would disappear, that is, God's blessing upon another, this is the envious person. It is obligatory for a person, when he sees that God has bestowed a blessing on someone else, to ask God for His bounty. God will give him what He has given. The Exalted said: ﴿And do not wish for that by which God has favored some of you over others. For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned. And ask God for His bounty⁠﴾ [al-Nisa' 32]. Let the blessing of God upon your brother be his, but He who gave it is able to give you, and more. Do not envy, for no matter how much you envy, you will not reverse the blessing of God upon others. No matter how much you envy, you cannot reverse it. The envious person, in reality, increases in envy only as a fire blazing in his inner self. And whenever God's blessings upon His servants increase, his grief increases. In reality, although he hates God's blessing upon this other person, he is opposed to God in His decree and His predestination, because he hates that God would bless this person, while God has bestowed the blessing and decreed it for him. Thus he opposes God in His judgment.

Then, the envier, the one who envies, however much God gives him of blessing, does not see God's favor in it, because he sees that another is better than him. Even if we suppose that he has excelled in much wealth, and a merchant came and profited, made a great profit in a specific commodity, you find that this envious person envies him for this profit, while he himself has great millions. Likewise with knowledge: some envious people, for example, when someone excels in a matter of religious knowledge, you find that if this man were more knowledgeable and more beneficial to people than him, he envies him for this matter in which he excelled, or which became the talk of the people, because he wrote about it, or said it, or something similar. This also means that he did not see God's blessing upon him in what He gave him. So, O brothers, envy is a grave matter, its consequence is disastrous. People are in goodness, and the envious person is in evil. People are reassured and at ease, but this envious person, may God protect us, pursues the blessings, God's blessings upon His servants. And whenever he sees a blessing, it becomes an ember in his heart. Therefore, a person must say: "This is from God's favor upon this man. I ask God to give me the like of what He gave him." So he asks God for His bounty. God has guided us to this: ﴿And do not wish for that by which God has favored some of you over others. For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned. And ask God for His bounty⁠﴾ [al-Nisa' 32]. And if envy were not a character trait except that it is a characteristic of the Jews, it would be sufficient to repel one from it. They are the ones who envy people for what God has given them of His bounty. So the conclusion is that these Jews and Christians wish to turn the believers back to disbelief after their belief. Know that whoever loves something strives to attain it. He strives to attain it, right or not? So these Jews and Christians strive with all the strength they have, material, moral, or otherwise, and what do they seek? To turn the Muslims back to disbelief after belief. Look: God did not say "they will turn you into Jews or Christians," but ﴿disbelievers⁠﴾. Because the Jews and Christians know that a Muslim is far from becoming a Jew or a Christian, but their leaders say: "Your aim is to turn the Muslim away from belief, just take him out of belief only, and he goes (...)." Take him out of belief only, or make him doubt the religion, so that it is a stage, and then afterwards they deny, may God protect us. So we must be wary, because God says: ﴿wished⁠﴾, and wishing is pure love. And the one who loves something must strive for what? To attain it.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿out of their own selves⁠﴾: meaning this envy, or this wish which they wish, is not for God nor from God, but from their own selves. This is an indication that this is wickedness in their selves. Wickedness: their selves are corrupt, they do not want the truth, and they do not want good for this Ummah. Rather, they want the Ummah to apostatize out of envy from their own selves.

His words: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them⁠﴾: ﴿after it became clear⁠﴾ means it became manifest. ﴿To them⁠﴾: to whom? To these many. They, after the truth became clear to them and they knew that you are upon the truth, wished to turn you back into disbelief. If they had been ignorant that you were upon the truth, they might have said: "We did not wish that they be upon a doubtful religion," and then they would have had some excuse. But the truth has become clear to them, and they knew that the Messenger ﷺ is true, that his religion is true, and that the believers are upon the truth. Nevertheless, they wish this wish and strive in every way to reach their goal. ﴿After the truth became clear to them⁠﴾. We mentioned earlier that the truth (al-haqq) is that which is established. If it describes a ruling, what is meant is justice, and if it describes a report, what is meant is truthfulness. So truth is truthfulness in reports and justice in rulings. The religion of Islam is upon this, and what the Messenger ﷺ brought is upon this: his reports are true, and his rulings are just.

The Exalted said: ﴿So pardon and overlook until God brings His command. Indeed, God has power over all things⁠﴾. ﴿So pardon⁠﴾: the address is to the believers in general, and the Messenger ﷺ is included among them. Pardon (al-'afw) means to leave off holding someone accountable for a sin, as if it derives from "the trace vanished" (afa al-athar) when it disappears through the passage of time.

His words: ﴿and overlook⁠﴾. It is said that it is of the category of coordinating synonyms, like the words of the poet:
....................... and he found her words to be lies and falsehood.
Al-main and al-kadhib have the same meaning. Some said that ﴿pardon and overlook⁠﴾ have the same meaning. But the correct view is that there is a difference between them. Pardon is to leave off holding someone accountable for a sin, and overlooking (al-safh) is turning away from it, derived from "the side of the neck" (safhat al-'unq), that a person turns away as if nothing happened, turning the side of his neck to it. So overlooking means turning away from this entirely, as if it had never been. Accordingly, there is a difference: pardon means you do not hold him accountable for his sin, but there is no harm if something remains in your soul or you remember it. Overlooking means you turn away from it completely, as if nothing had happened. On this basis, overlooking is more complete, is it not? Overlooking is more complete, and it is most complete when combined with pardon. ﴿So pardon and overlook⁠﴾ until when? ﴿Until God brings His command⁠﴾. This is a glad tiding to the believers: the matter has an end. You now pardon and overlook, ﴿until God brings His command⁠﴾. The verb ﴿brings⁠﴾ (ya'ti) is in the subjunctive by what? By an implied "an" (that) after "hatta" (until), or by "hatta" itself, according to a difference between the Kufans and the Basrans (two schools of grammarians).

His words: ﴿God brings His command⁠﴾. Know that the "coming" (ityan) attributed to God, glory be to Him, is of two types: one is unrestricted, and the other is restricted. As for the unrestricted, like His words: ﴿Do they wait for anything but that the angels come to them, or your Lord comes, or some of the signs of your Lord come?⁠﴾ [al-An'am 158]. When it is unrestricted like this, what is meant is the actual coming of God, His coming Himself in reality. God comes in the manner that befits His majesty. The Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels in rows⁠﴾ [al-Fajr 22]. This coming, according to the People of the Sunnah and the Community, who are the Salaf in particular, and the People of the Sunnah and the Community are not on two paths, as some confused people have claimed, that the People of the Sunnah and the Community have two paths: the path of delegation (tafwid), as he says, and the path of interpretation (ta'wil). This is a lie. Interpretation is not something related to the Sunnah and the Community, for interpretation is in reality distortion (tahrif), distorting words from their places. The People of interpretation, and the more correct term is the People of distortion, as Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah called them in al-'Aqidah al-Wasitiyyah, say: ﴿And your Lord comes⁠﴾ [al-Fajr 22] for example, means "the command of your Lord comes," because God cannot come; He Himself cannot come, but rather His command comes. Without doubt this is a lie against God, for God addressed us in clear Arabic, and the Arabic language requires that when it is said "so-and-so came," the meaning is that he came himself. This is the requirement of the Arabic language. So when they say "the command of your Lord came," we say: You have lied against God, you have lied in two respects. In that you say: "He did not intend such-and-such," which is speaking about God without knowledge. Who told you that He did not intend this? By which book or which Sunnah? And you lied another lie when you said: "What is meant is that His command came," when you diverted it from its apparent meaning, and that He Himself did not come. Who says "His command came"? Perhaps an angel from His angels came, yes, not His command. Then they would all be interpreters who distort, for they have spoken about God without knowledge in two respects: (...) God's command. So what is meant is that this command comes. What is meant is that this command comes. The evidence for this is that the coming of God's command, which God made the goal here, is the order to fight. And it is correct for me to say: "God came with His command, when He ordered fighting."

Now, if a matter comes unrestricted in one respect and restricted in another, like His words: ﴿Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them in shadows of clouds?⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah 210]. ﴿In shadows⁠﴾. Here we say: it is like the unrestricted, because "fi" (in) here means "ma'a" (with). That is, God comes to them with shadows of clouds. We could take it at its apparent meaning, but if we take it at its apparent meaning, a meaning arises that is not correct: that clouds encompass God, and God, glory be to Him, is not encompassed by any of His creation. So the point is that this coming: God comes to them in shadows, like His words: ﴿And your Lord comes⁠﴾ [al-Fajr 22]. The meaning is: God comes Himself in shadows of clouds, meaning the shadows precede God's coming, then God, glory be to Him, comes in the manner He wills.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 109–114 (part 2 of 7):

His words: ﴿Until Allah brings His command﴾. What is meant by "command" here? It means the command to fight, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah (a tax levied on non-Muslim subjects under Muslim rule) willingly while they are humbled﴾ [at-Tawbah 29]. Fight them ﴿until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾. This is from the command of Allah, glorified and exalted, which He brought. So the Messenger ﷺ complied, pardoned and forgave.

It is also possible that the command here means the cosmic command, the cosmic command, meaning: until Allah brings about the cause for which you fight them. This is like the breaking of the covenant by Banu an-Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa' and Banu Qurayza. When the Messenger ﷺ first arrived in Madinah, what did he do with these Jews? He made a covenant with them. Then they broke the covenant, tribe by tribe, until, by Allah's praise, victory over them was achieved. So the meaning of "command" here may be not the legislative command but the cosmic, decreed command by which you become permitted to fight them. Good.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾, it means that among the perfection of His power, glorified and exalted is He, is that He will give you victory over them even with pardon and forgiveness. Allah, glorified and exalted, is able to change matters, and the dominion will be yours. This was so, by Allah's praise. The dominion was for the Muslims over all their enemies: over the Jews, and over whom? Over the Christians, over the polytheists, over the Magians. All of them, by Allah's praise, who opposed Islam, the dominion was for Islam. But after the Islamic nation declined, its conditions changed and it fell back, trials came, and the dominion passed to the enemies. When the Messenger ﷺ was at the Battle of Uhud, one act of disobedience occurred, one act of disobedience, after they had seen victory, after they had seen what they loved. And what was the result? Defeat. ﴿Until, when you lost courage and disputed over the matter and disobeyed﴾ [Aal 'Imran 152]. When? ﴿After He showed you what you love﴾ [Aal 'Imran 152], meaning there occurred the opposite of what you love. It was one act of disobedience, and after the presence of victory, or the glad tidings of victory, defeat occurred. How is this in a nation whose acts of disobedience may be very numerous? And now we try to be victorious without the causes of victory. It is impossible to be victorious, it is not possible except if we truly return to the religion. In reality, we praise Allah, glorified and exalted is He, that there is now an awakening (yaqadha) among the youth. I say awakening, which is better than my saying "sahwa" (a reawakening), because sahwa is from intoxication (sakar), and yaqadha is from sleep. Yaqadha is from sleep, even if there is a kind of intoxication from desire and sins. The point is that there is now among the youth an awakening and revival, but it requires perseverance and steadfastness. The Prophet ﷺ remained in Makkah for how many years? Thirteen years, while being supported by verses and by sincere Companions. In the end he left Makkah, he left Makkah in fear, ﷺ, until Allah honored him. Do you, O young man, seek victory over this nation and this overwhelming misguidance and these dark trials, seeking to win over them overnight? This is impossible. The path is long. Because you are building, for example, one brick, but there are tools that demolish a whole palace. There must be patience, steadfastness, perseverance and not becoming bored. As long as you are on a correct path, your reward is with Allah, whether you attain it or not. ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has already fallen upon Allah﴾ [an-Nisa' 100]. So I want from you resolve, patience and perseverance, and that you do not think the matter is easy, and that within a night or a morning we will transform these drifting, deviant peoples. This is impossible. But with patience and perseverance. And that Allah guides one man through you is better for you than red camels. Likewise, we deal with people with gentleness and kindness, each according to his capacity. ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom﴾ [an-Nahl 125]. This is better. I will say to you, for example: we have seen the impact of the Tabligh Jama'ah (Tablighi Jama'at). Although they have deviations in some matters, we have seen a great impact on Muslims and on non-Muslims, because they call people with kindness and gentleness, complete gentleness. And we have seen, for example, from some people or many people, aversion toward those who want people to take the Sunnah by force and coercion. "Right now, come on, let's ride the Sunnah right now!" Wait. First treat the wound until it heals, then strive to remove its trace. Beautification comes after removing the defect. In any case, look at Allah's discipline of His Messenger ﷺ and his Companions: ﴿Pardon and forgive until Allah brings His command﴾. We said the command here, what is the command? It may be legislative or decreed. As far as we are concerned, the legislative command is finished. We pardon and forgive until Allah brings His command, the decreed command. The decreed command or the legislative command? It is known now, finished.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾. I told you: its benefit is that Muslims should not despair of the change of conditions, for Allah, exalted is He, is over all things competent, and conditions change, and you are not (...).

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾ [al-Baqarah 110]. This also is among the causes of victory and help, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. ﴿Establish prayer﴾ means: say, "The prayer has been established."
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: No? And what does it mean?
* Students: Perform the prayer.
* Shaykh: Perform the prayer in its complete form. Because establishing a thing means making it upright, balanced and straight. So the meaning of ﴿establish prayer﴾ is: bring it complete with its conditions, pillars, obligations and complements. His saying: ﴿the prayer﴾ is general, including the obligatory and the voluntary. Among establishing the obligatory prayers is increasing supererogatory prayers, because it has come in a hadith that supererogatory prayers complete the obligatory ones on the Day of Resurrection. There is no person except that there is deficiency in his obligatory prayer, but these supererogatory prayers complete it and mend it.

His saying: ﴿And give zakah﴾, meaning give it. ﴿Give﴾ means "give", and here the second object is omitted, because zakah is the first object, and the second object is omitted, meaning its rightful recipients. Give zakah to its rightful recipients. Its rightful recipients Allah has specified in the surah of Bara'ah (at-Tawbah): ﴿Zakah expenditures are only for the poor﴾ [at-Tawbah 60] to the end.

His saying: ﴿give zakah﴾. Zakah linguistically means growth and increase, and from it the saying: "zakā al-zar'" when the crop grew and increased. In the legal sense it is the giving of a specific amount of property to a specific group, as an act of worship to Allah, mighty and majestic. This is zakah, and it was named zakah because it purifies the person, purifies him. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [at-Tawbah 103]. So it purifies the person in his character and faith, because it removes him from the enclosure of the miserly to the enclosure of the generous and noble. So it is a purification of the person and a cleansing of him from vices. His saying: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾, after He commanded patience, pardon and forgiveness, shows that a person should occupy himself with the essentials of his religion rather than with others, alongside calling to Allah. But every situation has its statement. However, for a person to turn away from establishing prayer and giving zakah in favor of a people who may not benefit from the call, this is not appropriate. For this reason it has come in a hadith: "When you see stinginess obeyed, desire followed, the world preferred, and every person of opinion pleased with his own opinion, then take care of your own self and leave aside the affair of the common people." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (4341), at-Tirmidhi (3058), and Ibn Majah (4014), from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani.]
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes? There is no harm in it. This shows that a person should not occupy himself with what returns to himself as good in order to benefit others, and he should arrange the interests and acts of worship, because they are ordered.

His saying: ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah﴾. The "ma" here is conditional, not relative. The evidence for that is that it apocopates (jazama) the verb in both the condition and the answer. ﴿Whatever you put forward﴾, its original form is (tuqaddimunahu), and ﴿you will find it﴾, its original form is (tajidunahu). His saying: ﴿Whatever you put forward for yourselves﴾, "put forward for yourselves" (...); because putting forward for oneself is according to following the Sharia.

So now we take the benefits. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Many of the People of the Scripture wish﴾ to the end.

Among the benefits of this verse: showing the intensity of the enmity of the Jews and Christians toward the Muslim nation.

Second: that among the Jews and Christians there are some who are not intensely hostile toward them, by His saying: ﴿Many wish﴾. Its implication is that some of them do not wish this.

Among the benefits of the verse also: that disbelief after Islam is called apostasy (riddah), by His saying: ﴿They would return you﴾. This is why the apostate who disbelieves after Islam is not called merely a disbeliever; he is called an apostate, because he has turned back from a religion better than the one he turned to.
* Student: (....).
* Shaykh: Which one?
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes. We do not say "some of them." And this "some" may be a believer and may not be a believer.

Among the benefits of the verse also: that envy is among the characteristics of the Jews and Christians.

Among its benefits also: the knowledge of the Jews and Christians that Islam is a great merit for its follower. From where is this taken?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: From envy.
* Shaykh: From envy, because a person is not envied except for something that is good and a merit.

Among its benefits also: the obligation to be wary of the Jews and Christians, as long as many of them wish this for us. It is obligatory for us to be wary of them.

Among the benefits of the verse also: showing the corruption of the intentions of those who wish disbelief for us. The corruption of their intentions is shown, because He said: ﴿from themselves﴾, not from a scripture, and not from any harm done to them by the Muslims, but from their own selves: corrupt souls that wish disbelief for the Muslims out of envy.

Among the benefits of the verse also: that those who wish disbelief for the Muslims have had the truth made clear to them. From this a derivative benefit is drawn: the testimony of non-Muslims that the Muslims are upon the truth, because the truth has become clear to them.

* Among the benefits of the verse: consideration of circumstances and the development of the Sharia, as He said: ﴿So pardon and forgive until Allah brings His command﴾. That is, even if they wish this matter, and whoever wishes something strives for it, we pardon and forgive until Allah brings the command.
* Student: The legislative command?
* Shaykh: Whether legislative or non-legislative. Even the command to pardon and forgive until Allah brings His command falls within what you mentioned, and that is consideration of circumstances and the development of the Sharia.

And also among the benefits of the noble verse: establishing the wisdom of Allah, mighty and majestic. The command to pardon and forgive until the command of Allah comes is from wisdom, since fighting before its causes and the availability of its causes, such as material and human strength, contradicts wisdom.

Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of the attribute of power for Allah, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾, and that it is general and comprehensive.

Among them: a refutation of the Mu'tazilah Qadariyyah (the Qadariyyah, who deny divine decree in human actions), because they say that the human being is independent in his deeds. If he is independent in his deeds, it follows that Allah cannot change them, because if He is able to change them, is the human being independent or not independent? He becomes not independent.
* Student: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ (...).
* Shaykh: The decreed will.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Because Allah is over all things competent.
* Student: A refutation of the Ash'ariyyah?
* Shaykh: (...) the Ash'ariyyah. The Qadariyyah, yes, in that they say the human being is independent in his deeds, and that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, cannot turn him away from it. So he is independent, and Allah has no relation to him at all. Whereas the verse says: if Allah is competent over all things, then is it a thing that He turns the person away from what he wants toward what Allah is able to do?

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah﴾. ﴿Whatever﴾ is conditional, ﴿you put forward﴾ is the condition verb, and ﴿you will find it﴾ is the answer of the condition. His saying: ﴿And whatever you put forward for yourselves﴾ means: when a person puts forward some good, he puts it forward for himself. For this reason, he has of his wealth only what he spent; what he delayed belongs to his heir. When He said: ﴿And give zakah﴾, He said: ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it﴾. So when you put forward something of your wealth, whether zakah, voluntary charity, or obligatory expenditure, you have put it forward for yourself, and what you delayed, you delayed for whom? For the heir, your heir. In His saying: ﴿for yourselves﴾ there is encouragement and incitement to advance it, because you put forward for yourself and what remains is for your heir. His saying: ﴿of good﴾ is an indefinite noun in a conditional context, so it indicates generality: whatever good you put forward for a person, whether much or little, you will find it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Protect yourselves from the Fire even with half a date." [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (1417), Muslim (1016/68), from 'Adi ibn Hatim.] "Half a date" means half of it. Perhaps half a date protects a person from the Fire, and this is a great good. His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿you will find it with Allah﴾ is derived from "wujud" (finding), meaning that you will meet it with Allah, exalted is He. When? On the Day of Resurrection, stored up for you on the Day of Resurrection. A good deed is multiplied by ten up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 261]. (...) there is also beyond that.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 109–114 (part 3 of 7):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ The phrase ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ is a sentence emphasised with (inna). Yet the address is an opening address (khitab ibtida'i), since it is not directed at someone who is hesitant or denying. When an address is not directed at a denier or a hesitant listener, it is called an opening address, and an opening address does not normally need emphasis. But we have mentioned several times that an opening address may be emphasised, not because of the condition of the listener, but because of the importance of its meaning. Here, it is very important that Allah informs us, glorified and exalted is He, that He is Seeing of everything we do.

His words ﴿of what you do﴾: (ma) is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul) that conveys generality, so it means whatever we do, inwardly and outwardly, verbally and physically. For the hearts have actions too, such as love, fear, hope, desire and the like. Whatever we do inwardly or outwardly, by deed or by word, Allah the Exalted is Seeing of it.

Now, ﴿of what you do﴾ is connected to what? To ﴿Seeing﴾. So why was it placed before it? For two purposes. The first purpose may be to observe the rhyme endings (fawasil), since what comes before it ends with the letter (ra'), ﴿Capable﴾, and what follows it is ﴿Seeing﴾. The second purpose may be that the fronting is for restriction (hasr). The restriction here, although it reduces the generality, conveys warning (tarhib) and encouragement (targhib), and both are included. Please pay attention. If it is asked which is better: to say that Allah is Seeing of everything, of what we do and what we do not know, or that He is Seeing only of what we do? Which is greater? The first is greater. So why was the object placed first, when we say that fronting the object conveys restriction? We say: the benefit of restriction here is great. It is a warning to a person or an encouragement to him, as if one were saying: even if Allah were not Seeing except of your deeds, He would still be Seeing. This is like a person who threatens his son by saying: "Go on, I know what you are saying." The father knows what the son says and what he does not say, but he says it as a threat. It may also be said as encouragement. So here we say: the benefit of restriction, even though it reduces the generality, is either encouragement or warning, so that we may be encouraged. It is as if Allah, if He were not Seeing, would still be Seeing of our deeds without any doubt.

And His words ﴿Seeing of what you do﴾: is this from (basar), meaning sight with the eye, or from (ibsar), meaning knowledge? It is the second, because we have mentioned that His words ﴿of what you do﴾ include both inward and outward deeds, and inward deeds are not the object of sight. So the meaning of (basir) here is: (Alim), the All-Knowing. Thus, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They say: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians.﴾ Who are ﴿They say﴾? The Jews and the Christians. ﴿They say﴾, that is, the Jews and the Christians: ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews﴾, and this is the saying of the Jews. ﴿Or Christians﴾, and this is the saying of the Christians. So the Jews said: no one enters Paradise except us, and the Christians said: no one enters Paradise except us. The Jews say: no one enters Paradise except a Jew; the Christians say: no one enters Paradise except a Christian.

(hud) is the plural of (ha'id), as (ud) is the plural of (a'idh), and (al-'awdh al-mataafil) refers to nursing mothers. So (hud) means (ha'id), and (ha'id) means returning, from His words: ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾ [al-A'raf 156], meaning we have returned. It has also been said that (hud) is the plural of (Yahud), that is, Yahudha, the name of their first forefather to whom they trace their lineage. His name is Yahudha with the letter (dhal), but when it was Arabicised it became (Yahud). And Allah knows best. In any case, they are this tribe of the Children of Israel who claim that they follow whom? Moses. As for the Christians, it has been said that the name is derived from (nusrah), help. It has also been said that it is derived from a relation to a town called Nazareth. Whatever the case, they are those who ascribe themselves to Jesus.

His words ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews﴾. On this view, according to the opinion of the Jews, the Christians will not enter Paradise, and neither will the Muslims. It has already been mentioned that they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few days﴾ [al-Baqarah 80], and then, they say, you will be replaced by us in it. The Christians likewise hold that the Jews will not enter Paradise. Is this correct? It is correct after Jesus was sent and whoever disbelieved in him will not enter Paradise. And the Muslims will not enter Paradise? This is not correct. Rather, we say: you, O Christians, and likewise the Jews, after the sending of the Messenger (ﷺ), when you disbelieved in him, you became people of the Fire, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, whether Jew or Christian, and then does not believe in what I have brought, except that he will be among the people of the Fire." [Reported by Muslim, no. (153/240), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]

The conclusion is that this statement is false from both sides? From both sides. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Those are their wishful thinkings﴾. ﴿Those﴾ means that saying, ﴿their wishful thinkings﴾. (Amani) is the plural of (umniyyah), which is what a person wishes for without a cause that brings it to him. This wish is when you wish for something but do not take the means that lead to it. Someone says: I wish that Allah would give me a son. We say to him: get married. He says: no, I am not married. Is this wish a wish or not? Yes (...). For this reason the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "The wise one is he who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death, and the incapable one is he who follows his desires and wishes baseless wishes from Allah." [Reported by al-Tirmidhi, no. (2459), and Ibn Majah, no. (4260), from the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws.] These people wish. They say: we are believers, so Paradise is ours. We say: this is a false wish. Work for Paradise and you will be among its people. As for mere false wishes, these are (...) anything. For this reason He said: ﴿Those are their wishful thinkings﴾. Then He judged with justice: ﴿Say: Produce your proof, if you are truthful.﴾ See the justice here. That is, we do not reject your statement unless you fail to establish proof for it. If you establish proof for it, it is accepted with all respect. ﴿Produce your proof﴾, ﴿Say﴾, that is, O Muhammad, ﴿Produce your proof, if you are truthful.﴾ And (hatu) is an imperative verb or a verb-noun (ism fi'l)? 
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, but the rule is that it is an imperative verb (fi'l amr), because it indicates a command and takes the marker of the imperative, so it is a fi'l amr. Thus one says (hatu), one says to a woman (hati), and one says to two people (hatya). So it is an imperative verb.
* A student: The marker?
* The Shaykh: The marker is that it can take the attached subject pronoun, and then it is an imperative verb.
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: We say this is indeclinable (mabni) on kasra.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: We said it is an imperative verb, yes. It is indeclinable in any case, whatever comes and whatever it is called.

His words ﴿Produce your proof﴾: (al-burhan) is the proof, from (barhana) meaning to clarify a matter, or from (barihat al-shay') meaning a thing became clear through a sign. In the first case the (nun) is original, and in the second case the (nun) is extra. In both cases, (al-burhan) is the proof by which the opponent's argument is made clear. Bring the proof by which your claim becomes clear, and we will accept it. Then He said: ﴿if you are truthful﴾. Look: when it is said ﴿if you are truthful﴾, it means that this is a matter that cannot happen. ﴿Then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Baqarah 94]. It is not going to happen. It is a challenge. If they are truthful that none enters Paradise except Jews and Christians, let them bring the proof. Will they bring it? No. Then they are liars. If they are truthful, let them bring the proof. If they do not bring it, they are liars. The phrase ﴿Produce your proof﴾ is an imperative verb intended as a challenge and an assertion of inability, that this is a matter that cannot be.

And know that among the propaganda of the missionaries now, the Christian missionaries, is that they come to young people in America and elsewhere and say: O people, you are Muslims, people who love justice. If you love justice, come, read the Gospels. Read the Gospel and see whether there is anything in it. It is all a call to goodness, all a call to tolerance, all a call to doing good, and so on. A person is deceived by them, because when they say these words, "we follow justice," see whether we are wrong or not. The naive person is deceived by that. Indeed, perhaps they are truthful, and he forgets that Allah has declared them liars, forgets everything in the Qur'an and the Sunnah, because their (dulal) deceived him. They also have no proof for what they say, because the Gospels that are known now, how many are they? Four. The Gospels are four, this is well known. Each of them does not agree with the others on the greatest matter of Christian belief, which is the story of the crucifixion and killing of the Messiah. They do not agree on it at all. The experts say, I have not studied these Gospels, but those who have read them say that they are all not in agreement on this story, although it is among the greatest things for the Christians. Likewise, they also say that among what is in them is that Jesus, upon him be peace, when he was killed and buried and remained three days, came out, came out of his grave, and they call this the Resurrection. All the Gospels rely on this, on the saying of an unknown woman. Can belief be established by the saying of an unknown woman? It is impossible. Likewise, they say that this woman was an adulteress, and that they brought her to him and asked him to stone her according to the law of the Torah, and he said to them: I will stone her, but let the one among you who has not committed a sin begin the stoning. So they dispersed, because each of them had committed a sin, and he wanted to say: she committed a sin, and so did you, so forgiveness is required. Then when only he remained, he said: I also cannot stone you, because I am not free from error. So he pardoned her, although she was an adulteress, and she was the one who testified that when he was buried he rose from his grave. In any case, the truth is that some people say: I see, but I do not agree with that view. Some teachers among the professors say: I see that the Gospels should be spread among people so that they may know the lies and contradictions of the Christians. But we do not see this, because it contains a harm, for not everyone who wants to read it will be thorough in the matter. He reads the sound, beautiful parts, which Islam came with something like them, better than them, and then leaves aside the things that show these people to be liars. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Produce your proof﴾, because they have no proof. So now the Gospels which they say are our proof and evidence that what we say is true, we say: this is not correct, because whoever reflects upon them finds that they are not correct. But they come to these naive people who have no knowledge and no worship, and then deceive them, so that at least a person has doubt: is Islam the correct one, or is Christianity the correct one?
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but they are naive, pitiable people, who do not know. Islam is known only by one who has not lived in disbelief, as Umar said: "Islam will be undone strand by strand by one who was not in disbelief."
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: Distortion occurred in them in wording (...)?
* The Shaykh: In wording and meaning, all of them. There is verbal distortion and distortion of meaning. ﴿Say: Produce your proof, if you are truthful.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Yes (bala)﴾. (Bala) is a refutation of the negation in their saying ﴿will not enter﴾. This is clear, although some exegetes say that (bala) here means (bal), meaning rather: whoever submits. But we say: no, (bala) here is a particle of response, and (bala) is a particle of response that conveys the refutation of the negation. That is, when they said ﴿will not enter﴾, what did Allah say? Yes, those who are not Jews or Christians will enter Paradise. Who are they? ﴿Whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good, will have his reward with his Lord.﴾ (man) is a conditional word and is the subject (mubtada'), and the response to the condition is His saying ﴿will have his reward﴾. And His saying ﴿whoever submits﴾, ﴿submits his face﴾. What is meant by face is intention, purpose and will. He submits it to Allah, that is, he makes his direction, his will and his purpose towards Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They said: He expressed it by face because it is what indicates a person's intention. When you intend something, do you walk on your back toward it or on your face? On your face. So He expressed it by face, because by it intention is known. For this reason they say: where was the face of so-and-so? That is, where was his intention and direction? He says: towards such-and-such a direction, for example.

His words ﴿submits his face to Allah﴾: this is an action of the heart, which is sincerity. ﴿while being a doer of good﴾: the clause is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial (hal) from the subject of (aslama), that is, he submits while in the state of doing good, and the state is that he is a doer of good. What is meant by doing good is following the Messenger (ﷺ) outwardly and inwardly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) combined them in his saying: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you." [Reported by Muslim, no. (8/1), from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab.] The difference between the two clauses: "that you worship Allah as if you see Him" is the worship of longing, and "if you do not see Him, He sees you" is the worship of fleeing and fear. Because a person's worship is either love of Allah and longing for Him, which love and longing carry him to it, or he is fearful of Him, fearing the watchfulness of Allah the Exalted and His observation of him. The first state is more complete than the second. This is ihsan (excellence), and it is necessary. Sincerity alone is not sufficient. Sincerity alone is not enough. For this reason there are now people from this nation who say: we love Allah, we want Allah and we strive to reach His Paradise, yet they are deviant in His worship. Do they enter this verse? They do not enter it. Take the Sufis now. Most of the Sufis are among the most ascetic people in this world. They say: we do not intend anything but the face of Allah, and we want nothing but the face of Allah, yet they have innovations and superstitions that none can count except Allah. Shall we say that these people enter this verse? No, they do not enter it. Why? Because they lack ihsan, and ihsan, as I told you, is following the Messenger (ﷺ). So on this basis the verse indicates the two essential conditions of worship, which are: sincerity and following the Messenger (ﷺ), while being a doer of good.
* A student: But it only mentions sincerity.
* The Shaykh: Yes, and where is the sincerity?
* The student: ﴿whoever submits his face to Allah﴾, this is sincerity, and "doer of good" includes both matters.
* The Shaykh: Following the Messenger. Ihsan is following the Messenger.
* The student: But we said ihsan is sincerity and following.
* The Shaykh: No, no, we did not say that. We said the verse includes this.
* The student: So, all of it.
* The Shaykh: The whole verse.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, it is not (...).

His words ﴿then he will have his reward with his Lord﴾: reward (ajr) is what a person is given for his deed, as if you hired a person to build for you and you paid him. Here what is meant is the reward (thawab). What is meant is the reward. Allah the Exalted likened it to a wage (ajr) because it is a right of the person. Who made it obligatory upon Allah? Allah Himself made it obligatory upon Himself. The poet said:

The commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 2, verses 109–114 (part 4 of 7):

مَا لِلْعِبَادِ عَلَيْهِ حَقٌّ وَاجِب ∗∗∗ كَلَّا وَلَا سَعْيٌ لَدَيْهِ ضَائِـــــعُ ؎إِنْ عُذِّبُوا فَبِعَدْلِهِ أَوْ نُعِّمُوا ∗∗∗ فَبِفَضْلِهِ وَهُوَ الْكَرِيمُ الْوَاسِعُ

"His servants have no right over Him that is binding. No, and no effort of theirs is lost before Him. If they are punished, it is by His justice, or if they are blessed, it is by His bounty, and He is the Generous, the All-Encompassing."

But Ibn al-Qayyim, in the Nuniyya, restricted this verse, because it is unqualified, and said:

مَا لِلْعِبَادِ عَلَيْهِ حَـــــــــــــــــــــقٌّ وَاجِبٌ ∗∗∗ هُوَ أَوْجَبَ الْأَجْرَ الْعَظِيمَ الشَّانِ

"His servants have no right over Him that is binding; rather, He Himself made the great reward binding (upon Himself)."

"Rather, He Himself made it binding" — because the first line, "His servants have no right over Him that is binding," might lead a person to understand that God is not obligated to reward the obedient. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, clarified that it is an obligation that He Himself imposed upon Himself, not one imposed on Him by others. He said:

.................... ∗∗∗ هُوَ أَوْجَبَ الْأَجْرَ الْعَظِيمَ الشَّانِ
.................... ∗∗∗ كَلَّا وَلَا سَــــــعْيٌ لَـــــــدَيْهِ ضَائِــــــــــــعُ

The first line is unqualified, but Ibn al-Qayyim restricted it:

.................... ∗∗∗ إِنْ كَانَ بِالْإِخْلَاصِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ

"Provided it is with sincerity and excellence (of action)."

That is, if the effort is not with sincerity, or not with excellence, then it is lost.

إِنْ عُذِّبُوا فَبِعَدْلِهِ أَوْ نُعِّمُوا ∗∗∗ فَبِفَضْلِهِ وَالْفَضْلُ لِلْمَنَّــــــــــــــــــــانِ

"If they are punished, it is by His justice, or if they are blessed, it is by His bounty, and bounty belongs to the Bestower."

Meaning: the verse agrees (with the Qur'an).

﴿أَجْرُهُ﴾ To whom does the pronoun in ﴿أَجْرُهُ﴾ refer? To ﴿مَنْ أَسْلَمَ﴾ ("whoever submits")? That is, for this one who submitted while doing good, his reward. Could it not refer to the deed, so that his reward means the reward of submitting his face and doing good? That is permissible, because the reward is in reality in return for the deed, so attributing it to the deed is clear, and it is also for the doer, so attributing it to the doer is also clear.

And His saying ﴿أَجْرُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ﴾ ("his reward is with his Lord"): He attributed it to "with Him" for two benefits.

The first is that it is great, because what is attributed to something great is great. For this reason, in the hadith of Abu Bakr, which the Messenger ﷺ taught him, he said: "So forgive me with a forgiveness from You" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (834), and Muslim (2705/48), from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him]. This "with You" is significant, because what is with the Great is great.

The second benefit, from His saying ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ﴾ ("with his Lord"), is that this will not be lost, because you cannot find anyone more protective than Allah. Is that not so? There is no problem with it. So this deed will not be lost, it will not be lost, because it is in the utmost security. And this undoubtedly encourages a person to act; it encourages him. Now, if you were to hand a trust to a person, do you think you would be completely confident in it? He is not entirely trustworthy. The outward condition of the man is that he is trustworthy, but perhaps things will come upon him that he has no power over, and so it is lost, or his condition changes and he betrays.

As for the Lord, the Majestic and Exalted, this is impossible with regard to Him. The reward is with Allah. So the benefit of this "with Him" is twofold:

The first is that it is a great reward, because what comes from the Great is great.

The second is that it is protected, and in the utmost protection, because it is with Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

He said: ﴿وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve") [al-Baqarah 112]: no fear regarding what lies ahead of their affairs, and they will not grieve over what has passed of their affairs. For when they are gathered on the Day of Resurrection and find the outcomes of their deeds (O Allah, make us among those who find good), when they find that, they will not grieve over what has passed. Grief and regret belong to whom? To the one who neglected and wasted: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ وَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness and do not believe") [Maryam 39].

But the believer does not grieve, because he has benefited from his life. As for the disbeliever, he will grieve, and Allah will show them their deeds as regrets upon them: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ الْخَاسِرِينَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ ("Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection") [al-Zumar 15].

﴿وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ يَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي اتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ سَبِيلًا (27) يَا وَيْلَتَى لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلَانًا خَلِيلًا (28)﴾ ("And on the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying: Oh, I wish I had taken a way with the Messenger. Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend") [al-Furqan 27–28]. And so on to the end.

The point is that they will not grieve on the Day of Resurrection, because they (...) find the results of their deeds and their fruits, the best of results and the best of fruit. So they are secure, are they not? They are secure from what lies ahead, and content with what has passed. There is no grief for them and no fear: ﴿وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾. When we recite this verse, we should not recite it merely as a report, but we should recite it as something that educates us, reciting it as a means of education, meaning that we submit our faces to Allah and do good in our deeds. Do you understand? And likewise, all of the Qur'an: we should not recite it only to understand its meaning, but to act upon it, as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did: when they recited ten verses they would not go beyond them until they had learned them and what they contain of knowledge and action. They said: "So we learned the Qur'an, and knowledge and action together" [narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: (1/80)].

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ ("And the Jews said: The Christians are not on anything") [al-Baqarah 113].

They are enemies of one another in one respect, and allies of one another in another respect. As for us, they are allies of one another, and as for what is between them, they are enemies of one another. But as regards us, they say: our enemy is common; Islam is a common enemy of Judaism and Christianity, so some of us must be allies with others. He says: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾. The word ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ is qualified by an omitted attribute, because they are certainly "on something": the Christians are on something, is that not so? They are on something, a religion. But what they mean is "on something beneficial," or "on something of value." That is, it necessarily implies an omitted attribute. Estimate it if you wish as "on something beneficial," or if you wish, estimate it as "on something of worth." That is: they are not on anything of worth that benefits them. As for His saying ﴿لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى﴾, how did He make the verb feminine? Why did He make the verb feminine?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Because of the plural. And Ibn Malik says:

وَالتَّاءُ مَعْ جَمْعٍ سِوَى الْسَّالِمِ مِنْ ∗∗∗ مُذَكَّرٍ كَالْتَّاءِ مَعْ إِحْدَى اللَّبِنْ

"And the tā' (feminine marker) is used with a plural other than the sound masculine plural, just as the tā' is used with one of the bricks."

(...) And the Christians likewise made a false claim, saying: None will enter Paradise except those who are Christians. Allah, the Exalted, refuted this claim with His saying: ﴿تِلْكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمْ قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ ("Those are their wishful thoughts. Say: Bring your proof, if you should be truthful") [al-Baqarah 111].

Allah, glorified and exalted, described the people of Paradise as those who combined two matters: sincerity to Allah, glorified and exalted, by submitting their faces to Him, and following His Law while being good-doers. This includes whoever submitted from this Ummah and from those before it, and everyone who submits to Allah while doing good, from this Ummah and others. They are the companions of Paradise, and it has already been mentioned that there is no fear for them regarding what lies ahead, nor grief over what has passed.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, clarifying that these Jews and Christians each deny the law of the other: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾, meaning: on anything of the religion, not of life. They are alive, eating, drinking, marrying, and enjoying themselves in this world, but they are not on anything of the religion, because, as they claim, their religion is false. The Jews did not believe in Jesus, and for this reason they denied that the Christians were on anything. The Christians responded in kind: ﴿وَقَالَتِ النَّصَارَى لَيْسَتِ الْيَهُودُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ ("And the Christians said: The Jews are not on anything") [al-Baqarah 113], meaning: not on anything of the religion. As for the claim of the Jews, it is false in every respect, because the Christians are undoubtedly on a religion. As for the claim of the Christians, it is not false in every respect; rather, the Jews are not on anything after the religion of the Christians, since it is obligatory upon them to believe in Jesus, and if they deny him, they are not on anything; they are disbelievers. So which of the two claims is closer to the truth: the claim of the Jews or that of the Christians? The claim of the Christians. The Jews' claim that the Christians are not on anything is false in every respect. As for the Christians' claim that the Jews are on something, it is correct, when? After Jesus. But before Jesus, the Christians' claim in that regard is false, for the Jews were on the religion and on a sound, upright law. Now, in the grammar: ﴿لَيْسَتِ الْيَهُودُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ and ﴿لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾. The Jews in the first is marked with a ḍamma and the Christians with a fatḥa, although the governing word, "laysat," is one. Why? The Jews in the first is marked with a ḍamma and the Christians with a fatḥa, although the governing word is one. Why?

* Student: Because the Christians do not show the markings.
* The Shaykh: That is, it is not marked with a fatḥa?
* Student: No, it is marked with an implied ḍamma.
* The Shaykh: On what?
* Student: On the alif.
* The Shaykh: On the alif? Correct? Yes, yes. Is it not confusing? The Jews show the ḍamma because its last letter is a sound consonant, which is the dāl; the Christians do not show the ḍamma because its last letter is a weak letter (ḥarf 'illah), which is the alif.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَهُمْ يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ ("while they recite the Scripture"). This clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyyah), and the pronoun "they" refers to the Jews and the Christians, meaning that these claimants all, while they ﴿يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾, that is, recite it. "The Scripture" here is a generic noun, so it includes the Torah, which the Jews recite, and the Gospel, which the Christians recite. The clause is circumstantial, and its purpose is to denounce this claim: how can they make this claim while they recite the Scripture? The Christians recite the Torah and know that the Jews follow the Torah, so they were on something; and the Christians likewise recite the Torah and recite the Gospel, and know that Jesus is true, but they disbelieved out of arrogance. There is no doubt that the one who denies the truth while reciting its document is uglier than the one who denies the truth out of ignorance of it. Do you agree with this?

* The students: We agree.
* The Shaykh: Yes, we agree, because the one who denies it while the document is in his hands is obstinate, stubbornly arrogant, unlike the ignorant. The ignorant may deny a thing because he does not know it, but the scholar has no excuse. For this reason He said: ﴿وَهُمْ يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾. And you know that the circumstantial clause, whether a sentence or a single word, is a description of its subject. The circumstantial (ḥāl), which the grammarians call the ḥāl, is a description of its subject. If you say: "Zayd came riding," it means that his description is what? Riding. And if you say: "Zayd came while he was on his camel," it is known that his description is also riding, and the clause is circumstantial.

Now, ﴿وَهُمْ يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾: I said, is "the Scripture" a generic noun or a specific one? A generic noun, so it includes the Torah and the Gospel. And His saying ﴿الْكِتَابَ﴾ is a verbal noun in the sense of a passive participle (fa'āl bi-ma'nā maf'ūl), because the books sent down from heaven are written and read. Especially since the Torah was written by Allah with His own hand, as is related in reports, and it is undoubtedly tablets that were given to Moses. Moses brought them from Allah, as in the story: ﴿وَأَلْقَى الْأَلْوَاحَ﴾ ("and he threw down the tablets") [al-A'raf 150]; ﴿وَكَتَبْنَا لَهُ فِي الْأَلْوَاحِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وَتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ ("And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything") [al-A'raf 145].

* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, how can that be? Because their saying "on anything," we do not know. We told you at the beginning: if they mean before the mission of Jesus, they are mistaken, for the Jews were on something.
* Student: The Christians disbelieved in Moses?
* The Shaykh: No, the Christians did not disbelieve in Moses. The Christians believe in Moses, but they deny the religion of the Jews. And you (...) "on something," we said: there is detail in it.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَهُمْ يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ ("And they recite the Scripture. Likewise said those who do not know, the like of their words") [al-Baqarah 113]. The grammarians say about ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾: the kāf in such a construction is a noun meaning "like," in the accusative as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), and that dhā, which is a demonstrative, refers to the verbal noun; that is: "like that saying, said those who came before them." Also, His saying, Exalted: ﴿قَالَتْ إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا وَجَعَلُوا أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَا أَذِلَّةً وَكَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ ("She said: Indeed, kings, when they enter a city, ruin it and make the most honored of its people the most humble, and thus they do") [al-Naml 34]: meaning, "and thus they do." Whenever such a construction occurs, they say that the kāf is a noun meaning "like," an absolute object, and it is in apposition to the demonstrative which refers to the verbal noun of the governing verb that follows it. Now, if I say to you, for example: "I said likewise," what is the meaning? I say: "I said a similar saying," "I did likewise," that is: "I did a similar deed," "I read a similar reading," that is: "I read a similar reading," and so on.

His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾. ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: Allah negated knowledge from them, meaning: "Likewise said those who do not know," that is, they did not read a book. ﴿مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ means: like the saying of these people. The phrase ﴿مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ is said to be an emphasis of ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ﴾, because we told you that ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ﴾ means "he said a similar saying," and it is known that a single governing word does not govern two accusatives in this way, so they said: "like their saying" is an emphasis of ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ﴾.

As for His saying ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: who are "those who do not know"? Some exegetes said: "Those who do not know" are earlier nations, like His saying in the second verse: ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ ("Likewise said those before them") [al-Baqarah 118]. So they are earlier nations who did not know. Other exegetes said: ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ means "among these," meaning that the Jews and the Christians who recite the Scripture said the like of the saying of those among them who do not know; so the saying of their learned and their ignorant became equal. Other exegetes said: what is meant by ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is the disbelieving Quraysh, the people of ignorance (jāhiliyyah), for they said that Muhammad ﷺ was not on a religion and not on anything. And the best of these views, the better one, is what? 

* Student: Everyone who does not know.
* The Shaykh: Yes, we say it in its generality, as Ibn Jarir and others chose. For when a verse contains multiple meanings that do not contradict one another, it is obligatory to take it in all these possibilities. This is from the breadth of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the comprehensiveness of its meaning. This is an established principle in exegesis, which a person should keep in mind: when a verse is explained by multiple sayings, and some of them do not conflict with others with respect to the noble verse, then it is to be understood according to both.

﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqarah 113]: meaning, they denied the truth. So they said, for example, about the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "They are not on anything." And those who denied the messengers also said: "The messengers are not on anything." And they also said to the people of knowledge and faith: "They are not on anything." And so on until the Day of Resurrection, this saying may be repeated, and to this day the ignorant say to the people of knowledge: "They are not on anything."

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ ("So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding that in which they used to differ") [al-Baqarah 113]. ﴿فَاللَّهُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction particle, and "Allah" is the subject (mubtada'), and the clause ﴿يَحْكُمُ﴾, the clause, is in the place of the predicate (khabar) of the subject. So "Allah judges," and this is for the future, the imperfect, or for the past? For the future, by the evidence of His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ ("on the Day of Resurrection").

His saying: ﴿يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: judgment means decision and separation between two things, and Allah, blessed and exalted, on the Day of Resurrection decides between people regarding that in which they differed. He makes clear to the one with the truth his truth and rewards him for it, and He makes clear to the one with falsehood his falsehood and requites him for it. The judgment of Allah, glorified and exalted, is divided into three categories: legislative (sharʿī), cosmic (kawnī), and recompensing (jazāʾī). The legislative is like His saying, Exalted, in Surah al-Mumtahanah: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ حُكْمُ اللَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ ("That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is Knowing and Wise") [al-Mumtahanah 10].

The ruling of God: is it legislative, or cosmic, or retributive? It is legislative. The cosmic ruling is like His words, exalted is He, about His brother Joseph: ﴿So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or God decides for me, and He is the best of judges﴾ [Yusuf 80]. That is cosmic. The retributive ruling is like this verse: ﴿God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Nisa 141]. The retributive ruling is the fruit of the legislative ruling, because if the deed is good the result is good, and if it is evil the result is evil. This judgment on the Day of Resurrection among people: is it by justice or by bounty? We say: it is either by justice, or by bounty, or by injustice, and injustice is negated. Injustice is negated; God has forbidden it to Himself and to His servants, as in the hadith qudsi: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and made it forbidden among you."[[Recorded by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari.]] What remains? Justice and bounty remain. So we say: as regards the rights of people among themselves, the judgment is by justice. As regards what is between the servant and his Lord, the judgment is by justice for the disbelievers and by bounty for the believers, because the disbeliever is recompensed with justice: ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾ [Ghafir 40]. As for the believer, he is recompensed with bounty: "A good deed is multiplied tenfold, and an evil deed is repaid with its like, or He pardons it."[[Recorded by Ahmad (16206) from the hadith of Luqayt ibn 'Amir, with the wording: "...and an evil deed is repaid with its like, unless He pardons," and in al-Bukhari (41) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri with the wording: "A good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, and an evil deed is repaid with its like, unless God overlooks it."]] Is this so or not? So the retributive judgment among creatures is by justice; the one who has a right must be given his right. Between a person and his Lord it moves between justice and bounty. Good, what is your answer regarding His words: ﴿so that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾ [Yunus 4]?
* Student: (...).
* Student: It is restricted (specified).
* Shaykh: We say: the answer, and God knows best, is that this is what is due to them by what God has obligated, and bounty is an addition. And this is by way of warning, meaning: a person does not receive for every deed [more than its due]; this is the basic principle for you, and this is the utmost justice. But bounty is an increase from God, exalted is He.

He said: ﴿He will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The Day of Resurrection, we have explained before, is named so for certain reasons. For what is the Day of Resurrection named?
* Student: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 6].
* Shaykh: ﴿Before the Lord of the worlds,﴾ yes.
* Student: On it justice is established.
* Shaykh: On it justice is established, yes.
* Student: ﴿Mankind will stand...﴾
* Shaykh: It has been mentioned.
* Student: The standing of the witnesses.
* Shaykh: Yes, the standing of the witnesses, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the Day when the witnesses will stand﴾ [Ghafir 51]. So it is the Day of Resurrection because people stand up from their graves before the Lord of the worlds, and because justice is established on it, and because of the standing of the witnesses.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The witnesses are to bear witness: the nations bear witness against them, the messengers bear witness, and this Ummah bears witness against the earlier nations, and the hands and the feet [bear witness].
﴿On the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. Because it is known that there is disagreement on it between the believer and the disbeliever, is it not? There is disagreement among the Christians, the people of the religion, all of them. The Christians and the Jews disagree; indeed the Christians now disagree about their creeds, disagree with one another in a fundamental way, a fundamental difference in the roots, not merely in the branches: in the manner of the crucifixion of Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, and in the resurrection which is claimed: that he was raised from his grave after three days, and other matters. So they disagree. The Jews likewise are in disagreement. Likewise the Muslims generally with the disbelievers. The one who judges between them is God, mighty and majestic, on the Day of Resurrection. This judgment is not based on conjecture and assumption, but on knowledge. Every person's deed is recorded in a book, and it is said: ﴿Read your book﴾ [al-Isra 14]. And every person has an attending watcher; when the Day of Resurrection comes, he is present: ﴿And his companion will say: This is what is ready with me﴾ [Qaf 23], meaning present. Likewise, on the Day of Resurrection, every person's limbs bear witness against him for what he did. So this judgment is based on the most upright evidence and the most just rulings.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned therein﴾ [al-Baqara 114].

(Man) is an interrogative noun and is the subject (mubtada'), and "more unjust" (azlam) is its predicate. The interrogative here carries the meaning of negation, meaning: no one is more unjust. What is the interrogative that carries the meaning of negation? In other words, what is the criterion that shows you that the interrogative carries the meaning of negation? That if you remove the interrogative and put the negation in its place, it is correct. So here, "who is more unjust," if you say, "No one is more unjust," does the sentence stand? It stands. What is the benefit of converting the negation into an interrogative? Because it is more emphatic in negation, since the interrogative that carries the meaning of negation is imbued with the meaning of challenge, as if he is saying: "Show me who is more unjust than such-and-such." So the benefit of the interrogative that carries the meaning of negation, the benefit of converting the negation, is that since the discussion here is about negation, but the benefit of converting it into an interrogative is that when it is converted, it is imbued with what? With challenge, as if challenging: who is more unjust? Go and find anyone more unjust than the one who prevented [the mosques].

His words, ﴿azlam﴾ (more unjust), is a comparative noun (ism al-tafdil) from injustice (zulm). Its original linguistic meaning is deficiency: that a person neglects what is obligatory, or transgresses what is forbidden. This is the definition of injustice. In language, the root of injustice is deficiency, as in His words: ﴿Each of the two gardens gave its produce and did not fall short therefrom in anything﴾ [al-Kahf 33]. "Did not fall short" means did not diminish. In the Shariah it has this same meaning, because injustice is an expression for neglecting an obligation or violating a prohibition, and this is a deficiency. No one is more unjust ﴿than one who prevents the mosques of God﴾ [al-Baqara 114]. ﴿Min man﴾: (man) is an interrogative noun; (min) is a preposition, since (min) is a particle of genitive, and (man) here is an interrogative? Is that right?
* Student: No, the first is a preposition and the second is a relative pronoun.
* Shaykh: (man) here is a relative pronoun with the meaning of "the one who." So: who is more unjust than the one who prevented the mosques of God?!

Regarding His words, ﴿than the one who prevented the mosques of God﴾: is the intended meaning a specific person? Because it is a singular noun, or does it encompass everyone who has this attribute?
It encompasses all, because it has already passed us in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) that all relative pronouns are general terms; all relative pronouns, whether singular, dual or plural, all convey generality. His words: ﴿prevented the mosques of God from having His name mentioned﴾. Preventing the mosques of God in reality has causes. Sometimes the mosques are prevented from being defiled, their carpets, floors, books or Qur'ans, so the doors are closed to protect them. Does this fall under it? No. ﴿Who prevented the mosques of God from having His name mentioned therein﴾: this prevention is preventing the holding of remembrance circles in them, preventing the holding of sermons in them, preventing the holding of prayers in them, preventing the recitation of the Qur'an in them. This is what is no longer mentioned in them, His name. As for preventing them from being corrupted, stolen from, or having their books and Qur'ans torn, this does not fall under this category. What falls under the category is "mentioning." That is why, regarding the grammatical analysis of ﴿an yudhkara﴾ (that it be mentioned), we say: either it is an explicative apposition ('atf bayan) or an inclusive substitution (badal ishtimal) of the phrase ﴿mosques of God﴾. Or we say: (an yudhkara) is in the accusative by removal of the preposition (naz' al-khafid), in a regular or irregular manner?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What is the evidence from Ibn Malik?
* Student: His words:
"Transmitted, and with (anna) and (an) it is regular, with security from ambiguity, like 'I was amazed that they...'"
* Shaykh: Good. The point is: "an yudhkara" (that it be mentioned): it is correct to say "from that it be mentioned." And the mosques are attributed to God as ﴿mosques of God﴾, because they are the place of His worship, so the attribution here is by way of honour. We have mentioned to you before that what is attributed to God is divided into two categories. Either they are attributes, or entities, or attributes in entities; three categories: either attributes, or entities, or attributes in created entities.
* Shaykh: Have you understood the division now? If what is attributed to God is an attribute, then it is one of His attributes and uncreated, like: the speech of God, the hand of God, the knowledge of God. If what is attributed to God is a self-subsisting entity, then it is created, and it is not one of His attributes, like: the mosques of God, the she-camel of God, the House of God. These are self-subsisting entities, so their attribution to God is the attribution of a created thing to its Creator by way of honour. And none of the created things is attributed to God, exalted is He, except for a specific reason particular to it; were it not for that reason, it would not be attributed to Him, it would not be singled out for attribution. Good. The third?
Attributes in created entities: these too are created. This we say, if the expression is acceptable, such as: ﴿And I breathed into him of My spirit﴾ [al-Hijr 29]. The spirit here is an attribute in the body, if it is correct to say "attribute." People differ about it: is it an attribute, or an entity, or a meaning? In any case, even if we say it is an entity, it falls under the second category; and if we say it is an attribute, it is a separate category, but it is an attribute in a created thing, so it is created. And His words here, ﴿the mosques of God﴾, include all mosques, whether these mosques have a special status like the three mosques, or have no special status, like mosques in general.
His words, ﴿the mosques of God﴾, exclude a place where prayer was performed but which has not been made a mosque, because until now it has not become God's. Such as a group who fenced off a place in the desert and prayed in it: does this become one of the mosques of God? No. It is a mosque, but it is not attributed to God, mighty and majestic, because it has not been established for permanent status as a mosque.
His words, ﴿that His name be mentioned therein﴾: "that His name be mentioned therein," (ism) is a deputy subject (na'ib fa'il) or a subject (fa'il)?
* Student: Deputy subject.
* Shaykh: Deputy subject, because "yudhkar" is an imperfect verb in the passive voice, the subject not being named, or in the passive; so it is a deputy subject. His words, ﴿that His name be mentioned therein﴾, and He did not say "that God be mentioned therein," even though He said in Surat al-Nur: ﴿Men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God and the establishment of prayer﴾ [al-Nur 37]. This is because God is mentioned only by His name. Mention by the tongue is only with the name of God. As for mention of the heart, it is mention of God and mention of His names; a person may reflect in his heart on the names of God and contemplate them, and this is a mention of the name. And he may reflect on the acts of God, mighty and majestic, His creation, and His legislative rulings. As for the tongue, what must there be in it? Mention of the name of God.

﴿Whose name is mentioned therein and who strives for their ruin﴾ [al-Baqara 114]. This is coordinated with ﴿prevented﴾. That is, he combines two attributes: preventing mosques in which His name is mentioned, and ﴿striving for their ruin﴾. Ruin (kharab) is the opposite of righteousness, as God said: ﴿They ruin their houses with their own hands﴾ [al-Hashr 2]. And in a reading[[Read with the shadda (doubling) by Abu 'Amr; see al-Nashr (2/293).]]: ﴿yukharribuna buyutahum bi-aydihim﴾ (they lay waste their houses by their own hands). Is the intended ruin here physical or spiritual? The apparent meaning, and God knows best, is that it includes both. Because some people may, God forbid, set out to demolish mosques physically, with mallets and bombs, is that not so? And they may ruin them spiritually. How is ruin spiritual? That they prevent God's remembrance in them, prevent God's remembrance in them. On this basis, ﴿strives for their ruin﴾ is an explanation of His words: ﴿prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned therein,﴾ for this is part of their ruin.

His words, ﴿and strives for their ruin﴾: "sa'y" (striving) means walking quickly, and it is also applied to mere action, even if not quickly. ﴿And strives for their ruin﴾: can we say that among the striving for their ruin is failing to attend congregation?
* The students: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes (...), but if this man remains absent, and this man, and this man, and the people do not pray in the mosque...
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No, we said: he strove for its ruin, the spiritual and physical ruin. If congregation is not held in it, that is spiritual ruin. But it may be said: one who abandons congregation, yes, if they all do so, this may fall under this matter, because they have left it idle. But if it is one person, when one person stays away, another comes, and his absence does not necessarily cause the mosque to be idle.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: (...) So deeds are by intentions.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Praise and speak about monotheism?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Praise the Messenger ﷺ with what befits him, peace be upon him, but do not exaggerate about him. I say: praise the Messenger and speak about monotheism.
* Student: They do not speak about monotheism (...).
* Shaykh: Innovated praise. This is among those who prevent the mosques of God from having His name mentioned therein. But you should come to an understanding with them, for example, you sit down, and do not oppose them, so that chaos does not result, and afterwards reason with them in the best manner.
* Student: In our mosques, a group comes on Wednesday, they bring white cloths and caps and seize the people by force, making them stay so they can remember and sway and chant "dhikr"?
* Shaykh: This is striving for ruin, because establishing innovations in mosques is a ruin of them.
* Student: Indeed, we said to them: "Good people, do not seize people. Whoever wants to sit with you, (...) let him sit, do not seize people by force."
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in God.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: The meaning of this is that when the Banu al-Nadir made reconciliation with them, and they realized that they were departing and leaving their houses, they began to ruin them, breaking the doors and destroying the things in them, so that if the Muslims took them, they would be in ruins.
* Student: And the hands of the believers.
* Shaykh: And the hands of the believers: as for them, they are in ruin; that is, they now ruined them against themselves when they occupied them.
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: "Mana'" (prevent) takes two objects.
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: "Masajid" is the first object.
* Student: Coordination (conjunction).
* Shaykh: Coordination of what? There is no "wa" (and) in it.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No. We told you: there are two possibilities.
