Everything is what Allah intends, whether it develops gradually or occurs suddenly; and I do not know of anything occurring suddenly like this except through development, because it is part of Allah the Exalted's way that development occurs in the law and in destiny; everything must have a gradation until it is complete and finished. And we now have the generality of ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ [Ali 'Imran 47], and every matter is decreed for Him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 115–119 (part 2 of 4):

﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ This is what can be excluded from this generality, except for something we know with certainty was excluded from it. It is correct that Adam's creation by Allah, by His hand, is something we cannot say means that whenever Allah wants to create something from him He says to him: "Be," and we cannot assert this. Allah, glorified and exalted, may by His will have brought him into being with His hand as He willed, and then said to him: "Be," meaning: be a complete human being. As for the hadith: «أَجْعَلُ مَنْ خَلَقْتُهُ بِيَدَيَّ كَمَنْ خَلَقْتُهُ بِكَلِمَتِي» [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (147) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]] this must be examined, and I do not know whether it is authentic; God willing, verify it for us.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ لَوْلَا يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ أَوْ تَأْتِينَا آيَةٌ﴾ [al-Baqarah 118] These are the ones who denied the messengers, and what is meant by them are those of the time of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ "Likewise said those before them." Those who do not know are those of the time of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. They said: ﴿لَوْلَا يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ أَوْ تَأْتِينَا آيَةٌ﴾ "Why does Allah not speak to us, or a sign come to us?" So they proposed to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, things, while the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had come with greater than them, and yet they did not believe in those either. This shows that their proposal was nothing but obstinacy and stubbornness, and not intended to reach the truth, because the Messenger ﷺ came with greater than what they proposed. ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ لَوْلَا يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ﴾. Does the truthfulness of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, necessarily fail because the sign they asked for, which is Allah speaking to them, is absent?
* Students: No, it does not necessarily follow.
* Shaykh: It does not necessarily follow, because what is established is not restricted to a single proof; that is, things may have multiple proofs. The establishment of the Messenger's prophethood, peace and blessings be upon him, does not depend on these signs they proposed, since he has brought signs stronger than them. For this reason, it is an established principle that the absence of a specific proof does not entail the absence of what it proves, why? Because what is proven has multiple proofs. If we assume it was not established by this proof, it has been established by another proof. When Abraham debated the one who said: "I give life and cause death," he brought another proof: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي بِالشَّمْسِ مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِهَا مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ﴾ [al-Baqarah 258]. The point is that to those who said: "Why does Allah not speak to us?" we say: Allah's speaking to you does not necessarily entail the truthfulness of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, nor does its absence entail his untruthfulness, because there are signs and proofs stronger than what you claim. So your saying: "It must come to us, this specific sign" is not accepted, since signs indicating his truthfulness exist. Your demand for this specific sign is stubbornness, like if you asked a person for a need and he fulfilled it for you, and you said: "No, I will only accept it from so-and-so, and it is the same need." What does this mean?
* Student: Stubbornness.
* Shaykh: The meaning of this is stubbornness. Your request has been fulfilled. As for your being stubborn about such and such without any cause, and these people without cause; for Allah speaking to them is not something they want as an honor from Allah to them through speech. They do not want this. If they wanted this, we would say: it is a reasonable request. But what do they want by it?
* Student: Incapacitating (the Messenger).
* Shaykh: They want by it to establish the prophethood of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. They say: "If you are truthful, let Allah speak to us." Do you understand or not? I am now saying: if they had asked that Allah speak to them as an honor for them, their request would have been reasonable, but they asked that Allah speak to them so that the Messenger's ﷺ prophethood would be established by that.
We say: this claim of yours is stubbornness, since the Messenger ﷺ came with something greater than this. Likewise they said: ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِينَا آيَةٌ﴾. Subhan Allah! ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِينَا آيَةٌ﴾? As if no sign had come to them proving the truthfulness of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and this is denial. So the first is stubbornness, and the second is denial. The first: stubbornness in their insisting on a specific thing, saying: "Will you bring it or we will not believe?" The second: denial and rejection, or "let a sign come to us"; for there is no doubt that great signs came to them. The greatest sign that came to them is this Qur'an. Allah, exalted is He, said to them: ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ﴾ [al-Baqarah 23]. Bring a surah like it. Could you?
* Students: No, Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Then, is the Qur'an from Muhammad ﷺ? No; if it were from Muhammad, they would have been able to bring its like, since they are like him, although he was the most eloquent of them because of the revelation sent down to him. So: ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِينَا آيَةٌ﴾ we say: this last proposal is undoubtedly denial and rejection. Why?
* Student: Because a sign has already come to them.
* Shaykh: Because a sign has already come to them, indeed signs. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqarah 118]. "Likewise" means: like this statement, said those before them. On this basis, ﴿مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ "like their statement" is an emphasis of His saying ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾, meaning: a statement like this was said and proposed by those before them. The people of Musa said: ﴿لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّى نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً﴾ [al-Baqarah 55]. "We will not believe you until we see Allah plainly," and "Show us Allah openly, or we will not believe you." This is the way of those who deny the messengers: they deny and they propose, and they were given signs greater than what they proposed. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾. The purpose of His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾ is to console the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Right?
* Students: Yes indeed.
* Shaykh: Because a person who is afflicted, when he sees that others have been afflicted, is consoled by that, and this is well known. Right? Suppose, for example, thieves raided houses and stole a hundred riyals from one person. Of course he grieves, but when another says: "Two hundred were stolen from me," what happens?
* Student: ... it becomes easy.
* Shaykh: It becomes easy for him, very easy. When al-Khansa's brother Sakhr died, she said:
"Were it not for the abundance of those weeping around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself. / They do not weep like my brother, but I console myself for him with consolation."
Allah, exalted, consoles His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that this statement said to you has been said to those before you: ﴿كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿تَشَابَهَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ Look: the earlier and later ones, their hearts are alike in rejecting and nullifying the truth, in obstinacy, stubbornness and denial, from the time the messengers were sent until their seal, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and even until the Day of Resurrection. The hearts of the people of disbelief, may Allah protect us, and obstinacy are alike; only the style differs, the subject is one, but the style differs. These may propose one thing and those another, but the discussion concerns the type of proposal and non-acceptance: ﴿تَشَابَهَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾. For this reason He said: ﴿تَشَابَهَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾. Notice: about the statement He says ﴿مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ﴾, and about the hearts He says ﴿تَشَابَهَتْ﴾. So does this mean that similarity (mushabahah) is the same as equivalence (mumathalah) or not? What we established earlier is that similarity is not like equivalence, because mushabahah means approximation, and mumathalah means equality, right?
* Students: Yes indeed.
* Shaykh: There is no doubt that hearts resemble one another even when statements are identical, since among these people there may be what is not among those, of intense disbelief and obstinacy, but the statements are identical.
Allah, exalted, said: ﴿قَدْ بَيَّنَّا الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ "bayyanna" means "we made clear," since (bâna) means "became apparent," and (bayyana) means "made apparent." And His saying ﴿الْآيَاتِ﴾ is the plural of āyah, which is the sign that specifies what it indicates; every sign that specifies what it indicates is called āyah. So the signs that specify the one to whom they are signs are called āyāt, and Allah's signs are the indications pointing to Him, that is, specifying Him, glorified and exalted. The scholars mentioned that they are divided into two types: legislative signs and cosmic signs. The legislative signs are what the messengers brought of revelation, and they are signs because there is no parallel to them in truthfulness of reports, goodness of narratives, and justice of rulings. The legislative signs of Allah have no parallel in human speech in these three matters: truthfulness of reports; goodness of narratives, that is, all the stories in the Qur'an (...) are all beneficial stories and great lessons; and the third, justice of rulings, for which there is no parallel at all. However much you find of systems, laws, and sayings, both well-known and not, you cannot find the like of this Qur'an. Therefore it is a sign from the signs of Allah.
Likewise the cosmic signs, whose manifestness is greater and clearer, because you can argue with them rationally against the one who denies Allah or not, like...?
* Student: The night and the day, the sun and the moon.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed, like the heavens and the earth, the sun and the moon, the night and the day, and everything.
"And in everything there is a sign that indicates that He is One."
These are signs, O brothers. Allah says that He has made them clear, but to whom? ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ The one with certainty, the signs become clear to him and he knows them, while the doubter is not made clear. The doubter does not get clarity, may Allah protect us, and matters may be obscured to him, and he may move from doubt to the stage of denial, because doubt, as you know, is a stage between two stages: between affirmation and denial. So it may be that with doubt, may Allah protect us, he reaches the point of denial. Doubt is not sufficient for faith. In this verse, ﴿قَدْ بَيَّنَّا الْآيَاتِ﴾ is evidence that Allah has established the proof, and that the signs do not benefit everyone; they benefit only the one who is certain. As for the doubter, the signs do not benefit him: ﴿وَمَا تُغْنِي الْآيَاتُ وَالنُّذُرُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [Yunus 101].
* Student: Shaykh, is this statement the statement of the Jews of Medina, that the surah is Medinan?
* Shaykh: Which of them?
* Student: Those who said the surah is Medinan.
* Shaykh: No, it is general. That is, ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is general, and (qala) is a past-tense verb that includes what existed at the time the verse was revealed and what preceded it.
* Student: (...) it is the splitting of the moon, the splitting of the moon (...) so does...?
* Shaykh: No, the scholars said: they asked for an unspecified sign.
* Student: Were they answered?
* Shaykh: Yes, they were answered with this sign, and those who are destroyed when they propose are answered; if they ask for a specific sign and are answered with it, they will be destroyed.
Allah, exalted, said: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا﴾ [al-Baqarah 119]. That is, the meaning is that those who say: ﴿لَوْلَا يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ﴾ are answered with this verse: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾. And "inna" is for emphasis. Where is its subject?
* Student: (...).
* Another student: Its subject is the pronoun.
* Shaykh: And where is the pronoun?
* Student: "We" (nahnu).
* Shaykh: And where is "we"?
* Student: "(na)", Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Its subject is (na), but the nun was deleted only to avoid the succession of similar sounds, although sometimes (innana) is not deleted, ﴿وَإِنَّنَا لَفِي شَكٍّ﴾ [Hud 62]. But do not say its subject is the alif, lest one of you say its subject is the alif, since the alif is not a pronoun except when attached to a verb, like qala, qama, and what is similar.
﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ To whom were you sent? The recipients are omitted to indicate generality, since the Prophet ﷺ is sent to all creation, while other messengers were sent to whom?
* Students: To their own people specifically.
* Shaykh: To their own people specifically. As for the Messenger: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾.
And His saying: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ The "bi" here is for accompaniment and association, meaning: We sent you accompanied by the truth; or the meaning is: carrying the truth with this message. That is, the verse may bear two meanings: one, that your sending is true; the second, that what you were sent with is true. Have you understood the difference between the two meanings?
Both meanings are established: the Messenger's prophethood, peace and blessings be upon him, is true, and accordingly the "bi" is for association; and what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent with is true, and accordingly the "bi" is for accompaniment, meaning your message is accompanied by truth, since what you brought is true. We said that truth is the opposite of falsehood, and it is what is firm and stable. If it is attributed to reports, it means truthfulness; if it is attributed to rulings, it means justice. What the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought is true in its reports and in its rulings: ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا﴾ [al-An'am 115]. It is apparently not hidden from everyone that truth is accepted and desired by every soul, is it not so?
* Students: Indeed.
* Shaykh: If so, whoever seeks the truth finds it, and whoever turns away from it to falsehood is punished by being deprived of it. Have you understood?
﴿بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا﴾ May Allah bless and grant him peace. ﴿بَشِيرًا﴾ is a circumstantial state (hal) of whom?
* Student: Of the kaf in ﴿أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾.
* Shaykh: Of the kaf in ﴿أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾, which is the object. And ﴿وَنَذِيرًا﴾: another circumstantial state by means of the conjunction. Thus Allah combined in him being a bringer of good news and a warner, because what he brought includes commands and prohibitions; what fits commands is good news, and what fits prohibitions is warning. Accordingly, the prophethood of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, combines glad tidings and warning. Who is given glad tidings by it, and who is warned by it?
Allah explained this in several verses: in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا مِنْ لَدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا﴾ [al-Kahf 2]. Likewise He said: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنْذِرَ بِهِ قَوْمًا لُدًّا﴾ [Maryam 97].
So the Messenger ﷺ is a bringer of good news to the God-fearing who do righteous deeds, and a warner to the lud, the plural of alladd, meaning the obstinate adversary. He warns them of worldly punishment, or otherworldly punishment, or both?
* Students: Both.
* Shaykh: Both, yes, both or one of them. Punishment must come to them; and if we say that punishment includes depriving a person of obedience and faith, then he must be punished with both: worldly and religious punishment. ﴿بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَلَا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾. In His saying ﴿وَلَا تُسْأَلُ﴾ there are two readings. One: ﴿وَلَا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ with the negative particle "la" and the verb in the passive voice, meaning: you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire; that is, Allah will not ask you about them, because you have delivered the message, and the reckoning is upon whom? Upon Allah. The second reading: ﴿وَلَا تَسْأَلْ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾, where "la" is a prohibitive particle and "tas'al" is an imperfect verb in the active voice: do not you ask, or: do not ask, O addressee.
According to the first reading, ﴿وَلَا تُسْأَلُ﴾ means you will not be asked about them, and how they did not believe; your duty is only to deliver, and ours is the reckoning.
According to the second reading, ﴿وَلَا تَسْأَلْ﴾ ﴿وَلَا تَسْأَلْ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ is meant as warning and threat; that is, do not ask about their conditions, for they are in a state that needs no asking, may Allah protect us, because they are the companions of the Blazing Fire. The Blazing Fire is the Fire; we ask Allah for well-being. "Ashab" (companions): a companion is one who is constantly with something; that is, does anyone ask about the condition of the companions of the Fire, whether they are in bliss or in affliction?
* Student: From the context this is known.
* Shaykh: Do not ask about their condition, for they are, may Allah protect us, in a state that a person cannot imagine, and this is the utmost of warning to these deniers, opponents, who are the companions of the Blazing Fire.
* Student: Bashir, from where is it derived?

Sheikh: Bashir (بشير) comes from al-bushra (البشرى, "good news"), a verbal noun of bashsha (بَشَّر, "to give good news"). The tabshir, as we said, I think has passed us before, but I can remind you of it again: al-bushra and al-bashara are the giving of news that gladdens, and it is not used for anything other than what gladdens, except occasionally. The reason it is called "bushra" is the visible effect it has on the skin (al-bashara), for when a person is pleased, the lines of his face brighten. "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was pleased, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon" (ﷺ). [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3556) and Muslim (2769/53), from the hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik, with the wording: "When he was pleased, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon."] This is something evident: you can tell that a person is sad by his face, and you can tell that he is happy when his face shines. The term al-bushara may also be used in mockery, or to emphasise how severely the news will strike them with something painful: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. As for al-indhar (الإنذار), it is informing of what is feared, i.e., of that which one fears. The Messenger (ﷺ) is undoubtedly a bringer of good news of what gladdens, which is Paradise, and a warner of what is feared, which is the Fire.

Student: That which harms the ill-omened person is that his facial features change, so its linguistic derivation is confirmed. What is this?

Sheikh: Yes, but by custom and usage, these two terms are only used for what gladdens, because a person's face changing due to what pleases him is something desirable, in which a person finds rest. For him to be given good news of something that affects him adversely, even though his face changes, the matter is disliked. Custom has established that bushra is only used for loved things. It may be used either as mockery, as some scholars said regarding His words: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾, or literally, on the basis that the body or the skin is affected by that.

Student: So each is according to what it is attached to and according to the meaning?

Sheikh: But the origin of bushra is only in what gladdens.

Student: The evidence?

Sheikh: Because a change in the skin due to this is something desirable that a person loves, so it is said only of what gladdens. Even if a person is affected by what pains him or what he fears, one does not say "bashsharahu" (he gave him good news) except as mockery or rarely. It does not follow that because the derivation has this meaning, it must extend to other meanings, as we said, for example, in the case of "jam'" (جمع): Muzdalifah is called Jam' because people gather in it, but 'Arafah is not called Jam' even though people gather in it. This is not a necessary implication.

He said: ﴿And you will not be questioned about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. ﴿Al-Jahim﴾ is the great Fire. It has many names, among them: al-Nar (the Fire), al-Jahim, al-Sa'ir, and Jahannam. All of these are for the differences in its attributes, though it is one.

Student: Is al-Hawiyah among its names?

Sheikh: No, it is not one of its names. But in reality it has a bottom, into which a thing plunges, yet it is not called al-Hawiyah.

Then he said: ﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion﴾. It seems the Prophet (ﷺ) loved to win over the Jews and Christians, and whoever loves to win them over loves that they be pleased with him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that these Jews and Christians are a people of obstinacy; they will never be pleased with you, however much you win them over, and however much you incline towards them through conciliation rather than affection, for they will never be pleased. For this reason, when the Messenger (ﷺ) first arrived in Madinah, he loved to agree with the People of the Book in matters that were not forbidden, but later he abandoned them and opposed them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion﴾, i.e., their religion. (...) That is, even though they do not believe until he speaks to them.

His words: ﴿Or a sign comes to us﴾. What is meant by it?

Student: ﴿Or a sign comes to us﴾, i.e., a miracle.

Sheikh: A sign of what?

Student: A sign of the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Sheikh: Yes.

His words: ﴿Those before them said the same as what they say﴾. Who is meant by "those before them"?

Student: The Jews and the Christians.

Sheikh: Yes. Do you remember anything of what they said?

Student: Their saying, the saying of the Jews: ﴿Show us Allah plainly﴾.

Sheikh: To Musa: ﴿We will not believe you until we see Allah plainly﴾ [al-Baqarah 55]. Yes. His words: ﴿Their hearts are alike﴾. What is the meaning of similarity?

Student: Similarity is close to (...).

Sheikh: The closeness of one thing to another.

His words: ﴿We have made the signs clear for a people who are certain﴾. What is its place in relation to what precedes it? Its position in meaning relative to what precedes it?

Student: Causal explanation (ta'lil).

Sheikh: Causal explanation of what?

Student: A causal explanation of the refutation of their claim, and that it is of no benefit, and that the Qur'an is complete, and that their saying is merely obstinacy, since the signs have been made clear to them.

Sheikh: That is, a refutation of their saying: ﴿Or a sign comes to us﴾. Allah then said: ﴿We have made the signs clear﴾, meaning the signs have come clear too, there is no ambiguity.

Student: Is it a circumstantial clause (hali), Sheikh?

Sheikh: No, it is an independent resumptive clause (isti'nafiyyah) to refute them, an independent clause to refute their saying: ﴿Or a sign comes to us﴾. It is not a circumstantial clause, because it is not a restriction on what precedes it; the circumstantial clause is a restriction on what precedes it. This clause is an independent one refuting their saying: ﴿Or a sign comes to us﴾, meaning that the signs have already come clear.

His exalted words: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾. What is the ba' (ب) here?

Student: Accompaniment (mulabasah).

Sheikh: Yes, and companionship (musahabah). What is the meaning of ﴿We sent you with the truth﴾?

Student: We sent you with the true word.

Sheikh: And what does "with the true word" mean?

Student: We sent you; i.e., affirming with the truth.

Sheikh: And what else?

Another student: It means that the truth accompanies you, and likewise you act upon the truth, meaning it is constant with you.

Sheikh: Accompaniment and companionship. The meaning of accompaniment is that your message is true; the message is true. The meaning of companionship is that what you brought is true, so the message is true, and what was brought with it, which was sent with it, is also true. What is the truth in terms of rulings?

Student: That which is established and firm.

Sheikh: That which is established and firm, well done. And when it is attributed to rulings, what is meant by it?

Student: Justice.

Sheikh: And when it is attributed to reports?

Student: Truthfulness.

Sheikh: What is meant by it is truthfulness.

His words: ﴿And you will not be questioned about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. There are two readings. What are they?

Student: The reading ﴿And you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ (with the jussive, tasal), and the reading ﴿And you will not be questioned﴾ (tus'alu, passive).

Sheikh: And what is the difference between them?

Student: "You will not be asked (tus'alu)": we will not be asked about their condition.

Sheikh: And their reckoning is with Allah, and "you will not ask"?

Student: That is: you will not ask about their conditions.

Sheikh: They are in a state to be pitied. We said previously that the two readings give two meanings, so it is as if He says: do not ask about them and do not be charged with them, and also they are in a state that does not require asking about them, because they are, may Allah protect us, in a punishment with no equal. We ask Allah for well-being.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west; so wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 115].

* Benefits drawn from this noble verse: the generality of Allah's dominion, because the east and the west encompass everything, so there is in it the generality of Allah's dominion.

Also: the all-encompassing nature of Allah the Exalted over everything, by His words: ﴿wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾.

Another benefit of the verse: because Allah's dominion over the east and the west is general, both in creation and in determination, He possesses the east and the west in terms of direction. We have told you that His words: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾ [al-Baqarah 106], all of it up to the abrogation of the qibla, is a preparation for changing the qibla. It is as if Allah says: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾ [al-Baqarah 142]; so if He wills, He makes the direction to the right, and if He wills, He makes it to the left, ﴿so wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾.

Another benefit of the verse: the permissibility of praying facing whichever direction you are in, in case of excuse, as many scholars have explained it that way: the permissibility of praying in case of excuse facing wherever your face is.

* Among its benefits: the permissibility of praying facing the direction of one's travel during a journey when the prayer is voluntary. The verse has been interpreted this way too, but the verse is broader than this.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Face for Allah, Glorified and Exalted, by His words: ﴿the Face of Allah﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Allah the Exalted has a place, by His words: ﴿there﴾ (fathamma), because thamma indicates a place. But where is He?

Student: Above the heavens.

Sheikh: Yes, in the height. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the slave girl: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the sky." [Narrated by Muslim (537/33) from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami.] In it is a refutation of two misguided innovations. The first: the innovation of the Hululiyyah, who claim that Allah is in every place in His essence; their saying is false, refuted by revelation, reason, and innate nature as well. The second: the saying of the negators (nufat) and the mu'attilah, who say that Allah is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither above the world nor below it, neither to the right of the world nor to its left, neither connected to the world nor separated from it. Some scholars said about this saying: if we were asked to describe non-existence, we would find no description more comprehensive for non-existence than this statement, because that is what is non-existent in reality.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: the affirmation of two of Allah's names: Wasi' (All-Encompassing) and 'Alim (All-Knowing). ﴿Wasi' 'Alim﴾: Wasi', in what respect? All His attributes are vast without limit; His knowledge has no end, His power has no end, His hearing has no end; everything of His attributes is at the highest degree of vastness and encompassing. Knowledge too encompasses everything: ﴿so that you may know that Allah is over all things competent, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [al-Talaq 12].

* Also from it we derive the affirmation of hearing and knowledge; we derive a second attribute from combining hearing and knowledge, to indicate that Allah's knowledge is vast, vast in the sense that nothing of every knowable thing escapes it, neither on earth nor in heaven.

* Among its benefits: the exclusivity of Allah's dominion. From where is this taken?

Student: From the fronting of the predicate (taqdim al-khabar).

Sheikh: The fronting of the predicate in His words: ﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west﴾.

﴿And they say: Allah has taken a son. Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah 116].

* Benefits drawn from this verse: the demonstration of human arrogance and transgression, in that they insulted Allah, Glorified and Exalted, with this great insult, saying that Allah has taken a son. In the authentic hadith: "The son of Adam insults Me, and he has no right to do so; and the son of Adam denies Me, and he has no right to do so. As for his insulting Me, it is his saying: Allah has taken a son. As for his denying Me, it is his saying: He will not restore me as He originated me." [Narrated by al-Bukhari (4974) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]

This is among the greatest transgressions, may Allah protect us. In it is evidence of the transgression of the human being as such and his arrogance, by His words: ﴿Allah has taken a son﴾. As mentioned in the tafsir, it refers to three groups: who are they?

* Students: The Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists.

Sheikh: The Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists.

Among the benefits of the verse: that Allah refuted this false claim in several ways:

First: in His words, Glorified be He, for His exaltation above deficiency requires that He be exalted above taking a son, because taking a son is intended for: 

* Student: Assistance.

Sheikh: Yes, assistance, and meeting a need, or preserving the lineage. Allah the Exalted is exempt from all that. He is also exempt from resemblance; if He had a son, he would be a likeness of Allah.

Second: Allah refuted this claim by His words: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾. A possession cannot be a son of its owner; indeed, if a person owns his son, what happens according to the Sharia? He is freed upon him. So the owned cannot be a son of the owner. Allah is the Creator, and all else is created. How can the created be a son of the Creator?

The third refutation of this claim: all the servants, every servant in the heavens and the earth, are humbly submissive to Him, and a son does not have the humility of a slave. If all are slaves to Him, how can any of them be a son to Him? Does a slave humble himself before his father as he humbles himself before his master? No.

The fourth: He, Glorified and Exalted, is the Originator of the heavens and the earth, i.e., their Creator. The One who is able to create the heavens and the earth is able to create a human without a father. They claim that He has no father, but His father is Allah, so He says: ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾. The One capable of originating them is capable of having a son, capable of creating a human without a father, as He said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir 57].

The fifth: ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. Whoever has this power, is it impossible for Him to produce a son without a father?

* Students: It is not impossible.

Sheikh: It is not impossible. Thus their doubt by which they argued that Jesus is the son of Allah is refuted.

* Student: Sheikh, "all are devoutly obedient to Him" includes rational and non-rational beings; and "devoutly obedient" (qanitun) applies to rational beings?

Sheikh: By way of predominance (taghlib). Now we have finished the evidences by which Allah refuted this false claim, and we return to the benefits of this verse. First: the impossibility of Allah having a son. What is the evidence?

Student: The five aspects.

Sheikh: The five aspects, these five aspects.

Second: the generality of Allah's dominion, Glorified and Exalted, by His words: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾.

* Among the benefits: that Allah has no partner in His dominion. From where is this taken?

Student: From the fronting of the predicate.

Sheikh: From the fronting of the predicate: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾.

* Also: qunut (devout obedience) is used with two meanings: a general meaning and a specific meaning. The specific meaning is the qunut of worship and obedience, as in His words: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing﴾ [al-Zumar 9]. This is the qunut of what?

* Students: Worship.

Sheikh: Obedience and lawful worship. And as in His words: ﴿She believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was among the devoutly obedient﴾ [al-Tahrim 12], and as in His words: ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate, and bow with those who bow﴾ [Al 'Imran 43].

The second meaning is the general qunut of humble submission, which includes everyone in the heavens and the earth, as in this verse: ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾. Even the disbelievers are devoutly obedient to Allah?

* Students: Yes.

Sheikh: Even the disbelievers, in this sense, are devoutly obedient to Allah, Glorified and Exalted.

* Also: the greatness of Allah's power, Glorified and Exalted, and what is it? In His originating the heavens and the earth, for they are great creations.

* Also: the wisdom of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, because these heavens and earth are in a marvelous, wondrous order. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You see in the creation of the Most Merciful no imbalance﴾ [al-Mulk 3].

This vast, great, magnificent system does not fail or change over the passing of years and ages, and what indicates this?

* Students: The power of Allah.

Sheikh: A power that is supreme and dazzling, and a great, supreme wisdom as well. Everything is arranged in a wondrous, harmonious way; nothing collides with another to corrupt it, and nothing changes another, but each proceeds according to what it was commanded. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾ [Fussilat 12].

So, ﴿the Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: benefits drawn from it: power, might, and wisdom.

* Student: (...) the heaven (...).

Sheikh: Yes.

* Also: the heavens are plural in number, for the plural indicates number. How many are they?

* Students: Seven.

The Shaykh: Seven, and they are, as Allah the Exalted says: stacked (*tibaq*), ﴿Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers?﴾ [Nuh 15]. One above another. The Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus of the Muslims all establish that the heaven is a perceptible body. It is not as the people of atheism say, that what is above us is a height with no end. This is disbelief: whoever believes it becomes a disbeliever, because he rejects the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus of the Muslims.

* Another benefit: Allah, glory be to Him, is not incapable of anything, and nothing can resist His command, because He says: ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [Ali 'Imran 47].

* Another: the establishment that *al-qada'* (divine decree/judgment) is of two kinds: *qada' qadari* (decree of divine predestination) and *qada' shar'i* (legislative decree). The *qadari* decree is like this verse: ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾, meaning: He determines it as a cosmic, created reality, ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ The *shar'i* decree is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him﴾ [al-Isra' 23]. Did He decree this as a *shar'i* or a *qadari* decree?

* The students: *Shar'i*.

* The Shaykh: *Shar'i*. For if He had decreed it as a *qadari* decree, no one would have associated partners with Allah, and all of mankind would have been worshippers of Allah. So it is a *shar'i* decree. The difference between them is that the *shar'i* decree may or may not take effect; that is, the one subject to it may or may not do it. The cosmic decree must take effect, and must occur in the one decreed upon. Just as I have now mentioned the difference between general *qunut* and specific *qunut*: specific *qunut* is praiseworthy for the one who is obedient, while general *qunut* is not praiseworthy, because it is submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in a cosmic and predestined sense.

* One of the benefits of the verse: the affirmation that Allah speaks, as in His saying: ﴿then He only says to it﴾.

* Another: that His speech is by letters.

* A student: ﴿Qul﴾ ("Say").

* The Shaykh: No, *qul* is not there; it is *kun* ("Be").

* The student: No, *kun*.

* The Shaykh: *Kun*. *Kun* consists of letters.

* Another: that the speech of Allah is heard. In ﴿then He only says to it, "Be"﴾, the particle *lahu* ("to it") explicitly directs the speech to the one addressed. Had He not been speaking so that it hears, there would be no point in directing it. For this reason, the one to whom the command is directed hears it and complies.

* Another: that inanimate matter is subject to Allah, glory be to Him, even inanimate matter. What is the basis for this? Because His saying ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ includes matters relating to living beings and matters relating to inanimate things. So when Allah says to inanimate matter, "Be," it is.

Another benefit of the verse, [the Shaykh continues]: that between Allah's command to bring something into being and its coming into being there is no delay. There is no delay at all; it occurs immediately. From where is this derived?

* A student: From the use of the particle *fa-* ("then").

* The Shaykh: Yes. From His saying ﴿fa-yakūnu﴾ ("and it is") with *fa-*, and *fa-* indicates immediate sequence, order and succession.

* A student: Does inanimate matter perceive?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it perceives.

* The student: Does this indicate, [from] ﴿They said, "We have come obedient"﴾ [Fussilat 11], that it is a real, actual speech?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is real.

* The student: Is the offering of the trust to the heavens real?

* The Shaykh: Yes, yes, it is real. There is no difficulty with that.

﴿then He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. Who disagreed that the speech of Allah, glory be to Him, is by letters and sound?

* A student: The Ash'aris.

* The Shaykh: The Ash'aris.

* The students: The Jahmiyya.

* The Shaykh: No, the Jahmiyya did not disagree. They said that Allah's speech is by letters and sound, but that Allah's speech is created and is not one of His attributes. The Mu'tazila are likewise. But the Ash'aris, the Kullabiyya and the Maturidiyya all say that speech is the meaning subsisting in the self, and that the letters and sounds are an expression of it or a narration of it. For this reason one of their verifiers said: "There is no difference between us and the Mu'tazila regarding speech. There is no difference between us and them, because we agree that what is between the two covers of the Mushaf is created."

But these [Ash'aris] say: the Mu'tazila say, "What is between the two covers of the Mushaf is the speech of Allah," whereas those [Ash'aris] say, "It is an expression." So in this respect the Mu'tazila were better than them. They were better than them in this regard, because they say, "This is the speech of Allah," whereas these say, "It is not the speech of Allah; it is an expression of it." Yet all agree that what is between the two covers of the Mushaf is created. The main point is that the people of the Sunnah and the community believe that Allah, glory be to Him, speaks with a speech that is by sound and letters, and that it is heard. But if someone says: how can we conceive of this, when we say that "There is nothing like unto Him" [al-Shura 11], and you say that He speaks by letters?

We say: Yes, the letters are letters. But is the manner of articulating them, and the reality of uttering them or of speaking, similar to the articulation and speech of creatures?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, it is not similar. From this we know that we are not *mushabbiha* (anthropomorphists) when we say He speaks by letters and sound, because we say: a sound not like the sounds of creatures, but as befits His greatness and majesty.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And those who have no knowledge say, "Why does Allah not speak to us, or a sign come to us?" Likewise said those before them, similar to their words. Their hearts are alike.﴾ [al-Baqara 118].

From this verse is derived: the people of falsehood only oppose the truth with falsehood. For their demanding that signs come according to their proposal is obstinacy and arrogance. Otherwise, what is the purpose? What is the purpose?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The purpose is the establishment of the message through signs, whether or not they propose them. Moreover, even if the signs came as they proposed, they would not believe: ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "Continuous magic."﴾ [al-Qamar 2]. "Our magic earlier, and our magic later."

So the people of falsehood can only oppose the truth with falsehood. This strengthens the holder of the truth in his firmness upon what he has, and in his rejection of falsehood. Do not be shaken so long as you are upon the truth, for the people of falsehood, all that they have is dust.

Another: describing those who do not submit to the truth as ignorant: ﴿And those who have no knowledge say﴾. Every person who stubbornly opposes the truth and rejects it is the most ignorant of people. From this we know that whoever named this age "the age of light," as if this statement implies restriction, is he mistaken or correct?

* The students: No, he is mistaken.

* The Shaykh: He is mistaken. For this age is in reality an age of darkness, except for those whose hearts Allah has illuminated. The age of light in reality is the age of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. That is the age of light. As for our age now, it is all ignorance, all obstinacy, all arrogance, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Another: that the polytheists acknowledge that Allah speaks by letters and sound. From where?

* The students: ﴿Why does Allah not speak to us?﴾

* The Shaykh: ﴿Why does Allah not speak to us?﴾ If speech were as the Ash'aris say, by the self alone, then Allah's speech would have no benefit for them, since they would not hear it in itself. So the polytheists acknowledge that Allah speaks, for in reality the legislation cannot be established without establishing the speech of Allah, since revelation is the speech of Allah. If we deny the speech of Allah...?

* A student: We deny His legislation.

* The Shaykh: How would revelation be established?

Another: that there is no messenger without a sign. For their saying ﴿or a sign come to us﴾ is a claim to what others have. Whoever has not brought a sign is not blamed for failing to believe him, is that not so?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: A man, for example, comes, whom we do not know, of our own kind, and says: "I am a messenger of Allah. Believe in me, or I will fight you and make your women and wealth lawful." Would we obey him?

* The students: No, that is not right.

* The Shaykh: No, we would not obey him. Even if we rejected him, we would not be blameworthy. But the messengers come with signs. The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no messenger except that Allah the Exalted has given him signs such that people believe on the basis of their like," [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7274) and Muslim (152/239), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra]. Allah the Exalted does not send messengers and leave them without support, ever.

* A student: The apparent meaning of the verses is the statement of the Jews: "You did not bring us a clear proof." How is that?

* The Shaykh: Arrogance. Even "or a sign come to us": we say, signs came to you, not just one sign.

* The student: But did He not answer this request?

* The Shaykh: How?

* The student: ﴿They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us a clear proof, and we will not abandon our gods for your saying, nor are we believers in you. We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil." He said, "I call Allah to witness, and bear witness, that I am free of what you associate, besides Him. So scheme against me all together, then do not give me respite."﴾ [Hud 53–55].

* The Shaykh: The greatest sign in this challenge to them is that he said: ﴿Scheme against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾ [Hud 55–56]. This means (...).

Likewise, * one of the benefits of this noble verse: that the statements of the people of falsehood resemble one another. ﴿Likewise said those before them, similar to their words.﴾ For if you reflect upon the false claims with which the polytheists rejected the message of the Messenger ﷺ from his time until today, you will find that they are similar. ﴿And when they see them, they say, "Indeed, these are misguided."﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 32]. And today they say of those who hold fast to the Qur'an and the Sunnah: "These are backward; these are dervishes who know nothing."

* Another: the similarity of the hearts of the disbelievers, from His saying: ﴿Their hearts are alike﴾.

* Another: the refutation of their claim ﴿or a sign come to us﴾, in His saying: ﴿We have certainly made the signs clear﴾.

* Another: that only those whom Allah has granted knowledge benefit from the signs, beneficial knowledge; for they benefit.

* Another: that the more a person's knowledge increases, the more his faith increases. For when his knowledge increases, there appears to him of Allah's signs what does not appear to others. For this reason, ﴿We have made the signs clear for a people who are certain﴾. So let us return to the first explanation. I said: ﴿We have made the signs clear for a people who are certain.﴾ *Al-iqan* (certainty) is affirmation without doubt, and affirmation without doubt is affirmation with no doubt in it. So every believing person has the signs of Allah made clear to him, which are not made clear to others, and whenever a person's faith increases, there become clear to him of Allah's signs what has not become clear to others.

* From the noble verse is derived: that for every believer the signs have become clear.

* And from it is also derived: that knowledge increases with faith, because among the signs of Allah is this revelation which the Messenger ﷺ brought, for revelation is one of the signs of Allah. So whenever you are a believer, there becomes clear to you from these signs what has not become clear to others. Thus, through faith, knowledge increases. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And We made none the keepers of the Fire except angels, and We made their number only a trial for those who disbelieve, so that those who were given the Scripture would be certain, and those who believe would increase in faith﴾ [al-Muddaththir 31].

Whenever a person is more believing, he is more knowledgeable, and whenever his knowledge increases, his faith increases. The two are mutually bound.

* A student: Like the Jews, who have knowledge but did not act upon it?

* The Shaykh: Yes, but when knowledge increases from faith, it increases the faith.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good news and a warner, and you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Baqara 119]. From this noble verse is derived: the establishment of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, from His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you﴾.

* And from its benefits: that the Prophet ﷺ is a messenger, not a liar, and not a lord. For the messenger cannot have the station of the one who sends him. Also he is not a liar, because Allah said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you﴾, emphasizing it with *inna* ("indeed").

* Another: that the message of the Prophet ﷺ is true and comprises truth, from His saying: ﴿with the truth﴾, which means justice in rulings, truthfulness in reports, and goodness in narratives: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Yusuf 3].

* Another: that the message of the Prophet ﷺ includes command and prohibition, and good news and warning, from His saying: ﴿a bringer of good news and a warner﴾. We have said that good news corresponds to those who perform the commanded acts, so it includes a command whose doer is given the good news of its reward; and warning is for those who commit the forbidden acts, so it includes a prohibition and a warning to its doer. Likewise, the Sharia of the Messenger ﷺ includes both: command and prohibition, i.e., positive and negative. The wisdom in this is clear: for a person may find it easy to perform the commands, yet find it difficult to abstain from the prohibitions. So if the Sharia were all commands, the trial, or the test of a person's ability to restrain himself, would not be made clear to us, would it?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: That is, some people find it easy to do, but not easy to refrain from. Others find it easy to refrain, but not easy to do. So the trial was through both the command and the prohibition. The great Shaykh finds it easy to abstain from fornication, does he not?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: He finds it easy to abstain from fornication, but he is not like the young man for whom abstaining from fornication is not easy. For the young man, abstaining from fornication may be difficult and arduous. Therefore people are tested with this and with that. The point, then, is that the trial is only complete through varying the obligations, is it not? This has come up with us often, and we said, for example: prayer is a bodily obligation, zakat is a financial obligation, and hajj is a bodily obligation.

* The students: And a financial one.

* The Shaykh: No, financial is not necessarily so, but it usually involves money, since a person cannot reach it except with money. And fasting? It is restraint. Fasting is restraint.

* A student: It is an act.

* The Shaykh: No, it is not an act. The person does not do anything; he only refrains from something.

* A student: He refrains from it.

* The Shaykh: So it is restraint, restraint from something loved. But prayer and zakat are performance. Therefore, all five pillars involve trial through both action and restraint, because submission is not complete except through these two things: performing what is commanded and abstaining from what is forbidden.

* Another: that the duty of the messengers is conveyance, and they are not responsible for people's deeds, for His saying: ﴿and you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. And according to the second reading we derive a second benefit: the severity of the punishment of the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us, from His saying: ﴿the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾, [read as] ﴿and you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 2, verses 120–123 (part 1 of 4)**

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Neither the Jews nor the Christians will ever be pleased with you until you follow their religion.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:120]

* Student: The imperative style in ﴿Indeed, We have sent you﴾, and the Messenger (...)?
* Shaykh: Imperative style?
* Student: A declarative statement, if the Messenger (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. But there are people in front of him who deny it, so He affirms before these deniers that He sent him. We mentioned earlier that something may be emphasized not in consideration of the addressee, but in consideration of its importance. Something may be emphasized because of its importance: the statement is made in an initial form and then emphasized, but this is because of its importance.
* Student: What is the ruling on the person who stops short (al-waqifi) and says: the Quran is the speech of Allah, but does not say "created" or "uncreated"?
* Shaykh: These are innovators (mubtadi'ah), because the early generations (salaf) said: uncreated, sent down uncreated. So these people oppose the salaf.
* Student: Should we not make them like the Jahmiyyah (Jahmites)?
* Shaykh: No, because the Jahmiyyah openly declare that it is created.
* Student: Did Imam Ahmad say: "These are Jahmiyyah"?
* Shaykh: That does not mean they are Jahmiyyah. It may be that Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, was referring to specific people. That is, there were particular people who concealed their views: when asked, they say, "We do not say this or that." Imam Ahmad understood from these people that they were saying it is created, but they concealed this by displaying suspension of judgment. So the waqifah (those who suspend judgment) may at times be like the hypocrites, concealing their true view. But considering the statement itself, regardless of who says it, there is no doubt that the one who suspends judgment is not like the one who says it is created. This is because there are three levels: one who says it is created, one who says it is uncreated, and one who suspends judgment. His suspension may be due, for example, to the evidence not being clear to him. So we cannot treat the one who says it is created the same as the one who keeps silent.
* Student: But Ibn al-Qayyim, in his Nuniyyah, mentioned that the waqifah are worse than (...)?
* Another student: You mean the Mufawwidah (...).
* Shaykh: No, no. The Mufawwidah (those who delegate the meaning) are in regard to all the attributes. Shaykh al-Islam mentioned that their view is among the worst statements of the people of innovation and heresy, those who say: "We delegate the meaning in all of Allah's attributes." There is no doubt that their view is among the worst views of the people of innovation.
* Student: Shaykh, His saying ﴿And you will not be questioned about the companions of the Hellfire﴾ passes judgment on those who say these things, that they are companions of the Hellfire. So in the verse, it is as if He is indicating to the Prophet ﷺ that there is no good in them, and so there is no need to call them. Because He judged that whoever says this is (...) among the companions of the Hellfire, this was the judgment of (...)?
* Shaykh: What you said is possible, and that when he despaired of them, he was commanded to leave them. Or it may be like His saying: ﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be distressed by what they plot﴾ [al-Nahl 16:127], meaning: do not grieve over this, and do not let yourself follow them, for you are not responsible for them. Or He consoles him with His saying: ﴿And you will not be questioned about the companions of the Hellfire﴾, meaning: even though they deny you, constrict your chest and sadden you, do not ask about them; We will punish them. What is in the verse is, in its meaning, a clear indication that does not allow for anything else, that what is intended is: turn away from them. It is true that it allows the meaning you mentioned about the Messenger, that Allah says: leave them and do not ask about them. But it also allows another meaning, that this contains consolation for the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, so that he would not grieve or be distressed by them.
* Student: So, Shaykh, He arranged these things and then said that they are companions of the Hellfire?
* Shaykh: Yes. He said: ﴿that they are companions of the Hellfire﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:113]. Its meaning is a consolation to him, the meaning is not...
Peace and blessings be upon him.

It is permissible that this address applies to everyone who is able to be addressed. That is: "Never will you be pleased with you, O believer."

As for His saying: ﴿the Jews﴾: they are the followers of Musa (Moses) who ascribe themselves to him. The name is derived either from Yahudha (Judah), their ancestor, to whom they were attributed, or from al-Hawd, meaning return, due to their saying: ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾ [al-A'raf 7:156].

As for the Christians (al-Nasara), the name is derived from a town called Nasran, well known in Palestine, to which they ascribe themselves. It was also said that it derives from al-Nusrah (support), because they supported ʿIsa (Jesus), peace be upon him, and so they were named by this name. They are those who ascribe themselves to ʿIsa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary).

* Student: Nasran or Nasira, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: Nasran. There is a town called Nasira, and I do not know whether they are ascribed to it or to the second one. But what I know is that it is Nasran. They ascribe themselves to ʿIsa, peace be upon him, and they finally called themselves al-Masihiyyin (Messianists) so that they might give themselves the appearance of legitimacy. But the Messiah ʿIsa ibn Maryam is innocent of them; if he came out, he would fight them, because they disbelieve in him just as they disbelieve in Muhammad ﷺ.

He says: ﴿Neither the Jews nor the Christians will ever be pleased with you﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:120].

His saying: ﴿nor the Christians﴾: the (lā) here is for emphasis (tawkid) and is not independent. If it were removed and it said: "the Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you," the sentence would be sound. But it was added for emphasis, so that no one would think that the meaning is that they would not be pleased when gathered together. Because if it said: "the Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you," the listener might think they would not be pleased when united, whereas the reality is that each group will not be pleased.

﴿until you follow their religion﴾: (ḥattā) is a particle of limit (ḥarf ghāyah). It puts the present tense verb in the subjunctive by itself according to the Kufans, and by the implied (an) according to the Basrans.

﴿their religion﴾: al-millah means religion, i.e., their religion which they followed. So the Jews will not be pleased with you until you become a Jew, and the Christians will not be pleased with you until you become a Christian.

But what is the sole answer to those who say: "O Muhammad, we will not be pleased with you until you follow our religion"?

The answer is His saying, ﴿Say﴾, responding to them regarding their lack of pleasure: ﴿Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (true) guidance﴾. And the guidance is not what you are upon; rather, the guidance of Allah alone, not the guidance you claim to be upon.

﴿it is the guidance﴾: ﴿it is﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl). It has been mentioned to us repeatedly that the pronoun of separation has three benefits:

The first benefit? 
* Student: Emphasis.
* Shaykh: Emphasis. The second is restriction (ḥaṣr), and the third is showing that what follows it is a predicate and not an adjective. Accordingly, this pronoun has no place in i'rab (grammatical analysis), and His saying ﴿the guidance﴾ is the predicate of (inna), while its subject is His saying ﴿the guidance of Allah﴾.

﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (true) guidance﴾. Whatever is other than it is misguidance. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿So what is there after the truth but error? Then how are you averted?﴾ [Yunus 10:32]. So everything that does not agree with the guidance of Allah is misguidance, and there is no intermediate between the guidance of Allah and misguidance.

Then He says: ﴿And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:120]. ﴿And if you follow﴾: to whom is the address? To the Messenger ﷺ, or to everyone who can be addressed? The closer view is that it returns to the Messenger ﷺ.

His saying ﴿if you follow﴾: this sentence contains a condition and an oath. When the condition and the oath come together, the answer of whichever comes later is omitted. Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyyah:

"Omit, when a condition and an oath come together, the answer of whichever comes last; it is then obligatory."

Where is the oath? The oath is what the lām indicates in His saying ﴿And if you follow﴾, since the implied meaning is: "By Allah, if you follow..." And where is the condition?
* Student: (in).
* Shaykh: (in). The answer: ﴿you would have from Allah no ally or helper﴾. ﴿You would have﴾ (mā laka) is the answer to the oath. If it were the answer to the condition, the (fa') would have to accompany it, since it is a negation. But it is the answer to the oath, so the (fa') does not accompany it. Where is the answer to the condition? It was said that it is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath. It was also said that it is not needed, since the sentence is complete without it. This second view is the preferred one: it is not needed for the sentence to be complete without it. The evidence for this is that it has not come in any style of the Arabic language. If it has not come in any style of the Arabic language, this shows that the sentence is independent of it and that there is no need for it.

He says: ﴿And if you follow their desires﴾. Notice: He said ﴿their religion﴾, then He said ﴿their desires﴾, because this religion they are upon is not a religion of guidance, but a religion of desire. Therefore He said: ﴿And if you follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge﴾, because they are upon desire and not upon guidance. For if they were upon guidance, the Jews would have been obligated to believe in the Messiah ʿIsa ibn Maryam, and all of them would have been obligated to believe in Muhammad ﷺ. But their religion is desire, not guidance. Likewise, every person who follows other than what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, brought, and is fanatical about it, we say: your religion is desire, not guidance.

His saying ﴿after what has come to you of knowledge﴾ refers to the revelation that came to the Prophet ﷺ, whether it was the Quran or the Sunnah.

His saying ﴿what has come to you of knowledge﴾: is it the knowledge that came to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him? Yes, knowledge. Allah says to him: ﴿And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you write one with your right hand﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut 29:48]. The Messenger was not a scholar; he was an unlettered prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who did not know, did not read, and did not write. But Allah sent down to him this knowledge, so that by it he became a prophet who brought beneficial knowledge and righteous action.

﴿you would have from Allah no ally or helper﴾. What is the i'rab of (mā laka)? What is the i'rab of (mā)?
* Student: Negation.
* Shaykh: Negation, yes, ﴿mā laka﴾.

His saying ﴿from an ally﴾: what is its i'rab?
* Student: A preposition.
* Shaykh: A preposition. And ﴿waliyy﴾?
* Student: Genitive.
* Shaykh: Genitive?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What is its position in i'rab, ﴿waliyy﴾? 
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It has no position in i'rab? That is, is it a direct object, for example, governed by something? What is its position in i'rab?
* Student: Genitive in form, nominative in position.
* Shaykh: What does that mean in terms of i'rab?
* Student: That it is the subject (mubtada').
* Shaykh: That it is the subject, correct.

﴿waliyy﴾ is a subject, nominative, marked by a presumed ḍammah on its final letter, prevented from appearing by the occupation of the position by the vowel of the preposition. ﴿min waliyy﴾. Its original form: "you have from Allah an ally," and ﴿laka﴾ is a prepositional phrase functioning as the fronted predicate. The clause ﴿mā laka min Allāh﴾ has no position in i'rab, because it is...?
* The students: The answer to the oath.
* Shaykh: Because it is the answer to the oath.

﴿mā laka min Allāh min waliyy﴾. As for the name of Allah, exalted is He, its explanation, meaning and derivation has already been discussed.

His saying ﴿min waliyy﴾: the waliyy is the one who takes charge of another by protecting and safeguarding him. So the meaning is: no one takes charge of your protection except Allah, mighty and majestic. And no one takes charge of your support, and there is no helper who repels (harm) from you. Then the punishment of Allah would befall you, even if you had many soldiers, many police, or great power. If you follow other than the law of Allah, no one will protect you from Allah, and no one will support you apart from Him. For support and guardianship come through guidance, by following the guidance of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with injustice, for them is security﴾ [al-An'am 6:82]. Security is only through faith and the absence of injustice. ﴿You would have from Allah no ally or helper﴾.

* Student: Shaykh, is ﴿waliyy﴾ a verbal noun (maṣdar) (...)?
* Shaykh: No, it is not a verbal noun. (walī) here is on the pattern (faʿīl) from wilāyah.
* Student: Shaykh, the restriction here, ﴿after what has come to you of knowledge﴾, does it have an implied meaning (mafhūm)?
* Shaykh: Yes, it has an implied meaning, because before the Messenger ﷺ was forbidden from following them, he used to love agreeing with the People of the Book. When he was commanded to oppose them, he was no longer able to oppose them.
* Student: In terms of the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl), is the one who follows (...) excused?
* Shaykh: Yes, the one who follows other than Islam without knowledge is excused. But if he is negligent, this will come to us in the benefits (of the verse), in the benefits of the verse, God willing.

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recitation﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:121]. ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿they recite it with its true recitation﴾ is said to be the predicate of the subject. In that case the second clause, ﴿they believe in it﴾, is a resumptive (istiʾnāfiyyah) clause. 

It was also said that His saying ﴿they recite it with its true recitation﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyyah), and that ﴿they believe in it﴾ is the predicate of the subject. Let us see by meaning which of them is more preferable.

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾: We gave them the Book. Is the giving here legislative or cosmic?
* The students: Legislative.
* Shaykh: Or all of it? It is cosmic and legislative: cosmic, because Allah decreed that He would give them the Book, and He gave it to them; and it is also legislative, because it contains the laws and the explanation. Those to whom He gave the Book are either this nation alone or it and others. The more preferable view is that it includes everyone to whom Allah gave the Book. The word "Book" is generic, so it includes the Quran, the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and other books of Allah, mighty and majestic.

His saying ﴿they recite it with its true recitation﴾: ﴿they recite it﴾. Recitation (tilāwah) is applied to the recitation of the wording, which is reading; to the recitation of the meaning, which is interpretation (tafsīr); and to the recitation of the ruling, meaning following it, which is adherence. So recitation applies to the recitation of the wording; recitation of the meaning means that a person follows the meaning and does not distort it; and recitation of the ruling is following what the Quran rules. These three meanings of recitation are included in His saying ﴿they recite it with its true recitation﴾. Verbal recitation means reciting the Quran with the wording it must have, with its i'rab as it came, without changing it. So one does not say, for example, "al-ḥamda lillāhi rabba al-ʿālamīn" with changes. Rather, one says ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ without alteration, because it was revealed that way, so it must be recited that way. Recitation of the meaning means that one explains it according to what Allah and His Messenger intended. For example, one says: "The meaning of this verse is such-and-such, according to what Allah intended." And how do we know what Allah intends by it? Did Allah say: "I intended by My speech such-and-such"? The answer is no, He did not say that. But He said: ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Shuʿaraʾ 26:195].

So we know what Allah, exalted is He, intends by this Quran, because it came in the Arabic language. And this meaning in the Arabic language is what this wording or this context requires. So we will have known the meaning of the speech of Allah, mighty and majestic. This is the recitation of the meaning. 

Recitation of the ruling: carrying out the commands, avoiding the prohibitions, and affirming the reports. This is the recitation of the ruling: that you follow what this Quran has ruled, and acknowledge what it has reported. You act, act how? And you abandon the prohibitions and believe the reports. Then you are reciting it with its true recitation. But if you are arrogant or deny it, then you have not recited it with its true recitation.

In His saying ﴿with its true recitation﴾, this is from the construction of a quality attributed to its qualified noun: that is, "the true recitation," meaning the recitation of earnestness, steadfastness, and not deviating to the right or left. As for i'rab, it is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), because it is annexed to the verbal noun, like His saying in the Alfiyyah:

"...like 'jiddan kulla al-jidd' (in earnest, wholly in earnest)..." Here: "recite it with its true recitation."

﴿They recite it with its true recitation; those believe in it﴾. ﴿Those﴾ refers back to "those who were given the Book," who were given the Book and who recite it with its true recitation. That is: those who possess this attribute, who recite the Book with its true recitation, believe in it. As for those who do not recite it with its true recitation, they are not believers in it. Rather, they have a deficiency of faith in proportion to their opposition. Faith increases and decreases; therefore He said: ﴿those believe in it﴾. Referring to them with the far demonstrative is evidence of their elevated rank, like His saying at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:5]. This is evidence of their high station and rank.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 120–123 (part 2 of 4):

He said: ﴿They are the ones who believe in it﴾. Iman (faith) linguistically means affirmation (tasdiq), but in the Shari'ah (sacred law) it is affirmation qualified by acceptance (qabul) and submission (idhan). Affirmation alone is not sufficient; acceptance and submission are also required. The evidence for this is that Abu Talib is not called a believer, even though he affirmed and acknowledged (the Prophet's message), but he lacked acceptance and submission. So a person who affirms what is said is not thereby called a believer. Some people rejoiced at Gagarin, Gagarin, I think you remember him, the Russian man who was the first to go up to the moon, I think, and he said: "I now acknowledge that this creation has a Creator who governs it." People rejoiced greatly and said, "He has believed!" Has he believed? Not at all, he did not believe, because this is merely a rational deduction that every intelligent person knows. Every intelligent person knows that this vast, orderly, wondrous universe has a Creator who governs and arranges it, just as we know that this mosque has a builder, and that this light has a source that lit it, and so on. The upshot is that this is not faith. Merely acknowledging Allah, glorified and exalted be He, does not count as faith, nor does merely acknowledging the Messenger (ﷺ). The hypocrites say: ﴿We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Munafiqun 1]. But even so, if they were sincere in their testimony, Allah would not have called them liars. He said: "They say, 'We bear witness,' but they are liars," because they have no submission or acceptance. Rather, their hearts reject it, and we seek refuge in Allah. Therefore, ﴿They are the ones who believe in it﴾ because they ﴿recite it with its true recitation﴾. Whoever does not recite the Qur'an with its true recitation, in the three senses we mentioned, is deficient in faith, and may lose it entirely.

He said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers﴾.

* Student: So what is the predicate (khabar), O Shaykh?

* Shaykh: We mentioned that scholars have two opinions regarding the predicate. One opinion is ﴿they recite it with its true recitation﴾, and the other opinion is ﴿they are the ones who believe in it﴾. According to this latter opinion, ﴿they recite it with its true recitation﴾ is a circumstantial clause (jumla haliyya), meaning: those to whom We gave the Book, while they recite it with its true recitation, they are the ones who believe in it. The judgment that they believe in it is then conditional on their being described as reciting it with its true recitation. The sentence's grammatical analysis (i'rab) on this reading is a single sentence, but the subject is qualified. On the second opinion, the statement consists of two clauses: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recite it with its true recitation﴾ and ﴿They are the ones who believe in it﴾. However, the first grammatical analysis is closer to the correct reading, because the discussion here concerns belief in what the Messenger, peace be upon him, brought. Only one who recites the Book with its true recitation believes in it, whether it is the Torah, the Gospel, or the Qur'an. None believes in it with true belief except one who recites it with true recitation. Accordingly, the qualifier "those to whom We gave the Book" with "they recite it with its true recitation" is better, meaning: whoever is given the Book and, being described thus, recites it with its true recitation, is the one who believes in it.

* Student: Should the statement of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿they recite it with its true recitation﴾ be taken as a predicate? It creates a problem, because the one who does not recite it with its true recitation has been placed first (...)?

* Shaykh: No, no, it is not a predicate (...). It is a pure predicate. This also strengthens that the clause ﴿they recite it﴾ is a circumstantial clause.

And His statement: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers﴾.

* Student: O Shaykh, can ﴿those﴾ be a second predicate?

* Shaykh: No, no. Whether it is a second predicate or a resumptive new clause depends on what we said about ﴿they recite it with its true recitation﴾ being the predicate.

* Student: If it is the predicate?

* Shaykh: The stronger view is that it is a circumstantial clause.

* Student: It cannot be the predicate.

* Shaykh: I say: the stronger view is that it is a circumstantial clause, and that it being the predicate is the weaker view.

His statement: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers﴾. Is ﴿whoever﴾ here a conditional particle that jussifies the verb? ﴿disbelieves﴾ is jussive, ﴿in it﴾ means in the Book, ﴿those are the losers﴾. The clause ﴿those are the losers﴾ is the answer of the condition, and it is joined by the particle fa' (then), because it is a nominal sentence. A nominal sentence that is the answer of a condition must be joined by fa', like its counterparts mentioned in the verse:

A nominal sentence, an imperative, a verb of praise (jamid), and with ma, qad, la (in), and with the future particles (tanfis), these seven, when they come as the answer of a condition, are joined with fa'.

And His statement: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers﴾. He did not say, "whoever disbelieves in it has lost," but rather used a nominal sentence, which conveys what? Permanence and continuity. He used the separating pronoun (damir al-fasl) in ﴿they﴾ to convey restriction (hasr) and emphasis. The meaning is: those who disbelieved in it are the losers and no others. Accordingly, everyone who is not a believer is a loser. This man has millions of dirhams, cars, real estate, sons, wives, family, and a kingdom, but he is a disbeliever. What do we say? He is a loser. In reality, he has not profited from this wealth, nor from his children. ﴿Say: Indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Zumar 15]. This wealth does not benefit him; rather it will be a source of regret for him, because he will lose it. He will lose it, or it will be lost to him. Either he dies leaving it behind, or it escapes him.

And His statement: ﴿Those are the losers﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿the losers﴾? The root of khusran (loss) is deficiency. For this reason it is said "he profited" (rabih), and its opposite is "he lost" (khasir). These are the ones upon whom deficiency has befallen, and no others, because however much of this world they are given, it is transient and perishing, so it does not benefit them.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ [al-Baqarah 122].

﴿O Children of Israel﴾. Israel is Ya'qub (Jacob) the son of Ishaq (Isaac), the son of Ibrahim (Abraham). The intended meaning of "his descendants" here is anyone who is descended from him, male or female, because it has already passed in our lessons that the word "banu" (sons of) is specific to males unless it refers to a tribe, in which case it includes male and female.

And His statement: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour﴾. The reminder here of the favour is not merely so that a person recalls that Allah previously bestowed a favour upon him. Rather, the intent is that one should take this favour, or this remembrance of it, as a path to thanking Allah, by complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition. That is, do not forget what He bestowed upon you and thereby disbelieve in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but believe in him and follow him as a repayment for this favour.
