So do not be deceived by the orientation of others toward falsehood if you are upon the truth. "For each there is a direction toward which he turns." And it includes what I mentioned a little earlier: it includes the legal direction, which is the difference of the laws among them. So do not suppose that the difference of the Islamic law from others means it is not the truth; for it is truth from Allah.
* And from the benefits of the verse: the obligation of racing to good, because of His saying: "so race to good deeds."
* And from it: that the command implies immediacy, because racing to good can only occur by hastening to do it. So this verse is among those cited as evidence that a command implies immediacy.
* And from it: the complete eloquence in His saying "fastabiqu al-khayrat," rather than "istabiqu ila al-khayrat." Although some people say that the preposition was omitted, this is not correct; the verse contains no omission, because "istabiqu al-khayrat" includes racing toward them and racing within them. The meaning is not that when you reach good you stop; rather, do not stop even with the very act of your good deed; be competitive. This resembles His saying: "Guide us to the straight path" [al-Fatihah 6]. He did not say "guide us to the path," because what is required is that a person reach the path and remain upon it. For this reason He said "guide us to the straight path." This is similar to it. Although some exegetes have inclined to say that it is accusative by omission of the preposition, with the implied "race toward the good deeds," the correct view is that it is not so.
* From the benefits of the verse: Allah's encompassing of creation wherever they are, because of His saying: "Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together."
* And from it: an indication of the resurrection; for when does the bringing together occur?
* Students: On the Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: On the Day of Resurrection, because of the Exalted's saying: "That is a Day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed." [Hud 103]
* And from the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of the power of Allah, mighty and majestic, "indeed Allah is over all things competent," and that it encompasses everything. And Allah the Exalted said: "Nothing in the heavens or on earth can ever escape Him. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent." [Fatir 44]
* A student: Shaykh, is it not derived from the verse a refutation of the Jabriyyah (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. It may be derived according to the reading "muwalliha" or "muwallaha," for there is a reading "huwa mu'allaha," and they may argue with it, but there is no harm in examining this. According to the reading "huwa muwalliha," it is clear that the agent is the person who turns. And according to the reading "huwa muwallaha," it means that Allah is the One who has caused him to face it, and there is no evidence in it for the doctrine of the Jabriyyah; that is, there is no proof for them that it is true, because "muwallaha" refers to the legal direction. The meaning of "muwallaha" is the legal direction, that is, "one caused to face it, directed toward it." It may also be for the predestined direction, and there is no harm; so Allah, glorified and exalted, causes him to face it when he deviates. When they turn aside from the truth, Allah turns their hearts aside.
* A student: Shaykh, "fastabiqu al-khayrat" (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. There is not even any evidence in it at all. He said: "And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque."
* The benefits of this verse: the obligation of facing the Sacred Mosque wherever a person is, because of His saying: "And from wherever you set out."
* And among its benefits also: that an important matter is repeated to establish it, to make it firm, and to repel opposition to it. Important matters, and this is an important matter, that Muslims are transferred from one direction to another for the qibla, is a matter of great importance. For this reason those among people who apostatised did so; we ask Allah for well-being. So it is repeated for three matters: to establish it, to make firm upon it, and to repel opposition, so that no one opposes it; because whenever it is repeated, it means it is a fixed and firm matter that must be held firmly: "So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque."
* And from the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of the sanctity of the Sacred Mosque, because of His saying: "the Sacred Mosque."
* And from its benefits: that facing the qibla is the truth, and that it is not issued from desire, because of His saying: "And indeed it is the truth from your Lord," where He affirmed its truthfulness, emphasised by "inna" and the "lam."
* And from the benefits of the verse: God's care for the Prophet (ﷺ) through the particular lordship: "from your Lord."
* And from its benefits: the perfection of Allah's knowledge and His watchfulness over His creation, which we take from His saying: "And Allah is not unaware of what you do," or "of what they do," the two readings.
(...) Because pure non-existence is not a thing, let alone being praiseworthy, for non-existence is not a thing; but it becomes a thing when it includes an affirmation. Everything that Allah negates from Himself is an attribute of deficiency and defect, and it includes how many things?
Two things: the negation of that specific negated attribute, and second, the affirmation of the perfection of its opposite. And by this we know that the attributes of Allah, glorified and exalted, are perfect, with no defect in them in any way whatsoever.
And among them: the attribution of the action to the human being, which constitutes a refutation of whom? The Jabriyyah, by His saying: "of what you do," or "of what they do"? There is no doubt that a person's action is attributed to him, and his action is an acquisition (kasb) for him if it is good, and an acquisition (iktisab) if it is evil: "For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has acquired" [al-Baqarah 286]. In any case, people on this question, as has passed with us in the study of creed, divide into three categories. One category holds that the human being is compelled in his action, does nothing by choice ever, and his voluntary act is like his involuntary act, like one who descends from the roof by the stairs step by step; he is in reality like one who fell from the top of the roof without his knowing. Have you understood? Is this acceptable to reason or not? It is not acceptable.
Among them are those who say that the human being is independent in his knowledge, and that Allah, glorified and exalted, does not direct the servant at all; the servant has complete freedom in his action, and the will of Allah has no connection to it, and the decree and creation of Allah have no connection to the action of the human being. The human being is completely free. In reality this is also a false view, because it necessitates that there be in the creation of Allah something Allah cannot control, is that not so?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Because as long as the human being is free in his conduct, it means he can oppose what Allah wills, and thus there would be in the creation of Allah something Allah cannot control, indeed something Allah does not will. This too is a false view. Once the falsehood of both this and that has become clear to us, the truth must lie elsewhere. So what is the truth? The truth is that we say: the human being performs the act by his choice, and by this we mean the voluntary act, which occurs from him by his choice, unlike the trembling of one who shivers or the movement of a sleeper who is unaware. But we mean what a person does by his choice, which occurs by his choice, yet it is under the will of Allah, and it is also by the creation of Allah. The reason it is by the creation of Allah is that the human being is created by Allah, and his action comes about through two things: by a sincere resolve and by power. Do you agree with this?
* Students: Yes.

Shaykh: Who created sincere determination and capability? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the One who created sincere determination and capability. So the human being, with his attributes, his parts, and everything in him, is all created by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is impossible for anything to occur in Allah's dominion that He does not will or intend; rather, it happens by His will. This is the middle position, which I have taken hold of with both hands, using all the evidences. Those who said that man is compelled (jabr) took hold of one piece of evidence and let go of the other evidence. Those who said that he is independent (in his acts) took hold of one piece of evidence and let go of the second. But the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), praise be to Allah, took hold of both pieces of evidence with their hands and said: Man acts by his own choice (ikhtiyar), but his conduct is under the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason, when an action occurs without his choice, its ruling is lifted from him. So the sleeper has no ruling on his actions or his words, and the one who is coerced into something has no ruling on his action. Moreover, even more so, the one who is ignorant of something has no ruling on his action, although he intended the act; yet, because of his ignorance, he is excused. All of this indicates that Allah, glorified and exalted, is Merciful to His servants. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 150–153 (part 1 of 6):

Then the Exalted and Glorified said: ﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾ [al-Baqarah 150]. This sentence has already been discussed, and it is repeated for emphasis and as a preparation for what follows, because the benefit here is emphasis and preparation for what comes after it, which is His saying: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾. We said a little earlier that repetition in such important matters is intended to serve three purposes: affirmation, reinforcement, and defense. For this reason He says here: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾.

* Student: Shaykh, does someone say that it applies to the different circumstances (al-ahwal)?
* The Shaykh: No, that is not apparent, because they are general; each one of them is general, and for that reason, if one of them came without the other two, the ruling would still be one.

As for His saying: ﴿so that people will have no﴾, the lam here indicates purpose (ta'lil), and it is joined by (an) the verbal particle (al-masdariyyah) and (la) the negative particle, and ﴿will have﴾ is a present-tense verb in the subjunctive, governed by (an) al-masdariyyah. The intervening of the negative (la) between the governing particle and the governed verb does no harm.

As for His saying: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾, what is the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿argument﴾? It is the noun of (yakun) if it is a naqisah (incomplete) verb, or the subject (fa'il) if it is a tammah (complete) verb.

As for His saying: ﴿so that people will have no﴾, who is meant by ﴿people﴾? The verse is general, so it includes everyone who argues against the Muslims about their change from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah. The Jews and the polytheists argued against the Muslims on this matter. As for the Jews, they said: "The man has abandoned his religion for the religion of his forefathers, so he is a man who worships according to his whims and is not upon guidance." This is the argument of the Jews, and we seek refuge in Allah! Only yesterday he was facing Bayt al-Maqdis, and now partisanship has seized him so that he faces the Ka'bah. There is no doubt that this is injustice, an injustice from the Jews, unless they know in their books, as some scholars have mentioned, that Muhammad (ﷺ) would face the Ka'bah, and that this would be among his attributes. For this reason some scholars said: the argument also belongs to the Jews. The argument belongs to the Jews, meaning ﴿so that people will not have﴾: this reason is a reason for remaining, not for changing. That is, so that people would not have an argument against you if you remained facing Bayt al-Maqdis. So what is the argument? The argument is that the Jews would say: "Muhammad faces the Ka'bah," and on this basis the Jews' argument would be from two directions, the negative and the positive. That is, if you remained, the Jews would argue against you that this is not Muhammad whom the Torah announced, because the Muhammad whom the Torah announced faces the Ka'bah. Another argument is that they would say: "If Muhammad were a messenger, he would not have faced Bayt al-Maqdis yesterday and now face the Ka'bah; rather, he is a man who follows his desire and flatters." In the beginning he flattered us, then partisanship seized him and he faced the qiblah of his forefathers and grandfathers. Thus the Jews' argument would be from two directions: whether he remained, their argument would be that since he did not face the qiblah, he is not the awaited messenger; and if he changed, their argument would be that he worships according to his desire and is not upon guidance from Allah, and we seek refuge in Allah. So the reason here is a reason both for changing and for remaining. Some scholars mentioned that the people also include the polytheists. The polytheists argue against the Messenger (ﷺ) saying: "This man opposed us in our creed, and opposed us in our qiblah when he migrated to Madinah, then he returned to our qiblah, so he will return to our religion." They argue with this. You know that people of falsehood distort; that is, they reverse, and we seek refuge in Allah: ﴿the embellished speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 112]. They turn truth into falsehood, because they intend a purpose, and Allah the Exalted tests His servants with such people who reverse realities and make truth into falsehood. Otherwise, how could it be an argument for these and those? There is no argument. Rather, his change, together with his great apprehension, peace be upon him, about the objections and harassment that occurred, and you know the matter, we do not fully grasp its reality, what actually happened, his change while anticipating these oppositions, because Allah the Exalted said to him: ﴿The foolish among the people will say: What has turned them away?﴾. So the matter would involve back-and-forth and harassment. His change despite these anticipations, what does that indicate? It indicates his truthfulness, and in reality it is not evidence for what these people claim; rather, it is the greatest proof of his truthfulness and that he worships by revelation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He was told: face this, and he faced it; he was told: face this, and he faced it. He did not wish to follow his desire, but rather to follow what came to him of revelation.

And His saying: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾: to whom does the pronoun in ﴿against you﴾ refer? To the believers in general, to the Messenger (ﷺ) and his followers, because every argument made against the Messenger to deceive and invalidate the call is in reality an argument against all his followers, since his followers followed him only because he was upon the truth. So if someone comes to confuse, it becomes a confusion of their path and method, and so it is an argument against all of them.

And His saying: ﴿so that people will have no argument﴾: is this argument a real argument or a false argument? It is a false argument, and arguing does not necessarily entail accepting it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is void with their Lord﴾ [al-Shura 16]. It is void. So not all arguments are accepted; if they are based on truth, they are accepted and valid, otherwise they are void, even if they are presented in the form of evidence and proof. Even if those who argue for them phrase them as evidence and proof, they are considered void. Have you considered the arguments of the philosophers according to their method, the arguments of the Mu'tazilah according to their method, the arguments of the Jahmiyyah according to their method, the arguments of the Qadariyyah according to their method, and so on? They bring great arguments, but as it was said:

Arguments that collapse like glass; you think them
true, yet every breaker is broken.

Yes, no argument of theirs stands; all their arguments are considered baseless doubts. As for those who want to argue against the Muslims about their change from Bayt al-Maqdis to Makkah or to the Sacred Mosque, is this argument correct? No, rather it is among the most invalid arguments. Nevertheless, there is no harm in a person arming himself, even with false arguments; for this reason Allah said: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you, except those of them who did wrong﴾. The ones who did wrong are meant as the obstinate and arrogant who do not yield to the truth no matter how clear it becomes. His saying: ﴿except those who did wrong﴾: scholars differ about the exception here: is it connected (muttasil) or disconnected (munqati')? That is, is the exception connected or disconnected? Some said it is connected, and some said it is disconnected. Those who said it is disconnected said: "except" means "but"; that is: so that people will have no argument against you, but those of them who did wrong, you will not escape their disputation and contention, so be cautious. Those who said it is connected said: so that people will have no argument against you except those who did wrong, so it is an exception from "people," since among people some are wrongdoers and some are not. The closer view to me, and Allah knows best, is that the exception is disconnected, because His saying: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾ is general and comprehensive, but whoever among them, Jews or polytheists, did wrong, will not be restrained by this wisdom which Allah the Mighty and Majestic has made clear, so that the arguments of these wrongdoers would not vanish.

* Student: Shaykh, does the objection not arise that if the exception were connected, ﴿The foolish among the people will say﴾ shows they did argue, so would they have no argument at all? Does it not mention an argument for them?
* The Shaykh: What is closer to this context is that it is disconnected.
* Student: Shaykh, what does it mean if it were connected?
* The Shaykh: It says: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you, except those who did wrong﴾, meaning that Allah the Exalted made clear to the Messenger (ﷺ) and his companions that no one would argue against them except the wrongdoers. But in reality this meaning is weak, very weak, so what appears to me is that the exception is disconnected. He said: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾. Allah is greatest! That is, whatever they say, whatever deceptive speech they utter, whatever harassment they inflict, do not fear them, do not fear them. Fear (khashyah) and fear (khawf) are close in meaning, but the scholars say that the difference is that khashyah is only with knowledge, based on His saying: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir 28], unlike khawf, for a person may fear something while not knowing its state. As for khashyah, it exists only with knowledge. The second difference they mention is that khashyah is due to the greatness of the one feared, while khawf is due to the weakness of the one who fears, even if the feared thing is not great; for example, you say that a child fears an adolescent. Yes, why? Because of the child's weakness. This is how it has been distinguished. In any case, if this distinction is correct, it is evident; but the first distinction is clear, namely that khashyah occurs only with knowledge.

* Student: (...) Is the difference that khashyah is stronger than khawf in terms of its usage?
* The Shaykh: No, that is not apparent. Some said it is stronger, because this root, kha' and shin, indicates strength, as in the expression "al-shaykh al-kabir" (the elderly man). But there is room for consideration.

He said: ﴿So do not fear them﴾: fear whom? Those who did wrong. Whatever their wrongdoing, do not fear them as long as you are upon the truth; do not fear anyone. ﴿But fear Me﴾: He placed the command after the prohibition, because, as it is said, clearing away comes before adorning: remove the obstacles first, then establish. First, empty your heart of every fear of other than Allah, then make room in your heart for the fear of Allah. Remove the impurities first so that the place becomes receptive; when the place is receptive, what comes to it lands on something with no obstruction. ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾. The command here, as will come to us Allah willing in the benefits, ﴿but fear Me﴾, for what? For obligation. It is obligatory without doubt: it is obligatory upon a person to fear Allah alone. ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you﴾: completion (itmam) of a thing is reaching its end, and His saying ﴿that I may complete﴾ is conjoined to His saying ﴿so that﴾ (li'allā yakūn), meaning so that people will have no argument, and that I may complete. ﴿My favor upon you﴾: completion is reaching the end of a thing, and it usually refers to perfection. His saying ﴿My favor﴾: what is favor (ni'mah)? It is what a person enjoys. It is said ni'mah and na'mah, but generally ni'mah is used for good, and na'mah is ease without gratitude, as the Exalted said: ﴿and luxury in which they were enjoying themselves﴾ [al-Dukhan 27]. His saying ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you﴾: when was this revealed? When was ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you﴾ revealed?

* Student: After Surah al-Baqarah, at the beginning of the Hijrah.
* The Shaykh: At the beginning of the Hijrah, at the change of the qiblah, meaning in the second year. It is not contradicted by His saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3], which was revealed on the Day of 'Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage. Yes, it is not contradicted, because what is meant in the verse of al-Ma'idah, ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you﴾, is the general completion in the whole Shari'ah, whereas here ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you﴾ refers to this particular Shari'ah, namely facing the Ka'bah instead of Bayt al-Maqdis. For it was established that "the Messenger (ﷺ) would turn his face toward the sky, awaiting when he would be commanded to face the Ka'bah,"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (399) from the hadith of al-Bara'.]] so this is undoubtedly among the favors of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, that He bestowed upon the Muslims that they face this House, which is the first House established for people, and which, as some scholars said, is the qiblah of all the prophets, as Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned: that the Ka'bah is the qiblah of all the prophets, and that the Jews' facing Bayt al-Maqdis and the Christians' facing the east are among the things they changed in their religion.

And His saying ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you﴾: Allah the Exalted attributed the favor to Himself, because He is its owner, the One who bestows it and confers it upon His servants. Were it not for this great favor, people would not remain for the blink of an eye. Consider His saying: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked anger﴾ [al-Fatihah 6–7]. Regarding the favor, He said: ﴿upon whom You have bestowed favor﴾, but regarding anger He did not say: "the path of those with whom You were angry," rather He said: ﴿those who have evoked anger﴾. Yes, and this is like His saying: ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them right guidance﴾ [al-Jinn 10]. Then, regarding those who have evoked anger, the anger upon them is not from Allah alone, but from Allah the Exalted and Glorified and from His friends among the messengers and their followers. ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided﴾: what does (la'alla) mean here?

* Student: For causation...
* The Shaykh: For causation; that is, and in order that you may be guided. Guidance, as we have already gone over, is of two kinds: knowledge-guidance and action-guidance, and it is also called guidance of direction (irshad) and guidance of success (tawfiq). Knowledge-guidance means that Allah opens to a person of knowledge what he needs in the affairs of his religion and his worldly life, and action-guidance means that he is granted success in acting upon this knowledge. The first is a means, and the second is the goal; for this reason there is no good in knowledge without action; rather, knowledge without action becomes a burden upon the one who is granted it.

His saying ﴿and that you may be guided﴾: this is the third of these causes. What is the first cause? ﴿so that people will have no argument against you, except those of them who did wrong﴾. The second cause: ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you﴾. The third: ﴿and that you may be guided﴾. Here guidance includes both knowledge-guidance and action-guidance, meaning in knowledge and in action. The reason it is comprehensive is this: they did not know that Allah's pleasure lies in facing the Ka'bah except through what Allah taught them; then Allah granted them success in being guided to it. Did they resist? Not at all. Rather, the people of Quba' received the news while they were praying the dawn prayer, with the imam facing north and the followers facing south, and he informed them that the qiblah had been changed to the Ka'bah. What did they do? They turned in their prayer toward the Ka'bah,[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (403) and Muslim (526/13) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]] so the imam came to face south and the followers faced north, and all of them had their faces toward the Ka'bah. This is a great action-guidance, because a person's immediate movement to what Allah has commanded, with such ease, despite expecting opposition and harassment, what does this indicate? It indicates the strength of his faith and his trust in his Lord, the Exalted and Glorified. Likewise every believer must, when Allah's command comes, comply with the command, and Allah the Exalted will make ease for him in His command, because fear of Allah brings ease to affairs. He should not say: "By Allah, I fear the harassment, I fear people will reproach me, I fear people will mock me." This does no harm, for ﴿Allah defends those who believe﴾ [al-Hajj 38].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 150–153 (part 2 of 6):

﴿And that I may complete My favour upon you, and that you may be guided﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:150–151]. This is also a fourth favour directed to the believers: ﴿as We have sent among you a messenger from among you﴾. That is, this falls under His words ﴿that there will not be for people against you any argument﴾, ﴿and that I may complete﴾, ﴿and that you may be guided﴾, just as you have also been sent this Messenger, the Prophet (ﷺ), among you, and so on. The meaning is that God's favour upon us in directing us to the Ka'bah instead of Bayt al-Maqdis is great, just as His favour upon us through the Messenger (ﷺ) is great. ﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from among you.﴾ ﴿A messenger from among you.﴾ Irsal (sending) means ba'th (dispatching), and ba'th also means irsal; that is, he is sent by God. This is because God, glory be to Him, created creation for worship. And how is He worshipped?

* Student: He is worshipped by what He has legislated.

* Shaykh: Yes, by what He has legislated. And how do we know which acts of worship God is pleased with and which He is not pleased with? This is not possible except through the messengers. If a person were left to his intellect in worship, he would not know how to worship God, would he?

* Students: Certainly.

* Shaykh: And if worship were left to our intellects, people would not have agreed upon the worship of God; each one would say, "This is the correct way," and go on with it. If a person were left to his intellect in worship, our nation would not be one nation. In any case, it is not possible for us, by our intellects alone, to comprehend how to worship God. A simple example: if you were told, "Perform ablution for prayer," and this ablution were not explained to you, how would you perform it? One person might say, "Ablution requires that I wash from the base of the thumb to the thumb," yes. Another would say, "I only wash the palms, the forehead, the nose, the two knees and the tips of the feet, because these are what is involved in prostration." And another would have a different form. So had God not made clear to us how to worship Him, we would not have known how to worship Him. This is among the favours of God in sending this Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), who explained everything to us. For this reason Abu Dharr said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed away, and there was not a bird that flaps its wings in the sky except that he had mentioned knowledge of it to us; even regarding birds in the sky, the Messenger (ﷺ) taught us about them."[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (21361) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] This is general in everything: everything we need in the matters of our religion and our worldly life, this Messenger has taught us. For this reason He said: ﴿reciting to you Our verses﴾. As for His words ﴿from among you﴾, what was mentioned before applies: does "from among you" mean from among your lineage or from among you as a kind? We have previously explained that when He says ﴿from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:128], the intended meaning is the kind (jins), and when it is said "from among you" or "from among them," the intended meaning is lineage (nasab). God says: ﴿It is He who has sent among the unlettered a messenger from among them﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 62:2], and God has said: ﴿God has certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:164]. And the believers include Arabs and non-Arabs.

﴿Reciting to you Our verses.﴾ What is the meaning of yatlu (recites)? It means reads: he reads to you Our verses, conveying them exactly as he heard them. God says: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:17–19]. These are three stages: collection and recitation through Jibril, ﴿So when We have recited it, follow its recitation﴾, ﴿then upon Us is its clarification﴾. Is its clarification for people all of them, of meaning or of wording? Of wording and meaning. For this reason, the Qur'an, praise be to God, is clear in its wording and its meaning. There is nothing in it that is unclear to people except a relative unclarity, such that it is unclear to one person and not to another, or in one state and not in another (...).

It is a confirmation of it (...), what do you say? A question: is His words ﴿and teaches you that which you did not know﴾ a confirmation of what came before, or is it additional to what came before?

* Student: Additional.

* Shaykh: If it is additional to what came before, then where is what the Messenger (ﷺ) taught us that lies outside the Book and the Sunnah?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: But we have concluded that it is general. The apparent view to me is that the statement that it is by way of restating what came before, ﴿and teaches you that which you did not know﴾, is more appropriate. Because if someone says, "He teaches us what we did not know of matters of the Hereafter," we say: this is included in the Book and the Sunnah and is not outside them. Whatever assumptions you make, you will find it included in the Book and the Sunnah. But it is mentioned as a confirmation and a demonstration of the favour, that He teaches us what we did not know. So, is the default state of the children of Adam ignorance or knowledge? The default is ignorance, because knowledge is acquired; so whatever knowledge we attain, it in reality arrives upon ignorance, and this indicates the deficiency of man, since his default is ignorance, but he learns through God's teaching.

His words ﴿and teaches you that which you did not know﴾ are not to be taken in their absolute generality, for what is excluded from it is what cannot be known, from the knowledge of the unseen. For example, the knowledge of the Hour: were we taught it? We were not taught it, even though we do not know it. For there are matters of the unseen that are not known, even the closest matters to us, which we do not know: the soul. ﴿And they ask you about the soul. Say, "The soul is of the affair of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:85]. Accordingly, ﴿that which you did not know﴾ means: that which you did not know but which you need to know. As for what cannot be known, we neither know it nor were we taught it, such as the matters of the unseen that none knows except God, like the knowledge of the Hour, the sending down of rain, and knowledge of the future, except what God has disclosed to His Messenger. Likewise, the knowledge of the modality (kayfiyyah) of God's names and attributes, for this cannot be comprehended. Everything related to God's attributes, its modality cannot be encompassed by knowledge. For this reason God, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him﴾ [al-An'am 6:103], even though eyes will see Him, and that is in the Hereafter. ﴿And He perceives [all] vision, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [al-An'am 6:103]. God has informed us of many of His actions: His istiwa' (settling) upon the Throne, His descent to the lowest heaven, His coming to judge between His servants, and other of His actions. Do we know the modality? We do not know it. God has informed us about Himself that He is amazed, by His words: ﴿Rather, you wonder, and they mock﴾ [al-Saffat 37:12], read with a dammah on the ta', which is a recitation of the seven readings. Likewise the Prophet (ﷺ) informed us that God laughs: "God laughs at two men."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (2826) and Muslim (1890/128) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] Can we then imagine or explain this modality? No, we cannot imagine it nor explain this modality, because it is unknown to us, and we cannot encompass it.

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:152].

First: the grammar of the verse. ﴿Remember Me﴾ (udhkurunī) is an imperative verb. It contains the nun of protection (nun al-wiqayah), the ya' of the object, and the waw of the subject. How many words does it become? Four words: an imperative verb, the waw is the subject, nun of protection, ya' is the object. This imperative verb has its answer: ﴿I will remember you﴾ (adhkurkum). Why is the verb jussed (sukkina)? Because it is the answer to the imperative, which is His words ﴿Remember Me﴾. So His words ﴿Remember Me; I will remember you﴾ mean: an action and a reward. The action is remembrance of God, the Mighty and Majestic; the reward is God's remembrance of His servant. Which of the two is greater? The latter is well known. That is, God's remembering you is greater than your remembering Him. For this reason God said: ﴿Say, "If you should love God, then follow me; God will love you"﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:31]. Would you love God?

* Students: No.

* Shaykh: ﴿God will love you﴾ is the answer, because this is the goal and the purpose: that God loves you, not that you love God. For this reason the answer did not come in the expected form. The expected form was: "If you love God, follow me, you will love God." But the answer is ﴿God will love you﴾, because the matter that matters most is that God loves you. Here ﴿Remember Me﴾ is a human's remembrance of his Lord, but the matter that matters most is ﴿I will remember you﴾. ﴿Remember Me; I will remember you.﴾ His words ﴿Remember Me﴾ are an imperative verb. And how is the remembrance of God done? It is done by the heart, by the tongue, and by the limbs. The primary is the remembrance of the heart. ''Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt.''[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599/107) from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]] Remembrance of God by the tongue or by the limbs without the heart is deficient; it is not remembrance. The reality of remembrance is the remembrance of God Most High by the heart. And how do I remember Him by the heart? I remember Him by the heart in that a person turns in repentance to God, relies upon Him, hopes in Him, fears Him, and calls to mind His love, His greatness, and other things. This is a necessary matter for a person. Likewise, a person observes in the cosmos things that are all signs of God: he observes the sun in its greatness, its regularity, its rising and setting; likewise the moon, the stars, the night and the day, and conditions ﴿And those days We alternate among the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:140], and so on. We derive evidence from these things for whom? For the One who arranged these things and created them. Each of them has a particular indication: some indicate greatness, some indicate the power of sovereignty, some indicate wisdom. All of them are wisdom, but some are more specific than others in what they indicate. This is remembrance of the heart through love, glorification, turning in repentance, fear, hope, contemplation, and so on.

Remembrance of God by the tongue includes the well-known remembrance such as: "There is no god but God, alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, and He is over all things powerful," "Glory be to God," "Praise be to God," "God is greatest," and what is similar to these. It includes recitation of the Qur'an, it includes supplication, and it includes every speech that brings one closer to God, the Mighty and Majestic; for every speech that brings one closer to God is an act of obedience, and obedience is commanded, and the one who performs an act of obedience feels that he does it for what reason? For obedience to God and seeking nearness to Him. Thus this is remembrance, this is the remembrance of God, the Mighty and Majestic. And if we take remembrance in this general sense, a person can make all his speech a remembrance of God if he is granted success. For this reason it is possible that the habit of those who remember becomes worship, and that the worship of the heedless becomes habit. All of this depends on intention. Remembrance by the limbs: how is remembrance by the limbs? By standing in prayer, bowing, prostration, jihad, zakah; all of them are remembrance of God, because when you do them you are obedient to God, and then you are remembering God in that act. For this reason God, Most High, said: ﴿And establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God is greater﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:45]. Some scholars said: "Because it includes the remembrance of God, which is greater." This is one of the two opinions regarding this verse.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: In this matter, we must know that meanings, when they are paired with other terms, are interpreted specifically, and when stated alone they are inclusive. For example: the faqir and the miskin, when they are mentioned together, each is interpreted by what is specific to it. Al-birr (righteousness) and al-taqwa (God-consciousness), when mentioned together, each is interpreted by what is specific to it; and when one of them is mentioned alone, it includes the other. So remembrance, when stated absolutely, is inclusive. But if one says, for example: "This man recited the Qur'an and remembered God," then here recitation of the Qur'an is specific and remembrance is specific.

As for His words, Most High, ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾: ﴿I will remember you﴾, is it one of God's attributes? And is it of the essential (dhatiyyah) attributes? And is it of the positive (ijabiyyah) or negative (salbiyyah) attributes? The answer to the first: is it one of God's attributes or not? It is one of God's attributes. As to the second: is it essential or active (fi'liyyah)? It is active. As to the third: is it positive or negative? It is positive.

As for His words ﴿Remember Me; I will remember you﴾, here it is unrestricted. But it becomes clear from the form of the command and the reward that the reward is of the same kind as the action. For this reason the authentic hadith says: "If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in himself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (7405) and Muslim (2675/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾ has a reading ﴿fa-dhkurūnī adhkurkum﴾ with a fatha on the ya', meaning the ya' of the speaker (the object pronoun 'me'). It is permissible to make it sukun (unvocalized), to vocalize it with a fatha, or to delete it for lightness. But in the Qur'an, these depend on transmission. From the standpoint of the Arabic language, fatha, sukun, and deletion are permissible. But regarding the Qur'an, they depend on transmission. Here there is a reading ﴿fa-dhkurūnī adhkurkum﴾.

As for His words ﴿And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾: ﴿ushkurū﴾ is an imperative verb from shakara (to thank). The scholars of Arabic grammar have differed as to whether ﴿ushkurū lī﴾ means "thank me" or something else. Some said: it is the same, and that shakara is transitive by itself and transitive by the preposition lam, so one says shakarahu (he thanked him) and shakara lahu (he thanked him). Others said: it does not have the same meaning, and that shakara is always transitive by itself, and that the object here, in such expressions as ﴿ushkurū lī﴾, is omitted; that is: "Thank Me for what I have bestowed upon you," or "for My favour," or something similar. The disagreement regarding this does not entail great benefit, because all agree that the intended meaning of this command is to carry out thanking God, the Mighty and Majestic, by complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition. Thanks is by the heart, by the tongue, and by the limbs, and it occurs only in return for a favour. Pay attention: its cause is more specific than the cause of praise (hamd), and its object is more general than the object of praise. I hope you will be attentive. Praise is by the tongue, but its cause is the perfection of the one praised and his bestowal of favour. So if its cause is the bestowal of favour by the one praised, then it is from thanks, meaning praise. But thanks (shukr): its cause is one. What is it?

* Student: The favour.

* Shaykh: The favour, the favour of the one thanked. As for its object, it has three: it is by the heart, by the tongue, and by the limbs. Pay attention to the difference between hamd and shukr; most people do not know the difference between them. They differ in cause and they differ in object. What did we say is the cause of hamd? The perfection of the one praised and his benevolence. So God, exalted be He, is praised for His perfection and for His bestowal of favour. And the cause of shukr? The favour, the favour of the one thanked. As for the object: hamd is by the tongue only, while shukr is by the tongue, the heart, and the limbs. On this is the saying of the poet:

"Favours from me have brought you three things:
My hand, my tongue, and the hidden inner heart."

So "my hand" is thanks by the limbs; "my tongue" is by speech; and "the hidden inner heart" is the heart.

What is thanks by the heart? Thanks by the heart is that a person acknowledges in his heart that this favour is from God, the Mighty and Majestic, and so loves God, Glorified and Exalted, for this bestowal. For this reason it is mentioned in a hadith: "Love God for what He nourishes you with of favours."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Jami' (3789) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] When a person feels that this favour is from God, he loves God, because souls are naturally inclined to love one who does good to them. This is the connection of thanks to the heart. Its connection to the tongue is speaking of God's favour, not boastfully but in thanks. God, Most High, said: ﴿As for the favour of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [al-Duha 93:11]. And the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no boasting."[[Narrated by Muslim (2278/3) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and by al-Tirmidhi in his Jami' (3148) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, and the wording is his.]] As for thanks by the limbs: it is that a person performs obedience to God and directs this favour to what it was made for. Directing this favour to what it was made for is itself the thanks for the favour.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 150–153 (part 3 of 6):

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Be grateful to Me﴾. On the view that shakara (to thank) is transitive by itself or with the lam, there is no difficulty in the matter, because the meaning of "be grateful to Me" and "thank Me" is one. As for the second view, that shakara is transitive by itself, the lam here is for sincerity (al-ikhlas); that is, "be grateful to Me and not to others," so it specifies the one to whom gratitude is due, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for He is the one deserving of gratitude.

His words, ﴿and do not be ungrateful to Me﴾. The question is: why is "lā" (the prohibitive "do not") followed by the nun (النون) when the verb is one of the "five verbs" (al-af'al al-khamsa)? The answer is that the nun here is the nun of protection (nun al-wiqaya), not the nun of i'rab (grammatical inflection). Similar to it is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, for those who wronged there is a share like the share of their companions﴾, so do they not hasten (فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ) or (وَلَا) "hasten Me" (يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ)? ﴿So let them not hasten Me (59) Then woe to those who disbelieved from their Day which they are promised﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 59–60]. So the nun here is the nun of protection. As for His words, ﴿and do not be ungrateful to Me﴾, that means: do not deny Me or deny My blessing, but rather establish its thanks, its proclamation and its manifestation. Therefore, when Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant, He loves that the effect of His blessing be seen upon him. If Allah bestows knowledge upon a scholar, Allah loves that the effect of this blessing be manifest upon him, first: in his own conduct, so that he is known for his knowledge, standing and acting by what he knows. Second: from the manifestation of knowledge is teaching; he teaches people as much as he is able. It is not necessary that he teach in circles; he may teach a person who prays beside him and errs in some matter of the prayer, so he teaches him. This is one of the methods of teaching. Third: among the effects of the blessing of knowledge is that a person calls to Allah with insight (ʿalā baṣīra), calling to Allah with insight, such that in every setting where he can speak of calling to Allah, he speaks to the extent he is able, even in private gatherings. If he is invited to a gathering, for example, and sees the benefit in speaking, let him speak. Some scholars, on a matter, are content with what is present: some people of knowledge have a book, either with them personally or with one of their students, and they read the book to those present, benefiting and benefiting others. This is good if people are known to accept it, having been accustomed to it and anticipating it from him. But if he has not accustomed them, it may burden them. Yet it is possible to open the way by raising an issue, such as a question, so that the way opens for people to ask and benefit. For some students of knowledge, their gatherings are like the gatherings of the common folk, from which people do not benefit. This is without doubt a deficiency, even if they may not be sinful, but it is a deficiency. Therefore, what is fitting for a student of knowledge, even if he is not asked, is to raise a question, in order to open the door for those present so that they may ask him. "Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him about Islam, faith, excellence, the Hour and its signs, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'This is Jibril; he came to you to teach you your religion.'" [Recorded by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.] Although he (the Prophet) taught Jibril, who answers whom? The Messenger ﷺ. But why did he make him a teacher? Why did he make him a teacher while he was asking?
* Student: Because he confirmed him.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Because he asked him, and because of his question...
* Shaykh: Knowledge came about; yes, because he caused this knowledge to come about. The point is, we say: ﴿and do not be ungrateful to Me﴾. It is from ingratitude for a blessing that its effect is not seen upon the one Allah has blessed; a person should not conceal it, because kufr (disbelief) in its origin is from this root (k-f-r), meaning concealment, and what is its origin in language? Concealment. From it comes al-kafurra, which the common people call "al-kafur," the sheath of the date-palm spathe, because it covers the fruit. So the person upon whom the effect of the blessing is not seen has not in reality manifested it, but has denied it.

﴿And be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful (152). O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer﴾. It has been mentioned to us before, and there is no harm in repeating it, that when speech begins with a call (nida'), it is an indication of giving it importance, because the call necessitates the addressee's attention to the one calling. Is that clear or not? It has also been mentioned to us that when Allah opens a ruling or a report with the attribute of faith, that is evidence that believing in it, if it is a report, is among the requirements of faith, and that adhering to it, if it is a ruling, is among the requirements of faith. If it is a report, like the verse: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something﴾ [al-Ma'idah 94], this is a report; and the ruling: ﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer﴾. The point is that when speech is opened with the attribute of faith, this indicates that adhering to it, if it is a ruling, and affirming it, if it is a report, are among the requirements of faith, and that opposing it or denying it is a deficiency in faith. Likewise, introducing a matter with the attribute of faith is in reality a form of incitement (al-igra'), inciting the addressee to adhere to the ruling or to affirm the report, as if it is said to them: "O you who have believed, because of your faith and because you are believers, do such and such, or do not do such and such, or such and such will happen, so affirm it." Just as you say to a man, "O man," and what is the meaning of "O man"? It means that the requirement of your manhood is that you avoid this thing, or that you do this thing, or the like. "O believer" is an incitement; that is: because of your faith, do such and such, or leave such and such.

﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer﴾: seek help through them; that is, make them an aid for you. ﴿Through patience﴾; that is, make patience an aid for you. ﴿And prayer﴾. Patience (al-sabr) in language is restraint (al-habs), and from it the saying: "So-and-so was killed sabran," that is, restrained (bound).

Technically, it is the restraint of the soul upon what it ought to be upon, or from what it ought not to be upon. It is of three kinds: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from the disobedience of Allah, and patience upon the painful decrees of Allah. Patience in obedience to Allah requires striving in two respects: the respect of psychological fatigue and the respect of physical fatigue. Patience in obedience is undergone by a person in two respects, what?
* The students: Psychological and physical fatigue.
* Shaykh: Psychological and physical fatigue. The psychological: you find him struggling with his soul to perform the act of obedience. The physical: he tires, performing wudu' in the days of the scorching cold, going out to the mosques in the darkness, and enduring hardships to reach the House of Allah, and so on. Patience in refraining from sin: what does it include? Only psychological fatigue, because it is restraint; you do not have to exert your body at all, just leave this thing. So there is psychological fatigue; the body has not moved at all, but he was asked to refrain. Thus it is psychological fatigue. Note that a person may undergo more psychological fatigue in abstaining from the forbidden than he undergoes in exerting himself in what is commanded, that is, in obedience. Take heed, brothers: there may be a strong motive to commit this sin, so that the person's struggle in leaving it is a severe and arduous matter, while performing the obedience, even if it is more excellent, is easier for him psychologically. Then the third kind: patience upon the painful decrees of Allah, there is suffering in it. Is it psychological or physical?
* Student: Psychological and physical.
* Shaykh: The painful decrees? In the painful decrees, what is there?
* Student: Psychological and physical; it may be that he has become ill, or broken a bone.
* Shaykh: Not quite, but that is not from his doing; that he suffers from a fracture or the like is not from his doing. But generally there is psychological suffering, psychological fatigue, because a person may see that to relieve himself he should slap his cheek, or tear his garment, or pull out his hair, and the like. This may bring him relief, even though this is from Satan, but he restrains himself from this matter, and this is psychological fatigue.

Which of the three kinds is best? Patience in obedience, or in refraining from sin, or upon the painful decrees of Allah? Patience in obedience is the best and closest to Allah. For this reason you find that among acts of worship are obligations of Islam; all the pillars of Islam are acts of obedience. But prohibitions other than shirk do not reach this level. Therefore we say: patience in obedience is the best of them, then patience in refraining from disobedience, because it is voluntary and active: you are able to act or not act. Patience upon the painful decrees is the lowest of them. That is because a person, as some of the salaf said: either he is patient with the patience of the noble, or he forgets like the forgetting of animals. That is, if he, for example, became distressed and was unable to be patient at the moment of calamity, in the end, will he have anything? Against his will he will be patient, and he will forget as if it never happened. Yusuf, peace be upon him, had several kinds of patience: he had patience in obedience, patience in refraining from sin, and patience upon the painful decrees. His patience upon the painful decrees is evident, or not? Regarding what his brothers did to him and what they plotted against him. And his patience in refraining from sin? Also evident, when the wife of the 'Aziz invited him to herself, but Allah, the Exalted, saved him when he sought refuge in Him: ﴿He said: "My Lord, the prison is dearer to me than what they invite me to. And unless You turn away from me their plot, I might incline toward them and be among the ignorant"﴾ [Yusuf 33]. When he turned to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with sincerity, what was the result and the answer? ﴿So his Lord responded to him and turned away from him their plot. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [Yusuf 34]. Glory be to Allah, the Mighty! O human, always turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Sometimes a person is heedless of Allah and then is struck by a calamity so that he turns to Allah and remembers, because a person with abundant blessings and absence of calamities forgets and continues in these blessings, going along with them and becoming heedless. But when he is struck by hardships, then he returns to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and is patient. Yusuf, peace be upon him, turned to Allah, and Allah answered his supplication: ﴿So his Lord responded to him and turned away from him their plot﴾. Did he have patience in obedience?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: And what?
* Student: His patience in calling to Allah in prison; he sat calling to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And his request to be entrusted with the treasuries of the land, which he presented to him, peace be upon him. Also: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law except that Allah willed﴾.
* Shaykh: Meaning several matters, and likewise his standing with the kingdom and organizing it, yes. All of these are patience in obedience. Good. ﴿And seek help through patience﴾, and also seek help through patience in the burdens and hardships of affairs. How excellent it is for a person to be patient, awaiting relief, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Know that victory comes with patience, and relief comes with distress, and with hardship comes ease" [Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (2803) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas]. Because when he is awaiting relief, patience becomes easy for him, since he hopes that affairs will pass and that a state lasting forever is impossible. If he hopes for reward in the Hereafter and hopes for relief in this world, patience becomes very easy for him. This is without doubt one of the praiseworthy qualities that Islam brought, and it is also evidence that affairs become easy by what? By patience. Whatever affairs reach you, be patient and they will become easy. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, made patience an aid, saying: ﴿Seek help through patience﴾. Likewise through prayer. Prayer: which prayer? What is prayer? Supplication? No; the legislated prayer. For this reason our Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, when a matter distressed him, would turn to prayer. Prayer is among the greatest aids in affairs. Why? Because the one praying stands before his Beloved, the Exalted, before Allah, and forgets all else. But this is the prayer of those who turn often (al-awwabin), not the prayer of those who play (al-la'abin). Yes, the prayer of those who turn often, not the prayer of the playful. We ask Allah to accept our repentance! When he stands before his Lord he forgets everything, turns to Him, is reassured by Him, and there comes to his heart light, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Prayer is light" [Recorded by Muslim (1/223) from the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari]. This joy, happiness and expansion of the breast eases affairs for you, does it not? Of course it eases; certainly it eases for you; certainly, not "of course" but certainly: it eases affairs for you. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The coolness of my eyes has been placed in prayer" [Recorded by al-Nasa'i (3939) from the hadith of Anas]. It eases affairs for you and makes difficulties easy. Moreover, within the prayer itself there are places for supplication, where you ask Allah, the Exalted, to help you with these matters, so the prayer itself is an aid, and what it contains of supplication is also an aid. Thus a person seeks help through it in all his concerns and calamities. The prayer is of great importance for one who performs it in the lawful manner, but regrettably we have wasted the prayer. We ask Allah to accept our repentance! We enter into it and leave it while remaining as we entered; indeed for some people it increases them in nothing but distance from Allah. We ask Allah for safety! So seeking help through prayer is a matter that Allah has commanded. Suppose, for example, you were in distress from your family, the world constricted upon you, the wife wants something, the child wants something, and the like. Then you perform wudu', turn to Allah, and address Him with His words and call upon Him with your needs; you forget, then you go out as if the whole world is spacious before you, with a light shining, and affairs become easy and light for you. And He who commanded us with this, "Seek help through patience and prayer," knows this, Glory be to Him, He is Knowing of it, and He is Merciful to us. Were this remedy not successful and effective, Allah would not have commanded it. ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾.
* Student: Has the hadith been declared weak?
* Shaykh: Which one?
* Student: That "when a matter distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he turned to prayer" [Recorded by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (1319), and Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir (1/618), from the hadith of Hudhayfah, and the wording is his]. But the verse supports it (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, the verse supports it, and I see that Shaykh al-Islam, Ibn al-Qayyim and Ibn Kathir all cite it as evidence.
﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾: this is a great glad tiding for whoever is patient. ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾, and He did not say "with those who pray." Why?
* Student: Because prayer is part of patience.
* Shaykh: Because prayer is obedience, and we said that among the kinds of patience is patience in obeying Allah; this is one aspect. The second aspect: patience is harder to undertake than prayer, because patience is bitter, brothers, patience is bitter.
"Patience, like its name, is bitter in its taste, but its outcomes are sweeter than honey."
Yes, it is bitter, which a person endures and suffers, and he undergoes agitation, his blood and face change, and he persists and struggles, to the point that whoever sees him might say: "This one is sick." Therefore the words "Allah is with the patient" came: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾. Yes. A third answer: if He is with the patient, then He is with those who pray all the more, by the evidence that it is established from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that the one who prays communes with his Lord, and that Allah is in front of his face [Agreed upon; recorded by al-Bukhari (406) and Muslim (547/50) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar], while He is upon His Throne, Glory be to Him. Based on this, the answer is from three aspects. If someone says: why did the verse not say "Indeed, Allah is with the patient and those who pray?" The answer: count for us the first aspect.
* Student: That prayer is part of patience.
* Shaykh: Yes, part of patience, so it is included within it. And the second aspect?
* Student: Patience is more general.
* Shaykh: This is what he said. Glory be to Allah!
* Student: That patience is harder than prayer.
* Shaykh: Yes, the struggle of patience is more arduous; therefore the companionship was attributed to the patient, so that they would be energized for this matter. The third aspect?
* Student: That if Allah is with the patient, He is with those who pray all the more.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 150–153 (part 4 of 6):

* The Shaykh: He is with those who pray all the more so, as the Sunnah has related. Take note, everyone. As for me, I think these three points I may review after a few days before presenting them; perhaps I will review them and not present them, because sometimes with explanation a person may find that God brings to him things that had not occurred to him, and he seeks them out one day and finds them coming to him. So be eager for these matters. Now we have: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾. Is this companionship (ma'iyyah) specific or general?
* Student: Specific.
* The Shaykh: This is specific, because every companionship that is attached to a cause that necessitates it is a specific companionship. Every companionship attached to a cause that necessitates it is a specific companionship. ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who are mindful of Him﴾ [al-Baqarah 194] is attached to taqwa, which is a cause; ﴿with the patient﴾, ﴿surely with the good-doers﴾ [al-'Ankabut 69], ﴿with those who are mindful﴾, and similar. As for the absolute companionship that is meant to convey Allah's encompassing of His creation in knowledge, power, hearing and sight, this is called general companionship, because it is not restricted to anyone; rather it is general. It has many examples in the Qur'an, some of which are general for all creation and some of which are restricted to a people as a warning to them. An example of the general for all creation is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? There is no private conversation between three but that He is their fourth, nor between five but that He is their sixth, nor between less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Mujadilah 7]. So His saying, ﴿there is no private conversation between three﴾, is it general or specific?
* Student: Specific.
* Another student: No, general.
* The Shaykh: No, general, general. Any three who converse secretly: believers, disbelievers, sinners, the righteous, whoever it may be. ﴿Nor between less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾. Likewise His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah sees well all that you do﴾ [al-Hadid 4]. This is general. It may also be specific, but it does not entail support and assistance; rather it entails a warning. So it is of the category of the general restricted, as in His saying: ﴿They conceal themselves from people but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, for He is with them when they plot by night in speech that He does not approve﴾ [an-Nisa' 108]. Here there is no doubt that the meaning is not "with them" in support and assistance. Why? Because they do not deserve it. Rather the meaning is to warn them with this encompassing. So we have general absolute, and general restricted to a people for warning. The specific also divides into two kinds: restricted by an attribute, and restricted by a person. Restricted by an attribute, such as? ﴿with the patient﴾, ﴿with those who are mindful﴾ [al-Baqarah 194], and so on. And restricted by a person, such as His saying to Musa and Harun: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46], and His saying to His Prophet ﷺ, relating what he said to Abu Bakr: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾. Then this companionship in its divisions does not necessitate that Allah, Exalted is He, be incarnate in the earth. It is not a companionship of indwelling and mixing, because that is impossible for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. No one understood it in this way except one whom the devils have led astray, removing him from his natural disposition, or one who is ignorant of the Arabic language. No one imagines this or says this: that it is companionship of indwelling, and that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is with us in place, except one who is ignorant of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and has not measured Him with His true measure, and likewise ignorant of the meaning in the Arabic language. Please pay attention to this matter, for it is important. Those who understood it in this way are the Jahmiyyah, and what is meant is their early ones, for the later Jahmiyyah abandoned this path and followed the path of pure negation (ta'til), saying: Allah, Exalted is He, is neither inside the world nor outside the world, neither connected nor separated... to the end of what has preceded us in the creed. But their early ones used to speak of incarnation. Among the strange things, and strange things are many, is that these people say: Allah is with us on earth, may God protect us, and they deny that He is in the heavens. They deny that He is in the heavens, so their minds were turned upside down. Then came a people who acted shrewd and became cunning, saying: We say that Allah is with us on earth, while He is upon His Throne in the heavens. They intend, in their claim, to reconcile the texts, but in reality they were cunning and were turned upside down, for this is not reconciling the texts; rather in reality it is nullifying the texts. How can Allah, Mighty and Majestic, be above His Throne in His essence and on the earth in His essence? Is this possible? It is absolutely impossible, unless it is, God forbid, by the plurality of creators.
He cannot be incarnate in the earth, and this is a view refuted by the textual, rational and natural proofs. The Qur'an and the Sunnah are filled with what is explicit or apparent that Allah, Exalted is He, is in the heavens. Reason also indicates that Allah, Exalted is He, is in the heavens, as we have mentioned, by two aspects. The first aspect: Is highness (al-'uluw) an attribute of perfection or an attribute of deficiency?
* The students: An attribute of perfection.
* The Shaykh: An attribute of perfection. So if it is an attribute of perfection, it must be established for Allah, because Allah, Exalted is He, is described with absolute perfection, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [ar-Rum 27].
The second aspect of the rational proofs for Allah's highness: it is said, what is the opposite of highness?
* The students: Lowness.
* The Shaykh: Lowness. Lowness is without doubt an attribute of deficiency, and Allah, Exalted is He, is free of deficiency, so highness must be affirmed for Him. As for the natural disposition, do not ask about it. Go to an old woman near the Haram and say to her: Where is Allah? What does she say?
* The students: In the heavens.
* The Shaykh: In the heavens. Go to the children in their schools and say to them: Where is Allah? They say: In the heavens. Ask any frightened person or one who supplicates: where does his heart rise?
* The students: To the heavens.
* The Shaykh: To the heavens. Ask all Muslims who, in their prostration, say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Where do they find their hearts rising?
* The students: To the height.
* The Shaykh: To the height. There is no problem with this. So the natural disposition indicates the affirmation of Allah's highness, Mighty and Majestic. The consensus of the Muslims, apart from the people of negation (ahl al-ta'til), is that Allah is in the heavens. This is clear. On this basis, whoever claims that Allah's companionship with His creation is a companionship of indwelling and mixing, his statement is refuted by these proofs; every proof that indicates highness indicates the falsehood of the view that companionship means indwelling and mixing. Is this clear?
So on this basis, Allah's companionship with His creation is a companionship befitting His majesty, and He, Exalted is He, is above His Throne, because Allah, Exalted is He, combined the two in one verse: ﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you﴾ [al-Hadid 4]. And any two things that Allah has combined cannot contradict each other.
We have said that whoever says companionship of indwelling and mixing opposes the legislative proofs establishing Allah's highness. Likewise, he does not know the Arabic language, because does the Arabic language require, in the true meaning of companionship, that one thing mix with another, or be incarnate with it in one place, gathered with it in its place?
No, it is not so. A person, for example, says: My wife is with me, while she is in the house and he is in the mosque, is that not so?
* The students: Indeed.
* The Shaykh: And this is true; this is real companionship, although one is in one place and the other in another. Likewise the officer or commander says to the soldiers: Go to the battle, for I am with you. Is it true or not?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: It is true. This word is used truly despite the difference between the two places, or not? Children now quarrel and fight with one another; one of the neighbours' boys comes and says: Come, you are with me, or with him? You are with me, not with him, correct or not?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: It is true, although each one goes home to his house. So companionship in the Arabic language does not require its reality; I mean it does not necessitate, and it does not entail, that it requires the incarnation and mixing of the two things. And I say: does not necessitate, and I do not say does not entail, because it may entail that, as if one said, for example: The water brought me milk with water, that is, mixed with it; and as one says: The soul with the body, that is, mixed with it. This may indeed entail it, but the Arabic language does not require it. For this reason Shaykh al-Islam, may God have mercy on him, said in al-'Aqidah al-Wasitiyyah: The meaning of His saying: ﴿And He is with you﴾ [al-Hadid 4] is not that He is mixed with creation, for the Arabic language does not require this. He said: It does not require it; rather the moon is one of the signs of Allah, among the smallest of His creatures, and it is placed in the heavens, and it is with the traveller and the non-traveller, wherever he is.
So the main point, O people, is do not think that the Qur'an contradicts itself.
* The students: Far be it.
* The Shaykh: And that if it is established that Allah is with us, this does not negate that Allah is in the heavens, for this is not possible. Rather we say: the Qur'an confirms its parts with one another and affirms one another. But among people, may we and you be asked for safety, are those in whose hearts is deviation, who follow what is ambiguous in it seeking discord and seeking its interpretation, and its negation from what Allah intended.
* Student: Shaykh, who among them first said that the companionship's specification contradicts the generality?
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: If we specify and say: the general companionship is a real companionship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and we say: companionship is specific, there is a specific companionship. Does specification contradict generality?
* The Shaykh: No, it does not contradict it. That is, the specific companionship must be believed to be combined with the general companionship; meaning, when it is said ﴿Indeed Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Baqarah 153], ﴿Indeed Allah is with those who are mindful and those who are good-doers﴾ [an-Nahl 128], its meaning is not a specific companionship stripped of the general companionship, for He, Glorified and Exalted, is with these also in knowledge, encompassment and general meaning.
* Student: O Shaykh, and who among them interpreted this matter, meaning said that He is everywhere although He is upon His Throne? He said: If He descends to the lowest heaven while He is upon His Throne, Glorified and Exalted, then perhaps His stopping at this, can one say the Throne is empty or not empty? But if He descends to the lowest heaven, there is no objection that Allah is not like anything?
* The Shaykh: No, no, this is not possible, this is not possible, no, it is not possible. Even descent to the lowest heaven, it is not permissible to say that the second heaven is above it; it is not permissible to say so.
* Student: We say, based on His saying: ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ [ash-Shura 11].
* The Shaykh: No, no, that is not sufficient, because as Shaykh al-Islam said: it is not permissible to rely in establishing attributes on negating resemblance and likeness, because meanings which in themselves contradict the perfection of Allah are not affirmed. Even if we said in a manner not resembling the attributes of created beings, this matter must be paid attention to; that is, not everything we affirm for Allah and say: not in what resembles the attributes of created beings. If it is a deficiency, it is negated from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, absolutely.
If someone said, for example: I affirm that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, becomes tired, not like the tiredness of created beings, for example, what do we say?
* The students: This is wrong.
* The Shaykh: We say: this is wrong. Every attribute of deficiency is not permissible to affirm for Allah absolutely. Then the attributes of perfection which Allah affirmed for Himself are those of which we say: in a manner that does not resemble the attributes of created beings, because it is not sufficient to negate deficiencies from Allah that we affirm for Him the deficiency and then say: "it is not like this," which is prohibited. As for the matter of the Throne being empty of Him if He descends to the lowest heaven, or not being empty: Shaykh al-Islam says that the more correct view is that the Throne is not empty of Him, because highness is established as one of the essential attributes.
Some scholars said: what we should do is remain silent; that is, the matter has three views. One view: that the Throne is empty of Him and He descends to the lowest heaven, in some manner we do not know how He descends; the point is that He, Glorified and Exalted, draws near to His servants by this descent.
The second view: they say: He descends and the Throne is not empty of Him, and Allah is capable of everything, and we do not know its manner.
The third view: suspension, suspending judgment on this entirely, we turn away from all of it with our tongues and hearts, and we say: Allah descends, and He, Glorified and Exalted, does what He wills; because the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did not put to the Prophet ﷺ this question: is the Throne empty of Him or not? So since they did not raise it, we should not raise it either, about ourselves or about others. This is a view with safety in it. But Shaykh al-Islam says that the majority hold that the Throne is not empty of Him, because Allah, Exalted is He, is not like anything.
He said: ﴿Be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Anfal 46]. ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer; indeed Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Baqarah 153].
﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead"﴾ [al-Baqarah 154]. (Lā) is a prohibitive particle, and "taqūlū" is a present-tense verb in the jussive mood after the prohibitive (lā), its sign of jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and the waw is the subject.
﴿for those who are killed﴾, meaning concerning those who are killed, because the one killed is not addressed as anything; he has been killed. But the meaning is concerning those who are killed in the way of Allah.
﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves who recites to you﴾ [al-Baqarah 151].
* It is derived from this noble verse: the explanation of Allah's blessing upon us by sending the Messenger.
I consider whoever comes merely to attend a listener, not a student, and so he does not feel that he came to receive a complete instruction.
