* Student: They gather on Wednesday and wear white robes and wear (...), and they sit for the remembrance: "Allah," I don't know what, they remember Allah, "O Subtle One," a thousand times...
* Shaykh: In any case, they are astray.
* Student: O Shaykh, a person must fight them in this.
* Shaykh: Fight them (...).
* Student: I used to sit with them before, and by Allah, Allah turned to us in repentance, praise be to Allah. Once they caught me after the Maghrib prayer, and I said to them: "What are you doing? Get out! Leave the deception."
* Shaykh: Praise be to Allah. After you were a Sufi, now you are sober.
* Student: By Allah, this really happened to me, the mosque every day...
* Shaykh: Thank your Lord that He rescued you. Praise be to Allah.

From the lessons of the verse: we mentioned that the repentance of the people of innovation, for example, is not complete except with clarification and reform, because of His saying: ﴿except those who repent, amend, and make clear﴾. Three conditions: repentance, returning from what occurred of concealment, and reform of what was corrupted by their concealment. That is, what was corrupted by their concealment, since when they hid the truth, corruption occurred, so reform is necessary. The third is clarification of what? Clarification of the truth. They must clarify with complete clarity. With this, their bad deeds are replaced by good deeds.

* Among the lessons of the noble verse: that every sin, however great, even calling to innovations, if a person repents from it, then Allah, the Exalted, turns to him in forgiveness. Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned that this is one of the distinctive features of this nation: that the one who calls to innovations and disbelief would not have his repentance accepted in previous nations. But if this is authentically reported from the Messenger (ﷺ), then it is to be accepted wholeheartedly, and it specifies the verse. If it is not authentic, then the apparent meaning of the verse is that this ruling is general for this nation and others, and that whoever repents from what he concealed, and reformed, and clarified, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness.

* Among the lessons of the noble verse: affirmation of two of Allah's names: al-Tawwab (the Accepter of repentance) and al-Rahim (the Merciful). Al-Tawwab is toward the one who sins, and al-Rahim is toward the one who is sincere and acts. Mercy brings good, and repentance repels evil. Repentance repels evil, and mercy brings good.

From the noble verse is derived: affirmation of two attributes of Allah. What are they?
* Student: Al-Tawwab.
* Shaykh: No, this is not al-Tawwab. Repentance and mercy.

From them is also derived: affirmation of two rulings from these two names: that Allah accepts repentance and shows mercy. For this reason He said: ﴿those I will turn to in forgiveness﴾.

From this noble verse is derived: linking the cause with the ruling, because He said: ﴿those I will turn to in forgiveness﴾, then He gave the reason for that by saying: ﴿and I am the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful﴾.

Also among the lessons of the noble verse: the frequency of Allah's acceptance of repentance, the Mighty and Majestic, the frequency of repentance from Allah, because His saying: ﴿al-Tawwab﴾?
* Student: It is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 158–164 (part 5 of 9):

* The Shaykh: It is an intensive form (sigha mubalaghah) indicating abundance: the abundance of Allah's acceptance of repentance, and the abundance of those whom Allah accepts in repentance.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers – upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together.﴾ We seek refuge in Allah. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ – in whom? In everything that must be believed in.

From this noble verse it is derived that the disbeliever deserves the curse of Allah, of the angels, and of all mankind; the curse is laid upon them.

It is also derived from this noble verse that for this ruling to apply, one must die in disbelief, since He says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers﴾. So if they disbelieve and then return from disbelief to Islam, this ruling is lifted from them.

It is also derived from the noble verse: the affirmation of the angels, since He says: ﴿and the angels﴾. The angels are part of the unseen world, from the world of the unseen; yet they sometimes appear. They are servants, not lords, and they are not children of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Rather, they are created among the creatures; Allah created them only for worship, and therefore they do not disobey Allah: ﴿They do not disdain His worship, nor do they tire. They glorify Him night and day, never slackening﴾ [al-Anbiya' 19–20]. They have will, and they have intellect, unlike the one who said they have no intellects. To the one who says they have no intellects, we say: it is you who lack intellect. As for the angels, they have will, intellect, and understanding; they understand His command from Allah and glorify Him with His praise. How could they have no intellects?! We say: if we took this claim to its necessary consequence, the sharia would be nullified, because who is the envoy between Allah and His messengers?

* The students: Jibril.

* The Shaykh: Jibril. So if we say he has no intellect, the bearer of the message becomes insane, and who trusts the message of a bearer who is insane? Thus all the sharia would be nullified, all of it. Therefore this claim, in reality, if it were said to be disbelief, would have a basis; if it were said that this claim is disbelief, it would have a basis.

Are the angels bodies or spirits?

* A student: Spirits.

* The Shaykh: Bodies without doubt, and they have spirits; for as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Who made the angels messengers having wings﴾ [Fatir 1]. And the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril in his own form in which he was created, and he had six hundred wings, which blocked the horizon.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the disbeliever is cursed by the disbeliever. The disbeliever is cursed by the disbeliever. From where do we take this?

* The students: ﴿and mankind, all together﴾.

* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿and mankind, all together﴾ – ﴿upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together﴾. And Allah the Exalted has informed about the people of the Fire that ﴿every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ [al-A'raf 38], and He informed: ﴿when those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment﴾ [al-Baqarah 166], to the end. So the disbeliever – we seek refuge in Allah – is cursed even by those who shared his disbelief (...).

﴿Abiding therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾

It is derived from this verse: those who die while disbelievers are eternally in the curse – we seek refuge in Allah – eternally in the curse of Allah, His rejection, and His distancing from His mercy.

It is also derived from it: the punishment is not lightened for them, not even for one day? Not even for one day. For this reason the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment"﴾ [Ghafir 49]. They did not ask that the punishment be lifted, nor did they ask that it be lightened permanently; they asked that it be lightened even for one day out of the endless ages – we seek refuge in Allah, and we ask Allah to protect us and you from the Fire. They wish for this and seek means through the angels, or through the angels to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, that He lighten the punishment for them for one day. But they are rebuked when they ask this: ﴿They said, "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?" They said, "Yes"﴾ [Ghafir 50]. Consider the great regret when they are told these words: ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?﴾ And what regret arises in their hearts? No one can imagine it. How? "If only we had done it, if only we had followed the messengers, if only we had believed, if only we had followed the Messenger." They wish; therefore they say: ﴿Yes﴾; they can never deny it. ﴿They said, "Then you supplicate"﴾ – you yourselves – ﴿but the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾ [Ghafir 50], in loss – we seek refuge in Allah. The point is that the punishment is not lightened for them.

* Among its benefits: they are not given respite, whether it is from "naẓar" (to look) or from "inẓar" (to grant respite); they are not given a delay even for one hour. For this reason: ﴿until, when they come to it, its gates will be opened﴾ [al-Zumar 71] – from the day they come to it, it is opened. The people of Paradise: ﴿when they come to it, and its gates have been opened﴾ [al-Zumar 73], because they do not enter it except by intercession and after retribution has been taken from some of them for others. When they come to it, they have been purified and cleansed; then the Prophet ﷺ intercedes for their entry into Paradise, and at that time ﴿its gates have been opened﴾ [al-Zumar 73]. For this reason the waw appears with the people of Paradise and not the people of the Fire – we seek refuge in Allah – for the people of the Fire are seized by the punishment unexpectedly. We ask Allah for well-being.

* A student: Is it understood from this that one curses the disbeliever when he dies..

* The Shaykh: When he dies upon his disbelief? We say: it may be permissible, but the hadith indicates that it is not permissible: «Do not revile the dead»[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (1393) from the hadith of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her).]]. And what is the benefit of cursing the disbeliever? In a general way it is permissible; you say: "O Allah, curse the disbelievers." 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) and Abu Hurayrah used to curse the disbelievers in the qunut[[The hadith of 'Umar is recorded by 'Abd al-Razzaq (4969); the hadith of Abu Hurayrah is agreed upon: al-Bukhari (797) and Muslim (676 / 296).]]: "O Allah, curse the disbelieving infidels." This is not objectionable, and these verses may be in a general sense: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers – upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together﴾ [al-Baqarah 161] – in a general sense: "O Allah, curse every disbeliever; O Allah, curse whoever conceals knowledge," and the like.

* A student: Regarding the human being (...).

* The Shaykh: ﴿One God﴾ [al-Baqarah 163] – the address is to all of mankind. ﴿And your God﴾ – O people, O humanity – that is, your true object of worship, whose worship is truly one: one God. "God" in the sense of "mahluh" (one who is worshipped), so it has the sense of the passive participle; and the mahluh means the one worshipped with love and veneration. This is the one who is worshipped with love and veneration, and who deserves worship: one God only, no more. This sentence ﴿And your God is one God﴾ has a first part that is definite and a second part that is indefinite and qualified, and it is emphasized by oneness: ﴿One God﴾, meaning: there is no god with Him. Then He emphasized this nominal sentence with a sentence that conveys restriction, saying: ﴿There is no god but He﴾. The position of this sentence in relation to what precedes it, in meaning, is what? It is emphasis (tawkid); tawkid is more eloquent than ta'kid; as the Exalted said: ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ [al-Nahl 91].

﴿There is no god but He﴾: the grammatical analysis of ﴿There is no god but He﴾ has already been presented to us, and that the correct analysis is: "lā" is a negation of the category (lā nāfiyah lil-jins), and "ilāh" is its noun, built on the fatha in a position of nasb, and its predicate is omitted, its estimate being: "there is no true god." As for one who said the estimate is: "there is no existing god," this is open to scrutiny, because there exist other gods besides Allah but they are false; unless he means that "ilāh" is qualified by an omitted adjective, estimated as: "there is no god truly existing," and if he intended this, it returns to the second opinion we estimated, which is that the predicate is omitted and its estimate is: "true." As for one who says in explaining it: "there is nothing existing but Allah," as Mustafa Mahmud said – the one who filled the horizons with speech in the media, and many people were impressed by him – this explains "lā ilāha illā Allāh" as: "there is nothing existing but Allah." This fully matches the interpretation of the people of the unity of being (wahdat al-wujud), who say that the Creator and the created are one thing; for if he says "there is nothing existing but Allah," it means creation is identical to the Creator, since there is nothing existing but Allah. From this we see that one must be wary of this man, especially when he speaks on matters of divinity (ilahiyyat). In his speech on divinity there is a great danger in taking his word. As for matters of the cosmos, he may err or be correct; but in matters of divinity, one must beware of him, because a man who explains the statement of tawhid by the notion of incarnation (hulul) and union (ittihad) is among the furthest of people from tawhid..

* A student: He did not state this explicitly in his books.

* The Shaykh: It is in his books; I have read it, I read it in his book "Muhawalat tafsir al-Quran bil-mafhum al-'asri" (An Attempt to Interpret the Qur'an by Modern Understanding); this is its title or the meaning of the title.

* A student: "The Qur'an: an attempt.."

* The Shaykh: Yes. So ﴿There is no god but He﴾ – we said the predicate of "lā" is omitted, and the estimate is "true." We estimated this because there are gods worshipped besides Allah, which He called gods, but they do not have – what do they not have? – a right to divinity. For this reason Allah called them in another verse: ﴿They are only names you have named﴾ [al-Najm 23], meaning: names without a reality for what they name.

We said: some grammarians and some scholars also estimated it, estimating the predicate with the word "existing," and this estimate does not match reality unless he means that the noun of "lā" is qualified by an omitted adjective, estimated as "truly": this is correct; "there is no god truly existing but Allah" is true. "Illā" is a particle of restriction; "huwa" (He) in "lā ilāha illā huwa" is a substitute for the omitted predicate, built on the fatha in a position of raf'. As for "illā Allāhu," it is a substitute in the nominative, and its sign of raf' is?

* A student: The apparent damma.

* The Shaykh: The apparent damma at its end. And you see us saying here it is built on the fatha, and there we say it is nominative by the damma? Because this is a pronoun and therefore built, while this is an apparent noun and therefore inflected.

And His saying: ﴿There is no god but He﴾ is a statement that we must believe; for if we did not believe it we would be deniers of this report, and denying the report of Allah and His Messenger is disbelief, clear disbelief. Therefore we must believe that there is no true god but Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and that everything worshipped besides Allah is false, because it neither benefits nor harms: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are unaware of their supplication﴾ [al-Ahqaf 5]. These idols, even if you call upon them until the Day of Resurrection, would not respond to you: ﴿If you call them, they do not hear your call; and if they heard, they would not respond to you; and on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association, and none can inform you like the One who is Acquainted﴾ [Fatir 14].

If someone says: these polytheists may be tested by these gods, so they call upon them and then what they called for comes to them? What is the answer to this verse? The answer: they are not the ones who brought it into existence, and Allah said: ﴿one who will not respond to him﴾ [al-Ahqaf 5]. Did these idols bring about that thing, or did Allah bring it?

* A student: Allah.

* The Shaykh: Allah brought it. But a person may be tested by the facilitation of the means of sin, a trial from Allah the Mighty and Majestic; so would this thing have come about for him?

* A student: No, by it.

* The Shaykh: No, by it: it came about for him, not by it.

﴿There is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾. His saying ﴿al-Rahman﴾ – what is its grammatical analysis?

* A student: It is the predicate of an omitted subject.

* The Shaykh: The predicate of an omitted subject; the estimate is? "He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." The sentence is resumptive: ﴿He is al-Rahman﴾, meaning: this God is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and whatever else is worshipped besides Him has no mercy in it at all; it is entirely devoid of mercy.

Regarding His saying ﴿al-Rahman al-Rahim﴾, Ibn Hajar said: the scholars agree that both are names of Allah. They agreed, even though their root is one, which is mercy. On this basis, "al-Ghafur" is a name, and "al-Ghaffar" is a name, though both derive from forgiveness; but since they differ in form, each became an independent name.

Regarding His saying ﴿al-Rahman al-Rahim﴾, the difference between them: the best I have seen on this is what Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his book "Bada'i' al-Fawa'id." The book "Bada'i' al-Fawa'id" is named for its title "bada'i'," but it is not arranged; he wrote whatever came to his mind, may Allah have mercy on him. It most resembles the book of Ibn al-Jawzi named "Sayd al-Khatir" (The Hunting of Thoughts): whenever a thing occurred to his mind, he wrote it down. Though there is a difference between them, Ibn al-Jawzi, may Allah have mercy on him, is inconsistent in the chapter on the attributes. He has a book named "Ta'wil Ayat al-Sifat" (Interpretation of the Verses of the Attributes), entirely according to the Mu'tazilah school; he denounces the affirmers with severe denunciation, to the extent that in some contexts he curses them – we seek refuge in Allah – he curses them, saying: how can you make for Allah an eye, a hand, and the like? Meaning you have made Him a human being. He openly expresses great denunciation in this. I saw that our Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote a commentary on this book, on the page where the book's title appears, saying: this is Ibn al-Jawzi's speech in which he opposed the school of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Yes indeed. The upshot is that we mentioned him because Ibn al-Jawzi, may Allah have mercy on him, has statements indicating that he is upright in this chapter; but this book he composed for this very purpose and refuted the affirmers with a grievous refutation.

So "al-Rahman" – I say: the best I have seen regarding the difference between them is that "al-Rahman" is considered with respect to description (wasf), while "al-Rahim" is considered with respect to action (fi'l). For this reason "Rahman" came in the pattern "fa'lan," which indicates vastness and fullness, and "Rahim" came in the attribute pattern "fa'il," which indicates action: so "al-Rahman" is with respect to His attribute, and "al-Rahim" with respect to His action, that is, the conveying of mercy to whomever He wills, glory be to Him and exalted is He. We have previously mentioned many times that the names of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, have three indications: they indicate by inclusion (dalalat al-tadammun); and what else?

* The students: Implication (iltizam).

* The Shaykh: And implication; and the third?

* The students: Correspondence (mutabaqah).

* The Shaykh: Correspondence. So the indication of the name upon the essence and the attribute together is what? Correspondence. And its indication upon the essence alone, or the attribute alone? Inclusion. And its indication upon what it entails of other attributes? Implication. Who will ask?

* A student: ﴿al-Rahman al-Rahim﴾ – what prevents it from being an adjective?

* The Shaykh: Which of them?

* The student: ﴿al-Rahman al-Rahim﴾.

* The Shaykh: Yes, both indicate mercy.

* The student: No, I mean an adjective grammatically?

* The Shaykh: Grammatically, an adjective of what?

* The student: An adjective of the pronoun?

* The Shaykh: They say that the pronoun is neither described nor described by.

* The student: What is the obstacle?

* The Shaykh: That is their statement.

* The student: If we consider it semantically, it is indeed an adjective?

* The Shaykh: If you say: "there is no god but the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate"? The speech would not be sound. "There is no god but He," then he resumed and said, "He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate": this is more eloquent; this is more eloquent, and although the other is permissible, it is on a weak basis.

We have remained with ﴿al-Rahman al-Rahim﴾. The people of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah affirm mercy for Allah the Mighty and Majestic as a real attribute, while the people of ta'wil say that Allah does not have a mercy which is an attribute of His, and they interpret mercy either as an action or as a will, meaning either as beneficence or as the will to be beneficent. This is the doctrine of the Ash'ariyyah and the Maturidiyyah, who say that the meaning of "Rahman" and the meaning of "Rahim" is: one who wills beneficence, or its meaning is: one who is beneficent in action. And what is their argument? They say: because mercy is tenderness and softness, and this attribute does not befit Allah the Mighty and Majestic. So we say to them in refutation of this:

Firstly: that mercy entails tenderness and softness is with respect to the mercy of the created; then even if it were supposed to entail that, where is the evidence that it is impossible for Allah the Mighty and Majestic to be gentle, compassionate, and merciful?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 158–164 (part 6 of 9):

There is no textual evidence prohibiting this. Nevertheless we say: if this does not befit the Lord, the Exalted, then the mercy you refer to is the mercy of the created being, whereas the mercy of the Creator befits Him and does not entail deficiency as the mercy of the created being does. Moreover, we said earlier that your claim, that mercy entails softness, tenderness and weakness, is not correct. Kings may be mighty, strong and severe, and yet show mercy, and it is not said that they were humbled or weakened before the one they showed mercy to.

Then we say to them: if you say that, then will (irada) is such that the one who wills wills nothing except for what brings him benefit or repels harm for him. This is the rational willer, meaning he wills nothing except that. Does this meaning befit Allah? It does not befit Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They say: this is the will of the created being, which wills only what brings him benefit or repels harm, but the will of the Creator befits Him. We say: then this is the mercy of the created being, and the mercy of the Creator befits Him.

Then it is strange that the texts on mercy in the Qur'an are more numerous than the texts on will. They come as an attribute, they come as a name, and they come as a verb, whereas will comes only as a verb. Is that not so?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And your Lord is the Forgiving, Possessor of mercy﴾ [al-Kahf 58]. This is an attribute. He says: ﴿The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾. This is a name. He says: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills﴾ [al-'Ankabut 21]. This is a verb. And yet these are interpreted away, while will is not interpreted away!

But, praise be to Allah, the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), may Allah guide them to the straight path, treated the entire category of the attributes as one category. How one category? Allah is described by what He described Himself with, and by what His Messenger ﷺ described Him with, without distortion (tahrif), without negation (ta'til), without modality (takyif), and without likening (tamthil). It is said: the description of the Creator befits Him, and the description of the created being befits it, and although they agree in the basic meaning, the reality of the meaning differs. Is that clear? And this, praise be to Allah, is established for us in creed, and has come before us many times.
* A student: Shaykh, some scholars explained ﴿Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim﴾ as two soft (raqiqan) names. If we return to the correct creed, should we understand that they mean two names, one of which is gentler (arfaq) than the other, because he holds the view that Allah is gentle (rafiq) and loves gentleness?
* The Shaykh: No, no, they do not mean this. They say "raqiqan," meaning each of them is more tender than the second.
* The student: We did not take into account that some scholars have sound and good creed and (...) gentle.
* The Shaykh: Yes, they say so.
* A student: Shaykh, if someone asks: what is the difference between the school of the People of the Sunnah and the Community and the school of the Mufawwidah (those who delegate meaning), if the People of the Sunnah affirm the attribute of mercy for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with a meaning other than the meaning found in the dictionary, because that meaning of tenderness befits the created being? Likewise, they say "Ar-Rahman," but the meaning of "Ar-Rahman" is other than what is known to them. So what is the difference between them?
* The Shaykh: The difference between them is that the Mufawwidah say: we do not know a meaning for this, we do not affirm any meaning at all. It is not only mercy: mercy, and istiwa' (settling), and nuzul (descending), and forgiveness, and love, and others, they affirm no meaning at all. They say: their meanings are unknown. There is no doubt that this is greatly harmful.
* The student: There is no meaning to the Qur'an?
* The Shaykh: Its meaning is: there is no meaning from the Qur'an. As Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah) said: the interpreter (al-mutawwil) comes, and the philosophers come and say: go away, you are ignorant, you do not know; we are the ones with knowledge. The interpreter comes and says: I have knowledge; the philosopher comes and says: I have knowledge. I am the one who (...) the Qur'an. But you have admitted your own ignorance. Can an ignorant person repel anything? He cannot repel anything. Therefore he (may Allah have mercy on him) says in his book Al-'Aql wal-Naql: this statement is among the worst statements of the people of innovation and heresy, the delegation of meaning (tafwid al-ma'na). As for delegating the modality (tafwid al-kayfiyyah), this is true: however much we are unable to know the modality of Allah's attributes, the Mighty and Majestic.
* A student: Shaykh, if someone comes forward and does not investigate the explanation of ﴿Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim﴾ (...), he does not know whether it is "rafiqan" or "raqiqan," on what do we carry it?
* The Shaykh: The known position is that they say "raqiqan," one of them is more tender than the other; this is how they express it. "Arraq" (more tender) is not confused with "arfaq" (more gentle).
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It does not contradict if he says "rafiqan" without pointing, then says "one of them is more tender," which is confused with "more gentle"? It is not confused, (...) "arraq" means "arraf," and that does not hold.
* A student: Ar-Rahman indicates the name and the attribute. The name Ar-Rahman. What is the benefit of Ar-Rahim?
* The Shaykh: Yes, good. Ar-Rahim indicates Him according to the form, and Ar-Rahman according to the necessary implication (iltizam). Or it is said: in such a case, when one is paired with the other, one of them indicates the name and attribute only, and the second indicates the name, the attribute and the act. There is no objection to a word having one meaning when alone and another meaning when combined.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens﴾. Pay attention to this verse, if we are people of intellect, because the verse ends with: ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. ﴿Indeed (inna)﴾ is for emphasis, ﴿in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ is its predicate, fronted, and ﴿signs (ayat)﴾ is its subject, postponed.

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾: their origin, their modality, their strength, what Allah deposited in them, and so on. This is one. ﴿The heavens (as-samawat)﴾ is the plural of "sama'," and it has already been mentioned that they are seven. ﴿And the earth (al-ardi)﴾ is singular, intended as a genus, and so it includes?
* The students: The seven.
* The Shaykh: It includes the seven. ﴿In the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾: this is one, their bringing into being, their continuance, and their modality, and everything connected to them which we do not know. Others, for example astronomers and geologists, know more than we know about this, and yet they have been given only a little knowledge. The heaven in its creation, with this height, this vastness and this strength: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength (bi-aydin)﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 47], meaning with power. ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾ [an-Nazi'at 27]. The answer?
* A student: The heaven.
* The Shaykh: The heaven. Then He elaborated, saying: ﴿He raised its structure and made it level﴾ [an-Nazi'at 27–28]. ﴿And We built above you seven strong ones﴾ [an-Naba' 12]. This is the great heaven. Likewise the earth, and what Allah deposited in it of benefits, in that He made it comprise and include everything that creation needs in its life and after its death, even after death: ﴿Did We not make the earth a container, for the living and the dead?﴾ [al-Mursalat 25–26]. Consider: what if Allah made this earth transparent like glass, so that the dead were buried in it and the living looked at the dead, and it would not be a container for them? And consider: what if Allah made this earth hard like iron or harder, would it be easy for us for it to be a container for our dead? No, nor for us in our lives. Then in this earth Allah deposited benefits and minerals that we cannot encompass, and they become clear to us little by little as industry advances. These heavens and earth, what Allah deposited in them of benefits and interests.

Second: ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾: the alternation of night and day in length and shortness, in light and darkness, in heat and cold, in victory and defeat, in everything connected to night and day. ﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 140]. These nights and days that revolve over the world: how many people have perished in them, how many have been honored in them, how many have been humbled in them, how many events have occurred in them that none knows except Allah. All this alternation is signs indicating Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His singularity in oneness, glory be to Him and exalted.

The alternation of night and day also in length and shortness: ﴿He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night﴾ [al-Hajj 61], in a hidden manner that people do not perceive: it increases little by little and decreases little by little. The sun does not rise suddenly from the Tropic of Cancer and the very next day from the Tropic of Capricorn. No, it moves between them little by little, until harmony and balance and the absence of catastrophes occur. If it moved suddenly from the Tropic of Cancer to the Tropic of Capricorn, what would happen? People would perish from intense heat to intense cold, and the reverse. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His wisdom and mercy made it move so that night and day alternate according to what His wisdom and mercy require.

﴿And the ships that run in the sea with that which benefits people﴾. Allahu akbar! This too is among the signs of Allah: a ship loaded with human beings, goods and provisions, running on the surface of the water. This is one of the signs of Allah. And there has come what is greater than it now, which is the vessel that runs in the air. The vessel that runs in the air. When Allah, may He be exalted, points to something of His signs in a matter, what is more fitting than it is greater in indicating that. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has informed us that the birds in the sky's atmosphere contain signs, has He not? Yes indeed: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Mulk 19]. These birds carry nothing but themselves, so Allah made them a sign. How then about these aircraft? They are greater and greater among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

And His saying: ﴿and the ships that run in the sea﴾. ﴿Tajri (run)﴾ means? It moves. And ﴿fi al-bahr (in the sea)﴾: "fi" is for location. Does the meaning mean within the sea itself, or upon the sea?
* A student: It includes them.
* The Shaykh: It includes this and that, yes. Because there is a vessel that runs on the surface of the water, and there is a vessel that runs beneath the water, is that not so?
* A student: Submarines.
* The Shaykh: Submarines. Submarines run in the sea with that which benefits people, because enemies are fought with them and the lands are protected with them. This is among what benefits people.
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, ﴿until when you are in the ships and they sail with them﴾ [Yunus 22]. So ﴿al-fulk (the ship)﴾ here is intended as plural. ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ [as-Saffat 140]: this is singular. I think I have mentioned to you what Ibn 'Aqil (may Allah have mercy on him), who was one of the jurists, said: the hunchback whose hump is like one bowing intends the bowing (ruku') in his heart. He said: like (fulk) in Arabic, one intends its plurality or its singularity while the wording is one. This hunchbacked person, if he wishes to bow while he is hunched, to the extent of bowing, how does he bow?
* A student: By intention.
* The Shaykh: By intention, yes. ﴿Al-fulk (the ship)﴾ covers both singular and plural. Here is it intended as plural or singular? ﴿And the ships that run in the sea﴾?
* A student: It is possible (both).
* The Shaykh: My brothers, we said that the descriptive term specifies the intended meaning. ﴿And the ships that run in the sea﴾?
* A student: Singular.
* The Shaykh: Singular? If he said "wal-fulku allati yajrina fi al-bahr" (the ships which they run in the sea), would it be?
* A student: Plural.
* The Shaykh: Plural, or not?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Ibn Malik says in the Alfiyya:
"With al-lat and al-la', which have been pluralized..." (...)
"Al-lati" is the singular. Therefore here al-fulk is singular, but it is singular intended as a genus, so it is general.

And His saying: ﴿runs in the sea with that which benefits people﴾. The "ba'" here is for accompaniment, meaning accompanied by what benefits people. From where?
* A student: The provisions.
* The Shaykh: From the provisions, the merchandise, the persons, the treasures, and others.
* A student: And hunting, fishing.
* The Shaykh: Yes, and others: with what benefits. Because "ma" is a relative pronoun that conveys generality: everything that benefits people. These are among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, indicating the perfection of His power, the perfection of His mercy, and His subjugation of things, as He said in another verse: ﴿And He subjected to you the ships to sail through the sea by His command, and He subjected to you the rivers﴾ [Ibrahim 32].

And from the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is that He ordained in the earth its sustenance. ﴿Qaddara (ordained)﴾ means: He made measure here, measure there, and measure here, so that people benefit. There are people among whom vegetables and greens and the like are not abundant; they are brought to them from another land. And there are people among whom a certain kind of plant is abundant, which is not found in another place, and it is transported to the other place. Thus people exchange provisions, benefit, and move about, each in what has been ordained for him.
* A student: Shaykh, submarines travelling a long distance under the water?
* The Shaykh: Yes, under the water.
* The student: How is it guided?
* The Shaykh: They have, may Allah keep you safe, radars that do not miss. Now they say there are missiles, where one sits in his place in the command room and strikes the target he wants. Now they have begun, God willing He spares us their evil, to arm the air; that is why they are in dispute over arming the air. They have finished arming the land and mining it with submarines and others, and they said: we will go just...
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, before the power of Allah.
* The student: (...) the Afghans are weak and few, or does he not have equipment...
* The Shaykh: Before the power of Allah there is nothing, because if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, willed, He would cause the earth to swallow them, and no trace of them would remain. Before the power of Allah there is nothing. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made His power conditional: ﴿If you support Allah, He will support you﴾ [Muhammad 7]. So when this condition is met, and we support Allah truly with our hearts, tongues and limbs, He supports us, as He supported those before us, may He be exalted. The matter is: our words are many and our deeds are few.
* A student: Someone spoke to us and said: they sent atomic bombs against them...
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: Atomic bombs. In (...) Afghanistan he says: they reached the tents' area, they did not reach the tents, and it took twelve days with the fire blazing and not ceasing, he says: by Allah, nothing came from them to anyone?
* The Shaykh: In any case, the reports about them are many. But we do not want time to pass. A trustworthy person told me two days ago, he came to me consulting me about the matter of jihad with them. He says: there are mountains where they wear out the fighters in bringing water up to these mountains; one carries the jugs with exhaustion and climbs this mountain, and they dig trenches so that when the planes come they strike them. They overturn all the planes. He says: there are planes that have begun to send bombs upon them; when the bomb strikes the ground, the ground bursts into springs. They began digging wells for them and they did not know it. This is Allah's power over all things. This is among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His support. We ask Allah to support them and make them firm upon the truth.
* A student: Ibn 'Aqil's statement about the hunchback (...): if he is hunchbacked, is intention sufficient?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it suffices.
* The student: Is it not required that he (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, no, it is not required, because it would then be contrary to the Sunnah in the form of bowing.
* The student: This one is incapable, and Allah says: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [at-Taghabun 16].
* The Shaykh: This is from the fear of Allah.
* The student: He did not bow.
* The Shaykh: His form is that of one bowing. They said it this way.
* The student: Does the form not differ between bowing and standing?
* The Shaykh: It is not a condition; intention suffices, like sitting, but he cannot move. Like the person who cannot move his head and intends it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: We do not know; we cannot affirm this, because we cannot say that the lowest heaven is of copper...
* The student: Because he did not say "and the earths."
* The Shaykh: We cannot. The earths are mentioned in the Sunnah: «He will be encircled with it from seven earths» [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (2452), and Muslim (1610/137), from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him.]
* The student: No, regarding the Qur'an.

**Shaykh:** Regarding the Qur'an, we cannot say that God mentioned the heavens in the plural because they are greater than the earth; rather, ﴿and of the earth, the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq 65:12] is in the same number.

**Student:** What is your view, Shaykh, on the opinion of those who say: when "the heavens" (al-samawat) is used in the plural, it refers to the celestial bodies, and when "the heaven" (al-sama') is used in the singular, it refers to height?

**Shaykh:** This is correct. When "the heavens" (al-samawat) is said, it undoubtedly refers to the celestial bodies. When "the heaven" (al-sama') is said, it may bear both meanings.

He said: ﴿And what God sent down from the heaven of water﴾. That is, "and in what God sent down from the heaven of water." ﴿sent down from the heaven﴾: here "heaven" means height. This is the correct view, although some have mentioned that it may refer to the celestial body, the protected heaven, and said that water descends from the heaven onto the clouds and then descends from the clouds onto the earth. But this contradicts reality and what the Qur'an indicates. The correct view is that "the heaven" here means height: ﴿And what God sent down from the heaven﴾. His words ﴿of water﴾ explain the word "what" in ﴿And what God sent down﴾. The word ﴿water﴾ here means rain. In what God sends down from the heaven there are great signs. Among them: that it descends from the heaven. What raised it up to the heaven? God, Mighty and Majestic. Likewise, that it descends as a light drizzle is one of the signs of God indicating His mercy. Had it descended in torrents, it would have destroyed the world. But it descends as a drizzle. And that it descends from the heaven and does not flow from the earth is also one of the signs of God, so that the plains of the earth and its mountains, its plains and its mountains, may benefit from it. Had it flowed like a current, the lower places would have been flooded before it reached the higher ones.

Likewise, among the signs of God: that it descends neither hot nor cold. Is that not so?

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** Hail comes upon us. God Most High mentioned hail in a context indicating that it is a form of punishment: ﴿And He sends down from the heaven mountains containing hail, and strikes with it whom He wills and turns it away from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight﴾ [al-Nur 24:43]. Although God, Glorified and Exalted, has made it a mercy, nevertheless (...).

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. It has been mentioned that "inna" (إن) has a subject and a predicate. Where is its predicate?

**Student:** ﴿in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ is fronted.

**Shaykh:** Yes, and what is conjoined to it.

**Student:** And its subject: ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾.

**Shaykh:** ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾.

God's words: ﴿in the creation of the heavens﴾, ﴿are signs﴾. Is "signs" (ayat) plural here? Is it that each individual of these kinds that God enumerated contains signs, each one of them having signs? Or are the signs distributed over each kind, so that each kind has a sign, and thus there are signs in all of them?

**Student:** It includes both.

**Shaykh:** Which of them is more eloquent?

**Student:** The more eloquent is that there are signs in everything.

**Shaykh:** Only one sign?

**Student:** Multiple signs.

**Shaykh:** Multiple signs, yes.

His words: ﴿in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. Show us three signs from this, ﴿in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. Explain to us three signs ﴿in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾.

**Student:** First: in their strength.

**Shaykh:** Yes, in their strength.

**Student:** Second: in their vastness.

**Shaykh:** In their expanse.

**Student:** And what God placed in them of stars.

**Shaykh:** Yes. What is the evidence that vastness is a sign of God, and that it is from God's power?

**Student:** And the earth, He spread it out.

**Shaykh:** No, no. The heaven?

**Student:** ﴿And the heaven We built with might, and indeed We are expanding it﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:47].

**Shaykh:** Yes. ﴿with might﴾ means strength, and ﴿expanding﴾ means the vastness of its expanses. Likewise, what God deposited in them of stars, planets, orbits and other things. And in the earth also: in God's bringing the earth into being, subjecting it, making it submissive, and what is in it of rivers, trees, mountains, plains and other things. All of these are signs of God.

**Student:** (...)?

**Shaykh:** No, no, it means "with strength." It is not "ayd" as the plural of "yad" (hand). No, because it is not attributed to God. It is a verbal noun from (ʾāda, yaʾīdu, ʾayadan), like (bāʿa, yabīʿu, bayʿan).

﴿and the alternation of night and day﴾. The alternation of night and day contains signs. From what standpoint does the alternation occur?

**Student:** From its signs is its alternation in length and shortness, and in coolness...

**Shaykh:** The entry of this into that?

**Student:** (...) its length in some regions (...).

**Shaykh:** This falls under length and shortness.

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** Does not the alternation of events fall under this? The alternation of events: that God honors some peoples and humiliates others, and that there is abundance and prosperity, or the opposite?

**Student:** It falls under it.

**Shaykh:** ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the other people. And those days We alternate among the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:140]. And the alternation of night and day...

**Student:** Prayer also differs at night and in the day?

**Shaykh:** No, it does not differ.

﴿and the ship that runs in the sea with that which benefits people﴾. We want to hold you accountable for your statement that each one contains signs. We want at least three signs from each one. ﴿the ships that run in the sea with that which benefits people﴾. Bring out for us three signs from it.

**Student:** Its running upon the surface of the sea, and in this age especially also...

**Shaykh:** We have not yet reached this age. Its running upon the surface of the sea, although it is water and the ship is heavy.

**Student:** That its floating upon the surface of the water is one of the signs. And second: transporting goods that are found in one place to a place where these goods are not found. The ships are what...

**Shaykh:** They are what carry them.

**Student:** (...) that dive inside the water.

**Shaykh:** (...).

**Student:** What is in the sea of great routes.

**Shaykh:** That is in the sea itself, but the reaching of what is in the sea by means of these ships, because they hunt in them.

**Student:** Is this not ancient, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** (...).

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** I do not recall that it is ancient.

**Student:** Collision at sea.

**Shaykh:** Yes, in ordinary ships, the sailing ones.

**Student:** I say: it is among the signs.

**Shaykh:** Yes, but this is from (...).

**Student:** (...) the ship, meaning that it is used for the schemes of enemies...

**Shaykh:** Yes, its use in wars, and also the transporting of people. A person may have a purpose in moving from one continent to another, or from one place to another. This too is among the signs.

**Student:** Knowing the directions.

**Shaykh:** The directing of the winds, besides that, has its own signs.

**Student:** Its moving on the sea (...).

**Shaykh:** By the wind, meaning? Yes. Then praise be to God. ﴿and the ship that runs in the sea with that which benefits people﴾; also its being with what benefits people. The benefits for people are without limit.

﴿And what God sent down from the heaven of water, and He gave life thereby to the earth after its death﴾. This too contains signs: God's sending down of water from the heaven.

**Student:** He sent down the water from the heaven in drops and not...

**Shaykh:** Not pouring. That is one.

**Student:** When water descends (...) it lives, and man lives.

**Shaykh:** The giving of life to the earth by it. But the giving of life to the earth, it is apparent that the very giving of life to the earth contains signs. The sending down of rain as a drizzle is one of God's signs. Notice that what we intend by God's signs is not only the signs indicating power and greatness, but also those indicating mercy and those indicating wisdom. They are all signs of God, are they not? Yes.

**Student:** Its storage in the depths of the earth.

**Shaykh:** Its storage in the depths of the earth, so that when people need it, ﴿He makes it flow as springs in the earth﴾ [al-Zumar 39:21]. They extract it and benefit from it.

**Student:** And the lifting of drought from the people.

**Shaykh:** Yes. Does it not enter into His words: ﴿and He gave life thereby to the earth after its death﴾?

**Student:** It is the giving of life to the earth, and this is the giving of life to what is upon it. This is the giving of life to what is on the earth.

**Another student:** That it descends from above.

**Shaykh:** Yes, that it descends from above and not from below. This too is among the signs of God, for if it moved along the earth it would flood the lower places before it reached the higher ones.

**Student:** That it is sweet (...).

**Shaykh:** Yes, that it has this sweetness, and that it is neither cold nor hot. It is not cold to the point of affecting vegetation, nor hot.

**Student:** That it is evaporated from the earth through the sun, then descends.

**Shaykh:** That it is what?

**Student:** That it is evaporated (intatah) through the sun, it vaporizes, then coheres, then descends. These are among the great signs.

**Shaykh:** That is, that it rises from the sea?

**Student:** Yes, then it forms as a drizzle, then...

**Shaykh:** This may be accepted, and it may not be accepted.

**Student:** Is it among the signs of God, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** Yes, it is among the signs of God, but it is not all (...). Sometimes it is so, and sometimes it is not.

**Student:** Then what other than this is it by which clouds form?

**Shaykh:** God knows best; by His saying "Be." That is why, for instance, we here in al-Qasim, where there are no seas around us, see the sky clear, and we see with our own eyes a small piece form, then spread out.

**Student:** Is the basic principle that it comes by evaporation, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** God knows best. We do not assert it with certainty.

**Student:** That it descends in a specific measure; if it descended in abundance it would drown...

**Shaykh:** Yes. The point now is that we have taken three signs from it.

And His words: ﴿and He gave life thereby to the earth after its death﴾. ﴿gave life thereby to the earth﴾. What is it that is made alive: is it the earth, or the plants in it? What is made alive is the plants in it. That is why God Most High said in another verse: ﴿and the earth becomes green﴾ [al-Hajj 22:63]. Those who claim that the Qur'an contains metaphor (majaz) may say: this is metaphor, since the life of the earth is attributed to the life of its vegetation. We respond to them by saying: this style in the Arabic language is by no means meant to refer to the life of sand, dust and stones. Rather, what is meant by it is...?

**Student:** The life of (...).

**Shaykh:** The fruits and crops that are in it. And since this is the meaning of this construction in the Arabic style, it remains a literal (haqiqah) truth, not a metaphor (majaz). For we have previously established a principle, namely that words are not clarified in meaning except by context and by their combination with one another. Many a word has one meaning in one context and another meaning in another context. Take for example "the town" (al-qaryah). The word "the town," which those who speak of metaphor harp upon, we say: "the town" is used to mean its people, and is used to mean its dwellings, in clear wording in both cases, and is used to mean its people by contextual indication (qarinah).

God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, We are going to destroy the people of this town﴾ [al-Ankabut 29:31]. What is meant by "the town"?

**Students:** (...).

**Shaykh:** No, brothers. ﴿the people of this town﴾: what is meant is the dwellings. Clear. ﴿the people of this town﴾: what is meant is the dwellings. ﴿And how many a town did I give respite while it was wrongdoing, then I seized it, and to Me is the destination﴾ [al-Hajj 22:48]. What is meant?

**Students:** Its people.

**Shaykh:** Its people. There is no doubt about this, because wrongdoing is not attributed to dwellings. Dwellings do not wrong. So the meaning of "the town" is its people, by the contextual indicator of His words: ﴿while it was wrongdoing﴾. No one can say that what comes first to the mind from the word "town" is the dwellings. No one says this, never. In that case, "the town" is not used here in its figurative sense; it is used in its literal sense, because the literal meaning of speech is what comes to the mind of the meaning. That is its literal sense, and it varies with the variation of context.

﴿And ask the town﴾ [Yusuf 12:82]. This is what those who say there is metaphor in the Qur'an have been harping upon. ﴿Ask the town﴾. They said: it is known what is meant by ﴿ask the town﴾. I go to the walls and say: O boy, did the brother of Joseph steal? Could anyone understand that this is the meaning? Never. No one understands this. And if anyone said that this is the apparent meaning of God's speech, he would in reality be mocking God's speech. God did not intend this at all, and this meaning is not understood at all from this word.

Thus it becomes clear that a word may have a meaning according to its context. The meaning that comes to mind from the context is the literal meaning of the speech, in whatever construction it occurs. In that case we say: ﴿He sent down from the heaven water, and gave life thereby to the earth﴾. The intended meaning is without doubt? The intended meaning is: He gave life thereby to the plants, because it is what is described as living and luminous. As for the earth itself, it is sand, stones and dust. It neither lives nor dies.

His words: ﴿and He gave life thereby to the earth after its death﴾ contain many signs: signs indicating mercy, signs indicating wisdom, and signs indicating power. Signs indicating mercy are by the great benefits in this giving of life: ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firm﴾ [al-Nazi'at 79:31-32], for whom? ﴿as enjoyment for you and your livestock﴾ [al-Nazi'at 79:33]. How many a great blessing is in these crops that God Most High gave life to by rain, is it not so? For us and for our livestock, as food, as medicine and other things. Is it clear? This indicates mercy.

There are signs indicating wisdom, namely: that the life of these crops came about through a cause, and what is that? The water that descended. From this we take that God, Mighty and Majestic, creates with wisdom and decrees with wisdom. God, Mighty and Majestic, is capable of saying to the earth: "Bring forth the crop," and it would bring it forth without water. But everything is tied to a cause. His, Mighty and Majestic, linking the giving of life to the earth with the descent of water: what does this indicate? It indicates wisdom, and that everything has a particular order that it does not exceed, from its creation until God permits the destruction of the world.

There are signs indicating power, namely: you see the earth humbled, lifeless, black, barren, with nothing in it. Then when God sends rain upon it, after about a month you come to it and find it stirring with blossoms, leaves and trees. ﴿When We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who gave it life is the one who will give life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent﴾ [Fussilat 41:39]. This is great power. By God, if all of mankind from first to last gathered to bring out a leaf from a seed, one single leaf from a seed, could they? They could not. And a seed that sprouts seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains: is this not evidence of great power? Yes, of great power that has no end. So there is a sign of power in it, and what remains? And wisdom, and mercy.

He said: ﴿And He spread throughout it from every creature﴾. Let us see: ﴿spread﴾, and what is conjoined to it? ﴿And what God sent down from the heaven of water, and He gave life thereby to the earth after its death, and He spread throughout it from every creature﴾?

**Student:** It is conjoined to ﴿gave life﴾.

**Shaykh:** To ﴿gave life﴾? Then its meaning is: He spread the creatures after the descent of rain. Apparently it is conjoined to His words ﴿sent down﴾, meaning: and in what He spread throughout it of every creature, or in what He spread throughout the earth of every creature, or in the earth and the heaven?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 158–164 (part 8 of 9):

﴿And He spread throughout it﴾, i.e., throughout the earth, ﴿every kind of moving creature﴾. The word "kull" (every) is used to indicate the varieties and the genera: varieties and genera of creatures on the earth, of which none has knowledge except He who created them. None knows their genera and varieties, let alone their individuals, except Allah, who created them, glory be to Him and exalted is He. He knows these genera, their varieties, their individuals, their conditions, and everything that sustains them. And in them are signs of Allah that point to the perfection of His power, His mercy, His knowledge, and His wisdom, which dazzle the intellects. Look, glory be to Allah the Mighty: you find these diverse creatures of many kinds, and the small insects, how Allah has guided them to that for which they were created. ﴿He gave each thing its creation, then guided it﴾ [Ta-Ha 50]. To the point that you see water entering the burrow of an ant, and the ant comes out of this burrow carrying its young. An ant carrying its offspring! What do you expect from these offspring?! But the mercy of the Most Merciful of the merciful placed in the heart of this ant a mercy that makes it carry its young to save them from drowning. I have witnessed it with my own eyes, and if you wish, test it yourselves.
* A student: (...) a heart?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it has a heart, and it has an intellect suited to it. The summary is that this is among the signs of Allah the Mighty. Likewise the beasts: the fierce predators that eat whatever is smaller than their young. You find that their young, which have grown larger than them, which they eat, what do they do with them? They show tenderness to them and raise them, until when they become independent and self-sufficient they become enemies to the mother, or the mother becomes an enemy to them. The cat raises its kittens, but when they become self-sufficient, she drives them away and becomes their enemy. This is among the signs of Allah the Mighty.
Among these creatures that Allah spread across the earth are signs of Allah: you see some creatures that crawl on the earth, crawling, yet you can hardly perceive their bodies, let alone their organs, let alone what is inside them. Yet they live, do they not? They live as they are, living and knowing their needs, knowing their burrow, and returning to it. This is one of the signs of Allah. In any case, we do not know the reality of these things; we have not studied biology, and whoever has studied biology finds in it what dazzles the intellects. So what Allah has spread across the earth of creatures, of their genera and varieties, contains signs of Allah that cannot be counted, because in every one of them there is a sign, and they cannot be counted as varieties or genera, let alone as individuals.
His saying: ﴿And He spread throughout it every kind of moving creature﴾ contains signs. That is, these great and numerous creatures are known to Allah, are they not? They are known, because He created them. Mercy is placed in them, because we see mutual compassion among them, and there are benefits for the servants in them. Is that not so? Yes. ﴿Do they not see that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners? And We subjected them to them, so some of them they ride﴾ [Ya-Sin 71–72].
Here is also a strange sign, which is the complete power of Allah the Mighty in creating opposites among animals. Among animals there is one that harms the children of Adam, and there is one from which the children of Adam benefit, while the Creator is one, the substance is one, and the genus is one. Yet this one is the utmost of harm, and that one has many benefits. Is that not so? The camel is larger than the scorpion. Is this known? It is known. The scorpion stings, harming or hurting, and perhaps kills. And the camel? It benefits. Allah has made it submissive. A small boy who tends it takes hold of its halter and leads it wherever he wishes, or he stands behind it and drives it wherever he wishes. There is no doubt that this is among the signs of Allah. He who created these great creatures and made some of them beneficial and some of them harmful, this is among the signs of Allah.
* A student: Shaykh, there are signs in it as a refutation of those who liken Allah to His creation, for these inanimate things differ with...
* The Shaykh: Yes, with the agreement of the name.
* The student: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. ﴿And He spread throughout it every kind of moving creature, and the turning of the winds﴾. I have another reading here: ﴿and the turning of the wind﴾ (singular). As for the reading in the singular, the intended meaning is the genus; as for the reading in the plural, the intended meaning is its varieties. ﴿The turning of the winds﴾: is there in it signs of the turning of the winds? Yes indeed, there are many signs. The turning includes: its turning in terms of direction, its turning in terms of intensity and its absence, its turning in terms of benefits and their absence. Is that not so? In terms of direction: Allah the Glorified and Exalted made them blow toward the south, the north, the west, and the east. These are the principal directions, and there are other directions between them called the "nakba," because they are not in a straight line with the east, west, north, or south; so they are deviating winds, turning away from the principal direction.
In the turning of these winds there are signs. If the wind remained from one direction, it would harm the world, but they oppose one another, so some break the intensity of others, and some remove, by what the others bring, the harm, germs, and other things. They meet and break one another. Likewise, in their turning there are signs regarding the clouds: some gather the clouds, some disperse them, some fertilize them, and some make them pour. ﴿Do you not see that Allah drives clouds, then joins them together, then makes them a heap, and you see the rain coming out from within them﴾ [An-Nur 43]. ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ [Al-Hijr 22]. The people of knowledge said: they fertilize within the clouds, and they also fertilize some plants; the pollen is carried to them by the winds. In the turning of the winds there are also signs for sailing ships. Is that not so? Yes. There are also signs in the destruction of some peoples and the salvation of others. Is that not so? Allah destroyed 'Ad by it, and drove the confederates away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by it, and Allah saved His Messenger ﷺ by this wind from the evil of the confederates. So there are signs in it, and whoever reflects on this knows what in it of the power of Allah, His mercy, His might, and His wisdom.
If all the machines of the world, every machine of the world, were gathered together and became at their strongest in blowing air, could they move anything still, except what is right around them only? Could they reach from the farthest north to the south, or the reverse? They could not. But Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, says "Be," and it is. You find a strong north wind, and in a moment it reverses and becomes a strong south wind. This is the complete great power which Allah the Mighty arranges by a command that humans cannot achieve; therefore the turning of the winds became among the great signs of Allah pointing to His power.
Moreover, in their turning there are also benefits for aircraft, for they have an effect on airplanes, as they say, and likewise for cars. Do they not have an effect? They do. So in truth the turning of the winds contains many great signs of Allah.
﴿And the subjugated cloud﴾: this is among the signs of Allah, the cloud subjugated between the heaven and the earth. The cloud is this vapor and mist, and it is called "saḥāb" because it is drawn along (yunsaḥabu) in the atmosphere. It does not leap; do you see the clouds now leaping? No, but they are drawn along by the permission of Allah. This subjugated, made-submissive cloud, which its Creator, the Majestic and Exalted, made submissive for the benefit of His servants, Allah sends it sometimes as mercy and sometimes as punishment. This subjugated cloud, made submissive between heaven and earth, contains signs. Signs pointing to what? To power, mercy, and wisdom, all of which are present in these signs. As for power: who can bring the cloud? Who? Allah the Mighty; no one else can. Then who can make this water pour from it? Allah the Mighty. Therefore He said: ﴿and sends down water﴾ [Luqman 34].
Then who can make this cloud sometimes piled up, piled up until it is like black mountains that frighten whoever sees it, and sometimes light, and sometimes swift, and sometimes slow, and sometimes you see it not moving? We have often seen it settled, not moving, because it moves by the command of Allah. It is subjugated and made submissive by the command of Allah the Mighty.
Then this cloud is also subjected by the command of Allah: it waters this land and does not water that land. You find it come over heads, thundering and lightning, and perhaps it settles somewhat without raining, then it turns toward other people and rains on them without thunder and lightning, because it is commanded. I think it is not hidden from you, or from most of you, the story of the man who heard a voice in the cloud saying: "Water the garden of so-and-so," and this is established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The man said: "I went and the cloud emptied its water into a stony tract, then the stream flowed along one part of the stony tract, and it watered that garden. He came to its owner and said: 'What is your name, O so-and-so?' He said: 'What do you want?' He informed him of his name, and it was the name he had heard in the cloud saying: 'Water the garden of so-and-so.' He said to him: 'What do you do with it?' He said: 'I divide it, or I apportion it into thirds: a third for cultivation, a third for my children, and a third I give in charity.'"[[Narrated by Muslim (2984/45), from Abu Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him.]] The point is that this cloud sends down its water by the command of Allah, and holds back by the command of Allah the Mighty. Likewise, it is not hidden from you what is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Anas concerning the story of the man who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to pray for rain. The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah to give them rain, while the sky was clear and there was not a wisp of cloud. Then Allah produced the cloud and it spread, thundered, lightened, and rained, and the Messenger ﷺ had not descended from the pulpit before the rain was dripping from his beard. Glory be to Allah the Mighty! If all creation gathered together to do this deed, they could not do it. But Allah created it, subjected it, and commanded it, so it descended. It is a sign from His signs, and a sign of the truthfulness of His Messenger ﷺ. On the second Friday they asked the Messenger ﷺ to pray for rain for them, and he said: "O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, upon the hills, the mountain tops, the bottoms of the valleys, and the places where trees grow," and he began pointing with his hand toward the areas around us, like this. Whenever he pointed to a direction in the cloud, it parted.[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (933) and Muslim (897/8), from Anas may Allah be pleased with him.]] Did it part by the command of the Messenger or by the command of Allah? By the command of Allah. But the Messenger ﷺ is a directing agent, just as he is a distributor while Allah is the Giver. The Messenger directs, but if the Messenger ﷺ commanded the cloud a thousand times and the Lord, the Majestic and Exalted, had not commanded it, it would not move. But this is by the command of Allah.
This is from the subjugation by Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, of this subjugated cloud. When we see this subjugated cloud, and I think some of you have ridden an airplane, you find that part of this cloud is beneath you, like the distance of the earth, and part of it above you, like the distance of the cloud from the earth. These are great layers. We used to think, before we ascended into the air, that the cloud was all in one layer, but it turns out to be great layers, distant and differing. We have also observed it on earth and in the air; we have seen it gather together and combine. People of expertise in these matters have told us that when one side of the cloud begins to thunder, the clouds start to gather toward it to thunder. They gather by the permission of Allah. You see them as though there were a magnet drawing the scattered cloud toward it. This too is among the signs of Allah the Mighty.
His saying: ﴿between the heaven and the earth﴾: what is meant by heaven? Heaven is the raised ceiling, and the earth is our earth. Does this "between" imply contact?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: No. Between them is without contact. I intended by this explanation to refute those who denied the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "Indeed, the hearts of the children of Adam are between two of the fingers of the Most Merciful,"[[Narrated by Muslim (2654/17), from Abdullah ibn 'Amr may Allah be pleased with them both.]] and they said: if this were true...
The evidence is this: ﴿and the subjugated cloud between the heaven and the earth﴾ [Al-Baqarah 164]. Likewise you say: Badr is between Makkah and Madinah. This is about place, and between them there is a clear distance.
* A student: And its carrying between heaven and earth, without anything?
* The Shaykh: Yes, this too is among the signs of Allah. He carries the great seas between heaven and earth. And also as Allah the Mighty said: ﴿Do you not see that Allah drives clouds, then joins them together, then makes them a heap, and you see the rain coming out from within them, and He sends down from the sky mountains containing hail, and He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills﴾ [An-Nur 43]. Here, in the air, there are mountains of hail. Do not be surprised at that. Do not be surprised that there are mountains of hail in it, carried by the power of Allah the Mighty and by His command. Even if it has a cause, Allah created it to carry it, but the important thing is that it is carried by the command and power of Allah. Last year we went in the summer from here to Dammam, and the pilot said over the plane's speaker that the temperature was twenty-five degrees below zero, while we on the earth were burning (...) in summer, though the heat comes at midday. Twenty-five degrees below zero, and what does that require? Solidity; it freezes, becomes solid. We say: how, by the permission of Allah, when summer comes and it is hot, what kind of hail falls? Usually hail falls in summer days. But we found that the atmosphere has great layers, great layers. This part of the atmospheric layers, whose temperature reached twenty-five degrees below zero, the water in it will certainly freeze and become mountains. Yet Allah the Mighty sends it down, as you see, sending it down as grains, small grains, when there is no harm in it, when wisdom does not require that it harm anyone. It descends as you see: fine grains that do not harm an animal nor destroy a tree.
His saying: ﴿Surely there are signs﴾: the lam here is for emphasis, and ﴿signs﴾ is the noun of "inna" in the accusative, and the sign of its accusative is an apparent kasra at its end.
* A student: (...) or substitution for (...).
* The Shaykh: The sign of its accusative is an apparent kasra at its end.
* The student: Is this correct?
* The Shaykh: No, you must clarify. The kasra is a substitute for the fatha, because if you say "an apparent kasra at its end," the listener may think that the kasra is among the signs of the accusative, and that is not so.
His saying: ﴿Surely there are signs﴾: you have learned earlier that each one of these kinds contains signs; each one contains signs. It does not mean that the signs are divided so that each one has one sign; each one encompasses signs.
His exalted saying: ﴿for a people who reason﴾. ﴿Reason﴾ means they have intellects. We have already mentioned that intellect is divided into two types: the intellect of perception and the intellect of right guidance. The intellect of perception is the basis of moral obligation (taklif), and the intellect of right guidance is the basis of praise and commendation. The first, when lost, causes the loss of moral obligation; the second, when lost, causes the loss of praise and commendation. Which is meant here by ﴿for a people who reason﴾? Is it the intellect that is the basis of moral obligation, which is the intellect of perception, or the intellect that is the basis of praise and commendation, which is the intellect of right guidance?
* The students: Right guidance.
* The Shaykh: The latter, the intellect of right guidance. So the intelligent person who uses his intellect for what benefits him, restraining it from what is not fitting, because the intellect is named that because it restrains its possessor from what is not fitting. The truly intelligent person, when he reflects on these things, finds in them signs pointing to their Creator, the Majestic and Exalted, and to their Originator. As for the person who turns away, even if his intellect is great and his intelligence strong, he does not benefit from it. Therefore Allah the Exalted described the disbelievers as not reasoning, although in the perceptive intellect they are intelligent, are they not? In the perceptive intellect by which they perceive what benefits and harms them, yes. But they do not reason. The intellect exists in them, does it not? It exists, but Allah negated it from them because they do not benefit from it, and because they lack the intellect of right guidance that would guide them to what is in their interest. ﴿Surely there are signs for a people who reason﴾.
* A student: "Baththa" is conjoined to "the water"; could it not be conjoined to "aḥyā"?
* The Shaykh: Yes, because if you say it is conjoined to "aḥyā," then the spreading would be ordered upon the sending down of water.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The fa' in His saying ﴿So He gave life thereby﴾ is consequent upon ﴿He sent down﴾. Thus the element coordinated with it would be consequent upon ﴿He sent down﴾, and that is not the case.

* In the noble verse: the God of creation is one God, and He is Allah; by His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And your God is One God﴾ [al-Baqarah 163].

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the name "God" (Ilah) and "One" (al-Wahid) for Allah: ﴿And your God is One God﴾. It has also come in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿For Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ibrahim 48], so He affirmed the name "the One" for Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

* Among its benefits: the exclusivity of divinity to Allah, by His saying ﴿There is no god but He﴾. In the commentary we pointed out the apparent difficulty between this verse and what Allah affirmed of the divinity of idols, and we said: the reconciliation between them is truth and falsehood. The divinity of Allah is truth, and the divinity of those is falsehood.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, namely: al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Ilah, al-Wahid, and al-Rahman al-Rahim.

* Among its benefits: the establishment, or affirmation, of what these two names include of attribute and judgment. Some scholars say: the attribute and the effect. What is the attribute? Mercy. The attribute is mercy, and the judgment is that He shows mercy with this mercy: ﴿the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾.

* The student: Shaykh, what is the attribute derived from the name "the One"?

* The Shaykh: Oneness (al-wahdaniyyah).

* Among the benefits of the verse: a name of Allah may have one meaning when it stands alone and another meaning when it is combined with another; for al-Rahman, if it stood alone, would indicate the attribute and the judgment, and when it is combined with al-Rahim, al-Rahman indicates the attribute and al-Rahim indicates the act.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day﴾ [al-Baqarah 164], and so on to the end.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the greatness of the creation of the heavens and the earth. What is its basis?

* The student: His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿Are signs﴾. Had it not been great, it would not be a sign; so it is derived from it that the creation of the heavens and the earth is great.

* Among them: that the heavens are multiple, taken from the plural: ﴿in the creation of the heavens﴾.

* Among them: that the heavens are created, and therefore they were non-existent before; so they are not eternal.

* From this benefit follows the refutation of the philosophers who say: the eternity of the celestial spheres. They say: the eternity of the spheres, meaning that they are pre-eternal, uncreated, eternal and everlasting. For this reason they denied the splitting of the moon, and they said: the upper spheres cannot be subject to change. They interpreted His saying, exalted is He, ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾ [al-Qamar 1] as meaning that the appearance of knowledge and light through the message of the Prophet ﷺ is intended. There is no doubt that this is a false distortion, contrary to the mutawatir authentic hadiths from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. So what do we derive from this verse? That the heavens are created, and therefore they are originated, not eternal, contrary to the philosophers who hold their eternity.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person should reflect upon these heavens and earth in order to arrive at the signs within them; for He said: "there are signs in them." So reflect in order to reach these signs.

* Among them: that the signs in the creation of the heavens and the earth are varied according to what they indicate of power, wisdom, mercy and so on. In them is power and wisdom, this orderliness, and in them is mercy for the creation.

* Among them: what is in the alternation of night and day of signs, by His saying: ﴿the alternation of the night and the day﴾ [al-Baqarah 164].

* Among them: that their alternation is from the mercy of Allah, for they contain mercy and power. It has been previously mentioned that the alternation of night includes?
