His saying, exalted is He, concerning His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [at-Tawbah 40]. This is being-with restricted to a person. With whom? With the Messenger (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr. And Allah said to Musa and Harun: ﴿Fear not, indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46]. This is restricted to persons.

As for being restricted to an attribute, such as His saying: ﴿with those who are mindful﴾, ﴿with the doers of good﴾, ﴿with the patient﴾, and similar, this is restricted to an attribute. The scholars call this being-with that entails victory, support, and steadfastness "special being-with", because it entails victory and support for that particular person by his attribute or his person.

As for the second, in His saying: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid 4] and ﴿nor less than that nor more, but He is with them wherever they are﴾ [al-Mujadila 7]. This is being-with that entails encompassment of creation in knowledge, hearing, sight, power, and governance, and other meanings of His lordship, exalted is He.

As for the third, which is attached to a blameworthy attribute, it entails, together with encompassment, a warning. It entails a warning to those who hide from people and do not hide from the Lord, mighty and majestic, while He is with them. These are the implications of being-with according to the People of the Sunnah and the Community. They denied in the strongest terms anyone who claims that its implication is that Allah is mixed with creation and dwells in their places or in their substances, we seek refuge in Allah. This is the doctrine of the Hulul (incarnationists) among the Jahmiyyah and others. They say that Almighty Allah is with creation in their places. We ask Allah for well-being. They do not even declare Allah free of what they would declare their lowest children free of. According to their corrupt and false opinion, it follows that Allah is with a person in the most vile place, or is it not so? Because this is their doctrine. And it follows, for those who say that He is mixed even with the substances of created things, not merely sharing with them in places, that the Creator, majestic and exalted, dwells in the very essence of the vilest animals. These people claim that they are of the People of the Qibla and that they are Muslims, and they have become viler than the Christians. The Christians, what did they say? That Allah dwells in whom?

*Students:* In Jesus.

*Shaykh:* In Jesus. Jesus is one of the prophets, one of the messengers, one of the steadfast messengers. But those people, we seek refuge in Allah, the proponents of incarnation, say that He dwells even in the vilest bodies of animals. We ask Allah for well-being. Leave aside those who speak of the unity of existence; those are other people, more vile than these.

So the being-with, according to the People of the Sunnah and the Community, does not entail, and we do not say merely that it does not necessarily entail, but it never entails under any circumstances that the Creator is mixed with creation, neither in their places nor in their essences. For Almighty Allah is above His Throne, separate from His creation. Is that clear? However, its implications vary according to what we have indicated. It may entail warning, it may entail victory and support, and it may entail mere encompassment and knowledge. So the matter will not be confused for you, and this corrupt doctrine will not occur to your mind or your understanding.

Among the wonders is that the early Jahmiyyah held the incarnation doctrine I mentioned, while their later followers held pure negation. They said: Allah does not exist in a place. So they said: Allah is neither inside the world nor outside the world, neither connected to the world nor separate from the world, neither above the world nor below the world. Nothing is left. For this reason some scholars said: If someone said to us, "Describe nothingness for us," we would not describe it better than this description. This is a comprehensive description. We ask Allah for protection and safety. The summary is that Almighty Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning what they differed about, by His permission. They said: We believe that Allah has established Himself on His Throne in His essence, that He is above His creation, and that His loftiness is an attribute of His essence. And what Allah has described Himself as, of descending to the lowest heaven, of drawing near to some of His servants, and of being with creation, all of this does not contradict His loftiness, because Almighty Allah encompasses everything. So He is, as Shaykh al-Islam said: near in His loftiness, high in His nearness.

But the thing that affects a person in these matters, and the doubts that afflict him, is when he supposes that the Creator is like the created. He says: How can He be in the heaven, above the Throne, and then you say He is with you? How can He be above the heaven, on the Throne, and then you say He draws near to you? "Whoever draws near to Me a hand's span, I draw near to him a forearm's length" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7405) and Muslim (2675) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him; the wording is Muslim's], and similar things. We say: this understanding only came to you because you supposed that the attributes of the Creator are like the attributes of the created. Now look into yourself, your soul that is between your two sides. Are its attributes like the attributes of the body?

*Students:* No.

*Shaykh:* No. It goes out at night when you sleep, to the right and to the left, and returns. When a person dies, it is raised up to the heaven, until it reaches the seventh heaven before he is buried, and then it returns. Can this be imagined, that a body could do this, or can it not be imagined?

*Students:* It cannot be imagined.

*Shaykh:* It cannot be imagined that a body ascends with such speed and returns with such speed. If this is true of one of the creatures of Almighty Allah, which you cannot compare to the body, how much more so of the Creator?

Some of the anthropomorphists among the people here in our country say: You say that Allah descends to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains. That means He is always descending, because the last third of the night is continuous, constantly continuous. When dawn breaks for us, and there is still a little left for those in the west? We say: they say the Messenger lied. Fine. The Messenger (ﷺ) said these words to a group whose minds were sounder than ours and whose understanding was deeper than ours. They did not raise this objection, because they knew that the Lord, mighty and majestic, is not like the created. It is correct for us to say that He is now descending in the last third of the night in this part of the earth. That is, He descended to the lowest heaven when it is the last third of the night in this part of the earth. And in the other part, where it is morning for them or the beginning of the night, is He descending or not?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 189–195 (part 5 of 6):

* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: It is not revealed, and Allah is over all things capable. It is not permissible for a person to deny what Allah has affirmed for Himself, or what His Messenger has affirmed for Him, by the likes of these ..
(...) for jihad in the way of Allah. Since the verse, as you see, is in the context of jihad, and it is also at the beginning of the verses on Hajj, at the beginning of the verses of Hajj, spending in Hajj is included in it, or not? Yes, it is included in it.
He said: ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾. He said: ﴿Do not throw yourselves with your own hands﴾. Some of them say that the particle "bi" (with) here is superfluous, meaning: "and do not throw your hands into destruction." The correct view is that it is original, not superfluous, and that the meaning of (alqa biyadihi, "he threw with his hand") is stronger than the meaning of (alqa yadahu, "he threw his hand"). This is because "alqa biyadihi" means that he placed his hand and it had no movement in it, unlike "alqa yadahu ila al-tahluka." Also, saying that the meaning is "alqa yadahu" is ruled out by His words ﴿into destruction﴾, for if the meaning were "alqa yadahu," He would have said "fi al-tahluka" (in destruction) and not "ila al-tahluka" (into destruction). So the "ba'" is original, and the meaning is: do not throw them (your hands) into destruction, in the sense that there should be no movement from them. One says "alqa biyadihi" just as one says "alqa bi'asahu" (he threw down his staff). "Alqa biyadihi ila al-tahluka" is as if he handed it over to destruction. And (al-tahlukah) is on the pattern (taf'ilah) from (al-halak), destruction. The meaning is: do not throw yourselves toward that which destroys you. So what is the meaning of His words ﴿Do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾? The meaning: do not throw them toward that in which there is destruction, physical or moral?
* A student: Both.
* The Shaykh: Or both? Both, yes. Because it was revealed concerning those who refrained from fighting or refrained from giving in the way of Allah. Is this physical destruction or moral?
* A student: Moral.
* The Shaykh: This is moral destruction, because they destroyed themselves by abandoning what was obligatory upon them of jihad and spending in it. Yet this moral destruction results in physical destruction, because if they abandon fighting the enemies, the enemies will fight them and dominate them. And if they abandon spending in the way of Allah for fighting the enemies, they will also be dominated by them. Likewise, throwing oneself into physical destruction is included in it. For this reason, it is not permissible for a person to expose himself to dangers. It is not permissible for a person to expose himself to dangers, such as throwing himself into fire, or into water that drowns him, or sleeping under a wall leaning to collapse, or what is similar to that. This is prohibited. The proof of this is the words of the Exalted: ﴿And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾ [An-Nisa 29], for within this verse ﴿do not kill yourselves﴾ includes everything that leads to harm to the body, even if it does not reach the level of killing. The evidence: "'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, when the Messenger (ﷺ) sent him on an expedition, became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) on a cold night, so he performed tayammum and led his companions in prayer. When he returned to the Prophet (ﷺ), the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: 'O 'Amr, you led your companions in prayer while you were junub?' He said: O Messenger of Allah, I remembered the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾, so I performed tayammum. The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed and approved of it."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (334), and al-Bukhari in suspended form (1/77), from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: "O 'Amr, you led your companions in prayer while you were junub?"]] Even though, if he had bathed, would he have certainly died?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: What (...) in any case. But the verse indicates that whatever is a cause of harm is included in the prohibition. Everything that harms the body, you are forbidden from it. And on the basis of this principle, we know that tobacco?
* The students: Haram.
* The Shaykh: Halal.
* The students: Haram.
* The Shaykh: Haram?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Why?
* The student: Because it harms.
* The Shaykh: Because it harms, by the agreement of physicians that it is harmful. Also, there is squandering of wealth in it, and the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the squandering of wealth.
So ﴿do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾ includes throwing oneself into physical and moral destruction.
﴿And do good. Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾. ﴿Do good﴾ is an imperative verb. Then He gave the reason for this command by His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾. The command to do good (ihsan) includes excellence in worshipping the Creator and excellence toward the creation, excellence in worship of the Creator and in dealing with the created. So what is excellence in worshipping the Creator? Excellence in worshipping the Creator was clarified by the Messenger (ﷺ) in his words: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50, 4777), and Muslim (9/5), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] The difference between the two clauses is very clear. The first is worship of seeking, and the second is worship of fear. "You worship Allah as if you see Him": you seek Him. "Or if you do not see Him, He sees you": you fear Him. Is the second level lower or higher?
* The students: Higher.
* The Shaykh: The second level is higher?
* A student: Lower.
* The Shaykh: Lower. For this reason he said: "And if you do not..." So the first level is higher: that you worship Allah seeking to reach Him, not out of fear of His punishment. Although worship may combine both, the first is higher, of greater rank. As for excellence in dealing with people, the Messenger (ﷺ) gathered it in one word: "That you treat people with what you would like them to treat you."[[Mu'jam as-Sahabah by Ibn Qani' (1/249), from the hadith of Sa'd ibn al-Akhram al-Ta'i, with the wording: "And you treat people with what you would like them to treat you."]] This is a comprehensive statement: that you treat people with what you would like them to treat you. If a man deals with people in this manner, does he do good or not?
* The students: He does good.
* The Shaykh: Good. Now, a man has a commodity that has a defect, but it is a defect that is not apparent. So he sold it to a person without informing him. Would he be a good-doer in the transaction?
* A student: Not a good-doer.
* The Shaykh: Why?
* A student: Because he did not inform him.
* The Shaykh: No. Because he would not like anyone to deal with him in this way. He would not like it. Therefore, he did not do good. But if he dealt with him and said: "There is a defect in this commodity, which is such and such." Would he be a good-doer?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: He would be a good-doer, right? Good. Now, some people, on this occasion, want to sell a commodity and know that it has a defect. So they put it up for sale and say: "Would you buy it in any condition? Consider every defect in it, every defect in it." If it is a car, he says: "I only sold it to you with its tires, and not its steering wheel, and not its ..." Is this permissible or not?
* A student: No.
* The Shaykh: Is it reasonable that someone buys, for example, for six thousand, on condition of the steering wheel or tires, which would be worth only two hundred riyals if it were new? Is this reasonable or not?
* A student: It is not reasonable.
* The Shaykh: But they say this so that if he finds a defect and comes saying, "I want to return it because of the defect," they say, "We stipulated with you [that you accept any defect]." So what is your opinion on this transaction? Is it good-doing or bad-doing?
* The students: Bad-doing.
* The Shaykh: Bad-doing. Therefore, it is obligatory that he clarify. Yes, if it is assumed that this man bought this car without knowing it had a defect, then sold it, and feared it would be returned to him for a defect, so he stipulated such conditions, then this is permissible. This is permissible. And this view is the stronger one, which Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah chose, on the basis that whoever knows of the defect and conceals it, even if he stipulates freedom from defects, is still bound by it. The [Hanbali] school says: if he released him from defects after the contract, he is cleared; if he released him before, he is not cleared. But the correct view is that the matter does not depend on the release before or after the contract, but on the knowledge of the person: the seller's knowledge of the defect or his lack of knowledge. If he knew, he is not cleared unless he specified it, saying: "There is such and such defect in it," and the buyer agreed. He entered with insight. If he did not know, he is cleared.
* A student: What is the school's view that he is cleared?
* The Shaykh: The school: I sold you a car, and on the day I sold it you bought it. We are now in the option period (majlis al-khiyar, the session of choice). You are going to be patient with every defect in it, and you said: "I am patient." He knows that it has such a defect, but he did not inform you. The school says he is cleared: if you find a defect, he is not obligated to return it to you. Why? Because you waived the right after it was established by the contract. But if I said: "I want to sell you this car, and you will find in it every defect," and you said: "I am content, and I buy it from you," then this does not bind me. If you find a defect, I return it to you. If he said: "Hey, I did not give you the option," I say: "Yes, you gave it before it was established, because the option is not established except after the contract." Is it clear?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: But the correct view, which Shaykh al-Islam mentioned, and which is reported from the Companions, is that the basis is what?
* The students: The seller's knowledge.
* The Shaykh: On the seller's knowledge or his lack of knowledge.
* A student: Clarifying the defect of the commodity, even if the buyer did not ask?
* The Shaykh: Yes, even if the buyer did not ask. "None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (13), and Muslim (45/71), from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]]
He said: ﴿And do good. Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾. Even if there were no excellence except this, it would be sufficient for the believer to establish excellence. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾. My brothers, a person may perhaps pour a glass of water for someone from the cooler to give him to drink. Is this excellence?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Excellence or not?
* The students: Excellence.
* The Shaykh: Excellence. If you do this, then feel that Allah loves you. Allah loves you, because this is an important and beneficial point: that when you do excellence, you feel that you hope through it to gain the love of Allah, because Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾. If you inform your brother of a matter of knowledge that you understood, is that excellence or not?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Excellence. Feel this meaning: that by this deed you have exposed yourself to the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And so on.
(...) the obligation of fighting the disbelievers until they cease from fitnah (sedition), based on His words: ﴿so that there is no fitnah and the religion is for Allah﴾.
* It is also derived from it: when the fitnah ends, and their opposition to the Islamic call ends, by paying the jizyah (poll tax), they are not fought.
* It is also derived from it: when they cease, either from shirk by accepting Islam, or from fitnah by submission, then they are not transgressed against, based on His words: ﴿But if they cease, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾.
* It is also derived from the noble verse: the wrongdoer is repaid with the like of his aggression, based on His words: ﴿then there is no aggression﴾. We have said previously that such an expression is meant to indicate equivalence to the act, meaning that calling the requital "aggression" is by way of equivalence, so that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The sacred month for the sacred month﴾. From this noble verse is derived: Allah the Exalted's consolation to the Muslims, that if they miss performing their 'umrah in a sacred month, they may make it up in a sacred month of the following year, as occurred.
* Among its benefits also: that sacred violations are subject to retaliation (qisas). That is, whoever violates your sanctity, you may violate his sanctity in the same way. For this reason, He made the following a consequence of it: ﴿So whoever has attacked you, then attack him in the same way as he attacked you﴾.
* It is derived from the noble verse: the aggressor is not repaid with more than his aggression, based on His words: ﴿in the same way as he attacked you﴾. So a person should not say: "I want to retaliate in order to satisfy myself." For this reason the scholars said: retaliation against the offender is not carried out except in the presence of the ruler or his deputy, out of fear of excessive aggression, that a person wants to satisfy himself, so he transgresses further and mutilates the offender, or the like.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of fearing Allah the Exalted in dealing with others, and in every state, based on His words: ﴿And fear Allah﴾.
* Among them: the affirmation that Allah is with the God-fearing, based on His words... Yes?
* The students: ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾.
* Among its benefits: the emphasis of this companionship. For this reason He said: ﴿And know﴾. He did not limit Himself to merely informing us of it, but commanded us to know it, and this is a command beyond mere information.
* Among its benefits also: the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah the Exalted over creation, and His support for the God-fearing who fulfill their piety. The reason for this is that it is known by reason, nature, the Book, and the Sunnah that Allah is above all creation. Yet He has affirmed that He is with creation. This is evidence of His encompassing, glorified and exalted be He. The meaning of His being with creation is not that He is mixed with them or dwells in their places, as the corrupt delusion of whom has gone?
* The students: The Hulûliyya (Incarnationists).
* The Shaykh: The Hulûliyya, among the Jahmiyya and others.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of piety, since the servant attains by it what? The companionship of Allah. It is known that when Allah is with you, He helps you, supports you, and makes you firm. This indicates the excellence of the cause, which is piety: ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾.
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And spend in the way of Allah﴾. From this noble verse is derived: the obligation of spending in the way of Allah.
* A student: ﴿Spend in the way of Allah﴾.
* The Shaykh: An obligation. From where did you know it is an obligation?
* The student: The command.
* The Shaykh: The default principle regarding a command?
* The student: Obligation.
* The Shaykh: Obligation. Does zakat enter into this or not?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it enters. It is the first thing to enter, because it is the most obligatory of obligations. The most obligatory form of spending in the way of Allah is zakat, more obligatory than spending in jihad, in maintaining kinship ties, and in honoring one's parents, because it is one of the pillars of Islam.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication of sincerity in action. From where?
* The students: ﴿in the way of Allah﴾.
* The Shaykh: From His words ﴿in the way of Allah﴾. And included in this, as we said in the exegesis, is intention and execution: that the intention be for Allah, and that the execution be according to the Sharia of Allah. Yes?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾ [Al-Furqan 67]. Do not say: "I want to spend," and spend everything. Be neither extravagant nor stingy.
* It is also derived from the noble verse: the prohibition of throwing oneself with one's own hands into destruction. From where is it taken?
* A student: ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands﴾.
* The Shaykh: From His words: ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾. It was previously mentioned in the exegesis that throwing oneself into destruction includes neglecting an obligation and committing a prohibited act, or, in a more general expression, it encompasses everything in which there is destruction for a person and danger to his religion or his worldly life.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the command to do good, based on His words: ﴿And do good﴾. Is the command for obligation or recommendation? As for the excellence by which the obligation is completed, it is for obligation. As for the excellence by which the deed is perfected, it is for recommendation. For example, if excellence is paired with justice, then excellence becomes, by way of...
* A student: Obligation.
* The Shaykh: No, by way of recommendation, because justice is the obligation. So excellence is an added virtue beyond the obligation, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾ [An-Nahl 90].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of excellence. From where is it taken?
* The students: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of love for Allah the Exalted, based on His words: ﴿Allah loves the good-doers﴾. It is real love, on its apparent meaning, and it is not meant to be reward or the desire for reward, contrary to the Ash'aris and others among the people of distortion (tahrif), who distort this great meaning into a meaning that is not of its stature. Mere will is nothing in comparison to love.

Ibn 'Uthaymin's commentary on Surah 2, verses 189–195 (part 6 of 6):

We have already stated many times that their argument is that love can only exist between two things that are alike, and we have shown the invalidity of this reasoning, and that it contradicts the text and the consensus of the early Muslims (al-salaf). It is also refuted by what is established through revelation and by direct observation: that love may exist between two things that are not alike. The Prophet (ﷺ) affirmed that Uhud, which is a mountain of stones, "is a mountain that loves us, and we love it" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4083) and Muslim (1393 / 504) from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. And a person finds that his riding animal loves him: when a camel hears the voice of its owner, it yearns for him and comes to him, and likewise other livestock.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 189–195 (part 1 of 6):

And His saying: ﴿They ask you about the crescent moons. Say: They are measures of time for the people and for the Hajj﴾ [al-Baqarah 189]. It means: they ask about the wisdom behind them, as shown by the answer.

As for what is mentioned in the books of rhetoric, that they asked the Messenger ﷺ about the crescent moon: why it appears small and then grows? Allah answered by explaining the wisdom. They said this falls under the device of "the wise answer" (uslub al-hakim): that the questioner is answered with something other than what he expects, to indicate that he ought to have asked about this instead. But the correct view is that they did not ask the Messenger about this. They asked him about the wisdom behind the crescent moons, and that Allah, glorified and exalted, created them in this form. The proof is the answer, because the original principle is that the answer corresponds to the question, until this is established by a sound text.

No sound text establishes that the Companions asked about the reason why it appears as a small crescent and then keeps growing little by little until it becomes full. There is no sound hadith on this. Accordingly, it is necessary that the question match the answer, because they asked: what is the wisdom?

* Student: (...) the opposite?
* Shaykh: No, and the answer.
* Student: (...) corresponds to the question.
* Shaykh: And likewise the question. That is, we now affirm that the question is about the wisdom, not about its appearing small. So we say: this answer must correspond to their question, and their question likewise corresponds to it.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: They are measures of time for the people﴾. That is, the crescent moons are measures of time for the people. It is the plural of miqat, from waqt (time), meaning that things are timed by them. For this reason people set by them everything related to their affairs: there are fixed periods tied to months, such as the waiting period of a widow, four months and ten days, and the waiting period of one who does not menstruate, how many? Three months; and the term of the one who takes an oath to abstain from wives: ﴿For those who swear off their wives, a waiting period of four months﴾ [al-Baqarah 226].

Likewise, people set by them the due dates of debts, rentals, and other things. So they are measures of time for the people.

Timing by lunar months is clearer and more evident than timing by imaginary months, which are the Western (Afranji) months now: imaginary months that have no basis. For this reason some of them have twenty-eight days and some thirty-one, three days... If people disagreed and had no calendars, to what would they refer? They would have nothing to refer to. But when people disagree about the crescent moons, the crescent decides between them. It is a sensible, visible sign. For this reason Allah, mighty and majestic, made the months measures of time for the people, for people in general, not only for Muslims, but for people generally; as He said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred﴾ [at-Tawbah 36].

And His saying: ﴿and the Hajj﴾ means: and measures for the Hajj, because the Hajj is in known months, beginning with the entry of Shawwal and ending with the end of Dhu al-Hijjah, three months.

If someone says: fasting too? ﴿So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it﴾ [al-Baqarah 185].

We say: Yes, but the context of the verses is a preface to explaining the Hajj, so He said: ﴿and the Hajj﴾. The discussion of fasting has already concluded.

﴿They are measures of time for the people and for the Hajj; and it is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs﴾ [al-Baqarah 189]. Good. ﴿They are measures of time for the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 189] has a grammatical point: (mawaqit) is the predicate of (hiya). My question: why was it not given tanwin so that it would be said: mawaqitun?

* Student: It is the form of the diptote plural (sigha muntaha al-jumu'), so it is not declined.
* Shaykh: Because it is diptote, due to the form of the final plural: (mafa'il). And Allah's saying ﴿al-Hajj﴾ is conjoined to ﴿lil-nas﴾.

﴿And it is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs﴾ [al-Baqarah 189].

Al-birr is goodness, and goodness was called birr because of the breadth it contains. From the same derivation comes al-barr, which is open land, apart from built-up areas, because of its vastness.

And His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter﴾, the (ba') is a prepositional particle: is it original or extra?

* Student: Extra.
* Shaykh: Extra, for emphasis. That is: and righteousness is not by your entering houses from their backs.

﴿by entering houses from their backs﴾: that is, from behind them, not from their doors. ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses﴾. In another reading: ﴿al-Buyut﴾, "al-buyut" is our colloquial dialect, yes, and it is an Arabic language, a Sab'i reading.

﴿by entering houses from their backs﴾: this (min) is explanatory (bayaniyya), meaning you come to them from behind. In the Jahiliyyah, out of their foolishness, when they entered the state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah, they would enter houses from their backs, except the Quraysh, who entered them from their doors. As for others, they said: we have entered ihram, so we cannot enter our houses from their doors; this would nullify the ihram. We must come in from the back so that the roof of the house does not shade us. Look at the ignorance: they would climb up the walls at the back of the houses, believing that this was righteousness and a means of drawing near to Allah, mighty and majestic. So Allah negated this and nullified it: ﴿And it is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs﴾. This is not righteousness; rather, it is the opposite of righteousness.

The reason is what it contains of hardship, and what it contains of opposition to wisdom and foolishness. It is contrary to righteousness. For this reason He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And enter houses by their doors﴾.

﴿But righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah﴾. In another reading: ﴿Wa lakini al-birru man ittaqa﴾, where (lakin) is the light (mukhaffafa) form of the heavy (thaqila), inactive (muhmala), and (al-birr) is its subject.

As for the reading with the doubled nun, ﴿wa lakinna al-birra﴾, it is operative and (al-birr) is its noun.

And His saying: ﴿al-birra man ittaqa﴾: (al-birr) is an abstract noun, and (man ittaqa) is a concrete noun. How does one predicate a concrete thing of an abstract noun?

We say: this has come up before many times, and it is interpreted in one of three ways. Who knows them?

* Student: The verbal noun here carries the meaning of the active participle: "wa lakinna al-barra" (the pious one), or with an implied element: "wa lakinna al-birra birru man ittaqa" (righteousness is the righteousness of one who fears Allah).

* Shaykh: Yes, or?

* Student: Or this is in the sense of absolute hyperbole (mubalagha mutlaqa), the verbal noun.

* Shaykh: That the one who fears Allah is himself righteousness. Good, correct.

﴿But righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah﴾: fears whom? He fears Allah, mighty and majestic; because fear in the context of worship is only intended as: "Fear Allah."

Righteousness is taqwa; this is the reality of righteousness, not that you avoid entering a house by its door, but that righteousness is that you fear Allah, mighty and majestic. For this reason He said: ﴿And enter houses by their doors﴾. Come to houses and to houses by their doors, that is, from the direction of the door, for this is goodness. This is part of the wisdom of Allah's teaching: when He forbids something, He directs people to the sound path: ﴿Do not say "Ra'ina," but say "Unzurna"﴾ [al-Baqarah 104].

Likewise is the teaching of the Messenger ﷺ to his community: when he closed a door for them by forbidding it, he opened for them the door of what is permitted. He said to one who came to him with good dates, and said: "We take a sa' of this for two sa's, and two sa's for three," he said: "Do not do that; sell the jam' (mixed inferior dates) for dirhams, then buy with the dirhams janib (good dates)." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2202), and Muslim (1593/95), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah.] That is, good dates. So he forbade him the unlawful and opened for him the door of the lawful.

Likewise, anyone who teaches people should, when he closes a door for them while they need to deal in it, open for them the door of permissibility.

﴿And enter houses by their doors﴾: for this is what conforms to custom, nature, and reason. Some scholars said: this should be a rule even in matters of the heart: you enter them by their doors; you do not force matters by force, but you come to them by their door, with wisdom and fine admonition, so that matters are accomplished for you. So there is an indication in it that spiritual matters too are approached by their doors, and that things are not forced by force, for that may not achieve the goal.

So if you wish, for example, to address a person of great rank, a senior dignitary, do you come to him straight away, speaking to him and addressing him as you address ordinary people? The answer: No, rather you come through the doors.

﴿And enter houses by their doors, and fear Allah that you may prosper﴾.

﴿Fear Allah﴾: that is, make for yourselves a shield from His punishment by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

﴿And fear Allah that you may prosper﴾: (la'alla) indicates cause; that is, in order that you may attain success. Falah is attaining what is sought and being saved from what is feared.

* Student: Good, for example, people who deal (...).
* Shaykh: He takes the rope, goes to gather firewood, comes back and sells it.

﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you﴾ [al-Baqarah 190]. "Qatilu" is an imperative verb, and al-muqatala is mutual action from both sides; that is, kill them by fighting them. But He said: ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, that is, in His religion and His law, and for its sake. So the way of Allah, glorified and exalted, encompasses the religion, and that fighting should be within the bounds of religion and in the lawful manner, and for Allah alone. For this reason He placed it first: He placed the cause for which one fights before the one fought against. This indicates that sincerity should be present in this fighting, because it is no small matter; the fighter exposes his neck to the swords of enemies. If he is not sincere to Allah, he loses both this world and the Hereafter: he may be killed without attaining martyrdom. So by placing the intended goal first, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, He alerts to the fact that this fighting must be founded on sincerity.

And His saying: ﴿those who fight you﴾: fight those who fight you. People have differed in their opinions about this object: ﴿those who fight you﴾. Someone might say: its implication is that those who do not fight you, you should not fight; and on this basis, our fighting of the disbelievers would be only defensive fighting, that is, against those who fight you only.

For this reason scholars differed on this in three views:

The first: that this verse is abrogated. Abrogated by what? By His saying: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾ [at-Tawbah 36]. Then the verse is not muhkam (definitive), this is one view.

The second: that this description is not a restriction, but serves to rouse us and to describe the reality: to stir us to fight them, and to describe their reality, that they are fighting us. On this view, the command to fight only increases in strength. That is, if a person says to you: "Fight the one who strikes you, man!", it means as if he is saying: "Take your revenge; how can you endure that he strikes you and you do not strike him?" So the intended meaning is stirring and describing the reality of these people: that they are fighting us, so how should we not fight them?

The third view: it is a restriction that excludes what is other than it. So we do not fight except those who fight us. As for one who does not fight us, who submits to our authority, pays the jizyah, and submits to the rulings of Islam, we do not fight him. This is the view of many later scholars: the verse only commands Allah that we fight those who fight us. As for one who does not fight us, who submits to our rule, is content with the rulings of Islam, and pays the jizyah, we do not fight them.

They cited as evidence that when the Messenger ﷺ appointed a commander over an army or a detachment, he would advise him and those Muslims with him to do good, and say to them: "Fight in the way of Allah; fight those who disbelieve in Allah; do not embezzle, do not betray, do not mutilate, and do not kill a child." Then he mentioned to him: when he comes upon a fortress, let him call them to Islam; if they embrace Islam, let him call them to migrate to the lands of the Muslims; if they refuse Islam, he should demand from them the jizyah; if they refuse, then let him fight them. [Related by Muslim (1731/3) from the hadith of Buraydah al-Aslami, may Allah be pleased with him.] This indicates that these people, if they pay the jizyah, are not to be fought, because they have submitted to the rulings of Islam and have come under our control.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose the middle view: that what is meant is stirring and describing the reality.

﴿Those who fight you, and do not transgress; indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾ [al-Baqarah 190]. Do not transgress in fighting. Transgression in fighting includes transgression against the rights of Allah and transgression against the rights of those fought.

As for transgression against the rights of Allah, it is like fighting them at a time when fighting is not permitted, for example, fighting them in the sacred months, according to the view that the prohibition of fighting in them has not been abrogated.

As for transgression against the fighters: that we not mutilate them. We do not mutilate them, based on the Messenger ﷺ's saying: "Do not mutilate." Nor do we kill a child, that is, a young boy, nor do we kill a woman, nor do we kill an aged elder, nor do we kill a monk in his cell, nor do we kill an old man who has no opinion in fighting. This is the meaning of transgression: do not transgress by fighting those who do not fight or do not assist in fighting.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾. This sentence here is the reason (ta'lil) for the ruling. Where is the ruling? ﴿Do not transgress﴾; ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾ is the reasoning. Are the transgressors in fighting only, or in fighting and other than it? The transgressors in fighting and other than it, because it is general; (al) here is general. It is a relative pronoun, since it is attached to a participle, and the (al) attached to a participle is regarded as a relative pronoun. Moreover, the cause is generally broader than the effect, broader.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾ (190). ﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them﴾ [al-Baqarah 190-191]. Whom does the pronoun in ﴿kill them﴾ refer to? To the disbelievers who fight us, by His saying: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you﴾.

﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them﴾: (haythu) is a adverb built on damma, an adverb of place or time? It is an adverb of place built on damma in the accusative position: kill them in any place.

Look: first He says: ﴿fight﴾, then He says: ﴿and kill﴾. Which is stronger? Killing is stronger. That is, whenever we find this combatant who fights us, actually or by implication, we kill him in any place, ﴿wherever you overtake them﴾. But there is an exception, which will come, Allah willing, in the verses: ﴿And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there﴾ [al-Baqarah 191].

* Student: Shaykh, what is the wisdom of the jizyah (...)?
* Shaykh: ﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them﴾, that is, in any place. What is excepted from it? The Sacred Mosque: ﴿Do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there﴾ [al-Baqarah 191].

﴿And expel them from where they expelled you﴾ [al-Baqarah 191]. He said: ﴿expel them from where﴾ and did not say: "expel them to where they expelled you," because expulsion is from one thing to another, whereas fighting is in a thing: fighting takes place in a place, and expulsion is from the place.

For this reason He said: ﴿expel them from where they expelled you﴾, that is, from the place from which they expelled you. For example, if it is assumed that the disbelievers prevailed over this land and expelled the Muslims from it, then the Muslims are obligated to fight them. When they fight them, will they expel them? Yes, they expel them from the lands from where they expelled us. They are the ones who transgressed against us and occupied our lands, so we expel them from where they expelled us.

Know that the people most worthy of Allah's lands are the righteous: ﴿And We had written in the Zabur, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 105].

And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous (al-muttaqin)﴾ [al-A'raf 128].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 189–195 (part 2 of 6):

The land belongs to no one in particular, nor to any particular people or group. The land is Allah's land. He bequeaths it to whomever He wills of His servants, and He has made clear that those who inherit it are His righteous servants. They are the ones who inherit it, both by the legislated command and by divine decree. By decree, Allah makes the good outcome belong to the God-fearing.

So, ﴿Expel them from where they expelled you﴾. We say: expel them from the lands from which they expelled you, because the right belongs to you. You are the ones who were wronged and driven out of your homes, so expel these disbelievers from them.

﴿And fitnah is worse than killing﴾ (al-Baqarah 191). What is fitnah? Fitnah is turning people away from their religion, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who persecute the believing men and believing women and then do not repent will have the punishment of Hellfire﴾ (al-Buruj 10). So persecuting people in their religion is worse than killing them, because the most killing can do is cut them off from the pleasures of this world, whereas fitnah cuts them off from both this world and the Hereafter. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If trial befalls him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾ (al-Hajj 11).

This indicates, though it should be listed among the benefits, that the colonization of ideas is worse than the colonization of lands, and that when disbelievers dominate Muslims by turning them away from their religion, that is greater than occupying their lands. Fitnah is worse than killing.

Did the Quraysh persecute the believers? Yes, they persecuted them with every kind of persecution. They tormented them, they killed them, and they made them suffer on scorching sand in the intense heat. It was harm beyond which there is no further harm. This is worse than killing. Even if it were assumed that Muslims killed some of the polytheists, the polytheists' persecution of the Muslims would be greater and more severe.

Student: Shaykh, the Muslims now have states. If one state is expelled from its lands, is it obligatory on all Muslims to…?

Shaykh: Yes, it is obligatory on them, when they are able, to help those people until they drive their enemies out of their lands.

Student: What about some states that have treaties with the disbelievers who expelled the Muslims? Is it obligatory on them, or not?

Shaykh: No. They should make the matter clear to them. But if the disbelievers break the treaty, then according to the scholars, when the treaty is broken against a group of believers, the treaty is void, even if there is a treaty between us and them. The Messenger (ﷺ) considered the Quraysh's breaking of the treaty, by aiding their allies, to be a violation of his treaty, even though they had only helped their allies against the allies of the Prophet (ﷺ), the allies of the Messenger, and they had not yet embraced Islam. So the Messenger (ﷺ) considered this a breach of the treaty. Therefore, if they attack any of the Muslims, they have broken the treaty. This will come, if Allah wills, in…

He says: ﴿And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there﴾ (al-Baqarah 191). Do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram, meaning in Makkah, because al-Masjid al-Haram itself is the mosque, and what surrounds it is the city. That is, do not fight them in Makkah until they fight you there.

Here, "fi" (in) is apparently for location, but it may also be for causation, meaning: until they fight you because of it.

﴿But if they fight you, then kill them﴾ (al-Baqarah 191). If they fight you even at al-Masjid al-Haram? Even at al-Masjid al-Haram. If they fight us even at al-Masjid al-Haram, then we will fight them.

Is this verse abrogated or not? No, this verse is not abrogated.

If someone says: the Messenger (ﷺ) said: «It was only permitted for me for an hour of a day, and it was not permitted for anyone before me, and if anyone permits himself to fight the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then say: Indeed, Allah permitted His Messenger, but He did not permit you»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1832) and Muslim (1354/446) from the hadith of Abu Shurayh al-'Adawi.]], then this is evidence that this verse is abrogated.

The answer to this is that the Messenger (ﷺ) only meant by this the fighting of the people of Makkah and entering upon them by force. That is not permissible. But if they fight us, then we fight them in self-defense. No one says that if a polytheist fights you in Makkah, you should surrender. Never. No one says this.

So we do not initiate fighting against them, even on the impossible hypothetical assumption that the people of Makkah apostatized. We would not fight them. I said "on the impossible hypothetical assumption" because the people of Makkah cannot apostatize. What is the evidence? The evidence is the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): «There is no hijrah after the conquest»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2783) and Muslim (1353/445) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]]. The negation of hijrah from Makkah after the conquest is evidence that it will remain a land of Islam. Otherwise, its people could apostatize and hijrah would become necessary from it.

In summary, we say: it is not permissible for us ever to initiate fighting against the people of the Haram. But if they fight us within the Haram, then we fight in self-defense until the strife subsides.

Therefore He said: ﴿But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ (al-Baqarah 191). "Such" refers to what preceded of the rulings concerning the command to fight. That is, a recompense like this, which is our command to you to fight the disbelievers who fight you. We recompense the disbelievers. Accordingly, the fighting is general for every disbeliever, because it is obligatory upon the Muslims to fight the disbelievers, as will come, Allah willing, in the verse after this, obligatorily.

Jihad in the way of Allah is in principle a collective obligation (fard kifayah), though it may become an individual obligation (fard 'ayn). The scholars mentioned that it becomes an individual obligation in several situations:

The first situation: when the enemy appears before a person, then it becomes an individual obligation on him, and he may not withdraw, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing [in battle], do not turn your backs to them. And whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless swerving [as a strategy] for war or joining [another] company, has certainly returned with anger from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾ (al-Anfal 15–16).

The second situation: when the enemy besieges one's city. If the enemy besieges him, fighting becomes specifically required, in order to lift the siege from the city, and because he resembles one who is present in the battle line.

The third situation: when the person is needed. If this man is needed by the people, whether for his opinion, his strength, or any work, then if he is needed, it becomes obligatory upon him.

The fourth situation: when the ruler calls the people to mobilize. If the ruler calls the people to mobilize, it becomes obligatory on them to go out, and no one may remain behind.

Otherwise, it is a collective obligation.

Know that an obligation, whether we say it is an individual obligation or a collective obligation, is not an obligation unless there is capability. Without capability there is no obligation, because of the general evidence that Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, and because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the ill, nor upon those who do not find anything to spend, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾ (al-Tawbah 91). So if we are unable to fight these people, it is not obligatory upon us. Otherwise, we would be sinning, all people together, while lacking capability. However, despite that, it is obligatory for us to have the resolve that if we become able, we will fight.

Therefore Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, restricted it: ﴿Nor upon those who do not find anything to spend﴾ (al-Tawbah 91). There is no blame on these three, on one condition, what is it? ﴿When they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾. But if they are not sincere to Allah and His Messenger, then blame falls on them, even if their excuses are valid in their case.

In summary, we say: fighting is a collective obligation, and it becomes an individual obligation in certain situations. This obligation, like other obligations, requires capability. In the case of incapacity, it is not obligatory. But it is obligatory that the resolve to fight be firmly held, so that when strength is available we strive in the way of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: «Whoever dies without having fought, and without having even resolved in his soul to fight, dies upon a branch of hypocrisy»[[Narrated by Muslim (1910/158) and Abu Dawud (2502), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], and we seek refuge in Allah.

There are readings (qira'at) here. What we have here: ﴿And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them﴾. The clauses are four: "and do not fight them," "until they fight you," "if they fight you," "then kill them." These are four clauses, all in the form of mufa'alah (reciprocal verb form, from qatala), except one, all in the form of "qatala" (fighting), except the last one: ﴿But if they fight you, then kill them﴾. Look at these readings I have. It says: ﴿And do not kill them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they kill you there. But if they kill you﴾, all four with the verb "qatala" without the mufa'alah form. ﴿And do not kill them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they kill you there, but if they kill you, then kill them﴾. Accordingly, all four are without the mufa'alah form. However, this reading is more eloquent, since Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade fighting except in response to fighting. When fighting occurs, do not restrict yourselves to mere fighting. What do you do? You kill. If they fight, then kill. This is more eloquent and more upright, although all of it is true, because all the readings were recited by the Prophet (ﷺ). Some of them indicate a meaning that the others do not. "Do not fight them" becomes "do not kill them until they kill you," but certainly it does not mean that you should not kill them until they kill all of you. If they kill all of you, there is nothing more. Rather, until they kill even one of you, because the killing of one of us is like the killing of all. For this reason, the scholars mentioned that when the protected people (ahl al-dhimmah, non-Muslims under a covenant of protection) break the covenant against one of the Muslims, the covenant is broken. They said: if he transgresses against a Muslim by killing, or by fornication, or something similar, his covenant is void, even though he has not broken the covenant with respect to the whole community. But one of us represents all of us, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said: «The protection of the believers is one; the least of them may extend it»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6755) and Muslim (1370/20) from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib.]].

﴿And if they cease, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (al-Baqarah 192). "If they cease," from what? From fighting. If they cease from fighting, then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: you should forgive them and not fight them.

Does this indicate that if they cease fighting, they are forgiven without becoming Muslim? No. But ﴿If they cease, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: forgive them, like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Except those who repent before you overpower them, so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (al-Ma'idah 34). That is, do not cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides, so long as they have repented. Likewise, these people, if they cease and do not fight you, then do not fight them.

Student: The verse may have another meaning, Shaykh: ﴿Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means that fighting is not obligatory upon you if they cease, because He is Forgiving toward you.

Shaykh: This also may be possible, ﴿And if they cease, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. There is some possibility in it, but it is somewhat remote. The apparent meaning is this. Some exegetes said: ﴿Then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward them, and they made "ceasing" general, covering cessation from fighting and from disbelief, like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease, they will be forgiven what has already passed﴾ (al-Anfal 38). So they made His saying ﴿If they cease﴾ mean from fighting you and from disbelief, ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Student: Even if they strike a large number of Muslims?

Shaykh: How?

Student: That is, they might begin the fighting and kill many, then say: that's it, we have ceased, we will stop?

Shaykh: We stop, but we call them to Islam. If they commit to the rulings of Islam, well and good; otherwise we kill them until we eliminate them.

Student: The answer to the condition…

Shaykh: No, it is the clause ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (…).

Student: It is a fronted predicate in every case.

Shaykh: It is a fronted predicate in every case.

Student: Would it become causal (explanatory)?

Shaykh: Which one?

Student: ﴿Then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Shaykh: If the discussion is about grammatical analysis (i'rab), then it is the answer to the condition in every case.

Student: And if we make it explanatory?

Shaykh: We do not need an explanation. We say: ﴿If they cease﴾, then Allah has described Himself as possessing forgiveness and mercy. So the meaning is: forgive them and show them mercy, do not confront them.

﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is for Allah﴾ (al-Baqarah 193). This is a decisive verse. ﴿Fight them until there is no fitnah﴾, meaning we must fight the disbelievers until there is no fitnah, that is, no turning away from the way of Allah, such that they do not transgress against anyone or lead him astray from his religion, whether it is everyone or some of them. Suppose we fought them, and they surrendered and abandoned fighting, but then began to slip books into the hands of Muslims, books of atheism and books of misguidance. Would we then stop fighting them? No, because Allah says: ﴿until there is no fitnah﴾. So we must fight them until they submit and their evil is completely removed. If any of their evil remains, then we are obligated to fight them.

For this reason He said: ﴿And religion is for Allah﴾. When we fight them and the rulings of Islam become the dominant ones, then religion is for Allah, and at that point we refrain from them. Otherwise, fighting them is obligatory. Unfortunately, these matters, although they are in the first surah of the Qur'an and in a Medinan surah revealed later, most of us are heedless of them. It is as if fighting has now become something merely mentioned rather than something that must be. It is as if they were theories, or the reading of past events and reports, as if we are not required to uphold them now. For this reason we have settled for this world, and the most important thing for us has become that this comfort remain for us. This insolence and arrogance is present among some people, and we have not paid attention to what we were created for, nor to what is obligatory upon us regarding the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Religion is now being crumbled everywhere, through means and methods. They do not come to a righteous country like ours, thanks be to Allah, and say: prostrate to idols, go to graves, seek refuge with the people of the graves. They do not say this, because they know that if they said this, children would stone them. Instead they slip in things by which they corrupt morals, and when morals are corrupted, there is no portion for us in the Hereafter.

The means that destroy morals are numerous and well known to many of you. For this reason their fitnah has become worse than killing. We have become content with these matters, our skins have grown cold, our resolve has weakened, until some of the Muslims now say: the Christians are our brothers. Allah says: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ (al-Kafirun 6). They have their religion and we have ours. What unites us is humanity! Humanity is what unites us! And the religion of Islam is a religion of breadth, a religion of mercy, and a religion of tolerance!

And similar things of this kind, by which they make comparisons. They do not know that the person who believes that the religion of the Christians is valid now is a disbeliever, because Allah says: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ (Al 'Imran 85), and He says: ﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam﴾ (Al 'Imran 19). This sentence is a restriction (hasr), with both its components defined: the subject and the predicate are both definite. ﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam﴾ means: there is no religion other than it. Even if they adhere to religion and enter monasteries, churches, and convents, that does not benefit them, and it is not permissible for us to believe it is a religion, because it is not a religion. Even if they hold to it, there is no religion in the sight of Allah. (…)

* * *

﴿They ask you about the crescent moons. Say: they are measures of time for the people and for Hajj…﴾ and so on to the end (al-Baqarah 189).

* In this noble verse there is the eagerness of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, for knowledge, and that they asked about matters of religion and matters of worldly life, because this is among what relates to the world.

* And in it there is also clarification. In it there is clarification of Allah's knowledge, His hearing, and His mercy. From where is this derived?

From his saying, ﴿they ask you﴾: God knew their question, heard it, and showed them mercy by answering.

* From the benefits of this verse: God, glorified and exalted is He, cares for His Messenger ﷺ, in that He answers the questions directed to him. This is part of God's support for the Messenger, peace be upon him, and His care for him, or not?

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the wisdom behind the crescent moons is that they are timekeepers for people in their religious and worldly affairs, based on His saying: ﴿Say: They are timekeepers for people and for the Hajj﴾.
And among its benefits, meaning: among the benefits of the noble verse, is that the timekeeping of all nations, the timekeeping which God has set for them, what is it? The crescent moons. So it is the universal timekeeper: ﴿timekeepers for people﴾, in general.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the Hajj is restricted to the (specific) months, based on His saying: ﴿and the Hajj﴾.

[It is] by adhering to what God has prescribed and being wary of disobeying Him, based on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿But righteousness is [in] one who fears God﴾.

* From its benefits: beliefs do not make what is not legislated into something legislated. From His saying: ﴿And it is not righteousness to enter houses from their backs﴾. Although they believed it to be righteousness, He said: ﴿It is not righteousness.﴾ So whoever believes in something not legislated, believing it to be righteousness, we tell him: it is not righteousness. If he believes it and draws closer to God through it, we warn him against that.

* A student: Shaykh (...) this faith (...) is this correct?

* The Shaykh: No. Because he did not take it as righteousness, he was not harmed by his adopting it. Once, when we were reaching the hadith, a man was asking me, saying: "By the Prophet, do you know such and such, by the Prophet?" I forbade him and said: "Brother, it is not permissible to swear by the Prophet. Swear by God, or do not swear." When he repeated the question, he said: "By the Prophet, I have never sworn by the Prophet in my life." It seems this was his situation.

We said: beliefs do not make what is not legislated into something legislated, because these people believed that righteousness is to enter houses from their backs. But God, the Exalted, invalidated this belief: ﴿But righteousness is [in] one who fears God﴾.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: a person should approach matters through their proper gates, based on His saying: ﴿And enter houses through their doors﴾. This verse includes sensory houses, and likewise it includes abstract matters.

* From the benefits of the verse: the obligation of God-consciousness (taqwa), based on His saying: ﴿And fear God﴾.

* From the benefits of the verse: taqwa is called righteousness. It has already been mentioned that when it is mentioned alone, it includes righteousness, and when righteousness is mentioned alone, it includes taqwa. When both are mentioned together, as in His saying: ﴿Cooperate in righteousness and taqwa﴾ [al-Ma'idah 2], righteousness becomes doing good or performing what is commanded, and taqwa becomes abstaining from what is forbidden.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: taqwa is a cause of success, based on His saying: ﴿so that you may succeed﴾. Taqwa has more than a hundred benefits. Some students previously wrote them down. We asked the students to write down the benefits of taqwa mentioned in the Qur'an only, and they wrote about a hundred, all of which are mentioned in the Qur'an. Whoever is able to do so should set aside half an hour, especially for one who has the Qur'an memorized by heart, and bring forth the benefits. This is good, and it will be a good deed for him.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And fight in the way of God those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors﴾ [al-Baqarah 190]. In this verse there is the obligation of fighting, based on His saying: ﴿And fight﴾; the obligation that it be in the way of God, that is, in His law and religion, based on His saying: ﴿in the way of God﴾; and the obligation of sincerity in it, based on His saying: ﴿in the way of God﴾.

* From its benefits: the speaker should mention to the addressee what will move him to comply.

* The students: ﴿those who fight you﴾.

* The Shaykh: Based on His saying: ﴿those who fight you﴾. This is if we say it is a qualifier for stirring up and encouragement. If we say it is a qualifier of meaning, intended to exclude those who do not fight us, the ruling differs.

* From the benefits of the verse: the prohibition of aggression, even against disbelievers, based on His saying: ﴿but do not transgress﴾. It is even more so against Muslims. For this reason, the Messenger ﷺ said: «Do not mutilate, do not embezzle from the spoils, do not betray, and do not kill a child»[[Reported by Muslim (1731) from the hadith of Buraydah al-Aslami, may God be pleased with him, with the wording: "Go out in the name of God, in the way of God. Fight those who disbelieve in God. Go out (to fight) and do not embezzle, do not betray, do not mutilate, do not kill a child. When you meet your enemy from among the polytheists, invite them to three (options)..." the hadith.]], because all of this is aggression.

* From the noble verse's benefits: affirmation of God's love. God loves. From where?

* A student: ﴿Indeed, God does not love the transgressors﴾.

* The Shaykh: Just that? ﴿Indeed, God does not love the transgressors﴾? This is a negation, and we are saying that the verse affirms God's love, meaning that God loves. This is a negation. What do you say?

* A student: That it be those who are not transgressors..

* Another student: Because it is not possible for one to not love except one who is of such a nature that he loves.

* The Shaykh: Yes. If He did not love at all, it would not be correct to negate His love only from the transgressors. His love is negated from these only while it is affirmed for others.

* From the benefits of the verse: the excellent teaching of God, the Mighty and Majestic, in that He pairs the ruling with its wisdom. The evidence?

* A student: ﴿do not transgress﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿but do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors﴾. We have previously mentioned that the benefits of (...) the wisdom are one, two, three. In the generality of the cause, the generality of the ruling by the generality of the cause, so it becomes four.

* A student: He mentioned it.

* Another student: This is qiyas (analogy).

* The Shaykh: Yes, but he did not state it. If qiyas is what he intended, but he did not express it, is it clear? The generality of the ruling by the generality of its cause. For example: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden immoralities, what is apparent of them﴾ [al-A'raf 33], and ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it, except that it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is an impurity﴾ [al-An'am 145]. ﴿Indeed it is an impurity﴾ is the cause. From it is derived that every impurity is forbidden, or not? So the benefits become four. Praise be to God, the benefits are four.

* A student: Is it deduction, or if it is qiyas..

* The Shaykh: Let us repeat them now, since we have not finished them. Let us repeat them. First: the explanation of the loftiness of the Sharia. Second: increasing the tranquility of the servant. Third: the generality of the ruling by the generality of the cause. But there is a fourth now, you mentioned..

* A student: The generality of the ruling by the generality of the cause.

* The Shaykh: That is it. This is what we mentioned last, and..

* Students: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, but if they become deduced, the qiyas becomes clear (...) the generality of the ruling by the generality of the cause. How did you count them as four, glory be to God?!

* Students: (...).

* The Shaykh: I did not understand that it is one.

* A student: Let us repeat them, Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: Let us count them. The explanation of the loftiness of the Sharia: this is one. Agreed?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Increasing the tranquility of the responsible person: this is two. Is each one different from the other, clear?

* A student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: And the third?

* The students: The generality of the ruling by the generality of the cause.

* The Shaykh: The generality of the ruling by the generality of the cause. What else?

* The students: And if it is qiyas.

* The Shaykh: And if it is qiyas. No, we did not count it. So they become three.

Good. Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them, and expel them from wherever they expelled you, and fitnah is worse than killing﴾, to the end. In this is the strengthening of the exhortation to fight these people. That is: kill them wherever you find them: ﴿kill them wherever you overtake them﴾. The pronoun in His saying ﴿kill them﴾ refers to ﴿those who fight you﴾, so what was mentioned before applies to it.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation to fight disbelievers wherever they are found, based on His saying: ﴿wherever you overtake them﴾. The obligation to fight them wherever they are found entails the obligation to fight them at any time they are found, because the generality of place entails the generality of time.

* Also from the benefits of the noble verse: that we expel these disbelievers as they expelled us, reciprocity, based on His saying: ﴿and expel them from wherever they expelled you﴾. For this reason the scholars said: if they mutilate us, we mutilate them; if they cut down our palm trees, we cut down theirs, like for like, equal for equal.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: that fitnah, through disbelief and barring from the way of God, is worse than killing. From this benefit it follows: the colonization of ideas is worse than the colonization of lands, or not?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Because the colonization of ideas is fitnah, while the colonization of lands, most of what it involves is either killing or plundering of resources and economies and the like. So fitnah is more severe, because it is the true killing, through which both religion and worldly life and the Hereafter are lost.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the glorification of the sanctity of the Sacred Mosque, based on His saying: ﴿And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque﴾.

* And also from its benefits: the permissibility of fighting at the Sacred Mosque if its people initiate it, based on His saying: ﴿until they fight you there﴾. If you say: Does this not contradict the saying of the Messenger of God ﷺ: «If anyone takes a concession to fight the Messenger of God ﷺ, say: God permitted His Messenger, but He did not permit you»[[Agreed upon; reported by al-Bukhari (1832) and Muslim (1354/446), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Abu Shurayh al-'Adawi.]]? If you say this contradicts the hadith?

* The students: No, it does not contradict it.

* The Shaykh: It does not contradict it. What is the difference, or what is the reconciliation? The reconciliation is that initiating fighting in order to enter Makkah is prohibited, forbidden, and not permissible under any circumstances. But if they fight us in Makkah, then we fight them by way of?

* The students: Defense.

* The Shaykh: By way of defense. For this reason we fight them only to the extent necessary to break their strength.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the strength of fighting the enemies, because He said: ﴿So if they fight you, then kill them﴾, meaning if they fight you in the Sacred Mosque, then kill them. As for the reading ﴿So if they kill you﴾, the meaning is: if they kill some of you, then let us kill them, because if they kill us, how can we kill them?! So the meaning is: they killed some of us, so let us kill them.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of God's justice, the Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿Such is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾, in that they fought, so we were permitted to fight them, and the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

* A student: O Shaykh, from His saying ﴿wherever you overtake them﴾, does it not imply the permissibility of fighting them in any place..

* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, except in Makkah. Except in Makkah is excepted, because He said: "at the Sacred Mosque." He said: ﴿So if they fight you, then kill them﴾. ﴿And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. So if they fight you, then kill them.﴾ Although it appears that the people of Makkah cannot apostatize, based on the saying of the Messenger, peace be upon him: «There is no hijrah after the conquest»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2783) and Muslim (1353/85) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both; the wording is al-Bukhari's.]], and this is a true report. But they may still fight, even if they are not disbelievers. So if they fight us there, we fight them.

﴿Such is the recompense of the disbelievers. But if they cease, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

From this noble verse is derived: the perfect justice of God, glorified and exalted, in that He made His rulings and punishments based on the aggression of those who deserve this punishment. Its direction? ﴿But if they cease, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: do not fight them, for He has forgiven them; or: forgive them and show them mercy. The meaning is that if these people cease fighting, then God's forgiveness and mercy encompass them.

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is for God. But if they cease, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾.

(...) This is a command limited by an end. Is the end negative or positive? Negative: ﴿until there is no fitnah﴾, meaning until fitnah does not exist. Fitnah is shirk and barring from the way of God. The second end is positive: ﴿and religion is for God﴾, meaning that religion is dominant and manifest, and nothing rises above Islam. Whatever is other than it is a religion subordinated, upon whose followers the jizyah (poll tax, a levy on non-Muslim subjects) is imposed, "from willing submission, while they are humbled." So fighting is obligatory until these two ends: that there be no fitnah, and second, that religion belong to God.

(...) is the subject, and (al-haram, "sacred") is its qualifier, and (bi-sh-shahr, "for the month") is a prepositional phrase serving as its predicate.

And His saying: ﴿and sacred things are subject to retribution﴾ is a subject and predicate. The meaning of His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿the sacred month for the sacred month﴾ is that the sacred month is in place of the sacred month.

He said: ﴿But if they cease, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾. ﴿If they cease﴾ means: from fighting you and return. ﴿Then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾, meaning that injustice has been removed from them, and then there is no aggression against them.

And His saying here: ﴿then there is no aggression﴾. It was said: its meaning is "then there is no way (against them)," as in His saying: ﴿Then there is no aggression against me, and God is Witness over what we say﴾ [al-Qasas 28]. This was in the story of Musa. The meaning of ﴿no aggression against me﴾ is: no way against me. It was said: there is no aggression against me, because He said: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him﴾. So the meaning of ﴿no aggression﴾ is: no fighting against them. This is of the type of responding to something with its like in wording, because the aggression is its cause.

﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to what he transgressed against you﴾: its meaning is not that your act is aggression, but since aggression became its cause, it is valid to express it with the same wording.

His saying: ﴿then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾. Where is the predicate of (lā, "there is no")? It is permissible for its predicate to be the prepositional phrase in His saying ﴿against the wrongdoers﴾, and it is permissible for its predicate to be omitted, the implied meaning being: then there is no aggression occurring or existing, except against the wrongdoers.

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿The sacred month for the sacred month﴾, and its discussion has already preceded.

This first sentence has two meanings. The first meaning: if they fight you in the sacred month, then fight them and do not regard that as grave, for your fighting them in the sacred month is like their fighting you in the sacred month, so this is in return for that.

It was also said: the meaning of ﴿the sacred month for the sacred month﴾ is that when they barred you at Hudaybiyah from performing the 'umrah in the sacred month, you would make it up in the sacred month of the following year. So your 'umrah in a sacred month would be in place of the sacred month, so the first sacred month is the sixth year after the Hijrah and the second is the seventh year after the Hijrah. That is: do not let it distress or grieve you, for if the 'umrah was missed in this month, it will not be missed in the second month. These are two meanings.
