* The student: And "those who purify themselves"..
* The Shaykh: Is that physical purification?
* The student: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: Fine, correct?
* The students: Correct.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Also derived from the noble verse: the justification (taʿlīl) of the legal rulings, based on His saying: ﴿It is a harm, so keep away﴾.
* Accordingly, it is also derived from it: the affirmation of the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that He does not legislate anything except for a wisdom. Is that not so?
Because He said: ﴿It is a harm, so keep away from women during menstruation.﴾ So since Allah gave this reason, it means He legislated it only for a wisdom, and this is what His name, Blessed and Exalted, al-Ḥakīm (the All-Wise), requires.
* Also derived from the noble verse, a benefit to consider: the wisdom of Allah, the Exalted, in a woman's menstruation. Some doctors said that there is a benefit for the man in it, because it restrains him from intercourse, and continuous intercourse is harmful to a person. There is a famous line of verse expressing this wisdom:
Three things destroy people, and they lead the healthy to sickness: continuous wine-drinking, continuous intercourse, and adding food upon food.
Yes, a man who has eaten, with his stomach foul, sweats on his friend, and when he has food, meat, sinew and the like, he eats the meat and sinew while his stomach is full. What is this? This is adding food upon food, which is dangerous for him. As for al-Madāmah, it is wine. It is well known that wine corrupts the mind, the religion and the body, especially when a person becomes addicted to it, may Allah protect us. Likewise intercourse exhausts the body. For this reason, among Allah's wisdoms, when a person has intercourse he must perform ghusl to purify himself and to restore the vigor of his body.
I say: can this benefit be derived from the verse: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in menstruation and in His command to men to keep away from women during it, so that they may to some degree preserve their health? Is this possible?
* A student: It is said that it was legislated for us because there is a benefit for us in our religion and our worldly life, since it contains harm for the man and the woman; that is why Allah forbade it to us, and all that He has legislated and permitted for us contains good.
* The Shaykh: There is no problem with that, but we want a specific benefit. Do we have evidence or not? We all know, thanks be to Allah, that Allah does not legislate anything except for a wisdom and for good for His servants in their livelihood and their hereafter. There is no problem with that. But we want that specific benefit: is it correct or not?
* A student: It seems that it is not clear, because the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted intercourse other than..
* The Shaykh: He permitted enjoyment?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Other than the genitals?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: But indeed that is correct.
* A student: I say: as for the woman, that is correct, but as for the man, it may (...).
* The Shaykh: No. Also, enjoyment other than the genitals can wear the body out even more, because that is natural enjoyment, while this is usually unnatural enjoyment, and it is not what Allah permitted.
In any case, I have withdrawn from this; there is no benefit in it.
Then He said, the Exalted.. is there a benefit other than this?
* A student: Regarding love, we said it is active. Why do we not say it is essential and active?
* The Shaykh: We may say it is essential and active. We can say so, because Allah knows that this man will be among those who repent and purify themselves, so He loves him, but He does not love him until this thing exists.
* A student: The affirmation of love (...), love and hatred for Allah. Is this what is established in the self?
* The Shaykh: It is established in the self without doubt. That is why we told you: active attributes are of two kinds: some are attributes of meaning and some are not; some are attributes of meaning and some are active. But we say that love is tied to the beloved, and the beloved is something that comes into being. However, Allah, the Exalted, knows that something will exist that He loves, so He loves that thing at the time of its existence.
* A student: Shaykh, some distinguish between ﴿taqrabūhunna﴾ and (taqrubūhunna)? That ﴿taqrabūhunna﴾ means to be involved with them, and (taqrubūhunna) means to draw near to them.
* The Shaykh: And which is preferable, what does it mean?
* The student: ﴿taqrabūhunna﴾ means you become involved with them.
* The Shaykh: No, no, that is not correct, because ﴿Do not approach fornication﴾ [al-Isra' 17:32] covers everything that leads to fornication. So he is forbidden from fornication and from its causes.
* The student: Shaykh, did He say it with the fatḥah because it is general and more comprehensive? Did He not say it with the ḍammah because it is specific to drawing near?
* The Shaykh: No, not at all. It is said qaruba yaqrubu and qarraba yaqrabu, but these are of the patterns that they call the wazn patterns, and I do not think there is this difference between them.
Then He said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:223].
* It is derived from this noble verse: that women are a tilth for men, meaning a place of cultivation.
* Also derived from this noble verse: that the man is free in this tilth: if he wishes he does, and if he wishes he does not, based on His saying: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾. However, according to some scholars it is limited to four months, or according to another view, to what custom has established.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the permissibility of coming to the woman in the place of the tilth from any direction, based on His saying: ﴿So come to your tilth however you wish﴾.
Is it also derived from the noble verse that it is legislated for a person to intend offspring in his intercourse?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: From where is it taken? Other than ﴿Put forward for yourselves﴾, in His saying: ﴿So come to your tilth﴾. Allah made coming to the tilth, as if it were an indication that a person should come to the woman in order to seek offspring. They have mentioned about Amir al-Mu'minin ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he had intercourse only with the intention of offspring, or only for the sake of offspring.
In any case, people differ on this, and there is no objection to a person intending offspring by it, and also intending the fulfillment of desire.
* Also derived from the noble verse: it is legislated for a person to put forward for himself during intercourse, based on His saying: ﴿And put forward for yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:223].
We have mentioned in the tafsir the meaning of His saying: ﴿And put forward for yourselves﴾, and that among its meanings is what?
Saying the basmalah, and intending to guard the chastity, and intending offspring, is that right?
* Also derived from the noble verse: that coming to the woman is among a person's private interests, based on His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And put forward for yourselves﴾. It is as if this is an indication from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that the benefit is for us and not for others, so put forward for yourself.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the obligation of fearing Allah, based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And fear Allah﴾.
* Also derived from it: the obligation of conducting oneself in dealing with one's family, both in coming to them and in abstaining from them, according to what? According to what Allah has legislated. That is because it is part of fearing Allah, so it is obligatory for you to conduct yourself in living with your family, in action and in restraint, according to what Allah has legislated.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the affirmation of the Resurrection. From where is this taken?
* A student: ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And know that you will meet Him.﴾
* Also derived from it: the affirmation of seeing Allah. From where is this taken?
* The students: ﴿That you will meet Him.﴾
* A student: It does not necessarily follow.
* The Shaykh: What is necessarily entailed by meeting in sight?
* A student: It does not necessarily follow.
* The Shaykh: He met him. What does that mean?
* A student: He faced him.
* The Shaykh: He faced him. And what is it that faces someone with its eyes covered? Some scholars used this verse as evidence that it indicates the affirmation of seeing Allah, because the basic meaning of meeting is the absence of a barrier. The basic meaning is the absence of a barrier, so it indicates the affirmation of seeing Allah.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the warning to a person against disobedience, because when He commanded taqwā (God-consciousness), He said: ﴿And know that you will meet Him.﴾

* It is part of eloquence (balagha) that when you inform a person of an important matter, you precede the report with something that calls for his attention. From where? 

* The students: ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿And know﴾. He did not say, "Fear Allah, for you will meet Him." He said, ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾, and this increases a person's attention and his preparation for that meeting.

* It is derived from the noble verse that the believers are saved from the defilements of this meeting, because of His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾.

* It is derived from it that the good tidings for the believers are unrestricted, since He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ and did not mention what they are good tidings of.

* It is derived from the noble verse that the good tidings for the believers are both in this world and in the Hereafter. The reason is the absence of restriction. Allah the Exalted has said in another verse: ﴿For them is good news in the worldly life and in the Hereafter﴾ [Yunus 64]. The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the good dream that a man sees or that is seen for him, and he said: «That is the early good tiding of the believer»[[Narrated by Muslim (2642 / 166) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]].

* It is derived from the noble verse: a warning to those who are not believers about this meeting. From where is this taken? Because when He commanded us to know that we would meet Him, He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, meaning: and warn those who are not believers. This is close to His saying: ﴿And He made for you garments that protect you from the heat﴾ [An-Nahl 81].

* The students: That means: and garments that protect you from the cold.

* The Shaykh: That protects you from the heat and the cold. So here He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾.

* It is derived from the noble verse: the virtue of faith, because Allah tied the good tidings to them, saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾.

* It is derived from it: the permissibility of a man having intercourse with his wife from her back, through her front (vulva). The evidence is His saying: ﴿So come to your tilth however you wish﴾. The Jews, may Allah's curses be upon them, used to say that if a man has intercourse with his wife from behind through her front, the child will be cross-eyed. Allah the Mighty and Majestic refuted them.

* A student: Shaykh, is it derived from His saying: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, an exhortation for men to guard their wives, since He said: ﴿your wives﴾ and said: ﴿a tilth for you﴾?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is derived from it. From the attribution ﴿your wives﴾ and ﴿a tilth for you﴾ it is derived that a person should guard this woman who has been attributed to him, and that she is his tilth, just as he guards the tilth of his land.

* It is also derived from it another benefit: that a person should not reduce offspring, because of His saying: ﴿a tilth for you﴾. If she is a tilth, when a person cultivates land, does he reduce the planting or does he increase the planting?

It is increased. This is the usual practice, without doubt. He increases the planting. So we say: it is also incumbent upon a person to increase children as much as he can.

As for the claim of limiting offspring, this is undoubtedly one of the schemes of the enemies of the Muslims. They want the Muslims not to multiply, because if they multiply, they will frighten them. If they multiply, they become self-sufficient and do not need them. If they multiply, they cultivate the land and run commerce, and the economy rises and so on. But if they remain few and weak, they become humiliated and need others in everything.

What is your opinion of a woman who says: "I want to take contraceptive pills, because when I become pregnant I get tired. Before pregnancy I used to climb to the roof and come down, go out and come back, sit calmly and stand calmly. But when I became pregnant, the belly grew large and the child became heavy, and I became tired. I stand over my cooking pot while kneading, and I sit with great difficulty, and I cannot climb the stairs, and when the delivery comes, do not ask about the exhaustion"? What do we say? "May Allah magnify your reward," what... "May Allah magnify your reward." But we say: this is a natural matter, for Allah says: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 15]. ﴿And We have enjoined upon man concerning his parents. His mother carried him in weakness upon weakness﴾ [Luqman 14]. This is a matter that cannot be avoided. How can a child come without any hardship?!

* A student: And do not let him marry another woman. She swallows the pills, and does not let him marry anyone else.

* The Shaykh: Amazing, this is the problem.

* A student: Shaykh, regarding His saying: ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾ [Al-Baqarah 223], the meeting includes both the disbeliever and the believer, and the seeing is specific to the believer?

* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. But the meeting of the disbeliever may be veiled from him by Allah, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 15].

* A student: So there is no evidence in it?

* The Shaykh: No, there is not. Because the basic principle regarding meeting is that there is no veiling unless there is evidence. What is it that meets someone without looking?

* A student: But, is every believer going to see Allah in Paradise?

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* A student: Every believer?

* The Shaykh: Every believer in Paradise sees Allah.

* A student: Are there not degrees in Paradise?!

* The Shaykh: Yes, there are degrees, but they differ in seeing Allah. Some of them see Him every day, and some see Him every week or every month, Allah knows best. But there is no doubt that they differ. Rather, every believer will see Allah: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 22-23], ﴿and faces that Day will be dismal, thinking that something of disaster is about to be inflicted upon them﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 24-25]. Allah did not mention other faces.

Then He said: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you will be righteous and conscious of Allah and make reconciliation among the people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [Al-Baqarah 224].

* The student: Is this not considered an objection to Allah?

* The Shaykh: What is it?

* The student: Limiting offspring (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, it is not an objection to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, but it is contrary to what is preferable. The Companions used to practice withdrawal (al-'azl) while the Qur'an was being revealed, and 'azl means preventing conception.

* A student: For an apparent reason?

* The Shaykh: No, the Messenger did not command them.

* A student: I say: for a reason. They did not present it to the Messenger ﷺ, so he went (...).

* The Shaykh: No. The hadith of Jabir: «We used to practice withdrawal while the Qur'an was being revealed»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5207) and Muslim (1440 / 136), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.]]. But they asked the Messenger about withdrawal, and he said: «That is the hidden burying alive»[[Narrated by Muslim (1442 / 141) from the hadith of Judamah bint Wahb.]].

This indicates that the preferable course is to abandon it, and that it should not be done except out of necessity. However, the scholars say: it is forbidden for a man to practice withdrawal with a free wife without her permission, because offspring is her right.

﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you will be righteous and conscious of Allah and make reconciliation among the people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾.

* It is derived from the noble verse: the prohibition of excessive swearing, because of His saying: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾. This is because the verse has two meanings, as mentioned earlier. But according to the view of those who say: ﴿do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾ means do not swear by Him excessively in order to be among the people of righteousness, piety and reconciliation, then according to this opinion there is evidence in the verse that a person should not swear by Allah excessively. And this is supported by His saying: ﴿And guard your oaths﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 89].

According to the second opinion, it is derived from it that a person should not, or a person is forbidden from, making an oath a barrier that prevents him from righteousness, piety and reconciliation. So the meaning differs, does it not?

It differs, because the meaning according to the second view is that if a person swears to something and it is an act of righteousness, he should not say, "By Allah, I will not do it, because I swore to abandon it." If he swears to do something that is forbidden, he should not do it and say, "Because I swore." Therefore He said: ﴿that you will be righteous﴾, this concerns doing good; ﴿and conscious of Allah﴾ concerns doing or abandoning what is forbidden; ﴿and make reconciliation among the people﴾ is clear.

* It is derived from the noble verse: the obligation of reverence toward Allah the Mighty and Majestic according to the first meaning, because of His saying: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾.

* It is derived from it: that if a person has sworn an oath and sees something better than it, he should do the good and make expiation for the oath, because of His saying: ﴿that you will be righteous and conscious of Allah and make reconciliation among the people﴾.

* It is derived from it: the exhortation to righteousness. Its reasoning is that if Allah has forbidden us from making an oath a barrier to doing righteousness, then how much more so when there is no oath at all?!

And likewise the exhortation to piety and to reconciliation.

* It is derived from the noble verse: the virtue of reconciling between people, because of His saying: ﴿and make reconciliation among the people﴾. He specified it even though it is part of righteousness. Specifying something after generalizing indicates what? It indicates concern for it and attention to it. There is no doubt that reconciliation between people is among important matters, because it mends rifts, gathers scattered affairs and unites the community. This is the opposite of those who, may Allah protect us, do things that cause estrangement between people, such as tale-bearing (namimah). Tale-bearing causes estrangement between people. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «The tale-bearer will not enter Paradise»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6056) and Muslim (105 / 168), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.]].

* The Shaykh: * It is derived from it: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, As-Sami' (the All-Hearing) and Al-'Alim (the All-Knowing), and what they include of attributes, and what they include of ruling and effect.

* It is derived from it: a warning to a person against opposition. Its reasoning is that if Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, then beware of opposing what He has commanded you. For if you oppose Him in what your hearing hears and what your knowledge knows, then beware of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

* A student: Regarding the first opinion on oaths, he says: "Do not make Allah (...)."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 222–224 (part 1 of 4):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They ask you about menstruation.﴾ This sentence is linked to the preceding sentences in which the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ asked questions. This differs from the questions of the Jews to their prophet Musa (peace be upon him), when he commanded them to slaughter a cow, and they said: ﴿Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is﴾ [al-Baqarah 68], until Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they were not about to do it﴾ [al-Baqarah 71]. As for the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, they asked the Prophet ﷺ about the rulings so that they might act in accordance with what the answer required.

His saying: ﴿about menstruation (al-mahid)﴾. The word al-mahid may be a noun of place or time (mim-prefixed verbal noun), so it can mean the menstruation itself, and it can be a noun of place, meaning the place of menstruation, or a noun of time, meaning the time of menstruation. Let us consider which of these possibilities best fits the context of the verse. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: it is an injury﴾. This is the answer, ﴿it﴾, i.e., menstruation (al-mahid), ﴿is an injury (adha)﴾. This supports the first possibility, that al-mahid is a mim-prefixed verbal noun, meaning that they ask you about menstruation: ﴿Say: it is an injury.﴾ An injury to whom? To the husband, to the wife, or to both together? Medicine has established that it is an injury to both of them together, and that it causes harm to the husband just as it causes harm to the woman. For this reason He said: ﴿it is an injury﴾. The word adha applies to something disliked and to something repulsive, and it is indeed both.

﴿So keep away from women during menstruation﴾. The fa' here is for consequence or causation, meaning: upon its being an injury, there follows the directive to you to keep away from women; or, because of its being an injury, keep away from women during menstruation. His saying: ﴿keep away from women﴾ means the menstruating women, as shown by His saying: ﴿during menstruation﴾. The word al-mahid here means both the place of menstruation and its time: keep away from women, so do not have intercourse with them in their private parts, because that is the place of menstruation, and not during the time of menstruation, because that is the time of menstruation. Thus al-mahid here is both a adverb of time and an adverb of place: keep away from women during menstruation. As for His saying: ﴿keep away from women﴾, in what respect? There is no doubt that it means sexual intercourse. It does not mean that we should keep away from them in eating together, drinking together, or living together; no. Because what the prohibition relates to, namely the place or time of menstruation, is benefited from only by what? By sexual contact, by intercourse. So the meaning is: keep away from them in intercourse.

﴿And do not approach them until they are purified﴾. ﴿Do not approach them﴾, i.e., the women during menstruation, until they are purified. In His saying ﴿do not approach them﴾ there is evidence that it is obligatory to avoid intercourse and what is around it. On this basis, it is not permitted for a man, with his wife when she is menstruating, to enjoy anything except what is above the waist-wrapper; as for what is below it, it is not permitted, because Allah says: ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them﴾. Many of the people of knowledge held this view, as we will explain, Allah willing, in the benefits (fawa'id).

His saying: ﴿And do not approach them until they are purified, then when they have purified themselves﴾. In another reading: ﴿until they purify themselves (yattahharna), then when they have purified themselves (tatahharna)﴾. This reading suits the following sentence. As for the reading ﴿until they are purified (yathurna)﴾, the meaning is: until they become clean from menstruation. The two readings, then, are: ﴿yattahharna﴾, i.e., they wash themselves (yaghtasilna), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves (fattahharu)﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6]; so ittihar means ghusl (ritual bathing). As for ﴿yathurna﴾, the meaning is: they become clean from menstruation. It is said: the woman became clean (tahurat) from her menses, i.e., it ceased. The sign of a woman's purity is the white discharge (al-qassah al-bayda'), namely that a cotton swab does not get stained when she inserts it; i.e., if the cotton is inserted into the private part and comes out white, this is the sign of purity. This is the usual case among women, that purity is whiteness; but some women do not see this, and they know purity only by the cessation of menstruation and do not see the white discharge. On this basis, the noble verse indicates the prohibition of approaching a woman until she is purified from menstruation, and purity is determined according to the woman's condition; the usual sign of purity is the white discharge.

His saying: ﴿Then when they have purified themselves, come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾. ﴿Purified themselves﴾: is the purification meant washing the whole body, or is it purifying the place from blood even if she has not bathed?

* A student: The first.
* The Shaykh: Some scholars held that what is meant is that they wash off the menstrual blood. But the majority of the people of knowledge hold that ﴿when they have purified themselves﴾ means they have bathed. They said: the Qur'an explains part of itself by part, for Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6], and the meaning of ﴿purify yourselves﴾ is not "wash away the traces of janabah" but "bathe." Accordingly, His saying ﴿when they have purified themselves﴾ means they have bathed. According to the reading ﴿until they purify themselves, then when they have purified themselves﴾ there is no difference between the two clauses. But according to the reading ﴿until they are purified, then when they have purified themselves﴾, the apparent meaning of the noble verse, with ﴿until they are purified﴾, is that once the woman becomes pure, her intercourse is not like her intercourse before purity, even though it is prohibited. But is it not like it?
* The students: Before purity.
* The Shaykh: Yes, that is so. Intercourse with her after she has become pure but before she has bathed does not require expiation according to the view that it is obligatory. Also, it permits her to fast once she has become pure, though she has not yet bathed. Also, divorce becomes permissible, because she is now pure and so divorce is in the period of 'iddah. It thus becomes clear that there is a difference in rulings between being pure (tuhr) and purifying oneself (tatahhur).

His saying: ﴿Then when they have purified themselves, come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾. The fa' here connects the answer to the conditional, which is His saying ﴿when they have purified themselves﴾. His saying ﴿come to them﴾ means have intercourse with them; the coming is a euphemism for intercourse.

His saying ﴿come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾. It is said: min here means fi (in), i.e., come to them in the place Allah has commanded you to come, namely the private part. It is also said: min is for beginning and remains in its basic sense, i.e., come to them by this way, from where Allah has commanded you. What has Allah commanded us? ﴿Come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾: Allah has commanded us to have intercourse with them in the private parts, as shown by His saying in the following verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾. The tilth is the place of sowing, and the place of sowing is the front passage (al-qubul). So the meaning of ﴿come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ is: from their front passage, and not from the rear. And His saying ﴿come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾ does not specify the direction from which the woman is approached. For this reason it is permissible for a man to have intercourse with his wife from the front or from behind, that is, from in front or from behind, but in one orifice only, namely the private part: ﴿come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾.

Ibn Hazm, may Allah have mercy on him, held that it is obligatory upon a man to have intercourse with his wife every time she becomes pure, based on His saying ﴿Then when they have purified themselves, come to them﴾, since the basic meaning of a command is obligation.
* A student: Obligation and immediacy.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. But the majority disagreed with him, as will come, Allah willing, in the explanation in the benefits.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾. This is a justification for the preceding commands: keeping away from women during menstruation, and coming to them from where Allah has commanded. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant﴾, i.e., He rewards them for their repentance.
* A student: .(...)
* The Shaykh: No, how? Your teacher who is saying it now, your teacher says: "loves" means "rewards those who repent for their repentance."
* A student: The teacher interpreted it first, so we cannot...?
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: The teacher went first.
* Students: Interpretation (ta'wil).
* The Shaykh: Yes, that means that if our teacher errs, we must correct him. So: ﴿loves the constantly repentant﴾. Love is an attribute distinct from reward; reward is one of the effects and necessary consequences of love. Love is an attribute of the Essence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, a real love befitting His majesty and greatness, not resembling the love of creatures for creatures. This is what the early generations of this Ummah and its imams held. This matter has been discussed often, and we have explained that some people of knowledge, indeed some Muslims, distorted this meaning and said that the meaning of "loves" is "rewards," but this is not correct.

His saying: ﴿at-tawwabin (constantly repentant)﴾. The word tawwab is on the pattern fa''al, and the pattern fa''al comes for intensity, i.e., abundance, and it also comes to denote attribution even if it happened only once. What is meant here? ﴿at-tawwabin﴾ those who repent much, or ﴿at-tawwabin﴾ those attributed to repentance even if only once?
* A student: It includes this and that.
* The Shaykh: Apparently it includes both, it includes this and that. We should not restrict it to mere attribution, because if we restricted it to mere attribution, then whoever sins, repents, sins, repents, sins, repents, would be unloved by Allah. Yet Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah loves the constantly repentant﴾. Even the one who frequently commits sin and follows it with repentance, Allah, Glorified and Exalted, loves him. For this reason, it is not a condition of repentance that one never returns to sin. That is not one of its conditions. The condition of repentance is that one resolves not to return to it. If he returns, and his soul tempts him to return, then Allah accepts his repentance if he repents. So the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, loves the constantly repentant. Who are the constantly repentant? The constantly repentant are those who repent much. And repentance is returning from disobedience of Allah to obedience to Him. We have previously mentioned that its conditions are five?
* A student: Giving up the sin, regret for what was done, and not returning to the sin.
* The Shaykh: And not returning, or resolving not to return?
* The student: And resolving not to return to the sin; I know three of them.
* Another student: And if it involves rights, returning the rights and wrongs to their owners.
* The Shaykh: No, that is included in giving up the sin.
* A student: That it be before death and before the sun rises from the west.
* The Shaykh: That it be in the time of acceptance.
* The student: In the time of acceptance, and before the sun rises in the west.
* The Shaykh: The time of acceptance includes this and that. One more remains?
* A student: Sincerity.
* The Shaykh: Sincerity to Allah. So the conditions of repentance are five: sincerity to Allah, regret for the sin, giving it up, resolving not to return, and that repentance be in the time of acceptance. As for the first, the condition of repentance is sincerity, because repentance is among the most noble acts of worship, and acts of worship require sincerity. So if a person repents from his sin out of regard for someone's feelings or to show off to people, his repentance is not accepted. And if he does not regret what passed of the sin, and committing the sin and abstaining from it become equal, his repentance is not accepted, because he was not truthful in his return. The truthful returner is the one who regrets and says: "I wish I had not done it." And if he does not give it up, he is not truthful; rather, he is closer to mockery than to repentance. A man says: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You from backbiting," then says: "O so-and-so, did you see that bad-tempered fellow?" Did he repent or not?
* A student: He did not repent.
* The Shaykh: He did not repent. Someone says: "O Allah, I repent to You from consuming usury," then says: "Come here, boy, take a hundred for a hundred and twenty." Is he repentant?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: He has not repented. Someone says: "O Allah, I repent to You from wronging people's rights," yet before the judge he claims what is not his and denies what he owes. Is he repentant?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: He is not repentant; he is not a penitent. Repentance is returning, and this one has not returned. The fourth: resolving not to return in the future. If he does not resolve, he is not truthful in his repentance; it is as though he says, "I will not return," while inwardly, if the opportunity arose, he would commit the sin. This is not a penitent.
The fifth: that it be in the time of acceptance, which is: before the appointed time arrives. If it is after the appointed time has come and hope has ended, it is not accepted, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾ [al-Nisa' 18]. It does not benefit after one has witnessed the punishment. ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾ [Ghafir 84-85]. ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims"﴾ [Yunus 90]. What was said to him? ﴿Now?﴾ [Yunus 91]. It does not benefit: ﴿Now, while you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus 91]. This is not repentance. Likewise, repentance is not accepted once the sun rises from the west; when it rises from the west, repentance does not benefit. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith﴾ [al-An'am 158]. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, explained some of the signs of Allah as the sun rising from the west. And in a hadith from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "Migration will not cease until repentance ceases, and repentance will not cease until the sun rises from its west."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2479) from the hadith of Mu'awiyah.]] These are the conditions of repentance. Is it a condition of repentance that one give up all sins, or is repentance from one sin valid while persisting in another? Let us now look at the conditions we have: is it among the conditions that one not persist in a sin?
* A student: No.
* The Shaykh: No. So repentance from one sin is valid while persisting in another. But this penitent does not deserve the absolute description of the penitent, because one who has repentance from some but not repentance in general does not deserve the unqualified description of the penitent, nor the unqualified praise and commendation for the penitent. Some people of knowledge said: repentance from one sin is not valid while persisting in another of the same kind. Do you understand? For example, if he repents from forbidden looking but speaks forbidden words with women, is his repentance accepted? Some scholars said: it is not accepted, because the kind is one. Likewise, if he repents from fornication, the illicit intercourse, while persisting in illicit looking, touching, walking, and speech, it is not accepted, because the kind is one. But the majority hold that this is not a condition, and that repentance from one sin is valid while persisting in another, even of the same kind.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and loves those who purify themselves﴾. Repentance is purification of the heart, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ is purification of the bodies: He loves those who purify themselves from impurities and filth, and among them are those who abstain from intercourse with a menstruating woman, because they are in reality purified. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves the constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾. ﴿Your wives﴾ means your spouses. ﴿A tilth for you﴾, i.e., a place of sowing for you, just as the earth is a tilth for the farmer, into which he casts the seed, and the seed comes forth, grows, and is benefited from. Likewise, women are, for men, a tilth into which a man deposits this gushing water, which is sown in the womb until it grows and emerges as a complete human being. Thus women are a tilth for men. For this reason He said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth﴾. The fa' here is for causation or consequence: ﴿so go to your tilth however you wish﴾. What is meant by tilth here? The place of sowing, which is the private part. Go to it ﴿however you wish﴾: (anna) here means "where," so it is an adverb of place, meaning: come to this tilth from whatever direction you wish: from the front, i.e., from in front; from behind; from the side; from any direction. The main thing is that the coming be into the tilth. The Jews claimed that if a man came to his wife from her rear while in her front passage, the child would be cross-eyed, and they lied in that; and Allah revealed their refutation in this verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾. The benefits on these sentences, many benefits, will come, Allah willing.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 222–224 (part 2 of 4):**

He said: ﴿And send forth for yourselves﴾. And what is it that one sends forth? One sends forth acts of obedience and what benefits us with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He said ﴿send forth for yourselves﴾ after His saying ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾ so that we would not become preoccupied with these women from sending forth what benefits us on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And send forth for yourselves﴾. Among sending forth for oneself is that a person seeks, through intercourse, the protection of his own chastity and the chastity of his wife, seeks righteous offspring, says the basmalah (tasmiyah) during intercourse, and similar righteous deeds that accompany intercourse through intention. For example, a man may have intercourse with his wife, but among people there is one who only desires the mere satisfaction of his need. This is undoubtedly beneficial, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "And in the intimacy of one of you there is a charity." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, does one of us fulfil his desire and still have a reward for it?" He said: "Do you not see that if he had placed it in the unlawful, would he have a burden of sin? Likewise, if he places it in the lawful, he has a reward."[[Recorded by Muslim (1006 / 53) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] But more beneficial than that is what Allah pointed to in this noble verse: ﴿So go to your tilth﴾ ﴿and send forth for yourselves﴾. By what?

* Student: By righteous deeds.
* Shaykh: By intention in the righteous deed that follows from intention. A person intends, for example, by his intercourse, the satisfaction of his need, the enjoyment of what Allah has permitted him, and self-sufficiency through it from what Allah has forbidden. Second: he intends by it the protection of his chastity and the chastity of his wife, because there is no doubt that this contains protection of chastity. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "If one of you sees a woman who pleases him, let him go to his wife, for with her is what is with that woman (meaning with his wife) like what is with her."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (1158) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]] So intercourse is a protection of chastity; otherwise the soul would become attached to the one he saw and temptation would occur.
Third: he intends by his intercourse that Allah, Exalted, grant him a righteous child. How excellent is a child when a person is granted a righteous child who benefits him in his life and after his death. The Prophet ﷺ said: "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three: an ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is derived, or a righteous child who prays for him."[[Recorded by Muslim (1631 / 14) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]
Fourth: that he does what should be done during intercourse, such as saying the basmalah during intercourse, saying: "In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You have provided us." The Prophet ﷺ said: "For if a child is decreed between them, Satan will never harm him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (141) and Muslim (1434 / 116) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] All of this falls under the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And send forth for yourselves﴾.
Then He said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾. Allah is greatest! When He commanded us to send forth for ourselves, He commanded us to avoid what Allah has forbidden us, so He said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾. This includes everything related to women in the matter of intercourse that contradicts the law of Allah, such as having intercourse with her in the rear, for this is not from the piety of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rather it is from disobedience to Him.
As for His saying: ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾, look at ﴿know﴾. This is an alert to a person that he should know. It is like His saying, Exalted: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been set forth, so listen to it﴾ [Al-Hajj 73]. Listen to the parable. Here He said ﴿know﴾ as an alert, because you should know that you will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that you will meet Him﴾. Is this meeting a real meeting, or is the intended meaning ﴿meeting Him﴾ meaning meeting His reward or His punishment? The first: a real meeting, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "None of you will be without Allah speaking to him, with no interpreter between him and Allah."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7443) and Muslim (1016 / 67) from the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim.]] Every person will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so prepare for this meeting. Look at what you have prepared for it. By Allah, this meeting is not far; how near it is. However long time seems to you, it is close. ﴿As if, on the day they see what they were promised, they had not remained but an hour of a day﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 35]. ﴿As if, on the day they see it, they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [Al-Nazi'at 46]. How swift is this meeting that will be between you and your Lord, when He speaks to you, the Mighty and Majestic, speaking directly to you with no interpreter between you and Him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "He looks to his right and sees only what he sent forth; he looks to his left, the more wretched side, and sees only what he sent forth; and he looks in front of his face and sees only the Fire before his face. So protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date."[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (7512) from the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim.]] As for His saying ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾, does that include looking at the Noble Face of Allah? Yes, it perhaps includes it. It may include it, as some scholars have used it as evidence, or some scholars have used it as evidence for the affirmation of seeing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the Hereafter.
Then He said, after this great warning: ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾. If our hearts were alive, this statement would have an impact on our souls, because it is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, introduced with ﴿know﴾. But by Allah, the hearts are dead, and complaint is to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then, after bringing this great, warning, frightening sentence, He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾. Praise be to Allah. ﴿Give good tidings to the believers﴾. This meeting is a meeting of goodness. Here He said ﴿give good tidings to the believers﴾ and did not mention what the good tidings are, so that it is general for everything in it that is good news in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Those who believed and were fearing Allah. For them are good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter﴾ [Yunus 62–64]. For this reason He said here: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ and did not mention the time of the good tidings, nor their place, nor their type. Therefore it is good tidings that are general and comprehensive. Indeed, the Messenger ﷺ said: "That is the early good tidings for the believer: the true dream that he sees, or that is seen for him."[[Recorded by Muslim (2642 / 166) from Abu Dharr.]] So you give every believer good tidings of every goodness, even in meeting Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; give him good tidings, for when Allah, Glorified and Exalted, confronts the believer with his sins, what does He say to him? He says: "I concealed them for you in this world, and today I forgive them for you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441) and Muslim (2768 / 52) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar.]] An easy reckoning, with the end being this great good news: "I concealed them for you in this world, and today I forgive them for you."

* Student: Shaykh, does this verse have another occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul)?
* Shaykh: Which one?
* Student: The verse ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 223].
* Shaykh: Yes, we mentioned it a little while ago: the story of the Jews who said that if a man has intercourse with his wife from behind, into her front, the child will be cross-eyed. So Allah said: ﴿So go to your tilth however you wish﴾.
* Student: Some exegetes said that the Muhajirun used to do such-and-such and the Ansar did not?
* Shaykh: It is included in this. I say: it is included in this.

He says: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths to be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾. The scholars differed concerning His saying, Exalted: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾. Some of them said: the meaning is, do not multiply swearing when you intend righteousness, piety and reconciliation. Do not multiply swearing by Allah, so do not make Allah constantly exposed to your oaths. There is no doubt that this is forbidden, and that a person should not multiply swearing by Allah. Rather, there must be in his heart such glorification of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that prevents him from making Him an obstacle in everything, exposing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in everything.

Some exegetes said: do not make Allah a barrier to your oaths preventing you from righteousness, piety, and reconciliation among people. ﴿Do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths to be righteous﴾, meaning an obstacle preventing you from righteousness, piety and reconciliation. This meaning is closer than the first, although the first is a possible meaning. But this one is closer, and it is supported by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "By Allah, if Allah wills, I will not swear to an oath and then see other than it as better, except that I will release myself from my oath and do that which is better."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3133) and Muslim (1649 / 7) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] He also said to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah: "If you swear an oath and then see other than it as better, expiate for your oath and do that which is better."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6622) and Muslim (1652 / 19) from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah.]] Based on this, the meaning of the verse is: do not make your oaths an obstacle preventing you from righteousness. And His saying ﴿an tabarru﴾ (that you be righteous) is to be interpreted as a verbal noun in the accusative by omitting the preposition, meaning: an obstacle away from your righteousness (ʿurḍatan ʿan birrikum). And His saying ﴿an tabarru﴾ is when one swears to abandon an obligation: we say, do not let the oath prevent you from performing an obligation. What does he do?

* Student: He expiates for his oath.
* Shaykh: He expiates for his oath and performs the obligation. For example, if he says: "By Allah, I will not speak to so-and-so," and so-and-so is a believer whose boycott is forbidden. We now say: you swore, and what is it upon him?
* Student: An expiation (kaffarah).
* Shaykh: For what?
* Student: For abandoning the obligation.
* Shaykh: For abandoning the obligation. So it is obligatory upon you to expiate for your oath and to speak to him. He says: "By Allah, I will not pray with the congregation." Pray with the congregation, boy, pray with the congregation. "No, by Allah, out of defiance toward you, by Allah I will not pray with the congregation." This may happen from some foolish people. What do we say to him? Pray with the congregation. He says: "By Allah, I swore, it's already done, an oath has passed from me." What do we say to him? Do not make Allah an obstacle to your oaths from righteousness. Perform the obligation and expiate for your oath.

As for His saying ﴿and fear Allah﴾, this is in the case where one swears to perform a forbidden act, not to abandon an obligation, to perform a forbidden act. He says: "By Allah, I will deny the property of so-and-so that I owe." He swore to what?

* Student: Something forbidden.
* Shaykh: To performing a forbidden act, which is denying a right that is obligatory upon him. What do we say to him? We say: expiate for your oath and render the right to its owner. "By Allah, I swore an oath, it has passed from me that I will deny it." We say: this oath does not hinder you from piety. Fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and do what Allah has obligated you to do, giving the one with the right his right.

Now, a person says: "By Allah, I will hit so-and-so." He had committed no crime, but something has arisen in his soul against him, and he says: "By Allah, I will hit so-and-so." A dispute has arisen between them, and he says: "By Allah, I will hit him. By Allah, I will not be done until I wound his head and break his neck." What do we say? We say: O brother, this is forbidden. Fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, expiate for your oath, and do that which is better. Expiate for your oath and do not hit this man, or break his neck, or not. For this reason the scholars said: breaking an oath (al-hinth) is subject to the five legal categories: sometimes it is obligatory, sometimes forbidden, sometimes recommended (sunnah), sometimes disliked (makruh), and sometimes permissible (mubah). But in the category of the permissible, keeping the oath is preferable. Keeping the oath is better in the permissible.

He said: ﴿that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among people﴾. Also, some people reconcile between two men and they receive harm from them. He says: "By Allah, I will never in my life reconcile between people." Why? He says: "Because I reconciled between them and harm came to me from them. By Allah, it is enough for you to be protected from the evil of the one to whom you do good." What do we say to him?

* Student: Fear Allah and reconcile.
* Shaykh: We say: expiate for your oath and reconcile between the servants of Allah. He says: "Has an oath passed from me?" We say: this oath, praise be to Allah, everything can be made lawful (yuhall). If one expiates for the oath before breaking it, it is called what? It is called tahillah (a dissolution of the oath), and if one expiates after breaking it, it is called kaffarah (expiation). Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution (tahillah) of your oaths﴾ [Al-Tahrim 1–2]. For this reason, in the hadith to which I alluded a little while ago, there is: "Unless I release my oath – or he said: from my oath – and do that which is better."[[Previously cited.]] Based on this, we say to the one who swore not to reconcile between people: reconcile between people and expiate for your oath, or release yourself from your oath and reconcile between people.

Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾. This sentence undoubtedly contains a kind of warning, for when a person makes Allah an obstacle to his oaths from righteousness, piety and reconciliation between people, he undoubtedly deserves blame and punishment, for Allah has forbidden him. For this reason He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾. Hearing of what is said, Knowing of what is done, indeed Knowing of everything, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿That you may know that Allah is competent over all things and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [Al-Talaq 12]. Are these two names among the names of Allah that are transitive (muta'addiyah) or intransitive (lazimah)?

* Student: Transitive.
* Shaykh: Transitive. Therefore faith in them is not complete except with three conditions. First: that one believes they are names of Allah indicating the essence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Second: one believes they indicate an attribute of Allah that includes this. Third: that one believes in what follows from them of rulings and effects. So "Samee'" (Hearing) means one who possesses hearing by which he hears, and "'Aleem" (Knowing) means one who possesses knowledge by which he knows. The purpose, or wisdom, of concluding the verse with these two noble names is the warning against a person opposing his Lord, for if he opposes Allah, then Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

* Student: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions. The first benefit, the benefits of His saying, Exalted: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾, the verse.
* The first benefit: that the word iman (faith) is more specific than the word tawhid (monotheism), because of His saying ﴿until they believe﴾, and because of His saying ﴿until they believe﴾. He did not say: "And do not marry polytheistic women until they affirm the oneness of God," nor did He say: "And do not marry polytheistic men until they affirm God's oneness." The second benefit...

So the twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth: affirmation that answering the call of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, occurs only by His permission, because of His saying, Exalted: ﴿And Allah calls to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission﴾ [Al-Baqarah 221].

The twenty-sixth: affirmation of permission (idhn) to Allah. The meaning of permission is not what is established by hearing; the meaning of permission is command, because of His saying: ﴿by His permission﴾. We have already explained in the tafsir that the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is divided into three categories.

* Student: It is divided into two categories.
* Shaykh: Into three.
* Student: Two.
* Shaykh: Are you certain? Into two: legislative permission (idhn shar'i) and universal permission (idhn kawni). This is among the benefits, and perhaps a person, if he reflects, will find more than this.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿And they ask you about menstruation﴾ [Al-Baqarah 222].

﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾. What is meant by al-mahid (menstruation)?

What is said in this verse is what was said about what came before it, from His saying ﴿and they ask you﴾. * From it is derived: the succession of the questions of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* It is also derived from this verse: the eagerness of the Companions for knowledge, since they would ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about such matters.
* It is also derived from it: a person should not be shy about asking about knowledge, whatever the matter, even about hidden matters, based on His saying: ﴿And they ask you about menstruation.﴾
* Also derived from it: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, may Himself take on the answer to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked, as He said: ﴿Say: It is a harm.﴾
* Also derived from the noble verse: placing the cause (ʿillah) before the ruling (ḥukm), so that the ruling arrives in the mind while it is prepared to accept it. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿It is a harm, so keep away from women during menstruation﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:222].
The benefit of placing the cause before the ruling is the one we pointed to: that the ruling arrives in the mind while it is ready to accept it.
* Also derived from it: menstruation is a harm, and it is menstruation itself, because it is filth and impurity. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that it be washed, both little and much. Women used to get menstrual blood on their garments and would ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about it, and he would order them to scrub it: rub it first, then scrub it with water, then sprinkle it, then pray in it.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the obligation of keeping away from a woman during menstruation, based on His saying: ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation.﴾ The Sunnah has explained what is to be avoided during it, which is intercourse, based on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: «Do everything except sexual intercourse.»[[Narrated by Muslim (302/16) from the hadith of Anas.]]
* Also derived from the noble verse: the favor of Allah toward the man and the woman in their keeping away during menstruation, because it is a harm that harms the woman and harms the man: intercourse during menstruation.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the prohibition of approaching them until they become pure, based on His saying: ﴿And do not approach them.﴾ If you say: How can this verse be reconciled with the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) saying: «Do everything except sexual intercourse»[[Previously cited.]], since that implies approaching them?
We say, or the answer is that we say: the prohibition on approaching is explained as meaning that a person should not approach intercourse. For this reason some scholars held that if a man cannot control himself, he should not approach the genitals, and should not enjoy anything below the waist-wrap. They took this as a way of reconciling the Prophet's (ﷺ) answer when he was asked: What is lawful for a man with his wife when she is menstruating? He said: «Whatever is above the waist-wrap»[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (212) from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn Saʿd, and (213) from the hadith of Muʿadh ibn Jabal, and the wording is his.]], with his saying: «Do everything except sexual intercourse.»[[Previously cited.]]
* Also derived from the noble verse: the prohibition of intercourse after purity and before the ghusl (ritual bath), based on His saying: ﴿So when they have purified themselves, come to them﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:222]. In another reading: ﴿until they have bathed (yaṭṭahharna)﴾, meaning: until they have performed ghusl. This refutes the view of some scholars who said that what is meant is washing the place and removing the harm, and that it is permissible for a man to have intercourse with his wife after her menses ends even if she has not bathed, once the place has been washed.
The evidence: His saying: ﴿When they have purified themselves﴾, whose meaning is: when they have bathed, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:6]. So ittiharr and tatahhur mean ghusl.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the obligation of a man having intercourse with his wife after she has become pure from menstruation.
* A student: It is not obligatory.
* Another student: According to the view of the Ẓāhirīs (the literalist school).
* Another student: It is permissible.
* The Shaykh: ﴿So come to them.﴾
We say: Yes, some scholars held this. He said: It is obligatory on the man, when his wife has bathed from menstruation, that he have intercourse with her, because Allah says: ﴿So when they have purified themselves, come to them.﴾ But this view is very weak, and the correct position is that the command here is to lift the prohibition, and we do not say it is for permissibility. The correct position is that a command after a prohibition lifts the ban. It removes the prohibition, and then leaves the ruling as it was before the prohibition.
Pay attention to the difference between our saying that a command after a prohibition is for permissibility, and saying that a command after a prohibition lifts the ban. There is a difference. If we say a command after a prohibition is for permissibility, its meaning is that the prohibition cancelled the first ruling, and then the command after the prohibition made the forbidden thing permitted. But if we say that a command after a prohibition only lifts the ban, its meaning is that the prohibition has been removed and the ruling has remained as it was before the prohibition. On this view, His saying ﴿So come to them﴾ is a command after a ban, indicating that the ruling returns to what it was before the prohibition. Coming to the woman, if it entails living with her in kindness, is then part of the required command; otherwise it is not.
There is no doubt that women differ. Some women desire that the husband come to them, so his coming to her is part of living with her in kindness, which is required in His saying: ﴿And live with them in kindness﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:19].
Some women do not care about that, and some women may even dislike it.
The conclusion is that the command here lifts the ban, so the matter returns to what it was before the ban. We say to Abu Muhammad ʿAli ibn Hazm:
What do you say about His saying: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:2]?
Would you make it obligatory for the one in ihram, when he has left ihram, to carry a crossbow in order to hunt game?
He would say: No. The command in this verse is like the command in the verse of al-Ma'idah, because Allah said: ﴿Do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands, nor those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and His pleasure. And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:2]. So this is a command after a prohibition. The conclusion is that the correct view is that a command after a prohibition lifts the ban and returns the command to what it was before the ban.
* Also derived from the noble verse: it is not permissible for a person to transgress the limits of Allah, in time or in place, in what Allah has permitted him regarding coming to his wife. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿So come to them from where Allah has commanded you.﴾
* Also derived from the noble verse: the affirmation of the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who turn back in repentance﴾. The love of Allah is real, in the manner befitting Him. Likewise everything Allah has described Himself with, such as love, good pleasure, dislike, anger, wrath, and others, is all established as real for Allah in the manner befitting Him.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the affirmation of the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that His command must be obeyed according to what the textual evidences require, based on His saying: ﴿From where Allah has commanded you﴾.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the virtue of repentance, and that it is a required matter. From where?
* The student: From His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who turn back in repentance﴾.
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: If Allah loves those who repent, then it is required.
* The Shaykh: It is required of a person to do what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loves.
So, it is derived from the noble verse: the virtue of repentance, and that it is one of the causes of Allah's love for His servant.
* Also derived from the noble verse: that the attribute of love is one of Allah's active attributes (ṣifāt fiʿliyyah), not essential attributes (ṣifāt dhātiyyah). How?
Because it is linked to repentance, and repentance is an act of the servant that is renewed. Likewise the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is linked to its causes. And every attribute of Allah that is linked to its causes is one of the active attributes.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the love of Allah, the Exalted, for those who purify themselves, based on His saying: ﴿And He loves those who purify themselves﴾.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the excellence of the Qur'an's style, because in this verse it combined inner purification and outer purification. From where is this taken?
* The verse teaches the excellence of the Qur'an's style, in that it combined physical purification and inner purification.
* A student: Physical purity is the purity of the body (...), and inner purity is the purity of..
* The Shaykh: No, I have no knowledge of that.
* A student: ﴿And do not approach them until they become pure﴾.
* The Shaykh: No, no.
* A student: ﴿Indeed Allah loves those who turn back in repentance and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:222], from the last part of the verse?
* The Shaykh: Fine. Where is the outward and inward purification, or the physical and inner?
* The student: "Those who turn back in repentance" is inner repentance.
* The Shaykh: Yes, repentance is inner purification.
* The student: And "those who purify themselves"..
* The Shaykh: Is that physical purification?
* The student: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: Fine, correct?
* The students: Correct.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Also derived from the noble verse: the justification (taʿlīl) of the legal rulings, based on His saying: ﴿It is a harm, so keep away﴾.
* Accordingly, it is also derived from it: the affirmation of the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that He does not legislate anything except for a wisdom. Is that not so?
Because He said: ﴿It is a harm, so keep away from women during menstruation.﴾ So since Allah gave this reason, it means He legislated it only for a wisdom, and this is what His name, Blessed and Exalted, al-Ḥakīm (the All-Wise), requires.
* Also derived from the noble verse, a benefit to consider: the wisdom of Allah, the Exalted, in a woman's menstruation. Some doctors said that there is a benefit for the man in it, because it restrains him from intercourse, and continuous intercourse is harmful to a person. There is a famous line of verse expressing this wisdom:
Three things destroy people, and they lead the healthy to sickness: continuous wine-drinking, continuous intercourse, and adding food upon food.
Yes, a man who has eaten, with his stomach foul, sweats on his friend, and when he has food, meat, sinew and the like, he eats the meat and sinew while his stomach is full. What is this? This is adding food upon food, which is dangerous for him. As for al-Madāmah, it is wine. It is well known that wine corrupts the mind, the religion and the body, especially when a person becomes addicted to it, may Allah protect us. Likewise intercourse exhausts the body. For this reason, among Allah's wisdoms, when a person has intercourse he must perform ghusl to purify himself and to restore the vigor of his body.
I say: can this benefit be derived from the verse: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in menstruation and in His command to men to keep away from women during it, so that they may to some degree preserve their health? Is this possible?
* A student: It is said that it was legislated for us because there is a benefit for us in our religion and our worldly life, since it contains harm for the man and the woman; that is why Allah forbade it to us, and all that He has legislated and permitted for us contains good.
* The Shaykh: There is no problem with that, but we want a specific benefit. Do we have evidence or not? We all know, thanks be to Allah, that Allah does not legislate anything except for a wisdom and for good for His servants in their livelihood and their hereafter. There is no problem with that. But we want that specific benefit: is it correct or not?
* A student: It seems that it is not clear, because the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted intercourse other than..
* The Shaykh: He permitted enjoyment?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Other than the genitals?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: But indeed that is correct.
* A student: I say: as for the woman, that is correct, but as for the man, it may (...).
* The Shaykh: No. Also, enjoyment other than the genitals can wear the body out even more, because that is natural enjoyment, while this is usually unnatural enjoyment, and it is not what Allah permitted.
In any case, I have withdrawn from this; there is no benefit in it.
Then He said, the Exalted.. is there a benefit other than this?
* A student: Regarding love, we said it is active. Why do we not say it is essential and active?
* The Shaykh: We may say it is essential and active. We can say so, because Allah knows that this man will be among those who repent and purify themselves, so He loves him, but He does not love him until this thing exists.
* A student: The affirmation of love (...), love and hatred for Allah. Is this what is established in the self?
* The Shaykh: It is established in the self without doubt. That is why we told you: active attributes are of two kinds: some are attributes of meaning and some are not; some are attributes of meaning and some are active. But we say that love is tied to the beloved, and the beloved is something that comes into being. However, Allah, the Exalted, knows that something will exist that He loves, so He loves that thing at the time of its existence.
* A student: Shaykh, some distinguish between ﴿taqrabūhunna﴾ and (taqrubūhunna)? That ﴿taqrabūhunna﴾ means to be involved with them, and (taqrubūhunna) means to draw near to them.
* The Shaykh: And which is preferable, what does it mean?
* The student: ﴿taqrabūhunna﴾ means you become involved with them.
* The Shaykh: No, no, that is not correct, because ﴿Do not approach fornication﴾ [al-Isra' 17:32] covers everything that leads to fornication. So he is forbidden from fornication and from its causes.
* The student: Shaykh, did He say it with the fatḥah because it is general and more comprehensive? Did He not say it with the ḍammah because it is specific to drawing near?
* The Shaykh: No, not at all. It is said qaruba yaqrubu and qarraba yaqrabu, but these are of the patterns that they call the wazn patterns, and I do not think there is this difference between them.
Then He said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:223].
* It is derived from this noble verse: that women are a tilth for men, meaning a place of cultivation.
* Also derived from this noble verse: that the man is free in this tilth: if he wishes he does, and if he wishes he does not, based on His saying: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾. However, according to some scholars it is limited to four months, or according to another view, to what custom has established.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the permissibility of coming to the woman in the place of the tilth from any direction, based on His saying: ﴿So come to your tilth however you wish﴾.
Is it also derived from the noble verse that it is legislated for a person to intend offspring in his intercourse?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: From where is it taken? Other than ﴿Put forward for yourselves﴾, in His saying: ﴿So come to your tilth﴾. Allah made coming to the tilth, as if it were an indication that a person should come to the woman in order to seek offspring. They have mentioned about Amir al-Mu'minin ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he had intercourse only with the intention of offspring, or only for the sake of offspring.
In any case, people differ on this, and there is no objection to a person intending offspring by it, and also intending the fulfillment of desire.
* Also derived from the noble verse: it is legislated for a person to put forward for himself during intercourse, based on His saying: ﴿And put forward for yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:223].
We have mentioned in the tafsir the meaning of His saying: ﴿And put forward for yourselves﴾, and that among its meanings is what?
Saying the basmalah, and intending to guard the chastity, and intending offspring, is that right?
* Also derived from the noble verse: that coming to the woman is among a person's private interests, based on His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And put forward for yourselves﴾. It is as if this is an indication from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that the benefit is for us and not for others, so put forward for yourself.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the obligation of fearing Allah, based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And fear Allah﴾.
* Also derived from it: the obligation of conducting oneself in dealing with one's family, both in coming to them and in abstaining from them, according to what? According to what Allah has legislated. That is because it is part of fearing Allah, so it is obligatory for you to conduct yourself in living with your family, in action and in restraint, according to what Allah has legislated.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the affirmation of the Resurrection. From where is this taken?
* A student: ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And know that you will meet Him.﴾
* Also derived from it: the affirmation of seeing Allah. From where is this taken?
* The students: ﴿That you will meet Him.﴾
* A student: It does not necessarily follow.
* The Shaykh: What is necessarily entailed by meeting in sight?
* A student: It does not necessarily follow.
* The Shaykh: He met him. What does that mean?
* A student: He faced him.
* The Shaykh: He faced him. And what is it that faces someone with its eyes covered? Some scholars used this verse as evidence that it indicates the affirmation of seeing Allah, because the basic meaning of meeting is the absence of a barrier. The basic meaning is the absence of a barrier, so it indicates the affirmation of seeing Allah.
* Also derived from the noble verse: the warning to a person against disobedience, because when He commanded taqwā (God-consciousness), He said: ﴿And know that you will meet Him.﴾

* It is part of eloquence (balagha) that when you inform a person of an important matter, you precede the report with something that calls for his attention. From where? 

* The students: ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿And know﴾. He did not say, "Fear Allah, for you will meet Him." He said, ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾, and this increases a person's attention and his preparation for that meeting.

* It is derived from the noble verse that the believers are saved from the defilements of this meeting, because of His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾.

* It is derived from it that the good tidings for the believers are unrestricted, since He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ and did not mention what they are good tidings of.

* It is derived from the noble verse that the good tidings for the believers are both in this world and in the Hereafter. The reason is the absence of restriction. Allah the Exalted has said in another verse: ﴿For them is good news in the worldly life and in the Hereafter﴾ [Yunus 64]. The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the good dream that a man sees or that is seen for him, and he said: «That is the early good tiding of the believer»[[Narrated by Muslim (2642 / 166) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]].

* It is derived from the noble verse: a warning to those who are not believers about this meeting. From where is this taken? Because when He commanded us to know that we would meet Him, He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, meaning: and warn those who are not believers. This is close to His saying: ﴿And He made for you garments that protect you from the heat﴾ [An-Nahl 81].

* The students: That means: and garments that protect you from the cold.

* The Shaykh: That protects you from the heat and the cold. So here He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾.

* It is derived from the noble verse: the virtue of faith, because Allah tied the good tidings to them, saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾.

* It is derived from it: the permissibility of a man having intercourse with his wife from her back, through her front (vulva). The evidence is His saying: ﴿So come to your tilth however you wish﴾. The Jews, may Allah's curses be upon them, used to say that if a man has intercourse with his wife from behind through her front, the child will be cross-eyed. Allah the Mighty and Majestic refuted them.

* A student: Shaykh, is it derived from His saying: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, an exhortation for men to guard their wives, since He said: ﴿your wives﴾ and said: ﴿a tilth for you﴾?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is derived from it. From the attribution ﴿your wives﴾ and ﴿a tilth for you﴾ it is derived that a person should guard this woman who has been attributed to him, and that she is his tilth, just as he guards the tilth of his land.

* It is also derived from it another benefit: that a person should not reduce offspring, because of His saying: ﴿a tilth for you﴾. If she is a tilth, when a person cultivates land, does he reduce the planting or does he increase the planting?

It is increased. This is the usual practice, without doubt. He increases the planting. So we say: it is also incumbent upon a person to increase children as much as he can.

As for the claim of limiting offspring, this is undoubtedly one of the schemes of the enemies of the Muslims. They want the Muslims not to multiply, because if they multiply, they will frighten them. If they multiply, they become self-sufficient and do not need them. If they multiply, they cultivate the land and run commerce, and the economy rises and so on. But if they remain few and weak, they become humiliated and need others in everything.

What is your opinion of a woman who says: "I want to take contraceptive pills, because when I become pregnant I get tired. Before pregnancy I used to climb to the roof and come down, go out and come back, sit calmly and stand calmly.
