What is this? This is legislative. Likewise His saying, the Exalted, in Surat al-Mumtahanah, when He mentioned what is obligatory regarding the emigrant women: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 10]. This is a legislative judgment.

From the cosmic judgment is the saying of one of the brothers of Joseph: ﴿I will never leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decrees for me﴾ [Yusuf 80]. Is this legislative or decreed? It is a decreed judgment, because a legislative judgment is not prohibited by the Shari'ah; it is the one judged for, that he may leave the land. But he wanted a cosmic judgment.

As for His saying ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin 8], what is meant by it? It includes both. It includes both together: He is the most just of judges cosmically, and the most just of judges legislatively.

Then we return and say: wisdom relates to both kinds, that is, to the cosmic and the legislative judgment. So the wisdom of Allah the Exalted is inherent in both the cosmic and the legislative judgment. Then we say a second time about wisdom: wisdom has a form and has an end. Its form means that this thing is in this specific manner, and its end means that its purpose is a praiseworthy end for which the judge is praised. This is established for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in both judgments, is it not? It is established in both judgments. The creation of things, and the judgment upon them and their actions, is entirely in accordance with wisdom. Then the purpose of this creation is also in accordance with wisdom. This is the explanation of the noble verse, its grammatical analysis, and its recitations.

As for its benefits: several matters are derived from it. Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the wife's marital status continues even after death?

*Students:* Yes.

*Shaykh:* Yes. From where is it derived?

*Students:* From His saying: ﴿and leave wives behind﴾.

*Shaykh:* From His saying ﴿wives﴾. Could not someone say that what is meant is according to what was previously the case?

*Student:* That is contrary to the original principle.

*Shaykh:* Contrary to the original principle? If you say: she remains a wife, the problem arises for us that she is not lawful to anyone after him?

*Student:* Restricted.

*Shaykh:* Restricted to what?

*Students:* Until the year.

*Student:* Until the end of the waiting period ('iddah).

*Shaykh:* Or by the end of the waiting period. What indicates this is that when a woman's husband dies, it is permissible for her to wash him. If the rules of marriage were completely severed, it would not be permissible for her to wash her husband.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the husband bequeaths to his wife, by a bequest from Allah, after his death, that she remain in his house for a full year and that she be provided for from his estate, or not? That the husband bequeaths to his wife a bequest from Allah (I said it this way so that it includes both readings), he bequeaths by a bequest from Allah, I mean so that it includes both meanings, he bequeaths to his wife by a bequest from Allah that she remain in his house for a full year, and that she be provided for from what? From his estate. This is what the verse indicates. So is this ruling abrogated? Because we now have two rulings. The first ruling: she takes something from his wealth for a period of one year. The second ruling: she waits in accordance with the content of his bequest for a period of one year.

Scholars differed regarding this verse. Some said: it is abrogated in both matters; some said: it is abrogated in the matter of bequeathing property; and some said: it is not abrogated in either. So there are three opinions: abrogated in both matters, not abrogated in both, and abrogated in property but not in the rest. Let us see. Those who said it is abrogated in both said: as for remaining in the house for a period of one year, it has been abrogated by the words of Allah the Exalted mentioned earlier: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days. And when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you concerning what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:234]. This is the view of the majority of the commentators (mufassirun), and the hadith in al-Bukhari indicates it, when 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked: "Why did you leave this verse in place while it is abrogated?" And why did you place it after the abrogating verse? It would have been better for the abrogated verse to come before the abrogating verse, in keeping with the order. "So 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) replied that he would not change anything that had preceded him from before"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4530, 4536) from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. That is, because the order of the verses is tawqifi (fixed by revelation), it cannot be changed. These verses remained after the Messenger (ﷺ) passed away and are recited in the Qur'an, and as they were, they cannot be changed. On this basis, this verse is abrogated by the preceding verse with respect to what? With respect to the waiting period ('iddah). As for property, they said: it is abrogated by the verses of inheritance, due to His words: ﴿And for them is one-fourth﴾ [al-Nisa 4:12] ﴿then for them is one-eighth﴾ [al-Nisa 4:12], and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has given every rightful person his right, so there is no bequest to an heir"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2870, 3565), al-Tirmidhi (2120) and Ibn Majah (2713) from the hadith of Abu Umamah al-Bahili (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. Accordingly, it is abrogated with respect to both rulings. Some scholars said: there is no abrogation in either of the two places. As for the first, the waiting period, this verse does not refer to the 'iddah, because the 'iddah requires that the woman remain in her husband's house. Rather, this verse means that a person is commanded to make a bequest for his wife that she remain in his house for one year, to console her and so that she does not suffer both the separation from her husband and the separation from the house for a year. In the Jahiliyyah, the woman would remain after the death for a full year, not marrying and not leaving her house, and yet not being in her house either; rather, she would be in a small hafsh, a small hut in the middle of the house. She would not purify herself, nor would she take care of her grooming: her hair, her nails, her dirt, and the stench of her menses—all of that would remain for a year. When the year ended and she came out, they would bring her some animal, a bird, a sparrow, or any kind of animal, and they would say: rub yourself with it. The hadith says: "So rarely did she rub herself with anything but it died"[[A hadith agreed upon by al-Bukhari (5337) and Muslim (1489) from the hadith of Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, as a mawquf report, with the wording: Humayd said: I said to Zaynab, "What is the meaning of throwing the dung on the head of the year?" Zaynab said: "When a woman's husband died, she would enter a hafsh, wear her worst clothes, not touch perfume or anything else until a year had passed. Then she would be brought an animal—a donkey, a sheep, or a bird—and she would rub herself with it. Rarely did she rub herself with anything but it died. Then she would come out and be given a piece of dung, which she would throw away, and then she could resume using whatever perfume or other things she wished."]]. And what is the reason? *Students:* The foul smell. *The Shaykh:* The foul smell. Then she would come out and take a camel's dung, take it and throw it away. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "One of you used to throw dung at the end of the year"[[A hadith agreed upon by al-Bukhari (5336) and Muslim (1488) from the hadith of Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her).]]. This is an indication of what? That all these things she underwent are easier for me than throwing this dung (...). *A student:* After death, His words: ﴿and leave wives behind﴾. *The Shaykh:* But this we must comment on: is this not general across all rulings? This is the first benefit, and this is its last; and it is not general across all rulings, and the connection is also severed upon completion of the 'iddah. The second benefit, you said? *A student:* That the husband makes a bequest from Allah to his wife after his death, and that she remains in his house for a full year, and she is provided for from his estate. *The Shaykh:* Yes, what comes after that? *A student:* And we said: he makes a bequest from Allah. *The Shaykh:* You said: this is so that it covers both meanings. We mentioned: this is what the verse indicates. Is this ruling abrogated as two rulings? The first ruling: that she takes something from his wealth for a period of one year; the second ruling: that she waits according to the requirement of his bequest for a year. *The Shaykh:* Is this ruling abrogated by the two rulings? *A student:* (...) if she remains (...) does not marry (...) a small child in the middle of the house, and she has already been [...]. *The Shaykh:* In the middle of the house. *The student:* Yes, in the middle of the house. *The Shaykh:* And we comment on the rest. Now we understand that some scholars say: the verse is not abrogated in either place, neither regarding the bequest that she remain in the house, nor regarding her remaining for the full year. As for her remaining in the house, they said: this is among matters in which custom has been lenient; so if a husband bequeaths to his wife that she remain in his house, this is a small matter, and it is not a bequest of property deducted from his wealth for her. As for her remaining for a full year, this is not on the basis of obligation, so that we would say it was abrogated by the verse of the 'iddah; for the verse of the 'iddah indicates that it is obligatory upon the woman to remain in her husband's house for the duration of the 'iddah—if she is pregnant, until she gives birth, and if she is not pregnant, four months and ten days. As for this verse, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But if they leave, there is no blame upon you﴾. And it is impossible for something recommended to be abrogated by something obligatory, since there is no contradiction. We have known from what preceded that one of the conditions of abrogation is that reconciling the two is impossible; so if reconciliation is possible, there is no abrogation. In my view, the opinion that it is abrogated concerning the bequest of property, namely residence and provision, is a strong opinion; but as for the 'iddah, there is no abrogation, since reconciliation is possible, and wherever reconciliation is possible, there is no abrogation.

From this noble verse it is derived: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is possessed of vast mercy, to the extent that He enjoined the husband to make a bequest for his wife, although Allah has placed in the husband mercy toward his wife, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy﴾ [al-Rum 30:21]. Thus the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is greater than the mercy of the husband toward his wife.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that if a husband bequeaths that his wife remain in the house, it is permissible for her to leave, and his bequest need not be carried out, due to His words: ﴿But if they leave, there is no blame upon you﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:240], because this is a matter that concerns her, and the husband has no interest in it. From this a further benefit branches: if he bequeaths that his wife not marry after him, must she carry out his bequest? No, it is not binding upon her; for if she is not bound to remain in the house for a year, then, all the more so, she is not bound to remain unmarried.

Likewise, it may be derived by analogy: whoever bequeaths to a person something that concerns that person himself—the right belongs to the legatee in carrying out the bequest or not carrying it out.

From this noble verse is derived: that the men are responsible for the women, from His words: ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, addressing the men, although the context concerns the women.

And it is derived from it: that the men bear sin if the woman departs from what is recognized in the Shari'ah, due to His words: ﴿there is no blame upon you concerning what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner﴾. This indicates that if they do what is not acceptable, we bear the sin.

A further benefit branches from this: that every guardian of a person, if he is able to establish (the good) for him and prevent him from wrongdoing, then he is sinful (if he fails). Does this contradict His words: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am 6:164]? For example, I am a guardian of my son, and he commits a wrongful act, and I am able to prevent him from it: am I sinful? Yes, I am sinful. Does this not contradict His words: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾? No; for as long as I am responsible, if I neglect my responsibility I become a bearer of burdens, and my burden is upon myself.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: it is not permissible for a woman to depart from what is recognized in any of her circumstances. What is recognized is what the Shari'ah and custom both approve. So if she departs in her clothing, her walking, or her voice from what is recognized by the Shari'ah, she is sinful, and it is not lawful for her to go out; and when she goes out, or attempts to go out, it is our duty to restrain her.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, al-'Aziz (the Mighty) and al-Hakim (the Wise), and the affirmation of the attributes they contain, whether by necessary implication, by direct correspondence, or by inclusion.

An important rule has already passed us in this regard: "Every name of Allah includes an attribute, but not vice versa," since not every attribute is contained in a name. This is because the names of Allah, the names of His Messenger, and the names of His speech are all names derived from their meanings, unlike human names, for example, which are not derived from their meanings. We may name a man 'Abd Allah ("servant of Allah") while he is a servant of Satan, among the most disbelieving of Allah's servants; and we may name this man Muhammad while he is blameworthy (mudhammam) and has no praiseworthy quality. But the names of Allah, His Messenger, and the Qur'an are all names that carry their meanings. Accordingly, we say: every name includes an attribute, and it may be one attribute, two attributes, or more, as has passed us.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of might and wisdom in an absolute sense, since Allah stated them without restriction: ﴿'Aziz﴾ and ﴿Hakim﴾, so He is Mighty in every state and likewise Wise in every state.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 241–242 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the God-conscious.﴾ ﴿And for divorced women there is provision﴾ The sentence here consists of a subject and a predicate, and the predicate is placed first: ﴿for divorced women﴾, while the subject is placed after it, which is his saying: ﴿provision according to what is reasonable﴾. For this reason it was permissible to begin with it although it is indefinite, because it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun when the subject is postponed. His saying: ﴿ḥaqqan (a duty)﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar) (...) because ﴿for divorced women there is provision﴾ means a declarative sentence that establishes the right, or not? Like the saying of Ibn Malik:
.................... ∗∗∗ ...kabnī anta ḥaqqan ṣirfā (as in "You are truly my son")
Because this is a verbal noun emphasizing the content of the sentence, it needs no governing verb, and in any case it is in the accusative as a verbal noun. And ﴿al-muttaqīn (the God-conscious)﴾ means those possessed of taqwā (God-consciousness), and taqwā has been explained to us many times as acting in obedience to Allah with knowledge and insight. How excellent is what Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Taqwā is that you act in obedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah, and that you abandon what Allah has forbidden upon a light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.
Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿For divorced women there is provision﴾. The word "divorced women" (muṭallaqāt), as we all know, is counted among the general terms (alfāẓ al-'umūm), among the expressions of generality, or not? Because the definite article (al) in it is a relative pronoun, as Ibn Malik said:
And an explicit adjective is the complement of al ∗∗∗ ................... So ﴿al-muṭallaqāt (the divorced women)﴾ is general, every divorced woman without exception. And ﴿matā' (provision)﴾ means what she enjoys of clothing and other things.
His saying: ﴿bi-l-ma'rūf (according to what is reasonable)﴾ is attached to (matā'); meaning this provision is restricted by what is reasonable, i.e., what people recognize. This may be explained by the verse mentioned earlier: ﴿upon the wealthy according to his means, and upon the straitened according to his means, a provision according to what is reasonable﴾ [al-Baqarah 236]. The meaning of ﴿a provision according to what is reasonable﴾ is: upon the well-off according to his wealth, and upon the poor according to his poverty. In this verse Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty﴾, meaning a fixed and obligatory matter upon every person who is God-conscious toward Allah the Mighty and Majestic. His saying: ﴿upon the God-conscious﴾ does not mean that it is not obligatory upon those who are not God-conscious, but restricting it to the God-conscious is by way of incitement (al-igrā') and encouragement, like the saying of the Messenger ﷺ at times: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day that she should..." such and such. That is, among the examples: "that she mourn for a dead person for more than three [days]"[[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5334) and Muslim (1486/58) from the hadith of Umm Ḥabība, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, with the wording "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three," and so on.]]. So his saying: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day" does not mean that it is lawful for one who does not believe in Allah and the Last Day, but this is by way of incitement and encouragement, just as if I said to you: "It is not fitting for a man to do such and such," or "only men do this"; the purpose of such speech is incitement and encouragement. Also, restricting it to the God-conscious indicates that committing to it is part of the God-consciousness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and that whoever does not commit to it has a deficiency in his taqwā.
Let us return to the noble verse here and examine whether this verse is abrogated (mansūkh) or not. And if we say it is unabrogated (muḥkam), is it general, meaning generality is intended, or general in wording but specific in intent, or general with specification (mukhaṣṣaṣ)? So we now have several investigations:
The first investigation: Is the verse abrogated or unabrogated?
The second investigation: If we say it is unabrogated, is it inclusive of every divorced woman, or are some divorced women excluded from it, or was generality never intended from the outset, but it is a general term by which specificity is intended? Let us look at the noble verse: the generality in it is apparent. From where is it derived?
From his saying: ﴿And for divorced women﴾, for Allah the Exalted did not exclude anything. He did not exclude the woman divorced before consummation, nor the one for whom a dower was named, but stated it absolutely, so it includes the woman divorced before consummation, the woman divorced after consummation, and others.
Then we say: The woman divorced before consummation when no dower was named for her, Allah the Exalted has mentioned for her a provision previously. Where is the provision? ﴿And if you divorce them﴾ [al-Baqarah 237] ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or specified for them an obligatory dower; but provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the straitened according to his means﴾ [al-Baqarah 236]. Then in this verse there is no abrogation, because the woman divorced before consummation for whom no dower was named, is her ruling in accordance with this verse or not in accordance?
* The students: In accordance.
* The Shaykh: In accordance? Both verses indicate the obligation of provision, is that so or not? And if the general verse indicates the obligation of the provision in question, and that particular verse indicates the obligation of provision, then the principle among the verifying scholars is that (mentioning some individual instances of the general under a ruling that agrees with the general does not require specification). This principle has passed us before, and accordingly the earlier verse: ﴿and provide for them, the wealthy according to his means﴾ is an instance of this verse, and then there is no difficulty in it.
The woman divorced before consummation for whom a dower was specified: what is obligatory for her? Half of what you specified: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have specified for them an obligatory dower, then half of what you specified, unless they forgive﴾ [al-Baqarah 237].
Must her husband provide for her in addition to halving the dower? Or is it said that since a dower was specified, the provision here is half the dower? What do you say?
* A student: (...) The provision is the apparent view.
* The Shaykh: Because half the dower is undoubtedly a provision, especially in our time: if the dower becomes forty thousand, for example, how much is half of it?
* The students: Twenty.
* The Shaykh: Twenty, a provision, by Allah's grace; clothing, food and everything is obtained. Yes, perhaps we may say this, and say: whoever is divorced before consummation after a dower was named, half the dower suffices in place of the provision. If we say so, does it contradict this verse, or does it agree with it, but since the dower in it was fixed, one suffices with the determination, which is half?
* A student: The latter, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Yes. If you say it agrees, there is no difficulty; if you say it contradicts, then this verse is general but specified by what?
* A student: By the one for whom a dower was named.
* The Shaykh: By the one divorced before consummation for whom a dower was named. The fourth: divorced after consummation.
* The students: The third.
* The Shaykh: The third: divorced after consummation for whom a dower was named?
* A student: Does she enter into this?
* The Shaykh: Does she enter into the verse?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: If we say she enters into the verse, it means that he is obligated to her dower and to provision for her. If she has received the dower, then the obligation of provision is evident; if she has not received it, the meaning becomes that he is bound by what he named and what else? And the provision, so he is bound by both. But this is problematic, because we say: if you say that the woman divorced before consummation for whom a dower was fixed is obligated only to what God has determined for her, which is half, then the woman divorced after consummation is obligated to her husband only for what was named for her, which is a clear analogy, since there is no difference between before and after consummation. As for when he has delivered the dower to her and she has spent it, in this case we may say the provision is obligatory; but the majority hold that it is not obligatory, providing in this case is recommended, and interpreting the verse as recommendation is certainly far from correct, because this verse, as you see, affirms the obligation of provision in three respects: his saying ﴿for divorced women there is provision﴾, and if it is for them, the meaning is he must fulfill their right. The second: he said ﴿ḥaqqan (a duty)﴾. The third: ﴿upon the God-conscious﴾. How can we say this is recommended?! For this reason Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, went to the view that provision is obligatory even in this case, even for the one divorced after consummation whose dower was named, and said: this verse is explicit and there is no abrogation in it.
The fourth: The one divorced after consummation for whom no dower was named: what is obligatory for her?
* A student: Is the dower obligatory?
* The Shaykh: Provision is obligatory beyond doubt. But what is the provision? It is the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl), as was authentically related from Ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that he judged by it, and the Prophet ﷺ had preceded him: "Ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about a woman whom her husband contracted with and then died, without a dower having been named for her. He said: She is entitled to the dower of her women, and to inheritance, and she must observe the 'iddah. A man stood up and said: The Prophet ﷺ judged in the case of Bi'r' bint Wāshiq, a woman from among us, by what you have judged." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2116) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. For this fourth woman, divorced by her husband after consummation without a dower being named, what is obligatory for her? The equivalent dower is obligatory for her, and this is provision, as this verse requires. So the divorced women are now four: two before consummation and two after consummation; two before consummation: one for whom a dower was named, and the second for whom none was named; two after consummation: one for whom a dower was named, and the second for whom none was named.
There remains a fifth: the one for whom a condition was stipulated in her contract that there be no dower, such as saying: "I accept the marriage on condition that there is no dower upon me." What do you say about her?
* The students: Defective... invalid.
* The Shaykh: There is a difference of opinion on this. The well-known position in the school is that the invalid element is the condition; when the condition is invalid, its presence is like its absence, and she becomes like a woman delegated (mufawwiḍa), i.e., for whom no dower was named, and then the equivalent dower is obligatory for her. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya chose that the marriage is void and not valid, because Allah only made lawful for us what is other than the prohibited, on condition that we seek it with property. He said: ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that, that you seek with your wealth﴾ [al-Nisā' 24]. And because when the negation of the dower is stipulated, the reality of the matter becomes a gift, and gift is among the special privileges of the Prophet ﷺ.
His view is closer to the truth. Accordingly, if he has not consummated with her, the contract is renewed anew; if he has consummated with her, they are separated, and the equivalent dower becomes obligatory for her by his intercourse with her, if he had intercourse with her; and the contract is renewed according to the view of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya. So the conclusion now is that we have learned the divorced women are four.
* The students: Five.
* The Shaykh: Five, the divorced women are five, and this last one you have learned (...).
* A student: Shaykh, the third case?
* The Shaykh: If it was after consummation, then she has the equivalent dower (...). The one who was divorced and for whom no dower was named has provision, do you understand? Obligatory, it has been stated before that it is obligatory. But they mention a report which, if authentic, would be clear: "A man, when the first verse was revealed: ﴿And provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the straitened according to his means, a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the good-doers﴾, said: Allah has made it a matter of kindness; if I wish I provide, and if I wish I do not provide. So Allah revealed here: ﴿For divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the God-conscious﴾."[[Narrated by al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsir (4/412) from the hadith of 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd, as a mawqūf report.]]. So Allah made it obligatory. These scholars say: the verse is general but intends the specific. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, holds that it is general for every divorced woman and that it is obligatory; this is one view. The second view: it is general for every divorced woman and obligatory, except the one divorced before consummation for whom a dower was fixed, because Allah has clarified what is obligatory for her, which is half the dower. Do you understand?
When we look at the noble verse and its apparent meaning, we find it general, and that even the one divorced before consummation for whom a dower was fixed has half her dower by determination, and enjoys what exceeds it based on this verse; this is the apparent meaning of the verse. But it is problematic: the determination by half means that it is a dividing limit beyond which there is no provision. Accordingly we say: what the Lawgiver determined we limit ourselves to, and what he did not determine we add provision to it. So if he divorces before consummation and a dower was fixed for her, what is it? Half. Before consummation with no dower fixed, provision is not obligatory by agreement of the two verses, is that so or not? By agreement of the two verses. After consummation with a dower fixed, the whole dower, the full dower; is provision obligatory? It is based on the disagreement in this issue. And if it were said that a distinction is made between when the dower has not been delivered, for her receiving it at divorce suffices her in place of provision, or when it has been delivered and she has spent it, in which case provision is obligatory, if this view were said, it would have a basis.
The fourth: one divorced after consummation for whom no dower was fixed; for her is the equivalent dower, and it may be said that she is sufficed by it in place of provision, because they are two financial rights obligatory by one cause, or at least by two causes, but they coincide, so it is necessary to limit to one of them. But if we say that provision is recommended, and that it is general, then there is a difficulty for that in his saying ﴿for divorced women﴾, where the lam indicates entitlement, and his saying ﴿ḥaqqan (a duty)﴾, and his saying ﴿upon the God-conscious﴾.
* A student: Shaykh, is the view that it is recommended about the divorced woman or (...)?
* The Shaykh: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses that you may understand﴾. ﴿Thus﴾ means: like that clarification. The kāf here is in the position of an absolute object (maf'ūl muṭlaq), and its governing word is his saying ﴿yubayyinu (makes clear)﴾; that is, like that previous clarification, Allah makes clear to you His verses. The meaning of bayān is clarification: that Allah the Exalted clarifies it so that no obscurity remains in it. His saying ﴿lakum (to you)﴾ may be understood as the lam indicating transitivity of the verb "yubayyinu," or the lam may indicate cause, i.e., He makes the verses clear for your sake so that they become clear and evident to you. His saying ﴿āyātih (His verses)﴾ includes cosmic and legislative verses, for Allah, glorified and exalted, has made clear to us from His cosmic and legislative verses what leaves no slightest doubt that these verses are clear signs of the existence of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and of His wisdom, mercy and power.
A man related to me about a person who was on an outing with companions of his, and they, may Allah protect us, had become accustomed to drinking intoxicants. He entered the town one night and came out to them with bottles of intoxicant. When he left the town he found the ground rained upon, so he walked a short distance, and suddenly the ground was dry with no rain; he walked a short distance further, and it was rained upon again; he walked a short distance further, and there were five places, some dry and some rained upon. Then he stopped the car, put his hands on his head, and began to think: how is this? Who made this? So Allah cast faith into his heart, glory be to Allah the Mighty! He took the bottles and broke them, then went to his companions. When he reached them, they were waiting for him impatiently and saying: May Allah keep you safe, O Abu so-and-so, O Abu so-and-so, (...) upon us, you were slow with us, and such things. He said to them: Yes, I was slow with you, and I saw such and such, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic guided me, and these bottles of yours are broken. Whoever agrees with what I did is my companion, and whoever does not agree, I will not see his face again. This is a true, confirmed event. Is this one of the cosmic signs of Allah? And see how the man was guided by it! Likewise the rest of the cosmic signs Allah the Mighty and Majestic makes clear and manifests to us, so that by them we may discern the truth; the legislative signs are also clarified, made manifest, with no confusion in them and no obscurity; all of them are plain and clear.
His saying ﴿la'allakum ta'qilūn (that you may understand)﴾: "la'alla" here indicates purpose, meaning: so that you may understand. It is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand﴾. Likewise Allah makes the verses clear so that we may understand; these verses are understanding, comprehension and perception, i.e., both kinds of intellect.
From the noble verse it is derived ﴿for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable﴾: the obligation of provision for every divorced woman. And the basis of that is what? The generality in his saying ﴿for divorced women﴾. However, some scholars said: this is general but intends the specific. What is the specific that is intended?

He said: The specific (khass) one intended is the woman who is divorced before consummation and for whom no dowry was specified. In his view, this verse is merely an emphasis of the preceding verse and adds no new meaning. As for its outward sense, Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah), may Allah have mercy on him, adopted it in one place in his words, and in another place he said: mut'ah (provision) is obligatory for every divorced woman, except the one divorced before consummation for whom a dowry was set, in which case she is due half the dowry.

From the noble verse it is derived that it is appropriate to emphasize rights which people may be lax about. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿a duty upon the God-conscious (haqqan 'ala al-muttaqin)﴾.

It is also derived from it that it is appropriate to mention the qualities which move a person to act, or, to put it more accurately, which move a person to comply by doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿upon the God-conscious (ala al-muttaqin)﴾, because attaching this to the God-conscious is evidence that its opposite contradicts taqwa (God-consciousness), that failing to perform it contradicts taqwa, and that performing it is part of taqwa.

As for the second verse, among its benefits: the manifestation of Allah's favor upon His servants by clarifying the verses, based on His saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses (kadhalika yubayyinu)﴾.

Also among its benefits: the wisdom behind the rulings of marriage and divorce may be hidden from a person, because Allah made the clarification of that to Himself, saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the refutation of the mufawwidah (those who delegate meaning), the ahl al-tajhil (people of ignorance), and the ahl al-tahrif (distorters) who call themselves ahl al-ta'wil (interpreters). From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you His verses (yubayyinu Allahu lakum ayatihi)﴾, because the people of tafwid, who are the people of tajhil, say that Allah did not clarify what He meant in the verses and hadiths about the attributes, and that these verses and hadiths are like the disjointed letters whose meaning is not understood.

It also refutes the distorters. How so? Because the distorters say: Allah did not clarify, and clarification is only what we grasp with our intellects. We reply: if what you say were intended, Allah would have clarified it; since He did not clarify what you claim, it is known that it is not intended.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: praise of the intellect. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿so that you may understand (la'allakum ta'qilun)﴾. However, what is meant is sound intellect free from doubts and desires; intellects that are not sound are not really intellects but mere desires. Almighty Allah says: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ [al-Mu'minun 71].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: establishing causation (ta'lil) in Allah's actions. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿so that you may understand﴾.

Also among its benefits: it is impossible for there to exist in the Sharia a ruling that is not clarified. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾; "ayat" here is a plural construct, so it is general.

If someone says: we find some texts are hidden from us? The answer: that is either due to deficiency in our understanding or shortcoming in our reflection. As for the text in itself being unclarified, this is impossible. Is this clear?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 241–242 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the God-conscious.﴾ ﴿And for divorced women there is provision﴾ The sentence here consists of a subject and a predicate, and the predicate is placed first: ﴿for divorced women﴾, while the subject is placed after it, which is his saying: ﴿provision according to what is reasonable﴾. For this reason it was permissible to begin with it although it is indefinite, because it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun when the subject is postponed. His saying: ﴿ḥaqqan (a duty)﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar) (...) because ﴿for divorced women there is provision﴾ means a declarative sentence that establishes the right, or not? Like the saying of Ibn Malik:
.................... ∗∗∗ ...kabnī anta ḥaqqan ṣirfā (as in "You are truly my son")
Because this is a verbal noun emphasizing the content of the sentence, it needs no governing verb, and in any case it is in the accusative as a verbal noun. And ﴿al-muttaqīn (the God-conscious)﴾ means those possessed of taqwā (God-consciousness), and taqwā has been explained to us many times as acting in obedience to Allah with knowledge and insight. How excellent is what Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Taqwā is that you act in obedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah, and that you abandon what Allah has forbidden upon a light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.
Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿For divorced women there is provision﴾. The word "divorced women" (muṭallaqāt), as we all know, is counted among the general terms (alfāẓ al-'umūm), among the expressions of generality, or not? Because the definite article (al) in it is a relative pronoun, as Ibn Malik said:
And an explicit adjective is the complement of al ∗∗∗ ................... So ﴿al-muṭallaqāt (the divorced women)﴾ is general, every divorced woman without exception. And ﴿matā' (provision)﴾ means what she enjoys of clothing and other things.
His saying: ﴿bi-l-ma'rūf (according to what is reasonable)﴾ is attached to (matā'); meaning this provision is restricted by what is reasonable, i.e., what people recognize. This may be explained by the verse mentioned earlier: ﴿upon the wealthy according to his means, and upon the straitened according to his means, a provision according to what is reasonable﴾ [al-Baqarah 236]. The meaning of ﴿a provision according to what is reasonable﴾ is: upon the well-off according to his wealth, and upon the poor according to his poverty. In this verse Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty﴾, meaning a fixed and obligatory matter upon every person who is God-conscious toward Allah the Mighty and Majestic. His saying: ﴿upon the God-conscious﴾ does not mean that it is not obligatory upon those who are not God-conscious, but restricting it to the God-conscious is by way of incitement (al-igrā') and encouragement, like the saying of the Messenger ﷺ at times: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day that she should..." such and such. That is, among the examples: "that she mourn for a dead person for more than three [days]"[[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5334) and Muslim (1486/58) from the hadith of Umm Ḥabība, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, with the wording "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three," and so on.]]. So his saying: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day" does not mean that it is lawful for one who does not believe in Allah and the Last Day, but this is by way of incitement and encouragement, just as if I said to you: "It is not fitting for a man to do such and such," or "only men do this"; the purpose of such speech is incitement and encouragement. Also, restricting it to the God-conscious indicates that committing to it is part of the God-consciousness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and that whoever does not commit to it has a deficiency in his taqwā.
Let us return to the noble verse here and examine whether this verse is abrogated (mansūkh) or not. And if we say it is unabrogated (muḥkam), is it general, meaning generality is intended, or general in wording but specific in intent, or general with specification (mukhaṣṣaṣ)? So we now have several investigations:
The first investigation: Is the verse abrogated or unabrogated?
The second investigation: If we say it is unabrogated, is it inclusive of every divorced woman, or are some divorced women excluded from it, or was generality never intended from the outset, but it is a general term by which specificity is intended? Let us look at the noble verse: the generality in it is apparent. From where is it derived?
From his saying: ﴿And for divorced women﴾, for Allah the Exalted did not exclude anything. He did not exclude the woman divorced before consummation, nor the one for whom a dower was named, but stated it absolutely, so it includes the woman divorced before consummation, the woman divorced after consummation, and others.
Then we say: The woman divorced before consummation when no dower was named for her, Allah the Exalted has mentioned for her a provision previously. Where is the provision? ﴿And if you divorce them﴾ [al-Baqarah 237] ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or specified for them an obligatory dower; but provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the straitened according to his means﴾ [al-Baqarah 236]. Then in this verse there is no abrogation, because the woman divorced before consummation for whom no dower was named, is her ruling in accordance with this verse or not in accordance?
* The students: In accordance.
* The Shaykh: In accordance? Both verses indicate the obligation of provision, is that so or not? And if the general verse indicates the obligation of the provision in question, and that particular verse indicates the obligation of provision, then the principle among the verifying scholars is that (mentioning some individual instances of the general under a ruling that agrees with the general does not require specification). This principle has passed us before, and accordingly the earlier verse: ﴿and provide for them, the wealthy according to his means﴾ is an instance of this verse, and then there is no difficulty in it.
The woman divorced before consummation for whom a dower was specified: what is obligatory for her? Half of what you specified: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have specified for them an obligatory dower, then half of what you specified, unless they forgive﴾ [al-Baqarah 237].
Must her husband provide for her in addition to halving the dower? Or is it said that since a dower was specified, the provision here is half the dower? What do you say?
* A student: (...) The provision is the apparent view.
* The Shaykh: Because half the dower is undoubtedly a provision, especially in our time: if the dower becomes forty thousand, for example, how much is half of it?
* The students: Twenty.
* The Shaykh: Twenty, a provision, by Allah's grace; clothing, food and everything is obtained. Yes, perhaps we may say this, and say: whoever is divorced before consummation after a dower was named, half the dower suffices in place of the provision. If we say so, does it contradict this verse, or does it agree with it, but since the dower in it was fixed, one suffices with the determination, which is half?
* A student: The latter, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Yes. If you say it agrees, there is no difficulty; if you say it contradicts, then this verse is general but specified by what?
* A student: By the one for whom a dower was named.
* The Shaykh: By the one divorced before consummation for whom a dower was named. The fourth: divorced after consummation.
* The students: The third.
* The Shaykh: The third: divorced after consummation for whom a dower was named?
* A student: Does she enter into this?
* The Shaykh: Does she enter into the verse?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: If we say she enters into the verse, it means that he is obligated to her dower and to provision for her. If she has received the dower, then the obligation of provision is evident; if she has not received it, the meaning becomes that he is bound by what he named and what else? And the provision, so he is bound by both. But this is problematic, because we say: if you say that the woman divorced before consummation for whom a dower was fixed is obligated only to what God has determined for her, which is half, then the woman divorced after consummation is obligated to her husband only for what was named for her, which is a clear analogy, since there is no difference between before and after consummation. As for when he has delivered the dower to her and she has spent it, in this case we may say the provision is obligatory; but the majority hold that it is not obligatory, providing in this case is recommended, and interpreting the verse as recommendation is certainly far from correct, because this verse, as you see, affirms the obligation of provision in three respects: his saying ﴿for divorced women there is provision﴾, and if it is for them, the meaning is he must fulfill their right. The second: he said ﴿ḥaqqan (a duty)﴾. The third: ﴿upon the God-conscious﴾. How can we say this is recommended?! For this reason Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, went to the view that provision is obligatory even in this case, even for the one divorced after consummation whose dower was named, and said: this verse is explicit and there is no abrogation in it.
The fourth: The one divorced after consummation for whom no dower was named: what is obligatory for her?
* A student: Is the dower obligatory?
* The Shaykh: Provision is obligatory beyond doubt. But what is the provision? It is the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl), as was authentically related from Ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that he judged by it, and the Prophet ﷺ had preceded him: "Ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about a woman whom her husband contracted with and then died, without a dower having been named for her. He said: She is entitled to the dower of her women, and to inheritance, and she must observe the 'iddah. A man stood up and said: The Prophet ﷺ judged in the case of Bi'r' bint Wāshiq, a woman from among us, by what you have judged." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2116) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. For this fourth woman, divorced by her husband after consummation without a dower being named, what is obligatory for her? The equivalent dower is obligatory for her, and this is provision, as this verse requires. So the divorced women are now four: two before consummation and two after consummation; two before consummation: one for whom a dower was named, and the second for whom none was named; two after consummation: one for whom a dower was named, and the second for whom none was named.
There remains a fifth: the one for whom a condition was stipulated in her contract that there be no dower, such as saying: "I accept the marriage on condition that there is no dower upon me." What do you say about her?
* The students: Defective... invalid.
* The Shaykh: There is a difference of opinion on this. The well-known position in the school is that the invalid element is the condition; when the condition is invalid, its presence is like its absence, and she becomes like a woman delegated (mufawwiḍa), i.e., for whom no dower was named, and then the equivalent dower is obligatory for her. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya chose that the marriage is void and not valid, because Allah only made lawful for us what is other than the prohibited, on condition that we seek it with property. He said: ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that, that you seek with your wealth﴾ [al-Nisā' 24]. And because when the negation of the dower is stipulated, the reality of the matter becomes a gift, and gift is among the special privileges of the Prophet ﷺ.
His view is closer to the truth. Accordingly, if he has not consummated with her, the contract is renewed anew; if he has consummated with her, they are separated, and the equivalent dower becomes obligatory for her by his intercourse with her, if he had intercourse with her; and the contract is renewed according to the view of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya. So the conclusion now is that we have learned the divorced women are four.
* The students: Five.
* The Shaykh: Five, the divorced women are five, and this last one you have learned (...).
* A student: Shaykh, the third case?
* The Shaykh: If it was after consummation, then she has the equivalent dower (...). The one who was divorced and for whom no dower was named has provision, do you understand? Obligatory, it has been stated before that it is obligatory. But they mention a report which, if authentic, would be clear: "A man, when the first verse was revealed: ﴿And provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the straitened according to his means, a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the good-doers﴾, said: Allah has made it a matter of kindness; if I wish I provide, and if I wish I do not provide. So Allah revealed here: ﴿For divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the God-conscious﴾."[[Narrated by al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsir (4/412) from the hadith of 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd, as a mawqūf report.]]. So Allah made it obligatory. These scholars say: the verse is general but intends the specific. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, holds that it is general for every divorced woman and that it is obligatory; this is one view. The second view: it is general for every divorced woman and obligatory, except the one divorced before consummation for whom a dower was fixed, because Allah has clarified what is obligatory for her, which is half the dower. Do you understand?
When we look at the noble verse and its apparent meaning, we find it general, and that even the one divorced before consummation for whom a dower was fixed has half her dower by determination, and enjoys what exceeds it based on this verse; this is the apparent meaning of the verse. But it is problematic: the determination by half means that it is a dividing limit beyond which there is no provision. Accordingly we say: what the Lawgiver determined we limit ourselves to, and what he did not determine we add provision to it. So if he divorces before consummation and a dower was fixed for her, what is it? Half. Before consummation with no dower fixed, provision is not obligatory by agreement of the two verses, is that so or not? By agreement of the two verses. After consummation with a dower fixed, the whole dower, the full dower; is provision obligatory? It is based on the disagreement in this issue. And if it were said that a distinction is made between when the dower has not been delivered, for her receiving it at divorce suffices her in place of provision, or when it has been delivered and she has spent it, in which case provision is obligatory, if this view were said, it would have a basis.
The fourth: one divorced after consummation for whom no dower was fixed; for her is the equivalent dower, and it may be said that she is sufficed by it in place of provision, because they are two financial rights obligatory by one cause, or at least by two causes, but they coincide, so it is necessary to limit to one of them. But if we say that provision is recommended, and that it is general, then there is a difficulty for that in his saying ﴿for divorced women﴾, where the lam indicates entitlement, and his saying ﴿ḥaqqan (a duty)﴾, and his saying ﴿upon the God-conscious﴾.
* A student: Shaykh, is the view that it is recommended about the divorced woman or (...)?
* The Shaykh: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses that you may understand﴾. ﴿Thus﴾ means: like that clarification. The kāf here is in the position of an absolute object (maf'ūl muṭlaq), and its governing word is his saying ﴿yubayyinu (makes clear)﴾; that is, like that previous clarification, Allah makes clear to you His verses. The meaning of bayān is clarification: that Allah the Exalted clarifies it so that no obscurity remains in it. His saying ﴿lakum (to you)﴾ may be understood as the lam indicating transitivity of the verb "yubayyinu," or the lam may indicate cause, i.e., He makes the verses clear for your sake so that they become clear and evident to you. His saying ﴿āyātih (His verses)﴾ includes cosmic and legislative verses, for Allah, glorified and exalted, has made clear to us from His cosmic and legislative verses what leaves no slightest doubt that these verses are clear signs of the existence of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and of His wisdom, mercy and power.
A man related to me about a person who was on an outing with companions of his, and they, may Allah protect us, had become accustomed to drinking intoxicants. He entered the town one night and came out to them with bottles of intoxicant. When he left the town he found the ground rained upon, so he walked a short distance, and suddenly the ground was dry with no rain; he walked a short distance further, and it was rained upon again; he walked a short distance further, and there were five places, some dry and some rained upon. Then he stopped the car, put his hands on his head, and began to think: how is this? Who made this? So Allah cast faith into his heart, glory be to Allah the Mighty! He took the bottles and broke them, then went to his companions. When he reached them, they were waiting for him impatiently and saying: May Allah keep you safe, O Abu so-and-so, O Abu so-and-so, (...) upon us, you were slow with us, and such things. He said to them: Yes, I was slow with you, and I saw such and such, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic guided me, and these bottles of yours are broken. Whoever agrees with what I did is my companion, and whoever does not agree, I will not see his face again. This is a true, confirmed event. Is this one of the cosmic signs of Allah? And see how the man was guided by it! Likewise the rest of the cosmic signs Allah the Mighty and Majestic makes clear and manifests to us, so that by them we may discern the truth; the legislative signs are also clarified, made manifest, with no confusion in them and no obscurity; all of them are plain and clear.
His saying ﴿la'allakum ta'qilūn (that you may understand)﴾: "la'alla" here indicates purpose, meaning: so that you may understand. It is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand﴾. Likewise Allah makes the verses clear so that we may understand; these verses are understanding, comprehension and perception, i.e., both kinds of intellect.
From the noble verse it is derived ﴿for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable﴾: the obligation of provision for every divorced woman. And the basis of that is what? The generality in his saying ﴿for divorced women﴾. However, some scholars said: this is general but intends the specific. What is the specific that is intended?

He said: The specific (khass) one intended is the woman who is divorced before consummation and for whom no dowry was specified. In his view, this verse is merely an emphasis of the preceding verse and adds no new meaning. As for its outward sense, Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah), may Allah have mercy on him, adopted it in one place in his words, and in another place he said: mut'ah (provision) is obligatory for every divorced woman, except the one divorced before consummation for whom a dowry was set, in which case she is due half the dowry.

From the noble verse it is derived that it is appropriate to emphasize rights which people may be lax about. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿a duty upon the God-conscious (haqqan 'ala al-muttaqin)﴾.

It is also derived from it that it is appropriate to mention the qualities which move a person to act, or, to put it more accurately, which move a person to comply by doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿upon the God-conscious (ala al-muttaqin)﴾, because attaching this to the God-conscious is evidence that its opposite contradicts taqwa (God-consciousness), that failing to perform it contradicts taqwa, and that performing it is part of taqwa.

As for the second verse, among its benefits: the manifestation of Allah's favor upon His servants by clarifying the verses, based on His saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses (kadhalika yubayyinu)﴾.

Also among its benefits: the wisdom behind the rulings of marriage and divorce may be hidden from a person, because Allah made the clarification of that to Himself, saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the refutation of the mufawwidah (those who delegate meaning), the ahl al-tajhil (people of ignorance), and the ahl al-tahrif (distorters) who call themselves ahl al-ta'wil (interpreters). From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you His verses (yubayyinu Allahu lakum ayatihi)﴾, because the people of tafwid, who are the people of tajhil, say that Allah did not clarify what He meant in the verses and hadiths about the attributes, and that these verses and hadiths are like the disjointed letters whose meaning is not understood.

It also refutes the distorters. How so? Because the distorters say: Allah did not clarify, and clarification is only what we grasp with our intellects. We reply: if what you say were intended, Allah would have clarified it; since He did not clarify what you claim, it is known that it is not intended.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: praise of the intellect. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿so that you may understand (la'allakum ta'qilun)﴾. However, what is meant is sound intellect free from doubts and desires; intellects that are not sound are not really intellects but mere desires. Almighty Allah says: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ [al-Mu'minun 71].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: establishing causation (ta'lil) in Allah's actions. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿so that you may understand﴾.

Also among its benefits: it is impossible for there to exist in the Sharia a ruling that is not clarified. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾; "ayat" here is a plural construct, so it is general.

If someone says: we find some texts are hidden from us? The answer: that is either due to deficiency in our understanding or shortcoming in our reflection. As for the text in itself being unclarified, this is impossible. Is this clear?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 243:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not seen those who went out from their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death? Then Allah said to them, "Die," then He restored them to life.﴾ to the end of the verse.

The interrogative here, which precedes a negation, is intended to affirm and to express wonder as well in this verse. His saying ﴿tara﴾ (see) means "look at" (tanzur). The address is either to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ or to everyone who can be addressed, and which of the two is better? The latter, because it is more general.

﴿to those who went out from their homes, and they were thousands﴾ ﴿went out from their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death﴾. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not specify who these people who went out were. It has been said that they were from the Children of Israel, and it has been said that they were from others. The truth is that the lineage of these people is not important to us; what matters to us is, what? The story and the matter that occurred. As for their lineage, it does not concern us.

His saying ﴿went out from their homes﴾ means from their houses and their neighbourhoods to which they would retreat. His saying ﴿and they were thousands﴾ is a clause in the place of an accusative of circumstance (ḥāl) from the waw. The word ﴿ulūf﴾ is the plural of abundance (jam' kathrah) or the plural of paucity (jam' qillah)?

* The students: Abundance.

* The Shaykh: Let us see. The plurals of paucity are four:

"Af'ilah, af'ul, then fi'lah; then af'āl are the plurals of paucity."

﴿ulūf﴾ is from which of the four?
* A student: It is not from them.
* The Shaykh: It is not from them. Therefore it is a plural of abundance. So what is the number of these thousands? It has been said: eight thousand; and it has been said: eighty thousand. Undoubtedly they were a large multitude; ulūf. And if you look at the form of the word ﴿and they were thousands﴾, you find that it indicates more than four, and that ulūf is a large number.

﴿fearing death﴾ is an object of purpose (maf'ūl li-ajlihi), and its governing word is His saying ﴿went out﴾. "Went out" is its governing word, meaning they went out fearing death, that is, out of fear of it. And is this death the natural death, since a plague had descended upon their land, or death by fighting in the way of Allah? On this there are two opinions among the scholars. Some of them say, and they are the majority of the exegetes, that what is meant by ﴿went out from their homes﴾ is fear of death due to a plague that had struck the land, so they went out fleeing from the decree of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed to show them that there is no escape from Him except to Him. And it has been said that they went out fearing death, that is, death by killing, because the enemy had come upon them suddenly, but they were cowardly and went out for fear that the enemy would kill them. Those who said the first said: because if we take the verse by its apparent meaning, ﴿fearing death﴾, and it does not say "fearing fighting," this shows that a plague had descended upon their land, so they went out for fear of this plague that would kill them. Those who said the second said: because Allah said after it: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah﴾, so it is as if Allah, the Exalted, presented the story of these people who were cowardly and fled, then commanded us to fight in the way of Allah and to be patient.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted, says: ﴿Then Allah said to them, "Die," then He restored them to life﴾. Did He say to them a cosmic word or a legislative word?

* The students: Cosmic.

* The Shaykh: Cosmic; meaning He did not command them to die, because if He had commanded them with a legislative command to die, they would not have died, they would not have been able to. Can one cause himself to die?

* The students: He can.

* The Shaykh: Can he restrain himself or not? He cannot (...), nor does he will it. So the word is then a cosmic word, and it is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Yā-Sīn 82]. So Allah said to them, "Die." ﴿Then He restored them to life﴾: then He restored them to life after their death. The word ﴿thumma﴾ (then) indicates delay, and that He restored them to life after a period. And did He restore them to life by a cause or without a cause? Some exegetes said: a prophet of the prophets passed by them while they were thousands, scattered corpses, so he supplicated Allah, Glorified and Exalted, that He restore them to life, and He restored them. And some exegetes said: Allah restored them to life without the supplication of a prophet. And which of the two opinions is the apparent meaning of the wording? The second. The first has no evidence in the context. Accordingly, we say: Allah restored them to life so that He would show His servants His signs. ﴿Then He restored them to life﴾.

﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of﴾: the lām here is for emphasis, and ﴿dhū﴾ means "possessor of." ﴿bounty toward mankind﴾: bounty (fadl) means giving and favour. ﴿but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾: is it all people? Or a few of them? Most. So we have few, and we have all, and we have most, and we have equal, or not? Is it so?

* The student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: And what did we say?

* The student: We said: people are either many or few, or most.

* The Shaykh: Many, or most, or all, or few. ﴿most of mankind do not give thanks﴾. So among people there are those who give thanks? Yes, and His saying the Exalted proves this: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ [Saba 13]. So the majority is opposed by the few: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ [Saba 13].

If someone says: what is the aspect of bounty in this noble verse? We say: the aspect of bounty is that Allah, the Exalted, showed His servants the perfection of His dominion, and that there is no escape from Him. Undoubtedly this is from the bounty of Allah, that Allah the Exalted shows you His signs, His dominion, His power, and His wisdom. We also say: there is another bounty in it: that Allah, the Exalted, saved them. He saved them after He showed them the completeness of His power and dominion; He saved them. By what? By restoring them to life, so they were saved, either from the plague according to one opinion, or from the enemy according to another opinion. Is this bounty or not? This is bounty.

Several matters are derived from this noble verse:

Firstly: that the story of these people was well known, because His saying ﴿Have you not seen﴾ indicates what? Affirmation and wonder, and that this is an actual matter. Look at its examples in the Qur'an and you will find them thus: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh 1]. Is it known or not known? Known.

﴿Did We not make for him two eyes?﴾ [al-Balad 8]. Known or not known? Known. ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord extended the shadow?﴾ [al-Furqan 45]. Known. ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ [al-Fil 1]. Known or not? All this is a known matter, so it is as if the story of these people was famous and known, and for this reason it came in the form of affirmation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is not permissible for a person to flee from the decree of Allah. From where is this taken? From the saying of Allah: ﴿Then Allah said to them, "Die"﴾. And it is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ that the Prophet ﷺ said concerning plague: "If you hear of it in a land, do not enter upon it; and if it occurs while you are in it, do not leave it fleeing from it"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (5729), and Muslim (2219/98), from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may Allah be pleased with him.]] fleeing from it. As for leaving for another reason, there is no harm.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the completeness of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by His saying ﴿Die﴾, and they died, or not?

* The students: Yes, they died.

* The Shaykh: They died; by the evidence of His saying ﴿Then He restored them to life﴾. So it is derived from it the completeness of His power in causing the living to die and the dead to live.

* Among its benefits: that it contains an indication of resurrection. What is its aspect? That these people were restored to life after He had caused them to die. And this surah has already mentioned the proof of Allah's power to revive the dead in five places, which I think have passed?

The first place: in the case of the people of Moses, that the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking, then Allah resurrected them after their death.

The second: the story of the murdered man, when Allah commanded that a cow be slaughtered and that some of it be placed on him, so they struck him with part of it and Allah revived him.

The third story: this one (...). The fourth verse: the one who passed by a town that was fallen upon its roofs, and said: ﴿How will Allah revive this after its death?﴾ So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then resurrected him [al-Baqarah 259], and it will come, Allah willing, Exalted is He.

The fifth story: the story of Abraham: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.﴾ He said: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾ He said: ﴿Yes, but that my heart may be at rest﴾ [al-Baqarah 260]. Look, five events in one surah, all establishing the resurrection, and that Allah, the Exalted, is capable of that.

It is derived from the noble verse: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, making His signs clear to people and rescuing them from destruction is from His bounty, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah 243].

And it is derived from it: that Allah has a favour upon the disbeliever, by His saying ﴿toward mankind﴾, which is general. But Allah's favour upon the disbeliever is not like His favour upon the believer, because Allah's favour upon the believer is a favour connected to the favour of this world and the Hereafter, while upon the disbeliever His favour is in this world only.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the thankful among people are few, by His saying ﴿but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾.

* Among its benefits: that reason indicates the obligation of thanking the Benefactor, because He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty﴾, then He said: ﴿most of mankind do not give thanks﴾. And is this in the manner of blame or of praise? Blame. So whoever does not give thanks is blameworthy by reason and by the Sharia.

It is derived from the verse: the affirmation that Allah speaks: ﴿Then Allah said to them, "Die."﴾

And it is also derived from it: that the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿when He intends a thing, that He says to it, "Be"﴾ [Yā-Sīn 82] is that Allah speaks with what He wills; He does not merely say "Be," but He speaks with what He wills: "Be such-and-such"; because speech with the word ﴿Be﴾ is it general or specified? General. And when Allah said to the pen, "Write," it said: "My Lord, what shall I write?"[[Reported by Abū Dāwūd (4700) from the hadith of ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, may Allah be pleased with him.]] The meaning of His saying ﴿Be﴾ becomes: the command derived from this form, but it is a particular command. So if Allah wanted to send down rain, what would He say?

* A student: "Send down."

* The Shaykh: Yes, "Rain down, O cloud, rain," for example; He does not say only "Be," but it is in the form that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills.

Also among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of omitting what is known, and that this does not contradict eloquence, which the rhetoricians call ellipsis by omission (ījāz al-ḥadhf), ellipsis by omission. From where is this taken?

* A student: From (...).

* The Shaykh: No.

* A student: ﴿went out from their homes﴾.

* The Shaykh: No.

* A student: "Then He said to them."

* The Shaykh: ﴿Then Allah said to them, "Die," then He restored them to life﴾. Without doubt there is an omitted speech; the estimate is: "So they died," yes, "so they died, then He restored them to life." This is frequent in the Qur'an, and it is called ellipsis by omission, that is, restriction (iqtiṣār). It has passed with us that there is abridgement (ikhtiṣār) and there is restriction (iqtiṣār). What is the difference between them? Abridgement means what?

* A student: That its wording is few.

* The Shaykh: That its wording is few while its meaning is abundant; that is, you reduce the letters while the meaning remains. And restriction: you omit part of the matter and confine yourself to part of it.

* The student: (...) affirmation includes wonder.

* The Shaykh: Wonder, yes. Why?

The clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

* A student: And among the benefits of the previous verse.

* The Shaykh: The twelfth benefit of the verse as well: the praise of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, for Himself, meaning that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, praises Himself for what He has bestowed upon His servants. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "None is more fond of praise than Allah, Mighty and Majestic"[[Agreed upon; reported by al-Bukhārī (4637), and Muslim (2760/33), from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿūd; the wording is Muslim's.]]. He, Glorified and Exalted, loves to be praised and commended, because that is truth and right; He is most worthy of being praised and most worthy of being commended. He loves truth, Glorified and Exalted, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah 243].

The thirteenth: that it is part of human nature to flee from death, by His saying: ﴿went out from their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death﴾ [al-Baqarah 243].

From this benefit it follows: that a person should prepare himself for that which he fears, while he does not know when it will overtake him. Is it clear?

This is the end of what I have on this verse.

* A student: Shaykh, shall we add another benefit?

* The Shaykh: And what is it?

* The student: That the basic principle is settlement (istiṭān), not travel; that is, residing in one's homes is the basic principle, and leaving them is due to an external cause. Is this derived from this verse?

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* The student: ﴿went out from their homes﴾.

* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿went out from their homes﴾, correct.

* The student: Yes, meaning the basic principle is their remaining in their homes, but due to this external cause they left, yet the basic principle is their remaining in their homes.

* The Shaykh: I do not understand.

* A student: O Shaykh, is there no benefit in the great number of them, is there a benefit or as he said?

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is a benefit: even though they were many, it shows the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in that He caused them all to die and restored them all to life, though they were thousands. This perhaps has been alluded to before.

* The student: I say: that they became thousands does not imply that they would be patient.

* The Shaykh: Patient?

* The student: Patient, unlike if they had become few.

* The Shaykh: They were not patient; they went out, they all went out.

* A student: It is not derived, O Shaykh, that few of mankind are the ones who give thanks.

* The Shaykh: We have said it.

He said: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:244].

(Qatilu): the object has been omitted here, and the object is well known: it is the disbelievers. "Fight the disbelievers."

His words ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ mean "in His path." This covers both intention and action. As for intention, the person should intend by his fighting that the word of Allah be supreme, as is found in the authentic hadith: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about a man who fights out of zeal, and a man who fights out of bravery, and a man who fights to be seen in his position: which of these is in the way of Allah?" Which of them, the one motivated by zeal, the one motivated by bravery, or the one who fights to be seen for his position, out of showing off and reputation, is in the way of Allah? The Prophet (ﷺ) gave a balanced answer to all three and said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is supreme, he is in the way of Allah."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (123) and Muslim (1904/150), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] This is fighting in the way of Allah: that your intention be that the word of Allah is supreme, not your own word, nor the word of your leader whom you follow, nor the word of anyone else, but the word of Allah, the Exalted, that the word of Allah be supreme. That is so. This is in terms of intention. Likewise, "in the way of Allah" is in terms of action: that a person's action in his jihad conforms to the Sharia, so that he adheres to what the Sharia has required him to adhere to, such as obedience to the commander, not to go out to fight except with his permission, not to withdraw from fighting except with his permission, and similar things required by the actions of jihad.

So it includes both this and that, because (fi) indicates location, so it encompasses both matters together: the intention, and what else? And the action.

On this basis, it is not permissible for us to attack the disbelievers except in the manner the Sharia has permitted: ﴿But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:193].

His words ﴿in the way of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾: when He commanded killing, He warned against opposing Him, so He said: ﴿and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, Hearing of your words and Knowing of your states. The command here is for warning, not merely for informing us of knowledge, because merely knowing that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, without that having an effect on us by complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition, is of no benefit. I say: merely knowing that has no benefit. Rather, it must have an effect on our direction, which is to be careful not to oppose Him, so that we do not say or do what He does not approve, due to His saying: ﴿and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾.

In this noble verse there is a command to fight. Is this a command to fight itself, or a command to sincerity of intention in fighting?
