For this reason the king Talut said to them: ﴿Indeed God will test you with a river﴾, meaning He will examine you by it. ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it, he is of me, except one who scoops a handful with his hand﴾. So they became three groups. That is, he made for them three states: whoever drinks from it until he is quenched, he is not of me, and I am free of him, because whoever cannot endure thirst and cannot endure the orders of the commander will not be able to endure facing the enemies, so he is prevented from entering the battle. ﴿And whoever does not taste it﴾, meaning he never tasted it at all, ﴿he is of me﴾, the opposite of the first who drank until he was quenched. ﴿Except one who scoops a handful with his hand﴾, meaning: he may be of me, because a handful is small and a person may need it, and he is compelled to it to wet his throat. So now it has become clear that he set for them three states. The first?

* Student: Those who drink from it, if they drink from it until they are quenched, then they are not of it.
* Shaykh: Those who drink until they are quenched, then they are not of it.
* Student: And one who scoops a handful with his hand.
* Shaykh: And one who does not taste it at all, he is of it. And one who drinks a handful with his hand is of it, but his rank is below the rank of one who did not taste it. What is this test for? We said: so that it may be known who endures hardship and who does not. It is like training and drilling in patience. This is one. Second: so that it may be known who carries out the orders of the commander and who does not. ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it, he is of me, except one who scoops a handful with his hand﴾. What was the result of this trial and examination? He said: ﴿So they drank from it, except a few of them﴾. So most of them drank, and most of them were not fit for fighting, because they were unable to endure the thirst, and they were not sincere in carrying out the commander's order. ﴿They drank from it, except a few of them﴾. It was said: they were eighty thousand, and they drank from it except about four thousand. It was said otherwise, and God knows best. But the important point in the Qur'an is that these many great chieftains all drank, except a few of them. Who were these few? They were those who were not disowned, whether they did not taste it or scooped a small handful with their hands. ﴿Then when he crossed it, he and those who believed with him﴾. ﴿Crossed it﴾ means passed beyond it, and it does not necessarily mean that they crossed over it from above. The point is that they went beyond it. ﴿He﴾, that is Talut, ﴿and those who believed with him said: "We have no strength today against Jalut (Goliath) and his armies."﴾ ﴿They said﴾: to whom does the pronoun refer?

* Student: The context.
* Shaykh: It was said that it refers to all of them: ﴿They said: "We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies."﴾ And it was said that it refers to those who crossed over, those who crossed it with Talut, those who believed with him. On the first view, all the people had crossed it, but those who drank from it hesitated to drink, then joined them afterward. And those who did not drink from it were what? In the company of Talut, they had not separated from him.

As for the second view, it says: those who drank did not cross it, but remained at the river and said: "What do we have to do with fighting?" And those who said: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies﴾ were those who were with Talut. So on the first view, those who said ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies﴾ were those who drank and others who said that out of cowardice and fear. But if we say: he and those who believed with him, then it was not cowardice on their part, rather they were brave, but they saw that they had little equipment and their enemy was numerous and strong, and they were led by Jalut, a man of the chiefs of the Palestinians, while those with the king were from the Children of Israel. ﴿They said: "We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies."﴾ Look: ﴿no strength﴾ means no capacity, and that fighting them is beyond our capacity. And their saying ﴿today﴾: the "al" here is for specific reference (al-'ahd). Which specific reference? The reference of the present (al-'ahd al-huduri). As for the future, it is possible that we will have strength against them, either because God will support us with numbers or because they will become weak. But today we have no strength against Jalut and his armies. ﴿Those who thought that they would meet God said﴾. This supports the view of those who said that those who said "We have no strength against Jalut and his armies" were all the troops, both those who drank and those who did not.

﴿Those who thought that they would meet God said﴾: ﴿thought﴾ means "were certain," because "thought" may be used to mean certainty, although the basic meaning of "thought" is probability. But here it means certainty. ﴿That they would meet God﴾: when? On the Day of Resurrection, when they will meet God, glory be to Him, and He will call them to account. It is known that whoever is certain of meeting God will act for that meeting. When a person knows that he will meet someone, he prepares for him. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal when he sent him to Yemen: "Indeed you are going to a people of the Book." And here we are, looking at those who want to enter upon the great, preparing for them with speech, appearance, walking and other things. So whoever is certain of meeting God will prepare for that meeting. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿O man, indeed you are labouring toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq 6]. You will certainly meet Him. ﴿That they would meet God﴾: who are these who think that they will meet God? They are the sincere believers. And it is not far-fetched that they are those who did not taste it, and that the two groups, the one that drank and the one that scooped, were not included in this.

They said: ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of God﴾. ﴿How often﴾ here: is it for multiplicity or for interrogation?

* The students: For multiplicity.
* Shaykh: For multiplicity. ﴿How often has a company...﴾ means: how many small companies there have been that overcame large companies. Is there a parallel to this verse in the Qur'an?
* Student: ﴿And how many an angel there is in the heavens﴾ [An-Najm 26].
* Shaykh: No, that is not it. It is not evidence for "kam" except that a small company overcomes a large company. ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two companies which met: one fighting in the way of God and another disbelieving; they saw them as twice their number by sight. And God supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾ [Ali 'Imran 13]. So they saw them as twice their number with their own eyes, and yet God gave them victory. ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of God﴾. By His legislative permission or His cosmic permission?

* Student: The cosmic permission.
* Shaykh: By His cosmic permission, whether the victorious party is one whom God loves or one whom God does not love. The small victorious company may be one whom God does not love, but He, glory be to Him, permits that for a wisdom that requires this permission. An example: the expedition of Hunayn. The ones with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, were twelve thousand, while Hawazin were three thousand five hundred. A great difference. Yet when the Muslims took pride in their numbers and said, "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers," they were defeated by this small number. By what? By the permission of God. God, mighty and majestic, has wisdom in His creation. He may decree things in a way whose benefit is hidden from us, but it is a great benefit in the knowledge of God. In the end, by the praise of God, victory went to the Muslims, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, overcame them and took very many spoils from them. The summary: ﴿How often has a small company﴾: is it a believing company, or is that not a condition?

* The students: It is not a condition.
* Shaykh: It is not a condition. For this reason they did not say, "How often has a believing company," but ﴿How often has a small company﴾, meaning a small group ﴿overcome a large company by the permission of God﴾. Then they said, encouraging their peoples: ﴿And God is with the patient﴾. That is: be patient, so that God may be with you. Here, these groups who thought they would meet God, look at the benefit of faith: its benefit is that they prepared these people and steadied them. ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company﴾: this is in terms of matters that are witnessed. ﴿And God is with the patient﴾: this is in terms of matters that are known, because God's companionship is not witnessed but is known by its effects. But how many a small company is witnessed, or not? The small company overcoming the large company is witnessed. So they steadied them and prepared them by mentioning these two matters: do not say these are many and we are few, for how often a small company has overcome a large one, and if you are patient, God is with the patient. Many times we have already mentioned that patience is divided into three kinds: patience in obeying God, which is the highest; patience in refraining from His disobedience; and patience in His painful decrees. Jihad involves patience in obeying God, patience in refraining from the disobedience of God, and patience in the decrees of God. So it encompasses all three kinds of patience. Patience in obeying God, why? Because the one who strives in the way of God is obedient to God, mighty and majestic. What did he expend in this obedience? He expended what is most precious to him, which is himself. He exposes his neck to the swords of the people seeking the face of God and complying with His command. Patience in refraining from the disobedience of God: he did not flee when he met the enemy, but stood firm. So in it is patience in what?

* Student: Disobedience.
* Shaykh: Patience in refraining from the disobedience of God. Patience in the decrees of God: he is wounded and broken, and in that he is patient. God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, then indeed they are suffering as you suffer; but you hope from God what they do not hope﴾ [An-Nisa 104]. Do not think that the pain of war is upon you alone. It is upon you and upon them, and you are distinguished from them by a distinction, which is ﴿you hope from God what they do not hope﴾ [An-Nisa 104]. You fight, hoping for the high ranks of Paradise, while they fight, may God protect us, not hoping for that from God. Rather their slain are in the Fire. As 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said when Abu Sufyan said at the battle of Uhud, "A day for a day of Badr, and war is by turns," they said to him, "Not equal: our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire." Is there equality between them? Never. A great difference. Where then is the "turns" between us and you? The point is that the saying of this believing company who thought they would meet God contained steadying from two directions: from a witnessed direction and from a known direction perceived by its effects. The witnessed: ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of God﴾. The known: ﴿And God is with the patient﴾. And patience in its three kinds is realized in jihad in the way of God.

He said: ﴿And God is with the patient﴾ (249). ﴿And when they went out to Jalut and his armies﴾. ﴿They went out﴾ means they appeared, from "al-baraz," which is the wide, open, visible land. They went out, the two groups met, and they saw themselves as weak. God, mighty and majestic, always gives victory to those whose hearts are broken, who see themselves as weak. When they went out to Jalut and his armies, they did not rely on their own strength, but turned to God, mighty and majestic, and said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience, make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people﴾. They asked for three things. They said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾, meaning fill our hearts with it. The word "pour" (ifragh) of something upon something indicates its comprehensiveness: fill our hearts and our bodies with patience so that we may stand firm, and this involves the removal of what prevents it. ﴿And make firm our feet﴾, meaning make them firm so that they do not slip, so that we do not flee or run away. The word "feet" may also be meant more generally, to include the steadfastness of the hearts as well. The third request: the outcome of this battle, which is ﴿and help us against the disbelieving people﴾. They did not say, for instance, "help us against our enemy" or something similar, but "against the disbelieving people," whom we fight because of their disbelief, not for revenge on ourselves, but because these people are disbelievers, and we fight them for their disbelief. Notice that fighting based on conviction is the fighting in which the enemy is truly harmed, whereas fighting out of zealous partisanship and nationalism is failed fighting. If you wish, and you return to history, you will know this. Who liberated Palestine from the armies of the Christians?

* Student: Salah al-Din.

The Shaykh: Saladin al-Ayyubi. It has been said that he was not Arab. Who was it that wanted to liberate Palestine from a handful of Jews? The Arabs. But they did not liberate it. Rather, it has punished them with humiliation and penalties many times, because they do not fight for a creed. They fight for a nationalism in which the atheist, the Jew, the Christian, the Muslim, and everyone who joins Arabism are equal. But if they fought for a creed and for faith, and said: "We fight the Jews not because they are Jews and we are Arabs, but we fight them because they are disbelievers and we are Muslims," then, if the matter were so, the saying of Allah the Exalted would apply to us: ﴿They will not fight you all together, except in fortified towns or from behind walls﴾ [al-Hashr 14]. ﴿They will not fight you﴾ means: you, in your faith and Islamic description, not because you are Arabs. ﴿They will not fight you all together, except in fortified towns or from behind walls﴾ [al-Hashr 14]. As for you, when you fight because you are Arabs, they will fight you not from behind walls but from above, from the horizon, until they finish you off. Do you understand now? Here those of this group, when they met the enemy, say: ﴿Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and make firm our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. It is not about a people merely because they are our enemies, but because they are disbelieving people. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, answered their supplication, because He, glory be to Him, answers the call of one who is in need of Him. Be in need of Allah and be sincere in your neediness toward Him. Believe that you have no power and no strength, that the whole matter is in the hand of Allah, and trust that Allah will answer you. But the problem is that we call upon Allah as if we were not in need of this supplication, as if we were free of it, or as if our supplication were a routine matter, as they say. Every day we say between the two prostrations: "O Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, provide for me, and grant me well-being." Every day we say it. Do we, when we call upon Allah with this, feel that we are in need of these things, and that we truly ask Allah for them?

A student: Except those whom Allah wills.

The Shaykh: Except those whom Allah wills. But they are few, and this is few. Most people say it, and so one knows he is sitting between the two prostrations by the time, not by the words. If he prostrates immediately after the second, he says: "By Allah, it is as if I have not said any of them at all." In sum, when you are sincere with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in seeking refuge in Him and trusting Him, then Allah, glory be to Him, answers the supplication of those in distress. These people, Allah answered their supplication.

﴿So they routed them by the permission of Allah﴾, not by their own power and strength, but by the permission of Allah, Exalted. Is it His universal (kawni) permission or His legislative (shar'i) permission?

The students: The universal.

The Shaykh: The universal. Some say: the universal and the legislative. But the universal is more apparent. They routed them by the permission of Allah. Those many troops, when they saw them, immediately said: ﴿We have no power today against Jalut and his troops﴾. But they were routed by the permission of Allah.

﴿And Dawud killed Jalut﴾. Dawud, and what brought Dawud? He was one of the troops of Talut, from his soldiers. But he, peace be upon him, was strong and brave. It is said that Jalut demanded single combat. He demanded single combat and said: "Who will fight me?" For this Jalut was a tyrant, stubborn, powerful commander. Dawud came out to him. It is said that he came out to him with a sling. Do you know the sling?

The students: No.

The Shaykh: No. The sling is a cord with a pouch in its middle. In this pouch one places a stone, a stone like an egg for example. Then the person whirls it like this, whirls it so, then releases it, and one end is released while the other end remains in his hand. When he does this, the stone comes out and strikes whatever is in front of him.

A student: Like a catapult (manjaniq)?

The Shaykh: Yes, on the pattern of the catapult. When he came out to him with the sling, that wicked Jalut, it is as if he became furious and enraged and said: "You come out to me with a sling, and I am the brave and daring one?" But he slung it like this, and it split his head, and he fell. Then he cut off his head and brought it to Talut. This is the manner of the killing, and we have no great benefit in it. Is that right or not? Is there great benefit in it? We have no great benefit in it. Therefore Allah did not describe the killing. He said: ﴿Dawud killed Jalut﴾, and the intended goal is the outcome, and it was achieved: Dawud killed Jalut. I think you know that when the commander is killed, the army is routed. For this reason Satan shouted at Uhud. What did he say? He said: "Muhammad has been killed," in order to terrify the people so that they would scatter. Even in hunting, perhaps the brothers who hunt know that when a herd of gazelles comes, usually there is a leader, one in front leading them. When the hunter comes, he does not go to kill the last one; he kills the leader. Once the leader is killed, the group disperses. Even among birds, look at a flock of birds, you will find that there must be a leader in front. When the leader is killed, they scatter; that means they can be overtaken.

When He said: "Dawud killed Jalut," the power and bravery of Dawud became clear to the people, and that he was worthy of being a king, worthy of being a king. It is said that Talut married him to his daughter and ceded the kingship to him. This is, of course, one of the reports of the Children of Israel: it may be so, and it may not be. The essential point is that the kingship passed after Talut to whom? To Dawud, whether he ceded it or Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took him. Allah knows best. The essential point is that the kingship passed to Dawud. For this Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And Allah gave him the kingship and wisdom﴾. ﴿Gave him﴾ means bestowed upon him. Allah gave him the kingship and wisdom. ﴿The kingship﴾: of course, not absolute kingship over everything, because absolute kingship over everything belongs to Allah, the One, the Subduer. Rather, kingship in this part of the earth only.

﴿And wisdom﴾. Wisdom is said to be revelation, and it is said to be the Psalms (Zabur), because it contains wisdom. Allah says: ﴿And We gave Dawud the Zabur﴾ [an-Nisa 163]. In any case, Allah gave Dawud two great matters: one by which he governed the world, and the second by which he governed both the world and the religion. The world: the kingship. The religion and the world: the wisdom.

Then He said: ﴿And taught him from what He willed﴾. He did not teach him everything. He taught Dawud from what He willed. Among what He taught him: ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you to protect you from your violence﴾ [al-Anbiya 80]. Allah taught him from what He willed, because no one knows anything except what Allah has taught him: ﴿And Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers knowing nothing﴾ [an-Nahl 78]. So whatever we know, whether rational or sensory, it is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and were it not so, we would not walk a span. He said: ﴿And taught him from what He willed﴾, meaning from what He wills. The verse here is general, but we may say: among what He taught him was the making of armor, the making of coats of mail for you.

﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted﴾. ﴿Repelling﴾ (daf'); and in another reading: ﴿defense﴾ (difa'), and it is one of the seven readings (sab'iyyah). Here the i'rab (grammatical analysis): ﴿daf'u Allah﴾ is a verbal noun (masdar) annexed to its subject; ﴿an-nas﴾ is the direct object; ﴿ba'dahum﴾ is a substitute (badal) for it; and ﴿bi-ba'd﴾ is attached to daf'. ﴿Were it not for Allah's repelling people by means of others﴾: where is the predicate of the subject? It is omitted, its estimate being "existent"; meaning, were it not that Allah's repelling of people, some by means of others, exists (...) that He repels the disbelievers by the believers, so they fight in the way of Allah until the religion of Allah is established. He repels the disbelievers by means of one another so that neither of the two parties dominates the earth. What do you think now, for example? Among people there are what are called the two superpowers. If control belonged to one of them, it would become tyrannical and dominate the earth. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed against this power something that checks it, restrains it, and frightens it; otherwise the earth would be corrupted. And how would it be corrupted?

Listen: ﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned would have been demolished﴾ [al-Hajj 40]. This is the true corruption on earth. Corruption is not that storms come and knock down fruit, or floods come and destroy buildings and drown crops. That is undoubtedly corruption, but the true corruption is that the religion of Allah and the landmarks of the religion of Allah be eliminated: ﴿monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned would have been demolished﴾. Has this happened or not?

The students: Yes.

The Shaykh: Yes. When the tyrannical disbelieving nations seized the lands of the Muslims, did they leave the mosques and the muezzins calling the adhan and raising the name of Allah? Never. Look at the lands that disbelief has controlled: they prevented them, prevented them from establishing the religion of Allah. And they, I mean the disbelievers, display themselves and inflate their bodies, claiming to be people of freedom and democracy, and they lied in what they said. But it is a claim like the saying of Satan to Adam: ﴿Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers﴾ [al-A'raf 21]. In sum, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes clear in this verse: ﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted﴾. By what? By the obliteration of the landmarks of religion and the spread of the landmarks of disbelief and sins. This is the true corruption. But the verse intends what is more general than that, including the corruption of homes, the demolition of buildings, the drowning of crops, and their burning at the hands of the oppressors. All of this is included.

﴿But Allah is full of bounty toward the worlds﴾, so He protected some by means of others. ﴿Full of bounty﴾ means possessor of bounty, and bounty is abundant, wide, plentiful giving. ﴿Toward the worlds﴾: meaning, all of them, or the knowing ones? Toward the worlds (al-'alamin), meaning all creation. Allah, Exalted, has bounty upon them. They are called a world ('alam) because they are a sign ('alam) pointing to their Creator, glory be to Him. So He, glory be to Him, is full of bounty toward all creation. From where does the disbeliever get his provision?

The students: From Allah.

The Shaykh: Who causes the crops to grow, makes the udder flow with milk, causes the rivers to run, and makes the springs gush forth, if not the disbeliever?

The students: No.

The Shaykh: No? Who did that?

The students: Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

The Shaykh: And who benefits from it? The disbeliever and the Muslim. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has bounty toward all the worlds. All the worlds have bounty from Him. But His bounty toward the believer extends into the Hereafter, and His bounty toward the disbeliever ends with death. Reflect on His saying concerning the pious believers, where He said about them: ﴿They do not taste death therein except the first death﴾ [ad-Dukhan 56]. "Except the first death." Is there a first death in Paradise? No. But since Paradise belongs to the pious and extends even into this world, the pious person is in Paradise even in this world, because Allah says: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [an-Nahl 97]. Taste, my brothers, the taste of this. Taste the taste of piety, so that you may be in the Paradise of this world extending to the Paradise of the Hereafter. And at death, where do they move? To Paradise. So it is true that they did not taste death in it except the first death only.

When Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, was imprisoned, and the door of the prison was locked upon him, he said: "What can my enemies do to me?" That is, what can they do? "What can my enemies do to me? My Paradise is in my breast. My imprisonment is a seclusion. My killing is martyrdom. My exile is wandering." He says: If they kill me, then I am a martyr; if they imprison me, then my imprisonment is a seclusion in which I am alone with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, away from people, and I fill my time with obedience to Allah; if they exile me, then it is wandering: I wander in the earth of Allah and reflect upon the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But the point is his saying, may Allah have mercy on him: "My Paradise is in my breast." And so is the believer. Try it and you will find it. By Allah, there pass over a person hours in which he says: "If the people of Paradise are in such bliss, then they are happy." Sometimes hours pass over you in which you are dazed by everything. And sometimes heedlessness overtakes us, and Satan comes to us from every side and adorns for us some worldly things, and we forget this. Hearts are like the earth, or even more affected than the earth: when the rain stops from it, it dries up; when the rain reaches it again, it is refreshed and brings forth growth. Indeed, hearts are more so, because hearts, may Allah grant us safety, their deviation is very near, very near. They are like a ship among waves: if a person does not keep it steady and set its anchors, it sinks. In sum, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is full of bounty toward the worlds in this world and the Hereafter, toward whom?

The students: Toward the believers.

The Shaykh: Toward the believers. And in this world only, toward the disbelievers, it is a trial and an examination from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Then He said: ﴿These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth﴾. Are the verses of Allah the legislative verses or the universal ones?

A student: It includes both.

The Shaykh: It appears that it includes both. The universal verses of Allah we inform you of, so that you witness and take heed, and the legislative ones, which are the Qur'an: ﴿That We recite to you of the verses and the wise reminder﴾ [Ali 'Imran 58]. So Allah, glory be to Him, recites to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from the verses of Allah, Exalted, both universal and legislative, what serves as a lesson for those who take heed. Then, does this recitation admit falsehood? No. For this reason He said: ﴿in truth﴾, meaning accompanied by truth; no falsehood can reach it in any way. Narrative accounts from other than the Qur'an may be false, but the Qur'an is true, that is, truthful, with no doubt and no falsehood in it.

﴿And indeed you are among the messengers﴾. The address is to whom? To Muhammad ﷺ. He emphasized this with inna and the lam: ﴿Indeed you are among the messengers﴾. Indeed he, peace be upon him, is the best of the messengers and the seal of the prophets ﷺ.

In His saying: ﴿And indeed you are among the messengers﴾ after His saying: ﴿We recite it to you in truth﴾, there is an indication that his ﷺ messengership is confirmed by the fact that what he reported matches reality, for what happened to those chiefs of the Children of Israel exists with evidence in the books of the Children of Israel. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them as a sign that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ And Allah knows best.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when Talut set out with the armies, he said: Indeed, Allah is going to test you with a river﴾, to the end. In this is evidence that the leader should inspect his soldiers, based on His saying: ﴿So when Talut set out with the troops﴾, meaning he departed with them, walked with them, considered their conditions, and arranged them.

Among its benefits is also that he should, indeed must, prevent anyone unfit for war from going, whether he is a discourager, a spreader of fear, or an atheist. The essential point is that whoever is not fit for war must be prevented. From where is this derived? Because He said: ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me﴾, meaning he is not fit for fighting. ﴿And whoever does not taste it is of me, except one who takes a handful with his hand﴾. So whoever is not fit must be prevented. What is the difference between the discourager (mukhadhdhil) and the spreader of fear (murjif)? The discourager is one who demoralizes the army; he says: "You will not be victorious." The spreader of fear is one who instills awe of the enemy. The first weakens, and the second instills awe of the enemy. This is the difference between them. The discourager mentions the attribute of weakness, and the spreader of fear mentions the attribute of the enemy's strength. Each of them must be kept away.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: it is obligatory to test the soldiers, which is now known as maneuvers. We must test the soldiers' capacity for endurance, steadfastness, and obedience. Are modern military methods derived from this, although they have developed with time, or are they not derived from this?

A student: Explain?

The Shaykh: He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is going to test you with a river; whoever drinks from it is not of me﴾, as drills.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: those people, despite knowing that Talut was fit for kingship, divided into three groups regarding him.

* Among its benefits: most of Allah's servants do not carry out the command of Allah. Most of them, as in His saying: ﴿So they drank from it, except for a few of them﴾. This is a matter witnessed by the situation. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ [Saba' 13]. So the obedient are few, and the defiant are many.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 249–252 (part 3 of 4):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible for a person to report a situation as it is, if he does not intend harm or if no harm results from it. They said: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his soldiers﴾. It may be said that the verse does not indicate this, and that it contains evidence that the coward is in constant fear and terror, from their saying: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his soldiers﴾.
* Among its benefits: among the benefits of faith is patience and endurance. ﴿Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said: "How often has a small company overcome a great company by the permission of Allah!"﴾ ﴿When Talut set out with the soldiers, he said: "Allah will test you with a river"﴾, and so on to the end.
  From this noble verse it is derived: the legitimacy of testing soldiers by their patience and their lack of patience. This resembles what is done today and is called military maneuvers (al-manawarat al-harbiyyah), for these maneuvers are a training and test of the soldiers: how do they carry out the plan they have learned?
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, tests His servants, either by abstaining from something beloved or by falling into something disliked, in order that He, glorified and exalted, may know their patience. There are parallels to this, among them what Allah related about the Children of Israel when He forbade them to hunt fish on the Sabbath. The fish would come on the Sabbath in abundance, and on other days they would see none. So what did they do? They devised a trick. This trick was that they set up nets on Friday, so when the fish came on the Sabbath they would enter the nets and become entangled in them, and on Sunday they would take them out. In this there was a trick against the prohibitions of Allah, and therefore Allah took vengeance upon them. This also happened to the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, in what?
* Students: In hunting.
* Shaykh: In hunting, when it was forbidden to them while they were in the state of ihram, and Allah tested them with game that their hands and spears could reach. But they, may Allah be pleased with them, refrained from it. Here, this river is what Allah, glorified and exalted, tested them with, and they became thirsty. Their Prophet said to them: ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is of me, except one who scoops up a handful with his hand﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: when testing, Allah, mighty and majestic, shows mercy to creation by providing what keeps their lives preserved. His saying here: ﴿except one who scoops up a handful with his hand﴾ shows this, because they must drink in order to be saved from death.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinist sect), from His saying: ﴿Whoever drinks﴾ and ﴿except one who scoops﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: only a few people are those who remain patient in times of trial, from His saying: ﴿Then they drank from it, except a few of them﴾.
Then Allah, exalted, said: ﴿When he and those who believed with him crossed it, they said: "We have no strength today against Jalut and his soldiers"﴾. This is evidence that among people there is one who is a mirjif (one who spreads alarm) or a mukhadhdhil (one who discourages). The difference between the mirjif and the mukhadhdhil is that the mirjif is the one who mentions the strength of the enemy and spreads fear by it, while the mukhadhdhil is the one who says: "We cannot do this," thereby revealing his own weakness. Here they said: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his soldiers﴾. Are these discouragers or alarmists?
* Students: Discouragers.
* Shaykh: Discouragers, and at the same time alarmists too, because they say: "We have no strength against them, for they are greater and stronger than us."
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: certainty drives a person to patience, endurance, hope and expectation, from their saying: ﴿Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said: "How often has a small company overcome a great company by the permission of Allah!"﴾ Look: with certainty they said this statement. Did they say it to themselves or to others? It was previously mentioned that they said it to others, when those (others) said: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his soldiers﴾, and they replied to them.
In this noble verse there is an affirmation of meeting Allah, from His saying: ﴿Those who were certain that they would meet Allah﴾. Allah, exalted, has said: ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 6]. Some of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah) have used this as evidence for the affirmation of seeing Allah, mighty and majestic, saying: meeting is not true unless each of the two who meet sees the other. This argument may be open to discussion, since meeting does not necessarily imply seeing.
* Among its benefits: the word "zann" (suspicion/assumption) comes in the place of certainty, meaning that it is used in the sense of certainty. From where is this derived? ﴿Those who were certain that they would meet Allah﴾, because the zann here does not mean a probable thing, since meeting Allah must be believed in by a person with certainty.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: what these certain believers mentioned, that a small company may overcome a great company by the permission of Allah. This has occurred in previous nations and has occurred in this Ummah, such as the Battle of Badr, for in the Battle of Badr a small company overcame a large company. It may also be the reverse: a large company may be defeated, even if the truth is with it, as in the Battle of Hunayn, but for a reason.
Also among the benefits of the noble verse: when a person mentions something, he should qualify it with "by the permission of Allah," or "by the will of Allah," or something similar, from His saying: ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾.
And among them: the affirmation of permission belonging to Allah, glorified and exalted. It has passed with us that it is divided into two types: kawni (universal, relating to creation) permission and shar'i (legislative) permission. In this verse, is the permission kawni or shar'i?
* Students: Kawni.
* Shaykh: Kawni. And in His saying about the sorcerers: ﴿And they could not harm anyone by it except by the permission of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 102]?
* Students: Kawni.
* Shaykh: Kawni also. And in His saying: ﴿Say: "Has Allah given you permission, or do you invent [lies] against Allah?"﴾ [Yunus 59], this one?
* Students: Shar'i.
* Shaykh: Shar'i. ﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them in religion that for which Allah has not given permission?﴾ [al-Shura 21].
* Students: Shar'i.
* Shaykh: This is shar'i also.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of patience, from His saying: ﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾.
And among them: the affirmation of Allah's companionship (ma'iyyah), mighty and majestic, from His saying: ﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾. If you say: the apparent meaning of this verse is that Allah's companionship is restricted to the patient, while in other verses Allah affirmed His companionship for people in general. He, exalted, said: ﴿He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid 4]. This is general. And He said: ﴿There is no secret conversation among three but that He is their fourth, nor among five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [al-Mujadilah 7]. So what is the answer?
We say: the answer is that this companionship is specific, and that companionship is general. The companionship that Allah attributed to Himself includes what implies a threat, what implies support, and what indicates encompassing and comprehensiveness. What implies support is like: ﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾, ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha 46], ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah 40], and its examples are many. What implies a threat is like His saying: ﴿They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from Allah, and He is with them when they spend the night in what He does not approve of of speech. And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do﴾ [al-Nisa 108]. And the general one is like His saying, exalted: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid 4].
* A student: Encompassing... (...)
* Shaykh: No, no, we have finished. It is comprehensiveness, it is encompassing. If you say: what is the reconciliation between affirming Allah's companionship, mighty and majestic, and affirming His exaltation (uluww)?
The answer is that there is no contradiction between them, for being with us does not require that He be present in the places where we are. Rather, He is with us while He is in the heavens, just as we say: the moon is with us, the Pole Star is with us, the Pleiades are with us, and similar things, even though they are in the sky.
﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾. His saying: ﴿with the patient﴾ includes patience with the decrees of Allah, patience in His obedience, and patience against His disobedience.
Then Allah, exalted, said: ﴿When they came out against Jalut and his soldiers, they said: "Our Lord, pour upon us patience, make firm our feet, and give us victory over the disbelieving people"﴾ [al-Baqarah 250].
Among the benefits of this verse: when a person faces hardships, he should turn to Allah, mighty and majestic, because here, when they came out and the two armies met, they turned to Allah and said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾.
And among its benefits as well: a person's turning to Allah is a cause of his success, because after that He said: ﴿So they defeated them by the permission of Allah﴾. And a person's reliance on himself and his pride in himself is a cause of his failure: ﴿And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you but it did not avail you at all, and the earth became constricted for you despite its vastness﴾. This is a tremendous scene in reality, for many people, when Allah, glorified and exalted, gives them a blessing in their body, wealth or family, consider that it comes from their own power and effort. This is undoubtedly a great error. Rather, it is from Allah, who bestowed it upon you. So look to the root, not to the branch. Looking at the branch and neglecting the root is an error of reason and thinking. Therefore, when Allah bestows a blessing upon you, it is incumbent upon you to praise Allah for it with your tongue, acknowledge it with your heart, and worship Him with your limbs.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a person's need to keep his feet firm in obedience to Allah, from His saying: ﴿and make firm our feet﴾. The opposite of making the feet firm is fleeing, and there is no doubt that fleeing when the two lines meet is one of the major sins.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: mentioning what can be a cause of answered supplication, from His saying: ﴿and give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. They did not say "over our enemies." Rather, ﴿over the disbelieving people﴾, as if they are saying: "Grant us victory over them because of their disbelief." This is in the utmost distance from tribalism and zealotry; that is, we did not ask You to give us victory over them except because they are disbelievers.
Then Allah, exalted, said: ﴿So they defeated them by the permission of Allah, and Dawud killed Jalut﴾, and so on to the end. In this there is evidence for what we pointed out earlier: that turning to Allah, exalted, is a cause of success, and that self-admiration is a cause of its opposite, failure.
Also among the benefits of the noble verse: attributing events to Allah, mighty and majestic, even though they are the acts of a person, from His saying: ﴿So they defeated them﴾. This is their action, but ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾. So Allah is the One who permitted the victory of these and the defeat of those.
* Among its benefits: Dawud, peace be upon him, was one of the prophets of the Children of Israel. ﴿Dawud killed Jalut﴾.
* A student: ﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel?﴾?
* Shaykh: No, no.
* The student: It was mentioned before.
* Shaykh: Because He said before: ﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa?﴾. This is evidence that Dawud was from the Children of Israel, and that he was also after Musa, because He said: ﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa?﴾, and Dawud was among them.
Also among its benefits: the courage of Dawud, peace be upon him, when he killed Jalut when Jalut came out against him. Courage in single combat has tremendous importance, for if the challenger is killed in front of his soldiers, it will undoubtedly put fear and terror into their hearts. But is it permissible in this situation for a person to deceive the one who challenges him?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: It is permissible?
* Students: It is permissible, as 'Ali did.
* Shaykh: Yes, it is permissible. Why is it permissible for us to deceive him, when deception is not good? Because the situation is one of war, and each of them wants to kill the other, so there is no harm in deceiving him. "It is related that when 'Amr ibn Wudd came out to challenge 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'Ali called out to him and said: 'I did not come out to fight two men.' So 'Amr thought that someone had come up behind him, so he turned, and 'Ali struck him." This is a trick, but it is permissible, because the situation is one of war, and he wants to kill me by every means.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Dawud, peace be upon him, was given kingship and prophethood, from His saying: ﴿And Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom﴾.
And among its benefits as well: the prophets, peace be upon them, have no knowledge except what Allah has taught them, from His saying: ﴿and taught him from what He willed﴾. The prophet himself is not knowledgeable; he does not know the unseen, nor does he know the law except what Allah, glorified and exalted, has given him.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's will, from His saying: ﴿and taught him from what He willed﴾.
And among the benefits of the noble verse as well: Allah, mighty and majestic, repels some people by means of others so that the earth and whoever is upon it may be set right. ﴿Were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted﴾. And by what is it corrupted? It is corrupted by sins and by abandoning obligations, as indicated by His saying, exalted: ﴿Were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques, in which the name of Allah is much mentioned, would have been demolished﴾ [al-Hajj 40].
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's wisdom, in that He made people repel one another and counter one another. Had He given authority to specific people, they would have corrupted the earth, because there would be no one to oppose them. But Allah, mighty and majestic, counters this with that. Consider this now regarding the strength of the disbelieving nations today. What do you think if one of these great states had absolute power over the other state? It would sweep it away and sweep away others as well. But Allah gave this one strength and that one strength, so that some may repel others.
Among them: sins and the demolition of places of worship are a cause of corruption. We have said that the corruption of the earth is explained in other verses, and so it is. The demolition of places of worship is undoubtedly one of the forms of corruption in the earth. Now, what about the one who prevents worship?
* A student: More severe and more deserving.
* Shaykh: More severe and more deserving. For this reason Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them﴾ [al-Baqarah 114].
And among them: the affirmation of the grace of Allah, glorified and exalted, over all creation, from His saying: ﴿But Allah is full of bounty to the worlds﴾. Even over the disbelievers? Yes, even over the disbelievers. But Allah's grace toward the disbelievers is a specific grace in this world only. As for the Hereafter, how does He treat them?
* A student: According to what they deserve.
* Shaykh: With justice. In this world He treats them with grace, but in the Hereafter He treats them with justice. This is regarding the disbelievers. As for the believers, Allah treats them with grace in this world and in the Hereafter.
Then Allah, exalted, said: ﴿These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah 252]. In this is an affirmation of Allah's verses, glorified and exalted, meaning the legislative verses, which is the Qur'an.
And in it: Allah, exalted, recites to His Prophet what He revealed to him, from His saying: ﴿We recite them to you in truth﴾. But is the one who recites this Allah, or Jibril?
* A student: Jibril.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 249–252 (part 4 of 4):

* The Shaykh: Recite in the verse of Qiyamah: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyamah 16–18]. Meaning: when Jibril recites it, then follow its recitation. Jibril recites it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he received it from Allah, glorified and exalted be He.
* Among its benefits: the entire Qur'an is true, all of it is truth from Allah and was sent down with truth. The "ba'" in His words ﴿with the truth﴾ also denotes accompaniment and association. So it was indeed sent down from Allah in truth, and it is also comprised of truth. It has not been falsely attributed to Allah, and there is no falsehood in its reports nor injustice in its rulings. Rather, all its rulings are just and all its reports are true.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Prophet's (ﷺ) messengership, based on His words: ﴿And indeed, you are among the messengers﴾.
And among them: that there are other messengers besides the Messenger, based on His words: ﴿among the messengers﴾. However, he (ﷺ) was the Seal of the Prophets, for there is no prophet after him.
This is what Allah has made easy for us of the benefits of these noble verses, although upon reflection they may bear more meanings than these.
* Student: (...): ﴿And Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom﴾?
* The Shaykh: Wisdom is the revelation that Allah revealed to him, whether it is the Sunnah or the Psalms (al-Zabur) which Allah revealed to him.

* Student: Shaykh, is it established that the keeper of Paradise is named Ridwan?
* Shaykh: No, but it is well known. It is well known, though its authenticity is not established. It is well known among the scholars.
(...) and he establishes among them commanding and forbidding.

﴿Their prophet said to them: "Indeed, God has sent Talut (Saul) to you as king."﴾ They found it strange that Talut should be king over them, because he was not of a distinguished lineage among them, nor did he have wealth among them, and he was also below them in rank, so they had a better claim to the kingship than he did. Their prophet explained to them that God's bounty is given to whomever He wills, and that God, exalted is He, had chosen him over them and increased him in breadth of knowledge and of physique. In knowledge: knowledge of statecraft (siyasa) and knowledge of the Sharia. In physique: the strength needed to carry out what he knows of the knowledge of the Sharia and of statecraft. Then God, mighty and majestic, gave them a sign of his kingship, which is the Ark (al-tabut) carried by the angels, containing a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron had left. It also contained, after the sign was completed for them, what indicates that he has the better claim to kingship and that he is fit to rule them, and to "arrange their ranks" (rattaba-hum), meaning to arrange the armies for fighting the enemies who had driven them from their homes and their wealth.

He said: ﴿When Talut set out with the armies﴾, meaning he departed with them, that is, he went forth with them and left his place.

﴿With the armies﴾: the plural of "jund," and they are the fighting army, on the basis that they fight in the way of God to save their homes and their sons. He said: ﴿When Talut set out with the armies﴾. He was an intelligent and sensible man, because God had increased him in breadth of knowledge and of physique, and he had knowledge of their circumstances beforehand, and that when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away except for a few of them. He made clear to them that God would test them with a river. The river is well known: it is flowing water. The people were thirsty, so he said: ﴿Indeed God will test you with a river﴾, meaning He will examine you by it, so that God, mighty and majestic, may know who is patient and who is not patient, since jihad requires hardship and patience. So God tested them with this river, to know who is patient and who is not. This is one purpose. And to know who obeys among those who do not obey. For this reason the king Talut said to them: ﴿Indeed God will test you with a river﴾, meaning He will examine you by it. ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it, he is of me, except one who scoops a handful with his hand﴾. So they became three groups. That is, he made for them three states: whoever drinks from it until he is quenched, he is not of me, and I am free of him, because whoever cannot endure thirst and cannot endure the orders of the commander will not be able to endure facing the enemies, so he is prevented from entering the battle. ﴿And whoever does not taste it﴾, meaning he never tasted it at all, ﴿he is of me﴾, the opposite of the first who drank until he was quenched. ﴿Except one who scoops a handful with his hand﴾, meaning: he may be of me, because a handful is small and a person may need it, and he is compelled to it to wet his throat. So now it has become clear that he set for them three states. The first?

* Student: Those who drink from it, if they drink from it until they are quenched, then they are not of it.
* Shaykh: Those who drink until they are quenched, then they are not of it.
* Student: And one who scoops a handful with his hand.
* Shaykh: And one who does not taste it at all, he is of it. And one who drinks a handful with his hand is of it, but his rank is below the rank of one who did not taste it. What is this test for? We said: so that it may be known who endures hardship and who does not. It is like training and drilling in patience. This is one. Second: so that it may be known who carries out the orders of the commander and who does not. ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it, he is of me, except one who scoops a handful with his hand﴾. What was the result of this trial and examination? He said: ﴿So they drank from it, except a few of them﴾. So most of them drank, and most of them were not fit for fighting, because they were unable to endure the thirst, and they were not sincere in carrying out the commander's order. ﴿They drank from it, except a few of them﴾. It was said: they were eighty thousand, and they drank from it except about four thousand. It was said otherwise, and God knows best. But the important point in the Qur'an is that these many great chieftains all drank, except a few of them. Who were these few? They were those who were not disowned, whether they did not taste it or scooped a small handful with their hands. ﴿Then when he crossed it, he and those who believed with him﴾. ﴿Crossed it﴾ means passed beyond it, and it does not necessarily mean that they crossed over it from above. The point is that they went beyond it. ﴿He﴾, that is Talut, ﴿and those who believed with him said: "We have no strength today against Jalut (Goliath) and his armies."﴾ ﴿They said﴾: to whom does the pronoun refer?

* Student: The context.
* Shaykh: It was said that it refers to all of them: ﴿They said: "We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies."﴾ And it was said that it refers to those who crossed over, those who crossed it with Talut, those who believed with him. On the first view, all the people had crossed it, but those who drank from it hesitated to drink, then joined them afterward. And those who did not drink from it were what? In the company of Talut, they had not separated from him.

As for the second view, it says: those who drank did not cross it, but remained at the river and said: "What do we have to do with fighting?" And those who said: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies﴾ were those who were with Talut. So on the first view, those who said ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies﴾ were those who drank and others who said that out of cowardice and fear. But if we say: he and those who believed with him, then it was not cowardice on their part, rather they were brave, but they saw that they had little equipment and their enemy was numerous and strong, and they were led by Jalut, a man of the chiefs of the Palestinians, while those with the king were from the Children of Israel. ﴿They said: "We have no strength today against Jalut and his armies."﴾ Look: ﴿no strength﴾ means no capacity, and that fighting them is beyond our capacity. And their saying ﴿today﴾: the "al" here is for specific reference (al-'ahd). Which specific reference? The reference of the present (al-'ahd al-huduri). As for the future, it is possible that we will have strength against them, either because God will support us with numbers or because they will become weak. But today we have no strength against Jalut and his armies. ﴿Those who thought that they would meet God said﴾. This supports the view of those who said that those who said "We have no strength against Jalut and his armies" were all the troops, both those who drank and those who did not.

﴿Those who thought that they would meet God said﴾: ﴿thought﴾ means "were certain," because "thought" may be used to mean certainty, although the basic meaning of "thought" is probability. But here it means certainty. ﴿That they would meet God﴾: when? On the Day of Resurrection, when they will meet God, glory be to Him, and He will call them to account. It is known that whoever is certain of meeting God will act for that meeting. When a person knows that he will meet someone, he prepares for him. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal when he sent him to Yemen: "Indeed you are going to a people of the Book." And here we are, looking at those who want to enter upon the great, preparing for them with speech, appearance, walking and other things. So whoever is certain of meeting God will prepare for that meeting. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿O man, indeed you are labouring toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq 6]. You will certainly meet Him. ﴿That they would meet God﴾: who are these who think that they will meet God? They are the sincere believers. And it is not far-fetched that they are those who did not taste it, and that the two groups, the one that drank and the one that scooped, were not included in this.

They said: ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of God﴾. ﴿How often﴾ here: is it for multiplicity or for interrogation?

* The students: For multiplicity.
* Shaykh: For multiplicity. ﴿How often has a company...﴾ means: how many small companies there have been that overcame large companies. Is there a parallel to this verse in the Qur'an?
* Student: ﴿And how many an angel there is in the heavens﴾ [An-Najm 26].
* Shaykh: No, that is not it. It is not evidence for "kam" except that a small company overcomes a large company. ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two companies which met: one fighting in the way of God and another disbelieving; they saw them as twice their number by sight. And God supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾ [Ali 'Imran 13]. So they saw them as twice their number with their own eyes, and yet God gave them victory. ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of God﴾. By His legislative permission or His cosmic permission?

* Student: The cosmic permission.
* Shaykh: By His cosmic permission, whether the victorious party is one whom God loves or one whom God does not love. The small victorious company may be one whom God does not love, but He, glory be to Him, permits that for a wisdom that requires this permission. An example: the expedition of Hunayn. The ones with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, were twelve thousand, while Hawazin were three thousand five hundred. A great difference. Yet when the Muslims took pride in their numbers and said, "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers," they were defeated by this small number. By what? By the permission of God. God, mighty and majestic, has wisdom in His creation. He may decree things in a way whose benefit is hidden from us, but it is a great benefit in the knowledge of God. In the end, by the praise of God, victory went to the Muslims, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, overcame them and took very many spoils from them. The summary: ﴿How often has a small company﴾: is it a believing company, or is that not a condition?

* The students: It is not a condition.
* Shaykh: It is not a condition. For this reason they did not say, "How often has a believing company," but ﴿How often has a small company﴾, meaning a small group ﴿overcome a large company by the permission of God﴾. Then they said, encouraging their peoples: ﴿And God is with the patient﴾. That is: be patient, so that God may be with you. Here, these groups who thought they would meet God, look at the benefit of faith: its benefit is that they prepared these people and steadied them. ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company﴾: this is in terms of matters that are witnessed. ﴿And God is with the patient﴾: this is in terms of matters that are known, because God's companionship is not witnessed but is known by its effects. But how many a small company is witnessed, or not? The small company overcoming the large company is witnessed. So they steadied them and prepared them by mentioning these two matters: do not say these are many and we are few, for how often a small company has overcome a large one, and if you are patient, God is with the patient. Many times we have already mentioned that patience is divided into three kinds: patience in obeying God, which is the highest; patience in refraining from His disobedience; and patience in His painful decrees. Jihad involves patience in obeying God, patience in refraining from the disobedience of God, and patience in the decrees of God. So it encompasses all three kinds of patience. Patience in obeying God, why? Because the one who strives in the way of God is obedient to God, mighty and majestic. What did he expend in this obedience? He expended what is most precious to him, which is himself. He exposes his neck to the swords of the people seeking the face of God and complying with His command. Patience in refraining from the disobedience of God: he did not flee when he met the enemy, but stood firm. So in it is patience in what?

* Student: Disobedience.
* Shaykh: Patience in refraining from the disobedience of God. Patience in the decrees of God: he is wounded and broken, and in that he is patient. God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, then indeed they are suffering as you suffer; but you hope from God what they do not hope﴾ [An-Nisa 104]. Do not think that the pain of war is upon you alone. It is upon you and upon them, and you are distinguished from them by a distinction, which is ﴿you hope from God what they do not hope﴾ [An-Nisa 104]. You fight, hoping for the high ranks of Paradise, while they fight, may God protect us, not hoping for that from God. Rather their slain are in the Fire. As 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said when Abu Sufyan said at the battle of Uhud, "A day for a day of Badr, and war is by turns," they said to him, "Not equal: our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire." Is there equality between them? Never. A great difference. Where then is the "turns" between us and you? The point is that the saying of this believing company who thought they would meet God contained steadying from two directions: from a witnessed direction and from a known direction perceived by its effects. The witnessed: ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of God﴾. The known: ﴿And God is with the patient﴾. And patience in its three kinds is realized in jihad in the way of God.

He said: ﴿And God is with the patient﴾ (249). ﴿And when they went out to Jalut and his armies﴾. ﴿They went out﴾ means they appeared, from "al-baraz," which is the wide, open, visible land. They went out, the two groups met, and they saw themselves as weak. God, mighty and majestic, always gives victory to those whose hearts are broken, who see themselves as weak. When they went out to Jalut and his armies, they did not rely on their own strength, but turned to God, mighty and majestic, and said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience, make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people﴾. They asked for three things. They said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾, meaning fill our hearts with it. The word "pour" (ifragh) of something upon something indicates its comprehensiveness: fill our hearts and our bodies with patience so that we may stand firm, and this involves the removal of what prevents it. ﴿And make firm our feet﴾, meaning make them firm so that they do not slip, so that we do not flee or run away. The word "feet" may also be meant more generally, to include the steadfastness of the hearts as well. The third request: the outcome of this battle, which is ﴿and help us against the disbelieving people﴾. They did not say, for instance, "help us against our enemy" or something similar, but "against the disbelieving people," whom we fight because of their disbelief, not for revenge on ourselves, but because these people are disbelievers, and we fight them for their disbelief. Notice that fighting based on conviction is the fighting in which the enemy is truly harmed, whereas fighting out of zealous partisanship and nationalism is failed fighting. If you wish, and you return to history, you will know this. Who liberated Palestine from the armies of the Christians?

* Student: Salah al-Din.

The Shaykh: Saladin al-Ayyubi. It has been said that he was not Arab. Who was it that wanted to liberate Palestine from a handful of Jews? The Arabs. But they did not liberate it. Rather, it has punished them with humiliation and penalties many times, because they do not fight for a creed. They fight for a nationalism in which the atheist, the Jew, the Christian, the Muslim, and everyone who joins Arabism are equal. But if they fought for a creed and for faith, and said: "We fight the Jews not because they are Jews and we are Arabs, but we fight them because they are disbelievers and we are Muslims," then, if the matter were so, the saying of Allah the Exalted would apply to us: ﴿They will not fight you all together, except in fortified towns or from behind walls﴾ [al-Hashr 14]. ﴿They will not fight you﴾ means: you, in your faith and Islamic description, not because you are Arabs. ﴿They will not fight you all together, except in fortified towns or from behind walls﴾ [al-Hashr 14]. As for you, when you fight because you are Arabs, they will fight you not from behind walls but from above, from the horizon, until they finish you off. Do you understand now? Here those of this group, when they met the enemy, say: ﴿Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and make firm our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. It is not about a people merely because they are our enemies, but because they are disbelieving people. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, answered their supplication, because He, glory be to Him, answers the call of one who is in need of Him. Be in need of Allah and be sincere in your neediness toward Him. Believe that you have no power and no strength, that the whole matter is in the hand of Allah, and trust that Allah will answer you. But the problem is that we call upon Allah as if we were not in need of this supplication, as if we were free of it, or as if our supplication were a routine matter, as they say. Every day we say between the two prostrations: "O Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, provide for me, and grant me well-being." Every day we say it. Do we, when we call upon Allah with this, feel that we are in need of these things, and that we truly ask Allah for them?

A student: Except those whom Allah wills.

The Shaykh: Except those whom Allah wills. But they are few, and this is few. Most people say it, and so one knows he is sitting between the two prostrations by the time, not by the words. If he prostrates immediately after the second, he says: "By Allah, it is as if I have not said any of them at all." In sum, when you are sincere with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in seeking refuge in Him and trusting Him, then Allah, glory be to Him, answers the supplication of those in distress. These people, Allah answered their supplication.

﴿So they routed them by the permission of Allah﴾, not by their own power and strength, but by the permission of Allah, Exalted. Is it His universal (kawni) permission or His legislative (shar'i) permission?

The students: The universal.

The Shaykh: The universal. Some say: the universal and the legislative. But the universal is more apparent. They routed them by the permission of Allah. Those many troops, when they saw them, immediately said: ﴿We have no power today against Jalut and his troops﴾. But they were routed by the permission of Allah.

﴿And Dawud killed Jalut﴾. Dawud, and what brought Dawud? He was one of the troops of Talut, from his soldiers. But he, peace be upon him, was strong and brave. It is said that Jalut demanded single combat. He demanded single combat and said: "Who will fight me?" For this Jalut was a tyrant, stubborn, powerful commander. Dawud came out to him. It is said that he came out to him with a sling. Do you know the sling?

The students: No.

The Shaykh: No. The sling is a cord with a pouch in its middle. In this pouch one places a stone, a stone like an egg for example. Then the person whirls it like this, whirls it so, then releases it, and one end is released while the other end remains in his hand. When he does this, the stone comes out and strikes whatever is in front of him.

A student: Like a catapult (manjaniq)?

The Shaykh: Yes, on the pattern of the catapult. When he came out to him with the sling, that wicked Jalut, it is as if he became furious and enraged and said: "You come out to me with a sling, and I am the brave and daring one?" But he slung it like this, and it split his head, and he fell. Then he cut off his head and brought it to Talut. This is the manner of the killing, and we have no great benefit in it. Is that right or not? Is there great benefit in it? We have no great benefit in it. Therefore Allah did not describe the killing. He said: ﴿Dawud killed Jalut﴾, and the intended goal is the outcome, and it was achieved: Dawud killed Jalut. I think you know that when the commander is killed, the army is routed. For this reason Satan shouted at Uhud. What did he say? He said: "Muhammad has been killed," in order to terrify the people so that they would scatter. Even in hunting, perhaps the brothers who hunt know that when a herd of gazelles comes, usually there is a leader, one in front leading them. When the hunter comes, he does not go to kill the last one; he kills the leader. Once the leader is killed, the group disperses. Even among birds, look at a flock of birds, you will find that there must be a leader in front. When the leader is killed, they scatter; that means they can be overtaken.

When He said: "Dawud killed Jalut," the power and bravery of Dawud became clear to the people, and that he was worthy of being a king, worthy of being a king. It is said that Talut married him to his daughter and ceded the kingship to him. This is, of course, one of the reports of the Children of Israel: it may be so, and it may not be. The essential point is that the kingship passed after Talut to whom? To Dawud, whether he ceded it or Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took him. Allah knows best. The essential point is that the kingship passed to Dawud. For this Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And Allah gave him the kingship and wisdom﴾. ﴿Gave him﴾ means bestowed upon him. Allah gave him the kingship and wisdom. ﴿The kingship﴾: of course, not absolute kingship over everything, because absolute kingship over everything belongs to Allah, the One, the Subduer. Rather, kingship in this part of the earth only.

﴿And wisdom﴾. Wisdom is said to be revelation, and it is said to be the Psalms (Zabur), because it contains wisdom. Allah says: ﴿And We gave Dawud the Zabur﴾ [an-Nisa 163]. In any case, Allah gave Dawud two great matters: one by which he governed the world, and the second by which he governed both the world and the religion. The world: the kingship. The religion and the world: the wisdom.

Then He said: ﴿And taught him from what He willed﴾. He did not teach him everything. He taught Dawud from what He willed. Among what He taught him: ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you to protect you from your violence﴾ [al-Anbiya 80]. Allah taught him from what He willed, because no one knows anything except what Allah has taught him: ﴿And Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers knowing nothing﴾ [an-Nahl 78]. So whatever we know, whether rational or sensory, it is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and were it not so, we would not walk a span. He said: ﴿And taught him from what He willed﴾, meaning from what He wills. The verse here is general, but we may say: among what He taught him was the making of armor, the making of coats of mail for you.

﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted﴾. ﴿Repelling﴾ (daf'); and in another reading: ﴿defense﴾ (difa'), and it is one of the seven readings (sab'iyyah). Here the i'rab (grammatical analysis): ﴿daf'u Allah﴾ is a verbal noun (masdar) annexed to its subject; ﴿an-nas﴾ is the direct object; ﴿ba'dahum﴾ is a substitute (badal) for it; and ﴿bi-ba'd﴾ is attached to daf'. ﴿Were it not for Allah's repelling people by means of others﴾: where is the predicate of the subject? It is omitted, its estimate being "existent"; meaning, were it not that Allah's repelling of people, some by means of others, exists (...) that He repels the disbelievers by the believers, so they fight in the way of Allah until the religion of Allah is established. He repels the disbelievers by means of one another so that neither of the two parties dominates the earth. What do you think now, for example? Among people there are what are called the two superpowers. If control belonged to one of them, it would become tyrannical and dominate the earth. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed against this power something that checks it, restrains it, and frightens it; otherwise the earth would be corrupted. And how would it be corrupted?

Listen: ﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned would have been demolished﴾ [al-Hajj 40]. This is the true corruption on earth. Corruption is not that storms come and knock down fruit, or floods come and destroy buildings and drown crops. That is undoubtedly corruption, but the true corruption is that the religion of Allah and the landmarks of the religion of Allah be eliminated: ﴿monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned would have been demolished﴾. Has this happened or not?

The students: Yes.

The Shaykh: Yes. When the tyrannical disbelieving nations seized the lands of the Muslims, did they leave the mosques and the muezzins calling the adhan and raising the name of Allah? Never. Look at the lands that disbelief has controlled: they prevented them, prevented them from establishing the religion of Allah. And they, I mean the disbelievers, display themselves and inflate their bodies, claiming to be people of freedom and democracy, and they lied in what they said. But it is a claim like the saying of Satan to Adam: ﴿Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers﴾ [al-A'raf 21]. In sum, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes clear in this verse: ﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted﴾. By what? By the obliteration of the landmarks of religion and the spread of the landmarks of disbelief and sins. This is the true corruption. But the verse intends what is more general than that, including the corruption of homes, the demolition of buildings, the drowning of crops, and their burning at the hands of the oppressors. All of this is included.

﴿But Allah is full of bounty toward the worlds﴾, so He protected some by means of others. ﴿Full of bounty﴾ means possessor of bounty, and bounty is abundant, wide, plentiful giving. ﴿Toward the worlds﴾: meaning, all of them, or the knowing ones? Toward the worlds (al-'alamin), meaning all creation. Allah, Exalted, has bounty upon them. They are called a world ('alam) because they are a sign ('alam) pointing to their Creator, glory be to Him. So He, glory be to Him, is full of bounty toward all creation. From where does the disbeliever get his provision?

The students: From Allah.

The Shaykh: Who causes the crops to grow, makes the udder flow with milk, causes the rivers to run, and makes the springs gush forth, if not the disbeliever?

The students: No.

The Shaykh: No? Who did that?

The students: Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

The Shaykh: And who benefits from it? The disbeliever and the Muslim. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has bounty toward all the worlds. All the worlds have bounty from Him. But His bounty toward the believer extends into the Hereafter, and His bounty toward the disbeliever ends with death. Reflect on His saying concerning the pious believers, where He said about them: ﴿They do not taste death therein except the first death﴾ [ad-Dukhan 56]. "Except the first death." Is there a first death in Paradise? No. But since Paradise belongs to the pious and extends even into this world, the pious person is in Paradise even in this world, because Allah says: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [an-Nahl 97]. Taste, my brothers, the taste of this. Taste the taste of piety, so that you may be in the Paradise of this world extending to the Paradise of the Hereafter. And at death, where do they move? To Paradise. So it is true that they did not taste death in it except the first death only.
