**The Shaykh:** ﴿You will surely see﴾: is it the answer to "law" (if)? Is this ﴿you will surely see﴾ the answer of "law" or not?

**The students:** Yes, no.

**The Shaykh:** No. For this reason it is obligatory to stop at ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾; you must stop there, because if you continued, it would give the false impression that His saying ﴿you will surely see﴾ is the answer to (law), and if it were the answer to (law), the meaning would differ greatly. For this reason some people, we hear them reading ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty (5) you will surely see﴾; this is not correct, because ﴿you will surely see﴾ is the answer to an omitted oath, whose estimate is: "By Allah, you will surely see." ﴿Then you will surely see it with the sight of certainty﴾ [al-Takāthur 7]. This is knowledge of certainty and sight of certainty. Where is the truth of certainty? At the end of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [al-Wāqiʿah 95].

Let us give an example that clarifies the matter. You say: I have a sweet apple, and you have trust in me. What is this?

**The students:** The report of certainty.

**The Shaykh:** Yes, the report of certainty. For me it is a report, and for you it is knowledge. Now you know that I have a sweet apple. Then I take it out of my pocket and say: "This is the apple," the sight of certainty. Then I give it to you, you eat it, and it is sweet. This is the truth of certainty. Is it clear? This is the difference between the knowledge of certainty, the sight of certainty, and the truth of certainty.

Ibrahim, peace be upon him, had the knowledge of certainty without doubt that Allah is capable of giving life to the dead, but he wanted the sight of certainty. For this reason Allah said to him: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾ He said: ﴿Yes, but to reassure my heart﴾. He says: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead﴾.

From the benefits of the verse: affirmation of Allah's voluntary acts, meaning that Allah, glorified and exalted, has acts connected to His will. In His saying: ﴿gives life to the dead﴾.

And from its benefits: the completeness of Allah's power, glorified and exalted, in giving life to the dead. In accordance with this came the noble verse: ﴿Those who disbelieved claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected"﴾ [al-Taghābun 7]. So their disbelief was by denying resurrection.

And from its benefits: affirmation that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, speaks: ﴿He said: "Have you not believed?"﴾, ﴿He said: "Take four"﴾. Allah, glorified and exalted, speaks what He wills, when He wills, however He wills: what He wills of speech, when He wills in time, however He wills in manner. The speech of Allah, glorified and exalted, is with audible sounds and readable letters, because what we are reading now before us is the speech of Allah, and Ibrahim heard the speech of Allah, did he not?

**The students:** Yes.

**The Shaykh:** So it is with a voice, with audible sounds and readable letters.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: affirmation that Ibrahim believed in Allah's power, Mighty and Majestic, to give life to the dead, due to His saying: ﴿Have you not believed?" He said: "Yes"﴾.

If you say: how do you reconcile this with what is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ, Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "We are more deserving of doubt than Ibrahim" [Agreed upon. Al-Bukhārī (4537) and Muslim (151/238), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah], affirming doubt in us and in Ibrahim, and that we are more deserving of doubt than Ibrahim?

The answer: the hadith does not mean this meaning, because this meaning contradicts reality. Does the Messenger ﷺ have any doubt about giving life to the dead?

**The students:** No.

**The Shaykh:** No. But the meaning is: Ibrahim did not doubt. So if it were supposed that he doubted, we would be more deserving of doubt than him. And since doubt is negated concerning us, it is even more negated concerning him, because if we supposed doubt in this matter, we would be what? More deserving of doubt than Ibrahim. So when it is known that we believe that Allah is capable, Ibrahim is more deserving of faith than we are. This is the meaning of the hadith, and it admits of no other.

If you say: the difficulty remains. Is Ibrahim more complete in faith than Muhammad ﷺ?

**The students:** No.

**The Shaykh:** No. But he said this ﷺ by way of humility. For this reason he linked it with his saying: "Had I remained in prison as long as Yusuf remained, I would have answered the caller" [Agreed upon. Al-Bukhārī (3372) and Muslim (151/238), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. How long did Yusuf remain in prison?

**The students:** Seven years.

**The Shaykh:** A few years. And the king's messenger came calling him. He said to him: I will not come out ﴿Return to your Lord and ask Him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands﴾ [Yūsuf 50]. Although he was the one imprisoned for seven years, and they said: come out, will he come out or not? This is what nature requires. But Yusuf, peace be upon him, was forbearing, firm and resolute. He said: I will not come out until my innocence is manifested completely: ﴿Return to your Lord and ask Him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands﴾, to the end of the story. Thus it becomes clear that the saying of the Messenger ﷺ does not necessarily mean that Ibrahim was stronger in faith than him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 260 (part 3 of 3):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: confirmation that faith (iman) increases in the heart. ﴿Yes, but so that my heart may be at rest﴾. This refutes those who say that faith neither increases nor decreases. There is no doubt that this view is weak, because reality contradicts it and the texts contradict it too. In the Qur'an, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿so that they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾ [al-Fath 4], and ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾ [at-Tawbah 124]. In the Sunnah, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have not seen anyone more deficient in intellect and religion who takes away the mind of a prudent man more than one of you women"[[Agreed upon: al-Bukhari, no. (304), and Muslim, no. (80), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]]. So faith increases. But does it increase in quantity, in quality, or in both quantity and quality?
* The students: In both quantity and quality.
* The Shaykh: In both quantity and quality. In quantity: one who glorifies Allah ten times has more faith than one who does so five times, and one who prays ten rak'ahs has more faith than one who prays five. By what does this increase occur?
* The students: By quantity.
* The Shaykh: By quantity. It increases in quality too. Someone who prays two rak'ahs with tranquility, humility and reflection, and someone who prays four rak'ahs quickly: the second has more in number, and the first has more in quality. Likewise, faith increases in proportion to the heart's affirmation. We have just mentioned the actions of the limbs. Faith increases in proportion to the heart's affirmation. The more signs a person has, there is no doubt that his faith becomes more firmly established. Read: ﴿And among the people is one who worships Allah on an edge﴾, meaning on the border, ﴿so if good befalls him, he is reassured by it, but if a trial afflicts him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Hajj 11]. This person's faith is weak and unsteady. If nothing of trial comes to him, he keeps walking; but if a trial comes to him, a doubt or a desire, he turns over on his face. Now, here among us, nobody contests us on creed. There are no Mu'tazilah, no Jahmiyyah, no Jabriyyah, and everyone is walking according to the natural disposition (fitrah). Is that correct or not?
* The students: Correct.
* The Shaykh: But if a person is tested, one of the clever devils from mankind comes, skilled in debate and argument, from the Mu'tazilah, he may influence him and he may turn away, because he has no firm foundation. Likewise, a person may have faith, but a woman of rank and beauty approaches him and entices him until he falls. Another person is approached by the same woman, but he says: "I fear Allah." You find the difference between the two. The point is that the preponderant view, about which there is no doubt, and which is indicated by both the textual evidence and the observed reality, is that faith increases and decreases.
* A student: Regarding our saying ﴿sa'yan﴾ (running): should we not say that the more appropriate meaning is that he walks on the earth quickly, since that is what the wording apparently means?
* The Shaykh: That is what comes to mind first.
* The student: What comes to mind first.
* The Shaykh: Yes. But these others say: the running of each thing is according to its nature. I say: the running of each thing is according to its nature, so birds run with their wings.
* The student: Is there an example in the Qur'an, O Shaykh, of running according to the nature of each thing?
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. How? ﴿So hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 9]. What is meant there is not that you run on foot.
* The student: But running on foot is the most common.
* The Shaykh: No. ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾. This is not the hastening that means running on foot.
* The student: Is this known from the context?
* The Shaykh: This is known from the context. Since hastening is attributed to birds, it is the hastening of birds. In any case, the matter allows for both. If we return to the wording, sa'y means on foot. If we return to the meaning, sa'y means with the wing.
* The student: O Shaykh, who said that the wisdom (hikmah) meant here is the Sunnah?
* The Shaykh: No, that is not what is meant here. Compare ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom﴾ [an-Nisa' 113]. It is correct that wisdom there means the Sunnah, although the correct view is that what is meant by His saying ﴿Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom﴾ is something more general: wisdom is the sharia placed in its proper place, and the Sunnah is part of it. That is why He said ﴿and teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾ [Al 'Imran 164], meaning the secrets of the sharia.
* A student: O Shaykh, the judgment (hukm), the decree (qada') and the will (iradah) all have cosmic and legislative divisions. What is the difference between them?
* The Shaykh: The difference between them is like the difference between their meanings. Will (iradah) is other than judgment (hukm), because Allah wills and then judges, as He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah judges what He wills﴾ [al-Ma'idah 1]. Each thing has its own independent meaning according to its nature, but they are divided. Likewise, decree, judgment and writing are cosmic and legislative, and there are many other things.
* A student: Are verses not concluded with names and attributes that fit them?
* The Shaykh: Indeed.
* The student: The verse ends with the name al-'Aziz in the context of Ibrahim's question about the reviving of the dead. Does this point to the prohibition of such a question in the future?
* The Shaykh: No. This will come to us under the benefits. We will see, God willing.
* A student: O Shaykh, he says: "Ibrahim said". Does "Ibrahim" mean that he spoke with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as Musa did, by direct speech (taklim) or by revelation?
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: I mean: how did Allah speak to Ibrahim? Did He speak to him by revelation or directly, as He spoke to Musa?
* The Shaykh: No. The apparent meaning is that it was direct. But we have already told you before why Musa was specifically called the one who spoke with Allah (al-Kalim).
* The students: Because of the message.
* The Shaykh: Because he was addressed with the message from Allah, not by revelation. Otherwise, Allah spoke to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and He spoke to Musa and spoke to Adam.
* A student: O Shaykh, can someone now ask the question of Ibrahim: "My Lord, show me how..."?
* The Shaykh: If it is possible, then it is permissible. If it is not possible, then it becomes transgression in supplication (i'tida' fi al-du'a').
* The student: O Shaykh, we said that power (quwwah) is stronger than capability (qudrah) in the second verse?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is more complete than capability in the case of one described as having strength.
* The student: This applies to created beings, and we gave an example of it, O Shaykh. But regarding the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, are they two continuous attributes?
* The Shaykh: Yes. But we say: the opposite of capability is incapacity ('ajz), and the opposite of strength is weakness.
* The student: This is for created beings, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: It is also true of the Creator. That is why He said: ﴿Nothing in the heavens or on the earth can ever escape Allah, for He is ever Knowing and Competent﴾ [Fatir 44].
* The student: Yes. Is it not from the aspect of perfection, O Shaykh? And is this just a variety of expression in the verses?
* The Shaykh: No, no. Capability is opposed by incapacity, without doubt.
* A student: O Shaykh, regarding matters of creed that arise for believing people, do they arise for the prophets too?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, perhaps. This is according to the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Indeed, the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an is this verse"[[Tafsir al-Tabari (4/629).]]. Others said: the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ [az-Zumar 53]. Others said: the most hopeful verse is: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa' 48]. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: these whisperings that Satan casts into a person's heart, Allah forgives the person for them. That is why He said: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾ He said: ﴿Yes﴾. So this whispering that may come to a person is removed and does no harm. Some scholars also included in this His saying: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them﴾ [Yusuf 110].
* A student: Should we not include His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, Satan threw something into his wish﴾ [al-Hajj 52]?
* The Shaykh: No, no, that is not of this type, because that refers to Satan casting into his recitation (umniyyah).
* The student: Because Satan may cast into his wish?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not his wish, what he desires in his heart. The correct view is that umniyyah here means recitation, like His saying: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book except wishful recitations (amani)﴾ [al-Baqarah 78]. And Satan may hear on the tongue of the Prophet what Satan is pleased with and the Prophet is not pleased with.
* * *
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿He said: Yes, but so that my heart may be at rest﴾ [al-Baqarah 260].
* Also in it: permissibility of answering with only the particle that indicates the answer. From where is this derived?
* The students: From His saying: ﴿Yes (bala)﴾.
* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿bala﴾. Accordingly, if a man is asked: "Did you not divorce your wife?" and he says: "Yes (bala), I divorced her," or if he is asked: "Did you marry so-and-so?" and he says: "Yes," the contract is valid, because the particle of response suffices in place of mentioning the whole sentence.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: refutation of those who say that faith neither increases nor decreases, based on His saying: ﴿but so that my heart may be at rest﴾, for tranquility is an increase in faith and strength.
* Also among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, testing His servant with that by which his faith increases, based on His saying: ﴿Take four birds﴾ up to His saying: ﴿they will come to you running﴾.
* Also among its benefits: the perfection of Allah's power, as the reviving of the dead took place, meaning the reviving of these birds merely by Ibrahim's call. They came, so they came running.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: confirmation of two names of Allah, namely al-'Aziz and al-Hakim.
* And confirmation of what these two include of attributes: might ('izzah) and wisdom (hikmah). This is because every name of Allah includes an attribute, but not vice versa. That is, not every attribute gives rise to a name, but every name gives rise to an attribute. Why? Because the names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are both proper names and descriptive names, whereas human names may be proper names and descriptive names, but most of them are merely proper names.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that direct knowledge is not like direct observation, based on His saying: ﴿Show me how You give life to the dead﴾. The degrees of certainty are three: knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin), sight-based certainty ('ayn al-yaqin), and truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). Which is highest?
* The students: The truth of certainty.
* The Shaykh: The truth of certainty. This becomes clear through an example. If I tell you: "I have a sweet apple," that is knowledge of certainty. If I show it to you, it is sight-based certainty. If you eat it, that is truth of certainty, is it not? The disbelievers were promised the Fire. When they see it on the Day of Resurrection, that is sight-based certainty: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will think that they are about to fall into it﴾ [al-Kahf 53]. When they enter it, that is truth of certainty.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 261:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven ears﴾ [al-Baqarah 261].

﴿Mathal﴾ (likeness, example) is used to mean a resemblance, and it is also used to mean a description or attribute. If a counterpart is mentioned, the word means resemblance; otherwise it means attribute. In His saying, ﴿The likeness of the Garden which the righteous are promised: in it are rivers of water unchanging﴾ [Muhammad 15], the word ﴿mathal﴾ here means attribute. Why? Because no counterpart is mentioned. But if one says, "This is like that," it means resemblance. So His saying, ﴿Their likeness is like that of one who kindled a fire﴾ [al-Baqarah 17], and so on to the end, here ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain﴾ means resemblance. That is, the state of these people is like the state of this thing. Now let us consider: is there a correspondence between the one being compared and the thing compared to? No, because the one being compared is the doer, and the thing compared to is the deed. The grain does not correspond to the spender, but to what is spent. Is that not so?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: Who corresponds to the spender?

* Students: The sower of the grain.

* Shaykh: The sower of the grain. For this reason some scholars said: the verse contains an elision, either in the subject or in the predicate. Either one supposes: "The likeness of the deeds of those who spend their wealth is like the likeness of a grain," or one supposes: "The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like the likeness of a sower of a grain that grows seven ears." As for this noble verse, there is in reality an abbreviation, and it is an abbreviation for a benefit: this comparison encompasses both the doer and the deed. ﴿The likeness of those who﴾ and ﴿like a grain﴾. So there must be a deed and there must be a doer. The comparison includes both together, and this is from the eloquence of the Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who spend﴾. What is the meaning of spending (infaq)? It means giving. "Wealth" (amwal) is the plural of "mal" (property), which is everything a person possesses, whether material objects or benefits. Material objects are examples of what? 

* Students: Cars and dirhams.

* Shaykh: Like dirhams, dinars, cars, houses, and what is similar to these. And benefits, like a rented object, for the renter owns the benefit. The point is that wealth includes, and what does it include? Material objects and benefits. Everything a person owns, whether an object or a benefit, is wealth.

His saying: ﴿in the way of Allah﴾. "Sabil" (way) means a path. The way of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is His sharia (divine law), because it guides to Him and leads to Him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'am 153]. So "sabil" here means the sharia. It is attributed to Allah for two reasons. The first reason: He is the One who laid it down for His servants and legislated it for them. The second reason: it leads to Him. The word "sabil" is sometimes attributed to the one who travels it, as in "the way of the believers," as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ [an-Nisa' 115]. Is there a contradiction between these two?

* Students: No.

* Shaykh: No, because it is attributed to the believers in view of their being the ones who travelled it, and to Allah in view of His being the One who laid it down and the One who leads to it. Likewise, "sabil" is also attributed to those who travel it from among non-believers. Allah the Exalted said, concerning Musa to his brother Harun: ﴿And reform, and do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾ [al-A'raf 142]. He said to the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾ [al-Jathiyah 18]. And He said: ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾ [al-An'am 55], and other verses besides these. This is because "sabil" means a path, and it is attributed to each person according to his own condition.

﴿in the way of Allah﴾. I say: what is meant by this is: in the sharia of Allah, because the sharia of Allah is His way. The meaning of their spending in the sharia of Allah is that it be sincerity to Allah and following His sharia. So whoever intends by his spending something other than Allah is not in the way of Allah, like showing off (riya'). A man spends in jihad, or gives charity to the poor, but he spends so that it may be said: "So-and-so is generous," or "He is noble." This is not in the way of Allah. Is the field of work in the way of Allah or not?

* A student: In the way of Allah.

* Shaykh: That is, this man took money and went and gave it in charity to the poor, or went to those who gather for jihad and gave them. This field, meaning the place of work in the way of Allah, is it or not?

* Students: Yes, in the way of Allah.

* Shaykh: But this person's work is not in the way of Allah. Why? Because he is showing off; he did not intend the face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So he did not intend the way that leads to Allah, and he does not care whether Allah accepts it from him or does not accept it. What matters is that people say of him that he is a noble or generous man.

﴿in the way of Allah﴾ also requires that it be in accordance with the sharia of Allah. If someone spends in a manner with which Allah is not pleased, it is not in the way of Allah. Is that right? And if someone is sincere to Allah, such as a man who spends on innovations (bid'ah). A person says: "I want by this the face of Allah," but he spends on innovations. This is common, like building lodges (ribat) for the deviant Sufis, building houses for the celebration of Christian festivals, or printing books that contain innovations. A person may intend by this the face of Allah, but he is astray. Is it then in the way of Allah?

* Students: No.

* Shaykh: No, this is not in the way of Allah. So ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ requires two things:

First: that it be purely for Allah.

Second: that in it the sharia of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, be followed.

﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain.﴾ Here, what is meant by ﴿in the way of Allah﴾? Does it mean everything Allah has legislated, or does it mean fighting the enemies of Allah? The term "the way of Allah" is most often used for fighting the enemies of Allah, but it may also be used for what is broader and more general, as in this verse, and so it includes everything.

﴿like a grain that grows seven ears﴾. A grain that a person sows grows seven ears, so one becomes seven. ﴿In every ear is a hundred grains﴾, so the total is seven hundred. Therefore the reward of spending in the way of Allah is seven hundred.

Is this a limit?

* Students: No.

* Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾. Allah the Exalted may multiply more than that for whomever He wills. The phrase ﴿for whom He wills﴾: with respect to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, there is no bare will. Rather, the will of Allah is joined with wisdom. He multiplies for whomever He wills, from among those whose wisdom requires that it be multiplied for them. We have already covered the causes of the multiplication of deeds. We mentioned that their causes are how many?

* Students: Seven.

* Shaykh: Seven. Among the most important is sincerity. Can we recall them now? Can we recall the causes of the multiplication of deeds?

* A student: (...)

* Shaykh: That is one.

* A student: Consideration of intention... time.

* Shaykh: You said by intention?

* A student: We say, this is a matter...

* Shaykh: By consideration of time... by consideration of place.

* A student: By consideration of the deed.

* Shaykh: The deed itself, its genus or its type?

* The student: Its genus and its type.

* Shaykh: Its genus and its type, good.

* A student: Sincerity.

* Shaykh: Sincerity, intention.

* A student: By consideration of the state.

* Shaykh: The state.

* A student: By consideration of the manner.

* Shaykh: By consideration of the manner?

* The student: What does not enter into the type of the deed.

* Shaykh: What does not enter into the type of the deed?

First: what is the evidence for what you said, consideration of the doer? What is the evidence?

* The student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Well done, this is by consideration of the doer. Is there another piece of evidence for it?

* The student: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they both offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other﴾ [al-Ma'idah 27].

* Shaykh: No, that one is not (...).

* The student: ﴿from the righteous﴾?

* Shaykh: No.

* A student: He said: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾.

* Shaykh: No.

* A student: His saying (ﷺ): "A dirham surpassed a thousand dinars," or something with this meaning. [Recorded by an-Nasa'i (2527) from Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "A dirham surpassed a hundred thousand dirhams."]

* Shaykh: Yes, no, no, this is by consideration of the state.

* A student: The reward of steadfastness in the last times is that the one who is steadfast has the reward of fifty.

* Shaykh: Correct, steadfastness in the last times, the doer has the reward of fifty. [Recorded by Abu Dawud (4341) from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani.]

* A student: Fifty what?

* Shaykh: Fifty of the Companions.

* A student: The state, isn't it implied in what he said, the hadith...

* Shaykh: The state, as in the Prophet's saying: "Which charity is best?" He said: "The effort of one who has little." [Recorded by Abu Dawud (1449) and an-Nasa'i (2526) from Abdullah ibn Hubshi.] Good. What about time?

* A student: His saying (ﷺ): "Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins are forgiven." [Agreed upon. al-Bukhari (37), Muslim (759/173) from Abu Hurayrah.] And "Fasting the day of 'Arafah expiates two years: the past year and the coming year." [Recorded by Ahmad (22535) from Abu Qatadah, and it is in Muslim (1162/196) with the wording: "Fasting the day of 'Arafah, I hope from Allah that it expiates the year before it and the year after it."] And the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

* Shaykh: And what is the evidence for the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah?

* A student: There is a hadith.

* Shaykh: What is it?

* The student: The saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days." [Recorded by Abu Dawud (2438) from Ibn Abbas, and its origin is in al-Bukhari (969).]

* Shaykh: You have the place.

* The student: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except the Sacred Mosque." [Agreed upon. al-Bukhari (1190), Muslim (1394/505) from Abu Hurayrah.]

* Shaykh: Good, and who?

* A student: The deed. At the battle of Badr the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "He does not know, perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" [Agreed upon. al-Bukhari (3007), Muslim (2494/161) from Ali ibn Abi Talib.]

* Shaykh: And what else?

* A student: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have obligated upon him." [Recorded by al-Bukhari (6502) from Abu Hurayrah.]

* Shaykh: Correct. So obligatory acts are better than the genus of voluntary acts. The type? That it be by consideration of the type as well?

* A student: Like the obligatory acts and the last ten nights.

* Shaykh: Obligatory acts are a genus, and the obligatory acts themselves differ. Prayer is better than zakat, zakat is better than fasting, and the Asr prayer is better than other prayers.

* A student: Obligatory acts or sunnah acts?

* Shaykh: Yes indeed. And by consideration of the type? Why do we not say prayer is better than zakat?

* A student: Shaykh, this is in general.

* Another student: Prayer is a genus.

* Shaykh: Look now, the genus of obligatory acts is better than voluntary acts. This is a genus. A genus is that which has types beneath it. Did we not study this in the definition of genus?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: A genus is that which has types beneath it. Obligatory acts have types beneath them: prayer, zakat, fasting, hajj. Is that right?

* A student: Yes, prayer.

* Shaykh: Then prayer is better than zakat, and zakat is better than fasting. Is it clear? This is by consideration of the type.

* A student: The evidence?

* Shaykh: The evidence is that whoever abandons prayer is a disbeliever, and concerning zakat there are punishments reported that are not reported for fasting and hajj. What remains for us: do voluntary acts also differ, or do they not differ?

* A student: They differ.

* Shaykh: They differ. Some are more emphasized than others. This is by consideration of the type. And what remains for us? Five, here, do you see?

* A student: The manner of following.

* Shaykh: The state, the manner of the deed... the manner?

* The student: The one who performs prayer with humility is better than the one who performs it without humility.

* Shaykh: Yes. The more a person follows the Messenger (ﷺ) in his worship, the more complete it is. So a prayer with humility is better than a prayer without humility.

* A student: By consideration of intention.

* Shaykh: Yes, by consideration of intention. The difference by consideration of intention. And this last one should be the first, because it has a great and far-reaching effect.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾. Is this on its absolute footing, that He multiplies, glorified and exalted is He, merely by bare will?

* Students: No.

* Shaykh: No, rather He multiplies for whom He wills from among those whose wisdom requires that it be multiplied for them. This is because we have already given the principle: that whatever is linked to the will of Allah, what is meant by it is will joined with wisdom. We gave as evidence for this His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30].

He said: ﴿And Allah is Vast and Knowing﴾. ﴿Allah is Vast﴾, and from His vastness is the vastness of His bounty and His reward. ﴿Vast﴾ means in all His attributes. His knowledge is the broadest of knowledge, His mercy the broadest of mercy, His forbearance the broadest of forbearance, and His giving the broadest of giving. Measure everything else by this. All His attributes are vast, great and lofty attributes. And ﴿Knowing﴾ means possessing knowledge. Knowledge is the perception of a thing as it is, a firm perception that corresponds to what it is. Is that correct?

* Students: Yes, correct.

* Shaykh: It was asked: When was the battle of Badr? He said: In the fifth year. Are you certain? He said: I am certain, just as you are speaking to me now. We say: this is not knowledge; it is called compound ignorance (jahl murakkab). We asked him about the battle of Badr and he said: "I do not know." Is he knowing or not knowing?

* Students: Knowing... not knowing.

* Shaykh: The question is for one person.

* The student: He said "I do not know," and he said: "He does not know, he does not have knowledge."

* Shaykh: Yes, is he knowing or not knowing?

* The student: He is not knowing.

* Shaykh: Not knowing, correct. But this is called simple ignorance (jahl basit), meaning not compound.

We asked him about the battle of Badr and he said: "Either in the second year or in the third," and it is more likely in my view that it was in the second. Which of these is knowledge?

* Students: Conjecture (zann).

* Shaykh: Conjecture, because he did not affirm. The third is called?

* Students: Doubt (shakk).

* Shaykh: No, look: the second, because he said, "I think it was in the second year."

* Students: Conjecture.

* Shaykh: This is conjecture, or the third?

* Students: Wahm (illusion).

* Shaykh: Wahm. He said: "I do not know whether it was in the second year or the third." What is this?

* Students: Doubt.

* Shaykh: This is complete doubt? These are the types of perception. ﴿And Allah is Vast and Knowing﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 262:

He says: ﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and then do not follow what they have spent with reminders [of their generosity] or injury – theirs is their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [al-Baqarah 262].

In ﴿Those who spend their wealth﴾, the phrase "alladhina" (those who) is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is the clause ﴿theirs is their reward with their Lord﴾. Allah, mighty and majestic, says this after He had mentioned, in what preceded, sincerity (ikhlas), which comes before the spending, and following the Sunnah (mutaba'ah), which also precedes the spending. Here He mentions ﴿those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah﴾, and then mentions what nullifies their spending. That is because spending has prior conditions (shurut sabiqah) and subsequent nullifiers (mubtilat lahiqah). The prior conditions are sincerity and following the Sunnah, that it be in the way of Allah. The subsequent conditions are that it is not followed by reminders of kindness (mann) and injury (adha). That is, a person may spend his wealth in the way of Allah in accordance with the Shari'ah, but this spending may be followed by reminders or injury toward those who receive it. So after that He said: ﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and then do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury﴾. As for the first part, ﴿those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah﴾, the discussion of it has already passed.

(Thumma) means: after the spending. He used (thumma), which indicates sequence and delay, meaning: then they do not follow it, even after a period of time. ﴿What they have spent with reminders or injury﴾. "Mann" (reminder of kindness) is that the giver makes the recipient feel that he has a favor over him, such as displaying himself as superior to him, as if, when he sees him, he says with his eyes, though not with his mouth: "Remember what I gave you." Is this possible or not?

* Students: It is possible.

* The Shaykh: It is possible. That is, you can sense from his features that he is saying: "Remember what I gave you." This is considered… If he makes this known to people, it is injury (adha), such as saying in front of people: "Look at this man, I gave him and gave him, I clothed him, built him a house, furnished the house for him, and brought him provisions, and yet to me he is just one of the people." What is this, then?

* Students: Injury.

* The Shaykh: It is injury. So the one who reminds the recipient of his favor, or harms him by words that indicate his favor over him, this nullifies his reward for that reason. The one who does not follow what he has spent with reminders or injury has his full reward. Therefore He said: ﴿theirs is their reward with their Lord﴾. Ajr (reward) is what a worker receives in return for his work, and from it comes the wage of a hired worker. Allah, glorified and exalted, called this reward "ajr" because He, mighty and majestic, guaranteed to the worker that He would recompense him for this work, so it became like the wage of the hired worker. Allah, exalted, also called the reward "qard" (loan), which is more eloquent in generosity: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [al-Baqarah 245]. As if the deed you did for Allah were a loan you lent to Allah. The point of resemblance between them is that in each there is a binding obligation to what? To fulfilment. So Allah called it a loan.

He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿theirs is their reward with their Lord﴾, meaning it is stored up with Him. This stored reward is a certain matter. Does the one who spends and does not follow his spending with reminders or injury have an advance reward? The answer is yes, as indicated by His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it﴾ [Saba' 39], meaning He will bring its replacement and substitute. So it is now clear that the person who spends in the way of Allah and does not follow his spending with reminders or injury has a reward stored with Allah, where a good deed is seven hundred, and he has immediate reward: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾.

* A student: Shaykh, for example, he mentions that he did it, but the one he gave to does not know about it. For example, he says: "I gave you," or "I did," in his absence?

* The Shaykh: Even this contains injury.

* The student: But this is not…?

* The Shaykh: No, this is injury, because those who know of it may mention it one day, and perhaps also the esteem of that recipient may decline in their eyes.

* A student: I say: if he does not intend a specific person and says: "I gave such-and-such"?

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no harm in that, but in this one fears showing off (riya') or self-admiration (i'jab).

* A student: Shaykh, what is obligatory upon the one who was given to, if he, for example, feels the reminder – should he return it to the giver, or…?

* The Shaykh: This does not bring benefits, but his question is important. He asks: if the recipient feels that the giver has reminded him or perhaps harmed him, is it better that he remain willing to receive, or that he return it?

* A student: He returns it.

* The Shaykh: He returns it, like that? Fine. If he returns it, is the giver obliged to accept it or not?

* A student: He is not obliged.

* The Shaykh: He is not obliged, because he has already owned it. The recipient now owns it, so its return to the giver means a renewed ownership, and he is not obliged to accept it. But he may say: either accept it, or restrain your tongue from speech and injury.

* The student: Shaykh, there is the hadith: "Every deed of the son of Adam is his, the good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundredfold"[[Recorded by Muslim (1151/164) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], and it specified the recompense up to seven hundred, while in this verse the recompense is not specified?

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no contradiction. Either it is said: this is specific to charity and spending, because a person is stingy with spending, as Allah the Exalted said describing him: ﴿And indeed he is intense in his love of wealth﴾ [al-'Adiyat 8], and He said: ﴿You love wealth with immense love﴾ [al-Fajr 20], and many people find deeds easy except spending. Or it is said: limiting it to seven hundred in the hadith does not preclude an increase, because Allah said: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾. So seven hundred is the reward that is definite, and whatever exceeds it is by Allah's grace.

* A student: The hadith has an addition: "And He multiplies it seven hundredfold to many multiples"[[Agreed upon. Al-Bukhari (6491), and Muslim (131/207) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]?

* The Shaykh: No, this is not in this hadith.

* The student: The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: "Indeed Allah wrote the good deeds and the bad deeds"[[The previous hadith.]].

* The Shaykh: No, that is not in this one; that is the hadith about fasting.

* The student: Shaykh, the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Do not revile my Companions, for if one of you spent gold equal to Uhud…"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3673), and Muslim (2541/222) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] to the end of the hadith. How do we reconcile this hadith with the saying of the Prophet ﷺ regarding patience in the last times, that one of them does not reach the like of fifty Companions? Here he says: "What one of them gives, not even a mudd or half of it…"?

* The Shaykh: Yes, the reconciliation between them has already passed. Do you remember it?

* The student: This is considering the origin of the deed.

* The Shaykh: Which of them?

* The student: The first hadith.

* The Shaykh: Which is it? Regarding the Companions or regarding patience?

* The student: No, regarding the Companions (...) this means his deed is one of the Companions. The second aspect: it does not prevent that he is one of the Successors, may be from the followers of some Companions, meaning from the origin of the origin.

* The Shaykh: No, that is not it.

* A student: The deed of some Companions may be more excellent than that of a Companion, but the Companion is preferred over him by companionship; companionship is above (...)

* Another student: For example, if this patient one reaches the deed of the Companions at that time, his reward is like the reward of fifty Companions. But if he does not reach the deed of the Companion, then he, in effect, does not reach it.

* The Shaykh: I did not understand; explain this statement to me.

* The student: That is, for example, if the patient one acts like the deed of a Companion.

* The Shaykh: That is, for example, he prays an obligatory prayer?

* The student: No, I mean deeds. Not only the obligatory prayer, but all their deeds, because the Companions' deeds were many.

* The Shaykh: Let it be in charity: a Companion gives a mudd and a patient one gives a mudd; how do we say?

* The student: For example, the sincerity of the Companion is not like… what is in the hearts is not what is in the hearts of the Companions.

* Another student: The first state: considering the era of the Companions, they are more excellent considering the worker, but at the end of time, considering the reward of the worker, it is greater, since he encountered from hardship what they did not encounter?

* The Shaykh: This means that the deeds of the Companions are more excellent than those after them without doubt, but this one has the reward of fifty because of the hardship and difficulty of the work. Like the one who was correct regarding the Sunnah in tayammum when he did not repeat the prayer, and the Prophet said to him: "You have acted in accordance with the Sunnah," and to the second he said: "You have two rewards"[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (338) and al-Nasa'i (433) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]]. Do we now say that this one is better than that one?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: No. It is said: none can approach the Companions in the excellence of deeds because of companionship, but this one is more excellent because of the struggle and constraint.

* A student: What is the difference between wasi' (Wide/All-Encompassing) and kabir (Great)?

* The Shaykh: The difference between them is that wasi' comes from sa'ah (breadth), which means reaching the utmost extent of a thing, whereas kabir returns to the essence and attribute, namely greatness (kibriya') only. So the object of wasi' is more comprehensive and general, since it includes all attributes, whereas kabir is specific to the attribute of greatness. Likewise, it refers to the greatness of the essence of Allah, mighty and majestic, for He is greater than everything.

* A student: Do we not say "wasi' in His essence"?

* The Shaykh: By Allah, I fear that someone may imagine from it that things are indwelling in Him, as in His saying: ﴿His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah 255], for the Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth. Therefore I avoid saying it like that; say "wasi' in His attributes."

* A student: Shaykh, there is a reading in it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is a reading in it: ﴿yudá'ifu﴾ (with doubled 'ayn).

* * *
* A student: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing (261). Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and then do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury – theirs is their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve (262). Kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, and Allah is Free of need, Forbearing (263). O you who have believed, do not nullify your charities with reminders and injury like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like a smooth rock with a little dust on it; a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything they have earned, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people (264)﴾ [al-Baqarah 261–264].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes﴾.

﴿theirs is their reward with their Lord﴾. Ajr is the reward, as we said earlier, and it is called ajr because Allah, glorified and exalted, undertook it for the worker in the way an employer undertakes the wage for his hired worker. This is from the utmost of Allah's grace, that He makes the reward for the workers like the wage owed by employers, just as Allah the Exalted called that a loan in His saying: ﴿If you lend Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you﴾ [al-Taghabun 17]. The point of resemblance to a loan is clear: each of them carries an obligation of fulfilment. So it is as if Allah, mighty and majestic, in His generosity and kindness, made the giving and spending for His sake like a loan whose repayment is binding on the borrower.

And His saying: ﴿theirs is their reward with their Lord﴾. The basic meaning of "indiyyah" (being with) is locational, but it may be used in a broader sense that includes location or obligation, as you say: "I have for so-and-so such-and-such," meaning: in my covenant and in my liability to him is such-and-such, even if it is not there in its place. So "indiyyah" may be used to mean location, and it may be used to mean what a person is bound to in his liability and covenant. Here ﴿with their Lord﴾ allows two meanings, and both are correct: it may mean that it is with Allah, the Exalted, as an obligation that He must fulfil; and it may mean another sense: that this reward is in the Garden whose ceiling is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and this is locational "with". It does not contradict what preceded regarding "with" as covenant and obligation to fulfil.

He said: ﴿And no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. No fear concerning them about what is to come, nor will they grieve over what has passed. Grief is distress or sorrow over what has already occurred, while fear and worry are about what will occur. So if these people do not grieve over what is lost and do not fear the future, their bliss is complete, because bliss is marred by regret or grief over what has passed when the bliss is entirely lost or when its completeness is lost. If it is entirely lost, a person wishes he had worked for this bliss; if its completeness is lost, he wishes that he had completed and perfected it. But these people never grieve, even if they are in dwellings below the lofty dwellings, because each one of the people of the Garden sees that no one is more blessed than he is. For if he were to see someone more blessed than himself, he would grieve, and he would see himself as not having complete bliss, whereas the people of the Garden do not see themselves except in complete bliss. In contrast, the people of the Fire – may Allah protect us – each one of them sees that no one is more severely punished than he is, so that he may not find solace in others. For when a person sees that others are punished, even with a punishment like his, he takes comfort in them and the matter becomes easier for him. But if he sees that no one can be like him, the punishment becomes more severe for him – may Allah protect us – from the psychological side.

So what is intended by this negation? It is intended to affirm the completeness of their bliss: they do not grieve over what is lost, nor are they concerned about the future, because one who grieves over what is lost undoubtedly sees his bliss diminish and not be complete, and you will find that Satan constantly opens for him the thought "if only I had done such-and-such, it would have been such-and-such." The fearful one also does not have complete bliss, because he does not know what his future will hold, so you find him estimating, looking and thinking, and not enjoying bliss. Thus the negation here is meant to establish the completeness of bliss.

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury.﴾

﴿A kind word﴾ is the mubtada' (the inchoative, i.e. the subject of the nominal sentence), and ﴿better﴾ is its khabar (the predicate). The use of an indefinite noun (nakirah) as a mubtada' is permitted here because it is qualified by a description. If you prefer, you may say instead that it is permitted because it conveys a complete meaning (ifadah), and the means by which it conveys that meaning is the description. Explaining it by the fact that it conveys a complete meaning is better, because this is what the grammarians have said. The evidence for this is the verse of Ibn Malik:

*It is not permitted to begin with an indefinite noun
unless it conveys a complete meaning, as in "near Zayd is a Namirah (a she-wolf)."*

*"Is there a young man among you? So a friend for us,
and a man of the noble ones with us."*

*"Desire for good is good, and a deed of righteousness
that adorns; let it be measured by what is not said."*

What example applies to this verse among these examples?

* The students: "And a man of the noble ones with us."

* The Shaykh: "And a man of the noble ones with us."

﴿A kind word﴾: the kind word (al-qawl al-ma'ruf) is that which the tongue utters and which is known (ma'ruf) in the Shari'ah and known in custom (al-'urf). This is because a word may be known in the Shari'ah without being known in custom, and it may be known in custom without being known in the Shari'ah. For example, if it were the custom of these people to speak with insults, abuse and the like, and they regarded this as something harmless, as some people habitually say: "Come here, you accursed one! Come here, you doer, you abandoner! O son of adultery, we seek refuge in Allah," and the like, and among them there are people who have become accustomed to this speech, and this evil has become known to them, then this does not fall within this verse, because...

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification that intelligible meanings are fixed through perceptible matters. The way this works is that Allah the Exalted has struck a parable for meanings through this story, or through this image that no one would wish for.

* And among its benefits: the correspondence between the showy person (al-mura'i) and the condition of this man. When the showy person spends his wealth, praise and commendation from people appear to him, so he grows and swells in his own self, and he thinks he has obtained what he wants. But when the Day of Resurrection comes, the time when he needs this, he finds no reward for what he did. Thus that deed, the deed mixed with showing off, is like the whirlwind that struck that garden.

* And among the benefits of the verse: the permissibility of coining a parable through a verbal account.

So is it permissible to coin a parable through a practical account, which is what is called tamthil (enactment)?

The answer: Yes, it is permissible, but on condition that it does not include anything forbidden. We will give examples of forbidden things in enactment. First: that it does not involve a man playing the role of a woman, or a woman playing the role of a man; a man should not portray a woman or the reverse. Why? Because the Prophet ﷺ cursed "the men who imitate women and the women who imitate men."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5885) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

Second: that it does not involve belittling those of virtue among the Companions and the imams of the Ummah, because belittling and despising them is forbidden. Enacting them lowers their standing, especially when it is known of the performer that he is a sinner, because usually, if he is a sinner and takes on the persona of that pious man who has his worth and virtue in the Ummah, this lowers the standing of the one who plays his role in the drama.

Third: that it does not involve imitating the voices of animals, such as playing the role of a dog or a donkey, because Allah has only made comparison with animals in a context of blame: ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like the likeness of a donkey﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 5].

﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our verses, but he detached himself from them, so Satan followed him and he became of the misguided. And had We willed, We would have raised him by them, but he inclined toward the earth and followed his desire. So his likeness is like the likeness of a dog: if you attack him he pants, or if you leave him he pants﴾ [al-A'raf 175–176], to the end. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "The one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2589) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

Fourth: that the enactment does not involve playing the role of a disbeliever or a sinner. That is, none of those performing the roles of this drama should play the part of a disbeliever or a sinner. Why?

* The students: (...).

* The Shaykh: Because it is feared that this would affect his heart, that he might one day recall that he played the role of a disbeliever, and so it affects his heart and Satan enters upon him from this direction. But if he does it, would he become a disbeliever?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, he does not become a disbeliever, because this man does not attribute disbelief (...) he portrays himself as a man who divorced his wife. If he has a wife, will the wife be divorced or not?

* The students: She is not divorced.

* The Shaykh: The wife is not divorced.

* A student: Why is the wife not divorced?

* The Shaykh: Because he does not attribute the divorce to himself, just as the one who played the role of a disbeliever does not attribute disbelief to himself; he attributes it to another. Some people have thought that if he plays the role of a disbeliever, he becomes a disbeliever and leaves Islam, and it becomes obligatory for him to renew his Islam. They cited the Qur'an and the words of the scholars.

As for the Qur'an, they cited the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only engaged in conversation and play." Say, "Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief"﴾ [al-Tawbah 65–66]. He said: ﴿Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.﴾

And as for the words of the scholars: whoever utters a word of disbelief, even in jest, becomes a disbeliever. They said: this man is joking, not serious. We say to them: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Three things, whether serious or in jest, are serious: marriage, divorce, and reconciliation."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2194) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]] So if a man says to his wife, "You are divorced," jesting with her, she is divorced. Do you say that if the actor plays the role of a man who divorced his wife, you would say that his wife is divorced? They will say: No, and everyone says: No. The difference is clear, because the one who jokes attributes the act to himself, while the actor attributes it to another. For this reason his wife is not divorced if he plays the role of one who divorces, and he does not become a disbeliever if he plays the role of a disbeliever. But I think it is impermissible from another standpoint, which is that perhaps his heart will be affected in the future when he recalls that he once played the role of a disbeliever. Can we bring evidence that illustrates the matter of a practical account?

* A student: Yes (...).

* The Shaykh: What is it?

* A student: "The Messenger ﷺ was one day with the Companions, and he drew a straight line and drew lines to its right and left."[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11109) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]?

* The Shaykh: Did you hear his words?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: He mentioned the lines that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, drew. He drew lines representing the human being, his hope and his term, and likewise he drew a line for the straight path of Allah and for the paths (al-subul). But this may be open to consideration.

* A student: The story of the leper, the bald man and the blind man, when the angel came to one of them in the form of a poor man, embodied.[[A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayhi): al-Bukhari (3464) and Muslim (2964) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. The angel came to the leper, the bald man and the blind man and asked them what they wanted. Each one mentioned his wish, and Allah gave them their wishes. Then the angel returned to them again: he came to the leper in his form and appearance, a leper and poor, and said to him: "I am a poor man and a wayfarer whose ropes have been cut off on my journey, so there is no means for me today except through Allah and then through you." Now the angel is enacting the role of a poor man, while he is not poor; he is an angel who needs neither food nor drink. The same applies to the bald man and the blind man. Some scholars have used this hadith and said: lying is false, and Allah the Exalted would not allow one of His angels to do something false. Rather, this was brought to clarify the image: instead of being related by speech, it was related by action. There is no doubt that striking parables by speech is abundant in the Qur'an: ﴿Allah strikes a parable: a slave owned, who has no power over anything﴾ [al-Nahl 75].

﴿Allah strikes a parable: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison?﴾ [al-Zumar 29], to the end.

The point is this: if the enactment does not include anything forbidden, from the examples we mentioned or others, then there is no harm in it, and it is not lying in any way, because lying is when a person attributes the matter to himself. For example, someone comes to you and knocks at the door, you say, "Who is it?" and he says, "I am Zayd," but he is not Zayd. That is clear lying. But if a person says, "I am playing the role of so-and-so," and people know that he is not so-and-so, then he has not lied. However, if he attributes a saying to a specific person, this requires that the saying be established as coming from that specific person. But if he relates the story of a man by describing him without naming him, there is no lie in it.

In this noble verse, among the benefits: that Allah the Exalted clarifies His verses to His servants. Are these the legislative verses (shar'iyyah) or the cosmic verses (kawniyyah)?

* The students: Both.

* The Shaykh: Both. The cosmic verses and the legislative verses are both made clear, or all of them are made clear in the Book of Allah the Exalted, in the most complete clarity.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the encouragement to reflect (tafakkur), and that it is an intended goal, due to His saying: ﴿So that you may reflect﴾. A person is commanded to reflect, because reflection leads to good outcomes. But this applies to what can be reached through reflection. He says: this applies to what can be what? Reached through reflecting upon it. As for what cannot be reached through reflection, then reflecting upon it is a waste of time and may lead to something prohibited, such as reflecting on how the attributes of Allah, mighty and majestic, are. That is not permitted, because you will not reach a conclusion. For this reason it has come in a report: "Reflect upon the signs of Allah, but do not reflect upon the Essence of Allah,"[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (618) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] because this is a matter that cannot be reached, and an end that cannot be encompassed: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision﴾ [al-An'am 103]. So if someone says: "Let me reflect on how Allah istawa (established Himself) over the Throne, and what is the color of His establishment over the Throne?" We say: Is this something required or not?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, this is not required. Rather, it is obligatory to refrain from it, because it will lead to a bad outcome: either to giving it a modality (takyif), or to likening (tamthil), or to negation (ta'til), and it is inevitable.

Is reflecting on the meanings of the names and attributes of Allah required or not?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is required, because the meaning, as Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said when he was asked: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha 5]: "How did He establish Himself?" He said: "The establishment is not unknown, the modality is not conceivable, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation."[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-I'tiqad (54).]]

Can we derive from the generality of His saying ﴿So that you may reflect﴾ that it includes reflection on cosmic matters, such as a person reflecting on how to reach the manufacture of weapons with which he defends Islam, and reaching the manufacture of aircraft with which people are carried, and the like? Yes, is that possible?

* A student: Yes, it is possible.

* The Shaykh: Can we say that it includes reflection on the layers of the earth and what may be extracted from these layers of flowing and solid minerals?

* A student: Yes, it is possible, O Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: It is possible. Therefore it is general.

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury.﴾

Enacting them lowers their standing, especially when it is known of the performer that he is a sinner, because usually, if he is a sinner and takes on the persona of that pious man who has his worth and virtue in the Ummah, this lowers the standing of the one who plays his role in the drama.

Third: that it does not involve imitating the voices of animals, such as playing the role of a dog or a donkey, because Allah has only made comparison with animals in a context of blame: ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like the likeness of a donkey﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 5].

﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our verses, but he detached himself from them, so Satan followed him and he became of the misguided. And had We willed, We would have raised him by them, but he inclined toward the earth and followed his desire. So his likeness is like the likeness of a dog: if you attack him he pants, or if you leave him he pants﴾ [al-A'raf 175–176], to the end. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "The one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2589) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

Fourth: that the enactment does not involve playing the role of a disbeliever or a sinner. That is, none of those performing the roles of this drama should play the part of a disbeliever or a sinner. Why?

* The students: (...).

* The Shaykh: Because it is feared that this would affect his heart, that he might one day recall that he played the role of a disbeliever, and so it affects his heart and Satan enters upon him from this direction. But if he does it, would he become a disbeliever?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, he does not become a disbeliever, because this man does not attribute disbelief (...) he portrays himself as a man who divorced his wife. If he has a wife, will the wife be divorced or not?

* The students: She is not divorced.

* The Shaykh: The wife is not divorced.

* A student: Why is the wife not divorced?

* The Shaykh: Because he does not attribute the divorce to himself, just as the one who played the role of a disbeliever does not attribute disbelief to himself; he attributes it to another. Some people have thought that if he plays the role of a disbeliever, he becomes a disbeliever and leaves Islam, and it becomes obligatory for him to renew his Islam. Say, "Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief"﴾ [al-Tawbah 65–66]. He said: ﴿Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.﴾

They will say: No, and everyone says: No. The difference is clear, because the one who jokes attributes the act to himself, while the actor attributes it to another. But I think it is impermissible from another standpoint, which is that perhaps his heart will be affected in the future when he recalls that he once played the role of a disbeliever. Can we bring evidence that illustrates the matter of a practical account?

* A student: Yes (...).

* The Shaykh: What is it?

* A student: "The Messenger ﷺ was one day with the Companions, and he drew a straight line and drew lines to its right and left."[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11109) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]?

* The Shaykh: Did you hear his words?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: He mentioned the lines that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, drew. He drew lines representing the human being, his hope and his term, and likewise he drew a line for the straight path of Allah and for the paths (al-subul). But this may be open to consideration.

* A student: The story of the leper, the bald man and the blind man, when the angel came to one of them in the form of a poor man, embodied.[[A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayhi): al-Bukhari (3464) and Muslim (2964) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. The angel came to the leper, the bald man and the blind man and asked them what they wanted. Each one mentioned his wish, and Allah gave them their wishes. Then the angel returned to them again: he came to the leper in his form and appearance, a leper and poor, and said to him: "I am a poor man and a wayfarer whose ropes have been cut off on my journey, so there is no means for me today except through Allah and then through you." Now the angel is enacting the role of a poor man, while he is not poor; he is an angel who needs neither food nor drink. The same applies to the bald man and the blind man. Some scholars have used this hadith and said: lying is false, and Allah the Exalted would not allow one of His angels to do something false. Rather, this was brought to clarify the image: instead of being related by speech, it was related by action. There is no doubt that striking parables by speech is abundant in the Qur'an: ﴿Allah strikes a parable: a slave owned, who has no power over anything﴾ [al-Nahl 75].

﴿Allah strikes a parable: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison?﴾ [al-Zumar 29], to the end.

The point is this: if the enactment does not include anything forbidden, from the examples we mentioned or others, then there is no harm in it, and it is not lying in any way, because lying is when a person attributes the matter to himself. For example, someone comes to you and knocks at the door, you say, "Who is it?" and he says, "I am Zayd," but he is not Zayd. That is clear lying. However, if he attributes a saying to a specific person, this requires that the saying be established as coming from that specific person. But if he relates the story of a man by describing him without naming him, there is no lie in it.

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, this is not required. Rather, it is obligatory to refrain from it, because it will lead to a bad outcome: either to giving it a modality (takyif), or to likening (tamthil), or to negation (ta'til), and it is inevitable.

* A student: Yes, it is possible.

* The Shaykh: Can we say that it includes reflection on the layers of the earth and what may be extracted from these layers of flowing and solid minerals?

* A student: Yes, it is possible, O Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: It is possible. Therefore it is general.

We say to them: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Three things, whether serious or in jest, are serious: marriage, divorce, and reconciliation."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2194) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]] So if a man says to his wife, "You are divorced," jesting with her, she is divorced. Do you say that if the actor plays the role of a man who divorced his wife, you would say that his wife is divorced? They will say: No, and everyone says: No. The difference is clear, because the one who jokes attributes the act to himself, while the actor attributes it to another. For this reason his wife is not divorced if he plays the role of one who divorces, and he does not become a disbeliever if he plays the role of a disbeliever. But I think it is impermissible from another standpoint, which is that perhaps his heart will be affected in the future when he recalls that he once played the role of a disbeliever. Can we bring evidence that illustrates the matter of a practical account?

* A student: Yes (...).

* The Shaykh: What is it?

* A student: "The Messenger ﷺ was one day with the Companions, and he drew a straight line and drew lines to its right and left."[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11109) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]?

* The Shaykh: Did you hear his words?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: He mentioned the lines that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, drew. He drew lines representing the human being, his hope and his term, and likewise he drew a line for the straight path of Allah and for the paths (al-subul). But this may be open to consideration.

* A student: The story of the leper, the bald man and the blind man, when the angel came to one of them in the form of a poor man, embodied.[[A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayhi): al-Bukhari (3464) and Muslim (2964) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. The angel came to the leper, the bald man and the blind man and asked them what they wanted. Each one mentioned his wish, and Allah gave them their wishes. Then the angel returned to them again: he came to the leper in his form and appearance, a leper and poor, and said to him: "I am a poor man and a wayfarer whose ropes have been cut off on my journey, so there is no means for me today except through Allah and then through you." Now the angel is enacting the role of a poor man, while he is not poor; he is an angel who needs neither food nor drink. The same applies to the bald man and the blind man. Some scholars have used this hadith and said: lying is false, and Allah the Exalted would not allow one of His angels to do something false. Rather, this was brought to clarify the image: instead of being related by speech, it was related by action. There is no doubt that striking parables by speech is abundant in the Qur'an: ﴿Allah strikes a parable: a slave owned, who has no power over anything﴾ [al-Nahl 75].

﴿Allah strikes a parable: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison?﴾ [al-Zumar 29], to the end.

The point is this: if the enactment does not include anything forbidden, from the examples we mentioned or others, then there is no harm in it, and it is not lying in any way, because lying is when a person attributes the matter to himself. For example, someone comes to you and knocks at the door, you say, "Who is it?" and he says, "I am Zayd," but he is not Zayd. That is clear lying. But if a person says, "I am playing the role of so-and-so," and people know that he is not so-and-so, then he has not lied. However, if he attributes a saying to a specific person, this requires that the saying be established as coming from that specific person. But if he relates the story of a man by describing him without naming him, there is no lie in it.

In this noble verse, among the benefits: that Allah the Exalted clarifies His verses to His servants. Are these the legislative verses (shar'iyyah) or the cosmic verses (kawniyyah)?

* The students: Both.

* The Shaykh: Both. The cosmic verses and the legislative verses are both made clear, or all of them are made clear in the Book of Allah the Exalted, in the most complete clarity.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the encouragement to reflect (tafakkur), and that it is an intended goal, due to His saying: ﴿So that you may reflect﴾. A person is commanded to reflect, because reflection leads to good outcomes. But this applies to what can be reached through reflection. He says: this applies to what can be what? Reached through reflecting upon it. As for what cannot be reached through reflection, then reflecting upon it is a waste of time and may lead to something prohibited, such as reflecting on how the attributes of Allah, mighty and majestic, are. That is not permitted, because you will not reach a conclusion. For this reason it has come in a report: "Reflect upon the signs of Allah, but do not reflect upon the Essence of Allah,"[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (618) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] because this is a matter that cannot be reached, and an end that cannot be encompassed: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision﴾ [al-An'am 103]. So if someone says: "Let me reflect on how Allah istawa (established Himself) over the Throne, and what is the color of His establishment over the Throne?" We say: Is this something required or not?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, this is not required. Rather, it is obligatory to refrain from it, because it will lead to a bad outcome: either to giving it a modality (takyif), or to likening (tamthil), or to negation (ta'til), and it is inevitable.

Is reflecting on the meanings of the names and attributes of Allah required or not?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is required, because the meaning, as Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said when he was asked: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha 5]: "How did He establish Himself?" He said: "The establishment is not unknown, the modality is not conceivable, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation."[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-I'tiqad (54).]]

Can we derive from the generality of His saying ﴿So that you may reflect﴾ that it includes reflection on cosmic matters, such as a person reflecting on how to reach the manufacture of weapons with which he defends Islam, and reaching the manufacture of aircraft with which people are carried, and the like? Yes, is that possible?

* A student: Yes, it is possible.

* The Shaykh: Can we say that it includes reflection on the layers of the earth and what may be extracted from these layers of flowing and solid minerals?

* A student: Yes, it is possible, O Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: It is possible. Therefore it is general.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 267 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have produced for you from the earth﴾ [Al-Baqarah 267]. His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. We have mentioned many times and repeatedly that opening an address with the call (nida') indicates what? It indicates its importance and the attention given to it, because the call includes alerting, and alerting to something is evidence of concern for it. Opening it with ﴿O you who have believed﴾ with this description conveys several benefits:

The first: Ighra' (encouragement and enticement), meaning urging the acceptance of what one is addressed with. For this reason Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "When Allah the Exalted says, 'O you who have believed,' then lend it your hearing, for it is either good that you are commanded to do, or evil that you are forbidden from."[[Recorded by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Tafsir (50) with the wording: "Then lend it your ear, for it is good that you are commanded to, or evil that you are turned away from."]] For this reason, if I call you by your description and say: "O man, O clever one, O generous one," it means: O one who is described by this, let the effects of this thing be apparent upon you. So the first benefit is ighra'.

The second benefit: that complying with what one is commanded is among the requirements of faith, as if He said: O you who have believed, your faith calls you to such and such.

The third thing: that opposing it is a deficiency in faith, because if one truly realized this description, he would carry out what he was commanded.

﴿O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned﴾. After Allah mentioned earlier the virtue of spending seeking His Face, and the bad outcome for one who reminds of his charity or spends for show, He urged spending. But the difference between what is here and what came before is that what is here explains what one spends from, while there it explains to whom one spends. Do you understand? Here it explains what one spends from: from where do we spend? He said: ﴿spend from the good things you have earned﴾.
