For this reason he is the one who caused it, and the one who pointed to this forbidden deed, so he has earned it.

Some scholars used this verse to show that acts of worship do not reach the dead, as they also cited His saying: ﴿and that there is not for man except what he strove﴾ [al-Najm 39]. Is this inference sound? We say: yes, it is sound in their view, because God attributed the deed to its doer: ﴿for it is what it has earned﴾, and the acts of worship performed by another, the one who earned them is the other. So if a person prays and says: "O God, I pray on behalf of so-and-so, so grant its reward to him," they say: this does not benefit so-and-so, it does not benefit him. If he gives charity and says: "O God, if this charity of mine is for so-and-so, grant its reward to him," they say: it does not benefit, except for what the text has provided, because God says: ﴿for it is what it has earned﴾ and ﴿and that there is not for man except what he strove﴾.

But the correct view is otherwise: that when a person intends by a righteous deed that it be for another, that other benefits from it. We have evidence for this, among it: the hadith of Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, may Allah be pleased with him, "that he had a garden (mikhraf, i.e., an orchard), and he wished to give it in charity on behalf of his mother, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ about that. He said: 'Yes,' and permitted him to do so." [Related by Abu Dawud, no. 2882, and al-Tirmidhi, no. 669.]

Among it also: "that a man came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: O Messenger of God, my mother died suddenly, and I think that if she had spoken she would have given charity; shall I give charity on her behalf? He said: 'Yes.'" [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari, no. 1388, and Muslim, no. 1004 (51), from Aisha.]

Among it: the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "Whoever dies owing fasting, his guardian shall fast on his behalf." [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari, no. 1952, and Muslim, no. 1147 (153), from Aisha.]

Among it: "that a woman asked the Prophet ﷺ about her father, upon whom God's obligation had fallen, and he was unable to ride on a mount, and she asked his permission to perform Hajj on his behalf, and he permitted her." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari, no. 1513, and Muslim, no. 1334 (407), from Ibn Abbas.] The examples of this are many.

**Commentary of Ibn ʿUthaymin (Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-Karīm) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 285–286 (part 6 of 7)**

If they say: "We confine ourselves to what the text has stated, and we do not include what it has not stated," the answer is: these are specific cases (*qadāyā aʿyān*), and specific cases do not prevent their rulings from being extended to others by analogy (*qiyās*). For example, if a questioner had come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I recite some Qurʾān, or pray two rakʿahs, and dedicate it to my mother?" we would not know whether he would say no or not. Yet the evidence requires that he would say yes, because all of these are righteous deeds. There is no difference between charity, fasting, Hajj, recitation of the Qurʾān, and prayer. If they say, "Charity is a financial act, or a financial act of worship from which others benefit," we reply: Is Hajj a financial act of worship or a physical one? It is physical. Fasting is a physical act of worship, and yet the Lawgiver permitted it. The distinction between the physical and the financial has no evidence supporting it at all. In that case we say: if a person intends that the reward of a righteous deed be for someone, then he may do so, and it reaches that person and benefits him.

If someone asks: "If you say that, is it then legislated for us to dedicate the reward of what we have done to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" For example, what appears in some copies of the Qurʾān at the end of the book, a supplication for completing the Qurʾān: "O Allah, make the reward of what we have recited and read, and such and such, for the spirit of our master Muhammad (ﷺ), and for the spirits of the family of our master Muhammad, and for such and such." Is it legislated for us to say that a person should dedicate acts of devotion to the one who has the greatest right over him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?

The answer: No, it is never legislated. Why? Because whatever deed you do, its reward reaches the Messenger (ﷺ) whether you dedicate it or not, since he is the one who guided to this deed. So he has no need of it. And if you dedicate the reward of your deed to him, the reality is that you have deprived yourself of its reward, because the reward of this deed already belongs to the Messenger (peace be upon him). Therefore it is not legislated.

Is it legislated to dedicate the reward to one's relatives? Some scholars say: it is not legislated, because this was only reported in a specific case (*fī al-aṣl*, i.e., in the original report). We say to him: this is an error. What was reported in the original case is not a statement that gives a general ruling for the whole community. It is only a specific case: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah asked permission to dedicate that for his mother, and the other man asked permission for it to be for his mother. But what do you say about the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Whoever dies with fasting owed upon him, his guardian shall fast on his behalf"?[[Hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhārī no. (1952), and Muslim no. (1147 (153)), from ʿĀʾishah.]] It includes his mother, his father, his brother, his paternal uncle, and everyone who was responsible for his affairs. So restricting this to the two parents has no evidence.

If someone asks: "Is it legislated for me to dedicate the reward to relatives, whether parents or others?" The answer: No, it is not legislated. But it is among the permissible matters, which the Messenger (ﷺ) did not forbid. And although he did not forbid it, he guided to what is more important and more excellent, which is supplication, when he said: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: a continuing charity (ṣadaqah jāriyah), or knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him."[[Narrated by Muslim, no. (1631 (14)), from Abū Hurayrah.]] Now reflect on the context of the hadith: is it about deeds or not? It is about deeds: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end." Then he turned away from saying "or a righteous child who acts on his behalf" to saying "or a righteous child who prays for him." This is a clear indication that acting on behalf of others is not what is required of a person; supplication is better. That is why we do not find this to be common during the time of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, despite their eagerness for good and kindness. From this we know that what many people do today, dedicating acts of worship to the dead, and the fact that when someone dedicates an act of worship to the dead he performs it more diligently than when he performs it for himself, as is observed, shows that this is a misuse and a lack of understanding of the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* **Student:** Is it permissible to dedicate the reward (...) to one's parents while they are alive?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, it is permissible, except in matters that require that they perform the act themselves, such as prayer. For example, if someone says, "I will pray on behalf of my father because he is tired," that is not valid.
* **Student:** Shaykh, we said, O Shaykh, regarding ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, that if Allah willed, He could burden people beyond their capacity. But O Shaykh, we said elsewhere that Allah, glorified and exalted, does nothing except for a wisdom, based on His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insān 30].
* **The Shaykh:** Well said, yes.
* **Student:** So it means that burdening a person with what he cannot bear (...).
* **The Shaykh:** That has not happened. We do not go to that until we look at its aspect. We say: if He willed, and we mentioned the wisdom. We said the wisdom in that is that He would punish them if they refused.
* **Student:** The wisdom is that Allah, glorified and exalted, punishes them for it. But Allah, glorified and exalted, punishes the soul for something, meaning it cannot bear it. Allah, glorified and exalted, knows that it cannot bear it (...) justice.
* **The Shaykh:** For this reason it has become non-existent. For this reason we say it is one of Allah's favours upon us. That is, if we said that this is impossible, there would be no favour in it, and every indication of (...) a heavy obligation would become a matter with no favour. We say: there is favour in it.
* **Student:** Yes, favour in the sense of imposing worship.
* **The Shaykh:** Good. So it is by Allah's favour that He did not impose on the servant what he cannot bear.
* **Student:** But the favour returns to the perfection of Allah's justice, glorified and exalted.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes.
* **Student:** (...) impossible.
* **The Shaykh:** We say: it is impossible now.
* **Student:** The explanation of the verse, the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾ [al-Najm 39]?
* **The Shaykh:** It will come to us, if Allah wills, the answer to it.
* **Student:** (...)
* **The Shaykh:** I say that it will come to us, if Allah wills, the answer to this, to their evidence, those who said that a person does not benefit from the deed of another. We mentioned the evidence of those who said that he does benefit, and we will answer, if Allah the Exalted wills, the evidence of those who say that he does not benefit.
* **Student:** O our Shaykh, the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three," or "a righteous child who prays for him." The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), "deeds come to an end," means that nothing comes to him (...) and he does not benefit from another's, rather supplication and his child (...)?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, there is no problem with this. It is a disconnected exception (*istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ*). Do you not know the disconnected exception? It is when the exception is not of the same kind as what it is excepted from.
* **Student:** How would the meaning be?
* **The Shaykh:** The meaning of the hadith is: when a person dies, his deeds come to an end, except for a continuing charity or knowledge from which benefit is gained. This is clear, this is from his deeds. Or a righteous child who prays for him: this is a disconnected exception. That is, if a righteous child prays for him, he benefits from it.
* **Student:** The hadith that was reported as the reason for the revelation of these verses, ﴿The Messenger believes﴾. The Companions came and said: "We have been burdened with what we cannot bear, and a verse was revealed that we cannot bear, and it is this verse." Is this evidence for the permissibility of burdening with what cannot be borne? Because the Messenger (ﷺ) approved of them and did not say to them "no." "Say: We hear and we obey" [[Narrated by Muslim, no. (126 (200)), from Ibn ʿAbbās.]] (...).
* **The Shaykh:** When the verse ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 102] was revealed, in reality, although some scholars called it *naskh* (abrogation), it is abrogation according to the terminology of the earlier scholars, meaning specification (*takhṣīṣ*). Although some of them applied the term naskh to it, the correct view is that it is not abrogation; it falls under specification.
* **Student:** When this was revealed: ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, they came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we cannot bear it." So here they said, "We cannot bear it," and the Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Say: We hear and we obey."
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, what they meant by not being able to bear it is that something comes upon our hearts that we cannot repel. This concerns the action of the heart. That is, when something comes upon the heart that cannot be repelled, one cannot bear it.
* **Student:** So there is no evidence for this?
* **The Shaykh:** There is no evidence. Perhaps what they meant by it is the severe difficulty in guarding against it.
* **Student:** Shaykh, the recitation of the Qurʾān, if it is general without specification, meaning (...)?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, except what the text has reported. For example, if someone recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ and dedicates it to the dead, there is nothing wrong with it, because it equals one third of the Qurʾān. Likewise al-Fātiḥah, the greatest surah in the Book of Allah.
* **Student:** Shaykh, the saying of the Messenger of Allah, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him, "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three," and he mentioned continuing charity. So if a person earns, for example, a person who built a place of amusement and died, is the sin of this place borne by one who engaged in it, meaning committed a sin? Does he bear its burden?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, yes, yes.
* **Student:** So his deeds did not come to an end?
* **The Shaykh:** This is not continuing charity. This is a continuing punishment.
* **Student:** Shaykh, as for when a person repents and he has an evil deed, and its sunnah spread among people (...) but he repented, is it not (...)?
* **The Shaykh:** It is obligatory for him to break that idol.
* **Student:** He was not able to.
* **The Shaykh:** If he is not able, the obligation falls from him, yes.
* **Student:** The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾, does it fall under the saying of Allah: "I have done"?
* **The Shaykh:** All these sentences say, "I have done."
* **Student:** The saying of Allah: ﴿and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾, does it include legislative and divine decreed burdens?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, yes.
* **Student:** (...) what they have no ability to bear.
* **The Shaykh:** No. You are now supplicating. Did you understand or not? You are asking Allah, glorified and exalted, with that. If you call upon Allah sincerely, then these calamities that some people may not be able to bear, Allah will carry them for you, and they will be easy for you, like the Day of Resurrection, which is easy for the believers and not easy for the disbelievers.
* **Student:** If they befall a person?
* **The Shaykh:** If they befall him, they become easy for him, as though they were nothing.
* **Student:** If they are not made easy, then either he did not supplicate, or he did not supplicate...
* **The Shaykh:** Or he did not supplicate sincerely, or for some other reason.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shayṭān. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the reward of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾ [al-Baqarah 286].

We have derived several benefits from this verse:

* One: the ease of the Islamic religion. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾.
* Two: that acts of worship vary according to the condition of the one who is obligated. We may require this man to pray standing, for example, and not require the other. We may require this one to spend, and not require the second. We may require this one to fight, and not require the second, and so on. Obligations vary according to the addressee, or according to the one who is obligated.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person has a limited capacity, from His saying: ﴿beyond its capacity﴾. A person has a limited capacity in everything: in knowledge, in power, in understanding, in memory. Everything has a limited capacity, and one is obligated according to his capacity.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person has what he earns, directly or through the agency of others, from His saying: ﴿It will have [the reward of] what it has earned﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person cannot be wronged by having even one of his good deeds diminished, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿what it has earned﴾. And ﴿what﴾ here is a relative pronoun that indicates generality, meaning everything it has earned.
* Also among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person bears the burden of what he has earned, from His saying: ﴿what it has earned﴾.
* It follows from the difference in expression that a person is not held accountable for merely intending an evil deed, from His saying: "earned" (*iktasabat*), and the ta' indicates what? It indicates the act itself and direct doing, unlike the reward for righteous deeds, since a person is rewarded for his intention. That is why He said: ﴿what it has earned﴾.
* Among them: it is not permissible for a person to bear another's burden for his own sin, but it is permissible for a person to have the reward of a righteous deed credited to another, from His saying: ﴿and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾. So if a person performs a forbidden deed and says, "O Allah, record the burden of this upon my enemy, so-and-so," is that possible?
* **The students:** It is not possible.
* **The Shaykh:** Good. If he performs a righteous deed and says, "O Allah, record the reward of this for my father, or my brother, or for so-and-so among the people," this is valid, and this is the benefit of His saying: ﴿It will have [the reward of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that righteous deeds are an acquisition (*kasb*) and sinful deeds are a loss (*gharm*). This is derived from His saying: ﴿lahā﴾ ("it will have") and from His saying: ﴿ʿalayhā﴾ ("it will bear"). For ʿalā (upon) clearly indicates a loss, and the lām clearly indicates an acquisition.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mercy of Allah, glorified and exalted, toward creation, in that He taught them a supplication to call upon, and answered them, in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾.
* Among its benefits: that a person should, in supplication, invoke the attribute that is appropriate, such as Lordship (*rubūbiyyah*), by which creation and its management exist. That is why most of the supplications in the Qurʾān all begin with an attribute of Lordship, such as "Our Lord" or "Lord." ﴿And Noah said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller﴾ [Nūḥ 26]; and Abraham said: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray﴾ [Ibrāhīm 36], and similar examples.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the lifting of accountability for forgetfulness and ignorance, from His saying: ﴿Do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾. Allah, the Exalted, said: "I have done."

Does lifting the requirement of repetition necessarily entail the removal of the demand? The answer: No. The lifting of accountability does not necessarily entail the removal of the demand. Whoever abandons an obligation through forgetfulness or ignorance must repeat it; the demand is not removed, and it becomes obligatory for him to perform it. That is why the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers it."[[Hadith agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhārī no. (597), Muslim no. (680 (309)), and al-Bazzār no. (6320), with his wording, from Anas ibn Mālik.]] And when the man who did not calm himself in his prayer prayed, he said to him: "Go back and pray, for you have not prayed,"[[Hadith agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhārī no. (757), and Muslim no. (397 (45)), from Abū Hurayrah.]] and he did not excuse him because of ignorance, even though he did not know how to do better than that. So the lifting of accountability for forgetfulness and ignorance does not remove the demand. Does it remove the sin of the prohibition? The answer: Yes, it removes the sin of the prohibition. Can we say that in the case of a prohibition the demand is not removed? Yes. How is the demand not removed? Because the prohibition is a demand to abandon it. If you do it through forgetfulness or ignorance, the ruling is not lifted; the ruling remains, and the demand to abandon it remains. But the difference between a prohibition and a command is that a command demands bringing something into existence, while a prohibition demands abstention. So this man who committed the forbidden act through ignorance or forgetfulness, we say: it is as though you had not done it. Therefore, if the prohibited act entails the invalidation of the act of worship, the act of worship is not invalidated. If it entails an expiation (*kaffārah*), the expiation is not established. Why? Because accountability for that forbidden act has been lifted, and when accountability for it is lifted, its existence becomes like nonexistence, as though nothing had happened. That is why we say: if a person ate while fasting through forgetfulness, his fast is valid, as the Sunnah has shown. And if he ate in ignorance, thinking the sun had set, and then it became clear that it had not set, his fast is valid, as the Sunnah has brought. But if he had sexual intercourse in ignorance that intercourse invalidates the fast?
* **Student:** (...)
* **The Shaykh:** Be careful: ignorant that it invalidates the fast, but he knows that it is forbidden. As long as he has knowledge, knowledge of the consequences of the forbidden act is not a condition. It is not a requirement, so long as you know that it is forbidden and that it has a consequence for you. So if he had intercourse, knowing that intercourse is forbidden, but not knowing that he is liable to this severe expiation, we say: the expiation is obligatory upon you, because you violated the prohibition knowingly. Do you understand now? Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) did not waive the expiation from the man who had intercourse during Ramadan, even though he did not know what he was liable for, and came asking what he owed. But he knew it was forbidden. This differs from a person who did not know it was forbidden: he bears no sin, no make-up obligation, and no expiation. The difference between them is, I think, clear.

A man has intercourse during Hajj before the first tahallul (the partial exit from ihram). He does not know the ruling and thinks that once a person has stood at Arafah, his Hajj is complete. On the night of Muzdalifah, the night of the Eid, he is with his wife, sleeps with her and has intercourse with her. It is said to him: Why? He says: Because the Messenger ﷺ said: «The Hajj is Arafah»[[Narrated by Ibn Majah (3015), al-Tirmidhi (889) and al-Nasa'i (3016), from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mur al-Dili.]] "The Hajj is Arafah," so I performed Hajj. This is what I understood. Is his Hajj invalidated? It is not invalidated. Is there an expiation (kaffarah) upon him? No, because the ignorant person, as the noble verse indicates, is not held accountable, and when a person is not held accountable for doing a prohibited act, its occurrence is like its non-occurrence.

A man swears that he will not speak to Zayd, then he sees a person among the people and speaks to him, but he does not know that it is Zayd. There is no expiation upon him, because he is ignorant. And God says, when He said: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾. He said: "I have done so." So this is the principle. If someone says: You mentioned that acts of obedience (al-awamir) must be performed as commanded, so what is dropped from him at that point? We say: What is dropped from him is the sin, because if he performed the commanded act in an invalid manner deliberately, he would be sinful, yes, in an invalid manner and deliberately, he would be sinful, because he would be like one who mocks the signs of God. For example, if he prayed while in a state of impurity (hadath) knowing that he was in that state, would he be sinful or not? He would be sinful. If he prayed in a state of impurity, forgetting his impurity, does he sin? He does not sin. So we have understood the absence of accountability. But do we oblige him to repeat the prayer? Yes, we oblige him, because this is an act commanded. Thus it becomes clear the reason why one who performs the commanded act in an invalid manner, while forgetful or ignorant, is not held accountable, and if we command him to repeat it, that is because he is not sinful by this act. Do you not know that Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: If a person prays in a state of impurity while knowing and remembering it, he has disbelieved, he has left Islam. Why? Because he is mocking the signs of God. We say: If he prayed forgetfully or ignorantly, he has not disbelieved and there is no sin upon him, because one is not held accountable for ignorance and forgetfulness. But, in view of the continuing demand, it is obligatory upon him to perform what is required.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person's act occurs by his own choice. In it there is a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists), who say that a person is compelled in his deeds, and that when a person does an act by choice, he is like one who is compelled in his act; the movement of a person by his choice is like the movement of a palm frond in the wind, not by its own choice. Do you understand? Is this view false or not? There is no doubt, it is false, both by revelation and by reason. As for revelation, the many texts confirm that a person's act occurs by his own will: ﴿Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾ [Al Imran 152] and ﴿for whoever among you wills to take a straight path﴾ [At-Takwir 28]. As for reason, if a person were compelled in his actions, God's punishment of him would be injustice, for how could He compel him to something and then punish him for it? Is it not so?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good. They claim that injustice is for a person to dispose of another's property, and God's disposal of His own property is not injustice, even if He punishes the obedient, He is not unjust. But we say: Even if it were supposed that He punished the obedient, that would be injustice, because God said: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, he will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾ [Ta-Ha 112]. So He negated injustice from Himself, may He be exalted. The point is that this is not the place to expand on this issue. But in the verse there is a refutation of the Jabriyyah, and the refutation is this: God lifted accountability from the ignorant and the forgetful, because the ignorant and the forgetful did not intend the violation. This shows that what a person is held accountable for is what proceeds from knowledge and awareness, and it occurs by what? By his will, because he is held accountable for it. He said: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that forgetfulness befalls human beings, and error befalls human beings. What is the evidence? ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾. If this were not something that befalls them, then supplicating for non-accountability for it would be meaningless and futile. Every person forgets, every person errs. «Every child of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent»[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2499) and Ibn Majah (4251), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «I am only a human like you; I forget as you forget»[[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (401) and Muslim (572), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]].

If someone says: What is the wisdom in God, glorified and exalted, making human beings forget and err?

We say: The wisdom is so that a person may realize his weakness, that he is weak, weak in comprehension and weak in retention, in every state; and so that thereby the bounty of God upon him in knowledge and memory may be made clear, and similar things through which forgetfulness and ignorance occur; and so that a person may be in need of his Lord, may He be exalted, in lifting forgetfulness and ignorance from him, so he turns to God, may He be exalted, and says: O God, preserve for me what I have learned, preserve for me my religion, preserve for me my knowledge, and similar things, which make it necessary for a person to be in need of his Lord when he knows that his state is forgetfulness and what? Error.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: God's favor upon this Ummah by lifting the burdens (al-isr) which were laid upon those before us. Because of His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us﴾. Then God said: "I have done so." This shows that this Ummah has had the burdens and shackles that were upon those before it lifted from it, and this is indeed so, and praise be to God.

* Among them: that this Ummah has had the ruling of forgetfulness lifted from it.

﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾ [Al-Baqarah 286]

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that forgetfulness befalls human beings, and error befalls human beings. Its evidence: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾. If this were not something that befalls them, then supplicating for non-accountability for it would be meaningless and futile. Every person forgets, every person errs. «Every child of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent»[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2499), Ibn Majah (4251), and al-Darimi (2769), from the hadith of Anas. ]]. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «I am only a human like you; I forget as you forget»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (401) and Muslim (572/89), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. ]].

If someone says: What is the wisdom in God, glorified and exalted, making human beings forget and err?

We say: The wisdom is so that a person may realize his weakness, that he is weak, weak in comprehension and weak in retention, in every state; and so that thereby the bounty of God upon him in knowledge and memory may be made clear, and similar things through which forgetfulness and ignorance occur; and so that a person may be in need of his Lord, may He be exalted, in lifting forgetfulness and ignorance from him, so he turns to God, may He be exalted, and says: O God, preserve for me what I have learned, preserve for me my religion, preserve for me my knowledge, and similar things, which make it necessary for a person to be needy of his Lord when he knows that his state is forgetfulness and what? Error.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: God's favor upon this Ummah by lifting the burdens which were laid upon those before us, because of His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us﴾. Then God said?

* A student: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us﴾.

* The Shaykh: No, it is not like this. Did we not accept the burden?

* A student: God said: "I have done so."

* The Shaykh: God said: "I have done so."

So we say: God said: "I have done so," and this shows that this Ummah has had the burdens and shackles that were upon those before it lifted from it, and this is indeed so, and praise be to God.

* Among them: that this Ummah has had the ruling of forgetfulness lifted from it, because of His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾.

If someone says: What do you say about the saying of God, the Exalted, in the story of Adam: ﴿And We had already taken a pledge from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no resolve﴾ [Ta-Ha 115]?

We say: This is among what God lifted from this Ummah: forgetfulness was lifted from this Ummah. As for Adam, he was held accountable for it, because He said: ﴿He forgot, and We found in him no resolve﴾ [Ta-Ha 115]. So in the law of Adam a person was held accountable for forgetfulness. Moreover, some of the people of knowledge said: The intended meaning of forgetfulness in the story of Adam is abandonment, because forgetfulness is used to mean abandonment, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They forgot God, so He forgot them﴾ [At-Tawbah 67], meaning: He abandoned them.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that those before us were obligated with what is greater than what we were obligated with, because of His saying: ﴿as You laid upon those before us﴾ [Al-Baqarah 286], and we have previously mentioned an example of this in the tafsir. Who will bring it?

* A student: First: among the Jews, if a person killed one of them, he would be killed for it, whether his guardian pardoned him or not. And among the Christians, if a person killed one of them, the obligation is pardon.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* A student: God, may He be mighty and majestic, revealed to the Children of Israel that if they wanted to repent, they should kill themselves.

* The Shaykh: When they worshipped the calf specifically, God made their repentance to be that they kill themselves. Two examples suffice.

Good. ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾.

* Also derived from the noble verse: that a person should ask God for well-being, such that He does not burden him with what he cannot bear. In it there is a refutation of some of the Sufis, I mean the Sufiyyah, who said: "We do not ask God, exalted, to protect us from what is difficult for us, because we are His servants, and if what is difficult befalls us, we will endure it." There has passed before us the story of Sahnun the Maliki, who said, among what he said addressing God: "However You will, test me," meaning: I am patient, however You will, test me. So he was tested with difficulty in urination, and he could not urinate easily. He would come to the kuttab (Qur'an schools), to the small children in the schools, and say: "Pray for your uncle, the liar." He came to the small children because they are closer to being answered, since sins are not recorded against them. He says: "Pray to God for me, your liar uncle," why? Because he lied. Did he endure patiently or not?

* The students: He did not endure.

* The Shaykh: He did not endure. Therefore a person should ask God for well-being, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «Do not wish for the encounter with the enemy, but ask God for well-being; and when you meet them, be patient»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2966) and Muslim (1742/20), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa.]]. This is derived from His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that a person should ask God for pardon, because a person is not free from shortcoming in the commanded acts, so he asks God for pardon for his shortcoming, as in His saying: ﴿and pardon us﴾, and asking God for forgiveness of the sins he has committed, because if a person is not forgiven, sins accumulate upon him, cover his heart, and perhaps destroy and ruin him. Because of His saying: what?

* The students: ﴿and forgive us﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿and forgive us﴾.

* Also among its benefits: that a person should ask God to have mercy on him in the future of his affairs, so He pardons what has passed, forgives, and has mercy in what? In the future. Because of His saying: ﴿and have mercy on us﴾. And through this we know the difference between these three expressions: seeking pardon for neglect in what?

* The students: In acts of obedience.

* The Shaykh: In acts of obedience, in the commanded, and seeking forgiveness for committing prohibited acts, and mercy regarding what a person faces in his time, that God has mercy on him and enables him to do what is in his interest.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the believer has no protector except his Lord. Because of His saying: ﴿You are our Protector﴾. In it is the affirmation of God's guardianship, may He be mighty and majestic. It has passed before us in the tafsir that guardianship is of two kinds: general and specific. The general means that God manages all the affairs of creation, whether believer or disbeliever, righteous or wicked, sinful or just. And the specific, which is His guardianship of whom?

* The students: Of the believers.

* The Shaykh: Of the believers. ﴿Unquestionably, the allies of God will have no fear, nor will they grieve. Those who believed and were fearing God﴾ [Yunus 62, 63]. We also say, regarding the most specific guardianship, which is for the messengers, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed God is his Protector﴾ [At-Tahrim 4].

* Also among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of God's active attributes (sifat fi'liyyah), may He be mighty and majestic: "Pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people."

This is the position of the Salaf (the early generations): that God, may He be mighty and majestic, has attributes connected to His will and His volition, whose type is eternal and whose individual instances are temporal. The type is eternal, and it is the genus of the act, while the individual instances are temporal. All the acts that God performs, their genus is eternal, because God has always been and still is an active doer. As for their individual instances, they are temporal. Let us suppose, for example, that God provides sustenance for a person. When does He provide it? When it exists. So is this act temporal or not? It is temporal. Yes, God descends to the lowest heaven every night; this occurs, every night there is a descent, and when dawn rises the descent ends. Likewise, regarding all the active attributes, we say: our belief concerning them is that their genus or type is eternal and their individual instances are temporal.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person must turn to God, may He be mighty and majestic, for victory over the disbelieving people, because of His saying: ﴿so grant us victory over the disbelieving people﴾.

* Among its benefits: taking the means, or alerting to taking the means, because of His saying: ﴿so grant us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. Because it is not possible to ask for victory while you are on your bed; you must act. ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ [Al-Anfal 60]. For everything you ask God, may He be mighty and majestic, you are commanded to perform its causes. If someone says: "O God, grant me victory over the disbelieving people," but he does not move in his house, this is not sound. Well, will He grant you victory over the disbelieving people while you do not fight them?

Victory requires action, and victory is a help in this; God helps you against them.

If someone says: "O God, grant me a righteous child," but he has not married, is this possible? From where will the child come? Will it sprout from his head?! It is not possible. He must marry, otherwise the supplication is void. So everything you ask God, may He be mighty and majestic, you are commanded to perform its causes, because your asking the Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, is so that He will help you and facilitate the causes that you cannot accomplish by yourself. You may marry, for example, you can marry, you have married for example. Can you create a child? No: ﴿Have you considered what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 58, 59].

So this is up to God, and the origin of facilitating marriage, for example, is from God, may He be exalted; you turn to God.

Likewise, seeking victory over the disbelieving people also requires performing the cause.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disbeliever is an enemy to us. For this reason we asked God to grant us victory over him, not that we grant him victory. The evidences that the disbeliever is an enemy to the believer are many in the Book and the Sunnah. And since he is an enemy to us, reason and the Law require that we take him as an enemy, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ [Fatir 6].

As for knowing that he is an enemy and then taking him as an ally, this is foolishness in reason and error in religion. It is obligatory that we not trust any disbeliever, however much friendship and affection he displays, for he is an enemy; because of His saying: ﴿so grant us victory over the disbelieving people﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 285–286 (part 1 of 7):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers...﴾ to the end of the verse.

We explained His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers﴾, and we explained: ﴿Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers﴾ to the end of the verse. Is that right or not?

He said: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord﴾, meaning he believes in what was sent down to him of revelation in the Book of Allah and in what is revealed to him of the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.

In His saying: ﴿what has been sent down to him from his Lord﴾ there is a special lordship (rububiyyah), because it is attributed to the Messenger ﷺ. The lordship attributed to the messengers is the most specific type of lordship, followed by the lordship attributed to the believers, and then the most general, the lordship attributed to all people, such as: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah 2]. This special lordship undoubtedly entails a special nurturing that no other nurturing of the nurtured can match.

As for His saying: ﴿and the believers﴾, it is in the nominative, coordinated with His saying ﴿the Messenger﴾, meaning: and the believers likewise believe in what was sent down to the Prophet ﷺ from Allah. So they believe in the Messenger, they believe in the One who sent him, and they believe in what he was sent with: three things. The sender, who is Allah; the one sent, who is the Messenger ﷺ; and what he was sent with, which is the revelation: the Book and the Sunnah.

And as for His saying: ﴿The Messenger believes﴾ and ﴿and the believers﴾: if someone asks, "How does He say ﴿and the believers﴾ and describe them with belief, when they are believers?" We say: this is from the category of affirmation (tahqiq), meaning that the believers have realized (haqqaqu) faith, and their faith is not merely outward, as is the case with the hypocrite who displays faith while concealing disbelief.

﴿Each one⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ ﴾, meaning of the Messenger and the believers: ﴿Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers﴾ to the end. ﴿Each one believes in Allah﴾: the word (āmana, believed) has come up for us many times, and what is meant by it is an acknowledgment that includes acceptance and submission, not merely belief in the existence of Allah. That is not faith in the full sense, which would entail accepting what He brought, accepting what He informed of and what He commanded, with submission and surrender.

And His saying: ﴿Each one believes in Allah﴾: belief in Allah includes four matters. The first: belief in His existence. The second: belief in His lordship. The third: belief in His divinity. The fourth: belief in His names and attributes. Faith must include these four things. Belief in the existence of Allah is to guard against those who deny the existence of Allah and say: this universe is nothing but things interacting, with one producing another, wombs expelling and earths swallowing, and there is nothing (we seek refuge in Allah). We must believe in the existence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and we must believe in His lordship. When we say "we believe in His lordship," we mean His being singular in lordship, that He is the absolute Lord, and that the lordship of anything other than Him is restricted, not comprehensive, not general, and not complete, but deficient and restricted as well: deficient in its limits and deficient in its authority. As for the lordship of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it is complete and vast; there is no one to repel His judgment, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

The third: belief in His divinity, the true divinity, and there is no divinity for other than Him. Everything to which divinity is ascribed is false, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾ [al-Hajj 62].

The fourth: belief in His names and attributes: that He has names and attributes in which He is unique, and none resembles Him in them. So we affirm the names and attributes and negate partnership or likeness, for this is the reality of tawhid.

Thus, whoever does not believe in the existence of Allah is not a believer. Whoever believes in His existence but not His lordship, by saying that He has a partner or helper in creating the heavens and the earth, or that there is another god who alone created what was created, we say that this person has not believed in Allah. And whoever believes in the existence of Allah and His lordship, and that He alone possesses complete lordship, but denies His divinity, by saying as the disbelievers said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing﴾ [Sad 5], then he has not believed in Allah. And whoever believes in the existence of Allah, His lordship and His divinity, but does not believe in His names and attributes, has not believed in Allah either. His faith may be nonexistent or may be deficient, according to what has been established in his heart of faith and assent, or denial and rejection.

Thus, those who believe in some of the names and not others, we say: they have not realized belief in Allah. Those who believe in the names but not the attributes have not realized belief in Allah. Those who believe in some attributes and disbelieve in others have not realized belief in Allah. Then, if their denial of what they deny of that is rejection and repudiation, they are what?

* The students: Disbelievers.

* The Shaykh: Disbelievers (kufrah). If it is a ta'wil (interpretation), they are not disbelievers, but one looks at their interpretation: whether it has a basis, or whether it is an interpretation that amounts to denial, in which case they are judged according to what their condition requires.

If someone asks: how do we establish the proofs for the existence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? We say: we establish them in several ways: by the senses, by reason, by revelation, and by innate nature (fitrah). As for reason: we say, these existing beings, which change morning and evening through non-existence, existence, and changes of state, who changes them? Do we look to who? Does so-and-so change them, or so-and-so, or so-and-so?! Never. They cannot change them; rather they are themselves changed. So these beings necessarily require a Creator who brings into existence and changes, and we find none but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. We find none but Allah. For this reason Allah pointed to it in His saying: ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [al-Tur 35]. We find the heavens and the earth: who created this earth? Were they workers who made it and put in it the sands, the mountains, the valleys, the rivers and the seas?

The answer: No. Even if the whole world gathered with all its workers, they could not do that. Therefore it must have a Creator. The heavens likewise, and greater: no one can create them except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason He said: ﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-Tur 36]. The answer: No. ﴿Rather, they are not certain.﴾ This is a rational proof for the existence of Allah, and no one denies it.

If someone said to you: "This lamp was made by no one," what would you say? You would say: "Take this man quickly to the madhouse, because he is insane, isn't that so?"

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: And if he said: "This recorder was made by no one," we would say the same. It is related that a group of the Samaniyya, atheists among the Indians, came to Abu Hanifa in Baghdad and said to him: "How can we establish the existence of a Creator?" He lowered his head and was silent. They said: "Answer!" They thought he had been cut off and had become incapable. He said: "I am thinking about a ship that has anchored in the water of the Euphrates or the Tigris without having a sailor, and unloaded its cargo without workers, and departed without a captain. Look, is this possible or not?"

* The students: Not possible.

* The Shaykh: He was saying this to them. So look: is this possible or not? They said: "This cannot be; imagine it, it is madness. Is it reasonable that a ship comes loaded, unloads its cargo, and leaves without a sailor and without workers?!" He said: "By God, if you claim that the heavens, the earth, the sun, the moon and the stars came into being without a maker and move without a mover, then this ship is easier. ﴿So they were overcome there and turned back humiliated﴾ [al-A'raf 119]." So this is a rational proof.

The sensory proof for the existence of Allah is also established. Among its greatest evidences is the answering of supplication: when a person calls upon his Lord, He answers him, and the Qur'an is full of this. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them: they denied Our servant and said, "He is a madman," and he was rebuffed. (9) So he called upon his Lord: "Indeed, I am overpowered, so help [me]." (10) So We opened the gates of the sky with pouring water﴾ [al-Qamar 9–11]. When he said: "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me," ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾ [Nuh 26], the Lord answered him and sent upon them the flood, and opened the gates of the sky with pouring water, ﴿and We caused the earth to gush forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar 12], and they were drowned, every one of them, except those who believed. Does this indicate the non-existence of the Lord or His existence?

* The students: His existence.

* The Shaykh: His existence. And this remains a matter perceived, witnessed and felt. Even a person calls upon his Lord for something, then sees it with his own eyes, as a plain sight, having occurred. So what does this indicate for the existence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? The senses and reality.

As for innate nature (fitrah): every human being whom the devils have not seduced and whom the environment has not changed acknowledges with necessary knowledge that he has a Creator who alone created him without asking anyone. But the environment may corrupt him and the devils may seduce him, so he denies this. We have remained with what?

* The students: Revelation (shar').

* The Shaykh: The fourth: revelation. The Book, the Sunnah, and all the earlier scriptures are full of establishing the existence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason, no atheist can stand firm in denying the Lord except by obstinate arrogance, and the arrogant person has no cure. The one who is obstinate and says, "This is not the sun," can one treat him and convince him? It is impossible. As for belief in His lordship, belief in His divinity, and belief in His names and attributes, their matter is clear: that Allah is the Lord of everything, its Sovereign, its Manager, and the One who disposes of it.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Each one believes in Allah and His angels﴾, meaning: and believes in His angels. The Messenger and the believers all believe in the angels of Allah. The grammarians said that the word for angels (malā'ikah) is the plural of (malak), whose original form is (ma'lak), because it derives from (al-alūkah), which means message. They said there is metathesis (taqdim and ta'khir) in its letters, a change (i'lal) by means of metathesis. The angels are messengers, as Allah said: ﴿Who made the angels messengers having wings﴾ [Fatir 1]. Are they entities (dhawat) or spirits and meanings?

* The students: Entities.

* The Shaykh: Entities, who are seen, with wings. It is established in the authentic collection that the Prophet ﷺ saw Gabriel in his original form, which he was created with, having six hundred wings that filled the horizon.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3232) and Muslim (174 / 280), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, in similar wording.]] Six hundred wings that filled the horizon: how swift is this angel? His speed is great, like the blink of an eye, because six hundred wings all beating with tremendous force means that he is swifter than the blink of an eye. For this reason Allah made him the envoy between Himself and the messengers, sending him with revelation.

The angels were created from light, as is established in the authentic collection.[[Recorded by Muslim (2996 / 60), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] The angels do not eat or drink, because they are free of bodily hollows, so they have no need of food and drink. Rather, "they glorify Him night and day, they do not slacken" [al-Anbiya' 20], meaning they do not tire, do not become bored, and do not grow weary, because there is nothing that takes away their energy and diminishes it. For this reason they have no need of eating and drinking.

The angels are of various categories in their duties. Among them is the one entrusted with revelation, who is Gabriel; the one entrusted with rain and plants, who is Michael; the one entrusted with blowing the Trumpet and with bearing the Throne, who is Israfil; the one entrusted with Paradise, who is Ridwan; and with the Fire, who is Malik; and with death, who is the Angel of Death. As for what has been reported about calling him "'Azra'il," this is not authentic. He is the Angel of Death, as Allah said: ﴿Say: The Angel of Death who has been charged with you will take you﴾ [al-Sajdah 11].

Among them are those who worship Allah, the Exalted, night and day, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The heaven has creaked, and it has the right to creak. There is not a space of four fingers except that there is an angel standing for Allah, or bowing, or prostrating."[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2312) and Ibn Majah (4190), from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] This indicates their great number. Among them are those entrusted with recording the deeds of the children of Adam: ﴿on the right and on the left, seated﴾ [Qaf 17]. Among them are those entrusted with guarding the children of Adam: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd 11]. Whatever has come in the Book and the Sunnah regarding these deeds and attributes of the angels, we are obligated to believe in it and accept it, whenever it is authentically established in the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.

As for His saying: ﴿believes in Allah, His angels and His books﴾, and in one reading: ﴿and His Book﴾. As for the reading "books" (kutub), there is no difficulty, since the books are many. As for the reading in the singular ﴿and His Book﴾, it is a singular noun in construct, which conveys generality.

As for the books sent down upon the prophets, what appears from the texts of the Book and the Sunnah is that they are as many as the prophets, as Allah said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾ [al-Hadid 25], ﴿and sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Mankind was one community, so Allah sent prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed﴾ [al-Baqarah 213]. However, we do not know individually except a few of them: the Qur'an, the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, the scrolls of Abraham, and the scrolls of Moses, if they are other than the Torah; and if they are the Torah, the matter is clear. We know these and believe in them by their specific identity, and the rest we believe in generally.

But how is belief in these books? We say: belief in the Qur'an is belief that it is from Allah, and that Allah truly spoke it in its wording and meaning. It is the speech of Allah, letters and meanings. This is one point. We also believe in every report that Allah reported in the Qur'an.

Third: we accept every ruling that Allah ruled in the Qur'an.

Fourth: we implement every ruling that Allah ruled in the Qur'an.

These are four things. The first, to repeat it a second time: that the Qur'an is from Allah, sent down from Allah, and that it is His speech, letters and meanings.

Second: we affirm every report in the Book.

Third: we accept every ruling; we do not reject any of it.

Fourth: we implement the rulings, because there is a difference between acceptance and implementation. A person may implement without accepting, and may accept without implementing. How? A person may accept that prayer is obligatory but not perform it; and he may perform prayer but not accept that it is obligatory, saying it is voluntary: if he wishes he does it, and if he wishes he does not. For this reason, legal rulings require two things: acceptance of the ruling and what after that? And implementation of the ruling and carrying it out. Neither suffices in place of the other.

As for the earlier books, we are obligated to believe that they are from Allah; that is, that Allah the Exalted sent down the Torah to Moses. But we are not obliged to believe that the Torah in the hands of the Jews is the Torah that Allah sent down to Moses, why? Because it has been distorted and concealed: ﴿Say: Who sent down the Book which Moses brought as a light and guidance for the people, which you make into scrolls, displaying some and concealing much﴾ [al-An'am 91]. And what else? ﴿and concealing much.﴾ There are things that were hidden and removed, and there are things that were distorted. So we believe that the Torah which Allah sent down to Moses is true, that every report in it is true, and that every ruling in it is true. Is that correct?

* The students: Correct.

**The Shaykh:** Do we implement these rulings or not? No, we do not implement them except with evidence from our own Sharia. Our scholars differed over whether the law of those before us (*shar' man qablana*) is law for us. It was said: it is not law at all. It was also said: it is law for us as long as our Sharia does not contradict it. The question is well known in *usul al-fiqh* (the principles of jurisprudence). Likewise, regarding the Injil, we believe that Allah sent down to Isa ibn Maryam a book called "the Injil," that this book came from Allah in truth, that every report in it is true, and that every ruling in it is true. As for acting upon and implementing it, that follows the details found in the Torah. The Injil also completes and perfects the Torah; it is not independent as the Torah is independent. For this reason Allah mentions the Torah frequently in the Qur'an, and mentions the Injil in relation to the Torah only rarely. As for the Zabur, we believe that Allah gave Dawud a Zabur, that it is from Allah in truth, that its reports are true, and that its rulings are true. As for acting upon them, it is as previously stated. We say the same regarding the scrolls of Ibrahim. This is the faith in the books.

Allah sending down books to His servants is undoubtedly a mercy from Him toward them, because they are the path they walk upon, and they reject whatever is other than it. Whoever turns away from them to a ruling other than them has become a disbeliever.

His saying ﴿وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ ("and His messengers"): it is the plural of *rasul* (فَعُول) in the sense of *mursal* (مُفْعَل, "one who is sent"), not in the sense of *fa'il* (فاعِل, "one who sends"). So the *rasul* means one who is sent. Who sent him? Allah, the Exalted, sent him to the creation. ﴿And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them﴾ [Fatir 24]. Every nation had a warner who came to it. But do we know of every warner who came to the creation?

No. Was every warner who came to the creation related to us? No. ﴿And We have already sent messengers before you; among them are those We have related to you and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78]. ﴿And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd 38]. So we believe that Allah the Exalted sent messengers, that these messengers were truly messengers from Allah, that whatever books were revealed to them is true, and whatever rulings they brought is true. As for following, whom do we follow? We follow Muhammad (ﷺ). As for what those messengers brought, it is subject to the difference we mentioned earlier: is the law of those before us law for us, or not? The correct view is that it is law for us as long as our Sharia has not come with something contrary to it.

He said: ﴿We make no distinction between any one of His messengers﴾. "We make no distinction": here there is an *iltifat* (shift in grammatical person). From what to what?

**A student:** From the third person (*al-ghayba*) to the first person (*al-takallum*).

**The Shaykh:** From the third person to the first person, yes. And the first person indicates presence. For He did not say: "They do not make distinction," ﴿Every one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction"﴾. And the expected pattern, had the speech remained in one style, would have been: "they make no distinction between any of His messengers." But He said ﴿We make no distinction﴾. The benefit of *iltifat*, which all its types share, is alerting the listener. The benefit of *iltifat* is alerting, because when speech follows one uniform pattern, a person grows absorbed in it and may lose attention. When *iltifat* comes, it is as if it knocks on the mind, saying: "Pay attention." Naturally, when a person proceeds in one continuous context, he may become drowsy. But when a shift comes, it is as if it strikes his thought to say: "Be alert." So this shift from the third person to the first person has a benefit beyond alerting. It is that these believers say "We make no distinction," meaning: each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers, saying and believing: "We make no distinction between any one of His messengers." All the messengers, in our view, are equal in the truthfulness of what they brought of the message. Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah and truthful in what he brought of the message. Isa ibn Maryam is truthful, Musa is truthful, Salih is truthful, Lut is truthful, Ibrahim is truthful, and so on. We make no distinction among them in this matter, that is, in the truthfulness of their message and in believing in it. But we do distinguish among them in what we were obligated to, so we act upon the Sharia of Muhammad. As for the Sharia of those others, it is subject to the difference we mentioned.

Does the negation of distinction here negate preference? That is, do we make no distinction among any of them even in ranking?

The answer: No, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others﴾ [al-Isra' 55], and He said: ﴿Those messengers — We preferred some of them over others﴾ [al-Baqarah 253]. So in ranking we do distinguish, and we place each one of them in his rank. But in the station of prophethood and the truthfulness of what they brought, they are equal. We believe in all of them.

His saying: ﴿We make no distinction between any one of His messengers, and they say﴾. This is conjoined to His saying ﴿The Messenger has believed﴾, meaning "and they say," that is, the Messenger and those who believed with him ﴿We hear and we obey; [we seek] Your forgiveness﴾. "*Ghufranaka*" (غفرانَ): is the object of "we heard" and "we obeyed."

**A student:** "We heard and we obeyed."

**The Shaykh:** "*Sami'na*" is a verb and subject, and "*ata'na*" is a verb and subject, and "*ghufranaka*" is in the accusative. Could it not be an object of "*sami'na*" and "*ata'na*"?

**The students:** No (...).

**The Shaykh:** No, no. For this reason it is good to pause and say: ﴿And they say, "We hear and we obey"﴾, then begin anew: ﴿[We seek] Your forgiveness﴾, because "*ghufranaka*" is the object of a deleted verb whose estimated form is: "We ask You for Your forgiveness."

His saying: ﴿And they say﴾, that is, the Messenger and the believers, ﴿We hear and we obey﴾, meaning: we hear what You commanded us and we obey it; we hear what You forbade us and we obey You. The first is the command, which we carry out; the second is... what? We avoid it.

Know that people, at the station of revelation and receiving it, divide into categories. Some do not listen and turn away completely: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, at that a faction of them turns away in refusal﴾ [al-Nur 48]. They do not listen at all. Some listen but do not obey. Some listen and obey. Can a fourth category occur, one that obeys but does not listen?

**The students:** No.

**The Shaykh:** It is not possible, because one will only obey what he has heard. So people, with regard to receiving revelation, divide into three categories. One category is the averter, who does not listen, does not obey, and does not pay attention; rather he is arrogant. Another is the obstinate one, who listens but does not obey. He has knowledge of what Allah revealed and of Allah's limits, but he does not obey. They say, "We hear and we disobey"; we ask Allah for well-being. The third category listens and obeys. These are the believers, who say "We hear and we obey." But even so, do they seek facilitation after submission and obedience?

The answer: Yes, they seek facilitation when possible. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that the pots in which donkey meat had been cooked be broken, they said: "Shall we wash them?" He said: "Or that" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4196) and Muslim (123), from Salamah ibn al-Akwa']. They did not defy him; they only sought leniency. Seeking leniency does not contradict submission. But if they had said, "We will not do it," that would undoubtedly be disobedience. The believers say "We hear and we obey," and yet they may ask for leniency.

﴿And they say, "We hear and we obey"﴾. Allah said in His Book: ﴿And do not be like those who say, "We hear," while they do not hear. Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason. And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾ [al-Anfal 21–23].

**A student:** What is the difference between seeking leniency and asking in general, as in His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made apparent to you, would distress you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 101]?

**The Shaykh:** These people ask about things about which Allah has revealed no ruling, saying: "Is this forbidden? Is this obligatory?" and similar. Then Allah may reveal prohibition or obligation, and it grieves them, because it was made obligatory upon them due to their questioning and their obstinacy. This is what happened to the Children of Israel when Musa said to them: "Slaughter a cow." They said: ﴿Ask your Lord to make clear to us what it is﴾ [al-Baqarah 68]. When he informed them, they said: ﴿Ask your Lord to make clear to us what its color is﴾ [al-Baqarah 69] — when he informed them, they said: ﴿Ask your Lord to make clear to us what it is﴾ in its work. The first concerned its age, the second its color, and the third its work. They made it difficult, so Allah made it difficult for them. Had they slaughtered a cow from the beginning, the matter would have been easy.

**A student:** Regarding the reading of the Book: could we not say that "the Book" (*al-kitab*) and faith in the Qur'an entails faith in the books?

**The Shaykh:** We cannot say that, because the two readings explain each other. When the plural was joined in the second reading, it became known that the singular in the first reading is meant as a plural, and so that all the words together indicate plurality.

**A student:** The Prophet's (ﷺ) saying in Sahih al-Bukhari: "Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3395) and Muslim (2377/167), from Ibn 'Abbas] (...).

**The Shaykh:** No. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said that when he saw the dispute that had arisen between the Ansar and the Jews. He feared that a strife might occur, so he said: "Do not prefer me over this one," because this could be interpreted as partisanship, as though you, O Ansar, or you, O Arabs, were partisan for the Arab Prophet rather than for the truth.

**The student:** Does one who does not know these rulings, who does not know some of the rulings in the Qur'an, get described as not believing in the Qur'an?

**The Shaykh:** Yes, he is not a believer with complete faith, and he is given the description that he deserves, as long as his neglect of this specific act does not necessitate disbelief, in which case he would be a disbeliever.

* * *

**A student:** ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah 286].

**The Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes﴾. First: His saying ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾. What is meant here by *taklif* (burden)?

**A student:** Imposition (*al-ilzam*).

**The Shaykh:** Imposition. And *wus'* (capacity) means?

**The student:** Ability (*al-taqah*).

**The Shaykh:** In the sense of ability. Well done. Is this negation *kawni* (a matter of cosmic decree), meaning *qadari* (by divine decree), or *shar'i* (legal)?

**The student:** *Shar'i* (legal).

**The Shaykh:** *Shar'i*.

**The student:** Because Allah, glorified and exalted, in His mercy and grace, has not burdened us except with what we can bear.

**The Shaykh:** Yes. He said: ﴿It will have what it has earned and it will bear what it has earned﴾. What is the difference between *kasabat* and *iktasabat*?

**A student:** The difference...

**The Shaykh:** Yes, go ahead.

**A student:** *Ma kasabat*: what good it has earned, and *ma iktasabat*: what...

**The Shaykh:** What evil.

**The student:** Yes, *la-ha ma kasabat* from...

**The Shaykh:** That is, *kasaba* and *iktasaba* have the same meaning, but they are distinguished by what they are connected to: *laha* and *alayha*. Do you agree?

**The student:** No, Shaykh, there is another difference.

**The Shaykh:** Then what is it?

**The student:** That *kasabat* is used for good deeds and acts of obedience, and *iktasabat* for sins; this is what the reality indicates, that is the meaning.

**The Shaykh:** So the meaning is that there is a difference between them. There is an opinion that they have the same meaning, and an opinion that there is a difference between them.

**The student:** They are not the same meaning; they must say that it depends on what they are connected to.

**The Shaykh:** Yes, they have the same meaning, and what specifies the meaning is what they are connected to. And the second opinion?

**The student:** That the root of the word has a difference.

**The Shaykh:** Then what is the difference?

**The student:** That *kasb* is from good deeds, equal to good deeds.

**The Shaykh:** Why?

**The student:** Because changing the form of a word is only done to change its meaning.

**The Shaykh:** That is not apparent!

**A student:** Shaykh, this verb takes *al-lam* (ل), and the verb takes *ala* (على). When it takes *al-lam*, in the sense of (...) His saying, and when it takes *ala*, like His saying: ﴿And if you do evil, it is against yourselves﴾ [al-Isra' 7].

**The Shaykh:** Yes, ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself; and whoever does evil, it is against himself﴾ [Fussilat 46]? That is what the brother said, and he also said it.

**The student:** *Ma kasaba* differs from *iktasaba*. *Iktasaba* is of the form *if'talaa*, which indicates effort and exertion, whereas *kasaba* happens with the slightest cause.

**The Shaykh:** Well done.

**The student:** As for *iktisab*, it does not occur except through deliberate action.

**The Shaykh:** Yes, correct. It also occurs from one person on behalf of another: a good deed can occur from one person on behalf of another, unlike *iktisab*. For example, if a man steals and says, "O Allah, place its burden upon so-and-so," does it take effect?

**The students:** No.

**The Shaykh:** But if he gives charity and says, "O Allah, make it for so-and-so," does it take effect?

**The students:** It takes effect.

**The Shaykh:** His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes﴾. What is the difference between forgetting (*nisyan*) and error (*khata'*)?

His saying: ﴿We make no distinction between any one of them﴾ [al-Baqarah 136]: the negation of distinction here is by what?

**A student:** We make no distinction among them, meaning among them in conveying and in confirming, the conveying of the message, or the truthfulness of the one who conveys it.

**The Shaykh:** What is the meaning of conveying the message?

**The student:** (...) The messengers, I mean...

**The Shaykh:** And what is the meaning of "we make no distinction"? Distinction is by our action, not by theirs.

**The student:** I mean we make no distinction among them, among these messengers, in conveying the message, meaning all of them are confirmed, or in the creed itself, or in what the Sharia of Allah brought. The creed is one.

**The Shaykh:** Yes.

**The student:** We make no distinction in confirming that they are all from Allah, with all His messages. So we believe in every messenger who came...

**The Shaykh:** In the validity of their message, in the truthfulness of their reports, and in accepting what they reported. But as for following?

**The student:** Following.

**The Shaykh:** Then we follow Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. And as for ranking?

**The student:** Then Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Those messengers — We preferred some of them over others﴾ [al-Baqarah 253].

**The Shaykh:** So we rank some of them over others, is that right or not?

**The student:** Yes.

**The Shaykh:** So we make no distinction in four matters... no, we make no distinction in three matters: in the validity of their message, in the truthfulness of their reports, and in accepting what they brought. As for following, we follow Muhammad (ﷺ). Do we distinguish among them in ranking? The answer: Yes.

His saying: ﴿And they say, "We hear and we obey; [we seek] Your forgiveness"﴾. "Ghufranaka": what is its grammatical analysis (*i'rab*)?

**A student:** A verb.

**The Shaykh:** Have you not studied grammar?! It seems you have no kinship with Sibawayh! From where did you say it is a verb?!

**A student:** A verbal noun (*masdar*).

**The Shaykh:** Yes, but what is its *i'rab*?

**The student:** In the accusative.

**The Shaykh:** Yes.

**The student:** An object of a deleted verb whose estimated form is "we ask."

**The Shaykh:** Yes, its estimated form is "we ask You for Your forgiveness." Correct. Forgiveness (*al-maghfirah*): what is forgiveness?

**The student:** Forgiveness means concealing the sin and overlooking it.

**The Shaykh:** And overlooking it, concealing the sin and overlooking it. What is the evidence for what you said from the standpoint of derivation?

**A student:** *Al-maghfirah*, *al-ghafr*, and *al-ghufran*.

**The Shaykh:** No.

**The student:** That is, its meaning in language is covering.

**The Shaykh:** Subhan Allah!!

**The student:** That *al-maghfirah* comes from *al-mighfar*.

**The Shaykh:** From *al-mighfar*.

**The student:** What the fighter wears to protect himself.

**The Shaykh:** To protect himself from arrows, and it contains concealment and protection. What is the evidence from the Sharia, or from the text, that forgiveness means concealment and overlooking? Is this evidence from language, or evidence from the text?

**A student:** The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When He is alone with the servant on the Day of Resurrection..."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verse 285–286 (part 3 of 7):

* The Shaykh: "Indeed Allah will take His believing servant aside and make him acknowledge his sins"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4685) and Muslim (2768 / 52) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, with similar wording.]].
* The student: "Then He will say: I concealed them from you in the world, and I forgive them for you now."
* The Shaykh: Correct, "I concealed them from you in the world, and I forgive them for you today."
Regarding His words ﴿وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ ("and to You is the final return"): does "al-masir" mean the Day of Resurrection, or is there something more general than that?
* Student: "And to You is the final return" is general; everything returns to Allah, and it includes the Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: Well said. It includes the Day of Resurrection and other things; the return of creation is to Allah in this world and in the Hereafter.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the reward of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned.﴾ Then He says: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes.﴾ This sentence is a quotation of a verb of saying that has been omitted; that is, [it means] "Say: Our Lord," or it refers back to His words ﴿The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord﴾ and ﴿They say, "We hear and we obey"﴾; they said: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes.﴾ The point is that this sentence here is a quotation of an omitted verb of saying.

His words ﴿Our Lord﴾ are a vocative from which the particle of calling (yā') has been dropped, for brevity and conciseness of speech, and for seeking blessing by beginning with the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Our Lord﴾. They invoked His lordship (rubūbiyyah) as a means of approach, because the rabb is the Creator, the Owner, the Governor. Here they ask Allah for something, and giving this thing is among the matters pertaining to lordship. For this reason you find, in most of the Qur'an, supplication linked with lordship, because giving is an act, and every act's connection is to what? To lordship.

In His words ﴿Our Lord﴾ there is, clearly, the expression of tenderness, of manifesting need and poverty. Whoever attributes the lordship of Allah to himself in this way undoubtedly manifests his need of this Lord, and that he is a servant, a worshipper, humbled before this Lord.
