﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes.﴾ Accountability for a sin means being requited for it. Man is subject to forgetting and to error, and how much he forgets and errs!

Forgetting (nisyān) is the heart's lapse from something known. A person knows a thing and then it escapes him; we call this forgetting. For example, if I asked you, "What did you do yesterday?" and you said, "By Allah, I forgot." You are an agent, but you forgot. So the definition of forgetting is: the heart's lapse from something known. This is forgetting.

Error (khaṭa') is committing a disobedience, or in more general terms a violation, unintentionally; or, if you wish: a violation without intending to violate. This includes ignorance, for the ignorant person who commits what he has been forbidden has committed a violation without intending to violate, whether he is ignorant of the ruling or of the circumstance; he is included in His words ﴿or if we make mistakes﴾. Was this supplication answered? The answer is yes: Allah the Exalted said, "I have done so"[[Recorded by Muslim (126 / 200) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]], meaning He will not hold us to account either for forgetting or for error.

Know that it is said akhṭa'a, and it is said khaṭi'a. What is the active participle of the first?
* Student: khāṭi' (خاطئ).
* The Shaykh: No, it is mukhṭi' (مُخطئ), and from the second it is khāṭi' (خاطِئ). The triliteral form of this verb denotes one who commits a violation with intent to violate, and the quadriliteral denotes one who commits a violation without intent to violate. For example, a man who does a sin knowing it but intending it, we call him khāṭi'; and one who does it without intending it, we call him mukhṭi'. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿a lying, sinful forelock﴾ [al-'Alaq 16], meaning one who commits the violation deliberately. Here He said ﴿if we make mistakes﴾ (akhṭa'nā), and He said: ﴿and there is no blame upon you for what you have made a mistake in﴾ [al-Ahzab 5], meaning committing a violation without intending to violate. Allah the Exalted said, "I have done so."

﴿Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us﴾. We say regarding ﴿Our Lord﴾ what we said about the first, in terms of its grammatical analysis, its idafah (annexation), and the benefit of the annexation. But He said ﴿and do not burden us﴾, using the particle wa (and) to indicate that this sentence is conjoined to the one before it. The vocative was repeated seeking blessing through this noble Name and drawing near to Allah the Exalted, because that is one of the causes of the answering of supplication.

﴿And do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us﴾. ﴿Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden (iṣr)﴾: the iṣr is a heavy thing that weighs upon a person, whether of obligations or punishments.

And ﴿those before us﴾ had great obligations and were burdened with great punishments. For example, it was said to the Children of Israel who worshipped the calf, when it came to repentance: "We will not accept your repentance until you kill yourselves." Do you understand? This is without doubt a great obligation; they were ordered to be in darkness, each one taking a knife or dagger, and to strike whoever was in front of him, whether his father, his son, his brother, or his uncle. This without doubt contains a great iṣr and a heavy burden. As for us, it was said to us: ﴿except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good﴾ [al-Furqan 70]; even in shirk: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery—and whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation, except for those who repent﴾ [al-Furqan 68–70]. So Allah—to Him belong praise and grace—has not burdened us with an iṣr as He burdened those before us. The fats were forbidden to them: ﴿And for those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws; and of the cattle and sheep We prohibited to them their fat, except what their backs carry or the entrails or what is mixed with bone. That was their due for their rebellion. And indeed, We are truthful﴾ [al-An'am 146]. And He said: ﴿He makes lawful for them the good things﴾ [al-A'raf 157]. The Christians were prevented from taking retribution for a soul; it was said to them that if a killing occurs among you, retaliation is not permitted, and pardon is obligatory with no retaliation. This without doubt may involve humiliation of the self: that a person sees the killer of his father or his son walking in the market, and has been compensated for the most precious of people only with a few dirhams or the like. This is a degradation for the self.

And it was said to the Jews: there is no path for you to pardon the killer; let him be killed, even if he is the dearest person to you; kill him, and there is no path to pardon. This involves hardship for the self, does it not?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Perhaps someone kills your son, or a person who is among the dearest to you, perhaps dearer to you than your son, and you are told: kill him, kill him, as an obligation. As for us—to Allah belongs praise—it has been said to us: ﴿O you who have believed, retribution is prescribed for you in cases of murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever is pardoned by his brother [i.e., the victim's heir] in any [part] of it, then grant him [what is] acceptable and pay him with good conduct﴾ [al-Baqarah 178]. The door of pardon has been opened for us; indeed, we have been encouraged to pardon when it brings reform: ﴿So whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward is with Allah﴾ [al-Shura 40].

If you reflect on many things, you will find that Allah the Exalted has lightened this ummah and removed from it the burdens that were upon those before them.

﴿as You placed upon those before us﴾ [al-Baqarah 286]: who are they? The Jews, the Christians, and others among mankind; this includes everyone, all the previous nations.

﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾: is the intended meaning of the cosmic matters, or of the legislative matters, or both?
* Student: Both.
* The Shaykh: If you say both, there is a difficulty with what preceded: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾. We said its meaning is that Allah does not legally burden a soul beyond its capacity, and this is a statement of fact, and a statement of fact must be actual, must be actual. If it is actual, then the supplication in your words ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾ becomes superfluous, with no need for it, because from the outset ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾; so it is lifted from us from the start. In that case the meaning is: Our Lord, do not burden us with what we cannot bear, legally or by decree; not in terms of the origin of the law, but in terms of the state of the servant. Sometimes a person experiences something that prevents him from performing an act of obedience and he cannot bear it, due to illness or otherwise. If someone says: yes, this occurs, but in such a state Allah does not burden you with what you cannot do. The Prophet ﷺ said to 'Imran ibn Husayn: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then lying on your side"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari no. 1117 from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn.]], and Allah the Exalted said regarding fasting: ﴿And whoever is ill or on a journey, then an equal number of other days﴾ [al-Baqarah 185]. It has been lifted from you and you were not burdened with it. So the answer, and Allah knows best, is to say: if the obligation is lifted from you in this matter due to inability, then this means you ask Allah to complete for you the reward, to complete for you the reward accrued by this act that you cannot perform. This is the benefit of the supplication not to be burdened with what you cannot bear in legislative matters; for when the burden is removed, the person is as if he had performed it, so he does not bear the responsibility for it, and then the reward is written for him.

If someone says: according to this meaning, there is also an objection to you from His words ﷺ: "Whoever falls ill or travels, there is written for him what he used to do while healthy and resident"[[Recorded by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf no. 10901, and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat no. 236, from the hadith of Abu Musa.]]. A person unable to perform the worship he used to do in health, if he falls ill, has the full reward of the worship written for him; so is the supplication in this regard also superfluous, with no benefit?

We say: the answer to that is that although the Messenger ﷺ reported this, it may not be easily attainable for me, either because of a lack of sincere intention and determination, or for some other reason. It is true that the Messenger ﷺ said these words: "Whoever falls ill or travels," but this does not apply to each individual specifically, just as we all know that every believer enters Paradise, yet does this apply to each individual specifically? It cannot apply to each specific individual except one to whom the Messenger ﷺ has testified. So the benefit of the supplication here is that you ask Allah to fulfill what the Messenger ﷺ reported.

As for what we cannot bear from cosmic matters, its matter is clear, is it not? What we cannot bear of cosmic matters is clear. Pay attention! A person's asking that Allah not burden him with what he cannot bear includes two things: first, that this thing be averted from him so that it never befalls him at all; and second, that Allah strengthen him to bear it, so that it falls within his capacity. Pay attention! ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾: we say it includes two matters: that Allah not burden you with it at all, meaning He repels it from you; or, if He burdens you with it, He lightens it for you so that it falls within your capacity. For example, what cosmic matters fall outside capacity? Such as a person's oppression: someone wrongs you in your property or your body, and compels you to dig ten meters in one hour and carry away the mud in its entirety; he dominates you, saying: do it, or else imprisonment for life or execution. Is there capacity for this? There is no capacity: ten meters in an hour? Perhaps the ground is hard. This is beyond our capacity, so you ask Allah not to let anyone dominate you so as to burden you with what you cannot bear; or that Allah, in His wisdom, may send down upon you an illness that makes even movement difficult for you, is that not so? Or perhaps Allah tests you with difficulty in urination, or difficulty in defecation, or similar matters beyond your capacity. We now—to Allah belong praise and grace—say, speaking of the blessing of Allah: eating and drinking are easy for us; we eat wholesomely and pleasantly, and likewise elimination. But some people are tested so that they cannot eat, cannot drink, cannot find eating or drinking palatable; another person does these but finds elimination of them difficult. All of this falls under your words: ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾. So what we cannot bear of legislative obligations, and what else? And of the decreed matters.

Here let us look at the views of Sibawayh's school and the i'rab of ﴿مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ﴾ (i'rab: grammatical analysis).
* Student: ﴿مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ﴾ is in the place of the direct object (mafʿūl bihi) in the accusative.
* The Shaykh: The direct object of what?
* The student: ﴿تُؤَاخِذْنَا﴾.
* The Shaykh: No, ﴿تُؤَاخِذْنَا﴾ how?
* The student: ﴿وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا﴾.
* The Shaykh: The first object, or the second, or the third, or the fourth?
* The student: The second object.
* The Shaykh: The second, good.
* The student: ﴿لَا﴾, a negation particle.
* The Shaykh: Negating what?
* The student: Negating ﴿طَاقَةَ﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but what type of negation is it? So you have two grades?
* Student: Our Lord, and do not burden us.
* The Shaykh: No, no, a negation.
* Student: A negation of the genus (lā nāfiyah lil-jins).
* The Shaykh: Good, and what does it govern?
* The student: It governs like inna, yes.
* The Shaykh: Wait, what does inna govern?
* The student: Inna makes the noun accusative and the predicate nominative, and ﴿طَاقَةَ﴾ is its noun.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: It is built on the fatḥah in the place of accusative.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: And the prepositional phrase is in the place of nominative as the predicate.
* The Shaykh: Which one? ﴿بِهِ﴾ or ﴿لَنَا﴾?
* The student: ﴿بِهِ﴾.
* The Shaykh: And ﴿لَنَا﴾?
* The student: The first; the first prepositional phrase ﴿مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا﴾, meaning: what has no capacity existing for us.
* The Shaykh: An adjective to ṭāqah? Yes, good.

Then He said: ﴿And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us; You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah 286], and so on to the end. Since a human being has states, indeed two states: a state that has passed and a state yet to come. The state that has passed may involve neglecting the performance of commands, or committing what is forbidden; and the state yet to come is known to Allah. He said: ﴿and forgive us﴾, which is in contrast to committing what is forbidden, meaning: forgive us the sins we have committed, forgive us the sins we have done. A person is never free of sin: "Every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent often"[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi no. 2499, and Ibn Majah no. 4251, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]. Sins may be in the heart, in the tongue, or in the limbs; or a person may have neglected a command, failing in something commanded. Its counterpart is His words ﴿pardon us﴾; so pardon is in contrast to falling short in what is commanded, and forgiveness is in contrast to what? Committing what is forbidden.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 2, verses 285–286 (part 4 of 7):**

﴿وَارْحَمْنَا﴾ in the future, meaning: show us Your mercy, so that we do not fall into committing what is forbidden or into negligence in what is commanded. This is better than the view of some exegetes (mufassirun) that these phrases are for emphasis, because pardon (al-'afw) and forgiveness (al-maghfirah) both mean erasing sins, while mercy means attaining what is sought. We say: No. A person has two states: a state that has passed and a state that is yet to come. In the past state, he may have either fallen short in what was commanded, or committed what was forbidden.

﴿اعْفُ عَنَّا﴾ corresponds to falling short in what is commanded. ﴿اغْفِرْ لَنَا﴾ corresponds to committing what is forbidden. ﴿ارْحَمْنَا﴾ refers to the future, so that You preserve us from what is forbidden and from neglecting what is commanded. Thus this supplication is comprehensive, one of the most comprehensive forms of supplication.

Suppose a man falls short in prayer, for example by not praying at the beginning of its time. We say this is falling short in what is commanded. If he turns his head during the prayer, this is committing what is forbidden, because the Messenger ﷺ forbade turning around in prayer[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, no. (7595), and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, no. (5275), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. Although turning here is disliked (makruh), it is still prohibited.

﴿أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا﴾ The sentence here is a declarative sentence (jumlah khabariyyah), composed of a subject and a predicate, both of which are definite. Do you agree with this or not? Do you agree with me?

* Student: No, only a subject.
* Student: No, teacher, a subject and a predicate.
* Shaykh: The sentence is a nominal declarative sentence composed of a subject and a predicate, both definite, right?
* Students: Right.
* Shaykh: Yes, correct. The scholars of rhetoric (balaghah) have said that a sentence composed of a subject and predicate that are both definite conveys exclusivity (al-hasr). So His saying ﴿أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا﴾ is not like saying "You are a protector for us." ﴿أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا﴾ indicates that there is no protector for us other than You, right? Now, "You are a protector for us" does not indicate this. It indicates that You are one of the protectors. You say to someone: "You are my beloved" (anta habibi), and you say: "You are a beloved to me" (anta habib li). Is there a difference between them or not? Yes. The first one indicates what? Exclusivity. The second does not indicate exclusivity. You say to a disbeliever: "You are an enemy to me" (anta 'aduwwun li), which does not indicate exclusivity. You say: "You are my enemy" (anta 'aduwwi), which indicates exclusivity. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said about the hypocrites: ﴿هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ فَاحْذَرْهُمْ﴾ [al-Munafiqun 4] ("They are the enemy, so beware of them"). It is as if He said: there is no enemy other than them. And there is no doubt that the enmity of the hypocrite toward the believer is more severe than the enmity of the disbeliever toward the believer, or not? Is that correct? Teacher, the hypocrite comes to you and says, "Welcome, dear brother, the believer, the righteous one." This is the problem. Yes indeed. We say: the enmity of the hypocrite toward the believer is more severe than the enmity of the disbeliever, because the disbeliever shows his enmity and we guard against him. But the real calamity is this one who fears Allah (in appearance) and shows that he is a friend while he is an enemy. So ﴿أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا﴾ is a declarative sentence that conveys exclusivity, or not? Yes, it conveys exclusivity. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَأَنَّ الْكَافِرِينَ لَا مَوْلَى لَهُمْ﴾ [Muhammad 11] ("That is because Allah is the protector of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector"), even though their supporters support them, but they do not benefit them.

﴿أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا﴾ What is the meaning of al-mawla? Does mawla mean the helper (al-nasir), or the one who manages all our affairs? The second, the second is better, because the second is general and comprehensive. That is: You are the one who manages all our affairs. Part of Your guardianship over us is that You have not burdened us except with what we can bear, that You are our refuge, our shelter, the object of our supplication, our desire, and our fear, and that You have legislated for us this easy religion. Everything that follows from this guardianship is included in His saying ﴿أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا﴾.

Then He said: ﴿فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ The fa' here is for consequence (li al-tafri'), meaning: by Your special guardianship, help us against the disbelieving people. The guardianship of Allah over creation is of two kinds: special guardianship and general guardianship. Special guardianship is Allah's guardianship over the believers, and general guardianship is His guardianship over every individual. Allah is the guardian (wali) of every individual in the sense of managing affairs, or not? As He said: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمْ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ (61) ثُمَّ رُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلَاهُمُ الْحَقِّ أَلَا لَهُ الْحُكْمُ وَهُوَ أَسْرَعُ الْحَاسِبِينَ﴾ [al-An'am 61–62] ("Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fall short. Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, judgment belongs to Him, and He is the swiftest of reckoners."). This is the general sense. The special is: ﴿اللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ [al-Baqarah 257] ("Allah is the guardian of those who believe") and ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ [Muhammad 11]. And this special guardianship also has an even more special form, which is Allah's guardianship of His Messenger, such as: ﴿أَنْتَ وَلِيِّي فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ [Yusuf 101] ("You are my guardian in this world and the Hereafter"), and His saying: ﴿وَإِنْ تَظَاهَرَا عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلَاهُ﴾ [al-Tahrim 4] ("And if you two support each other against him, then indeed Allah is his protector"). He alone, the Mighty and Majestic, is his protector, and the angels, and so on: ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ("and Gabriel and the righteous of the believers").

So we say: guardianship is of two types. Then we say: ﴿فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ "Help us against them," meaning: make victory ours over them. Victory over the disbelievers occurs by two means: by proof and clarification, and also by the sword and weapons. It occurs by sword and weapons. As for sword and weapons, it is clear. As for proof and clarification, a disbeliever and a Muslim may meet and debate a matter of creed. If Allah does not grant the Muslim victory, he is humiliated, and in this there is humiliation for him and for the religion he follows. This kind of victory through proof and clarification is specifically required regarding the hypocrites. Victory over the hypocrite is not by weapons, but by proof and clarification, because the hypocrite shows that he is with you and that he is one of you. For this reason, when the Messenger ﷺ asked permission to kill the hypocrites, he said: «لَا يَتَحَدَّثُ النَّاسُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا يَقْتُلُ أَصْحَابَهُ» ("Let not people say that Muhammad kills his companions")[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari, no. (4905), and Muslim, no. (2584 (63)), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]]. Outwardly, the hypocrite is like you. And it is a problem: if we unleash our swords against the hypocrites, we may kill one who is a believer, because what is in the heart is not known, except for one who has openly displayed his hypocrisy and it has become clear. According to the preponderant view, this person is invited to Islam. If he embraces Islam and his good faith becomes known, he is left alone; otherwise, not. Some scholars said: the hypocrite's faith is not accepted, we do not accept his faith. Why? He said: Because originally he shows what? He shows faith and that he is a believer. If we seize him and say: "Come, embrace faith, or we will kill you," what will he say? He will say that he is a believer, and there is no problem. I embrace it. I say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and I establish prayer. Will you not leave me alone when I come with you every day? Yes. I give zakah. Fine, and we give you what we gave you. I fast. Yes, it is a problem. But if it is known with certainty that he is a hypocrite, such that when he meets those who believe he says, "I believe," and when he is alone with his devils he says, "I am with you; we are only mocking them, playing with them," if we know this and it is established, we kill him. But is his repentance accepted? The well-known position in the school is that his repentance is not accepted and that he is killed. If he is sincere in his repentance, his reward is with Allah, his reward is with Allah. If he is lying, then the killing has taken place in its proper place or not? The second view: if we know for certain that he has repented, we lift the killing from him, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ فِي الدَّرْكِ الْأَسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ نَصِيرًا (145) إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا﴾ [al-Nisa' 145–146] ("Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper, except those who repent"). But notice that in the repentance of the hypocrite, conditions are mentioned: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَأَصْلَحُوا وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِاللَّهِ وَأَخْلَصُوا دِينَهُمْ لِلَّه﴾ ("except those who repent, amend, hold fast to Allah, and make their religion sincerely for Allah"). Four conditions. When they are fulfilled, those are with the believers.

And His saying: ﴿انْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾. Does "the disbelievers" here mean the disbelievers among the children of Adam, or even the devils? It includes both: it includes the disbelievers among the children of Adam and the disbelievers among the devils, because the devil is undoubtedly a disbeliever. So in this supplication there is a request for Your victory over the disbeliever among the children of Adam and over the disbeliever among the devils. It is thus equivalent to seeking refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan.

* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: There are people who commit what is forbidden, but in performing what is commanded they are among the best of people. There are people now who deal in usury, yet they are among the most eager people for prayer, zakah, fasting, and Hajj.
* Student: (...) Committing what is forbidden.
* Shaykh: But it is said that neglecting what is commanded and committing what is forbidden are both neglecting an obligation of abstention. They are interrelated, but there is a difference between them: what is commanded is what is sought to be performed, and what is forbidden is what is sought to be avoided and left out. This is the difference, or are they all interrelated?
* Student: Is there sin on the one who turns during prayer?
* Shaykh: No, there is no sin unless he turns his whole body. As for turning with his head, there is no sin, but it is disliked unless there is a need.
* Student: Teacher, some people speak about the Christian faith and say: "Their law says: if someone strikes you on your cheek, turn to him the other cheek," and other things that may be legislated among them. Is it permissible to disparage their law in this way, even if (...)?
* Shaykh: No, in terms of it being deficient—relative to Allah's legislation, it is not deficient, because it agrees with wisdom. But relative to it being fetters and burdens upon them, when we consider it compared with the Islamic law, it becomes deficient.
* Student: But should this statement be made or not?
* Shaykh: By Allah, we do not know. It depends on the intention of the one who says it. If his intention is to disparage and vilify their law, this is not permissible, because their law, in its time, was the law of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ We have taken its benefits. Did we discuss them? Yes, we will discuss the last verse.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ﴾ I think we also discussed its beginning?
He said: ﴿رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا﴾ What is the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا﴾?
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: The vocative particle has been deleted from it. What is the benefit and wisdom of deleting the vocative particle?
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: For brevity, and for seeking blessing by beginning with the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Good. In supplication, appeal is most often made by invoking the station of lordship (rububiyyah). Why?
* Student: Because lordship includes Allah's action and includes everything that surrounds a human being.
* Shaykh: Correct, because the answering of supplication belongs to matters connected with action, with Allah's action, and this is more connected with lordship than with other aspects of tawhid.
His saying: ﴿إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا﴾. What is the difference between them?
* Student: Forgetting is the heart's distraction from something known. As for error, it is doing something or violating something without intending to violate it.
* Shaykh: Violating without intending to violate it.
His saying: ﴿لَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا﴾ ﴿إِصْرًا﴾?
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: A heavy burden. Yes? Good.
﴿كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا﴾ And what was it that was laid upon those before us?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: When they were commanded to repent from worshipping the calf, that they should kill themselves. And this nation?
* Student: This nation, when it wants to repent, seeks forgiveness from Allah and repents with sincere repentance (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. Good. His saying: ﴿لَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ﴾ ﴿مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا﴾ Is this about legal obligations, or about trials and divine decrees?
* Student: Both.
* Shaykh: Good. How is that in the first case, legal obligations?
* Student: That He does not burden us with what we cannot bear of acts of worship, of all legislated acts of worship.
* Shaykh: Good. And the decree (al-qadar)?
* Student: They say: do not test us with matters we cannot endure.
* Shaykh: Like what?
* Student: All calamities and misfortunes.
* Shaykh: Like, give an example.
* Student: Like killing.
* Shaykh: Yes: trials, wars, hunger, fear, and other things.
﴿وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا﴾ What is the difference between these three supplicatory clauses?
* Student: Pardon is passing over a sin.
* Shaykh: No, I mean, what is the object of these three things? Pardon is related to what?
* Student: To sins.
* Shaykh: All of them to sins?
* Student: Pardon relates to falling short in obedience, that He pardon us for what we fell short in obeying Him. Forgiveness occurs in error or in committing sins.
* Shaykh: Correct.
* Student: ﴿وَارْحَمْنَا﴾ in the Hereafter.
* Shaykh: In the future.
* Student: In the future.
* Shaykh: Correct. So pardon and forgiveness are for what has passed, pardon relates to neglect of an obligation, forgiveness to violating what is forbidden, and mercy in the future, such that it preserves us from sins and transgressions.
His saying: ﴿أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿مَوْلَانَا﴾?
* Student: The meaning of His saying ﴿مَوْلَانَا﴾ is that we have no protector other than Allah.
* Shaykh: Yes, but what is the meaning of mawla?
* Student: The one who supports us and is a helper for us against (...).
* Shaykh: The one who manages our affairs, the one who supports us against others. Good. Does this sentence convey exclusivity?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: So that you know both parties.
* Shaykh: So that you know both parties. Can you not give an example that shows us this? You have the word "wajid" (one who finds) and "kathir" (much) (...), but we want one only. We want from "wajid" that you delete the point that is in the original.
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: No, an example from yourself, not necessarily from the Qur'an or the Sunnah.
* Student: If someone says: "I am the Muslim" (...).
* Shaykh: "I am the Muslim," meaning and others are not Muslim.
* Student: (...) or "You, for example, are my beloved" (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, I fear he says, "You are my beloved," that he is the owner of the restaurant!! In any case, if I say for example: "You are the one who strikes" or "You are a striker," or not?
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: Where is which one?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is not wrong. Good. His saying: ﴿فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ The fa' and what does it mean?
* Student: Consequence (ta'qib).
* Shaykh: Consequence? No.
* Student: Derivation (tafri').
* Shaykh: Derivation, meaning: because of Your guardianship we ask You to help us against the disbelieving people.

Let us take the benefits. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [al-Baqarah 285] and so on.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and is charged with believing in what was sent down to him, because His saying ﴿آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ﴾ is a declarative statement that requires it to be a description of him, if we do not say it means a command, is that right? Good. And we have already encountered in al-Bukhari that the Prophet ﷺ said: «أَشْهَدُ أَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ» ("I bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah") in the story of the debt of Jabir's father, may Allah be pleased with him[[Narrated by al-Bukhari, no. (5443), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, because of His saying: ﴿بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾. What is sent down is revelation, and speech is an attribute that can only subsist in a speaker; it cannot subsist on its own. Accordingly, the verse is evidence that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, the revelation sent down to Muhammad ﷺ.
* Also among its benefits: affirmation of Allah's exaltation (uluw), because descent (nuzul) only comes from above: ﴿بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
* Among its benefits: affirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ messengerhood in His saying: ﴿الرَّسُولُ﴾ and in His saying: ﴿بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾.
* Also among its benefits: the greatness of Allah's lordship and its special relation to the Messenger ﷺ, in that He said: ﴿بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾.
* And derived from this: that Allah, glorified and exalted, will help him, because special lordship requires that, especially since he will convey what was sent down to him from his Lord.

The benefits of this noble verse include: that the believers follow their Messenger ﷺ, since He said: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers﴾. The aspect of following: He mentioned the one believed in before mentioning the follower; He did not say "The Messenger and the believers believe in what was sent down to him." This shows that they are followers of the Messenger ﷺ and do not stand independently of him in a law of their own.

Another benefit: the stronger a person's faith in the Messenger ﷺ, the more intensely he follows him. The reason: He said: ﴿in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers﴾, meaning: they believed in what was sent down to Muhammad ﷺ from his Lord. Accordingly, whoever has stronger faith is more intense in following.

Another benefit: the faith of the Messenger ﷺ and the believers encompasses all the foundations of religion, by His saying: ﴿Each one believes in God, His angels, His books and His messengers﴾. Yes? ﴿Each one believes in God, His angels, His books and His messengers﴾.

A problem remains for us: He did not mention belief in the Last Day and belief in divine decree (qadar)?

The answer to that: it is included within belief in the books and the messengers, because belief in divine decree and belief in the Last Day are among the things brought by the books and the messengers, so they fall within belief in the messengers and belief in the books.

A benefit of the noble verse: the affirmation of the angels, by His saying: ﴿and His angels﴾. And the obligation to believe in them, by His saying: ﴿Each one believes in God and His angels﴾. We have already mentioned in the tafsir how one believes in them: that we believe in their names as far as we know them, in their attributes, in their deeds, and what else? In their functions, the particular tasks assigned to them, such as the scribes and the guardians of the children of Adam and what is similar to that, and the deeds they perform in a particular manner, such as those who glorify and prostrate and the like.

Another benefit of the noble verse: that belief in the messengers admits of no distinction. We do not say, for example: "We believe in Muhammad ﷺ but we do not believe in Jesus, because Jesus was from the Children of Israel." No, we do not distinguish between the messengers. We have already explained the meaning of His saying: ﴿We make no distinction﴾.

Another benefit of the noble verse: that among the qualities of the believers is hearing and obeying, by His saying: ﴿And they said: We hear and we obey﴾. We mentioned in the tafsir that people divide in this station into three categories: one who turns away, neither hearing nor obeying; the second, one who hears and obeys, the opposite; and the third, one who hears but does not obey, and this is worse than the first.

Another benefit of the noble verse: that every person is in need of God's forgiveness, by His saying: ﴿Your forgiveness﴾. So every person is in need of forgiveness, and even the Prophet ﷺ is in need of forgiveness. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ said: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God covers me with His mercy." [A hadith agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari, no. 5673, and Muslim, no. 2816 (73), from Abu Hurayrah.] And God Most High said: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory (1), that God may forgive you your past sin and what follows﴾ [al-Fath 1, 2]. Every person is in need of forgiveness. As for those among the scholars who held that the Messenger ﷺ never committed a sin, and that the seeking of forgiveness which he performed was only for teaching purposes, they have gone far astray; and likewise whoever said that the seeking of forgiveness which the Messenger used to perform was for the sins of his community. This too is an error, because God said to him: ﴿And seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and women﴾ [Muhammad 19]: He singled out his sin, then said: ﴿and for the believing men and women﴾. Know that a person may, after a sin, be of higher rank than he was before the sin, because before the sin he may have been complacent in his state, walking in what he was upon, thinking himself perfect and free of sins. When he sins and feels his sin, he returns to God, turns to Him in repentance, and humbles himself before Him, so his faith increases and his rank rises with God, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason God Most High said of Adam: ﴿Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray (121). Then his Lord chose him﴾ [Ta-Ha 121, 122]. He made the choosing come after this disobedience: "chose him," ﴿and He turned to him and guided him﴾. This often happens: when a person sins, he recognizes his own worth and that he is in need of God, returns to God, feels the wrong, increases his seeking of forgiveness, and his station after the sin becomes higher than his station before it.

A benefit of the noble verse: the affirmation that the return is to God, the Mighty and Majestic, in all things, by His saying: ﴿And to You is the return﴾. We have already mentioned in the tafsir that what is meant by this return is the return to God in the Hereafter and also the return to God in this world; He is the One who judges between people: ﴿And whatever you differ about, its judgment is with God﴾ [al-Shura 10].

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, to the end.

From this noble verse is derived the demonstration of God's mercy toward His servants, since He does not burden them except with what they are able to do. Had He willed to burden them with what they cannot do, He could have done so. If someone says: How could He do that when they cannot, and what is the benefit of commanding them to do something they cannot do? We say: the benefit is that He punishes them for not doing it. That is the benefit: if He burdened them with what they cannot do and they failed, He would punish them for that. But out of His mercy, Glorified and Exalted is He, what we cannot do we are not burdened with. This is a great principle of the foundations of the Sharia: ﴿God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, and it has parallels in the Qur'an and likewise in the Sunnah.

Another benefit: the affirmation of the well-known principle among the scholars, which is: "There is no obligation with incapacity, and no prohibition with necessity." Take note. However, if the obligation one is incapable of has a substitute, it is necessary to move to its substitute; if it has no substitute, it lapses. And if one is incapable of its substitute, and it has a substitute, it lapses. Is that correct or not? An example of that: if one is unable to purify with water, the obligation to purify with water lapses, but he moves to tayammum (dry ablution). If he is unable, it lapses too. If someone is a prisoner, shackled, unable to perform tayammum or wudu, we say: pray according to your condition, without wudu and without tayammum. Clear? Good.

A man kills a person by mistake. We tell him: you must free a slave. He says: I do not find one. You must fast two consecutive months. He says: I cannot. What do we say? It lapses from him, even if he has a great deal of money; he is not obliged to feed the poor.

A man had intercourse with his wife during the day in Ramadan. We tell him: free a slave. He says: I do not find one. Fast two consecutive months. He says: I cannot. Feed sixty poor persons. He says: I do not find any. What do we say? We say: there is nothing upon you. So the principle "there is no obligation with incapacity" is taken from this verse.

A man came when the row was full and he could not find a place to stand among the people. We say: pray alone behind the row, because the obligation of joining the row is what you are now unable to do, so it lapses from you.

A person who cannot pray standing in an obligatory prayer: we say, pray seated. He says: I cannot. Pray on your side. He says: I cannot, I have no movement at all. We say: pray with your heart. This principle, praise God, is consistent and never breaks.

As for prohibitions, we say: there is no prohibition with necessity, or there is no forbidden thing with necessity, but with a condition. Take note: the word "necessity" means that one cannot do without this prohibited thing. The second condition, along with it being unavoidable, is that the necessity be removed by it. If it does not remove the necessity, there is no benefit. Once you know that both conditions are required, what are they: that it cannot be done without by something else; and second, that the necessity is removed by it. Then there is no prohibition, and it becomes lawful for him.

A man was forced to eat carrion. Does he eat it?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Lawful? And he does not sin?

Students: And he does not sin.

* The Shaykh: He does not sin, because he has no other means, and because when he eats he benefits, and the necessity is removed.

A man was forced to treat himself with something prohibited?

* A student: It is not permitted.

* The Shaykh: It is not permitted. How?

* The students: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, it is not permitted. First, because he can do without it by means of something else, there are many other medicines; second, because if he treats himself with it, his necessity may be removed by it and he may be healed, and it may not be removed. So he would have committed a certain prohibition for the hope of an uncertain benefit. For this reason it is not permitted, in addition to the hadiths reported on this. Good. So does this break the principle or not? It does not break the principle, because it did not enter it at all so as to be a breach of it.

* A student: Say a person ate something, like (...).

* The Shaykh: First, this is forbidden (...). Is the question clear or not?

* The student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but he is now going to present an objection to our principle, its apparent intent: a man choked on a morsel, and could find nothing except wine, meaning the world was tight and he found only a cup of wine, and there was no cup of water?! But in any case, what do we do? He drinks of it only as much as will push down the morsel, because the condition is fulfilled: he cannot do without it, he has nothing else, and the necessity is removed by it. Clear?

* A student: And it does not break the principle, Shaykh, because this drink is not intended as a treatment, but only to push down the morsel.

* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, it does not fall under it.

A person who is in ihram needs to shave his head and is compelled to do so to remove harm. Is his shaving permitted or not? Yes, there is no prohibition with necessity; it is permitted. He brings a razor and shaves, at ease in mind. But God obligated him to a compensation of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice. How so? The scholars said: this one who violated the prohibition did not violate it out of necessity to himself, but to remove his harm through it. Therefore their jurisprudential principle is: whoever destroys something to remove harm from himself is not liable; and whoever destroys something to remove harm from himself through it is liable. Is this principle known? Whoever destroys something to remove his harm is not liable. If game attacks you while you are in ihram, and hunting game is forbidden to the one in ihram, is that not so? "O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram" [al-Ma'idah 95]. You fear for yourself, and that game cannot be repelled except by killing it, so you kill it: is there liability for you? No, because you removed its harm; it is the one that forfeited its sanctity by its harm. Clear?

If you are hungry and need to kill game to eat it, so you kill and eat it: your killing it is lawful, because you are compelled, but you must compensate for it. Why? Because you did not kill it to remove its harm, but to remove your harm through it, the harm and injury to you. When the one in ihram shaves his head to remove lice, here he did not shave the hair for the sake of the hair; the hair caused him no harm, but he shaved it for what? To remove his harm through it: because when he shaves it, the lice leave, he becomes clean, and there is no shade in which the lice can shelter, so he benefits. For this reason God obligated him to a compensation of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice, because he destroyed it to remove his harm through it. For this reason the jurists say: if a hair of the eye has grown inward and one plucks it with tweezers to remove the harm, is there liability? They say: no liability. This happens often, I think, though I do not know now how common it is. We used to know of it in the past in the eyelid: hairs emerge from inside it that harm the eye, and we often see them holding the man, then opening the eyelid like this with tweezers, and plucking the hairs. We say: this is to remove their harm, so there is no liability. This is based on the view that hair other than the head is not forbidden to remove in the state of ihram like head hair. We have already mentioned in the section on the prohibitions of ihram that the correct view is that the prohibition is specific to head hair only; as for other hair, there is no prohibition, and there is no evidence for prohibiting its removal in the state of ihram.

The summary now: from this noble verse, ﴿God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, we have derived two agreed principles: there is no obligation with incapacity, and there is no prohibition with necessity. But for the obligation we said: if it has a substitute, we move to its substitute; if we are unable, it lapses.

* A student: The second principle, Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: Yes, the second principle: there is no prohibition with necessity. But we said that one must know what necessity means. We said: necessity means that one cannot do without it, that is, without doing this prohibited thing, and it is required that the necessity be removed by it, otherwise not. Then we gave an incidental principle: if a person destroys something whose destruction is forbidden to him, while being compelled to it, we said: he is not sinful; there is no sin. But is there liability? There is detail: if he destroyed it to remove his harm, there is no liability; and if he destroyed it to remove his harm through it, he is liable. We have mentioned examples of this.

From the benefits of the noble verse: that a person does not bear the burden of another; by His saying: ﴿and upon it is what it has earned﴾. And that a person may benefit from the effort of another; by His saying: ﴿for it is what it has earned﴾, since ﴿for it is what it has earned﴾ includes what a person earned by his own deed and what he earned by the deed of another. As for sin, a person does not bear the sin of another.

If you say: there is an objection to you, because it is established from the Prophet ﷺ that "whoever establishes an evil practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts by it until the Day of Resurrection" [Muslim, no. 1017 (69), from Jarir ibn Abdullah]?

The answer: this is not an objection, because the one who first did it was followed by people, so their following him is among the effects of his deed; it is among the effects of his deed. For this reason he is the one who caused it, and the one who pointed to this forbidden deed, so he has earned it.

Some scholars used this verse to show that acts of worship do not reach the dead, as they also cited His saying: ﴿and that there is not for man except what he strove﴾ [al-Najm 39]. Is this inference sound? We say: yes, it is sound in their view, because God attributed the deed to its doer: ﴿for it is what it has earned﴾, and the acts of worship performed by another, the one who earned them is the other. So if a person prays and says: "O God, I pray on behalf of so-and-so, so grant its reward to him," they say: this does not benefit so-and-so, it does not benefit him. If he gives charity and says: "O God, if this charity of mine is for so-and-so, grant its reward to him," they say: it does not benefit, except for what the text has provided, because God says: ﴿for it is what it has earned﴾ and ﴿and that there is not for man except what he strove﴾.

But the correct view is otherwise: that when a person intends by a righteous deed that it be for another, that other benefits from it. We have evidence for this, among it: the hadith of Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, may Allah be pleased with him, "that he had a garden (mikhraf, i.e., an orchard), and he wished to give it in charity on behalf of his mother, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ about that. He said: 'Yes,' and permitted him to do so." [Related by Abu Dawud, no. 2882, and al-Tirmidhi, no. 669.]

Among it also: "that a man came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: O Messenger of God, my mother died suddenly, and I think that if she had spoken she would have given charity; shall I give charity on her behalf? He said: 'Yes.'" [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari, no. 1388, and Muslim, no. 1004 (51), from Aisha.]

Among it: the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "Whoever dies owing fasting, his guardian shall fast on his behalf." [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari, no. 1952, and Muslim, no. 1147 (153), from Aisha.]

Among it: "that a woman asked the Prophet ﷺ about her father, upon whom God's obligation had fallen, and he was unable to ride on a mount, and she asked his permission to perform Hajj on his behalf, and he permitted her." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari, no. 1513, and Muslim, no. 1334 (407), from Ibn Abbas.] The examples of this are many.

**Commentary of Ibn ʿUthaymin (Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-Karīm) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 285–286 (part 6 of 7)**

If they say: "We confine ourselves to what the text has stated, and we do not include what it has not stated," the answer is: these are specific cases (*qadāyā aʿyān*), and specific cases do not prevent their rulings from being extended to others by analogy (*qiyās*). For example, if a questioner had come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I recite some Qurʾān, or pray two rakʿahs, and dedicate it to my mother?" we would not know whether he would say no or not. Yet the evidence requires that he would say yes, because all of these are righteous deeds. There is no difference between charity, fasting, Hajj, recitation of the Qurʾān, and prayer. If they say, "Charity is a financial act, or a financial act of worship from which others benefit," we reply: Is Hajj a financial act of worship or a physical one? It is physical. Fasting is a physical act of worship, and yet the Lawgiver permitted it. The distinction between the physical and the financial has no evidence supporting it at all. In that case we say: if a person intends that the reward of a righteous deed be for someone, then he may do so, and it reaches that person and benefits him.

If someone asks: "If you say that, is it then legislated for us to dedicate the reward of what we have done to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" For example, what appears in some copies of the Qurʾān at the end of the book, a supplication for completing the Qurʾān: "O Allah, make the reward of what we have recited and read, and such and such, for the spirit of our master Muhammad (ﷺ), and for the spirits of the family of our master Muhammad, and for such and such." Is it legislated for us to say that a person should dedicate acts of devotion to the one who has the greatest right over him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?

The answer: No, it is never legislated. Why? Because whatever deed you do, its reward reaches the Messenger (ﷺ) whether you dedicate it or not, since he is the one who guided to this deed. So he has no need of it. And if you dedicate the reward of your deed to him, the reality is that you have deprived yourself of its reward, because the reward of this deed already belongs to the Messenger (peace be upon him). Therefore it is not legislated.

Is it legislated to dedicate the reward to one's relatives? Some scholars say: it is not legislated, because this was only reported in a specific case (*fī al-aṣl*, i.e., in the original report). We say to him: this is an error. What was reported in the original case is not a statement that gives a general ruling for the whole community. It is only a specific case: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah asked permission to dedicate that for his mother, and the other man asked permission for it to be for his mother. But what do you say about the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Whoever dies with fasting owed upon him, his guardian shall fast on his behalf"?[[Hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhārī no. (1952), and Muslim no. (1147 (153)), from ʿĀʾishah.]] It includes his mother, his father, his brother, his paternal uncle, and everyone who was responsible for his affairs. So restricting this to the two parents has no evidence.

If someone asks: "Is it legislated for me to dedicate the reward to relatives, whether parents or others?" The answer: No, it is not legislated. But it is among the permissible matters, which the Messenger (ﷺ) did not forbid. And although he did not forbid it, he guided to what is more important and more excellent, which is supplication, when he said: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: a continuing charity (ṣadaqah jāriyah), or knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him."[[Narrated by Muslim, no. (1631 (14)), from Abū Hurayrah.]] Now reflect on the context of the hadith: is it about deeds or not? It is about deeds: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end." Then he turned away from saying "or a righteous child who acts on his behalf" to saying "or a righteous child who prays for him." This is a clear indication that acting on behalf of others is not what is required of a person; supplication is better. That is why we do not find this to be common during the time of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, despite their eagerness for good and kindness. From this we know that what many people do today, dedicating acts of worship to the dead, and the fact that when someone dedicates an act of worship to the dead he performs it more diligently than when he performs it for himself, as is observed, shows that this is a misuse and a lack of understanding of the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* **Student:** Is it permissible to dedicate the reward (...) to one's parents while they are alive?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, it is permissible, except in matters that require that they perform the act themselves, such as prayer. For example, if someone says, "I will pray on behalf of my father because he is tired," that is not valid.
* **Student:** Shaykh, we said, O Shaykh, regarding ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, that if Allah willed, He could burden people beyond their capacity. But O Shaykh, we said elsewhere that Allah, glorified and exalted, does nothing except for a wisdom, based on His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insān 30].
* **The Shaykh:** Well said, yes.
* **Student:** So it means that burdening a person with what he cannot bear (...).
* **The Shaykh:** That has not happened. We do not go to that until we look at its aspect. We say: if He willed, and we mentioned the wisdom. We said the wisdom in that is that He would punish them if they refused.
* **Student:** The wisdom is that Allah, glorified and exalted, punishes them for it. But Allah, glorified and exalted, punishes the soul for something, meaning it cannot bear it. Allah, glorified and exalted, knows that it cannot bear it (...) justice.
* **The Shaykh:** For this reason it has become non-existent. For this reason we say it is one of Allah's favours upon us. That is, if we said that this is impossible, there would be no favour in it, and every indication of (...) a heavy obligation would become a matter with no favour. We say: there is favour in it.
* **Student:** Yes, favour in the sense of imposing worship.
* **The Shaykh:** Good. So it is by Allah's favour that He did not impose on the servant what he cannot bear.
* **Student:** But the favour returns to the perfection of Allah's justice, glorified and exalted.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes.
* **Student:** (...) impossible.
* **The Shaykh:** We say: it is impossible now.
* **Student:** The explanation of the verse, the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾ [al-Najm 39]?
* **The Shaykh:** It will come to us, if Allah wills, the answer to it.
* **Student:** (...)
* **The Shaykh:** I say that it will come to us, if Allah wills, the answer to this, to their evidence, those who said that a person does not benefit from the deed of another. We mentioned the evidence of those who said that he does benefit, and we will answer, if Allah the Exalted wills, the evidence of those who say that he does not benefit.
* **Student:** O our Shaykh, the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three," or "a righteous child who prays for him." The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), "deeds come to an end," means that nothing comes to him (...) and he does not benefit from another's, rather supplication and his child (...)?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, there is no problem with this. It is a disconnected exception (*istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ*). Do you not know the disconnected exception? It is when the exception is not of the same kind as what it is excepted from.
* **Student:** How would the meaning be?
* **The Shaykh:** The meaning of the hadith is: when a person dies, his deeds come to an end, except for a continuing charity or knowledge from which benefit is gained. This is clear, this is from his deeds. Or a righteous child who prays for him: this is a disconnected exception. That is, if a righteous child prays for him, he benefits from it.
* **Student:** The hadith that was reported as the reason for the revelation of these verses, ﴿The Messenger believes﴾. The Companions came and said: "We have been burdened with what we cannot bear, and a verse was revealed that we cannot bear, and it is this verse." Is this evidence for the permissibility of burdening with what cannot be borne? Because the Messenger (ﷺ) approved of them and did not say to them "no." "Say: We hear and we obey" [[Narrated by Muslim, no. (126 (200)), from Ibn ʿAbbās.]] (...).
* **The Shaykh:** When the verse ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 102] was revealed, in reality, although some scholars called it *naskh* (abrogation), it is abrogation according to the terminology of the earlier scholars, meaning specification (*takhṣīṣ*). Although some of them applied the term naskh to it, the correct view is that it is not abrogation; it falls under specification.
* **Student:** When this was revealed: ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, they came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we cannot bear it." So here they said, "We cannot bear it," and the Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Say: We hear and we obey."
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, what they meant by not being able to bear it is that something comes upon our hearts that we cannot repel. This concerns the action of the heart. That is, when something comes upon the heart that cannot be repelled, one cannot bear it.
* **Student:** So there is no evidence for this?
* **The Shaykh:** There is no evidence. Perhaps what they meant by it is the severe difficulty in guarding against it.
* **Student:** Shaykh, the recitation of the Qurʾān, if it is general without specification, meaning (...)?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, except what the text has reported. For example, if someone recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ and dedicates it to the dead, there is nothing wrong with it, because it equals one third of the Qurʾān. Likewise al-Fātiḥah, the greatest surah in the Book of Allah.
* **Student:** Shaykh, the saying of the Messenger of Allah, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him, "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three," and he mentioned continuing charity. So if a person earns, for example, a person who built a place of amusement and died, is the sin of this place borne by one who engaged in it, meaning committed a sin? Does he bear its burden?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, yes, yes.
* **Student:** So his deeds did not come to an end?
* **The Shaykh:** This is not continuing charity. This is a continuing punishment.
* **Student:** Shaykh, as for when a person repents and he has an evil deed, and its sunnah spread among people (...) but he repented, is it not (...)?
* **The Shaykh:** It is obligatory for him to break that idol.
* **Student:** He was not able to.
* **The Shaykh:** If he is not able, the obligation falls from him, yes.
* **Student:** The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾, does it fall under the saying of Allah: "I have done"?
* **The Shaykh:** All these sentences say, "I have done."
* **Student:** The saying of Allah: ﴿and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾, does it include legislative and divine decreed burdens?
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, yes.
* **Student:** (...) what they have no ability to bear.
* **The Shaykh:** No. You are now supplicating. Did you understand or not? You are asking Allah, glorified and exalted, with that. If you call upon Allah sincerely, then these calamities that some people may not be able to bear, Allah will carry them for you, and they will be easy for you, like the Day of Resurrection, which is easy for the believers and not easy for the disbelievers.
* **Student:** If they befall a person?
* **The Shaykh:** If they befall him, they become easy for him, as though they were nothing.
* **Student:** If they are not made easy, then either he did not supplicate, or he did not supplicate...
* **The Shaykh:** Or he did not supplicate sincerely, or for some other reason.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shayṭān. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the reward of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾ [al-Baqarah 286].

We have derived several benefits from this verse:

* One: the ease of the Islamic religion. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾.
* Two: that acts of worship vary according to the condition of the one who is obligated. We may require this man to pray standing, for example, and not require the other. We may require this one to spend, and not require the second. We may require this one to fight, and not require the second, and so on. Obligations vary according to the addressee, or according to the one who is obligated.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person has a limited capacity, from His saying: ﴿beyond its capacity﴾. A person has a limited capacity in everything: in knowledge, in power, in understanding, in memory. Everything has a limited capacity, and one is obligated according to his capacity.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person has what he earns, directly or through the agency of others, from His saying: ﴿It will have [the reward of] what it has earned﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person cannot be wronged by having even one of his good deeds diminished, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿what it has earned﴾. And ﴿what﴾ here is a relative pronoun that indicates generality, meaning everything it has earned.
* Also among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person bears the burden of what he has earned, from His saying: ﴿what it has earned﴾.
* It follows from the difference in expression that a person is not held accountable for merely intending an evil deed, from His saying: "earned" (*iktasabat*), and the ta' indicates what? It indicates the act itself and direct doing, unlike the reward for righteous deeds, since a person is rewarded for his intention. That is why He said: ﴿what it has earned﴾.
* Among them: it is not permissible for a person to bear another's burden for his own sin, but it is permissible for a person to have the reward of a righteous deed credited to another, from His saying: ﴿and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾. So if a person performs a forbidden deed and says, "O Allah, record the burden of this upon my enemy, so-and-so," is that possible?
* **The students:** It is not possible.
* **The Shaykh:** Good. If he performs a righteous deed and says, "O Allah, record the reward of this for my father, or my brother, or for so-and-so among the people," this is valid, and this is the benefit of His saying: ﴿It will have [the reward of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that righteous deeds are an acquisition (*kasb*) and sinful deeds are a loss (*gharm*). This is derived from His saying: ﴿lahā﴾ ("it will have") and from His saying: ﴿ʿalayhā﴾ ("it will bear"). For ʿalā (upon) clearly indicates a loss, and the lām clearly indicates an acquisition.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mercy of Allah, glorified and exalted, toward creation, in that He taught them a supplication to call upon, and answered them, in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾.
* Among its benefits: that a person should, in supplication, invoke the attribute that is appropriate, such as Lordship (*rubūbiyyah*), by which creation and its management exist. That is why most of the supplications in the Qurʾān all begin with an attribute of Lordship, such as "Our Lord" or "Lord." ﴿And Noah said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller﴾ [Nūḥ 26]; and Abraham said: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray﴾ [Ibrāhīm 36], and similar examples.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the lifting of accountability for forgetfulness and ignorance, from His saying: ﴿Do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾. Allah, the Exalted, said: "I have done."

Does lifting the requirement of repetition necessarily entail the removal of the demand? The answer: No. The lifting of accountability does not necessarily entail the removal of the demand. Whoever abandons an obligation through forgetfulness or ignorance must repeat it; the demand is not removed, and it becomes obligatory for him to perform it. That is why the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers it."[[Hadith agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhārī no. (597), Muslim no. (680 (309)), and al-Bazzār no. (6320), with his wording, from Anas ibn Mālik.]] And when the man who did not calm himself in his prayer prayed, he said to him: "Go back and pray, for you have not prayed,"[[Hadith agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhārī no. (757), and Muslim no. (397 (45)), from Abū Hurayrah.]] and he did not excuse him because of ignorance, even though he did not know how to do better than that. So the lifting of accountability for forgetfulness and ignorance does not remove the demand. Does it remove the sin of the prohibition? The answer: Yes, it removes the sin of the prohibition. Can we say that in the case of a prohibition the demand is not removed? Yes. How is the demand not removed? Because the prohibition is a demand to abandon it. If you do it through forgetfulness or ignorance, the ruling is not lifted; the ruling remains, and the demand to abandon it remains. But the difference between a prohibition and a command is that a command demands bringing something into existence, while a prohibition demands abstention. So this man who committed the forbidden act through ignorance or forgetfulness, we say: it is as though you had not done it. Therefore, if the prohibited act entails the invalidation of the act of worship, the act of worship is not invalidated. If it entails an expiation (*kaffārah*), the expiation is not established. Why? Because accountability for that forbidden act has been lifted, and when accountability for it is lifted, its existence becomes like nonexistence, as though nothing had happened. That is why we say: if a person ate while fasting through forgetfulness, his fast is valid, as the Sunnah has shown. And if he ate in ignorance, thinking the sun had set, and then it became clear that it had not set, his fast is valid, as the Sunnah has brought. But if he had sexual intercourse in ignorance that intercourse invalidates the fast?
* **Student:** (...)
* **The Shaykh:** Be careful: ignorant that it invalidates the fast, but he knows that it is forbidden. As long as he has knowledge, knowledge of the consequences of the forbidden act is not a condition. It is not a requirement, so long as you know that it is forbidden and that it has a consequence for you. So if he had intercourse, knowing that intercourse is forbidden, but not knowing that he is liable to this severe expiation, we say: the expiation is obligatory upon you, because you violated the prohibition knowingly. Do you understand now? Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) did not waive the expiation from the man who had intercourse during Ramadan, even though he did not know what he was liable for, and came asking what he owed. But he knew it was forbidden. This differs from a person who did not know it was forbidden: he bears no sin, no make-up obligation, and no expiation. The difference between them is, I think, clear.

A man has intercourse during Hajj before the first tahallul (the partial exit from ihram). He does not know the ruling and thinks that once a person has stood at Arafah, his Hajj is complete. On the night of Muzdalifah, the night of the Eid, he is with his wife, sleeps with her and has intercourse with her. It is said to him: Why? He says: Because the Messenger ﷺ said: «The Hajj is Arafah»[[Narrated by Ibn Majah (3015), al-Tirmidhi (889) and al-Nasa'i (3016), from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mur al-Dili.]] "The Hajj is Arafah," so I performed Hajj. This is what I understood. Is his Hajj invalidated? It is not invalidated. Is there an expiation (kaffarah) upon him? No, because the ignorant person, as the noble verse indicates, is not held accountable, and when a person is not held accountable for doing a prohibited act, its occurrence is like its non-occurrence.

A man swears that he will not speak to Zayd, then he sees a person among the people and speaks to him, but he does not know that it is Zayd. There is no expiation upon him, because he is ignorant. And God says, when He said: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾. He said: "I have done so." So this is the principle. If someone says: You mentioned that acts of obedience (al-awamir) must be performed as commanded, so what is dropped from him at that point? We say: What is dropped from him is the sin, because if he performed the commanded act in an invalid manner deliberately, he would be sinful, yes, in an invalid manner and deliberately, he would be sinful, because he would be like one who mocks the signs of God. For example, if he prayed while in a state of impurity (hadath) knowing that he was in that state, would he be sinful or not? He would be sinful. If he prayed in a state of impurity, forgetting his impurity, does he sin? He does not sin. So we have understood the absence of accountability. But do we oblige him to repeat the prayer? Yes, we oblige him, because this is an act commanded. Thus it becomes clear the reason why one who performs the commanded act in an invalid manner, while forgetful or ignorant, is not held accountable, and if we command him to repeat it, that is because he is not sinful by this act. Do you not know that Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: If a person prays in a state of impurity while knowing and remembering it, he has disbelieved, he has left Islam. Why? Because he is mocking the signs of God. We say: If he prayed forgetfully or ignorantly, he has not disbelieved and there is no sin upon him, because one is not held accountable for ignorance and forgetfulness. But, in view of the continuing demand, it is obligatory upon him to perform what is required.

Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person's act occurs by his own choice. In it there is a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists), who say that a person is compelled in his deeds, and that when a person does an act by choice, he is like one who is compelled in his act; the movement of a person by his choice is like the movement of a palm frond in the wind, not by its own choice. Do you understand? Is this view false or not? There is no doubt, it is false, both by revelation and by reason. As for revelation, the many texts confirm that a person's act occurs by his own will: ﴿Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾ [Al Imran 152] and ﴿for whoever among you wills to take a straight path﴾ [At-Takwir 28]. As for reason, if a person were compelled in his actions, God's punishment of him would be injustice, for how could He compel him to something and then punish him for it? Is it not so?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good. They claim that injustice is for a person to dispose of another's property, and God's disposal of His own property is not injustice, even if He punishes the obedient, He is not unjust. But we say: Even if it were supposed that He punished the obedient, that would be injustice, because God said: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, he will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾ [Ta-Ha 112]. So He negated injustice from Himself, may He be exalted. The point is that this is not the place to expand on this issue. But in the verse there is a refutation of the Jabriyyah, and the refutation is this: God lifted accountability from the ignorant and the forgetful, because the ignorant and the forgetful did not intend the violation. This shows that what a person is held accountable for is what proceeds from knowledge and awareness, and it occurs by what? By his will, because he is held accountable for it. He said: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that forgetfulness befalls human beings, and error befalls human beings. What is the evidence? ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾. If this were not something that befalls them, then supplicating for non-accountability for it would be meaningless and futile. Every person forgets, every person errs. «Every child of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent»[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2499) and Ibn Majah (4251), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «I am only a human like you; I forget as you forget»[[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (401) and Muslim (572), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]].

If someone says: What is the wisdom in God, glorified and exalted, making human beings forget and err?

We say: The wisdom is so that a person may realize his weakness, that he is weak, weak in comprehension and weak in retention, in every state; and so that thereby the bounty of God upon him in knowledge and memory may be made clear, and similar things through which forgetfulness and ignorance occur; and so that a person may be in need of his Lord, may He be exalted, in lifting forgetfulness and ignorance from him, so he turns to God, may He be exalted, and says: O God, preserve for me what I have learned, preserve for me my religion, preserve for me my knowledge, and similar things, which make it necessary for a person to be in need of his Lord when he knows that his state is forgetfulness and what? Error.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: God's favor upon this Ummah by lifting the burdens (al-isr) which were laid upon those before us. Because of His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us﴾. Then God said: "I have done so." This shows that this Ummah has had the burdens and shackles that were upon those before it lifted from it, and this is indeed so, and praise be to God.

* Among them: that this Ummah has had the ruling of forgetfulness lifted from it.

﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾ [Al-Baqarah 286]

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that forgetfulness befalls human beings, and error befalls human beings. Its evidence: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾. If this were not something that befalls them, then supplicating for non-accountability for it would be meaningless and futile. Every person forgets, every person errs. «Every child of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent»[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2499), Ibn Majah (4251), and al-Darimi (2769), from the hadith of Anas. ]]. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «I am only a human like you; I forget as you forget»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (401) and Muslim (572/89), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. ]].

If someone says: What is the wisdom in God, glorified and exalted, making human beings forget and err?

We say: The wisdom is so that a person may realize his weakness, that he is weak, weak in comprehension and weak in retention, in every state; and so that thereby the bounty of God upon him in knowledge and memory may be made clear, and similar things through which forgetfulness and ignorance occur; and so that a person may be in need of his Lord, may He be exalted, in lifting forgetfulness and ignorance from him, so he turns to God, may He be exalted, and says: O God, preserve for me what I have learned, preserve for me my religion, preserve for me my knowledge, and similar things, which make it necessary for a person to be needy of his Lord when he knows that his state is forgetfulness and what? Error.
