* Among the benefits of the noble verse: God's favor upon this Ummah by lifting the burdens which were laid upon those before us, because of His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us﴾. Then God said?

* A student: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us﴾.

* The Shaykh: No, it is not like this. Did we not accept the burden?

* A student: God said: "I have done so."

* The Shaykh: God said: "I have done so."

So we say: God said: "I have done so," and this shows that this Ummah has had the burdens and shackles that were upon those before it lifted from it, and this is indeed so, and praise be to God.

* Among them: that this Ummah has had the ruling of forgetfulness lifted from it, because of His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾.

If someone says: What do you say about the saying of God, the Exalted, in the story of Adam: ﴿And We had already taken a pledge from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no resolve﴾ [Ta-Ha 115]?

We say: This is among what God lifted from this Ummah: forgetfulness was lifted from this Ummah. As for Adam, he was held accountable for it, because He said: ﴿He forgot, and We found in him no resolve﴾ [Ta-Ha 115]. So in the law of Adam a person was held accountable for forgetfulness. Moreover, some of the people of knowledge said: The intended meaning of forgetfulness in the story of Adam is abandonment, because forgetfulness is used to mean abandonment, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They forgot God, so He forgot them﴾ [At-Tawbah 67], meaning: He abandoned them.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that those before us were obligated with what is greater than what we were obligated with, because of His saying: ﴿as You laid upon those before us﴾ [Al-Baqarah 286], and we have previously mentioned an example of this in the tafsir. Who will bring it?

* A student: First: among the Jews, if a person killed one of them, he would be killed for it, whether his guardian pardoned him or not. And among the Christians, if a person killed one of them, the obligation is pardon.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* A student: God, may He be mighty and majestic, revealed to the Children of Israel that if they wanted to repent, they should kill themselves.

* The Shaykh: When they worshipped the calf specifically, God made their repentance to be that they kill themselves. Two examples suffice.

Good. ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾.

* Also derived from the noble verse: that a person should ask God for well-being, such that He does not burden him with what he cannot bear. In it there is a refutation of some of the Sufis, I mean the Sufiyyah, who said: "We do not ask God, exalted, to protect us from what is difficult for us, because we are His servants, and if what is difficult befalls us, we will endure it." There has passed before us the story of Sahnun the Maliki, who said, among what he said addressing God: "However You will, test me," meaning: I am patient, however You will, test me. So he was tested with difficulty in urination, and he could not urinate easily. He would come to the kuttab (Qur'an schools), to the small children in the schools, and say: "Pray for your uncle, the liar." He came to the small children because they are closer to being answered, since sins are not recorded against them. He says: "Pray to God for me, your liar uncle," why? Because he lied. Did he endure patiently or not?

* The students: He did not endure.

* The Shaykh: He did not endure. Therefore a person should ask God for well-being, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «Do not wish for the encounter with the enemy, but ask God for well-being; and when you meet them, be patient»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2966) and Muslim (1742/20), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa.]]. This is derived from His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that a person should ask God for pardon, because a person is not free from shortcoming in the commanded acts, so he asks God for pardon for his shortcoming, as in His saying: ﴿and pardon us﴾, and asking God for forgiveness of the sins he has committed, because if a person is not forgiven, sins accumulate upon him, cover his heart, and perhaps destroy and ruin him. Because of His saying: what?

* The students: ﴿and forgive us﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿and forgive us﴾.

* Also among its benefits: that a person should ask God to have mercy on him in the future of his affairs, so He pardons what has passed, forgives, and has mercy in what? In the future. Because of His saying: ﴿and have mercy on us﴾. And through this we know the difference between these three expressions: seeking pardon for neglect in what?

* The students: In acts of obedience.

* The Shaykh: In acts of obedience, in the commanded, and seeking forgiveness for committing prohibited acts, and mercy regarding what a person faces in his time, that God has mercy on him and enables him to do what is in his interest.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the believer has no protector except his Lord. Because of His saying: ﴿You are our Protector﴾. In it is the affirmation of God's guardianship, may He be mighty and majestic. It has passed before us in the tafsir that guardianship is of two kinds: general and specific. The general means that God manages all the affairs of creation, whether believer or disbeliever, righteous or wicked, sinful or just. And the specific, which is His guardianship of whom?

* The students: Of the believers.

* The Shaykh: Of the believers. ﴿Unquestionably, the allies of God will have no fear, nor will they grieve. Those who believed and were fearing God﴾ [Yunus 62, 63]. We also say, regarding the most specific guardianship, which is for the messengers, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed God is his Protector﴾ [At-Tahrim 4].

* Also among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of God's active attributes (sifat fi'liyyah), may He be mighty and majestic: "Pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people."

This is the position of the Salaf (the early generations): that God, may He be mighty and majestic, has attributes connected to His will and His volition, whose type is eternal and whose individual instances are temporal. The type is eternal, and it is the genus of the act, while the individual instances are temporal. All the acts that God performs, their genus is eternal, because God has always been and still is an active doer. As for their individual instances, they are temporal. Let us suppose, for example, that God provides sustenance for a person. When does He provide it? When it exists. So is this act temporal or not? It is temporal. Yes, God descends to the lowest heaven every night; this occurs, every night there is a descent, and when dawn rises the descent ends. Likewise, regarding all the active attributes, we say: our belief concerning them is that their genus or type is eternal and their individual instances are temporal.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person must turn to God, may He be mighty and majestic, for victory over the disbelieving people, because of His saying: ﴿so grant us victory over the disbelieving people﴾.

* Among its benefits: taking the means, or alerting to taking the means, because of His saying: ﴿so grant us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. Because it is not possible to ask for victory while you are on your bed; you must act. ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ [Al-Anfal 60]. For everything you ask God, may He be mighty and majestic, you are commanded to perform its causes. If someone says: "O God, grant me victory over the disbelieving people," but he does not move in his house, this is not sound. Well, will He grant you victory over the disbelieving people while you do not fight them?

Victory requires action, and victory is a help in this; God helps you against them.

If someone says: "O God, grant me a righteous child," but he has not married, is this possible? From where will the child come? Will it sprout from his head?! It is not possible. He must marry, otherwise the supplication is void. So everything you ask God, may He be mighty and majestic, you are commanded to perform its causes, because your asking the Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, is so that He will help you and facilitate the causes that you cannot accomplish by yourself. You may marry, for example, you can marry, you have married for example. Can you create a child? No: ﴿Have you considered what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 58, 59].

So this is up to God, and the origin of facilitating marriage, for example, is from God, may He be exalted; you turn to God.

Likewise, seeking victory over the disbelieving people also requires performing the cause.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disbeliever is an enemy to us. For this reason we asked God to grant us victory over him, not that we grant him victory. The evidences that the disbeliever is an enemy to the believer are many in the Book and the Sunnah. And since he is an enemy to us, reason and the Law require that we take him as an enemy, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ [Fatir 6].

As for knowing that he is an enemy and then taking him as an ally, this is foolishness in reason and error in religion. It is obligatory that we not trust any disbeliever, however much friendship and affection he displays, for he is an enemy; because of His saying: ﴿so grant us victory over the disbelieving people﴾.
